# Bottom-up Layer Integration Point IP-10A

Freeze the smallest shared contract that allows the HumanEpochService consumer to land before the full assignment-controlled producer. Use only Provenance Decision/Evidence facts, typed material events, bounded Facts queries, ExactFact/CurrentFact conditions, and the sole Journal.Apply authority. Do not add a ledger, FSM, store, table, public revision, dynamic evidence kind, test-only authority, CLI flag, compatibility shim, or downstream command implementation.

## Exact ownership

- internal/tasks/epoch_service.go
- internal/tasks/epoch_service_contract_test.go
- new internal/tasks/epoch_authority.go
- new internal/tasks/epoch_authority_test.go
- internal/tasks/epoch_human_service.go only for mechanical extraction/adaptation of the existing candidate subject-state DTO and constructors into epoch_authority.go; do not add Implementation UAT or Land gates in this leaf

No material_events.go, policy_set.go, existing epoch_human_service_test.go, assignment/review/candidate command, CLI, handler, runtime, codegen, acceptance, Provenance, provadapter, generated, Nix, or hook file may change.

## Final public API

Add `type RepositoryID string` and `type GitRef string`. Change `SetSliceCandidateInput.Repository`, `SliceCandidateReplacement.Repository`, `RepositoryCandidate.Repository`, `PublishRepositoryInput.Repository`, and `PublicationResult.Repository` to RepositoryID; change `PublishRepositoryInput.Ref` to GitRef. Reuse provenance.GitOID. No compatibility aliases or string overloads.

Keep ImplementationUATInput and LandInput unchanged. They do not carry review fact IDs, publication fact IDs, journal revisions, or evidence arrays. The service resolves current authority from the store so the ratified CLI remains byte-exact and callers cannot nominate stale evidence.

## Private typed evidence contracts

Define private typed EvidenceKind constants:
- pasture.integration.candidate.v1: current candidate lifecycle state, retained as the single candidate-state family
- pasture.implementation-review.authority.v1: current implementation-review authority for one integration candidate
- pasture.integration.candidate-manifest.v1: immutable exact candidate membership
- pasture.integration.publication-set.v1: current complete publication verification set
- pasture.implementation-uat.review-binding.v1: exact review fact bound by one Implementation UAT

Define reviewAuthorityState as a closed nonzero enum: reviewStarted, reviewFinalizedRevising, reviewFinalizedClean, reviewInvalidated. Define reviewAxisAuthority as `{Axis ReviewAxis, Event provenance.JournalID, Verdict Verdict}`. Define implementationReviewAuthority as `{Epoch EpochRootID, Candidate IntegrationCandidateSetID, Round ReviewRoundID, State reviewAuthorityState, Axes [3]reviewAxisAuthority, Operation provenance.OperationID}`. Started has a round and zero axes; finalized states require canonical correctness/test-quality/elegance order with three distinct nonzero events; clean requires all ACCEPT; revising requires at least one REVISE; invalidated records the prior round and no accepted authority.

Define candidateMember as `{Repository RepositoryID, Candidate ImplementationCandidateID, Commit provenance.GitOID}` and integrationCandidateManifest as `{Epoch EpochRootID, Candidate IntegrationCandidateSetID, Members []candidateMember, Operation provenance.OperationID}`. Members are nonempty, unique by Repository and Candidate, and canonically sorted by Repository then Candidate. Empty/malformed repository IDs and Git OIDs fail before Apply.

Define repositoryPublication as `{Repository RepositoryID, Candidate ImplementationCandidateID, Ref GitRef, Commit provenance.GitOID, VerificationOperation provenance.OperationID}` and candidatePublicationSet as `{Epoch EpochRootID, Candidate IntegrationCandidateSetID, Publications []repositoryPublication, Operation provenance.OperationID}`. Publications are unique and canonically sorted by Repository then Candidate. The set is a complete current snapshot, not an append-only parallel ledger.

Move the existing candidate subject-state DTO to the shared file and replace its implicit decision-only source with a closed source union: human states carry exact DecisionLedgerEntryID plus DecisionKindID; assignment-produced current/reworked states carry the producing OperationID and no fabricated decision. Provide separate private constructors for human-decision and assignment-operation states. Preserve one candidate EvidenceKind and reject impossible state/source combinations.

Provide private constructors/decoders and exact selector helpers returning canonical provenance.Effect and provenance.Condition values. Review and publication-set selectors are task-exact CurrentFact selectors; manifest is task-exact ExactFact; candidate lifecycle uses task-exact CurrentFact. Constructors validate typed values and canonical order before creating EffectEvidence. Material events remain audit references and never become a second authority.

## Producer protocol frozen here

Later Slice 57.2 commands must use these production constructors in their existing single Apply:
- CreateIntegrationCandidate appends manifest plus assignment-sourced current candidate state.
- StartReview appends reviewStarted; FinalizeReview appends finalized-clean or finalized-revising in the same Apply as ReviewRoundFinalizedEvent; ReworkIntegrationCandidate appends reviewInvalidated and assignment-sourced reworked candidate state for the old candidate plus manifest/current state for the replacement.
- PublishRepository resolves the manifest, folds the prior publication set, replaces/adds exactly one member verification, and appends the complete sorted publication set in the same Apply as GitRemoteRefVerifiedEvent. It conditions on the exact manifest and prior current publication set.

## Compact contract proof

Use real file-backed Provenance and production constructors. Prove one clean review fact becomes stale after reviewStarted/reviewInvalidated under CurrentFact; prove one two-member manifest plus successively completed publication set rejects an old CurrentFact after republish; prove canonical ordering and duplicate/malformed rejection. Do not implement assignment commands or exhaustive permutations.

## Acceptance criteria

Given the shared contract compiles, when source ownership is inspected, then only the five declared files changed and epoch_human_service.go changes are mechanical extraction/adaptation; should not implement the consumer gates or downstream producers.

Given a clean finalized review fact, when a later review/rework authority fact is appended, then CurrentFact on the old clean row fails transaction-locally; should not scan a material event as authority.

Given a candidate manifest and publication snapshots, when publications are normalized, then exact repository/candidate/ref/commit values are unique and deterministic; should not use dynamic evidence kinds or one mutable row per repository.

Given public inputs, when API compatibility is checked, then repository and ref fields are strongly typed while ImplementationUATInput and LandInput expose no fact IDs/revisions; should not add optional legacy fields.

## Race-only gates

- nix develop path:. -c gofmt -d internal/tasks/epoch_service.go internal/tasks/epoch_service_contract_test.go internal/tasks/epoch_authority.go internal/tasks/epoch_authority_test.go internal/tasks/epoch_human_service.go
- nix develop path:. -c go vet ./internal/tasks
- nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...
- nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/tasks -run "TestEpochAuthority|TestEpochServiceContract"
- nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./internal/tasks
- nix develop path:. -c env CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -p=1 -race -count=1 -shuffle=on -fullpath -timeout=20m ./...
- nix flake check --no-build
- git diff --check

Every Go test command includes -race. Do not close tasks, commit, push, merge, modify hooks, or change GitHub.

# PROPOSAL-2: Codegen Body Integration (Simplified)

**Change from PROPOSAL-1:** Reviewer C (Elegance) correctly identified that `ProseSection` and `RecipeBlock` were over-structured for what is fundamentally verbatim markdown. The body content across all 7 skill files is free-form markdown (mixed headings, tables, ASCII diagrams, inline code, nested code blocks) that does NOT decompose cleanly into discrete typed sections. This revision simplifies `SkillBody` to a flat `Content string` with goldmark validation handling structural checks at generation time.

## Problem Space

**Axes:**
- **Parallelism:** 7 skill files can be converted independently (one slice per skill or group)
- **Distribution:** Single codebase — all work happens in `internal/codegen/` and `skills/`
- **Reliability:** Existing `TestGenerateIdempotent` tests provide safety net; goldmark adds structural validation

**Has-a / Is-a relationships:**
- A SkillFile *has-a* header (already generated) and *has-a* body (currently hand-authored)
- Body content *is-a* markdown string with an optional preamble
- BodyBehavior *is-a* ConstraintSpec (reuses existing G/W/T format — only for behaviors that appear outside the header section)
- A CodeExample *is-a* unified Example (merging ExampleElem + ConstraintExampleElem)

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Option A | Option B | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|----------|----------|--------|-----------|
| Body data structure | Typed Go structs (ProseSection, RecipeBlock) | Flat Content string + goldmark validation | **B: Flat Content** | Body content is free-form markdown; typed structs add overhead without enabling better composition. Goldmark validates structure post-render |
| Example type unification | Keep ExampleElem + ConstraintExampleElem separate | Merge into single Example type (Code optional) | **B: Merge** | URD R6 requires it; removes duplicate types |
| Template structure | New mega-template | Extend existing skill_header.go.tmpl | **Extend existing** | Rename to skill.go.tmpl; add body section below END marker |
| Goldmark usage | Test-only (current) | Production code for validation | **Production** | URD R3; validates generated heading structure |
| Migration approach | One skill at a time | All 7 at once | **All 7 at once** | URD R7; shared types must exist first |

## Scope: What Changes

### 1. Type Cleanup (R6) — Unblocks Everything

**Current state:** `schema_types.go` has both `ExampleElem` (line 154) and `ConstraintExampleElem` (line 422). They are nearly identical — ConstraintExampleElem adds a `Code string` field.

**Change:** Delete `ConstraintExampleElem`. The existing `Example` type in `specs.go` (line 22) already has `Code string`. All constraint examples already use `Example` in `ConstraintSpec.Examples`. The `ConstraintExampleElem` in `schema_types.go` is used only for documentation of the XML shape — update the comment to reference `Example` instead.

**Impact:** `schema_types.go` loses one type. No functional change.

### 2. New Types in `specs.go`

```go
// SkillBody is the complete body content for a role or sub-skill.
// It replaces hand-authored content below the END marker.
// Content is pre-formatted markdown rendered verbatim by the template.
// Goldmark validation runs post-render to check heading structure.
type SkillBody struct {
    Preamble  string           // optional intro line (e.g., link to PROCESS.md)
    Content   string           // pre-formatted markdown body (rendered verbatim)
    Behaviors []ConstraintSpec // body-specific G/W/T behaviors (reuses ConstraintSpec)
}
```

That's it. One new type. The `Preamble` is separated because every skill body starts with a PROCESS.md link that follows a consistent pattern. `Behaviors` captures G/W/T blocks that appear in the body (distinct from header behaviors already in RoleSpec). `Content` is the rest — verbatim markdown.

### 3. New Data in `specs_data.go`

Add a new top-level map:

```go
// SkillBodySpecs maps skill identifiers to their body content.
// Skill IDs are either role IDs (e.g., "supervisor") or command skill
// directory names (e.g., "supervisor-plan-tasks", "impl-review").
var SkillBodySpecs = map[string]SkillBody{
    "supervisor":              supervisorBody,
    "supervisor-plan-tasks":   supervisorPlanTasksBody,
    "supervisor-spawn-worker": supervisorSpawnWorkerBody,
    "worker":                  workerBody,
    "architect":               architectBody,
    "reviewer":                reviewerBody,
    "impl-review":             implReviewBody,
}
```

close_reason: Resolved in M1: Claude runtime contract now admits >=2.1.210,<2.2.0 and records observed host version; formal support matrix remains deferred in GitHub #63
description:
Found during S2-CLAUDE-ACTIVATION (commit 45a8cc4).

FACTS VERIFIED IN TREE:
  - internal/runtime/profiles.go builds harness contracts with mustExactContract, so VersionConstraint has min == max.
  - The Claude contract is pinned to exactly 2.1.210.
  - VersionConstraint.Allows (internal/runtime/version.go:322-330) requires min <= v <= max, so Allows(2.1.220) is FALSE.
  - The installed Claude Code on this machine is 2.1.220.

CONSEQUENCE: no Claude event can be Enabled against the pinned contract on the developer's own machine. To capture an authentic SessionStart payload, the S2 worker downgraded Claude Code to 2.1.210, captured, and restored to 2.1.220. Fixture digest sha256:30d524e5d2cb22d486faad05adbaa1a4b7e0d72cd6301f38fe18ca5e3f167003.

WHY THIS IS STRUCTURAL, NOT INCIDENTAL: Claude Code ships patch releases frequently. Exact pinning means one supported patch version at a time; every bump needs a re-pin, every re-pin needs a fresh authentic capture under P0-CAPTURE, and capture currently requires downgrading the user's editor. That is user-hostile and will not be done, which means the pin will silently rot behind reality.

There is also an unresolved safety question that S2 must answer either way: does the ingress path actually check Supports(hostVersion)? If it does, Pasture correctly withholds everything on 2.1.220 - safe but useless. If it does not, Pasture silently processes 2.1.220 payloads against a 2.1.210 descriptor - unsafe, and exactly the guessing this architecture exists to prevent.

OPTIONS:
  1. Widen to a range (>=2.1.210, <2.2.0). VersionConstraint already supports min/max; mustExactContract is only a helper that collapses them. Cheap. Risk: assumes patches never change payload shape, which is a guess.
  2. Detect and withhold on any unpinned version. Safe and honest, but the tool does nothing until someone re-pins.
  3. Invert the capture workflow: pin to whatever version the developer actually runs, and capture from it. No downgrade. Cost: the pinned set becomes whatever people happen to have.
  4. Range plus falsifiable skew detection. Admit a range, record the observed host version on every occurrence - it is provenance data we already store - and let strict per-event field validation surface a payload from an unpinned version carrying fields the descriptor does not know. Skew becomes visible EVIDENCE rather than a silent assumption, and the store-all body means the mismatch is recoverable after the fact.

RECOMMENDATION: option 4. It is the only one that neither guesses nor bricks the tool, and it fits machinery that already exists - CaptureDisposition already models unsupported schema, and the runtime contract is already recorded per occurrence. Needs a user decision because it trades a strict guarantee for a detectable one.
title: Exact version pinning makes Pasture unusable on any host but one

## VOTE: ACCEPT

### Axis: Correctness (spirit and technicality)

PROPOSAL-3 faithfully addresses the user's original request (REQUEST aura-plugins-36xu8: entire skill file produced by codegen, no hand-authored sections below END marker) and specifically incorporates all three UAT revision requirements from aura-plugins-vy4iy:

1. **Structured types restored (UAT item 1):** ProseSection + RecipeBlock + SkillBody types are present with 11 fields total. This directly satisfies URD R2 (structured Go data for body content) and the user's stated need for selective section access.

2. **Marker-bounded two-pass preserved (UAT item 2):** ReplaceBodyRegion complements the existing ReplaceMarkerRegion. The two-pass pipeline (Pass 1: header via ReplaceMarkerRegion, Pass 2: body via ReplaceBodyRegion) preserves independent regeneration of each region. This matches the user's explicit "Keep marker-bounded replacement" response in the UAT.

3. **Goldmark hybrid (UAT item 3):** Templates for generation + goldmark AST for validation AND selective section extraction via ExtractSection. This matches the user's "Hybrid: template + goldmark AST validation" response plus their note about wanting goldmark for extraction too.

### Technical Consistency

**Two-pass pipeline correctness:** The ReplaceBodyRegion pseudocode correctly identifies the END marker position and replaces everything after it. Combined with ReplaceMarkerRegion (which replaces between BEGIN/END), the two passes are orthogonal — Pass 1 modifies between markers while preserving the body; Pass 2 replaces the body while preserving the marker region. The ordering (header first, body second) is correct because Pass 1's output preserves the body that Pass 2 will then replace.

**Type simplification from PROPOSAL-1:** The removal of PhaseRef from RecipeBlock, Level from ProseSection, and Order from ProseSection is justified. I verified in the codebase:
- RecipeBlocks in skill files are not associated with specific phases (they are general bd command templates)
- Heading level is determined by template rendering (H2 for top-level, H3 for subsections), confirmed by the skill_body.go.tmpl pseudocode
- Order is determined by slice position in the Go data, which is how the existing header pipeline works (e.g., OwnedPhases, Constraints are ordered by slice position in specs_data.go)

**ConstraintExampleElem deletion:** Verified that ConstraintExampleElem appears only in schema_types.go (doc-only type for XML shape documentation) and one reference in llm/handoff.md. The existing Example type in specs.go already has the Code field. Deletion is safe.

### One Minor Observation (Non-Blocking)

**SkillBody.Behaviors type mismatch:** The proposal specifies `Behaviors []ConstraintSpec` in SkillBody, but the existing codebase distinguishes between `ConstraintSpec` (protocol constraints with ID, Command, Examples fields) and `BehaviorSpec` (role-tactical behaviors with only ID, Given, When, Then, ShouldNot). The body behaviors in actual skill files (e.g., reviewer line 227: "Given review complete when documenting then create review task...") are role-tactical and match `BehaviorSpec`, not `ConstraintSpec`. Using `ConstraintSpec` would carry unused Command and Examples fields.

This is a minor implementation detail that can be resolved during SLICE-1 without affecting the proposal's architecture. The implementer should use `BehaviorSpec` (or a shared interface) instead of `ConstraintSpec` for SkillBody.Behaviors, matching how RoleSpec.Behaviors already uses `BehaviorSpec`. This observation does not affect correctness of the overall design.

- SLICE-1 (type cleanup + new types): R6, R2
- SLICE-2 (body template + two-pass): R1, R4 (markers kept), UAT two-pass
- SLICE-3 through SLICE-6 (content encoding): R7 (all files at once)
- SLICE-7 (goldmark + integration): R3, R5 (impl-review), UAT goldmark hybrid

All URD requirements (R1-R7) are covered. All UAT revision items are addressed.

The 16-item checklist is complete and verifiable. Each item maps to a concrete implementation artifact.

### BDD Acceptance Criteria

All 7 BDD criteria are well-formed (Given/When/Then/ShouldNot) and testable. They cover: generation idempotency, body template rendering, validation, extraction, body region replacement, type cleanup, and migration fidelity.

File: internal/tasks/epoch_candidate_commands.go:452-469.

`validateReworkSubmission` checks only that the list is nonempty and each row has a valid finding/outcome/evidence shape. It never derives the prior review findings and never rejects missing, duplicate, or extra finding IDs. A rework can therefore claim completion without accounting for every review finding, contrary to the complete typed disposition contract.

Exact fix: load the current review round's exact finding set, require one disposition for every finding and no extras/duplicates, and condition that set in the same rework Apply. Add missing/duplicate/extra and fixed-without-evidence zero-write tests.

# FOLLOWUP_URD: Four-stage follow-up program — #24 wrap-up, arch refactor, M5, M4

Single source of truth for the post-M3 follow-up program. Continues the
lifecycle program (M1 Claude → M2 OpenCode → M3 Codex, all landed); this URD
covers the four remaining streams as a staged program.

# Program shape (user-decided)

- **One URD (this document), separate gated FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL per stage** —
  each stage gets its own proposal → 3-reviewer review → Plan UAT →
  ratification → FOLLOWUP_IMPL_PLAN → slices → code review → Impl UAT. A stage
  lands before the next stage's implementation begins (M2/M3 precedent).
- **Execution order: Stage 1 (#24 wrap-up) → Stage 2 (arch refactor) →
  Stage 3 (M5) → Stage 4 (M4).** Rationale: #24 clears coordination debt; the
  lifecycle-side refactor is upstream substrate for M5 (registry, inventory,
  provenance); M5 before M4 is permitted (verified: no dependency between
  them); M4 last.

# Requirements

## Stage 1 — #24 Codex bundle wrap-up

R1.1 Keep the Aura HM Codex projection: merge `461b569`
(`feat/codex-home-manager`, verified main+1, conflict-free) into aura-plugins
main.

R1.2 Land as ONE Aura PR: flake.lock advance to a Codex-bearing Pasture rev
(≥ `98fa2c8`) together with the 461b569 merge. Assertions must be provably
satisfiable at merge.

R1.3 `codex.skills.enable` / `codex.agents.enable` stay **default false**
(explicit opt-in). The asymmetry vs Claude/OpenCode (default true) is
intentional and must be documented.

R1.4 Positioning (user's words, verbatim): "the home-manager installation
exists for those who are using NixOS and want declarative opt-in. the
imperative `pasture install` work exists for those who are not doing so, or
want something more flexible with less overhead." README documents this
dual-path precedence and the divergence watch item (manifest may discover the
same skills).

R1.5 Regenerate `nix/hm-module-test-data` fixtures to real
`pasture.codex.agent.v1` content from the pinned rev so the eval check
exercises what pasture actually emits.

R1.6 Update AGENTS.md Home Manager Source Rules with the Codex destinations
(`~/.agents/skills`, `~/.codex/agents`); fix the pre-existing
skill.md/SKILL.md case mismatch.

R1.7 Emit the Codex activation audit report
`.codex/pasture-codex-activation.json` (parity with
`hooks/pasture-activation.json` and `.opencode/pasture-opencode.json`): 10
exhaustive entries from `activation.Codex0_146_0()`, 2 enabled, per-event
State/Reason/CaptureProof/ProductionProof. This un-defers k4p2z (#24 wrap-up
is the real consumer). The isolation test
`TestCodexActivationLeavesClaudeAndOpenCodeArtifactsIsolated` flips from
asserting absence to asserting presence + content; cross-harness isolation
assertions stay.

R1.8 Close out coordination: PR #52 closed WITHOUT merge with a supersession
note linking the audit; stale branches pruned (aura `origin/feat/codex-codegen`
12cc010, pasture `feat/codex-assets` after #52 closes, local M3/codex
worktree branches); GitHub #24 closed with a disposition summary.

Non-goals Stage 1: broader repo-hygiene sweep of untracked junk (explicitly
unselected); flipping Codex defaults to true; any second skill tree
(`.codex/skills`).

## Stage 2 — Architectural refactor (lifecycle-side + inventory)

R2.1 frontendRegistry: replace the hand-written `dispatchLifecycle` switch
(`internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go:160-192`) with a closed
`map[ir.HarnessID]lifecycleDispatch` registry (map-parity with codegen's
`harnessRegistry`).

R2.2 Bind-collapse: one generic Bind path typed by
`runtime.LifecycleContract[E]`; per-host data = contract constructor +
event→enum map + host label. **Behavior policy: strictest-common** — hoist
Claude's duplicate-name guard to all hosts; unified error template
parameterized by host label; error-text updates reviewed once. The per-host
typed identity field derivation and event→ordinal maps remain host-pinned
data.

R2.3 `findDeclaredField` deduplicated to a single shared source (currently
copied 4x: three frontends + waist).

R2.4 nativeresponse fold-in: the second harness switch
(`nativeresponse.Encode`) becomes a per-host encode member of the registry
row. Golden native response bytes are byte-identical after the refactor
(`{"continue":true}` Codex; `{"decision":"proceed"}` Claude/OpenCode).

R2.5 Inventory unification — namespace: ONE table keyed
`(harness, kind, id)` with closed kind enum
`{command, lifecycle-event, native-function}`. Existing IDs keep their
spelling; disambiguation is structural (typed axes), not string-prefixed.

R2.6 Inventory unification — cutover: **staged, authoring side first.** The
table becomes the SOURCE for what hostcontractgen/codegen generate
(registration manifests, activation catalogs, commandSkillDirs).
Native-function lists (`codexNativeFunctions`,
`deriveOpenCodeNativeToolNames`) remain contract-derived at runtime but are
VALIDATED against the table — the table must never bypass contract-derived
native truth. Frontends/receipts keep reading generated artifacts this stage.

R2.7 Provenance/identity/receipt semantics are NOT genericized. The typed
identity surface (Codex session_id/turn_id/tool_use_id; OpenCode
sessionID/callID; Claude's catalog) stays host-pinned. Receipts continue to
report precise host provenance (which host, which event, which fields).

Non-goals Stage 2: `codegen`→`artifactgen` rename (explicitly unselected —
recorded non-goal); full inventory consumer cutover (frontends/capability
checks read generated artifacts until a later stage); any change to emitted
artifact bytes beyond the new report and intended regenerations.

## Stage 3 — M5 (definition resolution, lineage, context disclosure, write gate)

R3.1 All four pillars are in the M5 MVP:
  (a) Definition resolution (R7): give `CodebookDefinitionRef` /
      `SemanticEnvelopeRef.Codebook` a real producer — versioned
      interpretation identity; every interpreted record answers "which
      codebook+version interpreted this". The Stage-2 inventory table is the
      codebook's vocabulary seed.
  (b) Lineage: committed occurrence links (populate the staked seams —
      `LifecycleLinkID` et al.); chains reconstructable per
      host+event+fields over time; read surface for provenance chains.
  (c) Context disclosure: `internal/lifecycle/context` — pure projection of
      committed state (ContextInput → ContextProjection) + durable disclosure
      plan/attempt/result facts.
  (d) Normative write gate — scope per R3.2.

R3.2 Write gate governs **Pasture-side write authority only**: the gate
legalizes Pasture's OWN durable writes (definition journal, disclosure facts,
state transitions), retiring the M1 static no-write proof in favor of a
normative gated path. Host responses remain Proceed-only and byte-identical.
Host-facing deny + input mutation stay DEFERRED (unchanged deferral).

R3.3 Event-set policy: **strictly current enabled sets** (Claude 8 / OpenCode
2 / Codex 2). Asymmetric lineage depth per harness is accepted and documented.
No new event enablement in M5.

R3.4 D11 disposition: **docs yield to code.** Retire D11's stated form via doc
correction in the M5 stage proposal: the activation gate IS the refusal
mechanism; M2/M3 already deliver Proceed encoding for enabled blocking events.
No code change for D11.

R3.5 Use the existing waist/legalize/backend/receipt/projection/Provenance
contracts. No second lifecycle IR, journal, or store.

## Stage 4 — M4 (raw-ingestion escape hatch, URD R4)

R4.1 Command surface: `pasture hook lifecycle raw --harness --event
--host-version --schema-version` + stdin. The extra path segment is the
visible mark; never the default path (authority §10).

R4.2 Architecture (user's words, verbatim): "raw input just adds an extra
parsing layer into each frontend adapter; after which should all flow into the
same pipeline." The raw decoder is typed and versioned, emits the same
delivery/binding material, and traverses the SAME L1→L2 verifier
(`waist.BindEvent` → `EventBinding.NewEvent`). No second semantic path, no
second L2 constructor.

R4.3 Visibility/trust markings (all required):
  (a) new closed-enum `CaptureOrigin` value (non-normative class, like
      `authored`);
  (b) occurrence envelope + receipt carry the raw-ingestion origin so
      read-back/projections always disclose the lower-trust source;
  (c) non-recommended marking in command help + generated docs + protocol
      docs;
  (d) same activation posture as native: raw path refuses events not enabled
      in the per-harness activation manifest — no wider event set through the
      hatch.

R4.4 The M5 write gate does NOT discriminate on origin ("origin marking
only"). Trust decisions remain a read-side concern.

# Priorities

1. Stage order is the priority order: #24 → arch → M5 → M4.
2. Within Stage 2: registry/Bind/findDeclaredField/nativeresponse (mechanical
   substrate) before inventory authoring-side cutover.
3. M5 pillars are one stage; internal sequencing is the M5 proposal's job.

# Design Choices (from URE, binding)

- Staged program, one URD, per-stage proposals and gates (M2/M3 precedent).
- HM dual-path positioning: declarative NixOS opt-in (HM) alongside imperative
  `pasture install` (flexible, low overhead) — both first-class.
- Codex HM defaults false (opt-in), documented as intentional.
- Bind-collapse behavior: strictest-common (dup guard hoisted to all hosts).
- Inventory: typed axes (harness, kind, id), staged authoring-side cutover,
  contract-derived native truth never bypassed.
- M5 write gate: Pasture-side authority only.
- D11: docs yield to code.
- M4: subcommand form, per-frontend raw parsing layer into the same pipeline,
  origin marking only (no gate discrimination).

# Standing deferrals (reconfirmed verbatim at this URE gate — ALL KEPT)

Rejection matrices (R8 tests); host-facing deny + input mutation; additional
event enablement (PostToolUse/Stop/SessionEnd on OpenCode/Codex and all other
not-yet-activated events); exhaustive catalogs; version matrix #63; live
Claude captures #55; issues #54, #57–#62; raw captures beyond the cleared set;
Strike provider; Grok Build provider.

Un-deferred by this program: M4 (Stage 4), M5+ (Stage 3), k4p2z Codex
activation audit report (Stage 1, #24 is the consumer).

End-vision provider set (unchanged): Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and planned
future Strike and Grok Build (no inferred host contract or implementation
scope for Strike/Grok).

# MVP Goals (per stage gate)

- Stage 1: #24 closed with all eight R1.8/R1.1–R1.7 outcomes true.
- Stage 2: registry + generic Bind + single findDeclaredField + folded encode
  + inventory table authoring generation, full suite green, golden bytes
  unchanged.
- Stage 3: four pillars operational over current enabled sets;
  Pasture-side gated writes; D11 docs corrected.
- Stage 4: raw escape hatch usable end-to-end with all four markings; native
  path untouched.

# End-Vision Goals

- One closed per-harness capability inventory that codegen, lifecycle,
  activation, and attribution all consume ("adding a host or capability is one
  row, not edits in N maps").
- Full provenance story: every durable record answers which host, which event,
  which fields, which codebook+version, and what led to it (lineage) — with
  lower-trust raw ingestion visibly marked end-to-end.
- Harness set eventually extends to Strike/Grok Build through the same
  registry + inventory "add data" path.

# Validation Cases (confirmed verbatim at URE final round)

## Stage 1 — #24 wrap-up
- Definition of done: PR #52 closed w/ supersession note; ONE Aura PR:
  flake.lock ≥98fa2c8 + 461b569 merged (defaults stay false); fixtures
  regenerated to pasture.codex.agent.v1; AGENTS.md Codex paths + case fix;
  README dual-path note; .codex/pasture-codex-activation.json emitted (10
  entries, 2 enabled, isolation test flipped); stale branches pruned; #24
  closed.
- Must pass: nix flake check incl. hm-module-test at new pin;
  codex.*.enable = true at Codex-bearing pin → exactly ~/.agents/skills/* +
  ~/.codex/agents/pasture-*.toml; report content == activation.Codex0_146_0(),
  no cross-harness leakage.
- Must fail: codex.*.enable = true at pre-Codex pin → actionable assertion;
  any second skill tree (.codex/skills) → rejected.

## Stage 2 — arch refactor
- Definition of done: registry map replaces dispatchLifecycle switch; generic
  Bind (strictest-common, dup-guard hoisted); one findDeclaredField;
  nativeresponse folded into registry row; inventory table (harness ×
  {command, lifecycle-event, native-function} × id), authoring-side cutover
  only.
- Must pass: full test suite (error-text updates reviewed once); zero
  unintended generated drift; golden response bytes unchanged
  ({"continue":true} / {"decision":"proceed"}); host-pinned identity fields
  remain per-host data.
- Must fail: table entry contradicting contract-derived native functions →
  build/CI rejects; any provenance/identity genericization → review BLOCKER by
  definition.

## Stage 3 — M5
- Definition of done: all four pillars on strictly-current enabled sets;
  Pasture-side write gate only; D11 doc correction (docs yield to code).
- Must pass: every interpreted record resolves codebook+version; lineage
  chains reconstructable over enabled events; disclosure facts durable +
  readable; Pasture writes legalize through the gate; host responses
  byte-identical Proceed.
- Must fail: host-facing deny/mutation attempt → not representable; new event
  enablement → out of scope.

## Stage 4 — M4
- Definition of done: pasture hook lifecycle raw; raw = extra parsing layer
  per frontend adapter flowing into the same pipeline; new CaptureOrigin +
  envelope/receipt tag + non-recommended help/docs + same activation gate;
  gate does not discriminate on origin.
- Must pass: raw payload (enabled event) → same L1→L2 verifier → receipt with
  raw origin visible in read-back; native-vs-raw equivalent payloads →
  equivalent L2 modulo origin.
- Must fail: raw payload for withheld event → activation refusal;
  malformed/oversized → capture disposition; no flags → native path untouched.

# Safety and delivery constraints (carried forward)

- Never install, enable, or modify Git hooks. Harness lifecycle hooks are in
  scope; Git hooks are not.
- Isolated worktrees for implementation; regenerate generated outputs from
  typed sources; zero generated drift at integration gates.
- `bd` runs from the aura-plugins workdir; pasture code lives in
  ~/codebases/dayvidpham/pasture.

# PROPOSAL-2: bin/aura-release (revised)

All BLOCKER and IMPORTANT findings from PROPOSAL-1-REVIEW addressed.

## Changes from PROPOSAL-1

### BLOCKER fixes
1. **Plugin selection by name**: marketplace.json plugins selected by name=="aura" predicate, not array index
2. **Section-anchored TOML parsing**: Regex anchored to [project] section. Match version= only between [project] header and next [...] header. Alternatively use tomllib (3.11+) for reading with regex replacement for writing (avoids reordering keys)
3. **--check mode fully defined**:
   - Standalone: `aura-release --check` (no bump argument required)
   - Exit 0: all versions consistent
   - Exit 1: drift detected (prints table of file → version)
   - --check --sync is invalid (mutual exclusion enforced)

### IMPORTANT fixes
4. **Pre-defined rollback list**: Before any writes, capture the 3 target files + CHANGELOG.md path in a rollback set. On any failure, git checkout all of them unconditionally
5. **No prior tag fallback**: If no vX.Y.Z tag exists, changelog includes all commits since initial commit (git rev-list --max-parents=0 HEAD)
6. **Source of truth explicit**: --sync reads pyproject.toml as canonical version, overwrites plugin.json and marketplace.json to match
7. **Explicit git add whitelist**: Commit stages exactly: pyproject.toml, .claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, CHANGELOG.md. Never uses git commit -a or git add .

### MINOR acknowledgments
8. **Double-bump warning**: If current version != last tag version AND no --sync, warn user and require --force or abort
9. **UTF-8 encoding**: subprocess.run with encoding="utf-8" for all git log calls

## Architecture

### File: bin/aura-release

Single Python 3.10+ script, stdlib only.

### Version parsing strategy

```python
# Read: section-anchored regex
def read_pyproject_version(path: Path) -> str:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    # Match version= only within [project] section
    m = re.search(
        r"^\[project\]\s*\n(?:(?!\[).*\n)*?version\s*=\s*\"(\d+\.\d+\.\d+)\"",
        text, re.MULTILINE
    )
    ...

# Write: targeted line replacement within [project] section
def write_pyproject_version(path: Path, old: str, new: str) -> None:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    # Replace only the first occurrence after [project]
    text = text.replace(f'version = "{old}"', f'version = "{new}"', 1)
    path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
```

### marketplace.json plugin selection

```python
def update_marketplace(path: Path, new_version: str) -> None:
    data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    data["metadata"]["version"] = new_version
    for plugin in data["plugins"]:
        if plugin["name"] == "aura":
            plugin["version"] = new_version
            break
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
```

### CLI interface

```
# Bump version
aura-release <major|minor|patch> [--dry-run] [--sync] [--no-changelog] [--no-commit] [--no-tag]

# Check consistency only
aura-release --check
```

Exit codes:
- 0: success (or --check with consistent versions)
- 1: --check found drift (prints version table)
- 2: pre-flight failure (dirty tree, detached HEAD, etc.)

### Workflow

1. Parse args
2. If --check: read all 3 files, compare versions, exit 0/1
3. Pre-flight checks:
   a. Not detached HEAD
   b. Working tree clean (git status --porcelain, ignore .beads/)
   c. Read versions from all 3 files
   d. If versions differ AND --sync not given: exit 2 with error
   e. If --sync: overwrite plugin.json + marketplace.json to match pyproject.toml
4. Compute new version from current + bump type
5. Define rollback set: [pyproject.toml, plugin.json, marketplace.json, CHANGELOG.md]
6. try:
   a. Update pyproject.toml (section-anchored replace)
   b. Update plugin.json (json.load/dump)
   c. Update marketplace.json (select by name=="aura")
   d. Generate CHANGELOG entry (git log since last vX.Y.Z tag, or since root)
   e. Prepend to CHANGELOG.md (create if missing)
   f. If not --no-commit: git add <whitelist> && git commit -m "chore: release vX.Y.Z"
   g. If not --no-tag: git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "Release vX.Y.Z"
7. except: rollback all files in rollback set via git checkout
8. Print summary

### CHANGELOG format (Keep a Changelog)

```markdown
# Changelog

## [0.3.0] - 2026-02-21

### Added
- feat: some new feature (#commit-short)

### Fixed
- fix: some bug fix (#commit-short)

### Changed
- refactor: some refactoring (#commit-short)

### Other
- chore: some chore (#commit-short)
```

Commit prefix → section mapping:
- feat → Added
- fix → Fixed
- refactor, perf → Changed
- docs → Documentation
- everything else → Other

## Nix integration
- flake.nix packages auto-wrap bin/* → aura-release included automatically
- No flake.nix changes needed

## Files
- bin/aura-release (NEW)
- CHANGELOG.md (created on first release)

File: journal_activity_condition_test.go, TestActivityCreate_ForeignOperationCollisionRollsBack (~line 118).

WHAT: The test verifies that ActivityID collision returns ErrActivityConflict and that LookupCommitted(opB) == CommittedAbsent. However, it does NOT call journalRowCount() before and after the collision attempt to verify that exactly zero new journal rows were written.

WHY: foldActivityCreateLocked writes to 'activities' (INSERT OR IGNORE, which is idempotent) and 'journal_activity_creations' (INSERT, which should be rolled back). If the SAVEPOINT rollback is broken, the activities row written in step 1 might persist even though journal_activity_creations rolls back. LookupCommitted(opB) = CommittedAbsent doesn't detect a partial write to the activities table.

WHERE: journal_activity_condition_test.go:165-183 (the collision attempt section has no row count check)

WHEN: At test time; correct runtime behavior expected, but not proven.

IMPACT: If the SAVEPOINT-based rollback of EffectActivityCreate is broken (e.g., activities INSERT persists while journal rows roll back), this test would not detect it. The journalRowCount check specifically catches this class of partial-write bug.

FIX: Before the opB Apply call, record before := journalRowCount(t, env.tr.Journal()); after the call, assert journalRowCount == before. Also verify that the activities table does not have a duplicate entry for actID by querying it directly or checking via a separate Apply with actID that succeeds (which it shouldn't, since actID is already claimed by opA).

VOTE: ACCEPT

## Axis: Elegance and Complexity Matching (Round 5)

### Focus: R9 + R10 + R11 — Merging Workflows, Operational Detail, and Figures

The central design question is how to unify three currently separate data structures — WorkflowStage (formal actions, exit conditions), ProseSection subsections (Ride the Wave operational detail), and FigureSpec (ASCII diagrams) — into a single coherent Workflows section in the rendered output. The proposal's UAT revision comment (09:53) lists three options. My assessment:

### Option Analysis

**Option 1: Convention-based matching by stage name/order**
Match WorkflowStage to ProseSection subsections by positional order (Stage 1 maps to subsection 0, etc.). This is fragile: it breaks silently if someone reorders stages or adds a stage without adding a matching subsection. There is no compile-time or test-time signal that the pairing drifted. Inelegant because it trades a small data model convenience for an ongoing maintenance hazard.

**Option 2: Add WorkflowRef to ProseSection**
Add a `WorkflowStageRef string` field to ProseSection. The template iterates WorkflowStage entries and, for each, looks up the corresponding ProseSection by matching its WorkflowStageRef. This is explicit, discoverable, and checkable at generation time. However, it creates a cross-reference between two separate data structures that must stay synchronized — essentially a foreign key without enforcement.

**Option 3: Embed operational detail directly in WorkflowStage**
Add an `OperationalDetail string` field (or `OperationalSections []ProseSection`) to WorkflowStage itself. The operational prose lives alongside the formal actions in the same struct. The template iterates one collection and renders everything in sequence.

### Recommendation: Option 3 is the most elegant — but only if scoped correctly

Option 3 is the right answer for the specific content that R9/R10/R11 require. Here is why:

1. **Colocation matches the rendering requirement.** R10 says "Ride the Wave stages belong WITH the Workflows section." R9 says "operational details complement the figure — render them adjacent." The template needs to interleave formal actions, operational prose, and figures per-stage. If the data is already colocated in WorkflowStage, the template is a trivial range loop. If the data is in separate collections, the template needs lookup/matching logic.

2. **No cross-reference synchronization.** With Option 2, you have a ProseSection with `WorkflowStageRef: "rtw-plan"` in specs_data_body.go and a WorkflowStage with `ID: "rtw-plan"` in specs_data.go. If someone renames the stage ID, the reference silently breaks. With Option 3, the operational detail is a field on the same struct — no foreign key to maintain.

3. **Proportional complexity.** Adding one `OperationalDetail string` field to WorkflowStage is a single-line struct change. The existing WorkflowStage already has `Name`, `Actions`, `ExitConditions` — operational detail is the same kind of per-stage data. This is not a new concept; it is filling in a natural gap in the existing type.

4. **FigureSpec already references workflows.** FigureSpec has `WorkflowRefs []string`. The template can match figures to workflows (it already does via `FiguresByWorkflow`). The existing mechanism for workflow-figure association is adequate. No change needed there — just render the figure after all stages of its referenced workflow, exactly as the current template does.

### What "scoped correctly" means

The Ride the Wave operational detail subsections (Stage 1: Plan, Stage 2: Build, Stage 3: Review) map 1:1 to WorkflowStage entries and contain per-stage operational guidance. These should move into WorkflowStage.

But NOT everything in the ProseSection tree should move. "First Steps", "Exploration (Ephemeral Explore Subagents)", "Critical Rules" — these are role-level operational sections that apply across the entire role, not to a specific workflow stage. They remain as standalone ProseSection entries rendered after the Workflows section.

The proposal's template ordering already has a place for both:
```
### Workflows
  ## Stage 1: ... (WorkflowStage.Actions + WorkflowStage.OperationalDetail + figure)
  ## Stage 2: ...
  ## Stage 3: ...

{preamble}
{body sections — non-workflow operational prose}
{body recipes}
```

This separation is clean: workflow-specific detail colocated with the workflow, role-level operational prose in its own section.

### Data Model Change

Concretely, the proposal should specify:

```go
type WorkflowStage struct {
    ID             string
    Name           string
    Order          int
    Execution      string
    PhaseRef       protocol.PhaseId
    Actions        []WorkflowAction
    ExitConditions []ExitCondition
    OperationalDetail string  // NEW: markdown prose rendered after formal actions
}
```

And the corresponding data migration: move the content from `supervisorBody.Sections[0].Subsections` (the three Ride the Wave stage subsections) into the `OperationalDetail` field of each WorkflowStage in `WorkflowSpecs["ride-the-wave"].Stages`. Then delete the `sup-ride-the-wave` ProseSection entirely (it becomes empty — its subsections moved to WorkflowStage, and its own Content was already "").

For the R11 heading level requirement (H2 not H3), the unified template renders each stage as `## Stage N: {Name} _({Execution})_`, which is straightforward.

### Why this is not over-engineering

One might argue: "just use convention matching (Option 1) and avoid changing WorkflowStage." But the data model change is one field. The alternative — convention matching — requires implicit positional coupling between two maps in two different files, plus template logic to zip them together. The added field is less complexity than the alternative, not more.

### Stale body content stripping (R3 revised)

Reviewer A (R4) correctly identified that "run go generate twice" does not work because ReplaceMarkerRegion is idempotent by design. The proposal must commit to explicit stripping. I agree with Reviewer A's finding and note it does not affect elegance — the fix is mechanical (a `dropSuffix` option or post-processing strip). The important thing is that it is specified concretely.

### Validation checklist stale items

Reviewer A (R4) also correctly flagged the stale "hand-authored content after END is preserved" checklist item. This is a correctness issue, not an elegance issue, but I concur it must be fixed in any revision.

### Summary

The proposal's overall architecture — single unified template, single context type, single render function, content organized by agent reading flow — is elegant and proportional. The R9/R10/R11 merge question has a clean answer: add `OperationalDetail string` to WorkflowStage, move the three Ride the Wave stage subsections there, and let the template render each stage as a self-contained unit (formal actions + operational prose + figure). This avoids cross-reference synchronization, convention-based fragility, and template lookup logic. The complexity of the data model change (one field) is proportional to the problem (interleaving two kinds of per-stage content).

The remaining issues (stale checklist item, "run twice" migration strategy) are correctness findings from Reviewer A and do not affect elegance. My vote is ACCEPT on the elegance axis.

# Proposal 26 review A: Correctness

- Reviewer: Terra
- Review effort: high
- Axis: correctness
- Vote: REVISE
- Counts: 2 BLOCKER / 2 IMPORTANT / 1 MINOR

## BLOCKER

### 1. Installer failure semantics lose pending uninstall transitions

Proposal 26 saves desired preferences before native actions, plans removal only
for `true -> false`, and treats `false -> false` as no action. If a removal
fails or remains unattempted after an earlier failure, the saved config already
contains `false`. On the next ordinary installer run, both previous and desired
effective values are false, so the component is never retried or removed.

This conflicts with the URE requirements that false actively uninstalls and
later invocations use ordinary idempotent operations. Printing `apply-cell`
remediation is useful but silently changes the promised rerun behavior to
manual repair.

Repair requires a user-confirmed choice because the current constraints cannot
all hold simultaneously:

- persist preferences only after successful actions;
- restore the previous preference snapshot after failure;
- make desired-false enforce absence on later runs; or
- explicitly ratify manual `apply-cell` remediation as the sole retry path and
  amend the validation cases.

### 2. Direct-file artifacts have no deployable runtime carrier or complete projection contract

OpenCode skills, agents, and hooks plus Codex agent TOMLs require the installed
`pasture` executable to materialize generated files. Proposal 26 and issue #39
refer only to target output roots/`TargetRootID`; they never specify `go:embed`,
an installed share tree, `fs.FS`, or another resolver that works outside a
Pasture checkout. This omits the URD requirement that a released CLI have
access to generated assets without the user's working directory being a
Pasture source checkout.

The singular `DirectFile(root, destination)` shape also does not define the
exact relative-file manifest needed to project many children into shared
directories while preserving unrelated entries. Collision and symlink
behavior is unspecified, including for the security-sensitive OpenCode hook
path.

Repair without adding a receipt or ledger:

- have #24/#27 publish immutable typed artifact manifests backed by embedded
  `fs.FS` values or an installed versioned share tree;
- make #39 consume exact relative-path/type/mode/destination entries;
- reject parent/leaf symlinks and unsafe path traversal;
- define whether an existing differing regular file is an actionable conflict
  or a confirmed overwrite;
- unlink only exact manifest leaves; and
- test the packaged CLI from an arbitrary empty working directory.

## IMPORTANT

### 1. Slice-close actor authorization has no defined identity source

`SliceCloseAuthorization` promises that workers cannot close slices, while
`MutationContext.ActorID` supplies the invoking actor. The frozen close CLI has
no actor flag, and the proposal only says mutations accept or resolve
`ActorID`; it never defines how the CLI obtains a non-spoofable or canonical
execution identity. Tests that merely inject worker versus supervisor IDs do
not prove the claimed policy.

Define the exact actor-resolution contract, forbid caller-supplied
supervisor/actor overrides on close, and state whether this is a security
boundary or protocol-policy validation. If it is a security boundary, bind the
actor to an authenticated execution/assignment context. If it is not, narrow
the claim and require the parent/supervisor's internal execution path to
perform closure.

### 2. The open capability model lacks a typed external binding-composition API

Issue #41 lets external packages define `Capability[In, Out]`, but #40
centrally owns all bindings and Proposal 26 shows only
`NewRuntimeContract(... ExhaustiveBindings)`. It does not show how an external
package or adapter contributes a version-bounded `RuntimeBinding` for its
descriptor without modifying #40, nor how duplicate/conflicting contributions
are rejected. As written, the open extension can define semantics but cannot
become runnable portably.

Add a typed build-time binding surface such as
`BindCapability(Capability[In,Out], CapabilityVersionRange,
RuntimeBinding[In,Out])`, composed before opaque contract construction.
Validate every requested capability exactly once, reject conflicts, and retain
the no-untyped-map/no-dynamic-tool-name boundary.

## MINOR

### 1. Secondary context ordering is undefined

`TaskEvent.Contexts` is a slice returned in raw stored-envelope JSON, but
neither Proposal 26 nor Provenance #4 defines deduplication or query order.
SQLite association-row order is not deterministic, so otherwise identical
event-list responses and OperationID canonicalization can vary.

Treat contexts as a set and canonicalize them by
`(EventContextKind, encoded identity)` at construction/persistence and query
boundaries.

## Harness verification note

The reviewer verified the pinned Codex 0.144.1 command spellings against the
installed CLI and the OpenCode 1.17.18 auto-discovery/config-write claims
against the pinned source. No additional harness-command mismatch was found.

acceptance_criteria:
Thus first-run false harnesses are untouched, a failed uninstall remains visible
and retryable after the preference already says false, and unrelated native
installations or identical external files are observed but never claimed or
removed. A global extension change fans out across the currently desired and
recorded managed cells.

The installer applies all cells, including its own direct-file destinations.
Home Manager independently renders the same effective schema from its per-
harness children but calls only native-managed cells; Nix owns direct-file link
transitions. Schema-validation, normalization, transition, and source-ownership
fixtures prove the two inputs agree for equivalent choices without conflating
their execution responsibilities.

Save failure invokes no native action. Any native/file failure stops immediately;
the postcondition probe updates the factual inventory where possible, earlier
completed actions remain, and later actions are unattempted. The error names what
failed, why, the cell/path/manager and stage, what remains or is unknown, caller
impact, `pasture install status`, and the exact executor-aware tagged
remediation. There is no rollback, background recovery, lock, authorization, or
cross-cell transaction coordinator. Native managers own plugin/update/cache
state; Pasture never writes private caches.

Pasture #45 publishes the exact legacy and split Claude package identities plus
fixtures; #39 alone owns this compatibility behavior. Before mutation #39
classifies native state as empty, exact v0.0.4 monolith only, split only, exact
monolith plus complete/partial known splits, or unknown. Unknown identity,
scope, version, or duplicate/conflicting rows perform zero mutation. For each
known state the frozen order is: probe/list and validate; ensure/update every
desired split; verify it; remove the exact user-scoped v0.0.4 monolith; verify
absence; remove any unselected known split; verify final state; record the
inventory. Failure at every action stops later actions, probes and records what
actually remains, and the next ordinary run resumes reconciliation without
rollback. Codex hooks finish as installed-but-requiring-native-trust-review until
the user approves them in Codex; this trust state is reported, not bypassed.

The v0.0.4 monolith transition is selection-wide and is implemented exclusively
by `apply-selection`, which has every Claude sibling's desired state. While the
monolith or an incomplete legacy transition exists, `apply-cell` fails before
mutation and instructs the caller to rerun the full installer/TUI or Home Manager
activation with an exhaustive desired selection. It never guesses sibling
intent, and a cell-level failure row prints that same full-selection remedy.

The group probes even for an all-false/no-inventory selection so the approved
monolith exception is discoverable when the supported manager is available. If
that optional read-only probe is missing, out-of-range, nonzero, or malformed,
all three never-recorded false rows are `completed` with operation
`no_op_unavailable` and a nonfatal diagnostic that unverified legacy state was
preserved; no inventory or mutation occurs. A supported valid-empty probe is the
same completed no-op, while an exact monolith enters the group removal.

A syntactically valid optional all-false/no-inventory response containing an
exact split component, near-match monolith, wrong scope/version, unknown selector,
or duplicate/conflicting rows performs zero mutation and writes no inventory.
Exact split components are reported `completed/no_op_preserved_external` with
their observed identity; near-match/unknown/duplicate/conflicting state is
`completed/no_op_preserved_ambiguous` with `ok=true` plus a preservation
diagnostic. This optional mode succeeds because no desired or managed cell
requires authority and preservation is the requested behavior.

If any Claude cell is desired true or has managed/unknown inventory, the same
initial probe failure is terminal before mutation: the first canonical required
row is `failed`, other executable rows are `unattempted`, prior inventory is
unchanged, and remediation names the exact binary/version/response repair.

In required mode, an exact desired split already present without inventory is
observed external and may satisfy desired true without adoption; an exact
external split under desired false is preserved. A near-match, wrong scope/
version, unknown selector, duplicate, or conflicting response is terminal
`failed/ambiguous_native_state` before mutation, leaves prior inventory unchanged,
and uses the appropriate ApplySelection/RerunInstaller or RerunHomeManager tagged
remediation. A managed/unknown inventory record that no longer matches exact live
identity is likewise a terminal conflict, never silently externalized.

The group crosses the classified legacy state with
all eight Claude desired combinations, executes each ensure/remove exactly once,
and skips the three ordinary Claude executors. On failure, it live-inspects all
three cells: rows already satisfying desired state are `completed`; the first
canonical unsatisfied row is `failed` with `group_stage` and the exact native
action; other unsatisfied Claude rows and later executable native rows are
`unattempted`. If all split postconditions match but monolith removal alone
fails, `claude-code.skills` is the fixed control/failure row and the diagnostic
names that shared legacy stage. Home Manager declarative rows remain live-
inspected `managed_declaratively`. Full-selection retry repeats the group probe
and converges without duplicate per-cell actions.

If live inspection after an action failure is itself missing/nonzero/malformed,
only rows with already verified individual postconditions remain `completed`.
The action-owning row is `failed` with both primary action and secondary probe
diagnostics and its inventory observation `unknown`; every other unverified
Claude cell is `unattempted`/`unknown`. No row is guessed from desired state.
Ordinary full-selection retry repairs the probe first and resumes from factual
inventory/live inspection.

## 13. Aura Home Manager migration and parity

New exact option nesting is:

```nix
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".enable = false;
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".skills.enable = true;
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".agents.enable = true;
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".hooks.enable = false;
```

OpenCode and Codex mirror this. Children remain inert until their parent is true.

The live options are not silently dropped. Aura #8 freezes this compatibility
table for one release:

| Old option | Compatibility behavior | New destination |
|---|---|---|
| `commands.enable` with all roles enabled | deprecated alias; enables Claude parent + skills | `harnesses."claude-code".{enable,skills.enable}` |
| `agents.enable` | deprecated alias; enables Claude parent + agents | `harnesses."claude-code".{enable,agents.enable}` |
| `opencode.skills.enable` | deprecated alias; enables OpenCode parent + skills | `harnesses.opencode.{enable,skills.enable}` |
| `opencode.agents.enable` | deprecated alias; enables OpenCode parent + agents | `harnesses.opencode.{enable,agents.enable}` |
| non-default `commands.roles.*` | exact legacy filtered DirectFile projection for one release | no aggregate-plugin equivalent; choose all skills or retain compatibility mode during the window |
| `commands.extraCommands` | additive user DirectFiles | `harnesses."claude-code".skills.extraFiles` |
| `agents.extraAgents` | additive user DirectFiles | `harnesses."claude-code".agents.extraFiles` |

The legacy filtered projection and the new aggregate Claude skills plugin are
mutually exclusive; selecting both is an evaluation error naming both option
paths and the two repairs. Extra files are active only when their harness and
extension are enabled, remain separate from generated plugin ownership, and are
rejected at evaluation when their canonical skill/agent identity collides with
the generated bundle or another extra. Every alias/mode emits its exact
replacement warning. Top-level module enable with no harness parent warns that
parent defaults changed to false. After the one-release window, removed legacy
role-filter options produce an actionable error; the additive `extraFiles`
destinations remain. Packages/protocol options remain unchanged.

Generated Pasture artifacts come only from the pinned Pasture source; explicitly
configured user `extraFiles` remain separately owned inputs and are never folded
into generated bundles.

Home Manager projects those pinned generated trees/files plus the separately
declared extras. Its current generation contains one fully explicit
`pasture.install.effective-selection/v1` desired document rendered from the nine
child options, and activation passes it to
`pasture install apply-selection --source home-manager`. The command
acts only on native-managed cells. Direct-file cells remain ordinary Home Manager
links at their documented paths and return `managed_declaratively` if inspected;
Nix never asks `apply-cell` to mutate them. There is no interactive TUI call,
duplicated native argv, or Nix-side operational state model. #39's native actions
update the same factual installation inventory so a failed native uninstall is
visible and retryable on activation rerun. Hooks require explicit true, Codex
hook activation preserves native trust review, and Aura #9 supplies the
validated aggregate marketplace plus gated `pasture-stable` ref.

## 16. BDD acceptance criteria

1. **Given** a typed Document, **when** constructors accept it, **then** every
   part is immutable/validated with source location and Goldmark AST, **and should
   not** expose a mutable optional-field runtime bag.
2. **Given** the canonical source roots and active-owner manifest, **when**
   inventory and strict compilation run, **then** independent discovery detects
   missing/stale/dead/symlinked owners, the scan is deterministic/read-only, a
   nonzero unclassified count blocks the gate, and post-zero native syntax names
   owner/node/range/fix with no output, **and should not** let the manifest hide
   an unlisted file or use regex-rewrite semantics.
3. **Given** a supported runtime contract, **when** an operation compiles,
   **then** exactly one exhaustive binding preserves its semantic contract and
   native fixtures pass.
4. **Given** an out-of-range/newer host or missing binding, **when** generation
   runs, **then** it fails actionably, **and should not** guess compatibility or a
   similarly named call.
5. **Given** a fresh agent continues an assignment, **when** it starts, **then**
   role/assignment/task/worktree/evidence/decisions/outstanding work are restored,
   **and should not** require session continuity.
6. **Given** SelectMany, **when** native UI lacks parity, **then** validated parent
   text returns the same distinct OptionIDs and verbatim record or reports
   unsupported, **and should not** become SelectOne.
7. **Given** an external typed capability, **when** its package contributes and
   invokes a binding through opaque descriptors, **then** its typed ID/version,
   codecs/effects/postconditions hold and exactly one compatible binding composes
   without editing #40, **and should not** expose a tool name/map or accept a
   missing, duplicate, conflicting, or out-of-range binding.
8. **Given** raw string/ID/wrong descriptor/mismatched input capability fixtures,
   **when** Go compilation/analyzer runs, **then** the specified invalid use fails
   under the accurately documented Go literal boundary.
9. **Given** a process recipe with env/dataflow/pipeline, **when** lowered, **then**
   structured argv/input/output edges preserve it, **and should not** hide
   unsupported constructs in `sh -c`.
10. **Given** any task/graph mutation, **when** Apply commits, **then** state and
    required attribution/events/contexts commit together, **and should not**
    leave either half.
11. **Given** a committed OperationID, **when** retried after reopen or
    concurrently with the same command, **then** the original result/EventIDs
    return; a read-only exact lookup returns the same result without executing
    Git or a mutation even after authority ends; absent and conflicting reuse
    are distinguished and write nothing.

13. **Given** an administrative actor and a material contributor, **when** events

14. **Given** a task-linked Activity, **when** start/end succeeds or fails, **then**

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-39 — Typed multi-harness compiler and authoritative task journal

## 1. Decision and correction from Proposal 38

Pasture will compile opaque, validated Go `Document` values into native Claude
Code, OpenCode, and Codex artifacts. Portable meaning lives in a
protocol-semantic IR. Markdown is parsed with Goldmark, not searched and rewritten
as an operational language. Native runtime calls are emitted only through an
exhaustive, version-bounded runtime contract.

Provenance will own one generic, ordered TaskEvent journal and the transaction
boundary that commits task/graph/Activity state with its events. Current task
tables remain authoritative; the journal explains post-migration changes and is
not an event-sourced replacement for historical state. Pasture owns typed
`pasture.*` event definitions and the `pasture task` CLI that generated workflows
use instead of Beads.

Native plugin registration is deliberately separate from runtime semantics. A
versioned activation contract describes public version probes, exact manager
commands or config mutation, package identities, and standalone destinations.
`pasture install` keeps the user's simple preferences separate from a narrow,
factual installation-state inventory. That inventory records what Pasture
confirmed it installed or removed, what remains, and the last actionable
failure. It is not a pending-operation queue, rollback log, authorization
system, lock, or cross-cell transaction coordinator.

Proposal 39 retains all accepted Proposal 38 invariants and resolves every
Proposal 38 Terra finding. OpenCode hooks are generated as an embedded,
auto-discovered TypeScript file for this wave; no npm publication or native npm
plugin mutation is required before the hook behavior has been verified. Target
packages publish target identity plus RuntimeContractID, while #39 alone binds
those artifacts into opaque activation contracts. Provenance lands as the strict
chain #4 -> #5 -> #14, with #4 dormant until #5 activates atomic journaling and
the migration baseline. Upstream issues publish fixtures/oracles; downstream
Aura issues alone own Home Manager parity and real `pasture-stable` promotion.
The proposal also freezes deployable embedded artifact bundles, observed
installation-state and retry semantics, authenticated-claim-free actor
resolution, one-subject/one-round clean-review evidence, complete event query
and legacy import semantics, the exhaustive nine-cell test matrix, and the
canonical implementation worktrees.

This epoch's original Plan-UAT skip is an explicit authorization scoped only to
REQUEST `aura-plugins-ydhf9`; it is not retroactively treated as a general rule.
Separately, the user now requests a reusable product feature: explicit,
default-off, per-epoch lower-interaction AFK mode. An active AFK session may defer
Plan-UAT questions and continue review/fix, ratification, implementation, and
review/fix progression, while recording every user and agent decision with typed
decider identity and stopping at Implementation UAT. It never authorizes landing,
hooks, destructive operations, secrets, unrelated external effects, or scope
outside its epoch. The current epoch continues under its existing Beads
authorization; future epochs use the typed AFK contract.
