## 9. Provenance authoritative task journal

### 9.1 Generic envelope and caller-owned payloads

```go
type EventID int64
type EventKind string
type OperationID string
type EventContextKind string

type EventContext struct { /* opaque validated kind + encoded identity */ }

func TaskContext(TaskID) (EventContext, error)
func ActivityContext(ActivityID) (EventContext, error)
func AgentContext(AgentID) (EventContext, error)
func GitContext(GitOID) (EventContext, error)

type ExtensionContextID interface {
    ~string
    EventContextDomain() EventContextKind
}

type ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID ExtensionContextID] struct { /* opaque */ }
func DefineExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    validate func(ID) error,
) (ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID], error)
func ExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    descriptor ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID],
    id ID,
) (EventContext, error)

type TaskEvent struct {
    ID          EventID
    TaskID      TaskID
    Kind        EventKind
    ActorID     AgentID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    OperationID OperationID
    Contexts    []EventContext
    Payload     json.RawMessage
}
```

EventID is database-generated and exposed once. Queries order ascending by
`(RecordedAt, EventID)` and expose both fields. EventKind/context kinds are
validated namespaced types. `EventContext` has no exported raw `ID string`
constructor or fields. Built-in constructors require the corresponding typed ID
and reject zero or structurally invalid values. Caller namespaces define a named
string-backed ID implementing the marker method plus a typed descriptor and
validator. `DefineExtensionContext` derives its kind from the named ID type's
marker; it takes no duplicate kind argument, rejects every reserved Provenance
built-in kind (task/activity/agent/git), and requires a valid caller-owned
namespace. At value construction the ID's reported kind must still equal the
descriptor kind. Built-in `string` cannot satisfy `ExtensionContextID`, so
`DefineExtensionContext[string]` is a compile failure. Only the internal
persistence codec serializes context kind plus text.

Provenance validates the generic envelope, identity syntax/references, contexts,
and payload well-formedness. It does not import or globally register Pasture
codecs. Pasture constructs an opaque typed event definition, validates its
`pasture.*` payload, encodes it, and passes it across this boundary.

Secondary contexts supplied during event creation commit atomically. A later
context attachment, when necessary, is itself a journalled mutation. Typed
constructors prevent TaskID, ActivityID, GitOID, and caller-defined IDs from
being accidentally interchanged even though storage uses a common textual
encoding. Contexts have set semantics: construction, persistence, operation
canonicalization, and query output deduplicate and sort by
`(EventContextKind, canonical encoded identity)`. Association-row insertion
order is never observable. Each context edge stores the EventID that attached
it (the original event for initial contexts, the journalled attachment event for
later contexts). Snapshot queries include only edges whose attachment EventID is
at or below SnapshotMaxEventID, so a later attachment cannot change an in-flight
filtered traversal.

### 9.2 Atomic command API and durable idempotency

```go
type MutationContext struct {
    ActorID     AgentID
    Authority   OperationAuthorityID // exact assignment or registered bootstrap identity
    OperationID OperationID
    Command     CommandDigest // opaque caller-domain canonical command identity
}

Apply(ctx context.Context, mc MutationContext, command Mutation) (MutationResult, error)

type CommittedOperationLookup interface {
    LookupCommitted(
        ctx context.Context,
        operation OperationID,
        expectedActor AgentID,
        expectedAuthority OperationAuthorityID,
        expectedCommand CommandDigest,
    ) (CommittedOperationResult, error)
}

// CommittedOperationResult is exactly one of Absent or Committed. Reuse of an
// OperationID with a different actor, authority, or command returns Conflict.
```

Provenance #4 owns the TaskEvent envelope, context storage, ordering/query APIs,
and internal append/schema primitives. It exposes no raw event-append bypass,
registered production migration, or baseline side effect. Its persistence tests
activate the schema explicitly in isolated test databases. Provenance #5
exclusively owns the public command/result table, `Apply`, and the read-only
`LookupCommitted` surface. #5 owns opaque validated `OperationAuthorityID`
constructors for exact AssignmentID-based and registered-bootstrap identities;
the ID includes authority kind and canonical underlying identity, never merely
AgentID. `Apply` records the supplied opaque CommandDigest and
the independently derived generic MutationDigest. On an already-committed
OperationID it compares actor plus CommandDigest and returns the stored result
before interpreting a newly supplied mutation; on first execution it also stores
the actual mutation digest for audit. ActorID, OperationAuthorityID, and
CommandDigest must all match for replay; exact ended authority may replay, while
same-Agent predecessor/successor assignments, slots/tasks, and bootstrap paths
conflict. The trusted typed adapter owns command-
identity construction—Provenance does not decode caller semantics.

Lookup performs no mutation: `Absent` means the
operation has never committed; exact actor/command agreement returns the stored
result map and EventIDs even when the initiating assignment has since ended; and
any OperationID reuse with different actor/command identity returns `Conflict`.
It never executes an absent command or revalidates current authority. #5 also
owns the production migration that installs the #4
schema, writes baselines, and activates atomic journaling. #4 and #5 ship in one
Provenance release tag after both merge; there is no released state in which a
database has a writable journal but non-journalled mutators.

The closed command family covers task lifecycle, typed relationships, labels,
comments, responsibility/supervision assignments, explicit attribution,
task-linked Activity start/end,
later event-context attachment, and a generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation for
caller-validated material events that change no current task state. Provenance
commits domain row(s), any required attribution, TaskEvent row(s), contexts, and
canonical operation/result through one `internal/sqlite` connection/transaction.
Pasture does not compose a fake transaction across separate tracker/audit
connections.

#5 also owns opaque `ConditionalMutationBatch` construction. It is a closed,
extension-safe declarative composition of existing generic mutations plus
caller-validated opaque material events; it is not a callback, raw SQL, or an
untyped predicate escape hatch. Its built-in preconditions cover exact task
kind/status/owner, exact active/ended assignment and active-slot set, typed
relationship presence/absence and exact incoming/outgoing typed set equality,
exact task revision plus immutable subject task/current-subject relationships, exact immutable EventID/task/kind/context
evidence, and absence of unresolved blocked-by children. Canonical typed local
handles let later batch mutations reference earlier allocated tasks/assignments;
the result returns their stable ID map. Preconditions are
rechecked inside the same SQLite transaction immediately before the ordered
mutations. Domain rows, assignment transitions, relationships, events,
contexts, attribution, and operation result all commit or roll back together.
Pasture #43 compiles review/transition/closure policy into these generic
preconditions and mutations; Provenance never decodes a `pasture.*` payload.

The closed batch API also owns one narrow zero-domain/event form:
`ConditionalExistingIDResult`. Exact typed preconditions create unforgeable
`ExistingTaskHandle`, `ExistingAssignmentHandle`, `ExistingActivityHandle`, or
`ExistingEventHandle` values; typed result-slot bindings may project only those
handles into the operation result. The form requires at least one exact current-
state/authority precondition and one handle projection, permits no allocation,
literal/scalar/arbitrary-map result, domain mutation, or event draft, and rechecks
all predicates in the Apply transaction. Success commits only the canonical
operation row and typed existing-ID result rows; rejection/fault commits nothing.
Publication uses an ExistingEventHandle produced by the exact canonical-evidence
precondition, so `pushed|already_at_target` is decoded from that protected event's
stored payload rather than injected as a result literal.
The public four-handle sum is validated table-wise in #5 and through #14: task,
assignment, Activity, and event each cover positive exact projection,
cross-domain rejection, zero and multiple projection rejection, response loss,
restart/replay, state/authority races, and every fault rollback boundary. No
public branch exists without these fixtures.

OperationID is durable idempotency identity. Same ID plus byte-equivalent
canonical command/actor/exact authority returns the originally committed
result/events after close/reopen or concurrent retry. Same ID with different
actor, authority, or command fails.
The operation row rolls back with the mutation, so there is no pending state.

Pre-1.0 direct mutator paths migrate to Apply or compatibility wrappers that
require MutationContext and delegate to the same transaction. No exported bypass
may mutate a task/graph without its event.

### 9.3 Responsibility CAS and cumulative attribution

```go
type TransferTaskResponsibility struct {
    Task          TaskID
    ExpectedOwner OwnerExpectation // OwnerIs(agent) or OwnerIsUnassigned()
    ExpectedAssignment AssignmentExpectation
    Successor     OptionalAssignmentDraft // absent means become unassigned
    Reason        string
}
```

The expected owner and current responsibility assignment are compared inside
the same transaction. Transfer ends the predecessor, optionally creates the
successor, changes Owner, and records attribution/events atomically. Two
distinct concurrent transitions have one winner; the stale loser changes no
owner, assignment, attribution, operation, or event row and receives an
actionable conflict. `ChangeTaskOwner` is only a compatibility constructor that
delegates to this transition when its full assignment expectation is supplied;
otherwise it rejects once the assignment migration is active.
This protects task assignment only; it is unrelated to plugin-installation
concurrency and introduces no installer transaction/CAS mechanism.

Task.Owner is role-neutral current responsibility. Prior/new material contributors retain
idempotent `attributed_to` edges. Administrative actors are not attributed merely
for changing a label/status; attribution occurs only for responsibility or
material contribution commands. Owner events record expected/previous/new owner,
actor, reason, OperationID, time, and EventID.

### 9.4 Activities, relationships, and graph events

`StartTaskActivity` and `EndTaskActivity` carry AssignmentID, ActivityID,
phase/stage, notes, and contexts; TaskID and AgentID are derived and validated
from that exact active assignment. Activity row state, task linkage, material event,
required attribution, and contexts commit together. Duration Activities remain
distinct from instantaneous transitions and do not encode structured changes in
notes. The state machine is closed: start requires a new ActivityID, existing
task, and actor resolved from the supplied active assignment; a new OperationID
cannot start an existing Activity. End requires the same linked task/agent and
an active Activity. End-before-start, wrong task/agent, invalid transitions, and
a second end under a new OperationID write nothing; same-OperationID retries
return the original result, and concurrent ends have one winner.

Task relationships accept TaskID targets. Attribution accepts AgentID. Activity
links accept ActivityID. A relationship involving two tasks writes a task-local
event to each timeline in one transaction, sharing OperationID and receiving
distinct EventIDs. Blocked-by cycle validation, edge persistence, and both events
share the same consistency boundary.

### 9.5 Current state and legacy migration

Current task/graph/Activity tables remain authoritative. The journal explains
all post-migration changes; it is not used to rebuild pre-journal state. When #5
activates the coordinated production migration, existing tasks each receive one
idempotent `provenance.migration.baseline` event containing the then-current
status/phase/owner and source schema version. In that same exclusive transaction,
every nonterminal assigned task receives a deterministic migration-time active
owner-responsibility assignment; every terminal assigned task receives an ended
migration assignment and has current Owner cleared; unassigned tasks receive no
assignment. Assignment IDs derive from schema version plus TaskID. Provenance
uses only its generic `provenance.role.legacy-owner` and
`provenance.slot.owner-responsibility`; it never invents a Pasture role. The task
baseline EventID is the active assignment's StartEventID at migration RecordedAt.
For a terminal legacy owner, a second ordered migration-time assignment-ended
event supplies EndEventID at the same RecordedAt; both are explicitly snapshot
events and never claim historical start/end time.

Legacy owner text that is not already a registered AgentID maps to a
deterministically registered `legacy-owner/<sha256>` SoftwareAgent whose payload
retains the original text; invalid/duplicate registration fails the entire
migration. Attribution and migration events retain that mapped owner but are
explicitly labeled snapshot/baseline evidence, never fabricated historical
start/end times. The post-migration invariant holds for every task kind: a
nonterminal nonnil Owner has exactly one matching active responsibility
assignment, while every terminal task has nil Owner and no active responsibility.
This marks the historical-completeness boundary.

The #5 production migration executes schema activation and every baseline row
inside one exclusive SQLite migration transaction. A fault after any number of
rows rolls back the schema marker, journal tables/changes, and all baselines;
reopen then performs the same migration from the pre-migration database. Empty
databases, every assigned/unassigned × terminal/nonterminal × task-kind case,
unmappable legacy owner text, repeat startup, and concurrent startup are explicit
fixtures. Baseline ActorID is the registered migrator; an absent legacy owner is
never fabricated.

Before any `pasture task` protocol/review/slice command is enabled against the
coordinated Provenance schema, the #43/application startup coordinator calls
#14's read-only legacy-assignment extraction API. #14 never invokes #43. #43
classifies only tasks carrying a reserved, versioned Pasture protocol kind and
validates the exact required topology before building one idempotent
`NormalizeLegacyAssignmentRoles` conditional batch. That batch performs
same-owner responsibility transfers from generic legacy-owner assignments to
the typed role/slot, preserving predecessor, attribution, and ordered events.
There is no separate normalization marker, table, task, snapshot, or event: the
authoritative completion predicate is a deterministic post-batch requery proving
that every eligible active assignment already has its exact mapped role/slot and
no eligible generic assignment remains. An empty eligible set therefore succeeds
without inventing a marker host.

The v1 mapping is closed and exhaustive:

| Persisted Pasture kind/topology | Normalized active owner role |
|---|---|
| REQUEST, ELICIT, URD, PROPOSAL, Plan-UAT, HANDOFF, and their FOLLOWUP forms | RoleArchitect |
| plan-review round/container | RoleArchitect |
| IMPL_PLAN, integration task, Implementation-UAT, landing container, supervisor-created follow-up epic | RoleSupervisor |
| implementation slice and explicitly typed Pasture implementation leaf | RoleWorker |
| code-review round/container and eager severity group | RoleSupervisor |
| implementation-review finding leaf | RoleWorker |
| review axis with exact correctness relationship | RoleReviewerCorrectness |
| review axis with exact test-quality relationship | RoleReviewerTestQuality |
| review axis with exact elegance relationship | RoleReviewerElegance |

Terminal or unassigned eligible tasks require no active transfer but are still
validated. A reserved known kind with missing/conflicting topology, or an
unknown future reserved Pasture kind, fails the entire batch and leaves the
database unchanged. Ordinary Provenance tasks and leaves without a reserved Pasture
kind are explicitly ineligible: their generic legacy-owner role remains valid,
they do not enter the batch, and they cannot block Pasture activation. Fault/
restart repeats the extraction and state-derived normalization safely. Protocol
commands remain unavailable until the deterministic post-batch inspection
succeeds.

Pasture #43 owns a closed, typed import command; #14 supplies only extraction and
adapter plumbing:

```go
type LegacyAuditRowID string
type LegacySchemaVersion string
type ImportLegacyAuditRow struct { /* unexported validated row */ }

func NewImportLegacyAuditRow(
    schema LegacySchemaVersion,
    row LegacyAuditRowID,
    actor LegacyActorRef,
    recordedAt time.Time,
    definition LegacyEventDefinition,
    contexts []LegacyContext,
    tasks []provenance.TaskID,

```

The constructor validates the source schema/row identity, maps the legacy kind
and payload through a typed #43-owned definition, validates every context, drops
duplicate task IDs, sorts the remaining typed IDs, and resolves the actor before
any Apply call. Unknown kinds/payload shapes or invalid/empty task fan-out fail
without writes. Pasture migrates actual legacy audit history without deleting or
updating source rows; pre/post byte hashes of the legacy tables are acceptance
evidence:

- #14's finite coordinator collects all rows and `context_edges`, validates the
  full extraction, sorts rows by `(recorded time, legacy row ID)`, and imports
  serially, stopping at the first failure so equal-time EventID allocation is
  deterministic across repeat/reopen;
- resolve every unique task ID represented by epoch/slice/review/follow-up task
  contexts;
- invoke one #43-owned `ImportLegacyAuditRow` command containing the source
  schema, legacy row ID, actor mapping, original time/payload, all contexts, and
  the sorted unique TaskIDs; it validates/encodes typed payloads and delegates
  once to Provenance's generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation;
- have that single Apply operation create one canonical TaskEvent per `(legacy
  schema, legacy event ID, resolved TaskID)`, attaching all of that row's legacy
  contexts;
- give the batch one stable migration OperationID derived from `(legacy schema,
  legacy event ID)` and deterministic event insert order `(legacy recorded time,
  legacy row ID, task ID)`; and
- enforce the compound legacy identity uniquely so repeat migration/reopen cannot
  duplicate events.

`ImportLegacyAuditRow` is atomic: every event/context/operation result for one
legacy row commits or none does. A retry with the same source identity returns
the canonical batch result and EventIDs; conflicting source content fails. An
injected failure after the first event rolls back the full row batch. This is a
finite schema import, not an event-sourcing or runtime transaction subsystem.

Migrated real events preserve their original RecordedAt and mapped AgentID. When
an old actor cannot be resolved, the migration uses an explicitly registered
`pasture-legacy-migrator` SoftwareAgent and retains the original actor text in the
typed migration payload; ActorID is never silently nil or forged. Baseline events
use a registered `provenance-migrator` SoftwareAgent and migration time. Stable
OperationIDs derive from the typed legacy-row identity through a documented
constructor, not from process-local counters.

Thus one old row linked to several tasks appears on every relevant task timeline
without losing its many-to-many contexts. #14 owns the separately named,
read-only `pasture legacy-audit event list` API for non-task legacy rows and its
raw source-identity/actor-text/context tests; #43 never folds those rows into a
task timeline. After auto-migration,
`pasture task timeline TASK-ID` reads canonical Provenance TaskEvents only; it
does not perform an unstable runtime merge with rows lacking EventID.

source or remove `bd`; issue #42 consumes the completed contract and owns that
finite conversion.

```text
pasture task contract --json
pasture task create|update|close|reopen|list
pasture task show TASK-ID [--revision DOCUMENT-REVISION-ID] [decision filters]
pasture task ready|blocked|dep tree
pasture task relation add|remove|list
pasture task assignment start|end|transfer|list
pasture task attribute add|list
pasture task label add|remove|list
pasture task comment add|list
pasture task activity start|end|list
pasture task event record|list
pasture task command canonicalize
pasture task protocol create|revise|transition|supersede|ratify|land
pasture task decision user-record
pasture task epoch afk enable|disable|show
pasture task uat plan-decide|implementation-decide
pasture task review start|submit|finalize
pasture task slice create|candidate set|rework|close
pasture task integration candidate-set|rework|publish-repository
pasture task context add|list
pasture task timeline TASK-ID [--json]
```

```text
pasture task slice close TASK-ID --assignment ASSIGNMENT-ID \
  --round REVIEW-ROUND-ID --candidate TASK-CANDIDATE-ID \
  --review-event correctness=EVENT-ID \
  --review-event test-quality=EVENT-ID \
  --review-event elegance=EVENT-ID
```

Every mutation accepts `--mutation-ref MUTATION-REF` and its exact initiating
`--assignment ASSIGNMENT-REF` or `--bootstrap-agent AGENT-REF`; typed JSON results expose
named bindings for created TaskRef/AssignmentRef/ReviewRoundRef values. Exact
flags/JSON schemas are frozen before generation. Generated workflow documents
carry typed ValueRefs plus the complete MutationContinuation; #14/#43 converts
them to authoritative Provenance IDs, resolves ActorID from the retained
historical initiating authority for committed replay and from that same active
authority for a new operation, and never accepts an actor/supervisor
override for review or slice closure. Bootstrap/administrative callers use a
separate registered-agent API and make no authentication claim. Queries are
side-effect free. Generic `task update` is available only to ordinary leaves and
changes only non-reserved descriptive metadata; it rejects every protected
subject/review/slice/protocol task and all status, phase, kind, owner, assignment,
body-revision, or relationship changes. `transition` accepts a kind-specific expected/from/to transition;
`supersede` atomically makes the successor the sole canonical proposal, relates
the successor as superseding the old artifact, and transitions the old one;
`ratify` requires accepted review-round evidence plus accepted Plan-UAT or an
exact active same-epoch `deferred_by_afk` event bound to the current
DocumentRevisionSubject, epoch root, ledger revision, and AFK session.
`land` performs no Git operation. It requires resolved dependencies plus clean
review and Implementation-UAT evidence bound to the same exact current
IntegrationCandidateSetSubject and one #43-owned typed
`pasture.git.remote-ref-verified/v1` material event per repository candidate.
It also CASes the exact current ledger `DocumentRevisionID` and recomputed required-
entry coverage digest named by that accepted UAT; any successor required entry
invalidates the UAT relation and defeats land.
That event is protected from generic recording. The sole executable producer is
the versioned application/#40 composite command `pasture task integration
publish-repository`. Its typed argv names exact current IntegrationCandidateSetID,
RepositoryID, CommitOID, TreeDigest, RemoteRef, ExpectedOldOID, controlling
AssignmentID, and MutationRef. In one Pasture process it executes this closed
sequence:

1. Before the first attempt, #40 passes the fully resolved typed request to
   #43's pure `command canonicalize` API. #43 canonicalizes one versioned
   `PublicationIntent` containing every task-command field except MutationRef and
   authority and returns its typed digest. The surviving parent then mints
   MutationRef and retains the complete continuation in AssignmentContext.
2. #40 passes the same request and complete continuation to #43's internal,
   side-effect-free `PrepareRepositoryPublication`. #43 recomputes and validates
   exact identity, rejects placeholders/mismatch, and asks #14 to map the ref,
   exact assignment-or-bootstrap authority, historical actor, and digest to #5.
   The returned opaque
   `PublicationPreparation` contains exactly the OperationID/CommandDigest pair
   plus OperationAuthorityID that any later #14 `Apply` records. An exact committed lookup returns the
   original status/EventID/result map without touching Git, including after
   authority has ended or Git is unavailable; `Conflict` fails; `Absent`
   continues. Neither #40 nor a caller can supply or inspect either digest.
3. The same #43 preparation performs a read-only publication preflight. It requires the exact current
   integration set and repository tuple, the controlling active supervisor
   assignment, one current fix-free accepted integration-review round, one
   accepted current Implementation-UAT decision, and either no canonical
   publication evidence or the one exact existing event for
   `(IntegrationCandidateSetID, RepositoryID)`. Stale, unreviewed, unaccepted,
   unauthorized, mismatched, or conflicting evidence fails before Git. Exact
   existing evidence produces an `existing_evidence` preparation without Git.
4. Only an eligible absent-evidence result calls #46 guarded push or verified
   already-at-target and retains that non-serializable success value in memory.
5. #40 returns the opaque preparation plus #46 result to #43. For
   `existing_evidence`, #43 uses #14's closed
   `ConditionalExistingIDResult`: the exact canonical-evidence precondition
   produces an ExistingEventHandle; the same current set/repository/review/UAT/
   ledger-revision/coverage/authority predicates are rechecked; and Apply commits
   only this OperationID's typed EventID result. It creates no domain row/event
   and cannot bind an arbitrary ID or scalar. For verified Git, #43 rechecks every preflight predicate inside
   one ConditionalMutationBatch and installs exactly one event/relation. The
   process-local Git proof gates this method but is excluded from
   `PublicationIntent`, so preparation, lookup, and Apply share identical command
   bytes. If a distinct operation wins the canonical evidence race, #43
   re-prepares and commits the result-only existing-event binding under the
   losing operation's same digest/OperationID. Conflicting evidence or any
   eligibility change writes nothing.

The command returns only `pasture.task.integration-publish-result/v1` with the
canonical protected event's stored `pushed|already_at_target` outcome and EventID/result
bindings—no portable verified token, evidence payload constructor, or record
subcommand exists. An existing-evidence or concurrent-convergence call returns
the original event's stored outcome. Every successful call has its own committed
operation/result row; lost-response
replay therefore returns the identical status, EventID, and bindings after
restart, ended authority, Git unavailability, or later integration rework.

Git then SQLite remains deliberately sequential, not transactional. Git failure
writes no evidence. If Git succeeds but Apply fails, retry of the same
MutationRef looks up Absent, passes a fresh read-only preflight, verifies
already-at-target, and appends; if Apply committed but the response was lost,
`LookupCommitted` returns the original EventID before any Git action. If
integration rework wins after preflight but before append, the guarded push may
have succeeded while evidence correctly fails: the error reports the advanced
remote OID, obsolete set, failed append predicate, and directs the supervisor to
construct a replacement integration set using that observed remote as its new
expected-old state, then rerun review and UAT. No rollback or stale evidence is
attempted. Partial multi-repository success is reported and resumed without
rollback. Cross-process JSON/native callers can
request only the full composite operation, so fabricated intermediate results
cannot cross the runtime boundary. #43 does not import #46; #40/application
composition imports both. Any candidate/tree/ref change invalidates the evidence
and requires new integration review/UAT. Generic `task close` rejects slice,
review, and protocol-container kinds. The exact slice CLI includes RoundID,
TaskCandidateID, AssignmentID,
and three accepted review EventIDs and lowers the §5.3 predicate and mutations
into one ConditionalMutationBatch.

`pasture task contract --json` returns the closed
`pasture.task.contract-probe/v1` schema containing CLI semver, TaskContractID,
supported schema IDs/ranges, and a canonical definition digest. Generated
artifacts embed their exact requirement. The runtime probes once before the
first task mutation and fails before writes on a missing command, malformed
probe, adjacent/unsupported version, digest mismatch, or semantic contract
mismatch; this covers separately upgraded generated packages and binaries.

Review/UAT/skill/git evidence uses typed Pasture event definitions. Protected
review definitions cannot pass generic `event record`. `event list` accepts a
versioned `pasture.task.event-query/v1`: TaskIDs are ORed, EventKinds are ORed,
typed contexts are ORed, and the non-empty dimensions combine with AND. The
first page captures `SnapshotMaxEventID`; every later page carries it plus an
exclusive `(AfterRecordedAt, AfterEventID)` cursor and ignores later inserts.
Rows are canonical stored envelopes ordered ascending by `(RecordedAt, EventID)`.
Concurrent/backdated appends therefore appear only in a new traversal, never
duplicate or disappear within the current snapshot.

`timeline TASK-ID` uses `pasture.task.timeline-query/v1` with the same snapshot
watermark and exclusive key. Its tagged rows are `point_event` or
`activity_interval`. A point sorts by `(RecordedAt, EventID)`; an interval sorts
by `(StartedAt, StartEventID)`, carries nullable EndedAt/EndEventID plus both
source EventIDs, and is open when no end event exists at the snapshot watermark.
Overlaps do not alter ordering. Folding creates no journal row, and human/JSON
renderings share the same schema. Non-task legacy rows remain only in #14's
separately named API. Errors name the effect, artifact/command, why/where/when,
impact, and fix. Issue #42's final generated-output gate rejects operational
`bd`.

Workers report completion with `pasture task activity end` followed by the typed
assignment-completed event. Generic `pasture task close` is only the ordinary-
leaf policy and atomically ends that leaf's responsibility assignment. CLI
fixtures prove that completion cannot close a slice, a worker cannot invoke
slice close, and the governing-plan supervisor can close it only with the
current accepted three-axis round through one conditional batch.

## 11. Target artifacts and independent packages

```text
generated/
  claude-code/{pasture-skills,pasture-agents,pasture-hooks}/
  opencode/{skills,agents,pasture-hooks/pasture-hooks.ts}/
  codex/{pasture-skills,pasture-agents,pasture-hooks}/
```

- Pasture #45 owns the previously missing Claude split packages.
- #27 owns OpenCode compiler/artifact output only, including the embedded hook
  TypeScript file. npm publication is deferred until native behavior is proven.
- #24 owns Codex output only: full skill directories with `agents/openai.yaml`,
  a `generated/codex/pasture-agents/` bundle containing five standalone
  `pasture_*.toml` agents, and separate skills/hooks plugins with
  `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`. The user-home destination is activation metadata,
  not the generation root.
- #39 later consumes all target outputs for activation; #24/#27/#45 do not depend
  on #39.
- Aura #9 consumes #24/#45 identities plus #39's completed contract to publish
  aggregate Claude/Codex marketplace manifests and promote `pasture-stable`.
- Whole skill/support trees survive packaging.
- Each target publishes a stable target/component descriptor plus
  RuntimeContractID and isolated-load oracle. Aura #8 later owns the exhaustive
  nine-cell Home Manager parity proof.
- Hook packages are independent and never transitively selected.

The completed explicit `EmitHarness(sourceRoot, outputRoot, ...)` work remains.
Partial regex runtime/OpenCode output is exploratory and replaced only after the
typed compiler/contracts pass.

## 12. Simple installer

Canonical preferences are exactly:

```yaml
install:
  harnesses:
    claude-code: false
    opencode: false
    codex: false
  extensions:
    skills: true
    agents: true
    hooks: false
```

This is one harness boolean map plus one global extension map—not a per-harness
extension matrix. The TUI has harness checkboxes, one global extension page,
saved choices, exact install/uninstall summary, confirmation, and progress.
Cancellation changes nothing.

After confirmation Pasture preserves unrelated YAML and saves preferences before
native actions. It normalizes the confirmed preferences to one immutable
`pasture.install.effective-selection/v1` desired document, then passes that to
`apply-selection --source installer`. TUI effective cells are
`harness && extension`. The persisted config remains simple global preferences
and never stores the normalized matrix or installation evidence.

The fixed reconciler is deliberately small:

- desired effective true: idempotently ensure present/update, including an
  unchanged true cell;
- desired effective false plus a Pasture-managed installed/unknown inventory
  record: inspect and idempotently remove the exact component; and
- desired false with no Pasture-managed or uncertain record: no mutation.

WHAT: DecodeReportedResult (decision.go:388-394) wraps EVERY error from rejectDuplicateJSONMembers as what: 'reported-result JSON has a duplicate member' — but rejectDuplicateJSONMembers returns raw io.EOF for an empty reader and raw syntax errors for malformed JSON (its decoder.Token() walk is the first thing that touches the bytes). So the two most common real-world failures — an empty/truncated stream and a JSON syntax error — are misdiagnosed as duplicate members; only the trailing ': <cause>' text tells the truth. Same wrap pattern in canonicalJSON (continuation.go:107-109, 'mutation request has a duplicate JSON member: %w').
WHY IT MATTERS: the actionable-error contract (what/why/where/phase/impact/fix, issue #38 acceptance criterion 'Diagnostics contain what/why/where/phase/impact/fix') requires the WHAT to describe what actually went wrong; a user staring at a truncated pipe being told to 'encode each field exactly once' is sent down the wrong path. Fails closed, so MINOR.
REQUIRED CORRECTION: have rejectDuplicateJSONMembers return a distinguishable sentinel/typed error ONLY for a genuine duplicate member, and let Token() syntax/EOF errors surface through a separate 'reported-result JSON is empty, truncated, or malformed' diagnostic (or pre-check len(data)==0 / json.Valid before the walk). Add tests for empty input, truncated input, and a syntax error asserting the diagnostic names the real failure, plus one genuine-duplicate case keeping the current message.

# User Requirements Document: Unified aura-swarm

## R1: Script Consolidation
Merge bin/aura-parallel and bin/aura-swarm into a single bin/aura-swarm script.
bin/aura-parallel becomes a deprecation wrapper that warns and delegates to aura-swarm.

## R2: Swarm Mode Flag
--swarm-mode {worktree,intree}
- worktree: creates git worktree per epic (current aura-swarm behavior)
- intree: operates in current working directory (current aura-parallel behavior)

## R3: tmux Destination Flag
--tmux-dest {session,window} (default: window)
- window: creates tmux windows in an existing or new session
- session: creates separate tmux sessions (legacy behavior)
- When not inside tmux: create a new session, then add windows to it
- Same session name → add window to existing session

## R4: XDG State Directory
All runtime state stored at $XDG_STATE_HOME/aura/swarm/ (default: ~/.local/state/aura/swarm/).
Use XDG_STATE_HOME env var, not hardcoded path.

## R5: Session Registry
Full observability session registry with BCNF-aligned schema.
Fields: session_id, permission_mode, model, pid, working_dir, started_at, parent_session_id, role, epic_id, task_ids, swarm_mode, tmux_session, tmux_window, status, last_activity_at, prompt_hash, git_branch, beads_task_id.
Backends: YAML per session (default), Temporal DB if aurad available.

## R6: Permission Inheritance
Parent permission mode propagated to children via session registry.
If parent is bypassPermissions, children default to bypassPermissions.
Explicit --permission-mode flag overrides inherited value.

## R7: Registry Lifecycle
- Write: aura-swarm writes entries on launch
- Cleanup: lazy on aura-swarm start/status + periodic via aurad if running

## R8: Unified Start Subcommand
--epic always required for start (both modes).
Add -n/--njobs flag for parallel instances.
Intree mode skips worktree creation but still uses beads task discovery.

## R9: Mode-Aware Subcommands
All subcommands work for both modes with appropriate behavior:
- start: in intree skips worktree creation
- status: shows all sessions regardless of mode
- attach: attaches to tmux session/window
- stop: kills agents, in intree no worktree to preserve
- merge: in intree is no-op (already in-tree)
- review: generates review docs in both modes
- cleanup: in intree just kills sessions, in worktree also removes worktree+branch

## R10: Skill Consolidation
Merge skills/parallel/ and skills/swarm/ into single unified skills/swarm/SKILL.md.
Document both --swarm-mode options in one file.

## R11: Nix Packaging Updates
Update flake.nix: remove aura-parallel package, update aura-swarm.
Add deprecation wrapper script for aura-parallel.
Update HM module references.
title: URD: Unified aura-swarm requirements document

description:
AXIS A (correctness). File: internal/effects/process.go ClassifyShellConstruct (lines 290-319).

WHAT: The classifier's token table omits several constructs that belong to the classes it claims to cover, so it returns ("", nil) — 'no unsupported construct' — for fragments that DO contain one, contradicting its own doc ('A fragment with no unsupported construct returns ("", nil)') and the worker's claim that control/expansion 'fail actionably'.

Concrete misses:
  - Control-operator class: a newline (and other command separators such as a bare tab-adjacent form) separates commands like ';' but is not in the token list {&&, ||, ;, &}. Fragment "echo a\necho b" classifies as clean.
  - Expansion class: '~' tilde (home) expansion is absent from {$(, ${, `, $}. Fragment "~/foo" classifies as clean.
  - Grouping/subshell: '(' ')' '{' '}' (subshell / brace group) are absent. Fragment "(echo hi)" classifies as clean.
  These are all in the broader shellMetaCharacters set (refs.go:18) that ExecutableRef rejects, so the two lists diverge.

WHY IT MATTERS (bounded): This is an ADVISORY helper, not the enforcement path. The structural safety guarantee holds regardless — there is no sh -c rendering anywhere, and ExecutableRef rejects these metachars, so nothing reaches a runner as shell. Worst realistic outcome when a future lowerer (S3.3+) trusts a false-negative: a multi-command fragment is silently mis-modeled as a single argv (semantic drop), not a shell injection. Hence MINOR, not IMPORTANT.

FIX: Make the token table total over the enumerated classes. # Axis A - Correctness

VOTE: REVISE

## Review basis

Independent design-only review of PROPOSAL-7. I read the complete UAT and all
comments first, then the URD update, request and comments, PROPOSAL-7
description/design, PROPOSAL-6 and its exhaustive disposition, and all six
PROPOSAL-6 reviews. I inspected the pinned Claude profile/payload/codegen tables,
the exact pinned Provenance commit `bcce71451b4a`, the Epoch FSM and codegen phase
tables, engine control/workflow/projection/activity writers, assignment/human
service, handlers, and audit writer/schema. No production or proposal file,
dependency, commit, or implementation was changed.

## Revision verification

### Exact 30-hook audit: verified

PROPOSAL-7 section 11 lists all 30 events exactly once and in the same order as
`internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go:8-40,42-96`. Identity additions and host
behavior match `internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go:268-320,323-361`; allowed
fields match both `internal/lifecycle/claude/payload.go:29-46,69-100` and
`internal/codegen/claude_hooks.go:148-183`.

The five high-risk corrections are exact:

- `PermissionDenied` has only `tool_name` and `tool_input`; reason/source are
  explicitly unresolved (proposal section 11 row 10;
  `internal/lifecycle/claude/payload.go:79`).
- `PostToolUse` has no duration or artifact identity; lineage requires separate
  enrichment (row 11; `internal/lifecycle/claude/payload.go:80`).
- `PostToolUseFailure` has no interrupt field (row 12;
  `internal/lifecycle/claude/payload.go:81`).
- `PostCompact` has only `trigger`, not summary (row 26;
  `internal/lifecycle/claude/payload.go:95`).
- `ElicitationResult` has one observed `response` and `MutationNone`, not an
  original/effective pair or overrider (row 30;
  `internal/lifecycle/claude/payload.go:99` and
  `internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go:359-360`).

Common-field presence is not promoted to identity or semantic truth, and
`transcript_path` remains a reference that ingress never opens (proposal section
11 lines 912-916; `internal/lifecycle/claude/payload.go:29-36`).

### T1 receipt path: implementable on the pinned API

The path is now exact: the process mints a fresh non-payload OperationID, uses
the fixed ordinal-1 software actor and persisted bootstrap authority through a
narrow evidence-only appender, calls one `Journal.Apply`, and returns the
database-assigned `ProducedJournalID` for mandatory slot `occurrence` (proposal
sections 3.1-3.2). The pin exposes `Apply`, `LookupCommitted`, result slots, and
bounded facts at `provenance@bcce714:journal_api.go:279-294`; its operation and
result shapes support this at `internal/journal/operations.go:142-235,275-295`.
The journal row is `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`
(`provenance@bcce714:internal/sqlite/operations.go:336-337`), and unscoped
`EffectEvidence` skips task-governance while retaining the existing authority
requirement (`internal/sqlite/operations_helpers.go:563-578`). Fixed-actor
activation is an idempotent `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` aggregate
(`internal/sqlite/actor_namespace.go:13-106`); Pasture already persists the
bootstrap result-slot authority (`internal/tasks/system_identity.go:41-53,235-283`).

Two byte-identical host process invocations mint different operation IDs and
therefore append different occurrence JournalIDs. Only a retry of the same
storage attempt reuses an operation ID. Native IDs remain envelope claims and
never become actor, occurrence, or authority identity.

### One graph, one FSM, and one normative writer: verified

Section 7 defines one concrete causal primitive: a typed `LinkV1` encoded as an
`EffectEvidence` lifecycle envelope, with typed relation/confidence/basis and
journal/result-slot endpoints. Its produced JournalID is the only link identity;
task `EffectEdgeAdd` is explicitly excluded and SQL rows are replay indexes.
This maps to the pin's opaque evidence payload and result-slot support without a
second graph.

Section 8.1 selects one private immutable PhaseSpec source, removes production
spec injection, and derives codegen adjacency from it. It closes the existing
drift between `pkg/protocol/state_machine.go:20-39,72-110` and
`internal/codegen/specs_data.go:74-90,162-178`, while keeping codebook
classification separate from adjacency ownership.

The current direct normative path is fully enumerated: in-memory advance in
`internal/engine/control.go:52-116` and `internal/engine/workflow.go:52-93`,
last-write-wins state in `internal/engine/projection.go:44-81`, transition audit
in `internal/engine/workflow.go:98-158` and
`internal/audit/sqlite.go:359-378`, transition activity in
`internal/engine/activities.go:44-84`, and direct handler projection consumers.
Section 8.3 routes all of them through `EpochControlService` at M6, makes audit,
activity, and phase rows compatibility projections, and requires the old writer
to be unable to advance state. Before M6 the old path is the sole writer; at M6
the cutover is one slice, so the plan does not require an authoritative
dual-write interval.

### T2, host boundary, malformed capture, and honesty: verified

Sections 4-7 provide a stable envelope, mandatory interpretation header,
bounded occurrence/snapshot inputs, pure `InterpretationDraft`, typed assertion
status, deterministic effect/result slots, and bounded readers. Unknown schemas
remain opaque to forensic reads and fail semantic policy closed. The Go layout
in section 12 makes target-neutral model/codebook/lowering/context unable to
import private host behavior; codegen receives only a generated mechanical
manifest. The tracked `BackendView` and behavior-bearing runtime model are
explicitly deleted/reworked in section 15.4.

Section 5.4 gives a coherent outcome for each invalid class. Only a trusted
generated contract/event coordinate permits malformed capture; payload-only
unknown events and unregistered caller events append nothing; store failure
never claims receipt; all temporary responses remain neutral. Sections 6.2, 7,
11, and 17 distinguish observed paths/tool results from correlated or verified
artifact lineage. Human-to-code queries return explicit links and confidence or
an unresolved gap, never timestamp inference.

Sections 2, 3.1, 6.2, 10, 14.4, and 15 gate T1/T2 before context M4 and control
M6. Receipt/interpretation writers expose only unscoped evidence drafts, pure
interpretation emits no context/control effects, and generated host code cannot
select operations or authorize. This satisfies the early-milestone capability
law in the plan.

### Elicitation authority: safe for the pinned contract

Sections 9.2-9.3 define request, capability, native-binding, revocation,
single-use consumption, and transition records. Section 9.4 correctly concludes
that Claude 2.1.210 cannot prove the required Pasture-owned challenge or an
original/effective response pair. Its `ElicitationResult` is therefore rejected
by `BindElicitation` for normative use; explicit registered-human CLI decisions
remain authoritative. Host request/server strings alone never authorize.

The generic future chain is structurally present, but its expiry member is not
yet transactionally implementable, as Finding 1 explains.

## Finding 1 - Wall-clock capability expiry cannot be transaction-local on the pinned Apply API

Proposal sections: section 8.2 lines 688-697; section 9.2 lines 742-779;
section 14.2 lines 1051-1069; design validation item "expire ... typed and
transaction-local".

`CapabilityScope` stores `expiresAt`, but the state machine has only Issued,
Bound, Revoked, and Consumed. Commit conditions only on the current Bound fact.
No proposal API or effect checks the deadline after SQLite has acquired write
ownership. The pinned Provenance contract exposes only `ConditionExactFact` and
`ConditionCurrentFact` (`provenance@bcce714:internal/journal/facts.go:55-89`).
Inside `Apply`, replay is checked and then only those fact selectors run
(`provenance@bcce714:internal/sqlite/operations.go:546-595` and
`internal/sqlite/fact_conditions.go:50-97`). There is no deadline condition,
transaction clock, or callback through which `EpochControlService` can test
`expiresAt` inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction.

A service-level injected-clock check before `Journal.Apply` is racy: an
operation can observe `now < expiresAt`, wait behind another SQLite writer,
acquire the write transaction after expiry, find the capability still Bound,
and atomically consume it with a phase transition. The proposed ordinary
"already expired" test can pass while this boundary race authorizes a late
transition. The existing human service illustrates the same public seam:
preflight is outside the transaction and only supplied Conditions become atomic
at `internal/tasks/epoch_human_service.go:451-529`.

Concrete fix: define expiry semantics at transaction admission and choose one
implementable contract before M6. Either defer/remove wall-clock expiry from MVP
and retain explicit revocation, or name a precise minimal upstream extension: a
closed deadline condition evaluated with an injected trusted clock after exact
replay lookup and inside the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, before effects. Keep exact
replay before deadline evaluation. Add a lock-spanning test that starts before
expiry, holds the SQLite writer through the deadline, then proves the fresh
operation is rejected with zero writes after lock acquisition; an already
committed exact retry must still return its original result.

## Finding 2 - The version envelope cannot identify the context policy that produced a disclosure

Proposal sections: section 4.4 lines 305-340; section 10 lines 842-881; section
14.3 lines 1071-1088; context acceptance criterion in the design field.

The proposal correctly separates context from interpretation, but
`ContextPolicy` has no `Identity()` and `ContextInput` contains no
`ContextPolicyRef`. The prose says version identity is required, yet no policy
definition is an input to `Project` or an output/basis of `ContextService.Plan`.
Likewise `EpochImplementationRef` carries a full metadata value but no immutable
definition JournalID, even though section 4.4 says build definitions are
`RecordDefinition` evidence. An interpretation/phase reference can identify the
facts used by policy, but it cannot identify which policy definition transformed
those facts into a packet.

Consequently two policy versions can project the same committed inputs without
the planned/sent/result disclosure proving which policy ran. Historical replay
can reproduce rows but cannot resolve the exact policy content or distinguish a
policy/config change from a transport result. This misses the UAT requirement
that versioned executable metadata determines progressive disclosure and the
review requirement that dependent records reference immutable definitions
without copying metadata.

Concrete fix: define an immutable `ContextPolicyRef` containing definition
JournalID, typed ID/version, and digest; add `Identity() ContextPolicyRef` to
`ContextPolicy`; require `ContextService.Plan` to resolve that exact definition
and journal it in the disclosure plan's definition refs. Transport results must
cite the plan, not restate policy metadata. Make the implementation/build value
reference its immutable build-definition JournalID (or specify and test exact
cross-validation against the envelope definition list). Add a two-policy
evolution test proving one ContextInput can produce two immutable disclosure
histories, each resolving its exact policy/build definition, with no implicit
latest selection.

| `dzaky` A4: host behavior can leak through runtime/BackendView | CLOSED | Sections 12 and 15.4 move behavior private, emit a mechanical manifest, remove behavior from model, and delete the same-package backdoor. |

boundary, one-journal representation, and validation path are otherwise clear
and correctly aligned with the UAT. The remaining defects affect whether an
expired capability can incorrectly advance the SDLC and whether agents can later
prove which policy disclosed their context. Both touch durable authority or
historical meaning and must be specified before implementation.

## Evidence
File: internal/tasks/epoch_human_service_test.go:98-131. Ratify and Land are now committed before close and retried after file-backed tracker reopen, but the assertions compare only DecisionID, ActivityID, and `len(EventIDs)`. They do not compare each EventID, inspect/restored the persisted precondition selector arms and AssertedJournalIDs, or snapshot the decision/evidence/activity/event/operation/result/status rows to prove the reopen retry added no rows.

## Why this matters
The implementation specifically persists transaction-local condition identity and reconstructs prerequisite-bound Ratify/Land drafts after reopen. A test that checks only an event count can pass if the replay binds a different event, restores the wrong condition, or appends duplicate effects. This is a narrow representative reopen proof; broader process/replay mutation coverage remains assigned to aura-plugins-8cus8.

## Exact fix
Before closing the file-backed tracker, capture complete persisted footprints and the original Ratify/Land result bindings. After constructing a fresh service through `NewEpochHumanService`, retry exact inputs and assert `Replayed`, byte/identity equality of DecisionID, ActivityID, every EventID, and all persisted condition selector arms/AssertedJournalIDs. Assert decision, evidence, activity, event, operation/result, and lifecycle status rows are unchanged.

## Finding
`cmd/pasture-release/promote.go:36-38` promises gates at the named revisions, but `buildPromotionGates` receives no revision. Its marketplace gate reads an arbitrary live path (`:107-115`, `:181-183`), its command gates run in the live Pasture checkout (`:193-203`), and `auraRepo` is explicitly unused (`:207`). `PromotionRequest.AuraRevision()` has no production consumer. The projection is built from the executing binary's embedded descriptor (`:96-104`), not from `--pasture-revision`. Only after all gates pass does `Promoter.Promote` resolve the Pasture revision (`internal/promotion/promote.go:92-105`). Consequently a clean working tree can be gated while a different commit/ref is published, any non-empty Aura revision is accepted, uncommitted or unrelated marketplace bytes can satisfy the Aura gate, and a symbolic revision such as `HEAD` can move between gating and resolution. This violates the ratified S6 contract that requested-revision mismatch fails with the old channel preserved and breaks the exact S5-to-S6 provenance chain.

## Required fix
Require full immutable commit OIDs for both revisions, resolve and verify them before gates, and run every gate against immutable materializations of those exact commits. Derive the target descriptor/manifests from the exact Pasture candidate commit and read marketplace metadata from the exact Aura candidate tree. Bind the successful gate evidence to both OIDs and reject working-tree/path/ref drift before calling the guarded push. Add negative CLI fixtures where HEAD/working-tree content differs from each named revision and prove the remote ref remains unchanged.
title: BLOCKER: Named revisions are not the revisions gated before publication

## VOTE: ACCEPT

### Axis: Elegance and Complexity Matching (Round 3)

This review evaluates the three updates made to PROPOSAL-2 since Round 2: the IMPORTANT-1 fixture update plan, the IMPORTANT-2 concrete test assertions, and the R7 styling consistency requirement.

### Assessment of Updates

**IMPORTANT-1 resolution (fixture updates): Proportional and well-scoped**

The concrete fixture update plan — renaming "Protocol Context" to "Protocol Reference" in `must_contain_headers`, adding body-originated H3 headers per role, and adding body-derived string entries — is exactly the right level of specificity. It constrains the implementation enough to prevent the "silently dropped body content" gap that Reviewer B identified, without over-prescribing the test implementation. The fixture approach (data-driven via skills.yaml) remains consistent with the existing test architecture. No new abstraction introduced, no test framework changes. This is good.

**IMPORTANT-2 resolution (sentinel test strategy): Clean and appropriately constraining**

The concrete test code using sentinel strings (SENTINEL_PREAMBLE_TEXT, SENTINEL_SECTION_TITLE, etc.) is the right technique. It avoids coupling tests to production body content that might change, and the marker extraction via `strings.Index` is the simplest approach that directly tests the key invariant. The assertion that content after END is empty whitespace when a SkillBody exists is the crucial inverse of what the current test checks, and specifying it as concrete code eliminates ambiguity.

This does put concrete Go test code in a proposal document, which is unusual. However, it is justified here: Reviewer B explicitly flagged the assertion strategy as underspecified, and the test is the single most important verification of the proposal's architectural change. Providing the code pattern in the proposal (rather than leaving it to the implementer) reduces implementation risk proportionally to the importance of the invariant. It does NOT over-specify because it uses sentinel strings (test-only data) rather than dictating production content.

**R7 styling consistency: Correct design choice, no added complexity**

The unified template MUST render ALL behaviors (both `RoleSpec.Behaviors` and `SkillBody.Behaviors`) using the structured bullet-list format:

```
**[{ID}]**
- Given: {given}
- When: {when}
- Then: {then}
- Should not: {shouldNot}
```

This is the right call. Currently, the same `BehaviorSpec` type is rendered two different ways by two different templates — structured bullets in `skill_header.go.tmpl` and inline prose in `skill_body.go.tmpl`. Since the proposal merges both into one template, having one rendering format is the natural consequence. The structured bullet-list format is the better choice because:

1. It matches the constraint rendering format (consistency within a single document)
2. It is more scannable for agents (each clause on its own line)
3. It eliminates a formatting code path — one template block handles all behaviors regardless of source

The inline prose format (`**Given** X **when** Y **then** Z **should never** W`) packs everything into a single paragraph, which becomes unreadable when clauses are long (see supervisor body behaviors — some are 2+ lines of inline text). The structured format solves this with zero additional complexity; if anything, it simplifies the template because there is only one behavior rendering block.

### Complexity Re-assessment

The three updates collectively do NOT increase the design complexity of the proposal:

- IMPORTANT-1 adds test data entries to an existing fixture file (skills.yaml). No new type, no new pattern.
- IMPORTANT-2 provides a test code pattern using standard Go testing idioms. No new test helper, no new framework.
- R7 removes a formatting variant (inline prose) rather than adding one. The unified template has fewer rendering code paths than the current two-template system.

The proposal remains a clean subtraction: two templates become one, two context types become one, two render functions become one, one body replacement function is deleted. The updates refine the test plan without expanding the architecture.

### Findings

No new findings. The three MINORs from my Round 2 review (large-but-justified context struct, heading level decisions, template naming) are all still accurate and unchanged by the updates.

### End-User Impact

Unchanged from Round 2. The end-user (an agent reading SKILL.md) will see behaviors in a consistent, scannable format throughout the document. The narrative flow (identity -> behaviors -> operations -> reference) remains intact.

### Decision

ACCEPT. The updates address Reviewer B's two IMPORTANTs proportionally — enough specificity to close the test coverage gaps, no unnecessary complexity added. R7 is the right design choice and actually simplifies the implementation by eliminating a formatting variant. The proposal is ready for implementation.
