   racing commit", with §21 requiring each to produce "a typed state error with zero partial
   writes … **and should not** collapse the three timings into one outcome".
3. Already-consumed — §16.2, with the exact expected value
   `CapabilityStateError{Observed: Consumed, Required: Bound}`.
4. Fresh operation against stale/revoked/consumed/expired — §16.2 "all four, not only
   expired", §21 "**should not** treat them as one case".
5. Build honesty — §16.2 restores all three: same VCS revision with two different build
   content identities ("neither overwriting the other, neither claiming to be *the* build for
   that revision"), dirty source (`BuildIdentityDirtySource` -> `UnresolvedUnverifiedBuild`,
   cannot back an Enabled activation, no context or control effects), and missing/unknown
   (`BuildIdentityUnresolved` permits T1, unresolved T2, no effect). Reinforced by §7.3, the
   §21 BDD, §20, and design AC 6, and made an M2 gate in §17.
6. Generated code cannot parse semantics — now a named operator,
   `MutateGeneratedPayloadParse`, in the §16.4 generated-artifact row alongside
   `MutateEnvSelectedOperation`, `MutateGeneratedSemanticBranch`, and
   `MutateGenericErrorToDeny`; restated in §13.2 and in §18.3's S2 L2 leaf.
7. Fixture anti-normalization — §16.3 restores the rule with the reasoning attached, the
   `Case.RawBytesPath` field enforces it structurally with the comment "Inlining them in YAML
   normalizes exactly the properties section 13.1 tests for", and §16.3 closes the loop:
   "A corpus loader that inlines raw bytes fails its own non-vacuity guard." That last
   sentence is the strongest single line in §16 — it makes the rule self-enforcing rather
   than declarative.

**Appendix B corrects the false "unchanged" claim — CLOSED.** Appendix B's preamble states it
directly: "PROPOSAL-8's Appendix A recorded four `aura-plugins-xwiuk` rows as ACCEPT, three of
which PROPOSAL-8 had in fact narrowed. `aura-plugins-237wx` B2 caught it. A revision may not
carry forward an acceptance it has narrowed, so the whole appendix was re-audited and every
narrowed row is now marked." The three rows are marked "**MODIFY — narrowed in PROPOSAL-8,
restored in PROPOSAL-9**" (complete test strategy; independent process races; concrete
human-to-code chain), and the fourth ("verified subset only") is correctly left as ACCEPT
unchanged. Appendix A also carries the honesty rule forward as a standing requirement: "It is
honest about narrowing: every row that carries an acceptance forward states whether the
acceptance is unchanged or narrowed." That is the right generalization of the finding.

**`aura-plugins-237wx` B3 (URD corpus idiom) — CLOSED on adoption, OPEN on mechanism (B3
above).** §16.0 adopts the idiom in form: `Expectation{MustPass, MustFail}`, `CaseID`,
`CaseProvenance{Origin, Reference}` with `CaseOrigin` distinguishing pinned-contract
transcription from review-driven additions from hand-authored oracles, `Case`, `Corpus` with
`ExpansionSpec` and `CoverageSpec`, `NonVacuityReport`, twelve named `MutationOperatorID`
values, and eight corpora each mapped to the prose matrix it replaces. `CaseProvenance.Reference`
is correctly constrained to a file path or public URL and "Never a Beads ID (AGENTS.md)". The
URD FIX-NOW is quoted verbatim and correctly — I checked it against `aura-plugins-hznvh`
comment 4413. Every prose matrix that had no named test now has one. That is a genuine and
large improvement. What is missing is the part that makes it bite: per-case mutation metadata
and operators for the seven behavioural corpora (B3), and coverage that its owner can meet
(B2).

**`aura-plugins-237wx` B4 (bounded-reader rule unguarded) — CLOSED.** §16.4 adds the guard
with a named rejection set (`database/sql` import, projection-internal package import, SQL
string literal), a named proving operator (`MutateDirectSQLInProductionTest`), and exactly one
named whitelisted exception (`lifecycletest.SnapshotPlaneDeltas`). §16.2 resolves the tension
the prior review flagged, and does so the right way round: the zero-write delta snapshots
"require table-level reads, which §12.2's rule otherwise forbids. They are therefore the **one
named exception** … The exception is visible and countable rather than ambient." §12.2, §20,
§21, and design checklist 11 / AC 13 all now say the rule is guarded rather than asserted.
§18.5 keeps the disposition of the live violation and §16.4 states plainly why a disposition
is not a guard. I re-verified the violation is still live and still reads as ordinary test
code: `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:133-138` opens
`sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+dbPath+"?mode=ro")`, `:139-142` runs `SELECT … FROM audit_events
WHERE event_type = 'LifecycleObserved'`, `:154-158` joins `activities`, `:164-175` counts
arbitrary tables, and `:177-195` reads `context_edges`. Only C3 remains (allowlist fails
open).

**`aura-plugins-237wx` A1 (retention gates M1) — ACCEPTED but incompletely executed.** The
gate moved; the ownership did not. See B1.

**`aura-plugins-237wx` A2 (no M3 human-signal issuance path) — CLOSED, and the reasoning is
better than what I asked for.** §16.1 item 4 names a real `UserPromptSubmit` occurrence
delivered through the generated registration and built binary, interpreted into
`FactHumanSignal`, and separates the *Pasture-issued* human decision
(`CapabilityRecordHumanDecision`) out to M6 item 8 where an issuance path actually exists.
§17 makes `UserPromptSubmit` Enabled an explicit M3 gate, and §16.1 pre-empts the obvious
objection: "It is turn-scoped, not per-tool-call, so the `aura-plugins-cvlu6` restriction in
§17 does not bar it." §14 row 4 is annotated "**This is the M3 human-signal leg (§16.1 item
4)**", §20 requires "no test-seeded human signal", and §21 and design AC 9 both forbid
"direct SQL, test exports, a test-seeded human signal, or timestamp proximity". The negatives
survive: missing and contradictory enrichment stay `RelationObservedPath` plus typed
unresolved facts, and no timestamp or session proximity promotes confidence.

below is a row of corpus `ingress_invalid.yaml` and is executed by exactly one named test,
`TestIngressInvalidDeliveryCorpus` (§16.1 item 3)", and item 3 requires the full production
path: "generated registration, built binary, file-backed journal, and public readers only",
with the exact `CaptureDisposition` where required, no later-plane effects, and no false
receipt from untrusted, unregistered, or store-failure inputs "without touching SQL". The
matrix grew from seven rows to eight, correctly, with the P0-PIN deadline row added. Coverage

**`aura-plugins-237wx` item 7 (say which races need processes) — CLOSED.** §16.2: "the T3
capability races and the lock-spanning expiry case (§16.1 item 7) require **separate
processes**, because a single process cannot demonstrate the property; the remaining races may
use independently opened handles, which exercise real WAL and `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` contention
through `internal/dbconn.SharedDSN`." §21 adds "**should not** be demonstrated with goroutines

production hostcontract" fix the second; `MutateRemovePayloadField` fixes the first.

---

# Where I am explicitly NOT asking for more

Checked for over-testing; I find none to remove, and I decline three plausible additions.

- **The all-30 catalogue is correctly scoped.** `claude_2_1_210_catalogue.yaml` covers all 30
  events as an independently-authored *oracle* of names, fields, identity additions, and
  behaviour class — not 30 authentic byte fixtures. Authentic per-event fixtures gate per-event
  activation through IP-3, and §17 keeps "all 30 Enabled" gating only the catalogue-completeness
  claim, explicitly "does not block earlier verified M1 events". Do not tighten this.
- **The cursor and race matrices should not be expanded.** §16.2's reader matrix already covers
  malformed, tampered, mismatched, future, and stale cursors, zero and over-limit page and
  lineage bounds, stable snapshots, no duplicate or skip, continuation, explicit cycles,
  node/edge/depth truncation, and defensive copies. That is thorough. My B2 asks for the coverage
  declaration to match the owner's milestone — it does not ask for more cases.
- **Not re-requesting the semantically-identical-different-byte ingress case.** The
  byte-identical double invocation in §16.1 item 1 strictly dominates it, the rejection is
  recorded in §13.1 and design tradeoff 8 rather than silently taken, and two prior rounds

  in items 1-8 and 10, and the alternative is the `aura-plugins-ay4yn` flake by construction.
- **The uncontended hold measurement should stay a report, not a gate.** §4.6 is right that a
  5 ms absolute p99 cannot be a gate at M1, and right to keep reporting it against the estimate
  so trigger (a) has an input.

Four edits, none large:

1. B1 — move retention ownership with the retention gate, make §18.1 UAT-conditional the way

4. B4 — assert delivery outcome in item 9, state how deadline-failed `Apply` calls enter the

# SLICE-2: Claude frontend

Owns exactly: `internal/lifecycle/claude/**` (+ tests). Touches nothing else.

A frontend is part of Pasture in the same sense a C parser is part of a C
compiler: written in Go, linked in, bound to one pinned contract, and its only
output is IR. Parsing Claude's native payload here is **approved and intended**.
What is forbidden is raw JSON being Pasture's *semantic API* — which is the
`__adapter invoke` path this replaces.

## Prototype status

`internal/lifecycle/claude/frontend.go` and `payload.go` exist from a superseded
design. Divergences to correct:

| Prototype | Required |
|---|---|
| calls the wide `NewEvent(binding, name, axes, identities)` | `binding.NewEvent(digest, identities)` |
| discards fields not in the identity set | still discards them, but the **digest is taken over the raw bytes by the caller**, so nothing is lost for replay |
| no digest handling | accept the digest from the CLI layer, or compute in `Parse` |

## Code shape

```go
package claude

type Frontend struct{ /* unexported; holds the pinned contract */ }

func New() Frontend
func (f Frontend) Harness() ir.HarnessID   // ir.HarnessClaudeCode
func (f Frontend) Parse(payload []byte, requested lifecycle.NativeEventName) (lifecycle.Event, error)
```

Must satisfy `lifecycle.Frontend`. Add a compile-time assertion:
`var _ lifecycle.Frontend = Frontend{}`.

## Parse algorithm

```
1. bound        len(payload) > lifecycle.MaxNativePayloadBytes -> error
2. digest       lifecycle.NewDigest(payload) over the EXACT bytes received
3. strict decode  json.Decoder with DisallowUnknownFields.
                  Unknown or duplicate field -> actionable error, no partial Event.
4. resolve      hook_event_name -> ClaudeLifecycleEvent, by exact match against
                the pinned catalog. Unknown spelling -> actionable error listing
                nothing (do not dump 30 names); say the event is not in the
                pinned contract for this host version.
5. cross-check  requested != "" && requested != payload's name -> hard error.
                A mismatch means a hook is misregistered, which is worth failing.
6. bind         lifecycle.BindEvent(runtime.ClaudeCode2_1_210Lifecycle(), event)
7. identities   for each mapping.Identities(): read that exact native field.
                Required and missing -> error. Build lifecycle.NewIdentity(...).
                Extract ONLY declared fields; ignore everything else.
8. construct    binding.NewEvent(digest, identities)
```

`Parse` is **pure**: no store, no clock, no environment, no effects. This is what
makes golden-IR tests possible with no host and no database.

## Payload shapes

The pinned profile declares only `session_id` (required) for most events, plus
`tool_use_id`, `request_id`, or `agent_id` for specific ones — see
`internal/runtime/lifecycle_profiles.go`, `claudeLifecycleMappings()`. Read the
mapping rather than hardcoding a per-event struct where possible; a single
decode into a struct carrying every declared identity field plus
`hook_event_name` is acceptable and simpler, provided `DisallowUnknownFields`
still rejects genuinely unknown input.

Note `SessionStart` also carries `source`, and other events carry extra native
fields. Since `DisallowUnknownFields` is on, every field the host can legitimately
send MUST be present in the decode target or valid payloads will be rejected.
Verify against the pinned allowed-field set; this is the most likely source of
false rejections.

## M1 scope

M1 exercises `SessionStart`, which is `SemanticObservation` in the pinned profile
(confirmed: `claudeLifecycleMappings()` maps it via `observe(...)`). The frontend
should nonetheless handle the full pinned catalog — refusing non-observation
events is `Lower`'s job (SLICE-3), not the frontend's. A frontend that silently
declined to parse gate events would hide the very refusal that must be loud.

## Testing (light — coverage deferred)

Golden-IR table test, no host, no database: for a handful of pinned events, feed
a realistic native payload and assert the resulting `Semantics` and
`Origin.NativeEventName()`. Include: unknown field rejected; missing required
identity rejected; `--event` mismatch rejected; oversized payload rejected.

## Definition of done

- `var _ lifecycle.Frontend = Frontend{}` compiles.
- Package imports `internal/lifecycle` and `internal/runtime` only — never
  `internal/handlers`, `internal/tasks`, `internal/engine`, and never another
  harness package.
- `gofmt`, `go vet`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...`, race tests for the package.

Do not commit, push, or close. Do not touch `internal/lifecycle/*.go` — that is
SLICE-1 and SLICE-3. If you need a change there, report it as a blocker.

# PROPOSAL-1: pasture standalone plugin (renamespace + frontmatter + CI fix + v0.0.1)

## Problem Space
pasture is a Go-generated PORT of the aura protocol that still emits the `aura:` namespace everywhere. To ship it as a standalone Claude Code plugin (`/pasture:*`), three codegen-level problems must be solved, plus distribution. Axes: mostly-sequential (codegen → regenerate → release); single-module; one-time refactor with a permanent guard.

## Engineering Tradeoffs — namespace mechanism
| Option | Pros | Cons | Decision |
|--------|------|------|----------|
| A. Pure literal sweep (aura:→pasture: everywhere) | Simple, mechanical | No define-once; future re-namespace repeats the sweep | Partial |
| B. Full data-model parameterization (strip prefix from CommandSpec.Name + LabelSpecs.Value, prepend Namespace everywhere, templatize prose) | Fully define-once | Large refactor; every Name/Value parser changes; templatizing 270 markdown literals is over-engineering | Rejected (YAGNI) |
| C. HYBRID (CHOSEN) | Namespace constant for programmatic emission (define-once where it matters); sweep free-text prose/recipe literals; guard test enforces zero-aura: | Prose literals are swept not derived | **CHOSEN** |

## Design
### 1. CI / provenance fix (R1 — SLICE-1, foundational)
- Drop `replace github.com/dayvidpham/provenance => ../../../../provenance` (go.mod:63).
- Require `github.com/dayvidpham/provenance v0.0.0-<...>-93ef75b` (the published commit pasture is built against). `go mod tidy` to populate go.sum.
- Add GITIGNORED `go.work` (`go work use . ../../../../provenance`) so local co-dev resolves the local checkout; CI (no go.work) fetches from github. Add `go.work`, `go.work.sum` to .gitignore.
- Verify ci.yml steps "Verify dependencies" (go mod verify) + "Vet" (go vet ./...) pass. NOTE: d2041 flake (internal/tasks SQLITE_BUSY) is separate and may still intermittently fail CI — out of scope (track on d2041); optionally quarantine in CI as a discovered task.

### 2. Renamespace aura:→pasture: (R2 — SLICE-2)
- Introduce `const Namespace = "pasture"` + `NamespacePrefix = Namespace + ":"` (new namespace.go in internal/codegen).
- Route programmatic emission through it: `subSkillsForRole` mainCmd (skills.go:184 `fmt.Sprintf("aura:%s", roleId)` → `fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", Namespace, roleId)`) and any sibling Sprintf points.
- SWEEP literal `aura:`→`pasture:` across the spec data: CommandSpec.Name (e.g. "aura:impl:review"→"pasture:impl:review"), LabelSpecs.Value (e.g. "aura:p1-user:s1_1-classify"→"pasture:p1-user:s1_1-classify"), and ALL recipe/prose literals in specs_data*.go + specs_data_body*.go (bd-label recipes, /aura:x, Skill(/aura:x), command labels). 278 refs total; sweep-in-place keeps Name/Value parsers (split on ":") unchanged.
- Prose branding "aura protocol/schema" → "pasture protocol/schema" (per URD R2).
- GUARD TEST (new): scan generated output (skills/**/SKILL.md, agents/*.md, schema.xml) and ASSERT zero tokens matching the aura: namespace (`/aura:`, `aura:p`, `aura:severity`, `aura:urd`, `aura:epic`, `Skill(/aura:`, `skills: aura:`). Actionable failure naming file:line of any stray ref.

### 3. Sub-skill frontmatter emission (R3 — SLICE-3)
- renderSubSkill/GenerateSubSkill (skills.go ~:486/:652) currently preserve the hand-authored `# H1` and replace only the BEGIN..END region — NO YAML frontmatter. FIX: prepend a frontmatter block ABOVE the H1: `---\nname: <skill-dir>\ndescription: <CommandSpec.Description>\n---\n\n`. name = skill dir (cmd suffix, e.g. user-uat); description from the cmd-* CommandSpec.
- Brings ~25 sub-skills to parity (all register as invocable /pasture:*). aura has 14 w/ frontmatter; pasture currently 6.

### 4. Distribution (R4/R5 — SLICE-4)
- plugin.json (DONE, v0.0.1) — verify name/version/desc.
- Add `pasture` github-source entry to PARENT aura-plugins/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (version 0.0.1, source github dayvidpham/pasture), mirroring agentfilter.
- pasture-release ALREADY version-syncs root .claude-plugin/plugin.json (subdirs:false) — no change needed for plugin.json; the marketplace entry is a manual parent-repo edit. (No pasture-release change proposed.)

### 5. Release (R6 — Phase 12 landing, not a slice)
- merge develop→main (brings SharedFragment work + this epic); cut v0.0.1 via bin/pasture-release; push pasture main + tag; push parent (marketplace entry).

## Slices (vertical, ordered) + Integration Points
- SLICE-1 CI/provenance (go.mod, go.work, .gitignore, go.sum). Independent; FIRST (green baseline).
- SLICE-2 Renamespace (Namespace const + sweep + guard test + regenerate). Depends: SLICE-1 green.
- SLICE-3 Frontmatter (renderSubSkill + regenerate + tests). Depends: SLICE-2 (avoid golden churn — both regenerate; SERIALIZE 2→3).
- SLICE-4 Distribution (plugin.json verify + parent marketplace entry). Depends: SLICE-2+3.
- IP-1: SLICE-2 & SLICE-3 both run go generate → SERIALIZED (2 then 3); each pins its goldens.
- IP-2: guard test (SLICE-2) must stay green after SLICE-3 frontmatter (descriptions are swept content → no aura:).
- IP-3: Python schema-sync — pasture diverges from aura on labels (pasture: vs aura:). Confirm pasture-only; the Python/aura side stays aura:. The pasture schema.xml regenerates to pasture: labels; verify pasture-side schema test (not the cross-repo Python one).

## Risks
- Sweep misses → guard test catches. - bd label divergence (pasture: vs aura:/Python) → accepted (pasture-only). - d2041 flake → separate. - main far behind → merge brings all landed work.

description:
File: pasture/internal/temporal/activities.go (lines 20-23, 187-226) and pasture/internal/audit/audit.go + memory.go

The temporal package defines its own AuditTrail interface (temporal.AuditTrail) and InMemoryAuditTrail that are structurally identical to audit.Trail and audit.InMemoryAuditTrail. This means:

1. pastured/main.go must call temporal.InitAuditTrail() with a temporal.AuditTrail, but separately creates an audit.SqliteAuditTrail for the SQLite path. The SqliteAuditTrail implements audit.Trail, NOT temporal.AuditTrail — so the wiring in main.go bridges this by returning a temporal.AuditTrail from initAuditTrail(), which means SqliteAuditTrail must satisfy BOTH interfaces.

2. A future audit backend author must implement two separate interfaces rather than one.

3. Violates DRY (D7: DI via struct) and creates a confusing two-interface hierarchy for what is one concept.

Fix: temporal/activities.go should import and use the audit.Trail interface directly. Remove the temporal.AuditTrail interface and temporal.InMemoryAuditTrail. InitAuditTrail should accept audit.Trail.
title: BLOCKER: Duplicate AuditTrail interface and InMemoryAuditTrail between internal/temporal and internal/audit

# PROPOSAL-1 — Graduate git_recorder.go from stub to production

Authored by the epoch/architect from the locked URE (nnpjm). Build EXACTLY to the URE decisions; do not relitigate them.

## Locked design (from URE)
- CLI-direct now (works WITHOUT pastured); daemon/Temporal signal path DEFERRED.
- Scope: git-commit path + extensible seam (not all 9 events).
- Subcommand: `pasture hook record --event git-commit --sha <sha>` (event = flag, single dispatch point).
- Payload: SHA + core metadata (message, author, branch, timestamp).
- Seam = MANAGER PATH: add HookGitCommit hooks.HookEvent; CLI builds HookPayload{HookGitCommit, Data{...}} -> hooks.Manager.Dispatch -> GitRecorder.Handle -> RecordCommit -> pasture.db. Same pipeline pastured uses (RegisterDefaultRecorders already wires it). CLI builds its own in-process Manager (no pastured needed).

## Files to add / modify
1. internal/hooks/hooks.go — add `HookGitCommit HookEvent = "git_commit"` to the enum + AllHookEvents.
2. internal/hooks/git_recorder.go — RegisterDefaultRecorders subscribes GitRecorder to HookGitCommit (WithSubscribedEvents(HookGitCommit)). Handle already extracts Data["sha"] + copies all Data keys into auditPayload -> RecordCommit; no Handle change needed (confirm).
3. cmd/pasture/hook.go (NEW) — parent `hook` cobra cmd + `record` subcommand: --event (required), --sha (required), --message/--author/--branch/--timestamp (optional). RunE -> handler.
4. internal/handlers/hook.go (NEW) — standalone HookRecord handler: (a) validate --event against a typed supported-set; unknown -> actionable error listing supported events (the extensible seam); (b) require --sha; (c) tracker := tasks.OpenTaskTracker(""); auditDB := tasks.OpenAuditDBForFreeFloating(dbPath); (d) mgr := hooks.NewManager(); RegisterDefaultRecorders(mgr, tracker, auditDB); (e) build HookPayload{Event: HookGitCommit, Data:{sha, message, author, branch, timestamp}}; (f) mgr.Dispatch(ctx, payload); (g) map result to exit codes (0 ok / 1 validation / 5 storage); actionable errors (what/why/where/impact/fix).
5. internal/handlers/hook.go — gatherGitMeta(sha) best-effort helper: if metadata flags omitted, attempt git show -s for message/author/branch/timestamp; isolated + skippable so handler logic stays testable without a git repo.

## Slice plan (1 cohesive slice; leaf count per real work units)
SLICE-1: pasture hook record — git-commit recording via Manager path
- L1: HookGitCommit enum variant + AllHookEvents (+ membership test).
- L2: GitRecorder subscribes to HookGitCommit in RegisterDefaultRecorders; Manager-dispatch test (dispatch HookGitCommit -> RecordCommit writes EventGitCommit row).
- L3: cmd/pasture/hook.go + internal/handlers/hook.go (subcommand + handler + event validation + tracker/auditDB open + Manager dispatch + exit codes + gatherGitMeta helper).

DEFER the full Claude-Code-session-fired shell smoke (firing a real Stop hook end-to-end) as a follow-up — it depends on the downstream hook wiring in aura-plugins/hooks/ and a live session, out of this slice's scope.

description:
## Finding

In workflow.py (lines 284-285), after the advance() call produces a TransitionRecord, the workflow replaces the last entry in transition_history with a new record using workflow.now():

    if self._sm.state.transition_history:
        self._sm.state.transition_history[-1] = deterministic_record

TransitionRecord is documented as 'Immutable audit entry for one transition' and is a frozen=True dataclass. The list itself (transition_history) is mutable (EpochState.transition_history: list[TransitionRecord]), so replacing the list entry is structurally legal in Python.

However, this pattern is unexpected and subtle:
1. The comment in advance() says 'Records the transition in transition_history' — the record written there has a non-deterministic datetime.now() timestamp
2. The workflow then silently overwrites the last record with a deterministic timestamp
3. Callers who query current_state() before the overwrite step (very unlikely in practice due to Temporal's scheduling, but possible) would see the non-deterministic timestamp
4. This is the only place in the entire codebase where a list element is reassigned post-hoc

## Alternative
Modify EpochStateMachine.advance() to accept an optional timestamp parameter:
    def advance(self, to_phase, *, triggered_by, condition_met, timestamp=None):
        ts = timestamp or datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)
        record = TransitionRecord(..., timestamp=ts)

The workflow passes workflow.now() directly; pure Python tests pass nothing (defaults to datetime.now()). This eliminates the post-hoc mutation entirely.
title: SLICE-5-REVIEW-C-1-F1: Workflow reassigns frozen TransitionRecord in transition_history list — breaks expected immutability guarantee

## Elegance Axis Evaluation — PROPOSAL-5 (Review Fixes)

### Context

PROPOSAL-5 is a delta document addressing 2 correctness issues (Reviewer A) and 5 test quality gaps (Reviewer B). My Round 1 review (aura-plugins-zqugx) ACCEPTed PROPOSAL-4. This review verifies that the fixes preserve the architectural elegance I approved.

### 1. `_check_tmux(search_path=...)` — Proportional, Not Over-Engineering

The proposed signature:

```python
def _check_tmux(search_path: str | None = None) -> bool:
    return shutil.which("tmux", path=search_path) is not None
```

This is **proportional** for three reasons:

1. **It forwards an existing stdlib parameter.** `shutil.which` already accepts a `path` keyword argument. The DI parameter is not an invented abstraction — it exposes a capability that already exists one layer down. The function remains a single expression.

2. **It follows the established codebase pattern.** `parse_args(argv)` accepts an explicit `argv` parameter for the same reason: testability without global state mutation. `resolve_connection(cli_args, env_dict, yaml_section)` uses the same pattern. The `search_path` parameter is consistent with both.

3. **The alternative is worse.** Without this parameter, the test must manipulate `os.environ["PATH"]` (global mutable state), which is a test isolation hazard — if the test crashes before restoring PATH, subsequent tests may fail in mysterious ways. Or the test must use `unittest.mock.patch`, which contradicts the project's no-mocking-framework pattern. The DI parameter is the cleanest option.

**Verdict:** Not over-engineering. One optional parameter on a private function. Zero cognitive overhead for callers who pass nothing.

### 2. Config Test Matrix — Clean DI, No New Abstractions

The 8-row test matrix passes explicit `cli_args`, `env_dict`, `yaml_section` dicts to `resolve_connection()`. This is the same DI-via-explicit-parameters pattern already established. No test fixtures, no config builders, no parameterized test abstractions beyond plain function calls with plain dicts.

The matrix is exhaustive without being redundant: 6 rows test all pairwise priority combinations (CLI>env, CLI>YAML, env>YAML, env>default, YAML>default, CLI>all), plus 2 error cases (missing file, malformed YAML). This is the minimum set needed to prove the 4-level priority chain works. Proportional test coverage.

### 3. Correctness Fix 1 (`state.review_votes`) — Zero Structural Impact

Pure field name correction. The `QueryStateResult.votes` external field name is preserved — only the internal reference changes from `state.votes` to `state.review_votes`. This decoupling (internal field name vs. external API name) is the right design choice. No elegance regression.

### 4. Correctness Fix 2 (Typed `query_events`) — Strictly Better

Changing `SqliteAuditTrail.query_events` from `phase: str = ""` to `phase: PhaseId | None = None` is an elegance improvement, not a regression. It enforces the project's "strongly-typed enums over stringly-typed API" principle. The implementation detail (`.value` for SQL WHERE clauses) is cleanly encapsulated inside the method. Callers pass enums; the method converts to strings only at the SQL boundary. This is the correct abstraction level.

The `None`-means-no-filter semantics is also cleaner than empty-string-means-no-filter. `None` has clear intent ("I did not specify this filter"). Empty string is ambiguous ("Did I forget to set it, or is empty string a valid filter value?").

### 5. Test Specifications — No Production Abstractions Added

All five test quality fixes add test specifications only:

- **signal complete BDD:** New Given/When/Then criteria. No production code changes.
- **Config test matrix:** Test-level specification of DI parameter usage. No production code changes beyond what `resolve_connection` already supports.
- **Exit code BDD:** New criteria for exit codes 2 and 3. Production code already defines these exit codes; the fix adds test coverage.
- **tmux DI parameter:** One optional parameter on one private function (discussed above).
- **Hook test boundary:** Subprocess tests with a mock `aura-msg` script. No production code changes. The mock is a 2-line shell script, not a framework.

### 6. New Decisions (D20-D24) — All Proportional

| Decision | Assessment |
|----------|------------|
| D20: `QueryStateResult.votes` field kept despite `state.review_votes` source | Correct — API stability over internal naming |
| D21: Typed query_events with enum `.value` for SQL | Correct — type safety at boundary |
| D22: `_check_tmux(search_path)` | Correct — minimal DI, stdlib forwarding |
| D23: Hook test via subprocess + mock script | Correct — tests shell script at its natural boundary |
| D24: 8-row config test matrix | Correct — exhaustive pairwise coverage |

None of these decisions introduce new abstractions, classes, or indirection layers.

### 7. End-User Impact

End-users are unaffected by PROPOSAL-5. All fixes are either internal correctness patches (review_votes, typed query_events) or test-level specifications. The CLI API, module boundaries, and user-facing behaviors remain exactly as specified in PROPOSAL-4. This is the ideal outcome for a review-fix iteration: the fixes improve internal quality without perturbing the external design.

### Comparison with Round 1

My Round 1 review (aura-plugins-zqugx) ACCEPTed PROPOSAL-4 based on:
- Clean module boundaries (config.py, formatters.py, sqlite_audit.py)
- No unnecessary abstractions (no DualWriteAuditTrail, no SessionManager, no RuntimeDependencyChecker)
- Go portability (all types map 1:1)
- Proportional complexity (not over-engineered, not under-engineered)
- Clean UAT amendment integration (edge additions, not core perturbations)

PROPOSAL-5 preserves all of these properties. The `search_path` parameter is the only production API change, and it strengthens (not weakens) the existing DI pattern. The typed `query_events` fix is an elegance improvement. Everything else is test-level specification with zero production impact.

## Conclusion

PROPOSAL-5 is a clean review-fix iteration. It addresses Reviewer A's correctness issues and Reviewer B's test quality gaps without introducing any new abstractions, modules, or complexity. The `_check_tmux(search_path)` DI parameter is proportional — it forwards a stdlib parameter, follows the established codebase pattern, and avoids the worse alternatives (PATH mutation or mocking framework). The design remains proportional to the problem. Vote: ACCEPT.

description:
We need to fix the supervisor skill. The Ride the Wave section needs to be re-worked. Having a standing team of cartographers is ineffective. The only thing that TeamCreate and Teammates should be used for are Workers. Workers should remain alive until they finish their slice AND their slice has a CLEAN REVIEW. A CLEAN REVIEW means that that there are no BLOCKERS or IMPORTANT findings from the reviewers. Thus, the supervisor is responsible for managing the worker-reviewer loop, where the loop can only exit if all slices end on a CLEAN REVIEW round. That means we cannot do a work->review->work fixing issues, then move to Phase 11 UAT. It must always end on a CLEAN REVIEW round. Supervisors also keep trying to implement work themselves, and they overly explore the codebase wasting their entire context window. We will need to turn them into an agent definition, where they don't have access to the Edit, Write, Update tools. They should defer all codebase exploration and context gathering to Explore subagents who are prompted to run the /explore skill. All code writing and implementation should go delegated to workers (teammates or subagents). Teammates should ONLY be used if there are many integration points between the layered slices. Seek to commit small and commit often. Aim for atomic commits. The supervisor should plan to integrate early and often between slices as well, to minimize drift.

Additional issues:
1. Stages that should proceed autonomously constantly stop and ask for user permission. For example "Should I proceed to phase 1 exploration?", "Should I proceed to URE?", "Should I handoff to supervisor?" — JUST DO IT. Should proceed autonomously, stopping ONLY for phases requiring explicit user-approval: Request/URE/UAT/Ratification and Phase 11 UAT.
2. All user inputs must be documented in the URD verbatim — URE, proposal UAT, and implementation UAT responses.
3. The example invocation that should be subsumed into the skill:
/aura:supervisor Yes, let's create the slices, also ordered topologically with dependencies set accordingly. Then afterwards, launch Sonnet worker SUBAGENTS NOT TEAMMATES to work on these. At integration points, commit, and send out reviewer waves. Worker-reviewer waves until no BLOCKERS or IMPORTANT findings. Then repeat for the next set of slices, until Phase 11, pausing for the UAT. MUST end on a clean reviewer wave with no BLOCKER or IMPORTANT findings before proceeding. Cannot end on a worker wave.

description:
File: internal/sqlite/fact_conditions_test.go, TestCurrentFactConditionStale (~line 227).

WHAT: The test's assertion accepts EITHER ConditionCurrentMismatch OR ConditionFactMissing (line 266). The test title and doc comment claim to verify the 'stale' scenario (CurrentMismatch: newer row exists). But its own comment says 'JID=1 is not a decision row', and it uses AssertedJournalID=1 which is not a decision-table row.

WHY: The test commited two decisions then asserts JID=1. Since latestFactSelectorLocked finds the actual latest decision (found=true, actual >> 1), checkCurrentFactLocked takes the 'found && actual != 1' branch → ConditionCurrentMismatch. But the dual-accept ('|| ConditionFactMissing') hides which branch was actually taken. If the DB happened to have no decision rows (which cannot happen here but illustrates the looseness), it would get FactMissing and still pass.

WHERE: internal/sqlite/fact_conditions_test.go:266 — the condition 'cf.Reason != journal.ConditionCurrentMismatch && cf.Reason != journal.ConditionFactMissing'

WHEN: At test time; no runtime impact.

IMPACT: Test gives false confidence. A bug that accidentally returns ConditionFactMissing instead of ConditionCurrentMismatch for the stale path would not be caught by this test.

FIX: Commit two decisions of the same kind. After the second Apply, call latestFactSelectorLocked to find the latest JID. Then call another Apply to add a THIRD decision. Now assert that the second JID (which is no longer current) produces exactly ConditionCurrentMismatch with ActualJournalID == third JID. Replace the dual-accept with 'cf.Reason != journal.ConditionCurrentMismatch'.
title: SLICE-1.2-REVIEW-B-10 IMPORTANT-1: TestCurrentFactConditionStale accepts CurrentMismatch OR FactMissing — does not independently prove stale path

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-21 — Typed multi-harness compiler and Provenance task journal

## 1. Outcome and structural reset

Pasture will compile one harness-neutral, typed protocol document into native
Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex artifacts. It will not parse operational meaning
out of prose during normal generation and it will not guess tool names. Exact
native calls are emitted only through a documented, version-bounded harness
contract; other operations use a validated parent-mediated expansion, an
explicit semantic instruction, or an actionable unsupported-capability error.

Provenance will become the source of truth for a task's ordered lifecycle. Every
persisted task or graph mutation and every material-work event is recorded in the
same data model. Mutation state and its journal event are committed in one
Provenance database transaction. Pasture adds its domain-specific event kinds and
payloads, exposes them through `pasture task`, and stops generating operational
`bd` recipes.

The previously accepted installer remains deliberately simple: it stores only
the user's harness and extension choices, delegates plugin-backed installation
to native managers, places only documented standalone artifacts itself, stops on
the first actionable failure, and has no receipt, ownership ledger, digest,
pending state, recovery state, rollback, lock, or installer transaction model.

This proposal supersedes Proposal 20's `RuntimeOperation` optional-field record,
regex/string-replacement projection, invented OpenCode calls, and separate
Pasture audit writes. It retains Proposal 20's accepted distribution choices,
simple installer configuration, Home Manager defaults, native-manager ownership,
independent extensions, and completed source/output-root cleanup.

## 2. Scope and explicit non-scope

### FIX-NOW

1. A typed Go `Document` API, with Goldmark as the Markdown parser/AST.
2. A protocol-semantic IR for orchestration, user decisions, workflow effects,
   and typed external capabilities.
3. Version-bounded harness contract packs and exhaustive lowering decisions.
4. Logical assignment continuity across fresh runtime agents.
5. A Goldmark inventory scanner followed by a finite strict rejection gate.
6. Provenance-owned ordered task events, atomic mutation journaling, mutable
   current ownership, and cumulative attribution.
7. `pasture task` as the first workflow-effect backend; generated operational
   material no longer uses Beads.
8. Native Claude Code, OpenCode, and Codex skills, agents, and hooks artifacts.
9. `pasture install`, the confirmed YAML preferences, native registration, and
   active uninstall when a selection becomes false.
10. Aura Home Manager parity using Pasture-generated artifacts.
11. The already completed Option-C source/output-root separation.

### USER-CONFIRMED DEFER

- Project-local Codex agent export under repository `.codex/agents/`.

### FOLLOW-UP, NOT SILENT MVP FALLBACKS

- Registered native Pasture tool bindings as an alternative workflow backend.
- A semantic-instructions-only, Markdown-files-only installation mode for users
  who do not install the `pasture` executable.
- Full interaction/agent-trace ingestion after Peasant Labs schema, village, and
  peasant are shipped.

### OUT OF SCOPE

- A generic third-party harness SDK/compiler framework (Pasture issue #15).
- Installer receipts, ledgers, ownership/digest identity, authorizations,
  pending operations, rollback/recovery, or concurrent-installer coordination.
- Git hooks, Beads hooks, `core.hooksPath`, or any implicit hook opt-in. The
  selectable `hooks` extension means harness lifecycle hooks only and defaults
  to false.

## 3. Repository ownership and release order

| Repository | Owns | Does not own |
|---|---|---|
| Provenance | generic task state, graph, mutable owner, cumulative attribution, ordered TaskEvent journal, atomic mutation API | epoch phases, harness calls, installer choices |
| Pasture | typed protocol documents/IR, Pasture event payloads, `pasture task`, harness contracts/lowerers, generated artifacts, installer/config | generic event persistence, Aura marketplace registry |
| Aura Plugins | aggregate marketplaces, Home Manager options and activation wiring sourced from pinned Pasture outputs | canonical skills/agents, protocol compiler, new Python protocol code |

Landing is dependency-ordered: Provenance journal release first; Pasture updates
its Provenance version and lands compiler/task/target/installer work; Aura pins
that Pasture revision and lands marketplaces/Home Manager. Cross-repository
fixtures pin the exact upstream commit or release used by each downstream gate.

## 4. Typed document model

Canonical generated content is assembled through a Go API. There is no directive
language hidden in Markdown comments and no production parser that attempts to
turn legacy tool-call prose into operations.

```go
type Document struct {
    Parts []Part
}

type Part interface {
    documentPart()
    SourceLocation() Location
}

type Markdown struct {
    Source []byte
    AST    ast.Node // Goldmark AST whose segments reference Source
    At     Location
}

type OperationPart struct {
    Operation Operation
    At        Location
}

type Verbatim struct {
    Content []byte // portable literal content; never interpreted as an operation
    At      Location
}

type TargetLiteral struct {
    Cases []TargetCase // one LiteralFor or LiteralUnsupported per enabled harness
    At    Location
}

type LiteralFor struct {
    Contract HarnessContractID
    Content  []byte
    Reason   string
}

type LiteralUnsupported struct {
    Harness HarnessName
    Reason  string
}
```

Constructors parse Markdown once with Goldmark and validate every part before it
enters a document. `TargetLiteral` is an explicit, reviewable escape for truly
harness-native text. Across the requested compilation target set it must contain
exactly one compatible literal or explicit unsupported case per enabled harness;
omission is an error. It is not a loophole for portable semantics.

Document compilation is a conventional multi-stage pipeline:

```text
typed Go specs
  -> validated Document
  -> semantic/type checking
  -> target contract selection
  -> exhaustive operation/effect lowering
  -> target-native Markdown/frontmatter/manifests
  -> native schema/loader fixtures
```

The compiler accumulates diagnostics with owner, source location, operation,
target contract, failed phase, caller impact, and remediation. Generation emits
nothing for a document that fails validation or lowering.

## 5. Protocol-semantic IR

`Operation` is a closed interface with concrete structs, not one record with
optional fields and not a string enum plus an untyped map.

### 5.1 Orchestration

The initial closed set is:

- `InvokeSkill`
- `DelegateAssignment`
- `ContinueAssignment`
- `SendAssignmentMessage`
- `CollectAssignmentResults`
- `StopAssignment`
- `RequestUserDecision`

Parallelism is expressed by a collection of assignments plus typed scheduling
metadata (`independent`, `dependency-ordered`, or `bounded-parallel`), not by a
Claude-specific team/session primitive.

Logical continuity is explicit:

```go
type AssignmentContext struct {
    Role       protocol.RoleID
    Assignment AssignmentID
    Task       provenance.TaskID
    Worktree   WorktreeRef
    Evidence   []EvidenceRef
    Decisions  []DecisionRef
    Outstanding []WorkItemRef
}
```

A target may continue an existing runtime agent or create a fresh one. Either is
correct only if the same role, assignment, Provenance task, worktree, evidence,
decisions, and outstanding work are reconstructed. A runtime session ID is never
the semantic identity.

### 5.2 User decisions

`RequestUserDecision` has result semantics `SelectOne`, `SelectMany`, or
`FreeText`. It carries the full question, all option labels/descriptions, any
definition/code shown, validation rules, and the required verbatim result. A
native UI binding is legal only when it preserves those semantics. Otherwise the
parent performs a validated textual interaction; if neither is possible, the
compiler reports unsupported capability instead of silently narrowing the
choice.

### 5.3 Workflow effects

The typed effect family covers the user-selected broader surface:

- task effects: create/update/assign/complete, add/remove dependency, add label,
  add comment, record material event, attach git evidence, and typed read/query
  operations for show/list/ready/blocked/timeline;
- git effects: repository status/evidence, stage, commit through the repository's
  required commit command, fetch/rebase/push when the workflow authorizes them;
- process effects: executable plus argv, working-directory reference, expected
  exit semantics, and effect classification;
- filesystem effects: read, write/replace, create directory, move, and remove an
  exact owned path.

These are typed values with validation, not shell fragments disguised as fields.
Markdown may still explain a recipe, but an instruction whose execution matters
to protocol behavior is represented by an effect. Security policy and user
authorization remain outside the IR; typing an effect never grants permission to
execute it.

For task effects, the only MVP binding is the versioned `pasture task` CLI. If it
is unavailable or too old, lowering returns an actionable unsupported-backend
error. Registered native tools and semantic-only task instructions remain the
explicit follow-ups above. Generated operational content contains no `bd`
commands after migration.

### 5.4 Typed capability escape hatch

Capabilities not in the closed IR use external, versioned descriptors:

```go
type CapabilityID string
type CapabilityVersion string

const CapabilityExample CapabilityID = "vendor.example/capability"

type Capability[I any, O any] struct {
    ID      CapabilityID
    Version CapabilityVersion
    Input   Codec[I]
    Output  Codec[O]
    Effects EffectSet
}

func InvokeTool[I any, O any](c Capability[I, O], input I) Operation
```

The document stores a type-erased internal operation only after the generic
constructor validates/encodes it. Capability descriptors live outside canonical
documents and declare typed input/output schemas, effect class, semantic version,
and target bindings. IDs and versions are named string types with declared consts;
raw strings cannot be passed where a capability, operation, contract, role, or
assignment ID is required.

Compilation fails when a capability is undeclared, the descriptor version is
outside the target binding's range, input/output codecs disagree, or no permitted
binding exists. An undescribed native tool can appear only in `TargetLiteral`,
which makes its non-portability and contract boundary visible.

## 6. Version-bounded harness contracts

```go
type HarnessContractID string
type HarnessName string

type HarnessContract struct {
    ID       HarnessContractID
    Harness  HarnessName
    Versions VersionRange
    Bindings map[OperationKind]Binding
    Fixtures []ContractFixture
}

type Binding interface { binding() }
type NativeCall struct { /* exact name and validated request/result schema */ }
type ParentMediated struct { /* typed expansion and context obligations */ }
type SemanticInstruction struct { /* explicit validated wording contract */ }
type Unsupported struct { Reason, Remediation string }
```

Each operation/effect/capability has exactly one classified binding per supported
contract. Missing map entries are compile errors. No adapter invents a native
tool because another harness has a similarly named one.

The first contract inventory is pinned to tested local/reference versions, then
validated in isolated fixtures:

| Harness | Evidence baseline | Required classification work |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | CLI 2.1.208 and current official plugin/tool contracts | use current Agent/SendMessage/TaskStop-era primitives where exact; do not emit removed TeamCreate/TeamDelete semantics; pin user-decision request/result shape |
| OpenCode | CLI 1.17.18, official docs, and pinned source | use documented skill/task/question surfaces only; treat unverified persistent-message/follow-up/wait/close names as parent-mediated, semantic, or unsupported |
| Codex | CLI 0.144.1, official plugin/skill/agent/hook docs and pinned source | bind only exposed collaboration/request-input functions with exact schemas; preserve logical continuity across fresh agents |

Every contract fixture includes supported version bounds, exact request/result
schema, semantic parity cases, and an out-of-range rejection. Updating a harness
requires a new contract ID or reviewed version-range expansion, not an unnoticed
renderer edit.

Generated packages carry their immutable `HarnessContractID` and supported host
range as build metadata, not installation state. `pasture install` probes the
selected harness's public version surface immediately before applying a cell and
rejects an out-of-range host; Home Manager either pins a matching harness package
or performs the same activation-time compatibility check. A native manifest host
constraint is used only when that field is documented by the pinned contract.
No adapter invents a manifest field, assumes `latest` is compatible, or stores a
second observation/receipt after the check.

## 7. Goldmark migration and strict gate

Migration is intentionally staged and finite:

1. A read-only scanner parses every active generated Markdown owner with
   Goldmark and reports candidate foreign/tool syntax by canonical owner, file,
   AST node, source range, snippet, and candidate class.
2. Every candidate is explicitly classified in Go-owned inventory data as
   typed operation/effect, portable verbatim text, target literal, explanatory
   false positive, or dead/deprecated owner.
3. Canonical specs are migrated to the typed `Document` API. The existing
   `runtime.go` regex and global string replacements are deleted; they are not a
   compatibility layer.
4. The scanner reaches zero unclassified active candidates.
5. The strict compiler gate is enabled and permanently rejects unclassified
   harness syntax in Markdown parts. Only typed operations, `Verbatim`, and
   contract-bound `TargetLiteral` can contain classified syntax thereafter.

The scanner may recognize legacy lexical forms for inventory reporting, but it
never rewrites production output and never assigns semantics. Regression fixture:
legacy prose containing `TeamCreate({...})` must not become the malformed
`task(({...})` output produced by Proposal 20's replacement strategy.

## 8. Provenance task lifecycle journal

### 8.1 Public model

Provenance adds reusable, task-centric types:

```go
type TaskEventID int64          // database-generated and stable
type EventKind string           // namespaced, e.g. provenance.task.updated
type OperationID string         // groups events from one logical mutation

type TaskEvent struct {
    ID          TaskEventID
    TaskID      TaskID
    Kind        EventKind
    ActorID     AgentID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    OperationID OperationID
    Payload     json.RawMessage // typed before the persistence boundary
}
```

Provenance owns generic `provenance.*` kinds and their payload codecs. Pasture
owns `pasture.*` kinds/payload structs for epoch phase changes, assignment
start/completion, plan/code review, UAT decision, skill run, and attached git
evidence. Unknown namespaces or unregistered payload codecs are rejected at the
typed API boundary; raw JSON is only the stable persistence/wire representation.

The public query and CLI order is always `(RecordedAt, EventID)`. Both fields are
returned in Go, JSON, and human output. Equal timestamps therefore have stable,
deterministic order; clients never infer order from UUID text or slice order.

### 8.2 Mutation commands and atomicity

All mutating tracker paths require a typed mutation context:

```go
type MutationContext struct {
    ActorID     AgentID
    OperationID OperationID
}

Apply(ctx context.Context, mc MutationContext, command Mutation) (MutationResult, error)
RecordTaskEvent(ctx context.Context, event MaterialEvent) (TaskEvent, error)
TaskTimeline(ctx context.Context, taskID TaskID) ([]TaskEvent, error)
```

`Mutation` is a closed command family for task create/update/close/reopen,
owner change, edge add/remove, label add/remove, and comment add. Provenance runs
the domain write, any required cumulative-attribution insert, and event insert through one
`internal/sqlite` connection and transaction. Attribution is inserted when the
command changes responsibility or records material contribution; administrative
actors are not mislabeled as contributors merely for issuing a label/status
mutation. It commits all required writes or none. Pasture
does not attempt a faux transaction across `provenance.Tracker` and a second
audit connection.

`OperationID` is also the idempotency identity approved in the URE. The same
operation replayed with the same canonical command returns its already committed
result/events without changing state or allocating another EventID. Reusing an
OperationID with a different actor or command is an actionable conflict. A small
Provenance operation row stores the canonical command and committed result in the
same transaction; because an uncommitted row rolls back with the mutation, this
introduces no pending/recovery state. Multi-task graph events share the operation
identity while retaining distinct EventIDs.

The pre-1.0 direct mutator API is migrated rather than left as an unjournalled
bypass: callers move to `Apply`; compatibility wrappers, if temporarily needed,
must themselves require mutation context and delegate to the same transaction.
A mutation cannot succeed without its event.

For a graph mutation involving two tasks, Provenance records task-local events
for both affected timelines in the same transaction and gives them the same
`OperationID`. Their distinct database EventIDs provide total order.

### 8.3 Ownership and attribution

`Task.Owner` remains the current assignee. Reassignment atomically changes the
owner, preserves every previous contributor through idempotent `attributed_to`
edges, and records old owner, new owner, actor, and reason in the task journal.
Any actor that records material work is cumulatively attributed to the task.
Replaying the journal reconstructs the same current owner and attribution set.
Duration-based Provenance Activities remain distinct from transition events;
when an activity is material to a task, its start/end event carries the typed
ActivityID so the generic task timeline can expose both without encoding
structured transitions in activity notes.

### 8.4 Coverage boundary

Record:

- every persisted task and graph mutation;
- assignment start/completion;
- plan and code review results;
- UAT decisions and FIX-NOW/DEFER dispositions;
- skill runs; and
- attached git evidence.

Exclude read-only queries and incidental shell/tool calls. This is the domain and
material-work log requested now, not the future full interaction trace.

### 8.5 Migration from Pasture's existing audit tables

Provenance's journal becomes canonical for new task lifecycle writes. A Pasture
migration copies each legacy audit row that has a resolvable task context into a
namespaced TaskEvent with a unique legacy reference; it never deletes the source
row. Unmappable, non-task historical rows remain queryable through the existing
legacy read path. New task mutation/material writes do not dual-write to the old
audit table. `pasture task timeline` reads the canonical Provenance journal and
merges only unmigrated legacy history, with a deduplication fixture.

## 9. `pasture task` workflow backend

Pasture extends the existing CLI rather than introducing another task tool:

- mutation commands accept/resolve the acting AgentID and OperationID;
- task create/update/assign/complete, dependency, label, and comment commands
  route through Provenance `Apply`;
- review/UAT/skill/git-evidence commands create typed Pasture material events;
- `pasture task timeline TASK-ID` exposes the generic ordered TaskEvent stream;
  epoch-specific views are projections over it, not a second lifecycle store;
- JSON output exposes typed IDs, kind, actor, recorded time, operation ID, and
  payload; and
- errors state what failed, why, where, when/which operation, caller impact, and
  how to remediate.

Harness lowerers compile task effects to argv-safe `pasture task` invocations
whose CLI contract is itself versioned. Canonical generated sources and final
generated artifacts have a guard that rejects operational `bd` commands.

## 10. Native generated artifacts and delivery

The accepted independent delivery units remain:

```text
generated/
  claude-code/{pasture-skills,pasture-agents,pasture-hooks}/
  opencode/{skills,agents,pasture-hooks}/
  codex/{pasture-skills,pasture-agents,pasture-hooks}/
```

- Codex skills are full directories with `SKILL.md` and generated
  `agents/openai.yaml`.
- Codex agents are five standalone `pasture_*.toml` files because the current
  plugin manifest has no custom-agent component.
- Codex skills and hooks use separate plugins with required
  `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifests.
- OpenCode skills and agents use documented discovery trees; hooks use a
  target-native plugin package.
- Claude Code uses independently selectable native plugin packages.
- Whole skill directories and support assets are preserved.
- Hooks are independently installable and remain off by default.

The stable nine-cell delivery table remains a private build contract consumed by
codegen, installer adapters, fixtures, and Aura. It contains package/destination
facts only, not desired state, observations, identities, receipts, or ledgers.
Each cell has an isolated native loader/package test with sibling extensions
absent.

The public activation surface for each cell is fixed before an adapter is
implemented:

| Harness | Skills | Agents | Harness hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | native `pasture-skills` plugin via marketplace/plugin CLI | native `pasture-agents` plugin via marketplace/plugin CLI | native `pasture-hooks` plugin via marketplace/plugin CLI |
| OpenCode | whole directories at `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/` | files at `~/.config/opencode/agent/<role>.md` | target-native `@dayvidpham/pasture-opencode-hooks` entry through documented public OpenCode configuration/package loading |
| Codex | native `pasture-skills` plugin via marketplace/plugin CLI | standalone `~/.codex/agents/pasture_*.toml` | native `pasture-hooks` plugin via marketplace/plugin CLI |

Claude and Codex adapters use only their public marketplace add/update,
plugin add/install, list, and remove commands as captured by the pinned install
contract; they never write private caches. OpenCode config resolution honors its
documented precedence and preserves unrelated JSON/JSONC while changing only the
exact hooks package entry. Native managers remain responsible for later plugin
updates.

The completed `EmitHarness(sourceRoot, outputRoot, ...)` cleanup is retained.
The partial `runtime.go`/OpenCode projection work is exploratory and is replaced,
not extended; generated outputs are regenerated only after the typed compiler
and contracts pass.

## 11. Simple installer and Home Manager

Canonical persisted preferences are exactly:

```yaml
install:
  harnesses:
    claude-code: false
    opencode: false
    codex: false
  extensions:
    skills: true
    agents: true
    hooks: false
```

`pasture install` follows the Peasant kickstart interaction grammar: harness
checkboxes, global extension checkboxes, restored prior choices, install/uninstall
summary, confirmation, then progress. Cancellation changes nothing. The writer
preserves unrelated Pasture config fields.

After confirmation, Pasture saves the selected preferences before applying
external actions. A save failure applies nothing and reports the config path,
failed operation, cause, impact, and fix. If a later native action fails, the
saved preferences remain the desired choices for an ordinary idempotent rerun;
there is still no pending or recovery record.

For each enabled harness, enabled global extensions are installed. A false
selection actively removes the known Pasture component through the native plugin
manager or exact standalone path. Native managers own plugin registry state and
updates. Pasture neither edits their private caches nor mirrors their state.

Actions execute deterministically and stop at the first failure. Earlier
successful actions remain; there is no rollback or intermittent-state recovery.
The error identifies harness, extension, native action, cause, impact, and retry
or repair command.

The known user-scoped Claude Code v0.0.4 monolithic `pasture` plugin is one
explicit compatibility case. The adapter establishes the exact Aura marketplace,
installs the selected split packages, and removes that exact legacy identity so
an unselected hooks payload cannot remain active. A different scope, identity, or
unrecognized version is reported for manual resolution; Pasture does not guess
what it owns. This is a stateless native-manager transition, not a receipt or
ownership system.

Home Manager exposes the direct translation for each harness:

```nix
"claude-code".enable = false;
"claude-code".skills.enable = true;
"claude-code".agents.enable = true;
"claude-code".hooks.enable = false;
```

OpenCode and Codex have the same shape. Child defaults are inert until the parent
harness is enabled. Home Manager sources whole generated directories/files from
its pinned Pasture input. Plugin-backed cells invoke only the supported stateless
native registration surface; standalone cells use exact declarative paths. No
shared reconciler or receipt is introduced.

## 13. Validation strategy

### Compiler and migration

- Unit tests for every operation/effect constructor and invalid state.
- Property/fuzz tests for typed IDs, version ranges, decision cardinality, and
  argv serialization.
- Golden contract fixtures for every operation × supported harness contract,
  including unsupported cases.
- Goldmark AST fixtures covering prose, inline/fenced code, nested lists,
  blockquotes, literals, and source locations.
- Inventory fixture proving every active candidate is classified before the
  strict gate flips.
- Regression proving `TeamCreate({...})` never becomes `task(({...})`.
- Clean generation and native manifest/loader tests for all three targets.

### Provenance

- Migration tests against existing databases and repeat migration.
- Transaction fault injection at every domain-write/event-write boundary.
- Same-timestamp events with IDs 101 and 102 return 101 then 102.
- Replaying one OperationID with the same command returns the same result/event
  identities; reusing it for different input is rejected.
- Owner reassignment atomically changes current owner, preserves cumulative
  attribution, and records old/new owner; rollback leaves neither half applied.
- Journal replay reconstructs task state and attribution.
- Concurrent mutations yield unique EventIDs and a deterministic query order.
- Generic task timelines work for non-epoch tasks and graph changes are visible
  on both affected task timelines.
- Legacy audit migration preserves source rows and deduplicates timeline output.

### Effects, delivery, and installation

- Generated operational content contains no `bd` commands.
- Missing/outdated `pasture task` fails actionably; it never silently falls back.
- Each of the nine harness/extension cells loads alone with siblings absent.
- Native CLI fixtures install/list/remove exact plugin identities in isolated
  homes; standalone fixtures touch only documented exact paths.
- First-run/rerun/cancel/false-means-uninstall/first-failure installer cases.
- Config-save failure proves no native install/uninstall action was attempted.
- Config round trip preserves unrelated YAML.
- Hooks remain false until explicit opt-in.
- Home Manager evaluation covers parent-off inert children and every effective
  cell, followed by Aura's required flake/build/help gates.

## 14. BDD acceptance criteria

1. **Given** a canonical skill containing typed Markdown and operations, **when**
   it is compiled for a supported pinned contract, **then** every operation is
   lowered through that contract and the native loader accepts the artifact,
   **and should not** require regex or global string replacement.
2. **Given** a harness version outside a binding range, **when** generation runs,
   **then** it fails with the required version, detected version, affected owner,
   caller impact, and remediation, **and should not** guess a call.
3. **Given** a contract without a native primitive, **when** a semantically
   equivalent parent-mediated expansion exists, **then** the expansion preserves
   the typed result and context obligations, **and should not** claim session
   continuity.
4. **Given** a fresh runtime agent continues work, **when** its assignment starts,
   **then** role, assignment, Provenance task, worktree, evidence, decisions, and
   outstanding work are reconstructed, **and should not** depend on a prior
   runtime session ID.
5. **Given** `SelectMany`, **when** a native decision UI cannot preserve multiple
   selections and verbatim stimuli/result, **then** the parent mediates a validated
   equivalent or compilation reports unsupported, **and should not** narrow it to
   `SelectOne`.
6. **Given** an external typed capability, **when** its descriptor and target
   binding versions match, **then** typed input/output/effects are validated and
   lowered, **and should not** expose a generic name plus untyped argument map.
7. **Given** an undeclared capability, raw string ID, incompatible version, or
   incomplete target literal, **when** validation runs, **then** compilation
   rejects it with an actionable diagnostic.
8. **Given** the classified legacy inventory reaches zero, **when** strict mode is
   enabled, **then** any new unclassified harness syntax in Markdown fails CI,
   **and should not** be auto-rewritten.
9. **Given** a task/graph mutation, **when** Provenance commits it, **then** the
   matching task event and cumulative attribution commit in the same transaction,
   **and should not** leave state without an event or an event without state.
10. **Given** a committed OperationID is replayed with the same mutation, **when**
    Provenance applies it again, **then** it returns the original result/events
    without changing state; reusing it for different input fails actionably.
11. **Given** two events share `RecordedAt`, **when** a task timeline is queried,
    **then** it orders by EventID and exposes both fields in API/CLI output.
12. **Given** ownership changes, **when** the new assignee starts material work,
    **then** `Task.Owner` names the current assignee, prior contributors remain
    attributed, and both changes appear in the ordered audit log.
13. **Given** an epoch advances, review completes, UAT disposition is recorded,
    skill runs, or git evidence is attached, **when** the task timeline is shown,
    **then** the material event appears with typed actor/kind/payload, **and should
    not** include incidental reads or shell calls.
14. **Given** a generated task effect, **when** it is rendered in the MVP, **then**
    it uses the versioned `pasture task` CLI, **and should not** emit `bd` or
    silently use a deferred fallback.
15. **Given** a first installer run, **when** the TUI opens, **then** all harnesses
    are false, skills/agents true, hooks false, and nothing changes before final
    confirmation.
16. **Given** saving confirmed preferences fails, **when** installation would
    begin, **then** no native action runs and the error names the config path,
    cause, impact, and fix.
17. **Given** a saved selection becomes false, **when** installation applies,
    **then** the exact Pasture component is removed through its native manager or
    documented standalone path, **and should not** alter unrelated components.
18. **Given** an install action fails, **when** the first error occurs, **then**
    processing stops with harness/extension/action/cause/impact/remediation and
    earlier successes remain, **and should not** create rollback or pending state.
19. **Given** Home Manager's harness parent is false, **when** child defaults are
    true/true/false, **then** no child is active; **when** the parent is true, the
    effective cells match the installer semantics.
20. **Given** only one of skills, agents, or hooks is installed for a harness,
    **when** that harness loads, **then** the selected extension works without its
    siblings and hooks were never implicitly enabled.

## 15. Ratification consequences

On Plan UAT acceptance, mark Proposal 21 ratified and every earlier proposal
superseded; preserve all task history. The prior handoff/implementation plan and
runtime leaf receive superseded comments and are not resumed. The completed
source/output leaf remains valid evidence. A new handoff will direct the
supervisor to create a replacement implementation plan from the GitHub tracker,
repository boundaries, integration table, and accepted validation cases.

WHAT: capabilitylint (internal/codegen/capabilitylint) is not invoked anywhere outside its own unit tests. Confirmed by inspection: `grep -rn capabilitylint` across the worktree (excluding the package's own _test.go/testdata) shows no reference from Makefile, .github/workflows/ci.yml, any cmd/ binary, or a go:generate directive. `go vet ./...` (Makefile:77, ci.yml:51/101) runs the stdlib vet, which does not know about this hand-rolled Check()/CheckFile API — there is no `-vettool=`/unitchecker wiring, and no standalone `cmd/capabilitylint` driver exists to run it against real (non-testdata) source.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is distinct from, and not a re-litigation of, the already-recorded, supervisor-approved deferral of promoting capabilitylint to a real golang.org/x/tools/go/analysis.Analyzer (that judgment call and its DEFER-to-Impl-UAT disposition are accepted as-is and are NOT being reopened here). Regardless of which library capabilitylint is eventually built on, the rule as shipped today has zero enforcement surface against any real, non-fixture source file in this repository or any future external package. A developer (in this repo or externally) who violates the canonical-declaration-site rule at a real DefineCapability call site gets no signal at all — not from CI, not from `go vet`, not from any local dev-loop command — because nothing calls capabilitylint.Check on anything but its own testdata fixtures.

WHERE: repo-wide — absence of any Makefile target, CI step, or cmd/ entrypoint invoking internal/codegen/capabilitylint.

PHASE: SLICE-2.3-REVIEW-B-1, Pasture #41 capability escape hatch, round 1, test-quality/effectiveness axis.

IMPACT ON CALLER: the "Analyzer fixtures reject literal IDs at canonical definition sites" acceptance criterion is met only in the narrow sense that the analyzer's own fixture-driven unit tests pass; the analyzer provides no actual, standing protection for the codebase it was built to protect until something wires it into a real gate.

REQUIRED CORRECTION (not necessarily this round — flagging for explicit supervisor/Impl-UAT disposition, likely bundled with the already-deferred x/tools promotion decision since a real analysis.Analyzer is the natural, standard way to wire this into `go vet -vettool=`): add a minimal enforcement point now (even ahead of any x/tools promotion) — e.g. a `make lint-capabilities` Makefile target or a small `cmd/capabilitylint` driver that walks real source directories and fails on any Finding — and wire it into ci.yml alongside the existing `go vet ./...` step. If the team decides to defer this alongside the x/tools decision, that should be an explicit, recorded decision (not a silent gap), since it changes the accepted contract's practical guarantee from "enforced" to "documented and unit-tested only."

description:
What: §3.2 lists exactly one FD ({JournalID, ResultSlotID} -> {ProducedJournalID}) and justifies BCNF as 'trivial — single composite key, one non-key attribute, no other determinant'. That 'no other determinant' claim is incomplete. A slot row's ProducedJournalID references a journal row whose ProducedByOperationJournalID (PBOJID, §2.1) is that row's producing operation; the contract intends a slot to map ONE of its OWN operation's allocations, so ProducedJournalID.PBOJID = journal_operation_result_slots.JournalID. Under that intended invariant the FD {ProducedJournalID} -> {JournalID} holds over the whole relation (it is the same derive-JournalID-from-the-produced-row's-PBOJID relationship). This is exactly the FD-enumeration-discipline gap round-1 finding yv8p9 flagged for the episodes near-key FD, which was accepted and fixed — the new relation should meet the same bar.

Two consequences the doc leaves unaddressed:
(1) Integrity invariant: nothing stated forces ProducedJournalID to be a row produced by the slot's OWN operation. The two FKs (JournalID -> journal_operations, ProducedJournalID -> journal) independently permit a slot row pointing at some OTHER operation's produced row, which would corrupt that operation's reconstructed CanonicalMutationResult (the §3.2 query filters WHERE JournalID = :anchor and returns whatever ProducedJournalID sits there). This is a reducer-level business rule the schema cannot express, exactly the §14.3 pattern.
(2) BCNF/candidate-key: whether ProducedJournalID is a second candidate key depends on whether slot-aliasing (two ResultSlotIDs -> one ProducedJournalID within one operation) is permitted. If forbidden (ProducedJournalID UNIQUE), {ProducedJournalID} is a second candidate key and BCNF is clean for a DIFFERENT reason than stated; if permitted, {ProducedJournalID} -> {JournalID} is a nontrivial FD whose determinant is NOT a superkey (it does not determine ResultSlotID) — controlled denormalization of JournalID, not 'no other determinant'.

Where/when: docs/journal-relational-contract.md §3.2; S1.0 cycle-2 relational-correctness re-review of provenance commit 19585c9.

Impact: doc-precision + one unstated reducer integrity invariant on a newly added relation; reconstruction is sufficient today because the reducer is the sole writer, but the contract's own FD/BCNF rigor standard is not met.

Required correction: (a) state the reducer invariant that a slot row's ProducedJournalID must be a row produced by the slot's own operation (ProducedJournalID's PBOJID = the slot's JournalID), per the §14.3 convention, with a must-fail corpus case (slot referencing a foreign operation's produced row); (b) add the induced FD {ProducedJournalID} -> {JournalID} to the FD list; (c) state whether ProducedJournalID is UNIQUE (no slot-aliasing -> second candidate key, BCNF via superkey) or aliasing is permitted (controlled denormalization of JournalID with the same honest treatment §2.1 now gives journal.ActorID).
title: S1.0-REVIEW-A-2-FINDING-M1: journal_operation_result_slots (§3.2) FD analysis is incomplete — omits the induced FD {ProducedJournalID}->{JournalID} and the own-operation integrity invariant it depends on
