### 7.4 Codex 0.144.1 activation

Aura issue #9 owns marketplace `aura-plugins` and its aggregate manifests.
Release automation advances a reviewed moving Git ref `pasture-stable`; it does
so only after target outputs, #39 activation fixtures, and Aura repository gates
pass at named revisions. This is intentionally not an immutable SHA: Codex's
native `marketplace upgrade` resolves the configured ref again, so later releases
can update without Pasture replacing the marketplace or maintaining update
state. The activation contract pins the source, ref name, host point version,
and expected plugin versions/schemas.

#39 proves only a synthetic moved-ref activation fixture: two local marketplace
commits and a temporary ref exercise native upgrade/re-add without publishing a
real Aura ref. Aura #9 alone owns the executable promotion surface:

```text
nix run .#promote-pasture-stable -- \
  --pasture-revision <reviewed-sha> \
  --aura-revision <reviewed-sha> \
  --expected-old <sha|absent> \
  --remote <git-remote>
```

Its tests use a temporary bare Git remote. Each target, activation, manifest,
Aura-gate, or requested-revision mismatch independently fails with the old ref
unchanged. The all-green case advances exactly to the reviewed Aura commit and
then proves Codex upgrade/re-add loads that promoted revision.
Immediately before publication the command resolves the remote ref again and
uses one guarded push equivalent to
`--force-with-lease=refs/heads/pasture-stable:<expected-old>`; `absent` requires
the ref not to exist. A racing publisher therefore causes a nonzero actionable
failure without overwriting its advance. Fixtures cover first creation,
matching update, stale expected-old, a race between final check and push, and
idempotent retry of the already-promoted revision.

```text
[codex, --version]
[codex, plugin, marketplace, list, --json]
[codex, plugin, marketplace, add, dayvidpham/aura-plugins,
  --ref, pasture-stable, --json]
[codex, plugin, marketplace, upgrade, aura-plugins, --json]
[codex, plugin, list, --marketplace, aura-plugins, --available, --json]
[codex, plugin, add, pasture-skills@aura-plugins, --json]
[codex, plugin, add, pasture-hooks@aura-plugins, --json]
[codex, plugin, remove, pasture-skills@aura-plugins, --json]
[codex, plugin, remove, pasture-hooks@aura-plugins, --json]
```

The selector is always `PLUGIN@MARKETPLACE`; no command also passes
`--marketplace`. False never removes the shared marketplace. There is no `codex
plugin install` or top-level `codex marketplace upgrade` spelling. After native
marketplace upgrade, `plugin add` intentionally rematerializes an already
selected plugin from the refreshed marketplace.

The 0.144.1 JSON codecs remain frozen:

```text
MarketplaceAddResult { marketplaceName, installedRoot, alreadyAdded }
MarketplaceListResult { marketplaces: [{ name, root, marketplaceSource? }] }
MarketplaceUpgradeResult { selectedMarketplaces, upgradedRoots, errors:
  [{ marketplaceName, message }] }
PluginAddResult { pluginId, name, marketplaceName, version, installedPath,
  authPolicy }
PluginRemoveResult { pluginId, name, marketplaceName }
PluginListResult { installed: [PluginRow], available: [PluginRow] }
PluginRow { pluginId, name, marketplaceName, version?, installed, enabled,
  source, marketplaceSource?, installPolicy, authPolicy }
```

`alreadyAdded:true` is success only when the subsequent list proves the same
source and `pasture-stable` ref. A targeted upgrade must select
`aura-plugins`; any `errors` entry is failure, while an empty `upgradedRoots` is
a valid no-change result. After add, the selector must be in `installed` with
`installed:true`, `enabled:true`, the expected marketplace, and matching
PluginAddResult. `PluginAddResult.version` proves the expected selected release;
an optional list-row version, when present, must agree. Missing version on other
valid rows is not an error. After remove it must be absent from installed rows;
remaining in available rows is valid. Unknown discriminants, missing required
fields, and incompatible selected values fail the contract.

Installing Codex hooks does not imply execution. Unmanaged hooks remain pending
Codex's native trust review; the result status is `installed_pending_trust` and
the UI/Home Manager message tells the user to review them through Codex's native
hooks UI. Pasture never writes private hook-trust hashes or claims the hooks are
active before native approval.

Generated packages carry immutable target/component identities,
RuntimeContractIDs, and point host ranges. #39 binds those descriptors to its
ActivationContractIDs. Every action probes the public host version first. A
manifest host constraint appears only when the native schema documents it.
These compatibility checks remain stateless contract validation. Their observed
postconditions feed the separate installation inventory; they are not inferred
from it.

## 8. Goldmark inventory and finite migration

This work has two dependency-distinct milestones rather than one inverted gate.

**Milestone A — inventory/classification (Pasture #47, after #38):**

1. A read-only scanner parses every active generated Markdown owner through
   Goldmark and reports candidate harness syntax with owner, file/section, AST
   node/range, snippet, and candidate class.
2. Maintainers explicitly classify each candidate as orchestration, decision,
   task/process/Git/filesystem effect, portable Verbatim, exhaustive
   TargetLiteral, neutral false positive, or dead owner.
3. The scanner independently walks a code-owned closed list of canonical source
   roots and explicit output/vendor/test-fixture exclusions, rejecting symlinked
   owners. It compares that discovered set with the checked-in owner manifest;
   the manifest is classification input, never the discovery source. Missing
   active files, stale entries, dead-owner dispositions, and exclusion drift are
   errors. The scan emits deterministic source/AST order and is proved read-only
   by byte-for-byte tree hashes before and after. Every classification—including
   neutral false positive and dead owner—is represented by a golden fixture.
4. The classified inventory is an input to #46, #43, and #40; those issues may
   not freeze their closed algebras/contracts before consuming it.

**Milestone B — typed migration and strict rejection (Pasture #42, after #47,

EventID is database-generated and exposed once. Queries order ascending by
`(RecordedAt, EventID)` and expose both fields. EventKind/context kinds are
validated namespaced types. `EventContext` has no exported raw `ID string`
constructor or fields. Built-in constructors require the corresponding typed ID
and reject zero or structurally invalid values. Caller namespaces define a named
string-backed ID implementing the marker method plus a typed descriptor and
validator. `DefineExtensionContext` derives its kind from the named ID type's
marker; it takes no duplicate kind argument, rejects every reserved Provenance
built-in kind (task/activity/actor/git), and requires a valid caller-owned
namespace. At value construction the ID's reported kind must still equal the
descriptor kind. Built-in `string` cannot satisfy `ExtensionContextID`, so
`DefineExtensionContext[string]` is a compile failure. Only the internal
persistence codec serializes context kind plus text.

`ActorID` is the one PROV-O actor identity for humans, model agents, and software
actors; kind is registered metadata, not a separate ID type. The durable wire
format remains `namespace--uuid`, and `AgentID` is a one-release source alias.
Provenance #5 adds a reserved-actor-namespace registry enforced by every generic
actor constructor. Pasture #14's coordinated migration claims namespace
`pasture-system` and UUID integer values 0 through 1023. UUID zero is the default
Pasture system actor. The UUID's 16 bytes are the ordinal encoded as one unsigned
128-bit big-endian integer, with no RFC version/variant bits inserted; therefore
ordinal zero is byte-for-byte `uuid.Nil`. #14 owns manifest v1 and seeds only
ordinal 0 as name `pasture-system/default`, kind `software_agent`; ordinals
1..1023 are reserved but unallocated until a future version explicitly assigns
them. Fresh absence atomically creates the exact claim/default row, exact repeat
is inert, and an exact claim with a missing default row repairs by inserting it.
A pre-claim actor row, unassigned-ordinal row, wrong claim/policy/name/kind/ID,
or conflicting partial state fails with no partial activation. Concurrent startup
converges and every injected fault rolls back claim plus actor rows. Empty
`ActorID{}` remains invalid because its namespace is empty; namespaced `uuid.Nil`
is valid only for the registered reserved default. Ordinary UUIDv7 creation
cannot claim the namespace.
System ActorIDs may author Pasture maintenance events but never satisfy a
harness-user AFK/UAT decision or an assignment-derived agent judgment.

Provenance validates the generic envelope, identity syntax/references, contexts,
and payload well-formedness. It does not import or globally register Pasture
codecs. Pasture constructs an opaque typed event definition, validates its
`pasture.*` payload, encodes it, and passes it across this boundary.

Secondary contexts supplied during event creation commit atomically. A later
context attachment, when necessary, is itself a journalled mutation. Typed
constructors prevent TaskID, ActivityID, GitOID, and caller-defined IDs from
being accidentally interchanged even though storage uses a common textual
encoding. Contexts have set semantics: construction, persistence, operation
canonicalization, and query output deduplicate and sort by
`(EventContextKind, canonical encoded identity)`. Association-row insertion
order is never observable. Each context edge stores the EventID that attached
it (the original event for initial contexts, the journalled attachment event for
later contexts). Snapshot queries include only edges whose attachment EventID is
at or below SnapshotMaxEventID, so a later attachment cannot change an in-flight
filtered traversal.

## 16. BDD acceptance criteria

1. **Given** a typed Document, **when** constructors accept it, **then** every
   part is immutable/validated with source location and Goldmark AST, **and should
   not** expose a mutable optional-field runtime bag.
2. **Given** the canonical source roots and active-owner manifest, **when**
   inventory and strict compilation run, **then** independent discovery detects
   missing/stale/dead/symlinked owners, the scan is deterministic/read-only, a
   nonzero unclassified count blocks the gate, and post-zero native syntax names
   owner/node/range/fix with no output, **and should not** let the manifest hide
   an unlisted file or use regex-rewrite semantics.
3. **Given** a supported runtime contract, **when** an operation compiles,
   **then** exactly one exhaustive binding preserves its semantic contract and
   native fixtures pass.
4. **Given** an out-of-range/newer host or missing binding, **when** generation
   runs, **then** it fails actionably, **and should not** guess compatibility or a
   similarly named call.
5. **Given** a fresh agent continues an assignment, **when** it starts, **then**
   role/assignment/task/worktree/evidence/decisions/outstanding work are restored,
   **and should not** require session continuity.
6. **Given** SelectMany, **when** native UI lacks parity, **then** validated parent
   text returns the same distinct OptionIDs and verbatim record or reports
   unsupported, **and should not** become SelectOne.
7. **Given** an external typed capability, **when** its package contributes and
   invokes a binding through opaque descriptors, **then** its typed ID/version,
   codecs/effects/postconditions hold and exactly one compatible binding composes
   without editing #40, **and should not** expose a tool name/map or accept a
   missing, duplicate, conflicting, or out-of-range binding.
8. **Given** raw string/ID/wrong descriptor/mismatched input capability fixtures,
   **when** Go compilation/analyzer runs, **then** the specified invalid use fails
   under the accurately documented Go literal boundary.
9. **Given** a process recipe with env/dataflow/pipeline, **when** lowered, **then**
   structured argv/input/output edges preserve it, **and should not** hide
   unsupported constructs in `sh -c`.
10. **Given** any task/graph mutation, **when** Apply commits, **then** state and
    required attribution/events/contexts commit together, **and should not**
    leave either half.
11. **Given** a committed OperationID, **when** retried after reopen or
    concurrently with the same command, **then** the original result/EventIDs
    return; a read-only exact lookup returns the same result without executing
    Git or a mutation even after authority ends; absent and conflicting reuse
    are distinguished and write nothing.
12. **Given** two responsibility transfers share the same expected Owner and
    assignment, **when** concurrent, **then** one atomically updates Owner plus

13. **Given** an administrative actor and a material contributor, **when** events
    record, **then** only responsibility/material contribution adds attribution.
14. **Given** a task-linked Activity, **when** start/end succeeds or fails, **then**
    Activity/link/event/context/attribution commit or roll back together and
    replay is stable, **and should not** accept duplicate start, end-before-start,

15. **Given** a relationship between tasks, **when** persisted, **then** both task

16. **Given** equal RecordedAt or concurrent/backdated appends, **when** raw
    event-list or composed timeline pagination runs, **then** public EventID,
    exclusive cursors, and the first-page snapshot watermark deterministically

description:
## Vote

REVISE

## What failed

Marker-present `Open` accepts a task projection whose nonterminal status or phase was changed directly in storage without a corresponding lifecycle event.

## Why it failed

`validateTaskLifecycleClosureTx` validates timestamp shape, closed-state projection, and the existence of at least one task event, but it does not replay the canonical lifecycle event stream to prove the current `tasks.status_id` and `tasks.phase_id` projections. An unrelated creation event therefore satisfies `task journal evidence`, while raw `open -> in_progress` and phase mutations remain invisible.

The migration-baseline close check also treats `EventID` alone as temporal order (`later.id > e.id`), although the ratified event order is `(RecordedAt, EventID)`.

## Where and when

- `internal/sqlite/activation_integrity.go:823-837`, during activation of a marker-present database.
- `internal/sqlite/activation_integrity.go:830-833`, while deciding whether a closed migration baseline is superseded.

## Caller impact

`Open` can accept a database in which the canonical audit log says one lifecycle state while the material task projection says another. Callers cannot rely on the required complete, ordered audit history or safely determine how the task reached its current status and phase.

## Required code repair

1. Replace the closed-only check with an activation-safe typed lifecycle reducer in `internal/sqlite/activation_integrity.go` (or a focused sibling module).
2. For each task, load lifecycle events ordered by `(recorded_at, id)`, initialize from the exact `provenance.task.created` payload or `provenance.migration.baseline`, and apply the typed task-update/status-change/phase-change/close/reopen transitions.
3. Validate each transition payload and prove the reducer's final status, phase, close fields, and lifecycle-derived update time agree with the `tasks` row. Fail closed with an actionable task/event-specific integrity error on missing, extra, malformed, or impossible transitions.
4. Use lexicographic `(recorded_at, id)` ordering anywhere the validator asks whether an event is later; do not compare IDs alone.
5. Preserve compatibility only through explicit migration-baseline semantics, not by accepting unexplained projection drift.

## Exact regression tests

Add marker-present, unchanged-on-failure activation tests that mutate a closed database and assert `Open` rejects:

- raw `open -> in_progress` without `provenance.task.status-changed`;
- raw `in_progress -> open` without a reopen/status event;
- raw phase change without `provenance.task.phase-changed`;
- a malformed, missing, duplicated, or impossible lifecycle transition payload;
- a lifecycle sequence whose timestamps and IDs demonstrate that canonical ordering is `(RecordedAt, EventID)`, including colliding timestamps;
- baseline-created open and closed tasks followed by valid transitions, proving compatible migrated stores still open;
- retry after repairing each corruption, proving activation is non-mutating and deterministic.

## Reproduction evidence

Against exact clean HEAD `df77eae39d752bbd71657be80079ff0ae9f87e35`, a read-only Go overlay ran:

```text
nix develop --command go test -overlay=/tmp/provenance_review_lifecycle_overlay.json ./internal/sqlite -run '^TestReviewProbeRaw(NonterminalLifecycle|Phase)Drift$' -count=1 -v
```

Both probes failed because `Open` returned success:

```text
marker-present Open accepted raw open -> in_progress projection without a status-change event
marker-present Open accepted raw phase projection without a phase-change event
```

The reviewed worktree remained clean.
title: SLICE-1.2-REVIEW-A-9 BLOCKER-1: replay full task lifecycle

Reviewer B (Test Quality) — SLICE-4 (interfaces.py) important-level findings.

## Finding: ConstraintValidatorInterface.validate() type annotation uses forward references (EpochState, ConstraintViolation) hidden behind TYPE_CHECKING — isinstance() test with inline ConcreteValidator returns True even though the type signatures differ (IMPORTANT)

In interfaces.py, the Protocol uses:
    from aura_protocol.constraints import ConstraintViolation  (TYPE_CHECKING only)
    from aura_protocol.state_machine import EpochState         (TYPE_CHECKING only)

The Protocol method signature is:
    def validate(self, state: EpochState) -> list[ConstraintViolation]: ...

At runtime (non-TYPE_CHECKING), EpochState and ConstraintViolation are NOT available as types in the Protocol method signature. Python's runtime_checkable only checks method PRESENCE, not signatures. The test:

    class ConcreteValidator:
        def validate(self, state: object) -> list:  # different type annotations
            return []
    assert isinstance(ConcreteValidator(), ConstraintValidatorInterface)  # True

This PASSES, which is correct Python behavior for @runtime_checkable. However, the test does not verify that the production RuntimeConstraintChecker (the intended implementor of this protocol) would itself satisfy isinstance(checker, ConstraintValidatorInterface).

Recommendation: Add a test that verifies isinstance(RuntimeConstraintChecker(), ConstraintValidatorInterface). This is the AC9 integration test that closes the loop between the Protocol definition and its actual production implementor.

description:
references: round=aura-plugins-91m18 slice=aura-plugins-r7g8k axis=A severity=MINOR round=2

WHAT: dbconn.SharedDSN deliberately sets _pragma=busy_timeout(5000) for the WAL concurrency contract; ReadOnlyDSN sets only mode=ro. WAL readers normally never block on writers, but they CAN receive SQLITE_BUSY during wal-index recovery or a RESTART/TRUNCATE checkpoint — and the PRIMARY use case for this command is live status while the daemon is actively writing. Without a busy timeout, those rare windows surface as raw lock errors to the user instead of a 5s auto-retry.
WHERE: internal/dbconn/dbconn.go ReadOnlyDSN.
FIX: append &_pragma=busy_timeout(5000) to ReadOnlyDSN (read-only + busy retry are orthogonal; this matches the documented concurrency contract in the package comment).
title: A2-MIN-3: ReadOnlyDSN omits busy_timeout — live status next to an active daemon can surface raw SQLITE_BUSY

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-20 — Native multi-harness extensions, with complete scope fixtures

## 1. Structural correction

Proposals 8–14 repeatedly treated a small preference-and-install feature as a
transactional deployment system. Each review fixed a local inconsistency by
adding another cross-cutting concept—ownership, digest identity, authorization,
pending state, recovery, observation, platform capability, or concurrency—and
the next review found that the new concept was incomplete elsewhere.

The problem is smaller:

```text
canonical protocol data
    -> harness-native generated files/packages
    -> nine effective harness/extension choices
    -> native install/remove command or exact standalone path
```

Proposal 20 has no receipt, ledger, reconciler, transaction, rollback, pending
state, recovery journal, ownership protocol, or concurrency model. It uses native
plugin managers for plugin-backed extensions, exact generated paths for
standalone extensions, and one preference-only YAML section.

## 2. Surface-to-data-model map

| Product surface | Existing owner | Minimal change |
|---|---|---|
| protocol behavior | `RoleSpec`, `CommandSpec`, constraints, workflows | remain harness-neutral canonical semantics |
| generated target | `HarnessName`, `TargetHarness`, `EmitHarness` | add Codex; split `sourceRoot` from `outputRoot` |
| runtime wording | raw operational examples inside generated bodies | replace runtime-sensitive instructions with bounded typed operations |
| component package | current root Claude plugin and OpenCode tree | emit explicit skills/agents/hooks package directories per harness |
| installer choice | absent | add typed `InstallConfig` matching the confirmed YAML exactly |
| installer action | absent | one private nine-row `ExtensionSpec` table builds three harness adapters |
| Home Manager choice | current `commands`, `agents`, and OpenCode booleans | expose parent harness and nested extension booleans with confirmed defaults |
| plugin registry/update | Claude, Codex, and OpenCode native state | invoke public native surfaces; do not mirror their state in Pasture |

`RoleSpec` and `CommandSpec` do not gain destinations, package names, install
booleans, hashes, or platform policy. Installer configuration does not enter the
protocol model.

## 3. Pasture codegen

### 3.1 Source/output split (Option C)

Change the outer generator API from a single overloaded root to explicit input
and output roots:

```go
func EmitHarness(
    sourceRoot string,
    outputRoot string,
    harness TargetHarness,
    figuresDir string,
    opts GenerateOptions,
) ([]GeneratedFile, error)
```

- Generated paths are always below `outputRoot`.
- Hand-authored marker files, support skills, figures, and hook assets are read
  only below `sourceRoot`.
- `copyVerbatimSkill` receives both roots explicitly.
- Normal `make generate` may pass the repository root for both arguments to
  preserve existing checked-in Claude/OpenCode developer outputs.
- Clean-output tests pass the repository as `sourceRoot` and a temporary empty
  directory as `outputRoot`; `seedVerbatimSourceDirs` is deleted.
- `tools/codegen -output <dir>` changes only `outputRoot`, not where canonical
  source material is discovered. Add `-source` for an explicit source checkout;
  its default remains the module root.

### 3.2 Target-native runtime operations

Current canonical prose embeds Claude operations such as `Skill(...)`,
`AskUserQuestion`, `Task(...)`, `TeamCreate`, `SendMessage`, and Task-tool
follow-up. A frontmatter-only Codex target would install successfully but give
incorrect instructions.

Introduce a small, exhaustive typed runtime-operation registry:

```go
type RuntimeOperationID string

type RuntimeOperation struct {
    ID       RuntimeOperationID
    Skill    string
    Role     protocol.RoleId
    TaskID   string
    Prompt   string
    Message  string
    Axis     string
}

type RuntimeDialect interface {
    Render(RuntimeOperation) (string, error)
}

type TargetHarness struct {
    // existing fields...
    Runtime RuntimeDialect
}
```

Canonical bodies use explicit typed operations for skill invocation, initial
spawn, follow-up dispatch, messaging, waiting, and user input. The operation ID
selects the bounded behavior and the typed operands carry role/skill/task/prompt
context; it is not one ID per paragraph. Rendering resolves each operation
through the selected target. Literal cross-harness documentation is explicitly
marked literal. Generation fails if an operation is unknown, lacks required
operands, or a target lacks a mapping.

Projection visits every active string owner: role behaviors, constraints,
workflows/actions/commands, command and support procedure bodies, skill bodies,
agent bodies, and generated figures that contain executable instructions. This
is not global search/replace and does not duplicate complete skill bodies.
Claude mappings preserve current behavior; OpenCode mappings repair the
currently inherited Claude examples; Codex mappings use supported Codex skill
and collaboration-agent operations. A generated-output guard rejects unresolved
markers and known foreign operational syntax.

### 3.3 Codex target

Add `HarnessCodex` to the existing registry with dedicated skill and agent
emitters:

- skills are full generated directories with Codex-compatible `SKILL.md`;
- each skill receives `agents/openai.yaml` generated from an exhaustive
  presentation registry (display name, 25–64 character short description, and a
  default prompt naming `$<skill-name>`);
- the five role agents emit as `pasture_epoch.toml`,
  `pasture_architect.toml`, `pasture_supervisor.toml`, `pasture_worker.toml`, and
  `pasture_reviewer.toml`;
- TOML contains supported `name`, `description`, and
  `developer_instructions`; optional model/reasoning/sandbox/MCP policy is
  omitted so the parent Codex session supplies it; and
- Codex plugin manifests declare only supported surfaces. They never invent an
  `agents` component.

### 3.4 Independent generated component packages

Keep the canonical semantic generator and add deterministic package projection
under a checked-in `generated/` tree:

```text
generated/
  claude-code/
    pasture-skills/   # skills-only Claude plugin
    pasture-agents/   # agents-only Claude plugin
    pasture-hooks/    # hooks-only Claude plugin
  codex/
    pasture-skills/   # skills-only Codex plugin
    pasture-agents/   # standalone TOML bundle, not a plugin
    pasture-hooks/    # hooks-only Codex plugin
  opencode/
    skills/           # standalone skill directories
    agents/           # standalone Markdown agents
    pasture-hooks/    # @dayvidpham/pasture-opencode-hooks npm package
```

Fresh `pasture-skills`, `pasture-agents`, and `pasture-hooks` identities prevent
the existing combined Claude `pasture` plugin from being mistaken for a split
package. The generator copies whole skill/support trees, not only `SKILL.md`.

Every extension is independently operational with the other two absent:

- skills dispatch through each harness's generic collaboration surface and the
  installed skill instructions; they never require a custom Pasture agent;
- agent projections inline the role's required command/procedure behavior from
  the same canonical Go specs, so they never require an installed skill; and
- hooks contain their own support assets and require neither skills nor agents.

Package-boundary tests reject an agents or hooks subtree inside a skills package,
a skills or hooks subtree inside an agents package, and any cross-extension
runtime requirement. Each of the nine cells receives an isolated load/smoke test
with its sibling extensions absent.

`generated/embed.go` embeds only the standalone runtime assets required by the
released CLI (OpenCode skills/agents and Codex agent TOMLs). Native managers
fetch plugin packages. Aura Home Manager reads the same checked-in generated
tree from its pinned Pasture input. No source checkout is needed at installer
runtime.

Hook intent becomes a small canonical Go specification for session-start context,
pre-compaction context, and pre-shell Git discipline. Claude JSON, Codex hooks,
and OpenCode plugin code are target emitters over that intent; no target copies
another target's schema.

OpenCode hooks are published as the exact npm module
`@dayvidpham/pasture-opencode-hooks`. Its generated `package.json` version comes
from the Pasture release version. PR validation runs package tests,
`npm pack --dry-run`, and installs the packed tarball in an isolated OpenCode
home. On a release tag, trusted npm publishing first publishes the exact version
under a `candidate` dist-tag, a clean-home gate installs and loads that exact
version, and only then the workflow promotes it to `latest` and completes the
Pasture release. The adapter registers/removes that exact package string;
removal updates only public OpenCode configuration because the current CLI has
no uninstall command.

### 3.5 One private nine-row build contract

Add a private compile-time table with exactly one row for each harness/extension
cell:

```go
type ExtensionSpec struct {
    Harness               Harness
    Extension             Extension
    Delivery              DeliveryKind // plugin | standalone-tree | standalone-files
    GeneratedRoot         string
    NativePackageID       string
    EmbeddedRoot          string
    StandaloneDestination string
}
```

It contains stable build facts only—no hashes, versions, ownership, desired
state, or observations. Codegen package projection and Go adapter construction
consume it directly. Aura reads standalone outputs from the documented generated
roots and delegates every plugin-backed cell to the stateless Pasture command,
so it duplicates no package ID or native command. The table is never emitted,
persisted, discovered, or treated as a runtime catalog.

## 4. Plugin marketplaces and native ownership

Aura remains the aggregate marketplace owner:

- update `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` with `pasture-skills`,
  `pasture-agents`, and `pasture-hooks` entries;
- add `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` with Codex `pasture-skills` and
  `pasture-hooks` entries; and
- validate both marketplace formats with their current native CLIs.

The installer contains only public package IDs and marketplace sources. Before
any split-package install or legacy removal it establishes marketplace readiness:

1. detect the exact Aura marketplace by configured source/name;
2. add it if absent, otherwise run `claude plugin marketplace update aura-plugins`
   or `codex plugin marketplace upgrade aura-plugins`;
3. list the refreshed public snapshot and prove every required split ID resolves
   to the expected Aura/Pasture subdirectory; and only then
4. perform legacy removal and desired cell actions.

A refresh/validation failure stops before removing any working legacy plugin.
The installer then uses:

- Claude: marketplace add/list plus plugin install/list/uninstall for
  `pasture-skills`, `pasture-agents`, and `pasture-hooks`;
- Codex: marketplace add/list plus plugin add/list/remove for `pasture-skills` and
  `pasture-hooks`;
- OpenCode: `opencode plugin @dayvidpham/pasture-opencode-hooks --global` for hook install,
  and a JSON/JSONC-preserving editor that removes only that exact package string
  from the native user-global `plugin` arrays for uninstall; and
- standalone discovery paths for OpenCode skills/agents and Codex agents.

Native managers own installed plugin state, caches, and updates. Pasture never
writes a private cache or stores a duplicate registration record.

After marketplace readiness is proven, the Claude adapter checks the public
native plugin list for the exact legacy identity `pasture@aura-plugins` and one
of the explicitly frozen published legacy tuples. The initial compatibility set
contains `pasture@aura-plugins`, version v0.0.4, native `scope=user`, 31 skills,
five agents, and zero hooks exactly as shipped. New historical tuples are added
only by a reviewed code change with a native fixture. A same-name plugin from
another marketplace is never removed; project/local-scope copies are reported as
separate actionable conflicts and are never conflated with or removed by the
user-wide installer. An exact user-scope Aura identity with an unknown
inventory/version stops with the observed tuple and manual native remediation
rather than being guessed or deleted. The adapter inspects all three scopes
before mutation. Any matching project/local copy stops before removing even a
coexisting user copy; after the caller resolves that scope, an ordinary rerun
performs the user-wide transition. If only the known user tuple is present, the
summary shows its removal and the adapter runs `claude plugin uninstall
pasture@aura-plugins --scope user --yes` before any split package is ensured.
Failure stops actionably. This single native transition is repeated safely until
the old plugin is absent; it has no migration record or Pasture state. An
isolated fixture seeded with the current combined plugin proves every new boolean
combination, especially skills=true/hooks=false, leaves only the selected split
packages active.

### 4.1 OpenCode public-config uninstall

Pinned OpenCode 1.17.18 conformance mirrors native global-file selection below
`${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/opencode/`: choose `opencode.json` when it exists,
otherwise choose an existing `opencode.jsonc`, otherwise create
`opencode.json`. When both exist, JSON wins because the pinned native candidate
order is JSON then JSONC. `OPENCODE_CONFIG` is a separate merged override and is
not where `--global` registers the package.
Uninstall:

- parses both user-global `opencode.json` and `opencode.jsonc` when present;
- accepts comments and trailing commas and rewrites only the top-level `plugin`
  array span, preserving comments, formatting, and every unrelated node;
- removes every exact `@dayvidpham/pasture-opencode-hooks` string and leaves
  similarly named/scoped packages untouched;
- treats a missing array/entry as absent, but rejects malformed files with path,
  line/column, impact, and repair guidance;
- publishes each changed file via same-directory temp, sync/close, and rename;
  failure stops without a rollback pass; and
- runs pinned `opencode debug config` afterward. If a project, managed source,
  `OPENCODE_CONFIG`, or `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` still activates the exact
  module, it reports that higher-precedence source actionably instead of claiming
  false was applied or mutating a non-global scope.

Fixtures cover only JSON, only JSONC, both files, duplicate exact entries,
similar package names, missing entries, malformed input, custom-config overrides,
no-file default creation, and write/rename failure. The real-CLI black-box test
first installs with
`opencode plugin --global`, then disables with the release-built stateless cell
command and verifies the resolved config no longer contains the module while all
unrelated values and comments remain.

## 5. Preference-only configuration

Add only the user-confirmed types:

```go
type InstallConfig struct {
    Harnesses  HarnessSelection  `yaml:"harnesses"`
    Extensions ExtensionSelection `yaml:"extensions"`
}

type HarnessSelection struct {
    ClaudeCode bool `yaml:"claude-code"`
    OpenCode   bool `yaml:"opencode"`
    Codex      bool `yaml:"codex"`
}

type ExtensionSelection struct {
    Skills bool `yaml:"skills"`
    Agents bool `yaml:"agents"`
    Hooks  bool `yaml:"hooks"`
}
```

`DefaultInstallConfig()` returns every harness false, skills/agents true, and
hooks false.

`internal/config` adds two focused operations:

```go
func LoadInstallConfig(path string) (InstallConfig, error)
func SaveInstallConfig(path string, selection InstallConfig) error
```

The loader starts from `DefaultInstallConfig` and overlays explicitly present
booleans, so a missing file, missing section, or partial section receives the
confirmed defaults while an explicit false remains false. Unknown or duplicate
keys inside `install` fail with the exact YAML path and valid keys. Other root
YAML nodes are retained as nodes and are not interpreted by the installer.

The saver replaces only the root `install` node. It first creates the resolved
parent directory with mode 0700 when absent, then writes a same-directory
temporary file, syncs and closes it, renames it over `config.yaml`, and removes a
leftover temp file on error. This is ordinary failure-safe single-file
publication, not an installer transaction: there is no journal, rollback pass,
or second persistent state file. A failed read/parse/write/rename returns a
structured actionable error and no adapter action begins.

Existing daemon Viper precedence and `PasturedConfig` remain unchanged.

## 6. Installer engine and TUI

### 6.1 Nine simple in-memory cells

```go
type Harness string   // claude-code | opencode | codex
type Extension string // skills | agents | hooks

type Adapter interface {
    Inspect(ctx context.Context, extension Extension) (Presence, error)
    Ensure(ctx context.Context, extension Extension, enabled bool) error
}

func Apply(ctx context.Context, selection InstallConfig, adapters map[Harness]Adapter) error
```

`Apply` walks a fixed harness order and `skills`, `agents`, then `hooks`. For an
enabled harness it passes the configured extension boolean. For a disabled
harness it passes false for every extension. Each adapter checks the public
native state or exact standalone path and performs an idempotent ensure-present
or ensure-absent operation.

Missing native executables are actionable errors when enabling a plugin-backed
cell. For a disabled cell, absence is a no-op only when the harness's documented
public config/registration state is absent or can be read and proves the exact
package absent. If that state shows the package present, is malformed, or cannot
prove absence, the command fails with the missing executable and exact removal
remedy; it never reports false as applied while a plugin may remain. A clean home
with neither executable nor native state therefore keeps the all-disabled first
run usable. Direct-file removal ignores only “not found.”

The embedded standalone package exposes an exact current-path list plus an
append-only retired-path list generated at build time. Ensure-present writes the
current files and removes retired exact Pasture paths; ensure-absent removes the
union. This handles renamed outputs without an ownership database or runtime
tombstone file.

The first adapter error stops the loop and is wrapped with harness, extension,
operation, cause, impact, and retry/remediation. Prior successful actions remain.
No rollback or intermediate state is written.

### 6.2 Interactive command

Add `pasture install` and a small Bubble Tea package under
`internal/tui/install`:

1. harness checkboxes;
2. extension checkboxes;
3. summary of ensure-installed/ensure-absent actions;
4. explicit confirmation; and
5. progress/result display.

The command loads saved choices before constructing the model. Back navigation
preserves selections. Space toggles, Enter advances/confirms, and Ctrl-C cancels.
Hooks start false and are visibly described as security-sensitive.

On confirmation the command saves `config.yaml` first. A save error starts no
adapter action. Cancellation saves and applies nothing. The TUI receives injected
load/save/apply functions, following Peasant's useful boundary without copying
its ignored-save-error behavior.

## 7. Aura Home Manager

Reshape `CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync` around the confirmed nested booleans:

```nix
"claude-code" = {
  enable = mkEnableOption "Pasture extensions for Claude Code"; # false
  skills.enable = mkOption { type = types.bool; default = true; };
  agents.enable = mkOption { type = types.bool; default = true; };
  hooks.enable = mkOption { type = types.bool; default = false; };
};
```

Add equivalent `opencode` and `codex` trees. Parent harness booleans gate every
child. Remove the current implicit-on behavior from `commands.enable`,
`agents.enable`, and OpenCode switches; all harnesses now default off as the user
confirmed. Keep unrelated package/protocol/extra-file options independently.

- OpenCode skills/agents and Codex agents use `home.file` links from the Pasture
  generated tree. Disabling them lets Home Manager remove those links.
- Claude component plugins, Codex skills/hooks plugins, and the OpenCode hook
  package use a narrow stateless Pasture command, `pasture install apply-cell
  --harness <h> --extension <e> --enabled=<bool>`. It reads no installer YAML,
  launches no TUI, and delegates to the same Go adapter used by `pasture install`.
  Aura invokes the exact pinned Pasture binary, so native package IDs and
  security-sensitive commands are not reimplemented in Nix shell.
- An enabled plugin-backed cell whose harness CLI is unavailable fails activation
  with the exact option, missing executable, consequence, and correction.
- Hook activation exists only behind `harness.enable && hooks.enable`.
- The module does not call `pasture install`, read its YAML, share its state, or
  coordinate concurrent invocations. It simply applies its own declarative
  booleans.

The current related `commands.enable`, role-enable, `agents.enable`, and old
OpenCode enable options are removed with `mkRemovedOptionModule` declarations
that name the exact new parent/child option. They are not translated: translating
their old true defaults would violate the confirmed all-harnesses-off default.
Unrelated package, protocol, and extra-file options remain.

## 8. Validation plan

### Reproducible native conformance toolchain

The Pasture Nix development/check surface pins the exact PR-time harness tools:

- Claude Code `2.1.208`;
- Codex CLI `0.144.1`; and
- OpenCode `1.17.18`.

Their Nix derivations use locked upstream packages/downloads and committed
fixed-output hashes. Required tests fail rather than skip if a pinned executable
is unavailable, print all three versions, and reject version drift before
asserting any manifest or command behavior. PR tests use local Claude/Codex
marketplace repositories and the packed local OpenCode hook tarball, so they do
not depend on an unpublished package or mutable public snapshot. The public npm
install is an additional post-publication release gate. Plugin-backed tests run
the release-built Pasture binary from a repository-unrelated cwd/home with only
the pinned CLIs and local fixtures available.

### Codegen and packages

- clean-output test proves `sourceRoot != outputRoot` and deletes source seeding;
- Claude baseline/parity tests prevent unintended semantic regression;
- complete sorted inventories for all role, command, and support skills;
- all five native agents per target with target-valid metadata and no mandatory
  dependency on an external skill package;
- runtime-operation completeness and foreign-syntax guards for every generated
  Markdown/TOML/YAML/JSON/JS output;
- deterministic generate-twice and checked-in drift tests;
- `$skill-creator` metadata constraints and `$plugin-creator` manifest validation;
- Claude/Codex native marketplace/plugin validation in isolated homes; and
- OpenCode hook package tests, packed-tarball install, public registry release
  install, and version parity;
- nine isolated cell smoke tests with both sibling extensions absent; and
- hand-authored per-target dialect/manifest fixture expectations, independent of
  the production runtime-operation and `ExtensionSpec` tables.

### Config, engine, and TUI

- missing config and missing `install` section return confirmed defaults;
- saved selections round-trip and unrelated audit configuration survives;
- malformed/read-only config errors are actionable and prevent apply;
- all 2×2 parent/child gating cases, with hooks false by default;
- adapters receive the exact nine desired booleans in deterministic order;
- native argv and public config edits are asserted with injected runners/temp
  homes; separate black-box tests run the built `pasture install apply-cell`
  against isolated real Claude/Codex/OpenCode CLIs; standalone files use real
  filesystem fixtures;
- repeated ensure-present/ensure-absent is safe;
- first failure stops later actions and leaves prior successes untouched;
- partial/default/unknown/duplicate YAML cases and failure-safe replacement;
- an entirely absent `~/.config/pasture` tree proves first-run parent creation;
- an explicit nondefault config path proves only its parent/file are created;
- injected read/temp-write/sync/close/rename failures preserve the old config and
  run zero adapters;
- failure on adapter two after a successful save proves the new YAML and action
  one remain, later actions do not run, no rollback/state file appears, and the
  next TUI run preloads the saved selection before ordinary retry;
- a release-built `pasture` binary run from an empty cwd/home proves embedded
  standalone installation needs no source checkout;
- cancellation, back navigation, preloading, confirmation, and save-before-apply
  are model-tested; and
- no code path writes Git hooks, Beads hooks, or `core.hooksPath`.

### Home Manager and repository gates

- Nix evaluation covers defaults and every parent/child gate;
- generated sources come from the Pasture input, never Aura protocol copies;
- activation tests build/evaluate the real module with isolated homes and the
  pinned stateless Pasture command, verifying resulting files/native plugin lists,
  legacy-plugin removal, hook opt-in, and fail-fast behavior—not shell argv only;
- old-option fixtures fail with the exact new-option remediation;
- the legacy-scope classifier has four independent native fixtures:
  1. user-only runs exactly `claude plugin uninstall pasture@aura-plugins
     --scope user --yes` once and proves the user tuple absent afterward;
  2. project-only runs zero uninstall commands, preserves the project install,
     and errors with its scope plus exact project-scope remediation;
  3. local-only runs zero uninstall commands, preserves the local install, and
     errors with its scope plus exact local-scope remediation; and
  4. simultaneous user+project runs zero uninstall commands, preserves both,
     reports the project conflict before user mutation, and succeeds on an
     ordinary rerun after the project fixture is removed;
- every scope fixture independently asserts exact list/uninstall argv, exit
  status, diagnostic text, and post-state rather than sharing the production
  classifier table as its expected-value oracle;
- Pasture: `go test ./internal/codegen`, `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...`,
  `make generate`, and `git diff --check` through `nix develop --command`;
- Aura: `nix flake check --no-build`, `nix build .#aura-swarm --no-link`,
  `nix run .#aura-swarm -- --help`, and `git diff --check`.

## 9. Implementation slices and integration points

1. **Codegen foundation:** source/output split, runtime operations, Codex target,
   native skills/agents, and clean-output/parity tests.
2. **Component packaging:** generated Claude/Codex/OpenCode packages, embedded
   standalone assets, manifests, marketplace projections, and release drift
   coverage.
3. **Config and installer:** typed preferences, YAML section update, adapters,
   TUI, structured errors, and installer tests.
4. **Home Manager and Aura marketplaces:** nested options, direct links,
   activation commands, both marketplace files, and Nix tests.
5. **End-to-end validation:** isolated native CLI discovery, complete generation,
   installer reruns/uninstalls, Home Manager equivalence, documentation, and all
   repository gates.

Integration points for the implementation supervisor:

| Contract | Owning slice | Consumers | Merge timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| generated component paths and names | 2 | 3, 4, 5 | slice 2 before adapter/HM finalization |
| `InstallConfig` booleans/defaults | 3 | TUI and validation; mirrored by 4 | freeze before TUI/HM tests |
| native package IDs and add/remove argv | 3 | 4, 5 | freeze with marketplace paths from 2 |
| runtime operation IDs and operands | 1 | all generated packages in 2 | slice 1 before package generation |

## 10. BDD acceptance criteria

1. **Given** canonical Pasture role/command semantics, **when** Claude Code,
   OpenCode, and Codex targets generate into a clean output root, **then** every
   target receives complete native skills and agents with resolved runtime
   operations, **and should not** require canonical sources to be copied into the
   output root first.
2. **Given** a first `pasture install` run, **when** the TUI opens, **then** every
   harness is unselected, skills/agents are selected, and hooks are unselected,
   **and should not** install anything before explicit confirmation.
3. **Given** saved installer preferences, **when** the command is rerun, **then**
   it preloads those booleans and preserves unrelated Pasture configuration on
   save, **and should not** create a receipt or applied-state file.
4. **Given** an enabled harness and extension, **when** installation applies,
   **then** its native plugin manager or exact discovery path contains the
   generated Pasture component, **and should not** edit private plugin caches or
   unsupported manifest fields.
5. **Given** a disabled harness or extension that is installed, **when** apply
   runs, **then** the native plugin entry or exact standalone Pasture path is
   removed, **and should not** treat false as “leave installed.”
6. **Given** hooks remain false, **when** either installer or Home Manager
   applies, **then** no harness lifecycle hook is activated, **and should not**
   write any Git or Beads hook under any selection.
7. **Given** one adapter fails, **when** installation reaches it, **then** the
   command stops with harness, extension, cause, impact, and remediation while
   earlier actions remain, **and should not** roll back or persist recovery state.
8. **Given** equivalent Home Manager booleans, **when** a generation activates,
   **then** the same effective extension cells are present from Pasture-generated
   sources, **and should not** enable child extensions while their harness is off.
9. **Given** a released `pasture` binary and registered marketplaces, **when** a
   user installs all selected cells without a source checkout, **then** native
   managers fetch plugins and embedded standalone assets install successfully,
   **and should not** depend on the working directory.
10. **Given** the complete validation and three-axis clean review, **when** the
    work reaches Plan UAT, **then** project-local Codex agent export is the only
    deferred item presented for confirmation, **and should not** reintroduce any
    unconfirmed state-management mechanism.
11. **Given** exactly one extension is enabled for a harness, **when** its native
    loader executes that package with both sibling extensions absent, **then** it
    remains operational from the same canonical Go semantics, **and should not**
    silently install or require another extension.
12. **Given** the legacy combined Claude `pasture` plugin is installed, **when**
    the user confirms any new selection, **then** the native adapter removes it
    before ensuring fresh split IDs and proves hooks absent when hooks=false,
    **and should not** accept the legacy plugin as the skills-only package.
13. **Given** an Aura marketplace snapshot that predates split packages, **when**
    apply begins, **then** the native manager refreshes and validates all expected
    split IDs before removing exact `pasture@aura-plugins`, **and should not**
    remove an unrelated same-name plugin or destroy the working legacy plugin on
    refresh failure.
14. **Given** valid OpenCode JSONC, both global config filenames, or a custom
    higher-precedence override, **when** hooks are disabled, **then** exact global
    registrations are removed without changing comments/unrelated settings and
    any remaining override is reported, **and should not** rewrite the wrong path
    or claim the module absent while it still resolves.
15. **Given** the actually released Claude v0.0.4 legacy inventory of 31 skills,
    five agents, and zero hooks, **when** split installation begins after
    marketplace readiness, **then** it is recognized as a bounded historical
    `pasture@aura-plugins` shape and removed natively, **and should not** require a
    hooks inventory that release never contained or delete an unknown shape.
16. **Given** user-, project-, and local-scope Claude installations can coexist,
    **when** the user-wide installer migrates the legacy plugin, **then** it
    removes a user-only frozen tuple with explicit `--scope user`, while any
    project/local copy produces a pre-mutation actionable conflict, **and should
    not** conflate scopes, mutate any copy in a conflict case, or rely on the
    CLI's default scope.

## Finding: No full end-to-end Temporal sandbox test — WorkflowEnvironment.start_time_skipping() tests are absent — AC6 and AC7 are tested via state machine integration only, not via actual Temporal signal delivery (IMPORTANT)

The test file explicitly documents this limitation in the module docstring:
  'When a Temporal server is available, full end-to-end sandbox tests should use WorkflowEnvironment.start_time_skipping() with the EpochWorkflow class.'

The proposal (AC6, AC7) describes Temporal-specific behavior:
  - AC6: 'advance_phase signal is received → state machine transitions and search attributes are updated atomically'
  - AC7: 'querying Temporal with filter AuraPhase=p9 → the workflow is returned in results'

The current tests verify that the LOGIC is correct (state machine integration tests) and that the STRUCTURE is correct (decorator introspection). They do NOT verify that:
1. The workflow's signal handler actually calls sm.advance() correctly (the wire-up is untested end-to-end).
2. workflow.upsert_search_attributes() is called with the correct values after a signal (search attr freshness is untested).
3. The workflow correctly drains the pending signal queue before advancing (the pending_*_signals pattern in EpochWorkflow.run() is untested).

Recommendation: Once a Temporal dev server binary is available in CI (via docker or pre-downloaded), add WorkflowEnvironment.start_time_skipping() tests for at least:
  - One full advance_phase signal → state transition → search attribute update path
  - One submit_vote signal → has_consensus() path

This should be tracked as a follow-up epic item. The current tests are a pragmatic v1 solution, not a permanent architecture.

## Finding
The remediation correctly moves harness-specific agent guidance into typed render contexts, but it obtains a harness-neutral agent introduction by deleting the instruction-source sentence from the shared RoleSpec.Introduction values in schema.xml/specs_data.go. RoleSpec.Introduction is also the source for generated role skills through renderSkill, and skill rendering has no agentHarness context or replacement Instruction Sources section. Consequently skills/{architect,reviewer,supervisor,worker}/SKILL.md, their .opencode copies, and embedded Claude skill assets silently lose their existing guidance to AGENTS.md, protocol/CONSTRAINTS.md, or active harness instructions.

## Evidence
- internal/codegen/specs_data.go:614-775 removes the shared instruction-source sentences.
- internal/codegen/skills.go:455-466 still feeds roleSpec.Introduction directly to skill generation.
- internal/codegen/templates/_skill_body.go.tmpl:90-95 renders that shortened value without harness replacement.
- The immutable diff changes all four generated role-skill families solely by deleting the guidance, while internal/codegen/agents.go:41-50 adds replacement guidance only for agent bodies.

## End-user impact
Users invoking a role skill receive less operational context than before, despite this remediation being intended to preserve compatibility while separating agent harness wrappers. In particular, the reviewer skill no longer points at the protocol constraint catalog that defines its coding and severity standards. This is not Codex-specific wording and therefore is not deferred to qnhu7.

## Required fix
Separate canonical role semantics from instruction-source guidance without mutating the skill-facing introduction, or add a typed harness-aware skill rendering contract and replacement guidance for every generated skill target. Regenerate all outputs and add a compatibility assertion that role skills retain their pre-remediation instruction-source semantics while Claude/OpenCode agent bodies differ only in the typed harness section.

This is deterministic and converts the false-pass window into a hard assertion.

## Reviewer: C (Elegance and Complexity Matching) — Round 2

references:
  proposal: aura-plugins-v01u

---

## Summary

PROPOSAL-2 fully resolves the two notes raised in my Round 1 ACCEPT (ProcedureStep scoping and SLICE-3 template contract). The 6 BLOCKERs from Reviewers A and B are addressed correctly. No new elegance concerns introduced by the revisions. ACCEPT stands.

---

## Axis C Re-evaluation: Each Sub-Axis

### 1. Module Decomposition — 5 modules, single-responsibility

The five-module architecture is unchanged and remains well-scoped:

- schema_parser.py — bootstrap extraction only (one-time, then verification)
- types.py — canonical Python SoT (runtime-importable, statically defined)
- gen_schema.py — Python → XML export
- gen_skills.py — Python → SKILL.md generation
- context_injection.py — runtime role/phase context lookup

Each module has exactly one axis of change. The dependency graph is clean: generators depend only on types.py, never on each other. context_injection.py imports only types.py, staying decoupled from generation concerns. This is correct.

### 2. Vertical Slice Separation

SLICE-1 → [SLICE-2, SLICE-3, SLICE-4] fan-out is correct. All three parallel slices depend on SLICE-1's expanded types.py and nothing else. No circular slice dependencies. The slices are appropriately sized — none is either trivially small or unreasonably large.

### 3. ProcedureStep Deferral — Boundary Quality

PROPOSAL-2 now explicitly states: 'ProcedureStep dataclass is defined in types.py (the type exists) but PROCEDURE_STEPS dict is left empty with a TODO comment.' This is the right boundary. The type definition reserves the namespace and signals intent; the empty dict makes the MVP scope unambiguous. The validation checklist item 'ProcedureStep type defined; PROCEDURE_STEPS dict empty with TODO' directly expresses this invariant. Workers will not be confused about scope.

The deferral does NOT create an awkward gap in MVP functionality because:
- SKILL.md bodies remain hand-written for MVP (the existing behaviour is preserved)
- The marker-based split in gen_skills.py handles the generated header without needing ProcedureStep content
- The follow-up is scoped correctly as post-generation-pipeline-proves-out

### 4. SKILL.md Marker-Based Split — Elegance and Safety

The marker design is elegant:
- Two HTML comments that are invisible to Markdown renderers
- BEGIN / END pair is the minimal safe delimiter (reversible, detectable)
- MarkerError on malformed markers (missing END, reversed) correctly refuses to guess rather than silently discarding hand-written content

The AC4a edge case matrix (missing END → raise, missing both → generate clean, reversed → raise) is the correct exhaustive coverage. The proposal correctly treats 'missing both markers' as the new-file case rather than an error — this is the right semantic.

One observation (not a concern): the proposal uses 'MarkerError(ValueError)' as the exception hierarchy. Inheriting from ValueError is appropriate — it signals a structural input error without requiring callers to import a custom exception type for basic isinstance checks. SchemaParseError(Exception) is a separate hierarchy for parsing failures. These two exception types serve distinct surfaces (file format vs XML parsing), which is clean.

### 5. Error Types — Appropriate Count and Scope

Two error types for two distinct failure surfaces:
- SchemaParseError — raised by schema_parser.py on malformed/incomplete XML input
- MarkerError — raised by gen_skills.py on malformed SKILL.md marker structure

This is the minimum necessary set. Neither is redundant with the other. A single unified 'GenerationError' would conflate two unrelated failure domains. Creating more specific subtypes (MissingEndMarkerError, ReversedMarkerError) would be premature for MVP. The count is right.

### 6. Bootstrap → Steady-State Transition

The two-phase architecture is natural and correctly scoped:

  BOOTSTRAP: schema.xml → schema_parser.py → SchemaSpec → verify → expanded types.py
  STEADY STATE: types.py → gen_schema.py / gen_skills.py / context_injection.py

The transition is a one-time event after which schema_parser.py's primary role becomes verification (round-trip consistency). This is a clean architectural seam — the bootstrap module does not pollute steady-state operation. AC10 (end-to-end pipeline test) correctly covers the full chain and validates the seam.

### 7. Naming Conventions — Consistency Check

Spec type names: PhaseSpec, ConstraintSpec, HandoffSpec, RoleSpec, CommandSpec, LabelSpec, ReviewAxisSpec, SubstepSpec, DelegateSpec, TitleConvention, ProcedureStep. The 'Spec' suffix is consistent across all protocol entity types; TitleConvention and ProcedureStep are convention/step nouns which is slightly inconsistent but acceptable given they are not protocol entities in the same sense. Not a blocker.

Dict names: PHASE_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS, HANDOFF_SPECS, ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, LABEL_SPECS, REVIEW_AXIS_SPECS, TITLE_CONVENTIONS, PROCEDURE_STEPS. The plural ALL_CAPS pattern is consistent. PROCEDURE_STEPS vs PROCEDURE_SPECS is a minor inconsistency with the Spec suffix naming — but since ProcedureStep itself doesn't use 'Spec', the dict name is correct.

Module names: schema_parser, gen_schema, gen_skills, context_injection. The gen_ prefix clearly distinguishes generators from the parser and runtime module. Clean.

### 8. Complexity Matching

The proposal's engineering response to the problem is proportionate:
- 1,314-line schema.xml with 7 distinct entity types → SchemaSpec with 7 dict fields (1:1)
- 38 SKILL.md files with header/body split → marker-based generator (no over-engineering)
- Role-level + phase-level context injection → two functions with typed return values (no framework)
- Jinja2 templates — dev-only, StrictUndefined, industry standard (not a custom template engine)

Nothing in PROPOSAL-2's revisions adds complexity. The additions (AC1a, AC3a, AC4a, AC5a, AC6a, AC8 parametrized, AC10) are test coverage expansions, not architectural changes. They make the plan more correct without adding modules or abstractions.

### 9. SLICE-3 Template Contract

PROPOSAL-2 adds: 'Worker derives template content from existing SKILL.md files. Handoff doc will specify which SKILL.md sections map to which template variables.' This is sufficient for a plan-level document. The handoff doc specification is the correct place to define the template contract rather than the proposal itself. Workers have a clear instruction: look at existing SKILL.md files and the handoff doc. This resolves my Round 1 note.

### 10. Confirming 38 SKILL.md Count

skills/ directory contains 38 directories total including protocol/. protocol/SKILL.md exists. The corrected count '38 SKILL.md files' is accurate. The AC1 correction to '38 SKILL.md files' (from Reviewer A's B1 fix) is verified.

---

## URD Coverage (Elegance Lens)

| Req | Status | Elegance Note |
|-----|--------|---------------|
| R1 | Clean | SchemaSpec mirrors schema.xml structure 1:1 |
| R2 | Clean | Python-as-SoT inversion is well-motivated |
| R3 | Clean | New spec types are frozen dataclasses (correct) |
| R4 | Clean | Marker-based split is minimal and safe |
| R5 | Deferred (type defined, dict empty) | Correct boundary for MVP |
| R6 | Clean | Two-function injection API, no framework |
| R7 | Clean | gen_schema.py → validate_schema.py round-trip |

---

## Conclusion

PROPOSAL-2 is architecturally clean. The revisions in response to Reviewer A and B BLOCKERs are correctly scoped — none of them introduce new complexity or change the module decomposition. The five modules remain well-separated. The four slices remain cleanly dependent. The error types are appropriately minimal. The ProcedureStep deferral is correctly expressed as type-defined, dict-empty.

VOTE: ACCEPT
