# PROPOSAL-10: Progressive hook activation on the shared acceptance corpus

## 0. Status, authority, and what changed

Design only. Not ratified. No implementation, no reviewer launch, no commit, no push follows
from creating it. No prior review vote transfers. The open post-hoc Plan UAT
(`aura-plugins-q5ams`) remains the later user gate for Section 19.

PROPOSAL-10 is a **surgical revision** of PROPOSAL-9, not a rewrite. The PROPOSAL-9 wave
returned 5 REVISE and 1 ACCEPT, and it verified an unusually large amount of settled material:
`aura-plugins-i5imy` re-checked all eight original Axis-A blockers against what PROPOSAL-9
actually edited and found all eight still closed; `aura-plugins-3hkoz` confirmed all twelve of
its own prior findings closed; `aura-plugins-bxwry` measured the type vocabulary mechanically
(structs 93→112, enums 30→37, **interfaces 15→15**) and traced all 29 added names to a cited
finding, concluding that **no seam moved**. None of that is reopened here. The complete
per-finding ACCEPT / MODIFY / REJECT / DEFER disposition is the PROPOSAL-9 disposition comment
and is re-stated in Appendix A.

### 0.1 The settled user decision, and its now-landed prerequisite

UAT `aura-plugins-q5ams`, 2026-07-30 01:31, user verbatim: **"Do A."**

Bound the ingress wait upstream. Keep the write budget as an honest SLO. Do not build
cross-process admission control.

**P0-PIN has landed.** Upstream `provenance` commit `0976165` on
`feat/governed-allocation-integration` is pushed; Pasture `f513772` pins
`v0.0.4-0.20260730015136-0976165224e9`. Verified in tree at `f513772`: `go mod verify` clean,
`CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` OK, `go vet ./...` OK, and the full `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race
-count=1 ./...` wave green across 38 packages. Measured upstream: a writer blocked on the SQLite
write lock gives up in ~303 ms with a deadline versus ~5.008 s without, and the test was
mutation-verified — reverting the plumbing failed at ~5.013 s.

**This proposal continues to reference the capability, not the signature.** What Pasture depends
on is *a context-bearing Apply that provides a caller lock-acquisition deadline, returning a
definite typed failure with zero writes when the deadline is reached.* The landed shape is the
**optional** interface `ContextJournal.ApplyContext` (`journal_api.go:298-304`, implemented at
`internal/sqlite/operations.go:419-432`). Because it is optional, the Pasture-side change is the
module re-pin **plus one type assertion and its non-contextual fallback path** — see §4.3, which
PROPOSAL-9 understated (`aura-plugins-bxwry` F4).

### 0.2 The six corrections from PROPOSAL-9

Everything the wave confirmed closed is preserved unchanged. Six things change.

1. **§16.0 now extends the committed shared corpus framework instead of inventing a second one.**
   `internal/acceptance` already exists in tree (`269c838`) with `Corpus`/`Case`/must-pass-or-fail,
   a strict data-only YAML loader, deterministic bounded mutation expansion with non-vacuity
   accounting, a bounded report, and a bounded read-only per-plane store snapshot. Four of six
   reviewers independently condemned the duplicate; `aura-plugins-emmh7` cited it line-exactly.
   This is the fifth instance of the "second X" defect this epic has rejected — second graph,
   second FSM, second descriptor table, and now second corpus framework. S1 extends
   `internal/acceptance`; `internal/lifecycle/corpus/**` is deleted from the plan (§16.0, §18.1).
2. **INV-1 is made total, and its fourth live instance is fixed.** Four journal-facing records
   were unclassified and `DisclosureRecord` carried a lifecycle status while spanning the
   no-status snapshot class. All four are classified, `DisclosureRecord` is split into three
   typed records, and an unclassified lifecycle record is now itself a guard failure (§3.0,
   §12.2, §16.4).
3. **Authority becomes type-enforced rather than prose-enforced.** A typed Pasture-issued request
   reference and a bound response-occurrence precondition are required before `Issue`/`Bind`/
   `CommitCandidate` can reach a human decision; scope is stated to be fixed at `Issue` and
   `Bind` never widens it; every axis states what it compares; the axis set is completed to cover
   all eight `NativeBindingKind` values (§11.2, §16.2).
4. **The retention gate and the retention ownership move together.** Retention gates M1, so its
   corpora and its production path get an M1-scoped conditional owner, an integration point, and
   one consistent per-capture-class statement (§15, §17, §18.1, §18.4, §19.1).
5. **The load test can now see the failure mode the pin created.** Bounding the wait converted
   contention into dropped receipts. Item 9 asserts delivery outcome, the ingress deadline gets a
   named Pasture type, and the p99 sample rule is stated (§3.1, §4.4, §4.6, §16.1, §22).
6. **Cross-reference, count, naming, and leaf hygiene.** Six dangling internal `§` references
   from PROPOSAL-9's own section shift, the stale 172-path carry-forward, the missing L4 leaf for
   the two load cases, the fail-open reader allowlist, the two-name corpus, the unpathed corpus,
   and three duplicate or single-valued type names (§4.6, §9, §10.1, §16.4, §18.3, Appendix B).

### 0.3 Binding UAT decisions carried forward unchanged

Every host delivery is appended as a distinct occurrence; database-generated journal order is
identity and timestamps are descriptive; evidence, normative control, and context disclosure are
separate planes; blocking host behaviour does not grant protocol authority; no deliberate deny
ships before its own UAT and internal lifecycle faults remain neutral and actionable; one
occurrence may produce zero-to-many versioned facts, links, unresolved facts, and candidates; and
Claude 2.1.210 `ElicitationResult` remains evidence/candidate only because the pin does not prove
a Pasture-owned challenge round trip.

## 1. End users and required result

The end users are humans directing and approving agentic work, agents receiving phase-appropriate
context, operators diagnosing lifecycle failures, and researchers tracing generated artifacts
through tools and agents back to human signals.

They must be able to answer, without timestamp inference or hidden SQL:

1. Which exact host deliveries reached Pasture, and in what local database order?
2. Which native IDs are claims, and which Pasture actors/tasks/assignments were independently
   resolved?
3. Which exact runtime, schema, codebook, interpreter, build, and context policy definitions
   produced each semantic record?
4. Which facts are asserted, unresolved, candidate, suppressed, rejected, or normatively
   committed?
5. Which explicit links connect a human signal to an agent action, tool call, worktree, artifact,
   and commit, in both directions?
6. Which context packet was planned, which delivery was attempted, and what did the host
   positively prove about delivery or acknowledgement?
7. Why is an event withheld from registration, and what proof is missing?

The simplest design — append native events plus typed labels — satisfies query 1 and fails 2
through 7. Query 1 is exactly M1, which ships first with a correspondingly thin surface. That
finding is `aura-plugins-oygyo`'s, it was re-confirmed by `aura-plugins-bxwry`, and it is
preserved as the proportionality argument for everything below.

### 1.1 Engineering axes

| Axis | Binding |
|---|---|
| Parallelism | Separate hook processes and readers share one SQLite file. `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, JournalID order, and transaction-local conditions decide races. |
| Distribution | MVP is multi-process local storage, not cross-machine consensus or total order. |
| Frequency | Every identifiable invocation appends; bytes, fields, effects, fanout, deadlines, and reads are statically bounded. |
| Reliability | T1 survives T2 failure; T2 cannot grant T3 authority; projections rebuild from the journal. |
| Cardinality | One occurrence has zero-to-many T2 batches; one batch has bounded facts, unresolved facts, links, and candidates. |
| Change rate | Host contracts, schemas, codebooks, interpreters, builds, policies, and execution cohorts evolve independently and have immutable identities. |
| Has-a | An occurrence has native claims and a capture disposition; an interpretation has exact definitions and outputs; a disclosure has a plan, attempts, and immutable outcomes. |
| Is-a | A candidate is evidence, not a transition; an observed path is not a commit; a host event is not authority; a projection is not truth; a snapshot is not a state. |

## 2. Preserved architecture and one-substrate ownership

```text
private hostcontract descriptor
       |
       +--> generated payload descriptors
       |
       +--> independent enabled/withheld activation manifest
                 |
                 +--> generated registration for Enabled events only
                              |
native bytes --> built `pasture hook lifecycle` process
                              |
                              +--> private bounded capture
                              |
                              +--> T1 Journal.Apply  (caller deadline, P0-PIN)
                              |      slot: occurrence
                              |      one new host delivery = one new operation
                              |
                              +--> T2 Journal.Apply
                              |      slot: interpretation
                              |      fact/link/candidate/unresolved slots
                              |
                              +--> pure ContextProjector over committed state
                              |      plan -> attempt -> immutable result facts
                              |
                              +--> EpochControlService
                              |      issue/bind/revoke, then
                              |      capability + deadline + phase CAS -> T3 Apply
                              |
                              +--> mechanical contract-specific response

Provenance Journal.Apply / Journal.Facts ---------------- canonical truth
Pasture lifecycle/lineage/disclosure/phase projections --- rebuildable indexes
```

The pinned Provenance journal is the only lifecycle semantic write substrate. Pasture's typed
application envelopes are `EffectEvidence` or existing typed task/decision effects. The existing
`pkg/protocol` phase machine is the sole normative FSM and the sole holder of phase adjacency. No
lifecycle SQL row, audit row, DBOS checkpoint, cache, cursor, or native host identifier has
independent semantic identity.

### 2.1 Transaction boundaries

- T1 appends one occurrence header through one `Journal.Apply`. Capture failure after a trusted
  registration coordinate becomes bounded occurrence evidence.
- T2 appends one interpretation header and all canonical sibling outputs through one
  `Journal.Apply`. T1 is never rolled back by T2.
- Context policy evaluation is pure. Plan, delivery attempt, and every result are separate
  `Journal.Apply` operations.
- T3 checks current capability, scope, assignment, phase, and transaction time inside the same
  `Journal.Apply` that consumes the capability and commits control.
- Mechanical host response cannot select an operation, policy, or authority.

### 2.2 One-substrate data ownership map

| Record | Canonical identity and writer | Projection / read index |
|---|---|---|
| Occurrence | T1 `EffectEvidence`, mandatory `occurrence` result slot; produced JournalID is `OccurrenceID` | Generic lifecycle record and native-binding indexes keyed only by source JournalID, **derived by replay at M1** |
| Definition body | Immutable definition evidence resolved by `DefinitionJournalID` | Historical body remains resolvable forever; no status stored in the body |
| Definition state | Separate append-only `DefinitionStateFact` (activated / retired) | `DefinitionStateRecord` folded in JournalID order; carries `SnapshotJournalID` |
| Interpretation | T2 header at `interpretation`; sibling produced JournalIDs | Interpretation/output indexes keyed by source JournalID and parent occurrence |
| Fact / unresolved / link / candidate | T2 evidence effects and same-operation result-slot refs | Typed search and forward/reverse indexes; no projection-local ID |
| Capability | Issued / Bound / Revoked / Consumed append-only fact family | `CapabilityStateRecord` folded in JournalID order; carries `SnapshotJournalID` |
| Phase commit | Existing task/decision effects plus `pasture.epoch.phase-state.v1` | Current phase and history rebuilt from journal facts |
| Disclosure | Separate plan, attempt, delivered, acknowledged, failed, suppressed, and revoked evidence | `DisclosureCurrentState` folded from immutable history |
| Artifact content | UAT-selected metadata-only, encrypted-local, or external content store | Journal keeps a policy-permitted typed reference and tombstone; metadata and causal history remain |
| Legacy `audit_events`, context, DBOS rows | Compatibility output only | Never a lifecycle writer; removable and reproducible |

## 3. Type foundations, the immutability invariant, and static bounds

The snippets in this proposal are the complete public design vocabulary for M1-M6 **for the
records, identities, services, and results named here**; per-slice internal helpers are not
public design vocabulary and are not enumerated. (PROPOSAL-8 overstated this; `aura-plugins-4acdq`
was right, and the missing control API is now present in §11.2.)

Types with slices or variable bytes have opaque fields in implementation, constructor validation,
and defensive-copy accessors. Struct fields are shown to make the semantic shape explicit;
implementation exposes no mutable slice and no `json.RawMessage`.

The snippets use existing `context.Context`, `time.Time`, `provenance.JournalID`,
`provenance.OperationID`, `provenance.AgentID`, `provenance.TaskID`, `ir.RuntimeContractID`,
`protocol.PhaseId`, and `protocol.RoleId`.

### 3.0 INV-1: the immutability invariant, now total

Three review rounds produced the same defect from three different reviewers:
`Semantics.Identities`, then `ContextDisclosure.State`, then `DefinitionSnapshot.Status`
(`aura-plugins-u2d51` BLOCKER 2). PROPOSAL-9 introduced INV-1 to stop the fourth point-fix — and
then shipped the fourth instance inside the same revision, invisible to INV-1's own guard,
because the guard's only data source was a table that omitted the offending type
(`aura-plugins-i5imy` BLOCKER A-1, `aura-plugins-wwyvw` BLOCKER A-2).

That is precisely the shape PROPOSAL-9 correctly diagnosed for the bounded-reader rule —
*asserted five times, guarded zero times*. Applying the proposal's own standard to its own
invariant: a rule whose completeness must be checked by hand has now failed four times. So the
rule is not restated more loudly. It is made **total**, and totality itself is checked.

> **INV-1.** Any type this design calls an *immutable snapshot* exposes no mutable field and no
> lifecycle status. Changing state is expressed as append-only facts plus a *derived projection*
> that carries the `SnapshotJournalID` it was folded at.
>
> **INV-1-T (totality).** Every exported type declared in the lifecycle model packages appears in
> exactly one of the four classes below. An unclassified exported type is itself a guard failure,
> not a documentation gap.

| Kind | Rule | Members |
|---|---|---|
| **Immutable snapshot** — resolved by JournalID from the journal | no status field, no mutable field, no lifecycle enum | `DefinitionSnapshot`, `OccurrenceRecord`, `EnrichmentSnapshot`, `DisclosurePlan`, `DisclosureAttempt`, **`DisclosurePlanRecord`**, **`DisclosureAttemptRecord`** |
| **Immutable fact** — one append-only record whose content includes what it asserts | may carry a status *as the content of the assertion*, never as mutable state | `DefinitionStateFact`, `DisclosureResult`, **`DisclosureResultRecord`**, `FactRecord`, `UnresolvedFactRecord`, `CausalLinkRecord`, `TransitionCandidateRecord`, `CommitRecord`, **`InterpretationRecord`**, **`CommittedTransition`**, **`BuildIdentity`**, **`IssuedRequestRecord`** |
| **Derived projection** — folded from facts in JournalID order | must carry `SnapshotJournalID`; writes no truth; deleting it and replaying reproduces it exactly | `DefinitionStateRecord`, `CapabilityStateRecord`, `DisclosureCurrentState` |
| **Build input** — source-controlled, not a journal record | may carry status because it is not a snapshot of journal state | `HookActivation`, `HookActivationManifest` |

**The four additions and one split, stated as corrections rather than as new design:**

- `InterpretationRecord` and `CommittedTransition` each already carried the self-annotation
  `// IMMUTABLE FACT` and were simply absent from the member list. Added, class unchanged.
- `BuildIdentity` is the validated content of a `DefinitionEpochImplementation` body. Its
  `BuildIdentityStatus` is *the content of the assertion* — "this artifact was built cleanly from
  this revision" — not mutable state, and it is nested inside an immutable definition body.
  Class 2, with that reason recorded rather than assumed.
- `IssuedRequestRecord` is new in §11.2 and is classified on arrival.
- `DisclosureRecord` is **deleted and split** into `DisclosurePlanRecord`,
  `DisclosureAttemptRecord`, and `DisclosureResultRecord` (§12.2). "Immutable snapshot *or* fact
  per Kind" is not a legal value under a rule that says *exactly one of four kinds*, and the
  union carried a `DisclosureDeliveryStatus` field that is meaningless for two of its three
  arms. Only the result arm has a status. The split is smaller than a tagged-union exemption and
  matches how §12.2 already gives every other record family its own concrete type
  (`aura-plugins-i5imy` fix option (a), `aura-plugins-wwyvw` fix).

**Static guard, in two rules.** Both live in the existing `go/ast` pass (§16.4):

1. **Shape.** A type in the immutable-snapshot set must not contain a field whose type is in the
   declared lifecycle-status enum set, and a type in the derived-projection set must contain
   `SnapshotJournalID`. Proven by `MutateMutableFieldInSnapshot`.
2. **Totality.** Every exported type declared in the lifecycle model packages must appear exactly
   once in the classification table. Proven by `MutateUnclassifiedLifecycleRecord`, which adds an
   exported record type without a table entry and must turn the guard red.

The table above is the guard's only data source, written once as data — which is exactly why
rule 2 exists. Without it, the guard's blind spot is silent and grows with every added type.

### 3.1 Identities

```go
type ContentIdentity [32]byte

type OccurrenceID provenance.JournalID
type InterpretationID provenance.JournalID
type LifecycleFactID provenance.JournalID
type UnresolvedFactID provenance.JournalID
type LifecycleLinkID provenance.JournalID
type TransitionCandidateID provenance.JournalID
type CapabilityID provenance.JournalID
type CapabilityStateID provenance.JournalID
type IssuedRequestID provenance.JournalID
type PhaseStateID provenance.JournalID
type DefinitionJournalID provenance.JournalID
type DefinitionStateID provenance.JournalID
type DisclosurePlanID provenance.JournalID
type DisclosureAttemptID provenance.JournalID
type DisclosureResultID provenance.JournalID

// Every typed view above declares exactly this accessor. No record carries a
// bare provenance.JournalID beside its typed ID; there is nothing to keep equal.
//   func (id OccurrenceID) JournalID() provenance.JournalID
//   func (id InterpretationID) JournalID() provenance.JournalID
//   ... and so on for each view above.

type ContractEventKind uint16
type NativeFieldID uint16

type Clock interface {
    Now() time.Time
}

type OperationIDSource interface {
    NewOperationID() (provenance.OperationID, error)
}

// One confidence type. EnrichmentConfidence and CausalConfidence had identical
// value sets, and Section 8's no-promotion rule must COMPARE them, so two types
// forced a hand-written conversion that can be written wrongly.
type Confidence uint8

const (
    ConfidenceObserved Confidence = iota + 1
    ConfidenceCorrelated
    ConfidenceVerified
)

// The 1-second hook ingress lock-acquisition deadline was the ONE failure mode in
// section 4 with no named Pasture type, in the section that exists because the user
// chose Option A (aura-plugins-bxwry F4). The landed pin surfaces a wrapped
// context.DeadlineExceeded; Pasture maps it exactly as section 11.3 maps
// ConditionTimeExpired to CapabilityExpiredError. An unnamed failure cannot be
// asserted on, diagnosed, or counted, and section 16.1 item 9 now has to count it.
type IngressDeadlineError struct {
    Deadline time.Duration // the configured caller deadline; 1s at M1
    Elapsed  time.Duration // measured wait before the definite failure
}
```

All typed JournalID views reject zero or negative values. `ContractEventKind` and `NativeFieldID`
are generated closed ordinals bound to one exact runtime contract; arbitrary event or field
strings never cross an API boundary.

### 3.2 Static budgets

| Budget | Exact value and failure |
|---|---|
| Native stdin | 1 MiB; read at most limit+1; trusted registration records `CaptureOverLimit`, otherwise no receipt |
| Native fields | 64; over-limit T1 only, no T2 |
| Native bindings | 16; over-limit T1 only, no T2 |
| One retained scalar | 64 KiB; never silently truncated as complete |
| T1 envelope | 64 KiB; reject before Apply and report no receipt |
| Definition snapshot body | 256 KiB; reject activation before Apply |
| Envelope parents / definitions | 64 each; reject before Apply |
| T2 operation | 1 MiB and at most 225 effects, below Provenance 8 MiB / 256 |
| Facts plus unresolved facts | combined maximum 96 |
| Links | 96 |
| Candidates | 32 |
| Context packet | 64 items and 256 KiB; suppress whole packet on overflow |

## 4. The shared-file write model: an honest SLO with a bounded wait

### 4.1 What is actually true about the shared file

Verified in the pinned tree, and independently re-verified by three reviewers:

- `internal/engine/engine.go:211,227-233` opens `pasture.db` through `dbconn.OpenSharedDB` and
  passes that same handle to DBOS as `dbos.Config{SqliteSystemDB: db}`. DBOS workflow status,
  step, and notification rows therefore share one file with the Provenance journal, the audit
  tables, and the engine projection.
- `internal/dbconn.SharedDSN` pins every handle to `journal_mode=WAL`, `busy_timeout=5000`,
  `synchronous=NORMAL`, `foreign_keys=ON`, and `_txlock=immediate`. WAL admits concurrent readers
  but exactly one writer, and `_txlock=immediate` takes the write lock at `BEGIN`.
- `internal/engine/slice.go:65` gives `SliceSubWorkflow` a 2-second window to receive
  `start_slice` through `dbos.Recv`. On timeout it deliberately does not fabricate success: it
  returns "the slice was enqueued but never started", fires `SliceFailed`, and reports
  `Completed=false`.
- That production deadline was actually missed under write contention (`aura-plugins-ay4yn`).
  Commit `3cc3ca7` correctly fixed it as a test-scaffolding defect by serializing the test's
  signal delivery, which also removed the only thing provoking the production characteristic.
- `internal/engine/review.go:45-59` already treats shared-WAL write pressure as a first-class
  constraint: the vote poll interval is 1 hour specifically so an idle review does not add roughly
  17,280 timeout rows per day.
- `internal/tasks/open_unified.go:194-199` opens Provenance with `provenance.OpenSQLite(dbPath)`,
  and the in-tree comment states that Provenance manages its own `*sql.DB`. **Pasture does not own
  the connection T1 writes through.** This is the fact that decides what M1 can and cannot
  measure.

### 4.2 The coupling, stated precisely

T1 places a write transaction on the hook path. `PreToolUse` fires on every tool call, and
subagent orchestration multiplies that by the number of live agents. The failure mode is not
"hook ingress is slower". It is spurious slice failures: a correctness-visible outcome produced in
a different subsystem.

Stated without the imprecision PROPOSAL-8 carried (`aura-plugins-4acdq` item 9): a contended
append can wait past the engine's window *inside the storage contract*, and concurrent appends can
starve the engine's own notification write, **because SQLite's busy handler is not fair**. A hook
sitting in the busy handler is sleeping, not holding the lock; what starves the engine is another
writer's hold time plus unfair wakeup. Storage success is not evidence that the coupling held.

Before P0-PIN, `busy_timeout` is 5 seconds and the start-signal deadline is 2 seconds. That
inversion is real. **P0-PIN removes it** by capping the connection-local busy timeout at the
caller's remaining deadline, so a contended hook append fails definitely at 1 second instead of
stalling to 5.

### 4.3 P0-PIN: satisfied, and what remains on the Pasture side

PROPOSAL-8 asserted a 1-second caller deadline that no pinned API could provide
(`aura-plugins-4acdq` BLOCKER A-1). PROPOSAL-9 declared it as an upstream prerequisite. **It has
since landed**, and all six PROPOSAL-9 reviewers verified it independently:

### 4.4 The write estimate, stated as an estimate

`aura-plugins-rw6ai` is right that 48 writers is not enforceable: `internal/engine/queue.go:64-112`,
`internal/engine/engine.go:329-334`, and `cmd/pastured/main.go:65-66` make slice concurrency
configurable, and independent hook CLI processes are outside that queue entirely. A p99 is an
observation, not a maximum, so `48 x 5 ms` cannot establish a worst case.

`aura-plugins-oygyo` is also right that an optimistic estimate is not a defect when degradation is
honest and the number is falsifiable.

Both hold. This proposal therefore states the following as a **documented observational SLO**, and
the words *ceiling*, *worst case*, and *enforced budget* do not appear anywhere in it:

| Component | Write transactions | Per unit |
|---|---|---|
| T1 receipt (M1) | exactly 1: one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` covering operation row, occurrence journal row, and evidence row; envelope <= 64 KiB | one host delivery |
| T2 interpretation (M2+) | exactly 1 additional, <= 225 effects | one interpreted occurrence |
| Lifecycle projection | **0 additional. M1 derives projections by replay.** | one delivery |
| Engine slice lifecycle | DBOS status/step/notification rows plus 1 audit row per transition | one slice transition |
| Idle review polling | about 24 | one idle review per day |

**Concurrent-writer estimate, itemised** (`aura-plugins-4acdq` item 10 asked for the missing 16):

| Source | Count | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Hook deliveries | 32 | `DefaultSliceQueueConcurrency = 8` (`internal/engine/queue.go:66`) x an assumed 4 live agents or subagents per slice |
| `pastured` daemon | 1 | one process |
| Engine slice workers | 8 | one per concurrent slice |
| DBOS notification / step writers | 4 | status, step, notification, and recovery paths |
| Interactive CLI | 2 | one user shell plus one scripted invocation |
| Audit / migration | 1 | one at a time by construction |
| **Total estimate** | **48** | this table is the single source the load harness reads its writer count from |

**K = 48.** The contention ratio bound in §4.6 is exactly this writer total, and this is the one
place it is defined. PROPOSAL-9's §4.4 referenced K without defining it while §4.6 and §20 both
claimed it was "named once in §4.4" (`aura-plugins-i5imy` n4, `aura-plugins-3hkoz` C1). §4.6 now
references this definition rather than restating it.

**Design estimate for T1 write-lock hold: p99 <= 5 ms.** This is a *documented estimate*, not a
test gate. §4.6 explains why it cannot be a gate at M1, and what is gated instead.

**Named revisit triggers.** The estimate is revisited when any one of these is observed:
(a) the uncontended hold measurement in §4.6 reports p99 above 5 ms on reference hardware;
(b) the contended/uncontended ratio exceeds K; (c) `aura-plugins-ay4yn`-shaped start-signal
starvation is observed in CI or in use; (d) a UAT activates more than two per-tool-call events; or
**(e) any delivery in the §16.1 item 9 sample returns `IngressDeadlineError` — that is, the
receipt-loss rate under the writer estimate is not zero.** Any trigger escalates to §4.5 option B.

Trigger (e) is new and it is the one the pin made necessary. Bounding the wait did not remove
contention; it converted contention into **dropped receipts**, a failure mode that did not exist
before `f513772`. `aura-plugins-3hkoz` B4 is right that PROPOSAL-9 measured everything about that
change except its actual consequence. §4.6 and §16.1 item 9 now measure it, and §22 records it as
a cost of Option A rather than leaving §22's "append every delivery — no silent undercount" row
implicitly denying it.

Two structural rules remain **hard requirements**, not estimates, because they are checkable by
counting rather than timing:

1. **T1 is exactly one write transaction per delivery.** A second per-delivery transaction — a
   separate projection write, a separate audit write, or a separate activation write — is a
   design violation.
2. **No hook path retries lock acquisition on a fixed sub-100 ms interval.** That retry shape
   produced the observed starvation.

### 4.5 Contention options: what is chosen and what is not

| Option | Status | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Bound the wait upstream (caller deadline) + honest SLO** | **CHOSEN** (user: "Do A.") | Turns an unbounded 5-second stall into a bounded, typed, fast failure. One-day upstream extension of a proven in-package pattern. Makes B measurable. |
| **B. Off-path spool: hooks append to a spool, a drainer moves it to the journal, hooks never take the SQLite write lock** | **AVAILABLE, NOT CHOSEN** | Deadline protected by construction, but 1-2 weeks, and it weakens receipt-before-response. **This is the recorded escalation** if any §4.4 revisit trigger fires. |
| **C. Cross-process admission control with bounded permits and a priority lane** | **REJECTED on design grounds, not cost** | `flock` leaks permits on crash; a daemon socket makes hooks FAIL when the daemon is down, which is worse than slow; SQLite-as-semaphore is self-defeating. |
| **D. Defer the T1 append off the blocking path** | **REJECTED** | Breaks receipt-before-response and append-every-delivery honesty; contradicts M1 as specified. |
| **E. Stage activation by fanout and blocking profile** | **ALREADY SELECTED** — the activation manifest in §5 is the throttle | Not an open question. `aura-plugins-oygyo` R4 was right that PROPOSAL-8 mislabelled this. |

One correction to option E's framing, preserved from PROPOSAL-8 because `aura-plugins-4acdq`
confirmed the analysis: activating `PostToolUse` before `PreToolUse` does not materially reduce
delivery count, because both fire once per tool call. What it changes is the blocking profile.
The genuinely fanout-reducing lever is preferring session- or turn-scoped events such as
`SessionStart` and `Stop` over per-tool-call events.

`aura-plugins-cvlu6` retains ownership of whether the 2-second start-signal deadline itself
remains defensible, and whether it should become configurable, budget-derived, or replaced by a
readiness handshake. It is a prerequisite for Enabling any blocking **per-tool-call** event
(`PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolBatch`). It does not gate M1 receipt on
session- or turn-scoped events.

### 4.6 What is measured, and the recorded override

`aura-plugins-237wx` B1 traced concretely that true in-transaction lock-hold instrumentation is
not available to S1 at M1: T1 appends through `Journal.Apply`, and
`internal/tasks/open_unified.go:199` calls `provenance.OpenSQLite(dbPath)` with the in-tree
comment at `:194-198` confirming Provenance manages its own `*sql.DB`. Instrumenting `BEGIN`-return
through `COMMIT`-return therefore requires an upstream change, which §17 schedules in S7 at M6,
while the measurement would gate M1.

**Recorded override.** `aura-plugins-oygyo` judged §14's resource quantification proportionate and
that judgement stands in general. I am overriding it **only on this instrumentation point**,
because B-general traced it to a specific line and the conflict is structural rather than a matter
of taste: a gate at M1 cannot depend on instrumentation that arrives at M6. This proposal therefore
does not attempt in-transaction hold instrumentation at M1. `aura-plugins-bxwry` re-confirmed the
override as correctly reasoned and correctly scoped.

What is measured instead:

| Quantity | How | Is it a gate? |
|---|---|---|
| **Uncontended hold** | One writer, no competitors. `Apply` wall time is hold plus call overhead because there is no wait to subtract. | **No.** Measured, recorded, and reported against the 5 ms design estimate. It is the calibration baseline and it is trigger (a)'s input. |
| **Contended ratio** | At the §4.4 writer estimate, contended p99 `Apply` <= **K** x the uncontended p99 measured in the **same run, same instrumentation, same race mode**. K = 48, defined once in §4.4. | **YES.** Self-calibrating, therefore invariant to `-race` overhead and to CI hardware. |
| **p99 sample composition** | **A deadline-failed `Apply` enters the sample at the full deadline value (1000 ms), not excluded.** | **Part of the gate above**, and stated because the two natural implementations give opposite gates. |
| **Delivery outcome** | Per run, count deliveries that returned a receipt and deliveries that returned `IngressDeadlineError`. **The deadline-failure count must be zero at the §4.4 writer estimate.** | **YES, absolute.** See below. |
| **Transaction count** | `PRAGMA data_version` delta on a Pasture-owned read handle across the delivery window, cross-checked against WAL commit-frame delta. | **YES, absolute.** Exactly one write transaction per *successful* delivery, and zero for a deadline-failed one. |
| **Retry shape** | Static: no fixed sub-100 ms retry loop anywhere on the hook path. | **YES, static.** |
| **Caller deadline honoured** | A contended append that cannot acquire the write lock within 1 second returns typed `IngressDeadlineError` with zero writes. | **YES.** Proven as a single-append property by §13.1 row 8; as a *rate* by the delivery-outcome row above. |

**Why the p99 sample rule had to be stated.** `aura-plugins-3hkoz` B4 traced both readings.
Exclude deadline failures and the contended distribution is truncated exactly where it is worst,
so the gate is systematically biased toward pass and becomes strictly *weaker* as contention
worsens. Include them at 1000 ms and, against a ~5 ms uncontended baseline, K = 48 puts the bound
near 240 ms, so even a handful of timeouts blows the gate. Leaving the choice to the implementer,
in the one measurement the whole write model rests on, is not a specification. **Inclusion at the
full deadline value is chosen**, because the tail the gate exists to see must not be the tail the
gate discards.

**Why the deadline-failure bound is zero rather than a tolerance.** The §4.4 estimate is 48
writers at a 5 ms design hold — roughly 240 ms of serialized work against a 1000 ms deadline. If
the estimate holds, zero failures is the honest expectation, so a nonzero count is not noise: it
is direct evidence the estimate is wrong. That is exactly the condition revisit trigger (e) exists
to catch, and gating at zero is what makes the trigger fire instead of being absorbed. A
tolerance would have to be invented rather than derived, and an invented tolerance is how a
ceiling gets smuggled back in after §4.4 removed one.

**Why this is not double-counting with the ratio gate.** They fail for different reasons and one
can hold while the other breaks: the ratio can stay inside K while a small number of deliveries
time out at the extreme tail, and conversely a uniform slowdown can inflate the ratio with zero
losses. `aura-plugins-3hkoz` B4's core observation is that both of PROPOSAL-9's gates got
*easier* as loss rose — a hook that gives up at 1 s stops competing for the write lock, so the
2-second start assertion becomes more comfortable, and the per-delivery transaction count is
satisfied by a failed delivery contributing zero. The delivery-outcome row is the only assertion
that moves in the right direction.

An absolute 5 ms wall-clock p99 as a gate is **rejected**: under the mandatory `-race` wave it is
either trivially green or permanently red, which is `aura-plugins-ay4yn` reproduced by design.
Sample size, percentile algorithm, delivery count, and flake policy are specified in §16.1
item 9; the `-race` carve-out is stated there and restated in §16.4.

The two load cases are split (`aura-plugins-0lbsy` BLOCKER 1) into availability and
honest-failure; see §16.1 items 9 and 10.

## 5. T1 receipt: append every delivery, expose no replay

### 5.1 Transport-stage input is private and is not an occurrence model

```go
type CaptureDisposition uint8

const (
    CaptureValid CaptureDisposition = iota + 1
    CaptureMalformed
    CaptureDuplicateField
    CaptureInvalidUTF8
    CaptureTruncated
    CaptureOverLimit
    CaptureUnsupportedSchema
    CaptureEventMismatch
)

type NativeBindingKind uint8

const (
    BindingSession NativeBindingKind = iota + 1
    BindingTurn
    BindingRequest
    BindingToolCall
    BindingAgent
    BindingMessage
    BindingTask
    BindingWorktree
)

type NativeBinding struct {
    Kind  NativeBindingKind
    Value string // opaque validated UTF-8, 1..512 bytes, no control/padding
}

type CapturedPayload struct { // private to ingress/retention packages
    Bytes []byte // copied; never enters the target-neutral model
}

type CapturedDelivery struct { // private transport value
    Contract ir.RuntimeContractID
    Event    ContractEventKind
    Bindings []NativeBinding
    Capture  CaptureDisposition
    Payload  CapturedPayload

```

`CapturedDelivery` exists only between the generated registration coordinate, the private host
frontend, and the retention codec. It has no occurrence ID, actor, timestamp, semantic fact,
candidate, policy, or response. It is never returned by a public reader and is not a second public
occurrence concept.

### 5.2 One canonical post-T1 occurrence

```go
type EvidencePayloadKind uint8

const (
    PayloadMetadataOnly EvidencePayloadKind = iota + 1
    PayloadEncryptedLocal
    PayloadExternalContentAddressed
    PayloadTombstoned
)

type EvidencePayloadRef struct { // opaque tagged union
    Kind      EvidencePayloadKind
    Content   ContentIdentity
    Retention RetentionPolicyDefinitionRef // typed, not a bare JournalID
}

type OccurrenceRecord struct { // immutable snapshot; opaque construction
    OccurrenceID    OccurrenceID
    Kind            ContractEventKind
    RuntimeContract ir.RuntimeContractID
    Envelope        OccurrenceEnvelopeRef
    ReceivedAt      time.Time
    Actor           provenance.AgentID
    Bindings        []NativeBinding
    Capture         CaptureDisposition
    Payload         EvidencePayloadRef
}

func (r OccurrenceRecord) JournalID() provenance.JournalID // == r.OccurrenceID.JournalID()

type EvidenceReceipt struct { // minimal public T1 result
    OccurrenceID OccurrenceID
}

func (r EvidenceReceipt) JournalID() provenance.JournalID

type ReceiptService interface {
    Receive(context.Context, CapturedDelivery) (EvidenceReceipt, error)
}
```

`OccurrenceID` is exactly the positive `ProducedJournalID` for the mandatory `occurrence` result
slot. The former `EvidenceJournalID` field is **deleted**: it was the same value under a second
name, and a constructor-enforced equality invariant is a worse contract than not having two fields.
There is no second row identity.

The process composition injects one `OperationIDSource` and one `Clock` into the receipt service.
Each CLI invocation mints one fresh operation ID before the service's bounded storage retry loop
and reads the T1 clock once. A retry inside that same invocation reuses the same operation input. A
second host invocation always mints a new operation ID, even when every byte and native binding is
identical.

The T1 operation uses static command identity `pasture.lifecycle.receipt.append/v1`, the fixed
`pasture-system/lifecycle-ingress` actor, the persisted bootstrap authority, and one
`EffectEvidence` at result slot `occurrence`. Reusing the same operation ID with identical
canonical input returns the same internal Provenance result. Reusing it with changed input returns
typed `OperationConflict` and zero writes. Neither path exposes a delivery replay status.

**Ingress never invokes the activation aggregate.** `internal/tasks/system_identity.go:87-89`
today calls `provadapter.ActivatePastureSystem` even on the already-persisted path, which reaches
`Tracker.RegisterFixedSoftwareAgent` and takes an unconditional `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
(`provenance@bcce714:internal/sqlite/actor_namespace.go:27-33`) before reading claims to discover
there is nothing to write. On the current path a hook invocation therefore acquires the write lock
at least twice. Lifecycle ingress resolves the persisted `(actor, authority)` pair **read-only**
through the new `internal/tasks/lifecycle_identity.go`. `internal/tasks/system_identity.go` and
`internal/provadapter/actors.go` are owned by S1 for exactly this change.
(`aura-plugins-4acdq` item 11(b).)

The following symbols and concepts are forbidden from lifecycle source and public results:
`ReceiptResult.Replayed`, `CommittedTransition.Replayed`, `RecordReplayed`, `ReplayKey`, content
deduplication, occurrence repeat counts, occurrence windows, and payload digest as occurrence
identity. Content hashes may identify retained evidence objects only. The static guard is scoped to
lifecycle results, so the pre-existing Provenance-operation idempotency flags at
`pkg/protocol/task_assignment.go:28`, `internal/handlers/epoch_command.go:1443`,
`internal/handlers/adapter.go:319`, and `internal/tasks/governed_create_slice.go:193` are untouched.

## 6. Progressive exact-version hook activation

### 6.1 Typed activation contract

```go
type HookActivationStatus uint8

const (
    HookEnabled HookActivationStatus = iota + 1
    HookWithheld
)

type WithheldReason uint8

const (
    WithheldMissingFixture WithheldReason = iota + 1
    WithheldContractMismatch
    WithheldProductionPathFailed
    WithheldExplicitlyDisabled
    WithheldUnverifiedBuild
    WithheldRetentionMatrixPending
)

type FixtureDefinitionRef struct {
    Content ContentIdentity
}

type ValidationRunRef struct {
    Content           ContentIdentity
    RuntimeDefinition ContentIdentity
    FixtureDefinition ContentIdentity
    BuiltBinary       ContentIdentity
}

type HookActivation struct { // BUILD INPUT (INV-1 class 4): source-controlled, not a journal snapshot
    Contract   ir.RuntimeContractID
    Event      ContractEventKind
    Status     HookActivationStatus
    Fixture    FixtureDefinitionRef
    Validation ValidationRunRef
    Reason     WithheldReason
}

type HookActivationManifest interface {
    Entries() []HookActivation // deterministic contract/event order, deep copy
}
```

Constructor rules are closed and non-vacuous:

- Enabled requires nonzero authentic fixture and exact-version validation refs, and `Reason` must
  be zero.
- Enabled additionally requires the build identity backing the validation run to be
  `BuildIdentityExact` (§7.3). A dirty or unresolved build yields `WithheldUnverifiedBuild`.
- Enabled additionally requires the UAT-selected retention matrix to have passed for the capture
  class the event carries; otherwise `WithheldRetentionMatrixPending`. This is the M1 retention
  gate (`aura-plugins-237wx` A1).
- Withheld requires exactly one nonzero typed reason.
- `WithheldMissingFixture` forbids a fabricated fixture or validation ref.
- `WithheldContractMismatch` and `WithheldProductionPathFailed` may cite the failed fixture/run.
- Enabled and Withheld are disjoint and their union equals the independent expected 30-event
  manifest exactly once.

### 6.2 Two disjoint manifests with different authority

There is one hand-authored independent expected 30-event manifest under testdata. It is the
catalogue-completeness oracle and does not import or iterate the production hostcontract.

There is a separate source-controlled activation manifest. It contains only typed contract/event
ordinals, status, proof refs, and typed withheld reasons. It contains no event names, fields,
identities, blocking/mutation/failure/stop behaviour, or semantic rules.

Registration generation consumes the activation manifest and registers only Enabled events. It
emits both the host-native registration file containing Enabled events, and a deterministic
`pasture-activation.json` support report containing every Enabled/Withheld event and its typed
reason and proof refs. `pasture hook lifecycle support` renders the same report for humans. A
support claim may name only the Enabled subset. The all-30 fixture corpus gates the
complete-catalogue release claim, not the first useful M1 event.

An event becomes Enabled only after its authentic exact-version raw fixture passes the real
generated registration/trampoline -> built binary/stdin -> file-backed journal -> public bounded
occurrence reader path. Self-derived payloads, direct frontend calls, direct `Apply`, or another
event's fixture do not count.

### 6.3 One host descriptor source, no second table

`internal/lifecycle/ingress/internal/hostcontract` is the sole typed source for exact event names
and ordinals; fields, scalar shape, requiredness, and identity additions; blocking, mutation,
reconciliation, failure, and stop-loop behaviour; and command surface and host timeout.

One generator under `internal/lifecycle/ingress/cmd/hostcontractgen` emits the closed
`ContractEventKind` constants, the Claude payload descriptors consumed by the frontend, the
registration candidate manifest consumed by activation/codegen, and the audit/completeness data
compared against the independent oracle.

Runtime, frontend, codegen, and generated host artifacts consume these derived files. They never
maintain another event/field/behaviour map. The fixture manifest remains an independent validation
oracle, never production input.

Enforcement is deliberately focused, not a general taint analyzer:

1. clean regeneration in an empty tree must produce no diff;
2. Go package visibility prevents the target-neutral model, codebook, and context packages from
   importing the private hostcontract;
3. a `go list` dependency test permits hostcontract imports only from its generator and owner
   package;

## 7. Immutable definitions, derived definition state, and build honesty

### 7.1 Definition identity and the removal of snapshot status

```go
type DefinitionKind uint8

const (
    DefinitionRuntimeContract DefinitionKind = iota + 1
    DefinitionLifecycleSchema
    DefinitionCodebook
    DefinitionInterpreter
    DefinitionEpochImplementation
    DefinitionContextPolicy
    DefinitionContextPacketSchema
    DefinitionRetentionPolicy
)

type DefinitionID string // opaque constructor, namespaced UTF-8, 1..128 bytes

type DefinitionRef struct {
    Definition DefinitionJournalID
    Kind       DefinitionKind
    Content    ContentIdentity
}

type DefinitionCodec uint8

const (
    DefinitionCanonicalJSON DefinitionCodec = iota + 1
)

// IMMUTABLE SNAPSHOT (INV-1 class 1). No Status field. The body of a definition
// never changes, so nothing about it can be Active or Retired.
type DefinitionSnapshot struct {
    Ref     DefinitionRef
    ID      DefinitionID
    Version uint32
    Codec   DefinitionCodec
    Body    []byte // opaque, defensively copied
}

type DefinitionLifecycleEvent uint8

const (
    DefinitionActivated DefinitionLifecycleEvent = iota + 1
    DefinitionRetiredEvent
)

// IMMUTABLE FACT (INV-1 class 2). One append-only record per state change.
type DefinitionStateFact struct {
    StateID    DefinitionStateID
    Definition DefinitionJournalID
    Event      DefinitionLifecycleEvent
    RecordedAt time.Time
}

// DERIVED ONLY. This enum never appears inside a snapshot.
type DefinitionStatus uint8

const (
    DefinitionStatusActive DefinitionStatus = iota + 1
    DefinitionStatusRetired
)

// DERIVED PROJECTION (INV-1 class 3). Folded from DefinitionStateFact in
// JournalID order. Carries the snapshot it was folded at.
type DefinitionStateRecord struct {
    Ref               DefinitionRef
    ID                DefinitionID
    Version           uint32
    Status            DefinitionStatus
    LatestState       DefinitionStateID
    SnapshotJournalID provenance.JournalID
}

type DefinitionQuery struct { // exact resolve, one kind and ID
    Kind DefinitionKind
    ID   DefinitionID
}

type DefinitionActivationInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Snapshot    DefinitionSnapshot // carries no status; activation IS the status fact
}

type DefinitionRetirementInput struct {
    OperationID provenance.OperationID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    Definition  DefinitionJournalID
}

type DefinitionResolver interface {
    ResolveActive(context.Context, DefinitionQuery) (DefinitionRef, error)
    ResolveHistorical(context.Context, DefinitionJournalID) (DefinitionSnapshot, error)
    ResolveState(context.Context, DefinitionJournalID, provenance.JournalID) (DefinitionStateRecord, error)
    Activate(context.Context, DefinitionActivationInput) (DefinitionRef, error)
    Retire(context.Context, DefinitionRetirementInput) (DefinitionStateID, error)
}
```

Queries are exact and bounded to one typed kind/ID. Activation appends the immutable definition
body and one `DefinitionStateFact{Activated}` in one operation. Retirement appends one
`DefinitionStateFact{RetiredEvent}`; it never deletes the body or the old decoder, and it never
rewrites a prior JournalID. A content mismatch under one definition JournalID is corruption and
fails closed. `ResolveHistorical` returns only the immutable body and ref; **historical resolution
never means latest, and never returns a status.** Status-filtered reads go through `ResolveState`
or the `DefinitionStates` reader (§11.2), both of which fold in JournalID order and both of which
carry their `SnapshotJournalID`.

### 7.2 Typed definition wrappers

```go
type RuntimeContractDefinitionRef struct {
    Definition DefinitionRef
    Contract   ir.RuntimeContractID
}

type LifecycleSchemaDefinitionRef struct { Definition DefinitionRef }
type CodebookDefinitionRef struct { Definition DefinitionRef }
type InterpreterDefinitionRef struct { Definition DefinitionRef }
type EpochImplementationRef struct { Definition DefinitionRef }
type ContextPolicyDefinitionRef struct { Definition DefinitionRef }
type ContextPacketSchemaRef struct { Definition DefinitionRef }
type RetentionPolicyDefinitionRef struct { Definition DefinitionRef }

type OccurrenceEnvelopeRef struct {
    Runtime        RuntimeContractDefinitionRef
    Schema         LifecycleSchemaDefinitionRef
    Implementation EpochImplementationRef
    Retention      RetentionPolicyDefinitionRef
}

type SemanticEnvelopeRef struct {
    Runtime        RuntimeContractDefinitionRef
    Schema         LifecycleSchemaDefinitionRef
    Codebook       CodebookDefinitionRef
    Interpreter    InterpreterDefinitionRef
    Implementation EpochImplementationRef
}
```

Constructors verify each wrapper's `DefinitionKind`, positive JournalID, content identity, exact
runtime contract, and active/historical resolution. Inline ID/version/digest metadata is a
validated projection of the immutable definition body, never another identity. Every semantic T2
envelope contains all five required definition JournalIDs before interpretation begins.

Occurrence evidence contains exact runtime/schema/build/retention definition refs. Interpretation
adds codebook/interpreter refs. Disclosure plans additionally name `ContextPolicyDefinitionRef` and
`ContextPacketSchemaRef`. A later result cites its plan rather than copying policy metadata.

**On `InterpreterDefinitionRef` versus `EpochImplementationRef`** (`aura-plugins-oygyo` R10). They
stay separate, and the reason is now stated rather than asserted: the two-argument
`InterpretationRegistry.Resolve` exists precisely because one build may ship several interpreters.
The asymmetry favours separation — over-separating costs one JournalID per envelope, while
under-separating costs unrecoverable ambiguity in an append-only ledger. Revisit only if a build
is ever proven to ship exactly one interpreter, at which point the pair fuses and the envelope
drops to four refs.

### 7.3 Build identity honesty

`DefinitionEpochImplementation` bodies carry a build identity, and its validity is typed rather
than assumed (`aura-plugins-0lbsy` BLOCKER 3; restores the PROPOSAL-7 §14.3 case dropped by
PROPOSAL-8 §15, `aura-plugins-237wx` B2 row 5):

```go
type BuildIdentityStatus uint8

const (
    BuildIdentityExact BuildIdentityStatus = iota + 1
    BuildIdentityDirtySource
    BuildIdentityUnresolved
)

type BuildIdentity struct { // validated content of a DefinitionEpochImplementation body
    Status       BuildIdentityStatus
    Revision     ContentIdentity // VCS revision identity; zero exactly when Unresolved
    BuildContent ContentIdentity // built-artifact content identity; zero exactly when Unresolved
}
```

Rules, each with a test in §16.2 and a named public-reader proof in §16.1 item 11:

- Two definitions with the **same `Revision` and different `BuildContent`** are two distinct
  definitions with distinct JournalIDs. Neither overwrites the other and neither is "the" build
  for that revision.
- `BuildIdentityDirtySource` and `BuildIdentityUnresolved` are recordable at T1 and T2. They
  produce a typed `UnresolvedUnverifiedBuild` fact rather than a clean envelope claim.
- Only `BuildIdentityExact` may back an Enabled activation (§6.1) or a normative T3 commit
  (§11.2). A dirty or missing build can be observed, but it cannot claim clean provenance and it
  cannot create context or control effects.

requireAcceptedDecision queries only DecisionPlanUATAccepted and returns a CurrentFact condition scoped to that one decision kind. The other Plan UAT outcomes use distinct decision kinds, so an accepted Plan UAT A remains the current accepted-kind fact after a later changes-requested or deferred Plan UAT B. Ratify can therefore validate and commit against stale acceptance A, close the proposal, and persist ratification even though the latest Plan UAT outcome is not accepted. This violates the exact/current Plan UAT eligibility contract and leaves the workflow wrong for end users.

Exact fix: make Plan UAT state one conditionable authoritative family (or use the existing shared pasture.plan.proposal.v1 evidence family) and, when ratifying, require the exact accepted decision ID plus a transaction-local CurrentFact condition whose asserted row is the latest Plan UAT outcome across accepted/changes-requested/deferred variants. Persist that condition in the operation-local precondition evidence so exact Apply replay restores it. Add a focused regression for accepted -> changes_requested/deferred -> ratify(old accepted) and assert typed failure with zero writes.

close_reason: VERIFIED-FIXED cycle-2: commit 298d1a2 gates every Session verb (journaled + un-journaled) on borrowed-handle liveness via sess.gate; doc's 'every read/write' guarantee is now literally true; confirmed against §16 (8 named verbs, all gated) and by running TestBorrowed_PostShutdown_SessionGated + full gate suite myself.
description:
Where: dbos_store.go borrowedTracker.As() (line ~176), delegating straight to b.inner.As(actor, authority) -> sqliteTracker.As() (session.go:58), which returns &Session{tr: <the raw inner sqliteTracker>, ...}. Session's mutation verbs (Create/Update/CloseTask/AddEdge/.../Atomic in session.go) call straight through s.tr with NO reference to borrowedTracker.available() and NO Ping check on the borrowed *sql.DB sentinel.

What went wrong: doc.go and dbos_store.go both assert, as the core Option-B safety invariant: "Every public operation first checks borrowed-handle liveness with a Ping sentinel; once the DBOS root that owns the handle shuts down (closing the pool), every Provenance read/write returns a StoreUnavailableError" (dbos_store.go top-of-file comment; doc.go package comment says the same). This is FALSE for any Session obtained via Tracker.As() on a borrowed tracker: those writes go directly to the zombiezen bridge connection, bypassing the sentinel entirely, for the Session's whole lifetime -- including after the borrowed *sql.DB (and its owning DBOS root) has shut down.

Why it matters (not just doc/code drift): per docs/journal-relational-contract.md §16, "Session is the mutation surface the Pasture task backend consumes" -- i.e. Session/As() is not a rare escape hatch, it is the PRIMARY mutation path real callers use (Create/Update/CloseTask, the three journaled task-lifecycle verbs). So in borrowed mode, the one safety property Option B was built to deliver (no writes proceed once the DBOS root has closed the shared handle/pool) does not actually gate the primary write path. A caller holding a Session across a DBOS-root shutdown (e.g. a long-lived actor session, or a session obtained just before shutdown) can keep writing into the shared SQLite file concurrently with/after the pool close, exactly the failure mode the sentinel was invented to prevent.

Worker judgment 5 flagged this for reviewer opinion, framing it as an intentional "documented boundary": "the lifecycle-gated borrowed write path is the adapter...; direct Session use in borrowed mode is the standalone convenience surface" (dbos_adapter comment / completion note). That framing undersells the actual delivered code: the doc does not disclose that As()/Session's writes are literally UNGATED (zero liveness check, not "less gated"), and it contradicts the "every Provenance read/write returns a StoreUnavailableError" sentence stated as an unqualified guarantee two paragraphs earlier in the same files.

Adjudication: this is a sentinel bypass, not a defensible documented boundary, because (1) the package doc states the guarantee without the As()/Session carve-out, so a caller reading the doc believes ALL operations are gated; (2) Session is the SDK's primary/only mutation surface per §16, not a niche convenience path, so the bypass is reachable by ordinary use, not just power-user misuse.

Fix (either is acceptable, reviewer defers to architect/worker on which):
(a) Gate Session in borrowed mode too -- have borrowedTracker.As() return a Session wrapping a liveness-checking indirection (e.g. a thin borrowed-aware tracker adapter satisfying whatever Session.tr needs), so every Session verb re-checks the sentinel before writing, OR
(b) If (a) is structurally hard (Session.tr is typed *sqliteTracker, a concrete struct, not an interface) and the intentional-carve-out design is kept, then the package doc, dbos_store.go top comment, and the amendment text must be corrected to state the TRUE guarantee precisely: "every operation reached through the borrowed Tracker's own methods (Show/List/.../Journal()) is gated; Session obtained via As() is NOT gated and can write after the borrowed handle's owner has shut down -- callers needing the liveness guarantee for domain mutations must use NewDBOSAdapter, never Tracker.As() directly on a borrowed tracker." The current wording is not accurate and must not ship as-is.

Where in the review: axis C (API/lifecycle coherence), S1.4-REVIEW-C aura-plugins-m33ll, wave aura-plugins-yixkb. Blocks aura-plugins-9y8gt per protocol (BLOCKER dual-parent).
title: S1.4: As()/Session bypasses the borrowed-handle liveness sentinel (contradicts documented guarantee)

# SLICE-8: Workflow integration + §7.12 epoch-ID validation

PROPOSAL-2 §7.11 (workflow integration), §7.12 (epoch-ID validation policy), §11 Scenario 2 (R13 SA dual-write), §11 Scenarios 8a–8e (emission side), §11 Scenario 13 (malformed epoch-ID rejection); IMPL_PLAN §3 S8.

## Scope

`Activities.RecordTransition` and `Activities.RecordAuditEvent` change internally: instead of `audit.Trail.RecordEvent(...)` directly, they call `protocol.TaskTracker.RecordEvent(...)` → returns `event_id`, then `protocol.TaskTracker.AttachContext(ctx, event_id, ContextEpoch, epochID)` to record epoch correlation. The `workflow.UpsertSearchAttributes(...)` in `internal/temporal/workflow.go` is **byte-identical** to today's (R13 preserved).

Activities pick the right `agent_id` from the `WellKnownAgentCache` (S7) based on which automaton fires (e.g., `CheckConstraints` uses `pasture/automaton/check-constraints` AgentID; `RecordTransition` uses an appropriate transition-gate agent). For `consensus-reached` and `create-followup` (UAT-1 first-class agents), wire emission points where consensus checks succeed and where follow-up epics get created (may be only stubbed if no caller exists yet, but agents are registered + emission tests verify the path).

§7.12 epoch-ID validation: in `cmd/pasture-msg/epoch.go` (CLI entry point) AND `internal/temporal/activities.go`'s `RecordTransition`, call `provenance.ParseTaskID(epochID)` before any signal/workflow start; reject malformed with `*StructuredError{CategoryValidation, ...}` per the §7.12 example (Fix containing `"pasture task create REQUEST"`).

## Files to create

- `pasture/internal/temporal/activities_test.go` — extend with integration test running `EpochWorkflow` start → advance → end, asserting all 4 layers (activities, audit_events, context_edges, SAs) populated correctly + Scenario 13 epoch-ID rejection.

## Files to modify

- `pasture/internal/temporal/activities.go` — modify `RecordTransition`, `RecordAuditEvent` to use `protocol.TaskTracker.RecordEvent` + `AttachContext`; pick agent_id from `WellKnownAgentCache`. Add §7.12 validation to `RecordTransition`.
- `pasture/cmd/pastured/main.go` — wire `protocol.TaskTracker` (instead of bare `audit.Trail`) into `Activities` (replace `Activities.Trail audit.Trail` with `Activities.Tracker protocol.TaskTracker`, OR keep both with `Tracker` precedence for new paths).
- `pasture/cmd/pasture-msg/epoch.go` — add `provenance.ParseTaskID(epochID)` validation in `epochStartCmd.RunE`; reject with `CategoryValidation` per §7.12.
- `pasture/internal/handlers/epoch_start.go` (if it exists) — same validation enforcement at handler boundary.

## BDD scenarios owned

- **Scenario 2** (R13 SA dual-write preserved) — full; snapshot-diff against captured pre-implementation SA values.
- **Scenarios 8a–8e** (emission side; registration side in S7) — for each AutomatonRole, run the workflow path that fires it; assert the resulting event row's `agent_id` matches the cached well-known agent for that role AND `pasture_agent_categories.automaton_role` matches.

- Integration test passes end-to-end (start → advance → end).
- All quality gates pass.

# Proposal 26 review C: Elegance

- Reviewer: Terra
- Review effort: high
- Axis: elegance
- Vote: REVISE
- Counts: 2 BLOCKER / 2 IMPORTANT / 1 MINOR

## BLOCKER

### 1. Shared `EffectSet` semantics have no authoritative type owner or dependency edge

Issue #41 depends only on #38 but exposes `EffectSet` in its public capability
API. The effect-algebra issue also uses `EffectSet`, while issue #46 owns the
concrete effect algebra and #38 does not define the shared type. This makes the
construction DAG and ownership ambiguous.

Repair with one explicit architecture:

- #38 owns a minimal opaque semantic-effect vocabulary consumed by #41 and
  #46, while #46 owns concrete operations; or
- #41 depends on #46.

Freeze ownership of the codec, equality, and compatibility semantics.

### 2. `SliceCloseAuthorization` cannot prove one fix-free clean review round

The proposed evidence can combine axes from different rounds or different
worktree subjects within one wave. Introduce a typed `ReviewRoundID` and
immutable reviewed-subject evidence. Require all three axes to accept the same
round and subject, prove the round was fix-free, and reject later material
mutation or REVISE. Add no-write tests for mixed rounds and mixed subjects.

## IMPORTANT

### 1. DirectFile assets have no owned runtime-delivery architecture

The released CLI must install generated assets without a source checkout, but
the proposal and #39 only map `TargetRootID` to destinations. Assign the target
packages ownership of embedded `fs.FS` bundles or define a deterministic
companion share tree. Require #39 to resolve `TargetRootID` through that API,
not the current working directory, and test a packaged CLI from an unrelated
empty directory. This does not require a receipt.

### 2. Issue #38's contract is stale

The proposal includes `SendAssignmentMessage`, while #38 omits it. Issue #38
also says #42 owns the legacy inventory, conflicting with #47 inventory and
#42 migration, and it does not own or name the foundational effect type.
Synchronize #38 with the exact closed core operations, shared types, and
current inventory ownership.

## MINOR

### 1. Issue #46 incorrectly lists #43 as a consumer

The effect-algebra draft says #43 consumes #46, while the proposal and tracker
keep them independent until #40. Remove #43 from the consumer list or add the
dependency; the cleaner design keeps them independent.

# PROPOSAL-1-REVIEW-B-1: Test Quality Review

## Axis: Test Quality
Reviewer: B (Test Quality)
Round: 1

## Summary Verdict

The proposal's test strategy is **adequate for a plan-level review**. The BDD acceptance criteria are complete, testable, and follow the Given/When/Then/Should Not format established by the codebase. The validation checklist covers the primary scenarios. The architectural decisions (Protocol-based AuditTrail, DI-injected config, subprocess integration tests) align with existing codebase test conventions. No BLOCKER-level test strategy gaps exist.

## Evaluation Against Test Quality Criteria

### 1. Integration tests favoured over brittle unit tests? YES

The proposal designs components in a way that naturally supports the codebase's established integration test pattern:

- **aura-msg CLI**: The existing `test_aura_msg.py` already uses subprocess-based integration tests (running the actual script, checking exit codes, parsing stdout/stderr). The proposal's nested subcommand rewrite preserves the `build_parser()` function that enables both importlib-based unit tests AND subprocess-based integration tests — the exact pattern already used.
- **aurad CLI**: Same pattern as above. The existing `test_aurad.py` uses importlib loading + subprocess integration. The proposal extends `parse_args()` with `--audit-trail` and `--config` flags, which fits directly into the existing `_load_aurad()` + `_clean_env()` test harness.
- **SqliteAuditTrail**: The proposal designs this to satisfy the `AuditTrail` Protocol, meaning it can be tested via `ActivityEnvironment` (Temporal's in-process activity test harness) — the same approach used in `test_audit_activities.py`.
- **SliceWorkflow**: The proposal mentions `WorkflowEnvironment.start_local()` for end-to-end sandbox tests, consistent with the bottom of `test_workflow.py`.

### 2. System under test NOT mocked — mock dependencies only? YES

The proposal's architecture supports this through DI:

- **Config loading**: `resolve_connection()` accepts `config_path` as a parameter, allowing tests to pass a `tmp_path` YAML file instead of mocking filesystem calls. No need for `unittest.mock.patch`.
- **AuditTrail selection**: The existing `init_audit_trail()` singleton injection pattern (see `test_audit_activities.py`) means `SqliteAuditTrail` can be tested by constructing it with a `tmp_path` db_path — no mocking needed.
- **DualWriteAuditTrail**: Composes `SqliteAuditTrail` via constructor injection. Tests can pass a real `SqliteAuditTrail(db_path=tmp_path / "test.db")`.

The codebase has exactly ONE use of `unittest.mock.patch` across 1300+ tests (in `test_session_registry.py` for `os.kill` side effects), and the proposal does not introduce any new mock patterns. The proposal's DI approach (constructor parameters, `argv=[]` parameter on `parse_args`, `config_path` parameter) is consistent with the codebase's test-friendly design.

### 3. Shared fixtures for common test values? ADEQUATE

- The proposal does not explicitly define new shared fixtures, but the new modules integrate with existing fixture infrastructure in `conftest.py` (e.g., `epoch_id`, `sm`, `sm_at_p4`).
- The `ConnectionConfig`, `AuradConfig`, `AuraMsgConfig` dataclasses are `frozen=True`, making them naturally suitable as fixture return values.
- The existing `_make_event()` helper in `test_audit_activities.py` can be reused for `SqliteAuditTrail` tests.

### 4. Assert observable outcomes, not internal state? YES

The BDD acceptance criteria correctly assert observable outcomes:
- Exit codes (0, 1, 2, 3) — externally observable
- stdout JSON content (`current_phase`, `workflow_id`, `run_id`) — externally observable
- stderr error messages — externally observable
- File creation at XDG paths — externally observable
- Event persistence across restart — observable via query
- Timeout behavior — observable via SliceResult

No acceptance criterion asserts internal variable values or private implementation details.

## BDD Acceptance Criteria Review

The proposal includes 8 BDD acceptance criteria, all in proper Given/When/Then/Should Not format:

| AC | Coverage | Testable? | Edge Cases? |
|----|----------|-----------|-------------|
| query state JSON output | R5 | Yes — subprocess + JSON parse | Should also cover `--format text` variant |
| epoch start | R8 | Yes — subprocess + JSON parse | Orphan cleanup on failure is a good edge case |
| missing --epoch-id | R3 | Yes — argparse SystemExit | Correct: validates before connecting |
| YAML config resolution | R4, R12 | Yes — tmp_path YAML file + assert connection | Good: tests fallback chain |
| aurad sqlite audit | R10 | Yes — tmp_path DB + restart test | Good: persistence across restart |
| SliceWorkflow timeout | R9 | Yes — WorkflowEnvironment + timer | Good: asserts bounded execution |
| SliceWorkflow shell command | R9 | Yes — WorkflowEnvironment + activity | Correct: checks stdout capture |
| Claude Code hook | R13 | Yes — subprocess + env var | Good: graceful degradation when aurad down |

**Assessment**: All 8 BDD criteria are testable using the codebase's established patterns. They cover the critical user-facing paths.

## Validation Checklist Review

The validation checklist has 18 items covering:
- CLI help output (item 1)
- Output formats JSON and text (items 2-3)
- All 4 subcommands (items 4-6)
- Error exit codes (items 7-8)
- Config loading and priority chain (items 9-10)
- SQLite audit trail (items 11-13)
- SliceWorkflow timeout and heartbeat (items 14-15)
- Claude Code hook (item 16)
- Rename verification (item 17)
- Regression check: all 1017 existing tests pass (item 18)

**Assessment**: The checklist is thorough. It correctly includes the regression guard (item 18).

## Minor Observations (Non-blocking)

1. **Missing BDD criterion for R2 (nested subcommands)**: The validation checklist covers `--help` showing subcommand groups (item 1), but there is no explicit BDD criterion for the structural change from flat to nested subcommands. The existing `test_aura_msg.py` tests flat subcommands (`start-epoch`, `signal-vote`, etc.) — the proposal should note that these tests will need to be rewritten for the new nested format (`query state`, `signal vote`, etc.). This is implicit in the proposal but not called out.

2. **Missing BDD criterion for config priority chain**: There is a BDD criterion for "YAML config when no CLI and no env," but no explicit BDD criterion for "CLI > env > YAML > defaults" as a full priority chain test. The validation checklist item 10 covers this, which is sufficient.

3. **DualWriteAuditTrail SA upsert testing**: The proposal correctly notes that SA upserts happen in workflow code, not in the activity. However, no BDD criterion explicitly tests the dual-write behavior (SQLite write + SA upsert together). This is acceptable for MVP scope since the SA upsert is documented as a workflow-level concern.

4. **SqliteAuditTrail concurrency**: No mention of concurrent write testing for the SQLite backend. Since `aurad` runs as a single worker process, this is acceptable for MVP, but worth noting for future slices.

These observations are non-blocking and do not rise to REVISE level. They are suggestions for the implementation slices to incorporate naturally.

## End-User Alignment Assessment

1. **Who are the end-users?** Developers using `aura-msg` CLI and Claude Code agents interacting via hooks. The test strategy tests the actual CLI (subprocess integration), which is exactly what end-users run.

2. **What would end-users want?** Reliable CLI with clear error messages and correct exit codes. The BDD criteria cover this with exit codes 0/1/2/3 and actionable error messages.

3. **How would this affect them?** If tests are inadequate, users would encounter untested failure modes. The test strategy covers the primary paths: success, user error, connection error, workflow error.

4. **Are there implementation gaps?** No significant gaps in the test strategy. The DI-based architecture ensures testability without mocks.

5. **Does MVP scope make sense?** Yes. The test strategy appropriately scopes to CLI integration tests and AuditTrail unit/integration tests, deferring full SliceWorkflow stress testing to later.

6. **Is validation checklist complete and correct?** Yes, with the regression guard (item 18) being particularly important.

## Vote

**ACCEPT** — The proposal's test strategy is adequate. BDD acceptance criteria are complete and testable using established codebase conventions (subprocess integration, ActivityEnvironment, importlib loading, DI via constructor parameters, no unittest.mock). The validation checklist is thorough and includes regression protection.

# M2-Only Stop Condition

This plan implements only the shared post-L2 derivation and OpenCode 1.18.10 M2 vertical. Codex profiles, fixtures, code generation, activation, workers, and M3 planning remain blocked until M2 receives a fix-free clean code-review wave and explicit Implementation UAT acceptance.

# Phase 8 User Decisions

Question shown verbatim: How many code-review/fix rounds should M2 allow per implementation slice before escalating or carrying non-blocking findings forward?

Initial response shown verbatim: 3 rounds (Recommended)

User correction shown verbatim: This should not be review/fix per SLICE: it should be review/fix per WAVE.

User execution correction shown verbatim: Waves are broken into parallel SLICES, each operating in ISOLATED WORKTREES, following the same pattern as @~/dev/peasant-labs/AGENTS.md

Final interpretation: implementation is organized into ordered waves. Each wave contains parallel slices in isolated worktrees. All completed slices are consolidated and reviewed together, while verdicts and severity trees remain per slice. Each implementation wave permits at most three review/fix rounds and must end with one fix-free 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR integrated review. A dirty third round escalates to the user and does not advance.

The user also explicitly prohibited aura-swarm and aura-parallel. The parent supervisor creates worktrees and coordinates Task workers directly.

# Corrected Current-Tree Facts

- The source tree is clean at the exact baseline.
- internal/lifecycle/middleend is new and must consume existing waist, legalize, backend, receipt, provenance, model, runtime, and registration contracts without duplicating enums or schemas.
- OpenCode remains pinned to 1.17.18 in runtime, codegen, tests, fixtures, and generated outputs; M2 replaces that active profile with exact 1.18.10 without dual-version support.
- The OpenCode host-contract generator owns registration and ingress payload outputs. Generated files are never hand-edited or hand-merged.
- OpenCode generated artifacts are opencode.json, .opencode/plugins/pasture-lifecycle.ts, and .opencode/pasture-opencode.json.
- hooks/pasture-activation.json and its embedded Claude asset are Claude-owned and remain byte-identical at SHA-256 f248de1b7dbd95373c6c01f1e052e69bbba766ab70f65770cdcbfd767c9a70b0.
- The repository has no .github CI workflow. This plan adds Bun only to the existing flake.nix test/development environment; it does not invent a new CI workflow.
- The documentation slice owns exactly the six paths ratified in proposal 3 and changes no runtime behavior.

# Wave Structure

| Wave | Parallel slices | Base | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | S1 shared Derivation; S2 OpenCode profile/fixtures/ingress/L2; S3 documentation | 0414ad9a7455905c6f865468fe0f2c23222d11b7 | Consolidated gates plus clean integrated review |
| 2 | S4 durable handler/CLI; S5 generated TypeScript/Bun | Accepted Wave 1 SHA | S5 production-proof leaf waits for S4 wiring leaf; consolidated gates plus clean review |
| 3 | S6 activation-last generated-to-read-back proof | Accepted Wave 2 SHA | Consolidated gates plus clean review, then Implementation UAT |

There are six slices and seventeen leaves. All leaves in a slice belong to one worker and one isolated worktree. The supervisor owns integration and conflict resolution. A later wave branches only from the accepted consolidated SHA of the preceding wave.

# Horizontal Integration Points

| ID | Contract | Owner | Consumers | Merge timing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IP-1 | middleend.Derivation and Derive | S1 | S4, S6 | Wave 1 consolidation |
| IP-2 | OpenCode 1.18.10 registration, ingress, frontend, verified L2 | S2 | S4, S5, S6 | Wave 1 consolidation |
| IP-3 | Post-commit backend.HostResponse handler/CLI contract | S4 | S5 final proof, S6 | S4 wiring leaf checkpoint in Wave 2 |
| IP-4 | Bun-executable generated OpenCode transport | S5 | S6 | Wave 2 consolidation |
| IP-5 | Correct M1 and privacy documentation | S3 | M2 UAT | Wave 1 consolidation |

# Review Protocol

Three independent reviewers assess every completed slice in the same integrated wave candidate across correctness, test quality, and elegance. Review tasks and eager BLOCKER/IMPORTANT/MINOR groups remain per slice, with one shared wave round number and integrated commit. All findings are fixed; none route to a follow-up epic. Review proceeds for at most three rounds per implementation wave. Only a fix-free 0/0/0 round closes slices and the wave barrier.

# Consolidated Validation Gates

- Every focused and full Go test command includes -race.

### R17: SecurityGate wires to Agentfilter (ACP-compliant)
- SecurityGate (currently NullSecurityGate) check_tool_permission() MUST use Agentfilter's ACP RequestPermission mechanism
- ToolPermissionRequest MUST align to ACP RequestPermission structure

## Dependencies

- Blocked on: Claude Code native ACP support (github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/6686) or community adapter maturity
