# Architecture decisions

## D1. frontendRegistry: static literal map replaces the dispatch switch (R2.1)

Replace the `dispatchLifecycle` switch body with a package-level closed literal in `internal/handlers`:

```go
// internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go
type lifecycleDispatch struct {
    name        string
    manifest    registration.Manifest
    activations func() ([]activation.Entry, error) // lazy: proofs are fallible; error path parity with today
    parse       func([]byte, registration.Event, string) lifecycleCapture
    bind        func(model.ContractEventKind, []model.NativeBinding) (waist.L1, []waist.Identity, error)
    encode      func(backend.HostResponse) ([]byte, error) // D4
}

var frontendRegistry = map[ir.HarnessID]lifecycleDispatch{
    ir.HarnessClaudeCode: { name: "Claude", manifest: registration.ClaudeCode2_1_210(), activations: activation.ClaudeCode2_1_210, parse: ..., bind: claudefrontend.Bind, encode: nativeresponse.CanonicalProceed },
    ir.HarnessOpenCode:   { ... },
    ir.HarnessCodex:      { ..., encode: nativeresponse.CodexContinuation },
}

func dispatchLifecycle(harness ir.HarnessID) (lifecycleDispatch, error) // map lookup; unknown-harness default error text unchanged
```

Semantics preserved exactly: `manifest` values come from generated infallible-by-construction constructors (they panic only on corrupted generated literals, which the suite and codegen-drift CI catch — same failure surface as today's first dispatch); `activations` stays a fallible call at dispatch time with today's wrapped error text ("dispatch %s lifecycle activation: %w"); the unknown-harness structured error (:189-190) is kept verbatim. `dispatchLifecycle` keeps its name and signature; the sole caller (:83) is untouched.

Scope guard (reconciles the prior rejection honestly — see Tradeoffs): the registry is COMPILE-TIME STATIC map construction over the closed `ir.HarnessID` enum. No `init()` registration, no reflection, no string reverse lookup, no arbitrary provider maps, no public registration API. Deferred issue #62 (generic native event-name lookup) remains deferred — this map is keyed by the typed harness ID the CLI already passes, not by native names.

## D2. Generic Bind with strictest-common semantics (R2.2, R2.7)

New root package `internal/lifecycle/frontend` (currently subdirectories only — no conflict; root does not import subpackages, so no cycle):

```go
// internal/lifecycle/frontend/frontend.go
package frontend

// Host is the per-harness data the generic Bind consumes. E is the harness's
// closed uint8 event enum (runtime.ClaudeLifecycleEvent, ...).
type Host[E comparable] struct {
    Label    string                              // "Claude" | "OpenCode" | "Codex" — error attribution
    Contract func() runtime.LifecycleContract[E] // pinned profile constructor (F10)
    Events   map[model.ContractEventKind]E       // closed ordinal→enum map — HOST-PINNED DATA (R2.7)
}

// Bind is the one shared frontend skeleton (strictest-common): ordinal→enum,
// contract.Mapping, waist.BindEvent, then per binding — declared-field check,
// duplicate-name guard, kind agreement, waist.NewIdentity — in Claude's exact
// check order (F4).
func Bind[E comparable](host Host[E], modelKind model.ContractEventKind, bindings []model.NativeBinding) (waist.L1, []waist.Identity, error)
```

Per-host packages shrink to data + a monomorphic wrapper (registry row signature unchanged):

```go
// internal/lifecycle/frontend/claude/claude.go — analogous for codex, opencode
var host = frontend.Host[runtime.ClaudeLifecycleEvent]{ Label: "Claude", Contract: runtime.ClaudeCode2_1_210Lifecycle, Events: claudeEventMappings }
func Bind(modelKind model.ContractEventKind, bindings []model.NativeBinding) (waist.L1, []waist.Identity, error) {
    return frontend.Bind(host, modelKind, bindings)
}
```

Behavior policy (ratified strictest-common — the ONLY permitted behavior change in this stage):

- Hoisted to all hosts: Claude's duplicate-name guard (F4) and Claude's separated undeclared-field vs kind-mismatch errors with binding index. One error template parameterized by `Label`; `Where` becomes the truthful generic location ("Binding a {Label} lifecycle event (internal/lifecycle/frontend/frontend.go in frontend.Bind)").
- Exact delta for OpenCode/Codex (enumerated; D6 proof P5 tests it):
  1. Duplicate identity name → NOW rejected at the frontend with the hoisted guard's text. TODAY rejected at L2 (`waist/event.go:332-343`). Admission unchanged; error site/text change only (F9).
  2. Undeclared-field and kind-mismatch → same rejections as today, but as two separated errors with index instead of one folded text (F5/F6).
- Exact delta for Claude: error-text template unification only (Where line + shared template); check order and admission identical.
- All error-text deltas are collected and reviewed ONCE (URD R2.2); the frontend/handler tests pinning old strings are updated in the same slice.
- R2.7 fence: `Events` maps, typed identity field derivation (`mapping.Identities()` content), and every receipt/provenance/identity surface remain host-pinned data. The generic engine moves CONTROL FLOW only. Any genericization of identity/provenance/receipt semantics is a review BLOCKER by definition (URD Stage-2 validation cases).

## D5. Inventory: one typed table, closed axes (R2.5)

New leaf package `internal/inventory` (hand-written types file imports `ir` only):

```go
// internal/inventory/inventory.go
package inventory

// Kind is the closed capability axis. Existing IDs keep their spelling;
// disambiguation is structural (typed axes), never string-prefixed (R2.5).
type Kind uint8

const (
    KindCommand        Kind = iota + 1 // e.g. "cmd-worker" (CommandSpecs vocabulary)
    KindLifecycleEvent                 // e.g. "PreToolUse", "tool.execute.before" (registration vocabulary)
    KindNativeFunction                 // e.g. "request-input" (contract-derived native calls)
)

// Key is the unique table coordinate.
type Key struct {
    Harness ir.HarnessID
    Kind    Kind
    ID      string // existing spelling, unmodified
}

// Row is one capability fact. Attribute payloads deliberately do NOT live here
// in this stage: consumers keep their authored attribute maps (skill dirs,
// permissions, proofs) keyed by table IDs and validated exhaustive against the
// table (D6). YAGNI: rows gain fields only when a consumer cutover needs them.
type Row struct{ Key Key }

// Table returns the merged, sorted, uniqueness-validated inventory. Duplicate
// keys fail with an actionable error naming both contributing sources.
func Table() ([]Row, error)

// RowsFor answers "what can harness X do" as one query.
func RowsFor(harness ir.HarnessID) ([]Row, error)
```

Row population — every row is DERIVED from its existing pinned source; the table is a projection/meeting point, never a new hand-authored authority (URE verbatim: the table "must not become a place to bypass contract-derived native truth with a literal"):

| Kind | Derived from (unchanged truth) | Emitted as |
|---|---|---|
| lifecycle-event | `hostcontract` pinned contracts (F14) | `internal/inventory/lifecycle_events.gen.go`, emitted by hostcontractgen in the SAME walk that renders registration (D6) |
| command | `CommandSpecs` (F13), fanned out per registered harness | `internal/inventory/commands.gen.go`, emitted by the codegen generation root |
| native-function | pinned `runtime` operation contracts (F15's sources) | `internal/inventory/native_functions.gen.go`, emitted by the codegen generation root |

## D6. Staged cutover: authoring side first (R2.6)

Cutover order is the URD's user decision, applied precisely:

1. **Generation (this stage, by construction):** hostcontractgen builds its rows in memory from the pinned contracts and renders BOTH `inventory/lifecycle_events.gen.go` AND the registration manifests from that single walk (main.go:19-30 today) — the table and registration cannot drift from each other or from the contracts. The codegen root emits command and native-function rows from their pinned sources the same way. `make generate` ×2 zero-diff covers all three new files.
2. **Validation (this stage, where authored maps remain):** authored attribute maps keep their content but lose enumeration authority — tests assert exhaustive agreement with the table, failing actionably on any missing/extra entry:
   - `registration.X().Entries()` == table rows (harness X, lifecycle-event) — belt-and-suspenders on top of by-construction emission;
   - `commandSkillDirs` key set == table command IDs (F13, via skill_registry_test.go);
   - `codexNativeFunctions()` and `deriveOpenCodeNativeToolNames()` == table native-function rows per harness — the emit-time derivations REMAIN the runtime truth (R2.6) and the committed rows are the independently-generated projection they are checked against. A table entry contradicting the contract-derived list fails build/CI (URD Stage-2 "must fail" case);
   - activation catalogs' exhaustiveness (one decision per generated event, already enforced by the emitters) now transitively validates against the table through registration.
3. **NOT cut over (explicit, deferred to a later stage):** frontends, receipts, activation gates, and capability checks keep reading generated artifacts and per-host data exactly as today. No runtime code imports `internal/inventory` in this stage. Frontend `Events` maps are NOT validated against the table: OpenCode/Codex deliberately map only their 2 proven events (F5/F6) while the table lists the full generated vocabulary — forcing equality would be wrong.

## D7. Stage-1 activation-report surfaces: leave as-is

The shared report types (F17) already carry the ratified YAGNI decision ("plain data, no shared builder"). Report derivation iterates each harness's registration manifest + activation catalog — both of which D6 validates against the table — so the reports are transitively table-consistent without touching `activation_report.go`, `emitClaudeHooks`, or `renderCodexActivationReport`. Folding report emission into the inventory would add a builder abstraction Stage 1 explicitly rejected, for zero consumer benefit. Decision: no change.

## D8. Stage boundary and the exact seams M5/M4 need

This stage pre-builds NOTHING for M5/M4 beyond what R2.x already mandates. The resume doc's dependency analysis (M5 ↔ architecture section) names the seams, and each is satisfied by a decision above without speculative extension points:

- M5 R7 codebook vocabulary seed = the inventory table (D5) — the resume doc: "the inventory table is the codebook's vocabulary seed".
- M5 lineage requires host-pinned provenance/identity intact — D2's R2.7 fence keeps it (resume doc: "genericizing identity/provenance would degrade M5 lineage").
- M5 write gate wants "add a per-host blocking terminal = add data" — D1's registry row is that shape.
- M4 raw ingestion = "an extra parsing layer into each frontend adapter; after which should all flow into the same pipeline" (user verbatim, URD R4.2) — the registry row's `parse`/`bind` members are exactly that seam: a future raw decoder is an alternative parse producing the same delivery/binding material into the SAME `bind` and verifier. No additional hook, interface, or option is added now.

Stages 3 and 4 receive their own proposals after this stage lands (URD program shape).

# Tradeoffs

| Choice | Selected | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| Registry as compile-time static literal map in handlers | Yes | Map-parity with codegen `harnessRegistry` (F11); one caller unchanged; closed enum key; actionable default preserved |
| Runtime/registration-style registry (init() hooks, reflection, string reverse lookup) | No | This was the substance of the prior ratified rejection and stays rejected (see reconciliation below); repo standard forbids init-registration/reflection (AGENTS.md) |
| Keep the static switch (status quo) | No | URD R2.1 is a ratified user decision; two switch sites + N-harness growth + M5 "add data" ergonomics changed the calculus since the prior plan (reconciliation below) |
| Generic Bind engine + per-host data (strictest-common) | Yes | User-selected at URE over "preserve per-host behavior exactly" (flags outlive the duplication) and "push all checks into waist" (loses early per-host attribution; widens the waist against authority §2) |
| findDeclaredField home = internal/runtime | Yes | Signature is fully runtime-typed; leaf package reachable from waist AND frontend root without cycles; alternative (method on LifecycleEventMapping) rejected as a larger API change for the same effect |
| Encode fold-in via handler-owned encode + new HookLifecycleNative | Yes | Removes the second switch; makes commit-before-stdout structural; CLI touch is 1 file; per-host golden logic and tests stay in nativeresponse |
| Neutral shared registry package consulted by both handlers and nativeresponse | No | New package + import churn for the same outcome; handlers is the sole dispatch consumer today |
| Inventory rows carry attribute payloads (dirs, permissions, proofs) | No | YAGNI this stage: enumeration authority + exhaustiveness validation kills the drift problem; attributes migrate only when a real consumer cutover needs them |
| Inventory rows hand-authored | No | Would create a second authority able to bypass contract-derived truth — the exact failure the URE verbatim forbids; all rows are generated/derived from pinned sources |
| Fold activation-report emission into inventory | No | D7: Stage-1 ratified "no shared builder"; reports are transitively table-consistent already |
| codegen→artifactgen rename | No | Explicitly rejected at URE; recorded non-goal |

## Reconciliation: why a registry now, when the prior ratified plan rejected one

The prior ratified plan (aura-plugins-e3r38) recorded: "Static provider dispatch — Four observed events do not justify a runtime registry or deferred generic reverse lookup", and its handoff added: "Do not add reflection, init registration, arbitrary provider maps, or deferred generic native-name lookup". Two things changed, and one thing never applied:

1. What was rejected was a RUNTIME registry — open registration, reflection, string reverse lookup (#62). D1 builds none of that: a closed compile-time literal over `ir.HarnessID`, the exact construction codegen's `harnessRegistry` has used all along (F11). The objectionable properties are absent by construction, and #62 stays deferred.
2. The calculus moved: at M2 planning there was one switch, two harnesses, four observed events. At 4679f0a there are two switch sites (F1, F2) × three landed harnesses, a five-harness end-vision, and M5 explicitly wanting per-host additions to be "add data" (resume doc). The URD ratified R2.1 on that basis; this proposal implements the ratified decision in the form that honors the original objection.

# BDD acceptance criteria

- **Given** pasture at the integrated Stage-2 candidate, **when** any of the three harnesses delivers an accepted lifecycle event through the production CLI, **then** dispatch resolves through the static registry and produces the identical durable receipt, response validity, and native stdout bytes as at 4679f0a, **and should not** change any golden byte, admission decision, or receipt/provenance field.
- **Given** an unknown harness value, **when** dispatch resolves, **then** the actionable unsupported-harness error matches today's text, **and should not** panic or fall through to any host row.
- **Given** an OpenCode or Codex payload whose bindings repeat a native identity name, **when** the frontend binds it, **then** it is rejected AT THE FRONTEND by the hoisted duplicate-name guard with the host-labeled template error, **and should not** change the end-to-end admission outcome relative to 4679f0a (it was already rejected at L2) or alter Claude's admission behavior in any way.
- **Given** the collapsed generic Bind, **when** any host binds any event, **then** ordinal→enum maps, pinned contract constructors, and typed identity fields are consumed as host-pinned data, **and should not** genericize identity, provenance, or receipt semantics (BLOCKER by definition).
- **Given** `make generate` runs twice on the candidate, **then** the second run is zero-diff and the only committed generated-file delta of the stage is the three new inventory row files, **and should not** modify any previously-committed generated artifact by even one byte.
- **Given** the committed inventory table, **when** a row is compared with its pinned source, **then** lifecycle-event rows equal the hostcontract-derived registration, command rows equal CommandSpecs, and native-function rows equal the contract-derived lists, **and should not** allow a table entry to override contract-derived truth (build/CI rejects the contradiction).
- **Given** Stage-2 lands, **when** M5 planning begins, **then** it finds the inventory as codebook vocabulary seed, intact host-pinned provenance, and registry "add data" rows, **and should not** find any speculative M5/M4 machinery pre-built in this stage.

description:
Found reviewing the parity guard (aura-plugins-noqor).

The parity guard proves every declared IDENTITY appears in the pinned payload shape. It cannot prove the payload shape matches what the host actually sends, because neither table records that - the payload shape is the only claim about it, so it cannot be checked against itself.

Concrete exposure today (Claude):
  SessionStart  claudeNativeFields = {source, model, session_title}; identity = session_id
                -> all three payload fields unguarded
  PreToolUse    {tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id}; identity = tool_use_id
                -> two of three unguarded

Delete an unguarded field and every production invocation of that event is rejected by the frontend's per-event allowed-set check, while the diff reads as a strictness improvement. Nothing goes red.

Two tests currently appear to guard this and do not:
  - the parity guard: only covers the identity subset
  - TestParseToleratesEveryFieldTheHostLegitimatelySends: iterates the same table it is meant to check, so removing a field silently removes the assertion

Needs: a corpus of authentic captured payloads per harness per event, checked into testdata, with the frontend asserted to accept every one. That is the only artefact that can falsify the pinned shape. Capture cost is real - it needs a live host per pinned version - so scope it deliberately rather than assuming it is cheap.

Relevant to Codex and OpenCode equally as those frontends land.

1. DEAD CODE CONFIRMATION (lines 33-57): Confirmed true dead code. Grep across the entire file shows _discover_repo_root, REPO_ROOT, VERSION_FILES, and CHANGELOG_PATH appear ONLY within lines 33-56. The repo_root() function at line 83 is decorated with @functools.lru_cache and is a function definition only — it is NOT invoked at module level. importlib.util.spec_from_file_location will import the module with zero git subprocess calls. This is correct.

3. SUBDIRECTORY HANDLING: discover_version_files correctly handles the case where root has no pyproject.toml but a subdirectory does. The logic at lines 240-251: it first checks root/pyproject.toml (skipped if absent), then iterates _subdirs(root) — sorted child directories excluding hidden and known junk dirs — and appends any subdirectory pyproject.toml that passes _has_pyproject_version(). The regex _PYPROJECT_VERSION_RE requires a [project] section with a version = 'X.Y.Z' field, so bare pyproject.toml files without a [project] version are correctly excluded. If MULTIPLE subdirectories have valid pyproject.toml files, all are returned and version-consistency is enforced downstream — this is correct monorepo behavior.

4. EDGE CASES: No missing critical edge cases for MVP scope. One minor cosmetic note that does NOT affect correctness: the comment on line 32 ('Conventional commit prefix -> Keep a Changelog section') currently appears above the dead code block rather than above COMMIT_SECTIONS. After deleting lines 33-57, this comment will immediately precede COMMIT_SECTIONS at what becomes line 33 — it will then correctly describe that dict. No action needed.

One behavioral difference between the dead _discover_repo_root (check=False, custom error + sys.exit(2)) and the live repo_root() (check=True, raises CalledProcessError) is irrelevant post-removal since all git calls go through repo_root().

The proposal is technically sound, MVP-scoped, and faithfully serves the end-user requirement of aura-release working correctly in repos where pyproject.toml lives in a subdirectory.

## Finding

GenerateSubSkill (skills.go:569) has 61.9% statement coverage. The Init=true code path — which prepends markers to a sub-skill file that lacks them, then optionally writes the prepended content before rendering — is not tested. skills_test.go only tests Init=true for GenerateSkill (TestGenerateSkill_InitMode), not for GenerateSubSkill.

The Init path in GenerateSubSkill has a nested Write branch (if opts.Init && !HasMarkers then PrependMarkers; if opts.Write then os.WriteFile). The write-failure error in that branch is also untested.

## Why It Matters

--init flag is a production workflow: when adding a new sub-skill file, the operator calls GenerateSubSkill with Init=true. If the PrependMarkers + Write branch has a bug, operators will see silent failures or corrupt files.

## How To Fix

Add TestGenerateSubSkill_InitMode to skills_test.go mirroring TestGenerateSkill_InitMode:
1. Write a file without markers (just a heading).
2. Call GenerateSubSkill with Init=true, Write=true.
3. Assert no error and that the heading prefix is preserved.
4. Assert the hand-authored content below markers is preserved.
5. Read back the file from disk and verify contents match.

At `pastured` startup, for each well-known name in §7.7.2, run the `ensureWellKnownAgent` flow per §7.7.3: lookup-by-name in `pasture_well_known_agents` (O(1) via UNIQUE on `name`); if absent, call `provenance.Tracker.RegisterSoftwareAgent("pasture", <name>, <version>, <source>)`; insert into `pasture_well_known_agents` (`agent_id PK, name UNIQUE`) AND `pasture_agent_categories` (with the corresponding `automaton_role` and `pasture_role=None`). UAT-1 enum decision is **binding**: drop `AutomatonRoleDerivation`; register `consensus-reached` (`AutomatonRoleConsensusReached`) and `create-followup` (`AutomatonRoleCreateFollowup`) as concrete first-class agents.

# PROPOSAL-1: Unified Pasture workflow record + observability

## Authoritative artifact
The full proposal text is at `docs/proposals/PROPOSAL-1-pasture-workflow-record.md` (uncommitted draft).
This bd task description is a summary for review/UAT/ratification tracking.
**Reviewers MUST read the full artifact before voting.**

## What this proposal builds
Unified Pasture workflow record + observability surface combining the existing
PROV-O task tracker (Provenance) and the existing Temporal-integrated audit
subsystem behind a single `pasture.TaskTracker` façade in pasture, backed by
a single SQLite file. Provenance is NOT modified; integration happens at
pasture's wrapper layer. audit subsystem expands scope to also cover slices,
reviews, follow-ups, hooks, skills, git events both inside and around
workflows. Event-context attachment moves to a normalised `context_edges`
table in BCNF.

## Settled design choices (D1-D12)
- D1: Provenance NOT modified (URE C4 binding)
- D2: pasture.TaskTracker (URD R7) revived as integration mechanism
- D3: Single SQLite file at ~/.local/share/pasture/pasture.db (URE C5)
- D4: Two tables (activities + audit_events) joinable on agent_id
- D5: Epoch ID = Provenance REQUEST TaskID = Temporal workflow ID
- D6: Scope expands beyond epochs (URE Round 1 Q1)
- D7: Rule automata = SoftwareAgent + pasture-side typed categories
- D8: context_edges many-to-many in BCNF (URE verbatim)
- D9: CLI under pasture task (URE Round 2 Q3)
- D10: Auto-migrate via schema_meta version table
- D11: Low write frequency = no message-queue interposition
- D12: R11 (Pasture URD) Temporal SA dual-write preserved at workflow boundary

## URE constraints C1-C5 (binding)
- C1: researcher/exploratory notes OUT OF SCOPE
- C2: free-floating scope = hooks + skills + git operations
- C3: granularity = two tables, not collapsed
- C4: Provenance library NOT modified
- C5: single .db file (verbatim user direction)

## Schema changes (audit-side)
- audit_events: add agent_id; drop role, epoch_id (post-migration)
- New: context_edges(event_id, context_kind, context_id) PK composite, BCNF
- New: pasture_agent_categories(agent_id PK, automaton_role, pasture_role)
- New: audit_schema_meta(version PK, applied_at)

## Implementation slices (11 total)
S1 schema migration foundation, S2 new tables, S3 agent_id attribution,
S4 EpochContext migration, S5 pasture.TaskTracker interface+impl,
S6 new CLI subcommands, S7 automaton agent registration at pastured startup,
S8 workflow integration, S9 free-floating event recording,
S10 cmd/pasture wiring, S11 docs + ADR finalisation.

## BDD scenarios (10) covered in §11 of artifact
1 single .db epoch alignment | 2 R13 SA dual-write preserved
3 Provenance unmodified | 4 auto-migration on open
5 newer-schema rejection | 6 free-floating git event
7 multi-context attachment | 8 automaton attribution via JOIN
9 hjsdt CLI unchanged | 10 researcher-note scope creep rejected

## Out of scope
Binary umbrella unification; bd→pasture-task skill migration;
web UI / ACP orchestration / marketplace; Provenance extensions;
researcher notes; cross-machine deployment.

## Review axes (Phase 4)
- A Correctness: faithfulness to URD R1-R14 + URE C1-C5; migration
  completeness; R13 preservation invariants
- B Test quality: BDD coverage; migration tests; -race compat;
  failure-mode tests
- C Elegance: pasture.TaskTracker interface size; 11-slice granularity;
  BCNF defensibility; over/under-engineering

# Status and stop condition

This proposal is planning authority only. It does not authorize fixture import, production edits, generated-output changes, activation, or worker dispatch. M2 requires plan review and Plan UAT before an implementation plan. M3 implementation remains additionally blocked on accepted M2 implementation UAT.

# Requirements traceability

| URD requirement | Proposal decision |
|---|---|
| R1 minimal shared post-L2 middle-end | D1 pure constructor-owned `middleend.Plan`; no new semantic enum or store |
| R2 strict sequence | D8 separate M2 and M3 implementation/review/UAT gates; no M3 worker before accepted M2 |
| R3 OpenCode 1.18.10 | D3/D4 exact observed profile, two authentic candidates, full session-smoke and Proceed-gate paths |
| R4 Codex 0.146.0 | D3/D4 exact observed profile, dedicated #65, staged SessionStart and PreToolUse paths |
| R5 four raw fixtures | D4 exact extraction/provenance; no redaction; no broader capture import |
| R6 identity and durability | D1/D2 preserve provider contract/origin and existing receipt/Provenance operation ordering |
| R7 Proceed only | D1/D5 reuse `backend.DecisionProceed`; no deny or mutation API |
| R8 positive acceptance only | D6 direct positive evidence and production tests; existing negative corpus unchanged |
| R9 issue/file ownership | D7 exact #56/#65 source and generated-output ownership; #27/#24 coordination-only |
| R10 safety and delivery | D5/D6 generated transport is mechanical, every Go test uses `-race`, no Git hooks |

# Problem space

## Engineering axes

- Parallelism: M2 documentation can run beside M2 runtime foundation, but generated transport, handler wiring, and activation converge on shared files. M3 is intentionally sequential after accepted M2.
- Distribution: each harness invokes a local Pasture subprocess, potentially from separate host processes. One SQLite/Provenance operation durably groups occurrence, interpretation, and optional consultation evidence.
- Multiplicity: providers are many; semantic operation/effect planning is one. Provider ingress and response encoding remain separate N-side adapters around one middle-end.
- Frequency and cost: hooks may fire many times per session. The middle-end is pure and allocation-bounded; durable cost remains one existing receipt operation per invocation.
- Trust boundary: native payloads and foreign adapters are untrusted transport. Constructor-owned Go values become trusted only after provider ingress, frontend binding, and `waist.EventBinding.NewEvent`.

## Relationships

- A provider has one ingress parser, one frontend mapping, one activation table, and one mechanical response encoder.
- A verified `waist.L2` is the input to the shared middle-end; it is not a provider payload.
- A `middleend.Plan` has one interpreted effect, optionally one consultation effect, and optionally one constructor-built `backend.HostResponse`.
- An authentic fixture is evidence for one observed provider/runtime. OpenCode callback capture bytes are not a separate native wire protocol.

# Current-tree facts

At baseline `0414ad9`, `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle.go` directly composes `legalize.Event`, `receipt.NewInterpreted`, and `backend.BuildConsultation`. There is no `internal/lifecycle/lower.go`, generic `Lower`, `EquivalentTo`, provider-neutral response result, OpenCode ingress/frontend, or Codex ingress/frontend.

The reusable production contracts already exist in `waist`, `legalize`, `backend`, `receipt`, `projection`, and the public lifecycle reader. The current handler is Claude-only and returns only `error`; the CLI reports internal errors to stderr, exits successfully by accepted policy, and emits no stdout response.

The generated OpenCode and Codex lifecycle artifacts still read caller-selected `PASTURE_ADAPTER_EVENT`, `PASTURE_ADAPTER_OPERATION`, and `PASTURE_ADAPTER_INPUT` and call `pasture __adapter invoke`. That command remains valid for non-lifecycle semantic adapter use. Only the generated lifecycle route is replaced.

# Architecture decisions

## D1. Add one thin pure post-L2 plan

Create `internal/lifecycle/middleend/evaluate.go`. It composes the existing pure stages and owns effect ordering. It does not add a provider, context, tracker, clock, operation ID, persistence API, or new semantic/decision enum.

```go
package middleend

type Plan struct {
    // unexported constructor-owned interpreted record,
    // optional consultation record and optional host response
}

func Evaluate(event waist.L2) (Plan, error)
func (p Plan) Effects() []provenance.Effect
func (p Plan) Response() backend.HostResponse
func (p Plan) IsValid() bool
```

`Evaluate` calls, in order:

1. `legalize.Event(event)`;
2. `receipt.NewInterpreted(event, event.Origin().Contract())`;
3. for a gate only, `backend.BuildConsultation(interpreted, legalized)`.

Observation and existing explicit-human-response semantics produce only the interpreted effect and an invalid zero `HostResponse`; explicit human response must retain the existing valid `NoAuthority` check. Gate consultation produces interpreted then consultation effects and a valid `DecisionProceed` response. `Effects` returns a defensive slice in canonical order. No caller can construct or reorder a valid plan through exported fields.

This is the missing middle-end boundary without reviving stale `Lower`, `BackendView`, replay-key, or actor machinery.

## D2. Return the existing typed response and use static provider dispatch

Change the internal handler boundary to:

```go
func HookLifecycle(
    ctx context.Context,
    in HookLifecycleInput,
) (backend.HostResponse, error)
```

A successful observation returns the invalid zero response and nil error. A successful gate returns the constructor-built Proceed response after its receipt commits. The CLI writes the canonical `backend.HostResponse` JSON to stdout only when `IsValid()` is true. Existing accepted error handling remains stderr plus successful hook process exit; new negative behavior is not part of this MVP.

Keep one explicit `switch in.Harness` in the handler. Each case selects a generated registration/activation manifest, provider ingress parser, and provider frontend. Do not add a runtime provider registry, reflection, `init` registration, arbitrary map, or generic native-name reverse lookup. Provider frontends mirror the current Claude boundary:

```go
func Parse(
    raw []byte,
    event registration.Event,
    observedVersion string,
    envelope model.OccurrenceEnvelopeRef,
) Capture

func Bind(
    event model.ContractEventKind,
    bindings []model.NativeBinding,
) (waist.L1, []waist.Identity, error)
```

OpenCode and Codex each maintain one explicit registration-event to runtime-event mapping, as Claude does. This does not reopen deferred GitHub #62.

## D3. Replace stale exact profiles; do not build compatibility

Replace internal OpenCode 1.17.18 and Codex 0.144.1 profile constructors/IDs with exact `opencode@1.18.10` and `codex@0.146.0` contracts. Update `PinnedContracts`, lifecycle constructors, generated metadata, manifests, target descriptors, tests, and headers together.

Do not retain dual old/new profiles, fallback selection, skew negotiation, or a support matrix. There is no persisted OpenCode/Codex lifecycle receipt compatibility requirement on the landed Claude-only path. Source-reprofile the closed host catalogs needed by existing code generation, but activate and authentically validate only the two selected events per provider. A source-derived catalog entry is not authentic event evidence.

Extend the static host-contract generator from one hard-coded Claude contract to a compile-time list of Claude plus the two selected OpenCode and Codex ingress contracts. Generate provider manifests/payload field maps and collision-checked shared event/field symbols. Do not hand-edit generated registration files and do not require exhaustive authentic fixtures.

## D4. Preserve the four exact raw candidates with provider-correct replay

Import exactly the four user-cleared candidates and provenance sidecars under provider ingress packages:

```text
internal/lifecycle/ingress/opencode/testdata/fixtures/
  session_created_1_18_10.capture.json
  session_created_1_18_10.provenance.json
  tool_execute_before_1_18_10.capture.json
  tool_execute_before_1_18_10.provenance.json

internal/lifecycle/ingress/codex/testdata/fixtures/
  session_start_0_146_0.json
  session_start_0_146_0.provenance.json
  pre_tool_use_0_146_0.json
  pre_tool_use_0_146_0.provenance.json
```

The OpenCode files preserve each selected JSONL record including its line bytes. Tests extract the nested callback `value` as `json.RawMessage` without normalizing it, because the host supplies an in-process object and the production plugin serializes that callback value. Provenance records both the parent lifecycle JSONL digest and extracted record digest, identifies callback-object observation, and never claims a native wire byte stream.

The Codex files copy exact command-hook stdin bytes. Every sidecar records observed runtime, inspected source revision, UTC capture time, method, source selector, exact digest, `origin: authentic-capture`, `redaction: none`, and user-clearance reference. No transcript, PostToolUse, Stop, final message, database, cache, or auth file is imported.

## D5. Replace lifecycle caller-selected operations with mechanical transport

OpenCode generated lifecycle code uses only `PASTURE_BIN` as an executable override. It invokes:

```text
pasture hook lifecycle --harness opencode 
  --event <statically generated event> --host-version 1.18.10
```

For `session.created`, stdin is the serialized callback event object and failure is logged without terminating the observation stream. For `tool.execute.before`, stdin is the serialized `{input, output:{args}}` callback value. The plugin requires canonical `{"decision":"proceed"}` stdout, then returns with `output.args` unchanged. It neither chooses an operation nor extracts semantic identities.

Codex generated event runners invoke the same command with harness `codex`, exact version `0.146.0`, and their statically generated event. The Python adapter forwards exact stdin, requires the canonical Proceed response for `PreToolUse`, and mechanically emits `{"continue":true}`. `SessionStart` is observe-only and emits the native default continuation object. Denial and `updatedInput` are absent.

Remove `PASTURE_ADAPTER_EVENT`, `PASTURE_ADAPTER_OPERATION`, and `PASTURE_ADAPTER_INPUT` from OpenCode/Codex lifecycle artifacts. Do not remove `pasture __adapter invoke` or its non-lifecycle tests.

## D6. Use direct positive evidence; do not weaken the Claude corpus

The current `activation.LoadCorpus` mandates multiple negative categories. Reusing it would silently implement the user-deferred rejection matrix. Leave that Claude contract and all existing tests unchanged.

For each new provider, use focused positive fixture/provenance checks plus built production-path tests. Verify exact fixture digests, provider/version/source metadata, production ingress/frontend/L2, `middleend.Plan`, one ordered durable operation, bounded public read-back, and mechanical native Proceed output. No new malformed, mismatch, provenance-tamper, deny, mutation, PostToolUse, Stop, or exhaustive-catalog tests are acceptance gates.

Execute generated foreign code in the positive integration seam rather than testing only source strings:

- M2 loads the generated TypeScript plugin under Bun with the built Pasture binary and a real temporary SQLite database, invokes the two captured callback values, verifies unchanged tool args/Proceed behavior, then verifies public read-back.
- M3 executes the generated Codex runner/Python adapter with the built binary and exact raw stdin, verifies valid continuation JSON, then verifies public read-back.

Test-local helpers may load authentic fixtures and construct isolated process state; they must not replace or mock the production parser, frontend, middle-end, receipt service, generated adapter, or CLI.

## D7. Keep issue and file ownership explicit

M2 runtime issue #56 owns the shared middle-end, OpenCode runtime/profile/ingress/frontend/activation, lifecycle handler/CLI changes, exact OpenCode lifecycle codegen source/output, and cross-provider Proceed proof. OpenCode issue #27 is coordination-only for these paths.

M3 runtime issue #65 owns the sequential Codex profile/ingress/frontend/activation, Codex lifecycle codegen source/output, handler/CLI extension, and two-live-provider proof. Codex issue #24 is coordination-only for these paths.

Shared files are modified sequentially: #65 starts from accepted M2 and becomes their sole M3 owner. Before worker dispatch, add ownership comments to #27 and #24 and ensure no concurrent branch owns a listed file.

Documentation issue #53 owns only documentation files and cannot change runtime behavior.

## D8. Ratify together, implement and accept separately

This proposal defines both milestones so the shared interface is reviewed once. After ratification, the supervisor creates only the M2 implementation plan. M3 receives a fresh implementation plan from the accepted M2 commit only after M2 code review and implementation UAT pass. No M3 worker, fixture import, profile change, or generated output starts earlier.

Within each milestone, activation is the last unlanded integration step after authentic fixture and production proofs pass. Independent review and implementation UAT evaluate the exact candidate with enabled selected entries. User acceptance authorizes landing that already-reviewed candidate; no unreviewed activation flip occurs after UAT.

# Tradeoffs

| Choice | Selected | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| Thin `middleend.Plan` over existing stages | Yes | Makes one testable post-L2 owner without a second semantic model |
| New universal operation/response IR | No | No observed caller needs it; conflicts with minimal API requirement |
| Static harness switch and explicit mappings | Yes | Compile-time inventory, easy tests, no speculative registry |
| Generic native-name lookup | No | Deferred #62 and unnecessary for four generated events |
| Replace old exact profiles | Yes | Matches user-selected observed-only versions without #63 compatibility work |
| Four raw exact fixtures | Yes | User-cleared, replayable authentic evidence; no redaction transform |
| Existing full rejection corpus for new providers | No | Would absorb explicitly deferred negative proof work |
| Canonical typed stdout response | Yes | Makes Proceed observable while keeping host mapping mechanical |
| Exit-code-only Proceed | No | Current accepted lifecycle CLI exits successfully even on internal errors |
| Parallel OpenCode/Codex implementation | No | User requires accepted M2 before M3 begins |
| Separate M3 runtime issue | Yes | Prevents #24 artifact scope from swallowing the runtime vertical |

# BDD acceptance criteria

- **Given** a verified L2 observation, gate, or existing explicit-human-response event, **when** `middleend.Evaluate` runs, **then** it returns the existing canonical interpreted effect, optional gate consultation, and optional constructor-built Proceed response in canonical order, **and should not** access a provider, tracker, clock, operation ID, database, or host payload.
- **Given** the exact OpenCode session candidate, **when** the generated OpenCode plugin and built CLI process its callback value, **then** provider/version-correct durable session smoke evidence is readable, **and should not** claim session equivalence with Claude or Codex.
- **Given** the exact OpenCode tool candidate, **when** the generated named hook processes it, **then** the shared middle-end returns Proceed, one durable operation contains ordered evidence, stdout is canonical, and args remain unchanged, **and should not** select an operation in TypeScript or an environment variable.
- **Given** the OpenCode gate and landed Claude regression path, **when** the positive plans are compared, **then** their common gate semantic, blocking mode, and Proceed decision agree while origins and identity values remain provider-correct, **and should not** claim a new live Claude capture or whole-payload equality.
- **Given** accepted M2, **when** M3 planning and implementation begin, **then** Codex reuses the same middle-end API and accepted M2 commit, **and should not** overlap M2 workers or revise the middle-end without a new reviewed proposal.
- **Given** the exact Codex SessionStart candidate, **when** the generated runner and built CLI process exact stdin, **then** provider/version-correct durable session smoke evidence is readable, **and should not** claim equivalence with OpenCode aggregate creation.
- **Given** the exact Codex PreToolUse candidate, **when** the generated runner processes it, **then** the shared middle-end returns Proceed, one durable operation contains ordered evidence, and the native output is `{"continue":true}`, **and should not** deny, rewrite input, or select semantics in Python or shell.
- **Given** authentic OpenCode and Codex gate candidates, **when** their positive plans are compared, **then** common gate semantic, blocking mode, and Proceed decision agree while identity, ordering, authority, failure, and mutation facts remain distinct, **and should not** flatten equivalence into whole-behavior identity.
- **Given** all positive fixture and production proofs pass in an unlanded milestone candidate, **when** independent review and implementation UAT accept it, **then** the exact reviewed static activation and generated outputs may land, **and should not** enable unselected events or change code after UAT without revalidation.

# Explicit deferrals

The following remain outside both implementation plans: the proposed malformed/provider/event/version/provenance rejection test set; deny and input mutation; PostToolUse, Stop, and other event paths; exhaustive authentic catalogs; dual-version support or a published matrix; live Claude captures; generic native-name reverse lookup; raw-ingestion escape hatch; retention/GC; status guard; cause boundary; panic proof; outer-budget receipt retries; coverage mutation machinery; Strike/Grok Build contracts; and any capture artifact beyond the four cleared candidates.

## Finding
The test calls `newIntegrationCandidateManifest` with a two-member slice and then only reads the returned members. It never mutates the caller-owned input after construction, mutates the returned slice, decodes the persisted payload, or attempts a same-candidate replacement. The file-backed portion checks only that some manifest fact has a JournalID. A constructor that aliases the input, or a path that permits a second mutable manifest, could therefore pass.

## Exact fix
After construction, mutate the original member slice and assert the manifest remains the canonical two-member value; in the real-store proof decode/compare the persisted payload and add one compact ExactFact/replacement assertion showing the original manifest remains immutable for that candidate (replacement must use a new candidate identity).

## Components Reviewed

### Component 1: Registry schema + validation
**Definition shown:** PluginEntry(name, path: Path, remote), MarketplaceEntry(path: Path, plugins), PluginRegistry(marketplaces) frozen dataclasses.

**Question:** Which validation behavior when loading a malformed plugin entry?
Options: Warn+skip (current proposal) / Fail+exit 2
**User response:** "Will error if trying to add a malformed entry with informative error message, but if user edits later, will warn+skip."
→ Delta: `registry add` validates and errors; `load()` warns and skips. Proposal already matches.

**Question:** Any concerns about registry schema or JSON structure?
**User response:** "No concerns — proceed"

---

### Component 2: Registry CLI — `registry add`
**Definition shown:** `aura-release registry add <name> [--path <local>] [--remote <url>] --marketplace <mp>`

**Question:** Path storage — absolute or relative?
Options: Always absolute / Store as-given
**User response:** "Always absolute (resolve at add time)"

**Question:** Duplicate handling — error or update?
Options: Error if exists / Update silently
**User response:** "Update verbosely. State what existed before, and should require interaction to update. Have --yes flag to update non-interactively."
→ **UAT DELTA**: Show old entry + interactive confirm prompt + --yes flag to skip. This is NEW behaviour not in PROPOSAL-2.

---

### Component 3: Plugin auto-detection + --plugin flag
**Definition shown:** Auto-detect by CWD.resolve() == PluginEntry.path.resolve(); explicit --plugin <name> override. Double-bump guard.

**Question:** When no registry match, what should happen?
Options: Proceed silently (proposal) / Warn and proceed / Error if --plugin given only
**User response:** "Error and stop verbosely in all cases if both auto-detect fails and registry file exists."
→ **UAT DELTA**: If registry EXISTS but no CWD match → error verbosely. Proposal said proceed silently. This is stricter.

**Question:** Should --check show registry info?
Options: Yes — show registry plugin + marketplace / No — unchanged
**User response:** "Yes — show registry info in --check output"
→ **UAT DELTA**: Add registry info to --check output. Not in PROPOSAL-2.

---

### Component 4: Test quality (aura-plugins-klac)
**Definition shown:** module-scoped aura_release_mod fixture + autouse _clear_caches (cache_clear only, not sys.modules).

**Question:** Migrate A-D to fixture or leave as-is?
Options: Migrate all A-E (current proposal) / Leave A-D unchanged
**User response:** "Migrate all (A-E) to aura_release_mod fixture (current proposal)"

**Question:** Any concerns about test quality changes?
**User response:** "No concerns — proceed"

---

### Catch-all
**Question:** Any gap or drift from original URE?
**User response:** "Nothing else — ACCEPT the plan"

## Final Decision
**ACCEPT** — with 4 deltas noted above that must be reflected in implementation:
1. `registry add` duplicate: interactive confirm + --yes flag
2. Path always stored absolute at add time
3. Registry exists + no CWD match → error verbosely (not silent)
4. --check output includes registry info when found

## Problem Space

**Axes:** code generation (schema → code, code → schema), drift elimination (38 SKILL.md files × 1 schema.xml), runtime context injection (role-level + phase-level), source-of-truth inversion (schema.xml → Python types.py)

**Has-a / Is-a relationships:**
- SchemaSpec HAS-A collection of PhaseSpec, RoleSpec, CommandSpec, ConstraintSpec, HandoffSpec, LabelSpec, ReviewAxisSpec
- RoleSpec HAS-MANY owned phases, invariants, label-awareness declarations
- CommandSpec HAS-A role-ref, phase-refs, creates-labels
- PhaseSpec HAS-MANY SubstepSpec (with startup sequences, TDD layers)
- Generator IS-A function (SchemaSpec → output format)
- ContextInjector IS-A function (RoleId|PhaseId → relevant constraints/phases/commands)

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Options | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|---------|--------|-----------|
| Source of truth | schema.xml / Python types.py / bidirectional | Python types.py | User requirement. Python is more expressive, testable, and directly usable at runtime. XML is for portability. |
| Bootstrap strategy | Manual expansion / auto-parse schema.xml | Auto-parse + human review | 1,314-line schema.xml with 12 entity types — too much to manually transcribe. Parse once, verify, then Python is SoT. |
| Template engine | Jinja2 / string.Template / f-strings | Jinja2 | Industry standard for prompt generation. StrictUndefined catches missing vars. Supports conditionals, loops, inheritance. Minimal dependency. |
| XML generation | lxml / xml.etree / template-based | xml.etree.ElementTree | Already in stdlib, already used in validate_schema.py. No new dependency. |
| SKILL.md split strategy | Full generation / marker-based split / includes | Marker-based split | User chose split: generated header + manual body. Markers are simple, git-friendly, no preprocessor needed. |
| Procedure storage | schema.xml / Python / separate YAML | Python dataclasses | User chose Python. Procedures generate into both schema.xml AND SKILL.md. Python is more readable for procedural text. |
| Runtime injection integration | State machine / standalone module | Standalone module + state machine hook | Keep injection logic decoupled from state machine. Hook into advance() for phase-level. Standalone for role-level. |

## MVP Milestone

### Architecture Overview

```
== BOOTSTRAP (one-time) ==
schema.xml → [schema_parser.py] → SchemaSpec → verify → expanded types.py

== STEADY STATE (ongoing) ==
types.py (SOURCE OF TRUTH)
    ├─→ [gen_schema.py] → schema.xml (portable export)
    ├─→ [gen_skills.py] → SKILL.md (generated headers with markers)
    └─→ [context_injection.py] → runtime role/phase context
```

### Module 1: `scripts/aura_protocol/schema_parser.py` — Bootstrap Schema Parser

Parses schema.xml into a comprehensive SchemaSpec. Used ONCE for bootstrap, then kept for round-trip verification.

```python
@dataclass
class SchemaSpec:
    """Complete protocol specification extracted from schema.xml."""
    phases: dict[str, PhaseSpec]        # PhaseId → PhaseSpec (expanded with substeps)
    roles: dict[str, RoleSpec]          # RoleId → RoleSpec (with invariants, standing teams)
    commands: dict[str, CommandSpec]     # command-id → CommandSpec
    constraints: dict[str, ConstraintSpec]  # constraint-id → ConstraintSpec
    handoffs: dict[str, HandoffSpec]    # handoff-id → HandoffSpec
    labels: dict[str, LabelSpec]        # label-id → LabelSpec
    review_axes: dict[str, ReviewAxisSpec]  # axis-id → ReviewAxisSpec
    title_conventions: list[TitleConvention]
    dependency_model: DependencyModel

def parse_schema(path: Path) -> SchemaSpec:
    """Parse schema.xml into a complete SchemaSpec.
    
    This is the bootstrap entry point. After initial extraction,
    types.py becomes the source of truth and this parser is used
    only for round-trip verification.
    """
```

### Module 2: Expanded `scripts/aura_protocol/types.py` — Protocol Types (SoT)

Add new spec dataclasses and canonical dicts:

```python

class SubstepSpec:
```

### Module 3: `scripts/aura_protocol/gen_schema.py` — Python → schema.xml Generator

```python
def generate_schema(output_path: Path) -> None:
    """Generate schema.xml from Python types.py canonical definitions.
    
    Output must pass validate_schema.py validation.
    Uses xml.etree.ElementTree (stdlib).
    """

def verify_round_trip(schema_path: Path) -> list[str]:
```

### Module 5: `scripts/aura_protocol/context_injection.py` — Runtime Context Injection

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RoleContext:
    """All protocol context relevant to a specific role."""
    role: RoleSpec
```

## Summary

The proposal is structurally sound and demonstrates proportionate decomposition. 4 slices map to 4 orthogonal modules. The categorized aggregation (4 groups by parameter signature) is a principled and minimal solution to the signature diversity problem — superior to a bloated mega-context object or forcing unrelated constraints into a single signature. The optional timestamp pattern, single audit trail for failed transitions, and conftest.py fixture approach all represent correct minimal choices.

## VOTE: ACCEPT

No BLOCKER issues. Two non-blocking observations recorded for implementors.

## Observations (Non-Blocking)

### OBS-1: check_all name is now semantically misleading
The proposal renames check_state_constraints → check_all, but check_all only covers Group 1 (7 of 22 constraints). Original PROPOSAL-1 described check_all as "Run all constraint checks against current state." The rename is justified (the method does run ALL state-checkable checks), but the name will cause confusion for callers who expect it to cover all 22 C-* constraints.

Suggestion: The module docstring MUST clearly state that check_all(state) means "all checks that take only EpochState" — not all 22. The validation checklist item "check_all(state) aggregates 7+ state-checkable constraints" captures this but the API name alone does not. Implementors should add a docstring note like: "Runs all state-only constraint checks (Group 1, 7 checks). For transition checks call check_transition_constraints(); for naming/structural checks call individual methods."

### OBS-2: severity_groups uses str keys instead of SeverityLevel enum
SLICE-1 adds EpochState.severity_groups: dict[str, set[str]]. The proposal rationale says "level→finding_ids" but uses bare str for the key instead of SeverityLevel enum. This is inconsistent with the strongly-typed enum invariant that is itself one of the core goals of FR3 (Type Safety Hardening). The rest of the design uses SeverityLevel for all severity-related fields.

Suggestion: Change to dict[SeverityLevel, set[str]] = field(default_factory=dict). This is a one-line change that maintains the typed invariant and enables check_severity_tree() to use SeverityLevel.BLOCKER/IMPORTANT/MINOR directly as keys rather than string literals.

### OBS-3: Group 4 constraint count is stale in proposal description
The proposal documents "Group 4: Structural (specific IDs/params) — 8" but enumerates 11+ items in the text. This is a documentation inconsistency only, not a code concern. Implementors should verify the actual count when implementing check_structural_constraints().

| Complexity proportionality | PASS — 4 slices for 4 orthogonal problem axes |
| API cleanliness | PASS with OBS-1 (docstring needed for check_all) |

| Minimal design | PASS — no gold-plating; every change addresses a named finding |

VOTE: REVISE - Two correctness issues found. One is a field name bug; the other is a type signature mismatch with the AuditTrail Protocol.

## Review Axis: Correctness

Reviewer A evaluated PROPOSAL-4 against the existing codebase (types.py, workflow.py, interfaces.py, state_machine.py, audit_activities.py, session_registry.py, flake.nix) for type alignment, data flow consistency, and requirement coverage.

## Findings

### ISSUE 1 (BLOCKER): `state.votes` should be `state.review_votes` in full_state query

In Section 5, the `full_state` query implementation references `state.votes`:

```python
votes=dict(state.votes),
```

But `EpochState` (state_machine.py line 48) defines the field as `review_votes`:

```python
review_votes: dict[ReviewAxis, VoteType] = field(default_factory=dict)
```

`state.votes` would raise `AttributeError` at runtime. The correct line is:

```python
votes=dict(state.review_votes),
```

**Fix:** Change `state.votes` to `state.review_votes` in the `full_state` query code sample.

### ISSUE 2 (IMPORTANT, not blocking): `SqliteAuditTrail.query_events` signature mismatch with AuditTrail Protocol

In Section 10, the proposed `SqliteAuditTrail.query_events` signature is:

```python
async def query_events(self, *, epoch_id: str = "",
                       phase: str = "", role: str = "") -> list[AuditEvent]:
```

But the `AuditTrail` Protocol in interfaces.py (line 140-146) defines:

```python
async def query_events(
    self,
    *,
    epoch_id: str | None = None,
    phase: PhaseId | None = None,
    role: RoleId | None = None,
) -> list[AuditEvent]:
```

Three mismatches:
1. `epoch_id`: `str=""` vs `str | None = None` — empty string vs None sentinel
2. `phase`: `str=""` vs `PhaseId | None = None` — loses typed PhaseId enum
3. `role`: `str=""` vs `RoleId | None = None` — loses typed RoleId enum

While Python runtime structural subtyping (isinstance) only checks method names, a static type checker would flag these as incompatible. More importantly, using `str` instead of `PhaseId | None` is inconsistent with the project's design principle of preferring strongly-typed enums over stringly-typed APIs.

**Fix:** Align `SqliteAuditTrail.query_events` signature with the AuditTrail Protocol:
```python
async def query_events(self, *, epoch_id: str | None = None,
                       phase: PhaseId | None = None,
                       role: RoleId | None = None) -> list[AuditEvent]:
```

## Items Verified Correct

1. **PROPOSAL-1 fixes carried forward:**
   - SliceResult.output field: correctly added as `output: str = ""` (backwards-compatible default)
   - available_transitions: correctly accessed via `self._sm.available_transitions` (property on EpochStateMachine, not EpochState)
   - VoteType case: correctly handled via `.upper()` at CLI boundary (VoteType is UPPER case StrEnum)

2. **Types alignment:** PhaseId, ReviewAxis, VoteType, RoleId, Transition, TransitionRecord, EpochInput all correctly referenced from their existing definitions in types.py / state_machine.py

3. **Data flows:** CLI → Temporal Client → Workflow signal/query → Activity chain is correct for all subcommands (query state, signal vote, phase advance, epoch start, session register)

4. **UAT-1 (SessionRegisterSignal):** Correctly specified as a new signal + query on EpochWorkflow, separate from the existing SessionRegistry (which is OS-level aura-swarm session tracking, not Temporal workflow session tracking)

5. **UAT-2 (auto-register on /epoch):** Correctly specified as a skill-level concern, not a workflow concern. The shell sequence (epoch start → session register → export AURA_EPOCH_ID) is logically sound

6. **UAT-3 (tmux detection):** shutil.which("tmux") in the activity is correct — activity code is allowed to be non-deterministic. Returning SliceResult(success=False) with an actionable error message is the right pattern

7. **QueryStateResult DTO:** Correctly avoids non-serializable EpochState fields (completed_phases uses set, severity_groups uses dict[SeverityLevel, set[str]]). Uses only JSON-safe types

8. **Config resolution:** 4-level priority (CLI > env > YAML > defaults) is consistent between aurad and aura-msg. The shared ConnectionConfig dataclass is a clean design

9. **Slice decomposition:** All 15 requirements + 3 UAT amendments are covered by the 7 slices with no gaps. Dependencies are logically sound

10. **Backwards compatibility:** Existing current_state and available_transitions queries retained alongside new full_state query

11. **Nix packaging:** aura-msg needs temporalio + pyyaml; aurad needs pyyaml + aiosqlite. Both need PYTHONPATH. Correct per flake.nix patterns

## End-User Alignment

- End-users (Claude agents + human operators) get a clean, consistent CLI interface
- Error messages are actionable (listing valid phases, etc.)
- Config resolution priority is intuitive (explicit > implicit)
- Session registration provides visibility into which sessions are participating in an epoch
- Validation checklist covers all user-facing behaviors

## Verdict

REVISE due to Issue 1 (field name bug that would cause AttributeError at runtime). Issue 2 is IMPORTANT but not blocking — it should be fixed for type safety consistency but would not crash at runtime.

# Axis A — Correctness

VOTE: REVISE

## Audit result

The 30-row Claude audit is enumerated exactly once: rows 1–30 match the pinned event catalog with no duplicate or omitted native event. The three columns distinguish AE/AT/H/A evidence, PT/CG/CT normative-control interaction, and IX/AD context/host interaction. The supersession finding is valid: the prior proposal’s payload-digest replay suppression, single semantic, retained target behavior, and same-package BackendView are incompatible with the accepted append-every-delivery requirement and the three-plane/versioned-codebook requirements.

## BLOCKER — authoritative capability and correlation boundary is not implementable

The normative-authority section and rows 1, 3, 18, 20, 24, and 30 require an active exact session binding, actor/role/assignment checks, a Pasture-issued single-use capability, and atomic consumption. However, the public interfaces define no capability issuance/registration operation, no persisted binding from native session/request/task/worktree/agent IDs to an Epoch/actor/assignment, and no exact input or consumption invariant for `CommitTransitionInput`. In particular, `ElicitationResult` carries only Claude `session_id` and `request_id`; the design never defines how Pasture issues the request, selects the registered human, or proves that this result is the answer to that exact Pasture request. A host string can therefore either be treated as authority (breaking deterministic provenance) or be rejected forever (making the stated CT paths non-functional).

**Exact fix:** define typed capability/binding contracts and their immutable persistence: a Pasture-issued request/delegation/lease capability scoped to runtime contract, native session/request/tool/agent/task/worktree, epoch, role, actor, and operation; an explicit issuance/bind operation before the host callback; and a transaction-local, single-use/expiry/revocation check consumed together with the control commit. Define `CommitTransitionInput` and the Elicitation → ElicitationResult correlation so unbound host claims append evidence/candidates only and can never commit control.

## BLOCKER — captured data cannot support the promised interpretations as typed

`NativeOccurrence` contains only native event, transport identities (described as session/turn/request/tool/agent/message), parse status, and an opaque `EvidencePayloadRef`; `Interpreter.Interpret` accepts only an `OccurrenceID`. Yet the audit claims deterministic H/A/PT/IX facts from prompts, responses, tool I/O, stop-loop flags, paths, tasks, worktrees, environments, and context files, while the operation legend and rows use AT for task/worktree/environment/path bindings that the declared binding set does not contain. The privacy section also permits payload content to be omitted/redacted/encrypted. As written, the interpreter has no guaranteed typed, immutable, privacy-safe representation from which those facts and correlations can be derived; choosing metadata-only retention can silently erase the inputs needed to distinguish them.

**Exact fix:** specify an immutable captured-payload contract (typed per-event fields or a canonical redacted field envelope plus a versioned payload reference) that retains every field required by the codebook, and make it available to interpretation by ID; expand/define `NativeBindingKind` for task/worktree/environment/context/artifact or move those into explicit typed facts. State the behavior when required data is unavailable: append the occurrence and an unresolved/candidate fact, never assert H/A/control/context delivery.

## IMPORTANT — disclosure history and stop-loop capture need explicit invariants

`ContextDisclosure` has a mutable-looking `State` (planned/delivered/acknowledged/revoked) but the proposal only forbids in-place reinterpretation, not in-place disclosure-state mutation; append-only provenance requires each delivery/ack/revocation fact to be immutable and queryable. Also, rows 6 and 21 promise AE for every delivery while saying consultation occurs only when `stop_hook_active` is inactive; specify that active-loop events are still appended with a typed suppressed-consultation fact and test that branch.

**Exact fix:** model disclosure state changes as immutable facts/projections with timestamps and interpretation refs, and make the active stop-loop path capture-first, then record a typed non-consultation result.

## Review scope

Design-only review. No production files were edited and no implementation tests were run.
