acceptance_criteria:
validates those predicates and stores the same digest. All four identity fields
must match for replay; exact ended authority may replay, while
same-actor predecessor/successor assignments, slots/tasks, and bootstrap paths
conflict. The trusted typed adapter owns command-
identity construction—Provenance does not decode caller semantics.

Lookup performs no mutation and returns a closed semantic result with nil error:
`CommittedAbsent` means the operation has never committed;
`CommittedExact` returns the stored identity, result map, and EventIDs even when
the initiating assignment has since ended; and `CommittedConflict` returns both
expected and stored actor/authority/command identity. Only store or transport
failure uses the Go error channel.
The read-only lookup does not accept a proposed Mutation and therefore does not
claim mutation equality. A subsequent Apply performs the four-field check; #6
also compares the proposed digest after a checkpoint return. Lookup never
executes an absent command or revalidates current authority. #5 also
owns the production migration that installs the #4
schema, writes baselines, and activates atomic journaling. #4 and #5 ship in one
Provenance release tag after both merge; there is no released state in which a
database has a writable journal but non-journalled mutators.

Provenance #6 owns the DBOS adapter without changing #5 command semantics.
`OpenBorrowedSQLite` borrows the exact `*sql.DB` configured on DBOS, applies
compatible Provenance migrations through it, and never closes it. Every read or
write after DBOS has terminally closed the handle returns
`StoreUnavailableError` with nonempty operation/store/stage/impact/fix fields and
the wrapped driver cause.

`NewDBOSAdapter` receives the configured not-yet-launched root DBOS context and
registers one stable `provenance.apply/v1` workflow before launch/recovery. It derives the actual
application version from `root.GetApplicationVersion()` and rejects a nonempty
mismatched `ExpectedApplicationVersion`. Public Apply accepts ordinary
`context.Context`, so a CLI/root call is valid; durable execution always uses the
registered root workflow. It never invokes RunAsStep outside a workflow or
inlines a nested step.

Apply purely canonicalizes the closed mutation and context into
`DBOSApplyInputV1`, computes one versioned fingerprint over adapter/input schema,
pinned DBOS contract, actual application version, ActorID, exact authority,
semantic OperationID, CommandDigest, and MutationDigest, then starts or retrieves
workflow `provenance.apply/v1/<sha256-fingerprint>` with that application version.
The registered workflow executes one durable step named
`provenance.apply-step/v1/<sha256-fingerprint>`. The name is a positional
determinism guard inside the deterministic workflow, not a second operation or
checkpoint identity. Callers cannot pass `dbos.WorkflowOption`,
`dbos.StepOption`, or override either identity.

The normative workflow exposes two unexported same-package-test hooks at the
exact crash boundaries:

```go
result, err := a.tracker.Apply(stepCtx, mc, mutation)
if err != nil {
    return encodeDBOSApplyFailure(mc.OperationID, mutation, err)
}
a.testHooks.afterDomainCommit()
return encodeDBOSApplySuccess(mc.OperationID, mutation, result)
```

```go
outcome, err := dbos.RunAsStep(/* closed callback above */)
if err != nil { return DBOSStepOutcomeV1{}, err }
a.testHooks.afterStepCheckpoint()
return outcome, nil
```

The step decodes/validates the canonical input, invokes
`tracker.Apply(stepCtx, mc, mutation)`, and checkpoints `DBOSStepOutcomeV1` with
a nil Go error for every domain success or domain failure. Its closed success
codec covers every #5 mutation-result binding through separate typed,
slot-sorted slices and stable emitted-event order; its
`CanonicalApplyFailureV1` exhaustively covers every public #5 error plus one
unexpected-failure variant. Pinned DBOS v0.16 string error serialization is
therefore never used to promise typed domain-error replay. Only DBOS
infrastructure failure uses the workflow/step Go error channel. After the
workflow outcome returns—even when DBOS skipped the already-checkpointed
workflow/step body—the adapter decodes the outcome and, for success, calls
read-only `LookupCommitted` and exhaustively switches over Absent, Exact, and
Conflict before comparing OperationID, MutationDigest, and canonical result.
Missing, conflicting, unknown-variant, or mismatched store state returns
`CheckpointDivergenceError` and writes nothing.

Public `Apply` checks caller cancellation before starting durable work and starts
the workflow only on the uncancelled adapter root. Waiting uses a DBOS-root child
whose cancellation is bridged from the caller without an orphaned `GetResult`
goroutine:

```go
func awaitWorkflowResult[T any](
    caller context.Context,
    root dbos.DBOSContext,
    workflowID string,
    operation OperationID,
) (T, error) {
    waitBase, cancelWait := context.WithCancelCause(root)
    stop := context.AfterFunc(caller, func() {
        cancelWait(context.Cause(caller))
    })
    defer func() { stop(); cancelWait(nil) }()

    waitCtx := dbos.From(root, waitBase)
    handle, err := dbos.RetrieveWorkflow[T](waitCtx, workflowID)
    if err != nil { return *new(T), err }
    result, err := handle.GetResult()
    if err != nil && caller.Err() != nil {
        return *new(T), &ApplyWaitCanceledError{
            Operation: operation,
            Stage: "await-workflow",
            Impact: "durable work continues",
            Fix: "retry the same operation to retrieve its outcome",
            Cause: context.Cause(caller),
        }
    }
    return result, err
}
```

Cancellation returns `ApplyWaitCanceledError` promptly but never calls
`CancelWorkflow`, cancels, or alters durable work; an exact later retry finds and
validates its committed outcome.

A crash after Provenance commit but before step checkpoint re-enters #5 with the
same four-field identity and produces zero duplicate writes. A crash after step
checkpoint but before workflow completion recovers the same closed step result.
DBOS owns workflow/step position and checkpoint recovery; Provenance owns
semantic operation identity and exact domain replay. Pinned v0.16.0 exposes no
reliable public nested-step discriminator, so #6 makes no nested-detection or
inline-nested-step claim. `OpenSQLite` and `OpenMemory` remain available for
standalone consumers.

The closed command family covers task lifecycle, typed relationships, labels,
comments, responsibility/supervision assignments, explicit attribution,
task-linked Activity start/end,
later event-context attachment, and a generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation for
caller-validated material events that change no current task state. Provenance
commits domain row(s), required attribution, TaskEvent row(s), contexts, and
canonical operation/result through one #5 transaction on either its standalone
store or #6's borrowed DBOS handle. Pasture does not compose a fake
transaction across separate tracker/audit connections.

#5 also owns opaque `ConditionalMutationBatch` construction. It is a closed,
extension-safe declarative composition of existing generic mutations plus
caller-validated opaque material events; it is not a callback, raw SQL, or an
untyped predicate escape hatch. Its built-in preconditions cover exact task
kind/status/owner, exact active/ended assignment and active-slot set, typed
relationship presence/absence and exact incoming/outgoing typed set equality,
exact task revision plus immutable subject task/current-subject relationships, exact immutable EventID/task/kind/context
evidence, and absence of unresolved blocked-by children. Canonical typed local
handles let later batch mutations reference earlier allocated tasks/assignments;
the result returns their stable ID map. Preconditions are
rechecked inside the same SQLite transaction immediately before the ordered
mutations. Domain rows, assignment transitions, relationships, events,
contexts, attribution, and operation result all commit or roll back together.
Pasture #43 compiles review/transition/closure policy into these generic
preconditions and mutations; Provenance never decodes a `pasture.*` payload.

The closed batch API also owns one narrow zero-domain/event form:
`ConditionalExistingIDResult`. Exact typed preconditions create unforgeable
`ExistingTaskHandle`, `ExistingAssignmentHandle`, `ExistingActivityHandle`, or
`ExistingEventHandle` values; typed result-slot bindings may project only those
handles into the operation result. The form requires at least one exact current-
state/authority precondition and one handle projection, permits no allocation,
literal/scalar/arbitrary-map result, domain mutation, or event draft, and rechecks
all predicates in the Apply transaction. Success commits only the canonical
operation row and typed existing-ID result rows; rejection/fault commits nothing.
Publication uses an ExistingEventHandle produced by the exact canonical-evidence
precondition, so `pushed|already_at_target` is decoded from that protected event's
stored payload rather than injected as a result literal.
The public four-handle sum is validated table-wise in #5 and through #14: task,
assignment, Activity, and event each cover positive exact projection,
cross-domain rejection, zero and multiple projection rejection, response loss,
restart/replay, state/authority races, and every fault rollback boundary. No
public branch exists without these fixtures.

OperationID is durable idempotency identity. Same ID plus byte-equivalent
canonical command/actor/exact authority returns the originally committed
result/events after close/reopen or concurrent retry. Same ID with different
actor, authority, or command fails.
The operation row rolls back with the mutation, so there is no pending state.

Pre-1.0 direct mutator paths migrate to Apply or compatibility wrappers that
require MutationContext and delegate to the same transaction. No exported bypass
may mutate a task/graph without its event.

### 9.3 Responsibility CAS and cumulative attribution

```go
type TransferTaskResponsibility struct {
    Task          TaskID
    ExpectedOwner OwnerExpectation // OwnerIs(agent) or OwnerIsUnassigned()
    ExpectedAssignment AssignmentExpectation
    Successor     OptionalAssignmentDraft // absent means become unassigned
    Reason        string
}
```

The expected owner and current responsibility assignment are compared inside
the same transaction. Transfer ends the predecessor, optionally creates the
successor, changes Owner, and records attribution/events atomically. Two
distinct concurrent transitions have one winner; the stale loser changes no
owner, assignment, attribution, operation, or event row and receives an
actionable conflict. `ChangeTaskOwner` is only a compatibility constructor that
delegates to this transition when its full assignment expectation is supplied;
otherwise it rejects once the assignment migration is active.
This protects task assignment only; it is unrelated to plugin-installation
concurrency and introduces no installer transaction/CAS mechanism.

Task.Owner is role-neutral current responsibility. Prior/new material contributors retain
idempotent `attributed_to` edges. Administrative actors are not attributed merely
for changing a label/status; attribution occurs only for responsibility or
material contribution commands. Owner events record expected/previous/new owner,
actor, reason, OperationID, time, and EventID.

### 9.4 Activities, relationships, and graph events

`StartTaskActivity` and `EndTaskActivity` carry AssignmentID, ActivityID,
phase/stage, notes, and contexts; TaskID and ActorID are derived and validated
from that exact active assignment. Activity row state, task linkage, material event,
required attribution, and contexts commit together. Duration Activities remain
distinct from instantaneous transitions and do not encode structured changes in
notes. The state machine is closed: start requires a new ActivityID, existing
task, and actor resolved from the supplied active assignment; a new OperationID
cannot start an existing Activity. End requires the same linked task/agent and
an active Activity. End-before-start, wrong task/agent, invalid transitions, and
a second end under a new OperationID write nothing; same-OperationID retries
return the original result, and concurrent ends have one winner.

Task relationships accept TaskID targets. Attribution accepts ActorID. Activity
links accept ActivityID. A relationship involving two tasks writes a task-local
event to each timeline in one transaction, sharing OperationID and receiving
distinct EventIDs. Blocked-by cycle validation, edge persistence, and both events
share the same consistency boundary.

### 9.5 Current state and legacy migration

Current task/graph/Activity tables remain authoritative. The journal explains
all post-migration changes; it is not used to rebuild pre-journal state. When #5
activates the coordinated production migration, existing tasks each receive one
idempotent `provenance.migration.baseline` event containing the then-current
status/phase/owner and source schema version. In that same exclusive transaction,
every nonterminal assigned task receives a deterministic migration-time active
owner-responsibility assignment; every terminal assigned task receives an ended
migration assignment and has current Owner cleared; unassigned tasks receive no
assignment. Assignment IDs derive from schema version plus TaskID. Provenance
uses only its generic `provenance.role.legacy-owner` and
`provenance.slot.owner-responsibility`; it never invents a Pasture role. The task
baseline EventID is the active assignment's StartEventID at migration RecordedAt.
For a terminal legacy owner, a second ordered migration-time assignment-ended
event supplies EndEventID at the same RecordedAt; both are explicitly snapshot
events and never claim historical start/end time.

Legacy owner text that is not already a registered ActorID maps to a
deterministically registered `legacy-owner/<sha256>` SoftwareAgent whose payload
retains the original text; invalid/duplicate registration fails the entire
migration. Attribution and migration events retain that mapped owner but are
explicitly labeled snapshot/baseline evidence, never fabricated historical
start/end times. The post-migration invariant holds for every task kind: a
nonterminal nonnil Owner has exactly one matching active responsibility
assignment, while every terminal task has nil Owner and no active responsibility.
This marks the historical-completeness boundary.

The #5 production migration executes schema activation and every baseline row
inside one exclusive SQLite migration transaction. A fault after any number of
rows rolls back the schema marker, journal tables/changes, and all baselines;
reopen then performs the same migration from the pre-migration database. Empty
databases, every assigned/unassigned × terminal/nonterminal × task-kind case,
unmappable legacy owner text, repeat startup, and concurrent startup are explicit
fixtures. Baseline ActorID is the registered migrator; an absent legacy owner is
never fabricated.

Before any `pasture task` protocol/review/slice command is enabled against the
coordinated Provenance schema, the #43/application startup coordinator calls
#14's read-only legacy-assignment extraction API. #14 never invokes #43. #43
classifies only tasks carrying a reserved, versioned Pasture protocol kind and
validates the exact required topology before building one idempotent
`NormalizeLegacyAssignmentRoles` conditional batch. That batch performs
same-owner responsibility transfers from generic legacy-owner assignments to
the typed role/slot, preserving predecessor, attribution, and ordered events.
There is no separate normalization marker, table, task, snapshot, or event: the
authoritative completion predicate is a deterministic post-batch requery proving
that every eligible active assignment already has its exact mapped role/slot and
no eligible generic assignment remains. An empty eligible set therefore succeeds
without inventing a marker host.

The v1 mapping is closed and exhaustive:

| Persisted Pasture kind/topology | Normalized active owner role |
|---|---|
| REQUEST, ELICIT, URD, PROPOSAL, Plan-UAT, HANDOFF, and their FOLLOWUP forms | RoleArchitect |
| plan-review round/container | RoleArchitect |
| IMPL_PLAN, integration task, Implementation-UAT, landing container, supervisor-created follow-up epic | RoleSupervisor |
| implementation slice and explicitly typed Pasture implementation leaf | RoleWorker |
| code-review round/container and eager severity group | RoleSupervisor |
| implementation-review finding leaf | RoleWorker |
| review axis with exact correctness relationship | RoleReviewerCorrectness |
| review axis with exact test-quality relationship | RoleReviewerTestQuality |
| review axis with exact elegance relationship | RoleReviewerElegance |

Terminal or unassigned eligible tasks require no active transfer but are still
validated. A reserved known kind with missing/conflicting topology, or an
unknown future reserved Pasture kind, fails the entire batch and leaves the
database unchanged. Ordinary Provenance tasks and leaves without a reserved Pasture
kind are explicitly ineligible: their generic legacy-owner role remains valid,
they do not enter the batch, and they cannot block Pasture activation. Fault/
restart repeats the extraction and state-derived normalization safely. Protocol
commands remain unavailable until the deterministic post-batch inspection
succeeds.

Pasture #43 owns a closed, typed import command; #14 supplies only extraction and
adapter plumbing:

```go
type LegacyAuditRowID string
type LegacySchemaVersion string
type ImportLegacyAuditRow struct { /* unexported validated row */ }

func NewImportLegacyAuditRow(
    schema LegacySchemaVersion,
    row LegacyAuditRowID,
    actor LegacyActorRef,
    recordedAt time.Time,
    definition LegacyEventDefinition,
    contexts []LegacyContext,
    tasks []provenance.TaskID,
) (ImportLegacyAuditRow, error)
```

The constructor validates the source schema/row identity, maps the legacy kind
and payload through a typed #43-owned definition, validates every context, drops
duplicate task IDs, sorts the remaining typed IDs, and resolves the actor before
any Apply call. Unknown kinds/payload shapes or invalid/empty task fan-out fail
without writes. Pasture migrates actual legacy audit history without deleting or
updating source rows; pre/post byte hashes of the legacy tables are acceptance
evidence:

- #14's finite coordinator collects all rows and `context_edges`, validates the
  full extraction, sorts rows by `(recorded time, legacy row ID)`, and imports
  serially, stopping at the first failure so equal-time EventID allocation is
  deterministic across repeat/reopen;
- resolve every unique task ID represented by epoch/slice/review/follow-up task
  contexts;
- invoke one #43-owned `ImportLegacyAuditRow` command containing the source
  schema, legacy row ID, actor mapping, original time/payload, all contexts, and
  the sorted unique TaskIDs; it validates/encodes typed payloads and delegates
  once to Provenance's generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation;
- have that single Apply operation create one canonical TaskEvent per `(legacy
  schema, legacy event ID, resolved TaskID)`, attaching all of that row's legacy
  contexts;
- give the batch one stable migration OperationID derived from `(legacy schema,
  legacy event ID)` and deterministic event insert order `(legacy recorded time,
  legacy row ID, task ID)`; and
- enforce the compound legacy identity uniquely so repeat migration/reopen cannot
  duplicate events.

`ImportLegacyAuditRow` is atomic: every event/context/operation result for one
legacy row commits or none does. A retry with the same source identity returns
the canonical batch result and EventIDs; conflicting source content fails. An
injected failure after the first event rolls back the full row batch. This is a
finite schema import, not an event-sourcing or runtime transaction subsystem.

Migrated real events preserve their original RecordedAt and mapped ActorID. When
an old actor cannot be resolved, the migration uses an explicitly registered
`pasture-legacy-migrator` SoftwareAgent and retains the original actor text in the
typed migration payload; ActorID is never silently nil or forged. Baseline events
use a registered `provenance-migrator` SoftwareAgent and migration time. Stable
OperationIDs derive from the typed legacy-row identity through a documented
constructor, not from process-local counters.

Thus one old row linked to several tasks appears on every relevant task timeline
without losing its many-to-many contexts. #14 owns the separately named,
read-only `pasture legacy-audit event list` API for non-task legacy rows and its
raw source-identity/actor-text/context tests; #43 never folds those rows into a
task timeline. After auto-migration,
`pasture task timeline TASK-ID` reads canonical Provenance TaskEvents only; it
does not perform an unstable runtime merge with rows lacking EventID.

## 10. `pasture task` algebra, Provenance backend, and CLI (#43)

Issue #43 owns the typed task-effect variants, their Provenance-backed execution,
the `pasture.*` material event definitions, closure-policy validation, composed
timeline projection, and this frozen command contract. Pasture #14 owns only the
low-level Provenance dependency adapter and legacy-import plumbing; it does not
define task effects or map them to commands. #43 does not migrate generated
source or remove `bd`; issue #42 consumes the completed contract and owns that
finite conversion.

```text
pasture task contract --json
pasture task create|update|close|reopen|list
pasture task show TASK-ID [--revision DOCUMENT-REVISION-ID] [decision filters]
pasture task ready|blocked|dep tree
pasture task relation add|remove|list
pasture task assignment start|end|transfer|list
pasture task attribute add|list
pasture task label add|remove|list
pasture task comment add|list
pasture task activity start|end|list
pasture task event record|list
pasture task command canonicalize
pasture task protocol create|revise|transition|supersede|ratify|land
pasture task decision append-agent
pasture task epoch interaction-mode set|show
pasture task uat plan-decide|implementation-decide
pasture task review start|submit|finalize
pasture task slice create|candidate set|rework|close
pasture task integration candidate-set|rework|publish-repository
pasture task context add|list
pasture task timeline TASK-ID [--json]
```

```text
pasture task slice close TASK-ID --assignment ASSIGNMENT-ID \
  --round REVIEW-ROUND-ID --candidate TASK-CANDIDATE-ID \
  --review-event correctness=EVENT-ID \
  --review-event test-quality=EVENT-ID \
  --review-event elegance=EVENT-ID
```

Every mutation accepts `--mutation-ref MUTATION-REF` and its exact initiating
`--assignment ASSIGNMENT-REF` or `--bootstrap-agent AGENT-REF`; typed JSON results expose
named bindings for created TaskRef/AssignmentRef/ReviewRoundRef values. Exact
flags/JSON schemas are frozen before generation. Generated workflow documents
carry typed ValueRefs plus the complete MutationContinuation; #14/#43 converts
them to authoritative Provenance IDs, resolves ActorID from the retained
historical initiating authority for committed replay and from that same active
authority for a new operation, and never accepts an actor/supervisor
override for review or slice closure. Bootstrap/administrative callers use a
separate registered-agent API and make no authentication claim. Queries are
side-effect free. Generic `task update` is available only to ordinary leaves and
changes only non-reserved descriptive metadata; it rejects every protected
subject/review/slice/protocol task and all status, phase, kind, owner, assignment,
body-revision, or relationship changes. `transition` accepts a kind-specific expected/from/to transition;
`supersede` atomically makes the successor the sole canonical proposal, relates
the successor as superseding the old artifact, and transitions the old one;
`ratify` requires accepted review-round evidence plus accepted Plan-UAT or an
exact same-epoch `deferred_by_afk` event bound to the DocumentRevisionSubject,
epoch root, input/output ledger revisions, agent actor, and AFK mode-entry cursor.
For AFK deferral it also folds the current ledger in the same transaction and
requires that exact entry still be the latest interaction-mode entry with result
AFK. Normal selection or any later mode entry makes the old deferral historical
and ineligible; AFK->normal->AFK requires a fresh Plan deferral.
`land` performs no Git operation. It requires resolved dependencies plus clean
review and Implementation-UAT evidence bound to the same exact current
IntegrationCandidateSetSubject and one #43-owned typed
`pasture.git.remote-ref-verified/v1` material event per repository candidate.
It also CASes the exact current ledger `DocumentRevisionID` and recomputed required-
entry coverage digest named by that accepted UAT; any successor ledger revision
invalidates the UAT relation and defeats land.
That event is protected from generic recording. The sole executable producer is
the versioned application/#40 composite command `pasture task integration
publish-repository`. Its typed argv names exact current IntegrationCandidateSetID,
RepositoryID, CommitOID, TreeDigest, RemoteRef, ExpectedOldOID, controlling
AssignmentID, and MutationRef. In one Pasture process it executes this closed
sequence:

1. Before the first attempt, #40 passes the fully resolved typed request to
   #43's pure `command canonicalize` API. #43 canonicalizes one versioned
   `PublicationIntent` containing every task-command field except MutationRef and
   authority and returns its typed digest. The surviving parent then mints
   MutationRef and retains the complete continuation in AssignmentContext.
2. #40 passes the same request and complete continuation to #43's internal,
   side-effect-free `PrepareRepositoryPublication`. #43 recomputes and validates
   exact identity, rejects placeholders/mismatch, and asks #14 to map the ref,
   exact assignment-or-bootstrap authority, historical actor, and digest to #5.
   The returned opaque
   `PublicationPreparation` contains exactly the OperationID/CommandDigest pair
   plus OperationAuthorityID that any later #14 `Apply` records. An exact committed lookup returns the
   original status/EventID/result map without touching Git, including after
   authority has ended or Git is unavailable; `Conflict` fails; `Absent`
   continues. Neither #40 nor a caller can supply or inspect either digest.
3. The same #43 preparation performs a read-only publication preflight. It requires the exact current
   integration set and repository tuple, the controlling active supervisor
   assignment, one current fix-free accepted integration-review round, one
   accepted current Implementation-UAT decision, and either no canonical
   publication evidence or the one exact existing event for
   `(IntegrationCandidateSetID, RepositoryID)`. Stale, unreviewed, unaccepted,
   unauthorized, mismatched, or conflicting evidence fails before Git. Exact
   existing evidence produces an `existing_evidence` preparation without Git.
4. Only an eligible absent-evidence result calls #46 guarded push or verified
   already-at-target and retains that non-serializable `effects.VerifiedGuardedPush`
   in memory.
5. The application composite calls the #43 task store directly:

   ```go
   prep, err := taskStore.PrepareRepositoryPublication(ctx, request, continuation)
   if err != nil { return Result{}, err }
   proof, err := effects.GuardedPushExactCommit(ctx, pushRequest)
   if err != nil { return Result{}, err }
   return taskStore.CommitRepositoryPublication(ctx, prep, proof, continuation)
   ```

   `CommitRepositoryPublication` accepts the opaque proof through #43's one-way
   import of `internal/effects`, rejects a zero or repository/commit/tree/ref/
   outcome mismatch, and rechecks all task/UAT/ledger predicates atomically. For
   `existing_evidence`, #43 uses #14's closed
   `ConditionalExistingIDResult`: the exact canonical-evidence precondition
   produces an ExistingEventHandle; the same current set/repository/review/UAT/
   ledger-revision/coverage/authority predicates are rechecked; and Apply commits
   only this OperationID's typed EventID result. It creates no domain row/event
   and cannot bind an arbitrary ID or scalar. For verified Git, #43 rechecks every preflight predicate inside
   one ConditionalMutationBatch and installs exactly one event/relation. The
   process-local Git proof gates this method but is excluded from
   `PublicationIntent`, so preparation, lookup, and Apply share identical command
   bytes. If a distinct operation wins the canonical evidence race, #43
   re-prepares and commits the result-only existing-event binding under the
   losing operation's same digest/OperationID. Conflicting evidence or any
   eligibility change writes nothing.

The command returns only `pasture.task.integration-publish-result/v1` with the
canonical protected event's stored `pushed|already_at_target` outcome and EventID/result
bindings—no portable verified token, evidence payload constructor, or record
subcommand exists. An existing-evidence or concurrent-convergence call returns
the original event's stored outcome. Every successful call has its own committed
operation/result row; lost-response
replay therefore returns the identical status, EventID, and bindings after
restart, ended authority, Git unavailability, or later integration rework.

Git then SQLite remains deliberately sequential, not transactional. Git failure
writes no evidence. If Git succeeds but Apply fails, retry of the same
MutationRef looks up Absent, passes a fresh read-only preflight, verifies
already-at-target, and appends; if Apply committed but the response was lost,
`LookupCommitted` returns the original EventID before any Git action. If
integration rework wins after preflight but before append, the guarded push may
have succeeded while evidence correctly fails: the error reports the advanced
remote OID, obsolete set, failed append predicate, and directs the supervisor to
construct a replacement integration set using that observed remote as its new
expected-old state, then rerun review and UAT. No rollback or stale evidence is
attempted. Partial multi-repository success is reported and resumed without
rollback. Cross-process JSON/native callers can
request only the full composite operation, so fabricated intermediate results
cannot cross the runtime boundary. #46/effects never imports #43/task; #43/task
imports #46/effects only for the opaque proof type, and #40/application wires the
closed composite. Any candidate/tree/ref change invalidates the evidence
and requires new integration review/UAT. Generic `task close` rejects slice,
review, and protocol-container kinds. The exact slice CLI includes RoundID,
TaskCandidateID, AssignmentID,
and three accepted review EventIDs and lowers the §5.3 predicate and mutations
into one ConditionalMutationBatch.

`pasture task contract --json` returns the closed
`pasture.task.contract-probe/v1` schema containing CLI semver, TaskContractID,
supported schema IDs/ranges, and a canonical definition digest. Generated
artifacts embed their exact requirement. The runtime probes once before the
first task mutation and fails before writes on a missing command, malformed
probe, adjacent/unsupported version, digest mismatch, or semantic contract
mismatch; this covers separately upgraded generated packages and binaries.

Review/UAT/skill/git evidence uses typed Pasture event definitions. Protected
review definitions cannot pass generic `event record`. `event list` accepts a
versioned `pasture.task.event-query/v1`: TaskIDs are ORed, EventKinds are ORed,
typed contexts are ORed, and the non-empty dimensions combine with AND. The
first page captures `SnapshotMaxEventID`; every later page carries it plus an
exclusive `(AfterRecordedAt, AfterEventID)` cursor and ignores later inserts.
Rows are canonical stored envelopes ordered ascending by `(RecordedAt, EventID)`.
Concurrent/backdated appends therefore appear only in a new traversal, never
duplicate or disappear within the current snapshot.

`timeline TASK-ID` uses `pasture.task.timeline-query/v1` with the same snapshot
watermark and exclusive key. Its tagged rows are `point_event` or
`activity_interval`. A point sorts by `(RecordedAt, EventID)`; an interval sorts
by `(StartedAt, StartEventID)`, carries nullable EndedAt/EndEventID plus both
source EventIDs, and is open when no end event exists at the snapshot watermark.
Overlaps do not alter ordering. Folding creates no journal row, and human/JSON
renderings share the same schema. Non-task legacy rows remain only in #14's
separately named API. Errors name the effect, artifact/command, why/where/when,
impact, and fix. Issue #42's final generated-output gate rejects operational
`bd`.

Workers report completion with `pasture task activity end` followed by the typed
assignment-completed event. Generic `pasture task close` is only the ordinary-
leaf policy and atomically ends that leaf's responsibility assignment. CLI
fixtures prove that completion cannot close a slice, a worker cannot invoke
slice close, and the governing-plan supervisor can close it only with the
current accepted three-axis round through one conditional batch.

## 12. Simple installer

Canonical preferences are exactly:

```yaml
install:
  harnesses:
    claude-code: false
    opencode: false
    codex: false
  extensions:
    skills: true
    agents: true
    hooks: false
```

This is one harness boolean map plus one global extension map—not a per-harness
extension matrix. The TUI has harness checkboxes, one global extension page,
saved choices, exact install/uninstall summary, confirmation, and progress.
Cancellation changes nothing.

After confirmation Pasture preserves unrelated YAML and saves preferences before
native actions. It normalizes the confirmed preferences to one immutable
`pasture.install.effective-selection/v1` desired document, then passes that to
`apply-selection --source installer`. TUI effective cells are
`harness && extension`. The persisted config remains simple global preferences
and never stores the normalized matrix or installation evidence.

The fixed reconciler is deliberately small:

- desired effective true: idempotently ensure present/update, including an
  unchanged true cell;
- desired effective false plus a Pasture-managed installed/unknown inventory
  record: inspect and idempotently remove the exact component; and
- desired false with no Pasture-managed or uncertain record: no mutation.

Thus first-run false harnesses are untouched, a failed uninstall remains visible
and retryable after the preference already says false, and unrelated native
installations or identical external files are observed but never claimed or
removed. A global extension change fans out across the currently desired and
recorded managed cells.

The installer applies all cells, including its own direct-file destinations.
Home Manager independently renders the same effective schema from its per-
harness children but calls only native-managed cells; Nix owns direct-file link
transitions. Schema-validation, normalization, transition, and source-ownership
fixtures prove the two inputs agree for equivalent choices without conflating
their execution responsibilities.

Save failure invokes no native action. Any native/file failure stops immediately;
the postcondition probe updates the factual inventory where possible, earlier
completed actions remain, and later actions are unattempted. The error names what
failed, why, the cell/path/manager and stage, what remains or is unknown, caller
impact, `pasture install status`, and the exact executor-aware tagged
remediation. There is no rollback, background recovery, lock, authorization, or
cross-cell transaction coordinator. Native managers own plugin/update/cache
state; Pasture never writes private caches.

Pasture #45 publishes the exact legacy and split Claude package identities plus
fixtures; #39 alone owns this compatibility behavior. Before mutation #39
classifies native state as empty, exact v0.0.4 monolith only, split only, exact
monolith plus complete/partial known splits, or unknown. Unknown identity,
scope, version, or duplicate/conflicting rows perform zero mutation. For each
known state the frozen order is: probe/list and validate; ensure/update every
desired split; verify it; remove the exact user-scoped v0.0.4 monolith; verify
absence; remove any unselected known split; verify final state; record the
inventory. Failure at every action stops later actions, probes and records what
actually remains, and the next ordinary run resumes reconciliation without
rollback. Codex hooks finish as installed-but-requiring-native-trust-review until
the user approves them in Codex; this trust state is reported, not bypassed.

The v0.0.4 monolith transition is selection-wide and is implemented exclusively
by `apply-selection`, which has every Claude sibling's desired state. While the
monolith or an incomplete legacy transition exists, `apply-cell` fails before
mutation and instructs the caller to rerun the full installer/TUI or Home Manager
activation with an exhaustive desired selection. It never guesses sibling
intent, and a cell-level failure row prints that same full-selection remedy.

The group probes even for an all-false/no-inventory selection so the approved
monolith exception is discoverable when the supported manager is available. If
that optional read-only probe is missing, out-of-range, nonzero, or malformed,
all three never-recorded false rows are `completed` with operation
`no_op_unavailable` and a nonfatal diagnostic that unverified legacy state was
preserved; no inventory or mutation occurs. A supported valid-empty probe is the
same completed no-op, while an exact monolith enters the group removal.

A syntactically valid optional all-false/no-inventory response containing an
exact split component, near-match monolith, wrong scope/version, unknown selector,
or duplicate/conflicting rows performs zero mutation and writes no inventory.
Exact split components are reported `completed/no_op_preserved_external` with
their observed identity; near-match/unknown/duplicate/conflicting state is
`completed/no_op_preserved_ambiguous` with `ok=true` plus a preservation
diagnostic. This optional mode succeeds because no desired or managed cell
requires authority and preservation is the requested behavior.

If any Claude cell is desired true or has managed/unknown inventory, the same
initial probe failure is terminal before mutation: the first canonical required
row is `failed`, other executable rows are `unattempted`, prior inventory is
unchanged, and remediation names the exact binary/version/response repair.

In required mode, an exact desired split already present without inventory is
observed external and may satisfy desired true without adoption; an exact
external split under desired false is preserved. A near-match, wrong scope/
version, unknown selector, duplicate, or conflicting response is terminal
`failed/ambiguous_native_state` before mutation, leaves prior inventory unchanged,
and uses the appropriate ApplySelection/RerunInstaller or RerunHomeManager tagged
remediation. A managed/unknown inventory record that no longer matches exact live
identity is likewise a terminal conflict, never silently externalized.

The group crosses the classified legacy state with
all eight Claude desired combinations, executes each ensure/remove exactly once,
and skips the three ordinary Claude executors. On failure, it live-inspects all
three cells: rows already satisfying desired state are `completed`; the first
canonical unsatisfied row is `failed` with `group_stage` and the exact native
action; other unsatisfied Claude rows and later executable native rows are
`unattempted`. If all split postconditions match but monolith removal alone
fails, `claude-code.skills` is the fixed control/failure row and the diagnostic
names that shared legacy stage. Home Manager declarative rows remain live-
inspected `managed_declaratively`. Full-selection retry repeats the group probe
and converges without duplicate per-cell actions.

If live inspection after an action failure is itself missing/nonzero/malformed,
only rows with already verified individual postconditions remain `completed`.
The action-owning row is `failed` with both primary action and secondary probe
diagnostics and its inventory observation `unknown`; every other unverified
Claude cell is `unattempted`/`unknown`. No row is guessed from desired state.
Ordinary full-selection retry repairs the probe first and resumes from factual
inventory/live inspection.

## 1. Decision, Plan-UAT correction, and Proposal-48 review merge

Pasture will compile opaque, validated Go `Document` values into native Claude
Code, OpenCode, and Codex artifacts. Portable meaning lives in a
protocol-semantic IR. Markdown is parsed with Goldmark, not searched and rewritten
as an operational language. Native runtime calls are emitted only through an
exhaustive, version-bounded runtime contract.

Provenance will own one generic, ordered TaskEvent journal and the transaction
boundary that commits task/graph/Activity state with its events. Current task
tables remain authoritative; the journal explains post-migration changes and is
not an event-sourced replacement for historical state. Pasture owns typed
`pasture.*` event definitions and the `pasture task` CLI that generated workflows
use instead of Beads.

Native plugin registration is deliberately separate from runtime semantics. A
versioned activation contract describes public version probes, exact manager
commands or config mutation, package identities, and standalone destinations.
`pasture install` keeps the user's simple preferences separate from a narrow,
factual installation-state inventory. That inventory records what Pasture
confirmed it installed or removed, what remains, and the last actionable
failure. It is not a pending-operation queue, rollback log, authorization
system, lock, or cross-cell transaction coordinator.

Proposal 49 retains all accepted Proposal 48 invariants and merges the concrete
API, schema, and test solutions from all three Proposal 48 reviewers. Provenance
becomes a first-class DBOS-compatible domain store without conflating DBOS

and a version-bounded adapter owns a deterministic one-shot DBOS workflow plus
step guard while preserving the caller's semantic `MutationContext.OperationID`
unchanged. This lets ordinary CLI/root contexts enter DBOS correctly. The adapter
checkpoints a closed typed success-or-failure outcome instead of relying on Go
error serialization, post-validates the exact committed Provenance
MutationDigest/result, and relies on ordinary replay across both workflow and

## 4. Opaque typed Document API

The following shows semantics, not exported mutable field layout:

```go
type Document struct { /* unexported validated parts */ }
type Part interface { /* closed within compiler package */ }
type RenderedTree struct { /* immutable validated relative files */ }

func NewDocument(parts ...Part) (Document, error)
func Markdown(source []byte, at Location) (Part, error)
func Operation(op SemanticOperation, at Location) (Part, error)
func Verbatim(content []byte, at Location) (Part, error)
func TargetLiteral(cases []TargetCase, at Location) (Part, error)
func Compile(document Document, target Target) (RenderedTree, error)
```

`Markdown` parses once through Goldmark. Its unexported AST segments reference an
owned immutable source buffer. Constructors retain source locations and reject
invalid states before a document exists.

`Verbatim` is a portable fragment preserved without operational interpretation.
`TargetLiteral` is a narrow raw-native escape. Across the requested target set it
contains exactly one validated `LiteralFor(RuntimeContractID, content, reason)`
or `LiteralUnsupported(harness, reason)` per enabled harness. Missing, duplicate,
or out-of-range cases fail. Target literals cannot masquerade as portable
operations.

Compilation stages are explicit:

```text
typed Go specs
  -> validated Document and Goldmark AST
  -> semantic/type/dataflow validation
  -> runtime contract selection
  -> exhaustive operation/effect/capability lowering
  -> target rendering and package projection
  -> native schema/loader validation
```

Diagnostics carry canonical owner, file/section and AST source range, semantic
operation, target contract, failed stage/time, caller impact, and concrete fix.
Compilation and every native schema/loader check operate entirely in memory and
return either one immutable complete #38-owned `RenderedTree` or an error plus no
tree. The compiler never opens an output path before successful validation, so
an existing output tree remains byte-identical on any compile/lower/load error.
Filesystem publication is a later #46 effect with its own explicit per-path
result and failure semantics. Successful publication is exact-tree convergence
over a publisher-owned generated root: reconcile create/update/remove against a
canonical prior-output manifest stored at a derived same-parent sidecar path
`.<payload-root>.pasture-manifest.json`, never inside the payload root, then
verify the payload root's final path/type/mode/content set equals the complete
`RenderedTree`. The payload grammar cannot name the sidecar, and an existing
unowned/unsafe sidecar is an actionable pre-mutation conflict. A failed publish
retains explicit partial results and the last confirmed manifest; retrying the
same RenderedTree may resume only paths whose live state equals either the old
manifest or that desired tree. It never claims rollback or compiler failure.
Unowned roots, unrelated file states, and changing the desired tree across an
unreconciled partial publish fail actionably before further mutation rather than
deleting unknown files. Publication verifies payload equality first and replaces
the sidecar manifest last using create-exclusive temp/write/flush/rename. Success
requires both exact payload and the new manifest; a failure before/during/after
that final replacement is explicit partial state eligible only for same-tree
retry.

## 5. Protocol-semantic IR

Semantic operations are closed concrete variants behind validating constructors,
not optional-field bags and not tool-name/arguments maps.

### 5.1 Orchestration and logical continuity

The closed orchestration set is:

- `InvokeSkill`
- `DelegateAssignment`
- `ContinueAssignment`
- `SendAssignmentMessage`
- `CollectAssignmentResults`
- `StopAssignment`
- `ir.RequestUserDecision`

Collections plus `independent`, `dependency-ordered`, or `bounded-parallel`
scheduling metadata express parallelism. Claude teams, OpenCode tasks, and Codex
agent handles are backend details.

Every delegation/continuation carries a validated logical context:

```go
type AssignmentContext struct {
    Role        protocol.RoleID
    Assignment protocol.AssignmentRef
    Task        protocol.TaskRef
    Worktree    WorktreeRef
    Evidence    []EvidenceRef
    Decisions   []DecisionRef
    Outstanding []WorkItemRef
    Mutations   []MutationContinuation
    Bindings    RuntimeBindings
}

type MutationContinuation struct {
    Ref         protocol.MutationRef
    Authority   MutationAuthority // exact initiating assignment or bootstrap actor
    Request     ResolvedMutationRequest // operation, schema, and immutable canonical request bytes
    Command     CanonicalCommandDigest
    Results     []ResultSlotDeclaration
    Scope       LexicalScopeSnapshot // exact typed bindings visible at construction
}

type MutationAuthority interface { mutationAuthority() }
// InitiatingAssignment(protocol.AssignmentRef) | BootstrapActor(protocol.AgentRef)
```

The target may resume an existing agent or spawn a fresh one. Both are correct
only when the full context above is reconstructed. Runtime session identity is
never the assignment identity.

Core #38 owns only the portable opaque `protocol.AssignmentRef` and
`protocol.TaskRef` used in generated documents. It does not import Provenance or
wait for #5. After the coordinated Provenance release, #14/#43 validate and
convert those refs to Provenance `AssignmentID`/`TaskID`; runtime bindings carry
the portable refs unchanged across a harness boundary. `protocol.RoleID` maps
through #43 to a typed `AssignmentRoleID`, and each Pasture-defined slot
constructor accepts only the matching role/axis. Raw strings never bridge these
ID domains.

Reusable artifacts never embed concrete runtime task, assignment, review, or
Provenance operation IDs. #38 owns opaque typed `BindingKey[T]` and
`ValueRef[T]` values for context inputs and prior operation results. Every
operation declares typed result slots; runtime lowering validates JSON result
schemas, binds concrete `TaskRef`, `AssignmentRef`, `ReviewRoundRef`, and other
values into the current lexical assignment scope, and later operations consume
only matching typed refs. Missing, duplicate, wrong-type, or out-of-scope
bindings fail before invocation.

#38 also owns portable `protocol.MutationRef`, distinct from
`SemanticOperationID` and Provenance `OperationID`. Mutation construction is
explicitly two-stage. After resolving every typed ValueRef, the runtime first
calls #43's pure, side-effect-free `pasture task command canonicalize` API with
the versioned typed operation/request. #43 returns normalized command identity
plus `CanonicalCommandDigest` without a MutationRef or state query. Only then
does the surviving parent mint one fresh MutationRef and retain the complete
`MutationContinuation`: exact initiating AssignmentRef or registered bootstrap
AgentRef, semantic operation and request schema, immutable canonical resolved
request bytes, canonical digest, typed result declarations, and a frozen lexical
scope snapshot in its parent-owned `AssignmentContext.Mutations`. This complete
value is sufficient for the parent to reconstruct the exact request when it
replaces a child runtime agent; neither a non-invertible digest nor a later owner
is treated as request storage. Parent/process crash recovery is explicitly out of
scope: there is no continuation database, pending queue, recovery codec, or
cleanup lifecycle. The first
stateful attempt receives that continuation; #43 recomputes canonical bytes from
the resolved request and rejects zero/placeholder/mismatched/caller-invented
digests before lookup or mutation. The same continuation is reused across retry
or fresh-agent continuation. #14/#43
validates and deterministically maps it into the durable Provenance OperationID
namespace. Distinct logical invocations always mint distinct refs; conflicting
reuse fails without writes. CLI JSON accepts one typed `--mutation-ref` plus the
typed initiating authority and returns canonical typed result bindings.

For every `pasture task` operation, #43 is the sole producer of canonical task-
command bytes and `CanonicalCommandDigest`. #14 owns a typed, byte-preserving
conversion to Provenance `CommandDigest`; it neither accepts a caller-supplied
digest nor recanonicalizes the command. #5 records exactly that converted digest
in both `LookupCommitted` and `Apply`. #40 passes the typed task request and
MutationContinuation to #43 unchanged and never maps MutationRef/OperationID or
calls #5 directly. The canonicalization CLI/API is read-only and emitted before
every generated task mutation; exact schemas ensure a fresh agent reconstructs
byte-identical request/digest before retry.

Replay lookup uses MutationRef/OperationID, canonical command, historical ActorID,
and exact typed initiating authority identity: AssignmentID plus assignment kind/
slot/task, or registered-bootstrap identity. If that exact
operation already committed, it returns the original result even when the
initiating assignment is now ended or responsibility transferred. If it has not
committed, the same assignment must still be active/current (or the bootstrap
actor registered) inside the conditional batch. A new MutationRef naming an
ended assignment writes nothing. Runtime continuation never re-resolves the
actor from whichever assignment happens to be current later. Two assignments for
the same ActorID, two slots, wrong-task authority, and bootstrap versus assignment
are replay conflicts, not aliases.

Within one ConditionalMutationBatch, #5 owns canonical typed local handles such
as `LocalTaskRef` and `LocalAssignmentRef`. Later mutations in the same batch may
refer to those handles; the canonical result maps them to allocated IDs. Same-
operation replay returns the same map, so `review start` creates and returns its
round, three axis tasks, and assignments atomically without pre-baked IDs.

Provenance #5 owns the authoritative assignment aggregate rather than leaving
`AssignmentID` as free evidence supplied by generated prose. Its public IDs are
opaque validated string types (`AssignmentID`, `AssignmentSlotID`, and
`AssignmentRoleID`), and its
immutable lifecycle projection contains the task, agent, slot, role, status,
start/end EventIDs and timestamps, and optional predecessor assignment. Exactly
one assignment may be active for a `(TaskID, AssignmentSlotID)` pair.

`StartTaskAssignment`, `EndTaskAssignment`, and assignment transfer use the same
atomic `Apply`/`OperationID` boundary as task mutations. A new child assignment
requires either an active parent AssignmentID or a registered bootstrap
SoftwareAgent, so the first assignment is explicit without creating a circular
dependency.

Task responsibility is role-neutral: architect, supervisor, worker, and reviewer
tasks all use the active owner-responsibility assignment as the sole assignment
authority for `Task.Owner`. `TransferTaskResponsibility`
atomically checks expected owner/assignment, ends the predecessor, starts the
successor, updates Owner (including assigned-to-unassigned), preserves
attribution, and writes events. Standalone owner mutation delegates to this
transition or rejects once assignment semantics are active. Closing a task ends
its owner-responsibility assignment and clears Owner in the same transaction. Reopen leaves the
task unassigned and requires an explicit new responsibility assignment; it never
reactivates an ended one.

Generic assignment start/end is limited to non-owner slots. Initial owner
assignment is a transfer from expected unassigned state; an owner-responsibility
assignment cannot end except inside responsibility transfer or task closure.

The IMPL_PLAN's own active owner-responsibility assignment has RoleSupervisor and
authorizes closure of child slices through an explicit `governs(parent, slice)`
relationship; there is no duplicate supervisor slot on the parent and it is
non-owning only relative to each child. Reviewer assignments are owner-
responsibility assignments on their own axis review tasks, with typed
correctness/test-quality/elegance roles. Duplicate, stale, ended, superseded,
wrong-task, wrong-slot, and concurrent start/end/transfer cases write nothing.

### 5.2 User decisions

`ir.RequestUserDecision` has result modes `ir.SelectOne`, `ir.SelectMany`, and
`ir.FreeText`.
It includes the full question, all option IDs/labels/descriptions in presentation
order, any code or definition shown, mode-specific cardinality including an
explicit `MinSelections`, and verbatim answer capture. `SelectMany` may be empty
only when `MinSelections == 0`; absence never silently implies that rule. A native widget
is used only if its request/result contract preserves those semantics. Otherwise
the parent performs a validated textual interaction; if neither is possible, the
operation is unsupported rather than silently narrowed.

### 5.3 Task/workflow effects

Task effects cover the entire approved surface:

- lifecycle: create, show, update, close/reopen, list, ready, blocked, dependency
  tree;
- typed task-to-task relationships: blocked-by, derived-from, supersedes,
  discovered-from, contains, and governs;
- responsibility assignment start/end/transfer with owner CAS plus non-owner
  supervision and reviewer assignment operations;
- typed task-to-Actor attribution add/query;
- label/comment mutations and queries;
- typed task-linked Activity start/end/query using `ActivityID`;
- typed transition/supersede/ratify/land operations and assignment/review/UAT/
  skill/git material events;
- secondary event-context add/query; and
- ordered task event/timeline queries.

Work completion is not task closure. A worker ends its task-linked Activity and
records a typed `pasture.assignment.completed` material event, but never closes a
slice. `CloseTask` is the reviewed task-status transition reserved to the
supervisor/protocol owner after the required review gate. There is no ambiguous
`CompleteTask` mutation or `pasture task complete` command.

Review identity is an explicit task-graph aggregate, not three loosely related
events:

```go

type DocumentRevisionID string
type TaskCandidateID string
type IntegrationCandidateSetID string

type ReviewSubject interface {
    reviewSubject()
    ReviewRef() ReviewSubjectRef
}
type DocumentRevisionSubject struct {
    ID            DocumentRevisionID
    DocumentTask  TaskID
    ContentDigest ContentDigest
}
type ImplementationCandidateSubject struct {
    ID          TaskCandidateID
    SliceTask   TaskID
    Repository  RepositoryID
    CommitOID   GitOID
    TreeDigest  ContentDigest
}
type IntegrationCandidateSetSubject struct {
    ID              IntegrationCandidateSetID
    IntegrationTask TaskID
    Repositories    []RepositoryCandidate // canonical unique RepositoryID order
}
type ReviewSubjectRef struct {
    Kind       ReviewSubjectKind
    SnapshotID TaskID
}

    RoundID      ReviewRoundID
    CandidateID  TaskCandidateID
    ReviewEvents [3]provenance.EventID

```

`ReviewSubject` is a closed sum. All variants are immutable protected subject
tasks stored in the ordinary Provenance task/relationship tables. #5 contributes
a generic immutable snapshot task kind/constructor whose payload bytes and
digest can never be update/close/reopened; it also CASes exact typed relationship
sets without learning Pasture semantics. #43 validates the subject variants and
payload codecs before constructing those generic snapshots.
Each variant has exactly one canonical identity, a validated const-string wrapper
over its immutable snapshot TaskID. `ReviewRef()` derives the closed sum-level
`ReviewSubjectRef{Kind, SnapshotID}` from that sole identity; it is never stored
as a second independently supplied ID. Constructors prove kind and payload
agreement. `DocumentRevisionID` is deliberately not named `TaskRevisionID`, so
it cannot be confused with Provenance's mutable-task CAS revision token.

`DocumentRevisionSubject` snapshots the exact protocol task ID, immutable body
revision ID, and canonical sha256 digest of title plus every reviewed body field
(description, design, acceptance, and typed amendment fields). Labels, comments,
owner/status, and audit metadata are excluded and cannot change the reviewed
body. `protocol create` creates the initial revision subject plus one reserved
`current-revision` relationship atomically. A PROPOSAL body is never edited:
changes create PROPOSAL-N+1 and supersede the old task. Other protocol documents
use typed `protocol revise` to create a new immutable revision and atomically
replace `current-revision`; if a round is live it closes/cancels/terminally
disposes it and resolves its dependencies in that same batch, and any prior
finalized review/UAT evidence remains historical but ineligible. Plan
review start/finalize, a typed AFK-bound Plan-UAT deferral, and ratify all require
the same exact current revision relationship and digest.

Proposal replacement never uses document `revise`. Typed `protocol supersede`
accepts the expected canonical proposal/revision plus a newly created
PROPOSAL-N+1 revision. In one conditional batch it makes the new proposal the
sole canonical proposal, relates the successor as `supersedes` the old proposal,
terminalizes any live old review round and all axes/assignments/dependencies,
invalidates any old Plan-UAT decision/deferral, and marks the old proposal
superseded. Finalized review and UAT records remain immutable history but are
ineligible for the successor. Concurrent review start/submit/finalize, Plan UAT,
ratify, and competing supersede operations have one winner; every stale loser
writes nothing. Ratification CASes the sole canonical proposal relationship.

`ImplementationCandidateSubject` stores repository identity, exact immutable Git
commit OID, base evidence, and canonical tree digest. Initial
`pasture task slice candidate set --expected none --commit ...` creates the
protected subject and `current-candidate` relationship only when the slice has no
candidate and no live round. Later deliverable bytes use only typed `slice
rework`, whose reason is a closed sum:

- `address_findings` is legal only after all three axis inventories have
  submitted. It requires at least one finding, a distinct replacement commit/tree
  identity, and a typed `FindingDisposition` for every finding across all three
  inventories. Each disposition binds the FindingID to worker Activity, Git
  evidence, test evidence, and the exact C2 subject claimed to address it.
- `independent_content_replacement` is legal whenever the slice/integration task
  is not closed/landed and has no live finding-bearing round: before any round,
  during a partial or all-submitted clean round, after clean finalize, after UAT,
  or after publication. It requires a distinct replacement, material-work
  Activity, and explicit drift/change reason. A live partial round is invalidated
  without claiming complete inventories; finalized review/UAT/publication remain
  immutable history but lose current eligibility.

Omitting a finding/evidence from `address_findings`, attempting that mode before
all three submissions, using independent replacement while a finding belongs to
the current subject/current live round,
binding evidence to a different replacement, or attempting C1 -> C1 writes
nothing.

The exact rework state table is total:

| Old subject state | Legal mode | Preserved terminal state | Batch changes before C2 swap |
|---|---|---|---|
| no round | independent | none | no review branch to terminalize |
| partial/all-submitted clean live round | independent | already-closed groups/axes and already-ended `submitted_clean` assignments remain byte-identical | close only open groups/axes as `invalidated_by_independent_subject_replacement`, end only live assignments, close round with that outcome |
| live finding-bearing round with fewer than three submissions | neither | submitted inventory remains live | reject until all three inventories submit |
| all three submitted with findings | address_findings | already-terminal clean axes/assignments remain byte-identical | close open findings/groups/finding-bearing axes, resolve dual-parent edges, close round `REVISE_REPLACED` |
| clean finalized, post-UAT, or post-publication | independent | finalized ACCEPT round, UAT decision, and publication events remain immutable history | invalidate/remove only their current eligibility relations and coverage; no second terminal disposition |
| slice closed or integration landed | neither | terminal artifact | reject with no writes |

The `address_findings` batch closes submitted findings as
`addressed_by_candidate_rework`; their severity groups close as
`superseded_by_candidate_rework`; BLOCKER edges to both group and reviewed task
are resolved; only still-open finding-bearing axis tasks close
`superseded_by_candidate_rework`; already-terminal clean axes/assignments are
unchanged; the round closes `REVISE_REPLACED`; and all old
dependency/current-round edges resolve. The batch then creates C2, binds every
finding disposition and fix evidence to C2, and swaps the exact
`current-candidate` relationship. Independent replacement follows the table,
invalidates any current UAT/publication/close authorization, installs C2, and
swaps the relation; it never rewrites a prior terminal task/disposition or emits
`addressed_by_candidate_rework`.
The old candidate and finding graph remain immutable history. A successor round
can start only on C2 and later relates itself to the terminal predecessor; the
same subject can never be the successor of a finding-bearing round.

`IntegrationCandidateSetSubject` is the final multi-repository deliverable. Each
epoch has one authoritative integration task governed by its IMPL_PLAN. Initial
`integration candidate-set --expected none` is legal only with no current set or
live integration round. It creates exactly one immutable
`RepositoryCandidate{RepositoryID,CommitOID,TreeDigest,ExpectedRemoteRef,
ExpectedOldOID}` per repository and atomically attaches the canonical unique set
through `current-integration-candidate`.

Every later merge, rebase, fix, repository-set, commit, tree, or ref change uses
typed `integration rework`, never `candidate-set`. One conditional batch checks
the expected current set and requires a distinct new set. It uses the same closed
reason sum and total algorithm as slice rework. Finding-addressing replacement
waits for all three inventories and binds every finding/group/BLOCKER edge to
complete Activity/Git/test evidence for the new set. Independent replacement is
allowed in every nonterminal no-finding state in the total table and records that
partial inventories were invalidated, not completed. Every open axis, live assignment,
round, and dependency receives its mode-specific terminal state before the exact
current-set swap. The batch also invalidates current
Implementation-UAT and publication-evidence relations, creates the new immutable
set, and swaps `current-integration-candidate`. Finalized review/UAT/publication
evidence remains historical but ineligible. A successor review can start only on
the new set, so no obsolete finding or `current-round` can strand the integration
task. Per-slice reviews prove slices; only a clean-reviewed and currently
accepted integration set is eligible to publish and land.

Plan and Implementation UAT are closed protected decisions, not comment
conventions. They distinguish ordinary interview interaction from actionable
feedback and from questions deliberately held for a later gate. The CLI-only MVP
uses explicitly **protocol-reported** harness results: they are durable, typed,
one-use, and attributable, but are not claimed to cryptographically authenticate
the human. Native/in-process attestation remains a deferred native-tool feature.
