```go
type SemanticOperationID string
type RuntimeContract struct { /* unexported validated profile */ }

type RuntimeBinding[In, Out any] interface { runtimeBinding() }
// NativeCall | ParentMediated | SemanticInstruction | Unsupported

type OperationDescriptor[In, Out any] struct { /* opaque */ }
type EffectDescriptor[In, Out any] struct { /* opaque */ }

type RuntimeBindingContribution interface { runtimeBindingContribution() }

func BindCapability[In, Out any](
    capability Capability[In, Out],
    versions CapabilityVersionRange,
    binding CapabilityRuntimeBinding[In, Out],
) (RuntimeBindingContribution, error)

func NewRuntimeContract(
    id RuntimeContractID,
    harness HarnessID,
    versions VersionConstraint,
    core CoreRuntimeBindings,
    capabilities ...RuntimeBindingContribution,
) (RuntimeContract, error)
func (c RuntimeContract) ID() RuntimeContractID
func (c RuntimeContract) Harness() HarnessID
func (c RuntimeContract) Supports(version HostVersion) bool
func LookupOperationBinding[In, Out any](
    c RuntimeContract,
    operation OperationDescriptor[In, Out],
) (RuntimeBinding[In, Out], error)
func LookupEffectBinding[In, Out any](
    c RuntimeContract,
    effect EffectDescriptor[In, Out],
) (RuntimeBinding[In, Out], error)
func LookupCapabilityBinding[In, Out any](
    c RuntimeContract,
    capability Capability[In, Out],
) (CapabilityRuntimeBinding[In, Out], error)
```

Values and all three descriptor families are opaque and constructor-validated.
#40 owns this build-time composition
API; external packages can bind a #41 descriptor without modifying #40, but can
never supply a dynamic name or untyped payload. Construction requires exactly
one binding for every requested operation/effect/capability, validates the
descriptor codec/semantics/effect set and version intersection, and rejects
duplicate or conflicting contributions. All lookup surfaces return explicit
errors for invalid, missing, duplicate, unbound, or incompatible descriptors;
there is no meaningful zero binding. Native bindings include exact
request/result schemas and fixtures. Missing bindings, unsupported required
operations, or host versions outside the range fail; no similarly named call is
guessed. `SemanticOperationID` is the protocol identity and is never reused as
Provenance's idempotency `OperationID`; operations, effects, and capability
descriptors cross separate typed lookup surfaces without conversion. Named
string IDs remain metadata exposed by descriptors, never direct lookup operands,
design:
so Go's assignable untyped-literal rule cannot bypass descriptor validation.

Initial evidence baselines are explicitly pinned:

| Harness | Initial point range | Contract rule |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | exactly CLI 2.1.210 plus pinned official/source schemas | use only Agent/SendMessage/TaskStop-era primitives where exact; never emit removed TeamCreate/TeamDelete semantics |
| OpenCode | exactly CLI 1.17.18 plus official docs/pinned source | use documented skill/task/question surfaces; unverified persistent message/follow-up/wait/close names are mediated, semantic, or unsupported |
| Codex | exactly CLI 0.144.1 plus official docs/pinned source | bind only exact exposed collaboration/request-input functions and preserve logical continuity across replacement agents |

Updating a host requires a new RuntimeContractID or reviewed range expansion.
“Current” and `latest` are not compatibility policies.

## 7. Native activation contracts

Installation mechanics do not enter the semantic IR:

```go
type ActivationContractID string
type ActivationContract struct { /* unexported validated profile */ }
type ComponentDescriptor struct { /* opaque validated harness/extension identity */ }
type ActivationStrategy interface { activationStrategy() }
// NativePlugin | DirectFile | NativePluginPendingTrust

func NewActivationContract(
    id ActivationContractID,
    harness HarnessID,
    hostVersions VersionConstraint,
    versionProbe CommandSchema,
    components ExhaustiveComponentActivations,
) (ActivationContract, error)
func NativePluginActivation(manager NativeManagerContract) ActivationStrategy
func DirectFileActivation(bundle artifact.Bundle, destination Destination) ActivationStrategy
func PendingTrustActivation(manager NativeManagerContract, review NativeTrustReview) ActivationStrategy
func (c ActivationContract) ID() ActivationContractID
func (c ActivationContract) Harness() HarnessID
func LookupComponentActivation(
    c ActivationContract,
    component ComponentDescriptor,
) (ComponentActivation, error)
```

`ExhaustiveComponentActivations` is opaque and created only by a validating
constructor that requires exactly one skills, agents, and hooks component—no
public mutable map. Each component contains exactly one closed activation
strategy, so invalid nullable marketplace/plugin/config combinations cannot be
constructed. Lookup accepts only an opaque validated component descriptor and
returns an explicit error for wrong harness, missing/unbound, or incompatible
components; raw ExtensionID/string literals and zero activations are not a
public surface. Native strategies carry exact package identity plus
install/list/update/remove schemas. Neutral upstream issue #48 owns package
`artifact`: opaque `Bundle`, `BundleID`, manifest/entry/digest codecs,
constructors, canonical validation, and the `go:embed`/`fs.FS` boundary. #48 is
an independent foundation with no #38 dependency. Construction walks the input
FS, requires an exact declared file set, snapshots every validated byte into
private immutable storage, derives `BundleID` as a domain-separated SHA-256 over
the canonical path/type/mode/content-digest manifest, and discards the backing
FS. `Open` accepts only declared leaves and returns a fresh read-only handle;
source mutation after construction cannot affect the bundle. Each
#24/#27/#45 target constructs and publishes an `artifact.Bundle`; #39 consumes
that upstream type and adds only activation destination/semantics. Paths must be
clean relative paths; traversal, absolute/duplicate leaves, parent/leaf
symlinks, and unsupported entries are constructor errors. The installed CLI
carries every DirectFile payload and never resolves from cwd/source checkout.
The private nine-cell table stores no mutable installation state itself.

Target artifacts do not carry an ActivationContractID. Each target publishes a
stable target/component identity, its opaque `artifact.Bundle`, and the
RuntimeContractID under which it was compiled. #39's private catalog consumes
those target descriptors
and binds each one to an ActivationContractID and closed strategy. This keeps
target generation upstream of activation without duplicating metadata.

The initial public activation matrix is:

| Harness | Skills | Agents | Harness hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `pasture-skills` native plugin | `pasture-agents` native plugin | `pasture-hooks` native plugin |
| OpenCode | whole directories at `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/` | files at `~/.config/opencode/agent/<role>.md` | embedded `pasture-hooks.ts` at `~/.config/opencode/plugin/pasture-hooks.ts` through pinned auto-discovery |
| Codex | `pasture-skills` native plugin | `~/.codex/agents/pasture_*.toml` | `pasture-hooks` native plugin, followed by native user trust review |

The Go values remain opaque implementation metadata. Cross-language consumers
use one public #39-owned command contract:

```text
pasture install apply-selection \
  --desired <selection-file> \
  --source <installer|home-manager> \
  --json

pasture install apply-cell \
  --harness <claude-code|opencode|codex> \
  --extension <skills|agents|hooks> \
  --enabled=<true|false> \
  --source <installer|home-manager> \
  --json
```

The command never accepts the persisted installer config directly. Both callers
produce this immutable desired-state document:

```yaml
schema: pasture.install.effective-selection/v1
cells:
  claude-code: {skills: false, agents: false, hooks: false}
  opencode:     {skills: false, agents: false, hooks: false}
  codex:        {skills: false, agents: false, hooks: false}
```

The schema requires exactly three harness IDs and exactly three extension IDs,
with no defaults or unknown keys. `apply-selection` validates the desired
`EffectiveSelection`, loads the separate typed installation inventory, inspects
any cell requiring reconciliation, constructs the ordered plan in memory, and
uses private `executeOrdinaryCell` steps or one selection-aware
`executeClaudeLegacyGroup`. The public context-free `apply-cell` is a separate
single-cell remediation surface and is never recursively called by the group.
The selection command writes no preference, rollback data, authorization, lock,
or cross-cell transaction record.

Cell and action order is canonical and public:

```text
claude-code.skills, claude-code.agents, claude-code.hooks,
opencode.skills, opencode.agents, opencode.hooks,
codex.skills, codex.agents, codex.hooks
```

For each cell in that order, desired true plans an idempotent inspect/ensure.
Desired false plans inspect/remove only when the inventory says Pasture manages
that cell or its last confirmed state is installed or unknown; a
never-recorded false cell plans nothing. Thus an uninstall failure remains
retryable on an ordinary TUI or Home Manager rerun even though the desired
preference is already false. Both commands emit one
transient `pasture.install.apply-result/v1` document. Each planned row contains
`index`, typed harness/extension IDs, `operation`, `management`, and exactly one
status from `completed`, `failed`, `unattempted`, `managed_declaratively`, or
`installed_pending_trust`. At most one row is `failed`; all later planned rows
requiring command execution are `unattempted`. Home Manager declarative rows are
live inspections, not command attempts, and remain `managed_declaratively`
regardless of an earlier/later native failure. `installed_pending_trust` is a successful Codex-hook install,
not a claim that the hook is active. A result contains `ok`, `source`, and rows
in canonical order. A pre-plan decode/schema/version failure emits
`pasture.install.apply-error/v1` with stage, optional cell/action, cause,
impact, and exact remediation. An action failure emits the same diagnostic in
its failed row, exits nonzero, and still returns the complete ordered result.
Neither result schema is accepted as future state; the narrower inventory below
is the only persisted operational evidence.

For `source=installer`, the TUI caller alone loads preferences, presents and
saves the user's confirmed global choices, derives the immutable effective
selection (`harness && extension`), then invokes `apply-selection`; the command
itself never reads or writes preferences and applies both native-managed and
direct-file cells from that document. `apply-cell` is only an explicit
single-cell remediation and also never changes preferences. For
`source=home-manager`, Nix renders desired effective cells from the current
generation's per-harness options. Aura #8 orders declarative link realization
before the Pasture native activation node. `apply-selection` first live-inspects every
declarative row, then acts only on `NativeManaged` cells in canonical native-
subset order;
`DirectFile` cells are explicitly skipped as `managed_declaratively` because
Home Manager adds/removes their links from the pinned Pasture generated tree.
`apply-cell --source home-manager` rejects a direct-file mutation with that
exact declarative remedy instead of writing the path. Thus both callers share
one transition schema and native-manager implementation without pretending they
own the same filesystem cells.

Every diagnostic carries one closed tagged `Remediation` rather than assuming
one command fits every executor: `ApplyCell{argv}` for ordinary installer-owned
cells, `ApplySelection{desired_document, source}`/`RerunInstaller` for the Claude
selection-wide group, `RerunHomeManager{option,path}` for declarative rows, or
`ManualNativeTrust{instructions}` for Codex trust, or
`ManualRepair{inspection,instructions}` for irreducible state-save/external
ambiguity. The selected remedy must be
executable for the failing state; Claude legacy errors never print the public
`apply-cell` command that is required to reject them.

### 7.1 Confirmed installation inventory and DirectFile safety

Preferences remain in `~/.config/pasture/config.yaml`. Confirmed operational
state for #39-mutated cells lives separately at
`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pasture/installations.yaml` under the closed
schema `pasture.install.state/v1`. Every recorded cell contains typed
harness/extension/strategy/source IDs, artifact identity and version, whether
the matching pre-existing component was created/updated by Pasture or merely
observed externally, the exact native selector/scope or managed file leaves,
the last confirmed observation (`installed`, `absent`, or `unknown`), native
trust disposition where applicable, and the last action/outcome/diagnostic.
Installer-owned direct-file leaves retain their expected type, content digest,
mode, and Pasture-created parent-directory evidence. Removed cells remain as
absent tombstones, so status can answer what was installed, whether uninstall
completed, and what remains. Home Manager DirectFile links are not inventory
members: Nix owns their declarative lifecycle, while `status --source
home-manager --desired ...` performs a read-only exact inspection and reports
`managed_declaratively` without persisting a second ownership/controller model.

Artifact/state content digests use the closed `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` codec
over exact file bytes; manifest leaves are canonical lexicographic relative
paths with explicit octal permission bits. State YAML rejects unknown/duplicate
cells and serializes the public nine-cell order. A state file symlink or unsafe
type is rejected before action, and no secret is stored. State save uses an
ordinary same-directory create-exclusive temporary file, flush, rename, and
directory flush. The live process best-effort removes only the exact temp it
successfully created. A crash orphan is never discovered, deleted, reused, or
treated as recovery input by a later run; the committed state file alone is
authoritative and a later save uses a fresh random temp. This deliberately avoids
a temp ledger, marker protocol, or crash-recovery subsystem.

When upgrading from a release with no inventory, every matching pre-existing
native component or direct file is observed as external and is never adopted or
removed by Pasture, even after a desired-true then desired-false cycle. The sole
exception is the exact published user-scoped Claude v0.0.4 monolith: the frozen
compatibility table recognizes that one legacy identity as an approved migration
candidate. Unknown or near-match scope/version/identity remains external and
causes zero mutation. Mixed simultaneous installer/Home Manager control of a
native cell is unsupported and reported with the recorded source and exact
single-controller repair; no concurrency protocol is introduced.

The inventory changes only after a postcondition is live-confirmed or after a
normal action failure is live-inspected. It stores last confirmed cell/managed-
leaf identity plus the last action/outcome/diagnostic; it does not persist a
prior/attempted manifest, per-entry step, nonce, temp path, or pending desired
state before action. Installer DirectFile replacement uses one create-exclusive
same-parent temp regular file per leaf, writes/flushes/closes it, and atomically
renames it to the sibling destination. The current process best-effort removes
only the exact temp it created if the operation fails before rename. After a
crash, a later run never scans, cleans, reuses, or infers ownership from temp
names; it live-inspects only final manifest destinations and creates a fresh
temp. Orphans are harmless external siblings and may be reported if explicitly
encountered, but are never automatic recovery state.

If an external action succeeds but inventory save fails, the command reports
that exact ambiguity and live state; the next run conservatively treats a
matching unrecorded component as external rather than adopting it. This is the
intentional cost of the user-approved simple model. State decode/write failures
identify path/stage/impact/fix and stop before the next mutation. Concurrent
invocations remain unsupported rather than coordinated. There is no background
worker, rollback, compensation, pending-work queue, temp ownership marker, or
same/newer-binary crash reconciliation.

`pasture install status [--json]` combines the inventory with live typed native
probes and exact-file inspection. It reports desired, recorded, observed, source,
trust, remaining managed targets, and the exact tagged executable remediation. A
normal `pasture install` run performs the same inspection before retrying an
installed/unknown false cell; users need not reconstruct the old preference.

Installer DirectFile reconciliation is exact and conservative:

- an absent manifest leaf is created as a regular file with its declared mode;
- a recorded Pasture-managed leaf may update only when its current
  `(type, digest, mode)` exactly matches the prior record;
- an identical pre-existing unrecorded leaf satisfies desired true but is
  recorded as external and is never removed by Pasture;
- a differing file, directory, dangling/foreign symlink, parent symlink, unsafe
  path, permission failure, or modified managed leaf is an actionable conflict,
  never an implicit overwrite;
- removal unlinks only recorded Pasture-managed leaves whose
  `(type, digest, mode)` still exactly matches, removes only recorded
  Pasture-created directories that are empty, and
  preserves every sibling; and
- Home Manager DirectFile links are reported `managed_declaratively` by
  read-only desired/live inspection and remain outside persistent inventory,
  while native actions invoked by Home Manager update the factual native-cell
  inventory.

The initial contract is a point contract for exact output `1.17.18`. All three

### 7.4 Codex 0.144.1 activation

Aura issue #9 owns marketplace `aura-plugins` and its aggregate manifests.
Release automation advances a reviewed moving Git ref `pasture-stable`; it does
so only after target outputs, #39 activation fixtures, and Aura repository gates
pass at named revisions. This is intentionally not an immutable SHA: Codex's
native `marketplace upgrade` resolves the configured ref again, so later releases
can update without Pasture replacing the marketplace or maintaining update
state. The activation contract pins the source, ref name, host point version,
and expected plugin versions/schemas.

#39 proves only a synthetic moved-ref activation fixture: two local marketplace
commits and a temporary ref exercise native upgrade/re-add without publishing a
real Aura ref. Aura #9 alone owns the executable promotion surface:

```text

  --pasture-revision <reviewed-sha> \
  --aura-revision <reviewed-sha> \
  --expected-old <sha|absent> \
  --remote <git-remote>
```

Its tests use a temporary bare Git remote. Each target, activation, manifest,
Aura-gate, or requested-revision mismatch independently fails with the old ref
unchanged. The all-green case advances exactly to the reviewed Aura commit and
then proves Codex upgrade/re-add loads that promoted revision.
Immediately before publication the command resolves the remote ref again and
uses one guarded push equivalent to
`--force-with-lease=refs/heads/pasture-stable:<expected-old>`; `absent` requires
the ref not to exist. A racing publisher therefore causes a nonzero actionable
failure without overwriting its advance. Fixtures cover first creation,
matching update, stale expected-old, a race between final check and push, and
idempotent retry of the already-promoted revision.

```text
[codex, --version]
[codex, plugin, marketplace, list, --json]
[codex, plugin, marketplace, add, dayvidpham/aura-plugins,
  --ref, pasture-stable, --json]
[codex, plugin, marketplace, upgrade, aura-plugins, --json]
[codex, plugin, list, --marketplace, aura-plugins, --available, --json]
```

The selector is always `PLUGIN@MARKETPLACE`; no command also passes

marketplace upgrade, `plugin add` intentionally rematerializes an already
selected plugin from the refreshed marketplace.

The 0.144.1 JSON codecs remain frozen:

```text

MarketplaceListResult { marketplaces: [{ name, root, marketplaceSource? }] }
MarketplaceUpgradeResult { selectedMarketplaces, upgradedRoots, errors:
  [{ marketplaceName, message }] }

```

`alreadyAdded:true` is success only when the subsequent list proves the same
source and `pasture-stable` ref. A targeted upgrade must select
`aura-plugins`; any `errors` entry is failure, while an empty `upgradedRoots` is
a valid no-change result. After add, the selector must be in `installed` with
`installed:true`, `enabled:true`, the expected marketplace, and matching
PluginAddResult. `PluginAddResult.version` proves the expected selected release;
an optional list-row version, when present, must agree. Missing version on other
valid rows is not an error. After remove it must be absent from installed rows;
remaining in available rows is valid. Unknown discriminants, missing required
fields, and incompatible selected values fail the contract.

Installing Codex hooks does not imply execution. Unmanaged hooks remain pending
Codex's native trust review; the result status is `installed_pending_trust` and
the UI/Home Manager message tells the user to review them through Codex's native
hooks UI. Pasture never writes private hook-trust hashes or claims the hooks are
active before native approval.

Generated packages carry immutable target/component identities,
RuntimeContractIDs, and point host ranges. #39 binds those descriptors to its
ActivationContractIDs. Every action probes the public host version first. A
manifest host constraint appears only when the native schema documents it.
These compatibility checks remain stateless contract validation. Their observed
postconditions feed the separate installation inventory; they are not inferred
from it.

## 9. Provenance authoritative task journal

### 9.1 Generic envelope and caller-owned payloads

```go
type EventID int64
type EventKind string
type OperationID string
type EventContextKind string

type EventContext struct { /* opaque validated kind + encoded identity */ }

func TaskContext(TaskID) (EventContext, error)
func ActivityContext(ActivityID) (EventContext, error)
func AgentContext(AgentID) (EventContext, error)
func GitContext(GitOID) (EventContext, error)

type ExtensionContextID interface {
    ~string
    EventContextDomain() EventContextKind
}

type ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID ExtensionContextID] struct { /* opaque */ }
func DefineExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    validate func(ID) error,
) (ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID], error)
func ExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    descriptor ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID],
    id ID,
) (EventContext, error)

type TaskEvent struct {
    ID          EventID
    TaskID      TaskID
    Kind        EventKind
    ActorID     AgentID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    OperationID OperationID
    Contexts    []EventContext
    Payload     json.RawMessage
}
```

EventID is database-generated and exposed once. Queries order ascending by
`(RecordedAt, EventID)` and expose both fields. EventKind/context kinds are
validated namespaced types. `EventContext` has no exported raw `ID string`
constructor or fields. Built-in constructors require the corresponding typed ID
and reject zero or structurally invalid values. Caller namespaces define a named
string-backed ID implementing the marker method plus a typed descriptor and
validator. `DefineExtensionContext` derives its kind from the named ID type's
marker; it takes no duplicate kind argument, rejects every reserved Provenance
built-in kind (task/activity/agent/git), and requires a valid caller-owned
namespace. At value construction the ID's reported kind must still equal the
descriptor kind. Built-in `string` cannot satisfy `ExtensionContextID`, so
`DefineExtensionContext[string]` is a compile failure. Only the internal
persistence codec serializes context kind plus text.

Provenance validates the generic envelope, identity syntax/references, contexts,
and payload well-formedness. It does not import or globally register Pasture
codecs. Pasture constructs an opaque typed event definition, validates its
`pasture.*` payload, encodes it, and passes it across this boundary.

Secondary contexts supplied during event creation commit atomically. A later
context attachment, when necessary, is itself a journalled mutation. Typed
constructors prevent TaskID, ActivityID, GitOID, and caller-defined IDs from
being accidentally interchanged even though storage uses a common textual
encoding. Contexts have set semantics: construction, persistence, operation
canonicalization, and query output deduplicate and sort by
`(EventContextKind, canonical encoded identity)`. Association-row insertion
order is never observable. Each context edge stores the EventID that attached
it (the original event for initial contexts, the journalled attachment event for
later contexts). Snapshot queries include only edges whose attachment EventID is
at or below SnapshotMaxEventID, so a later attachment cannot change an in-flight
filtered traversal.

### 9.2 Atomic command API and durable idempotency

```go
type MutationContext struct {
    ActorID     AgentID
    OperationID OperationID
    Command     CommandDigest // opaque caller-domain canonical command identity
}

Apply(ctx context.Context, mc MutationContext, command Mutation) (MutationResult, error)

type CommittedOperationLookup interface {
    LookupCommitted(
        ctx context.Context,
        operation OperationID,
        expectedActor AgentID,
        expectedCommand CommandDigest,
    ) (CommittedOperationResult, error)
}

// CommittedOperationResult is exactly one of Absent or Committed. Reuse of an
// OperationID with a different actor or command returns a typed Conflict error.
```

Provenance #4 owns the TaskEvent envelope, context storage, ordering/query APIs,
and internal append/schema primitives. It exposes no raw event-append bypass,
registered production migration, or baseline side effect. Its persistence tests
activate the schema explicitly in isolated test databases. Provenance #5
exclusively owns the public command/result table, `Apply`, and the read-only
`LookupCommitted` surface. `Apply` records the supplied opaque CommandDigest and
the independently derived generic MutationDigest. On an already-committed
OperationID it compares actor plus CommandDigest and returns the stored result
before interpreting a newly supplied mutation; on first execution it also stores
the actual mutation digest for audit. The trusted typed adapter owns command-
identity construction—Provenance does not decode caller semantics.

Lookup performs no mutation: `Absent` means the
operation has never committed; exact actor/command agreement returns the stored
result map and EventIDs even when the initiating assignment has since ended; and
any OperationID reuse with different actor/command identity returns `Conflict`.
It never executes an absent command or revalidates current authority. #5 also
owns the production migration that installs the #4
schema, writes baselines, and activates atomic journaling. #4 and #5 ship in one
Provenance release tag after both merge; there is no released state in which a
database has a writable journal but non-journalled mutators.

The closed command family covers task lifecycle, typed relationships, labels,
comments, responsibility/supervision assignments, explicit attribution,
task-linked Activity start/end,
later event-context attachment, and a generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation for
caller-validated material events that change no current task state. Provenance
commits domain row(s), any required attribution, TaskEvent row(s), contexts, and
canonical operation/result through one `internal/sqlite` connection/transaction.
Pasture does not compose a fake transaction across separate tracker/audit
connections.

#5 also owns opaque `ConditionalMutationBatch` construction. It is a closed,
extension-safe declarative composition of existing generic mutations plus
caller-validated opaque material events; it is not a callback, raw SQL, or an
untyped predicate escape hatch. Its built-in preconditions cover exact task
kind/status/owner, exact active/ended assignment and active-slot set, typed
relationship presence/absence and exact incoming/outgoing typed set equality,
exact task revision plus immutable subject task/current-subject relationships, exact immutable EventID/task/kind/context
evidence, and absence of unresolved blocked-by children. Canonical typed local
handles let later batch mutations reference earlier allocated tasks/assignments;
the result returns their stable ID map. Preconditions are
rechecked inside the same SQLite transaction immediately before the ordered
mutations. Domain rows, assignment transitions, relationships, events,
contexts, attribution, and operation result all commit or roll back together.
Pasture #43 compiles review/transition/closure policy into these generic
preconditions and mutations; Provenance never decodes a `pasture.*` payload.

OperationID is durable idempotency identity. Same ID plus byte-equivalent
canonical command/actor returns the originally committed result/events after
close/reopen or concurrent retry. Same ID with different actor/command fails.
The operation row rolls back with the mutation, so there is no pending state.

Pre-1.0 direct mutator paths migrate to Apply or compatibility wrappers that
require MutationContext and delegate to the same transaction. No exported bypass
may mutate a task/graph without its event.

### 9.3 Responsibility CAS and cumulative attribution

```go
type TransferTaskResponsibility struct {
    Task          TaskID
    ExpectedOwner OwnerExpectation // OwnerIs(agent) or OwnerIsUnassigned()
    ExpectedAssignment AssignmentExpectation
    Successor     OptionalAssignmentDraft // absent means become unassigned
    Reason        string
}
```

The expected owner and current responsibility assignment are compared inside
the same transaction. Transfer ends the predecessor, optionally creates the
successor, changes Owner, and records attribution/events atomically. Two
distinct concurrent transitions have one winner; the stale loser changes no
owner, assignment, attribution, operation, or event row and receives an
actionable conflict. `ChangeTaskOwner` is only a compatibility constructor that
delegates to this transition when its full assignment expectation is supplied;
otherwise it rejects once the assignment migration is active.
This protects task assignment only; it is unrelated to plugin-installation
concurrency and introduces no installer transaction/CAS mechanism.

Task.Owner is role-neutral current responsibility. Prior/new material contributors retain
idempotent `attributed_to` edges. Administrative actors are not attributed merely
for changing a label/status; attribution occurs only for responsibility or
material contribution commands. Owner events record expected/previous/new owner,
actor, reason, OperationID, time, and EventID.

### 9.4 Activities, relationships, and graph events

`StartTaskActivity` and `EndTaskActivity` carry AssignmentID, ActivityID,
phase/stage, notes, and contexts; TaskID and AgentID are derived and validated
from that exact active assignment. Activity row state, task linkage, material event,
required attribution, and contexts commit together. Duration Activities remain
distinct from instantaneous transitions and do not encode structured changes in
notes. The state machine is closed: start requires a new ActivityID, existing
task, and actor resolved from the supplied active assignment; a new OperationID
cannot start an existing Activity. End requires the same linked task/agent and
an active Activity. End-before-start, wrong task/agent, invalid transitions, and
a second end under a new OperationID write nothing; same-OperationID retries
return the original result, and concurrent ends have one winner.

Task relationships accept TaskID targets. Attribution accepts AgentID. Activity
links accept ActivityID. A relationship involving two tasks writes a task-local
event to each timeline in one transaction, sharing OperationID and receiving
distinct EventIDs. Blocked-by cycle validation, edge persistence, and both events
share the same consistency boundary.

### 9.5 Current state and legacy migration

Current task/graph/Activity tables remain authoritative. The journal explains
all post-migration changes; it is not used to rebuild pre-journal state. When #5
activates the coordinated production migration, existing tasks each receive one
idempotent `provenance.migration.baseline` event containing the then-current
status/phase/owner and source schema version. In that same exclusive transaction,
every nonterminal assigned task receives a deterministic migration-time active
owner-responsibility assignment; every terminal assigned task receives an ended
migration assignment and has current Owner cleared; unassigned tasks receive no
assignment. Assignment IDs derive from schema version plus TaskID. Provenance
uses only its generic `provenance.role.legacy-owner` and
`provenance.slot.owner-responsibility`; it never invents a Pasture role. The task
baseline EventID is the active assignment's StartEventID at migration RecordedAt.
For a terminal legacy owner, a second ordered migration-time assignment-ended
event supplies EndEventID at the same RecordedAt; both are explicitly snapshot
events and never claim historical start/end time.

Legacy owner text that is not already a registered AgentID maps to a
deterministically registered `legacy-owner/<sha256>` SoftwareAgent whose payload
retains the original text; invalid/duplicate registration fails the entire
migration. Attribution and migration events retain that mapped owner but are
explicitly labeled snapshot/baseline evidence, never fabricated historical
start/end times. The post-migration invariant holds for every task kind: a
nonterminal nonnil Owner has exactly one matching active responsibility
assignment, while every terminal task has nil Owner and no active responsibility.
This marks the historical-completeness boundary.

The #5 production migration executes schema activation and every baseline row
inside one exclusive SQLite migration transaction. A fault after any number of
rows rolls back the schema marker, journal tables/changes, and all baselines;
reopen then performs the same migration from the pre-migration database. Empty
databases, every assigned/unassigned × terminal/nonterminal × task-kind case,
unmappable legacy owner text, repeat startup, and concurrent startup are explicit
fixtures. Baseline ActorID is the registered migrator; an absent legacy owner is
never fabricated.

Before any `pasture task` protocol/review/slice command is enabled against the
coordinated Provenance schema, the #43/application startup coordinator calls
#14's read-only legacy-assignment extraction API. #14 never invokes #43. #43
classifies only tasks carrying a reserved, versioned Pasture protocol kind and
validates the exact required topology before building one idempotent
`NormalizeLegacyAssignmentRoles` conditional batch. That batch performs
same-owner responsibility transfers from generic legacy-owner assignments to
the typed role/slot, preserving predecessor, attribution, and ordered events.
There is no separate normalization marker, table, task, snapshot, or event: the
authoritative completion predicate is a deterministic post-batch requery proving
that every eligible active assignment already has its exact mapped role/slot and
no eligible generic assignment remains. An empty eligible set therefore succeeds
without inventing a marker host.

The v1 mapping is closed and exhaustive:

| Persisted Pasture kind/topology | Normalized active owner role |
|---|---|
| REQUEST, ELICIT, URD, PROPOSAL, Plan-UAT, HANDOFF, and their FOLLOWUP forms | RoleArchitect |
| plan-review round/container | RoleArchitect |
| IMPL_PLAN, integration task, Implementation-UAT, landing container, supervisor-created follow-up epic | RoleSupervisor |
| implementation slice and explicitly typed Pasture implementation leaf | RoleWorker |
| code-review round/container and eager severity group | RoleSupervisor |
| implementation-review finding leaf | RoleWorker |
| review axis with exact correctness relationship | RoleReviewerCorrectness |
| review axis with exact test-quality relationship | RoleReviewerTestQuality |
| review axis with exact elegance relationship | RoleReviewerElegance |

Terminal or unassigned eligible tasks require no active transfer but are still
validated. A reserved known kind with missing/conflicting topology, or an
unknown future reserved Pasture kind, fails the entire batch and leaves the
database unchanged. Ordinary Provenance tasks and leaves without a reserved Pasture
kind are explicitly ineligible: their generic legacy-owner role remains valid,
they do not enter the batch, and they cannot block Pasture activation. Fault/
restart repeats the extraction and state-derived normalization safely. Protocol
commands remain unavailable until the deterministic post-batch inspection
succeeds.

Pasture #43 owns a closed, typed import command; #14 supplies only extraction and
adapter plumbing:

```go
type LegacyAuditRowID string
type LegacySchemaVersion string
type ImportLegacyAuditRow struct { /* unexported validated row */ }

func NewImportLegacyAuditRow(
    schema LegacySchemaVersion,
    row LegacyAuditRowID,
    actor LegacyActorRef,
    recordedAt time.Time,
    definition LegacyEventDefinition,
    contexts []LegacyContext,
    tasks []provenance.TaskID,
) (ImportLegacyAuditRow, error)
```

The constructor validates the source schema/row identity, maps the legacy kind
and payload through a typed #43-owned definition, validates every context, drops
duplicate task IDs, sorts the remaining typed IDs, and resolves the actor before
any Apply call. Unknown kinds/payload shapes or invalid/empty task fan-out fail
without writes. Pasture migrates actual legacy audit history without deleting or
updating source rows; pre/post byte hashes of the legacy tables are acceptance
evidence:

- #14's finite coordinator collects all rows and `context_edges`, validates the
  full extraction, sorts rows by `(recorded time, legacy row ID)`, and imports
  serially, stopping at the first failure so equal-time EventID allocation is
  deterministic across repeat/reopen;
- resolve every unique task ID represented by epoch/slice/review/follow-up task
  contexts;
- invoke one #43-owned `ImportLegacyAuditRow` command containing the source
  schema, legacy row ID, actor mapping, original time/payload, all contexts, and
  the sorted unique TaskIDs; it validates/encodes typed payloads and delegates
  once to Provenance's generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation;
- have that single Apply operation create one canonical TaskEvent per `(legacy
  schema, legacy event ID, resolved TaskID)`, attaching all of that row's legacy
  contexts;
- give the batch one stable migration OperationID derived from `(legacy schema,
  legacy event ID)` and deterministic event insert order `(legacy recorded time,
  legacy row ID, task ID)`; and
- enforce the compound legacy identity uniquely so repeat migration/reopen cannot
  duplicate events.

`ImportLegacyAuditRow` is atomic: every event/context/operation result for one
legacy row commits or none does. A retry with the same source identity returns
the canonical batch result and EventIDs; conflicting source content fails. An
injected failure after the first event rolls back the full row batch. This is a
finite schema import, not an event-sourcing or runtime transaction subsystem.

Migrated real events preserve their original RecordedAt and mapped AgentID. When
an old actor cannot be resolved, the migration uses an explicitly registered
`pasture-legacy-migrator` SoftwareAgent and retains the original actor text in the
typed migration payload; ActorID is never silently nil or forged. Baseline events
use a registered `provenance-migrator` SoftwareAgent and migration time. Stable
OperationIDs derive from the typed legacy-row identity through a documented
constructor, not from process-local counters.

Thus one old row linked to several tasks appears on every relevant task timeline
without losing its many-to-many contexts. #14 owns the separately named,
read-only `pasture legacy-audit event list` API for non-task legacy rows and its
raw source-identity/actor-text/context tests; #43 never folds those rows into a
task timeline. After auto-migration,
`pasture task timeline TASK-ID` reads canonical Provenance TaskEvents only; it
does not perform an unstable runtime merge with rows lacking EventID.

subcommand exists. Every successful status, including `already_recorded` and a

Git then SQLite remains deliberately sequential, not transactional. Git failure
writes no evidence. If Git succeeds but Apply fails, retry of the same

attempted. Partial multi-repository success is reported and resumed without
rollback. Cross-process JSON/native callers can
request only the full composite operation, so fabricated intermediate results
cannot cross the runtime boundary. #43 does not import #46; #40/application
composition imports both. Any candidate/tree/ref change invalidates the evidence
and requires new integration review/UAT. Generic `task close` rejects slice,
review, and protocol-container kinds. The exact slice CLI includes RoundID,

and three accepted review EventIDs and lowers the §5.3 predicate and mutations

supported schema IDs/ranges, and a canonical definition digest. Generated
artifacts embed their exact requirement. The runtime probes once before the
first task mutation and fails before writes on a missing command, malformed
probe, adjacent/unsupported version, digest mismatch, or semantic contract
mismatch; this covers separately upgraded generated packages and binaries.

Review/UAT/skill/git evidence uses typed Pasture event definitions. Protected
review definitions cannot pass generic `event record`. `event list` accepts a
versioned `pasture.task.event-query/v1`: TaskIDs are ORed, EventKinds are ORed,
typed contexts are ORed, and the non-empty dimensions combine with AND. The
first page captures `SnapshotMaxEventID`; every later page carries it plus an
exclusive `(AfterRecordedAt, AfterEventID)` cursor and ignores later inserts.
Rows are canonical stored envelopes ordered ascending by `(RecordedAt, EventID)`.
Concurrent/backdated appends therefore appear only in a new traversal, never
duplicate or disappear within the current snapshot.

`timeline TASK-ID` uses `pasture.task.timeline-query/v1` with the same snapshot
watermark and exclusive key. Its tagged rows are `point_event` or
`activity_interval`. A point sorts by `(RecordedAt, EventID)`; an interval sorts
by `(StartedAt, StartEventID)`, carries nullable EndedAt/EndEventID plus both

leaf policy and atomically ends that leaf's responsibility assignment. CLI

## Axis: Test Quality

### Summary

PROPOSAL-2 demonstrates thorough test awareness. The proposal identifies all tests that need modification, correctly categorizes which tests to delete vs. rename vs. rewrite, and the BDD acceptance criteria are verifiable. There are no BLOCKER-level test quality concerns.

### Findings

**IMPORTANT-1: TestGenerateSkill_ContainsSections comment and nesting assertion need updating (not just the fixture)**

The proposal's Step 7 ("Update tests") mentions rewriting the two-pass tests but does not call out that `TestGenerateSkill_ContainsSections` (line 122-129 of skills_test.go) has a code comment referencing `## Protocol Context` and a nesting assertion that checks H3 sections are nested under the H1 role heading. The proposal's unified template renames `## Protocol Context (generated from schema.xml)` to `## Protocol Reference`, moving reference tables from the top of the generated block to the bottom.

The existing assertion logic will still PASS because it only checks H3-under-H1 nesting (not H3-under-H2-under-H1), but the code comment at line 123 ("The skill template places all H3 sections inside ## Protocol Context") becomes misleading. The implementation should update this comment.

Additionally, `skills.yaml` fixtures only check `must_contain_headers` at H3 level. The proposal introduces new H3 sections that move from body to inside markers (e.g., "### Role Behaviors (Given/When/Then/Should Not)" when body behaviors are merged). The fixture should add entries for these new H3 headers to verify the section reordering actually happened. Without this, the test could pass even if the body sections accidentally remain outside BEGIN/END.

Severity: IMPORTANT (not blocking -- existing tests will not regress, but test coverage has a gap for the primary invariant change).

**IMPORTANT-2: No test for the "body content is now INSIDE markers" invariant**

The proposal's key change is moving body content from after-END to inside-BEGIN/END. The renamed `TestGenerateSkill_BodyInsideMarkers` test is described but its assertions are underspecified. The proposal says "assert body content is between BEGIN/END" but does not specify HOW to assert this. The current `TestTwoPass_HeaderRegionUnchangedByBodyPass` (line 574-581) explicitly asserts body appears AFTER END -- the rewrite must invert this to assert body appears BEFORE END. The implementation should:
1. Extract the text between BEGIN and END markers
2. Assert that body section titles ("Test Section"), preamble text, and recipe content all appear within that region
3. Assert that nothing except trailing whitespace/newlines appears after END

This is the single most important test change in the proposal and it needs a concrete assertion plan.

Severity: IMPORTANT (the test direction is correct but underspecified; a careful implementer would catch this, but an explicit assertion plan would prevent regression).

**MINOR-1: TestGenerateSkill_BodyPreserved may need adjustment for "no body spec" semantics change**

`TestGenerateSkill_BodyPreserved` (line 412-429) uses `suppressBodySpec` and then asserts that hand-authored content after END is preserved. Under the unified template, if there is NO SkillBody entry, the behavior should be identical -- hand-authored content after END stays. However, line 428 asserts `assertIsNestedUnder(t, doc, src, "Worker Agent", "Constraints (Given/When/Then/Should Not)")` which implicitly tests that generated H3 constraints are nested under the H1 heading. This remains valid under the new template since constraints stay as H3 but move to the "Protocol Reference" section. No code change needed here, just noting it.

**MINOR-2: skills.yaml fixtures should add body-derived sections to must_contain**

The current `must_contain` entries in skills.yaml (e.g., "Workflows", "Startup Sequence") test content that was always in the header. After the merge, body content (preamble text, section titles from SkillBody) will also be inside the generated region. The fixture should expand `must_contain` to include body-derived strings like the preamble link text or section titles (e.g., "Ride the Wave" for worker, "Creating Vertical Slices" for supervisor). This ensures the unified template is actually rendering body content, not silently dropping it.

**MINOR-3: TestReplaceBodyRegion deletion count**

The proposal says "Delete 4 TestReplaceBodyRegion_* tests" but markers_test.go has exactly 4 TestReplaceBodyRegion tests (EndMarkerPresent, MissingEndMarker, PreservesHeader, EmptyBody). This is correct. No issue, just confirming the count.

### End-User Alignment

1. **Who are the end-users?** AI agents reading SKILL.md files during task execution.
2. **What would end-users want?** Content organized logically: identity first, then operational guidance, then reference material.
3. **How would this affect them?** Better comprehension order -- agents encounter "what to do" before "where to look things up."
4. **Are there implementation gaps?** The two IMPORTANT findings identify test coverage gaps that should be addressed during implementation, but neither blocks the proposal's approach.
5. **Does MVP scope make sense?** Yes -- the proposal correctly scopes to codegen changes only without touching runtime behavior.
6. **Is validation checklist complete?** Yes, all 10 items in the validation checklist are verifiable and cover the key invariants.

### Verdict

The proposal's test strategy is sound. The test modifications are correctly categorized (delete ReplaceBodyRegion tests, rename/rewrite two-pass tests, preserve idempotency test). The two IMPORTANT findings are gaps in the proposal's test specification detail, not problems with the approach. A competent implementer can fill these gaps from the BDD acceptance criteria.

What: StartReview resolves a governing assignment from the subject plus its graph ancestors, but lowers supplemental edges, the start event, and round authority against the exact reviewed subject. The governed composition reference fence admits only the parent-assignment ancestry and newly allocated children, not that descendant subject.
Why: A legitimate governing supervisor assignment on a plan/epoch ancestor is accepted by Pasture preflight but then rejected by the composed allocator before any batch can commit, so the command does not preserve the existing ancestor-scoped authority contract.
Where: pasture/internal/tasks/epoch_assignment_service.go:254-284 builds the subject/ancestor scope; pasture/internal/tasks/epoch_review_commands.go:263-274 and :295-304 emit effects on subjectTask, and :333-375 submit them with resolution.id as the composed parent.
When: The subject has no direct governing-supervisor assignment and the unique active supervisor assignment is on an allowed plan or epoch ancestor, which assignmentScope explicitly supports.
Impact: Valid plan or implementation reviews fail with an unrelated-supplement/reference-authority error instead of allocating their required 4/13 children, preventing normal workflow progress even though exact parent authority was resolved.
Fix: Add a typed, atomically validated reviewed-subject reference to the governed composition contract, allowing only the exact subject/related edges under the resolved parent and epoch, or otherwise make StartReview require/resolve a direct subject assignment with an explicit contract change; add an ancestor-assignment production integration test and never widen the fence to arbitrary task IDs.

description:
Found while fixing the load-flaky engine suite (aura-plugins-ay4yn, commit 3cc3ca7).

internal/engine/slice.go:65 gives SliceSubWorkflow a 2s window to receive its start_slice signal. On timeout the slice FAILS with 'enqueued but never started' - a real, user-visible failure, deliberately not a fabricated success.

The engine flake was caused by that production deadline being missed because 30 concurrent senders were contending on the DBOS SQLite notification store. The correct fix serialized the test's signal delivery, since a 10ms retry storm is not a realistic caller. But that removed the only coverage exercising slow signal delivery against this deadline, so the production characteristic is now untested.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY THEORETICAL: the lifecycle architecture under design writes to the same shared SQLite file on every tool call. With subagent orchestration the concurrent-writer count is genuinely high - the exact condition that starved this deadline. The pivot can reintroduce it in production as spurious slice failures.

Needs:
  1. A deliberate test that delays start-signal delivery and asserts the failure is honest and diagnosable, rather than relying on incidental contention to exercise it.
  2. A decision on whether 2s is defensible once hook writes share the database, or whether the deadline should be configurable, budget-derived, or replaced by an explicit readiness handshake.
  3. A measured write-contention budget for the shared SQLite file covering engine, audit and hook ingress together.

Route to the architecture work: the latency and write-budget sections must account for hook ingress competing with engine signal delivery.
notes: Residual outer-budget retry and contention policy tracked in GitHub #57.
title: Production 2s start-signal deadline is sensitive to shared-SQLite write contention

VOTE: ACCEPT

## Axis: Elegance and Complexity Matching (Round 6)

### Summary

PROPOSAL-2, with all accumulated resolutions (R1-R11, OperationalDetail on WorkflowStage, explicit truncation, H2 heading hierarchy), achieves an elegant design that is proportional to the inherent complexity of the problem. The 2-to-1 simplification is the right move, the data model extension is minimal, and the post-processing truncation is clean. No findings.

### 1. Unified Template: Proportional Design

The old system had a combinatorial structure: 2 context types x 2 render functions x 2 templates x 2 marker operations x 2 pipeline passes. The new system collapses each axis to 1. This is a genuine simplification, not just consolidation — it eliminates the coordination cost between two passes that had to agree on marker semantics.

The unified template section ordering (identity -> behaviors -> constraints -> workflows -> operational sections -> procedures -> reference tables) follows the agent's cognitive path: "who am I, what rules do I follow, what is my workflow, how do I execute it, where do I look things up." This ordering is derived from how agents actually consume the document, not from how the data happens to be organized in Go structs. That is the right design direction.

The template will be larger than either predecessor (it renders the union of both), but this is inherent — there is no way to render all content in one pass with less template surface area. The complexity of the template is proportional to the number of distinct content types it renders, and adding a content type means adding one template block, not modifying a coordination protocol between two templates.

### 2. OperationalDetail on WorkflowStage: Right Abstraction Level

Round 5 Reviewer A correctly identified that the proposal needed to commit to a concrete association mechanism for R9/R10/R11. The resolution (comment "RESOLVING R5 Reviewer A IMPORTANTs", 2026-03-26 10:01) chose Option 3: add `OperationalDetail string` to `WorkflowStage`.

This is the most elegant of the three options, for reasons my R5 review already detailed:

- **Colocation matches rendering.** The template iterates `Workflow.Stages` and, for each stage, renders `Actions`, then `OperationalDetail`, then per-stage figure. One range loop, no lookups.
- **No synchronization.** Options 1 and 2 both require maintaining a cross-reference between two data structures in two different files. Option 3 has one struct in one place.
- **Proportional change.** One `string` field on an existing struct. The struct already has `Actions`, `ExitConditions` — `OperationalDetail` is the same category of per-stage data.

The scoping is also correct: only stage-specific operational detail (the three "Ride the Wave" subsections) migrates into WorkflowStage. Role-level operational sections ("First Steps", "Exploration", "Critical Rules") remain as standalone ProseSections. This avoids overloading WorkflowStage with content that does not belong to a specific stage.

One could argue for `OperationalDetail []ProseSection` instead of `string` to allow structured subsections within the operational detail. But examining the actual data (specs_data_body.go lines 112-168), each stage's operational detail is a flat markdown string (bullet lists, code blocks). There is no subsection nesting within a stage's operational detail. A `string` is the right type today. If stage-level subsections emerge in the future, the field can be upgraded — but adding premature structure now would be over-engineering.

### 3. Explicit Truncation: Clean Post-Processing

The truncation approach (4 lines after `ReplaceMarkerRegion` to strip stale content after END) is clean for two reasons:

1. **It does not pollute ReplaceMarkerRegion.** The marker replacement function is general-purpose — it serves files that DO have legitimate hand-authored content after END (e.g., skill files without a SkillBody entry, or non-codegen files). Adding a "truncate after END" option to ReplaceMarkerRegion would couple a general function to an epoch-specific migration concern.

2. **It is self-eliminating.** After the first generation, there is no content after END, so the truncation is a no-op on subsequent runs. The 4 lines remain in the code as a safety guard, but they do nothing in steady state. This is the right tradeoff — removing the guard later would require proving that no future code path could introduce after-END content, which is not worth the effort for 4 lines.

The alternative — modifying `ReplaceMarkerRegion` to accept a `dropSuffix` parameter — would be technically equivalent but conceptually worse. It would add a parameter to a general function that is only meaningful for one specific use case.

### 4. Unified skillContext: Well-Scoped

The proposed `skillContext` struct (from Step 1) is the union of `skillHeaderContext` and `skillBodyContext`. Examining the fields:

- All `skillHeaderContext` fields are preserved (Role, Commands, Constraints, etc.)
- The `skillBodyContext` fields are decomposed: `Body *SkillBody` becomes `Preamble string`, `Sections []ProseSection`, `Recipes []RecipeBlock`, `BodyBehaviors []BehaviorSpec`
- `FiguresDir string` is dropped from the context (it was "reserved for future use" in `skillBodyContext` and is only needed during figure loading, not during template execution)

The decomposition of `SkillBody` into individual fields is the right call. Passing a nested `*SkillBody` to the template would require `{{ .Body.Preamble }}` in the template, while individual fields allow `{{ .Preamble }}`. This is a minor readability improvement, but more importantly it means the template does not need to check for a nil `Body` pointer — absent body content is simply empty strings/nil slices, which Go templates handle naturally with `{{ if .Preamble }}`.

The proposal's observation about keeping `Behaviors` and `BodyBehaviors` as separate fields (preserving provenance) vs merging into a single `[]BehaviorSpec` is a worker-level implementation decision, not a design issue. Either approach works. The R4 review correctly identified this as non-blocking.

### 5. Sub-Skill Treatment: Consistent

The proposal specifies `skill_sub.go.tmpl` as an analogous unified template for sub-skills with SkillBody entries. Currently three sub-skills have body content: `supervisor-plan-tasks`, `supervisor-spawn-worker`, `impl-review`. They get the same treatment as main skills: body content inside markers, single-pass rendering, truncation of stale content after END.

The `skillSubFigureContext` struct (for sub-skills WITHOUT body content) remains unchanged — it already renders everything inside markers. The proposal only adds a new template for the sub-skill-with-body case, which is the minimal change.

This is consistent and proportional. There is no attempt to create a single uber-template for both skills and sub-skills (which would be over-engineering given their different marker handling: dropPrefix=true for skills, dropPrefix=false for sub-skills).

### 6. No Premature Abstractions, No Missing Necessary Ones

The design does not introduce:
- A plugin system for template ordering (premature)
- A generic "content block" abstraction that unifies ProseSection, RecipeBlock, and BehaviorSpec (premature — they have different rendering semantics)
- A "migration framework" for the one-time truncation (premature — 4 lines suffice)

The design does introduce:
- One new struct field (`OperationalDetail string` on `WorkflowStage`) — necessary for R9/R10/R11
- One merged context type (`skillContext`) — necessary for the single-pass pipeline
- One unified template (`skill.go.tmpl`) — necessary for logical content flow
- One post-processing step (truncation) — necessary for R3 revised

Each addition serves a specific, stated requirement. None are speculative.

### End-User Alignment

1. **Who are the end-users?** AI agents reading SKILL.md files during task execution.
2. **What would they want?** A logical reading flow: understand identity and rules first, then workflows and operations, with lookup tables at the end.
3. **How would this affect them?** Positive: the unified template produces a document that matches the agent's cognitive workflow. Negative: none — the change is internal to codegen.
4. **Implementation gaps?** None on the elegance axis. All design decisions are concrete and implementable.
5. **MVP scope?** Proportional. The proposal does exactly what the user requested (R1-R11) without gold-plating.
6. **Validation checklist?** Complete. The stale item ("hand-authored content after END preserved") was corrected in the migration fix comment.

### Relationship to Prior Rounds

- R4 (ACCEPT): Section ordering, R3 simplification, R7 clarification, complexity proportionality — all remain valid.
- R5 (ACCEPT): OperationalDetail on WorkflowStage recommendation — adopted and correctly specified in the proposal's resolution comment.
- This round (R6) confirms that the accumulated resolutions maintain the elegance properties identified in R4 and R5, and the two IMPORTANTs from R5 Reviewer A are resolved without introducing new complexity.

### Conclusion

The design is proportional, the abstractions are at the right level, and the API is what we know we will need. ACCEPT.

## Problem Space

**Axes:** single-pass vs two-pass, template composition, marker region ownership

The current codegen pipeline has a wrong architectural assumption: it treats the BEGIN/END marker region as 'header only' and puts body content after the END marker via a second pass (ReplaceBodyRegion). This means generated body content lands in the hand-authored zone, conflating generated and hand-authored content.

**Has-a relationships:**
- A SKILL.md file HAS-A YAML frontmatter (above BEGIN), HAS-A generated region (BEGIN...END), HAS-A hand-authored section (after END)
- The generated region HAS-A protocol context (header) and HAS-A operational body (sections, recipes, behaviors)

**Is-a relationships:** None relevant — this is a structural fix, not a type hierarchy change.

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Option | Pros | Cons | Decision |
|--------|------|------|----------|
| A: Merge templates into one .tmpl | Single template, simple render | Giant template, mixes concerns | REJECT |
| B: Concatenate rendered strings before END marker | Templates stay focused, minimal template changes, only pipeline logic changes | Slightly more code in render function | **ACCEPT** |
| C: Nest body template as sub-template | Clean composition | text/template nesting complexity, context type changes | REJECT |

## Approach: Concatenate Before END Marker (Option B)

### Step 1: Modify header template — remove END marker

Remove the `<!-- END GENERATED FROM aura schema -->` line from the last line of `skill_header.go.tmpl` (line 191). The template now produces: YAML frontmatter + `# heading` + BEGIN marker + protocol context content (NO END marker).

Similarly, remove the END marker from `skill_sub_figure.go.tmpl` (line 13).

### Step 2: New unified render function

Create `renderSkillContent(roleID, figuresDir)` in skills.go that:

1. Calls `renderHeader(roleID, figuresDir)` → header content (without END marker)
2. If `SkillBodySpecs[roleID]` exists, calls `renderBody(body, figuresDir)` → body content
3. Concatenates: header + body + END marker line + newline
4. Returns the complete generated block (includes BEGIN and END markers)

Similarly for sub-skills: `renderSubSkillContent(commandID, figuresDir)` that:
1. Calls `renderSubSkillHeader(commandID, figuresDir)` → sub-skill header (without END)
2. If `SkillBodySpecs[dirKey]` exists, renders body
3. Concatenates: header + body + END marker + newline

### Step 3: Simplify GenerateSkill and GenerateSubSkill

Remove the two-pass logic (Pass 2: Body). Each function becomes:

1. Read file
2. Init markers if needed
3. Call the unified render function
4. Call ReplaceMarkerRegion (single pass)
5. Validate structure
6. Diff + write

### Step 4: Delete ReplaceBodyRegion

Remove `ReplaceBodyRegion` from markers.go. Remove its tests from markers_test.go.

### Step 5: Update tests

- `TestTwoPass_HeaderRegionUnchangedByBodyPass`: Rewrite to verify body content is INSIDE markers (not after END)
- `TestTwoPass_NoBodySpec_HeaderOnly`: Keep — still valid (no body = just header in markers)
- `TestGenerateSkill_BodyPreserved`: This tests hand-authored content after END is preserved — still valid
- `TestReplaceBodyRegion_*`: Delete (4 tests)
- `TestGenerateIdempotent`: Must pass after regenerating on-disk files

### Step 6: Regenerate on-disk SKILL.md files

Run `go generate ./internal/codegen/...` to regenerate all SKILL.md files. The body content that was after END will now be inside the markers. Hand-authored content that was after END (where there is no SkillBody) remains after END.

### Step 7: Update CONTRIBUTING.md

Update the pipeline description to reflect single-pass architecture.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `internal/codegen/templates/skill_header.go.tmpl` | Remove END marker from last line |
| `internal/codegen/templates/skill_sub_figure.go.tmpl` | Remove END marker from last line |
| `internal/codegen/skills.go` | Add `renderSkillContent`, `renderSubSkillContent`; simplify `GenerateSkill`, `GenerateSubSkill` (remove Pass 2) |
| `internal/codegen/markers.go` | Delete `ReplaceBodyRegion` function |
| `internal/codegen/markers_test.go` | Delete 4 `TestReplaceBodyRegion_*` tests |
| `internal/codegen/skills_test.go` | Update `TestTwoPass_HeaderRegionUnchangedByBodyPass` to assert body inside markers; keep other tests |
| `internal/codegen/specs.go` | Update `SkillBody` doc comment (no longer 'rendered via ReplaceBodyRegion') |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | Update pipeline description |
| `skills/*/SKILL.md` (7 files) | Regenerated — body content moves inside markers |

## Validation Checklist

- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/codegen/...` passes
- [ ] `go generate ./internal/codegen/...` produces zero diff
- [ ] TestGenerateIdempotent passes
- [ ] YAML frontmatter stays above BEGIN marker
- [ ] Hand-authored content after END is preserved
- [ ] Body content (preamble, sections, recipes, behaviors) is inside BEGIN...END
- [ ] ReplaceBodyRegion deleted from markers.go
- [ ] No references to ReplaceBodyRegion remain

## BDD Acceptance Criteria

**Given** a SKILL.md with BEGIN/END markers and a SkillBody entry **when** GenerateSkill runs **then** all body content (preamble, sections, recipes) appears between BEGIN and END markers **should not** place any generated content after the END marker

**Given** a SKILL.md with BEGIN/END markers and NO SkillBody entry **when** GenerateSkill runs **then** only header content appears between BEGIN and END markers, and content after END is preserved verbatim **should not** modify content after the END marker

**Given** the on-disk SKILL.md files **when** `go generate ./internal/codegen/...` runs **then** output is identical to on-disk (zero diff) **should not** produce any diff

**Given** a sub-skill SKILL.md with a SkillBody entry **when** GenerateSubSkill runs **then** body content appears inside markers and the hand-authored H1 prefix is preserved **should not** drop the prefix or place body after END

# Round 2 current-wave remediation

Resolve the complete Round 2 reviewer-mini wave as one compact HumanEpochService vertical. Preserve the public EpochHumanService inputs, results, decision kinds, state model, Provenance API/schema, fresh-command validation, exact-retry behavior, and ordinary CLI contract. Do not add another store, ledger, FSM, revision token, snapshot API, acceptance corpus, or generalized testing framework.

## Exclusive ownership

- internal/tasks/epoch_human_service.go
- internal/tasks/epoch_human_service_test.go

No other production, contract, policy, material-event, Provenance, provadapter, CLI/runtime, generated, YAML, or aura-plugins-8cus8 acceptance file may change. The implementation should remain a small replay-draft correction plus consolidation of focused tests and helpers.

## Production correction

The committed-operation branch of RecordPlanUAT remains before current proposal-state eligibility. Build one complete candidate draft from every caller-controlled field and submit it to the existing commit and Provenance Apply replay authority.

For planUATReplayDraft:

1. If the stored operation is deferred_by_afk and the requested outcome is also deferred_by_afk, reconstruct the candidate with the stored canonical ModeEntry. This preserves exact replay after interaction mode later changes and still makes changed interactions, feedback, or HeldQuestions part of canonical conflict identity.
2. If the requested outcome is deferred_by_afk but the stored operation is accepted or changes_requested, read the live InteractionModeCursor. A currently AFK epoch supplies its exact live ModeEntry to PolicySet.DraftPlanUAT, yielding the complete valid deferred candidate.
3. For requested accepted or changes_requested outcomes, retain normal mode lowering and all existing PolicySet validation.
4. Route the candidate returned by replay construction directly through commit. Do not rebuild it in a second helper and do not run current subject eligibility before Apply for an already committed OperationID.
5. Provenance Apply remains the sole replay authority. A valid changed candidate returns provenance.ErrOperationConflict with zero writes. Exact input returns the original result and exact original conditions. Invalid fresh input retains its existing actionable PolicySet or service validation.

The implementation may remove planUATDraftWithoutSubjectState if direct use of the constructed replay candidate makes it redundant. No public type, state value, evidence family, condition encoding, result slot, or command behavior changes.

## One shared real-store footprint and oracle

Replace subjectFootprint and humanDecisionFootprint count-only usage with one compact normalized helper used only by these representative tests. It accepts the relevant isolated-store task IDs and operation IDs and captures complete persisted identity, not only counts:

- complete decision rows for all seven human decision kinds, including JournalID, task, kind, effective actor, producing OperationID, RecordedAt, and canonical payload;
- complete evidence rows for epoch subject references, plan/candidate current-state evidence, prerequisite references, and pasture.epoch.precondition.v1, including JournalID, task, kind, actor, operation, digest, and payload;
- complete real Activity values;
- complete typed task-event rows for the relevant epoch, proposal, candidate, and alternate binding subjects, including exact JournalID/EventID, task, kind, actor, operation, timestamp, and payload;
- each relevant task status from the production tracker;
- LookupCommitted for every named winner, loser, retry, and rejected operation, normalized as presence/kind, anchor, exact ordered EmittedEvents, and exact ordered ResultSlots with Slot, ProducedJournalID, Kind, TaskID, and ActivityID;
- decoded pasture.epoch.precondition.v1 conditionSnapshot values, preserving order, ConditionKind, FactKind, exactly one DecisionKind or EvidenceKind selector arm, exact task, and AssertedJournalID.

Normalize copied slices and pointer values so equality compares values rather than aliases. Query every page needed for the selected isolated-store scopes. A no-delta assertion compares the complete normalized footprint. A committed-operation assertion requires the exact decision/activity/event slots and requires DecisionResult.EventIDs to equal LookupCommitted.EmittedEvents element-for-element. An absent-operation assertion requires LookupCommitted to report no committed result and no effect family or status delta.

Use one table-driven non-mode oracle for Plan UAT, Ratify, Implementation UAT, and Land. For each row assert:

- returned OperationID, Epoch, DecisionID, ActorID, ActivityID, and every EventID;
- the real Activity has the selected human, expected phase, StageComplete, and expected operation notes;
- the canonical persisted decision envelope has exact epoch, subject, actor, kind, decision ID, and branch payload;
- required current-state, prerequisite, and precondition evidence has exact references and canonical payload;
- EpochDecisionRecorded is reference-only and binds the exact epoch, subject, actor, decision, kind, and activity without decision detail;
- committed ResultSlots and EmittedEvents are exact;
- immediate exact retry returns Replayed with identical DecisionID, ActivityID, and every EventID and a complete no-delta footprint.

## Representative test consolidation

Keep coverage focused and table-driven:

1. Add a two-row same-operation Plan UAT conflict table whose original outcome is accepted or changes_requested. Set the live mode to AFK, retry the same OperationID as deferred_by_afk with one stable HeldQuestion, require errors.Is(err, provenance.ErrOperationConflict), and require a complete no-delta footprint. This is the production regression for aura-plugins-mmlkz.
2. Through production RecordPlanUAT, persist deferred_by_afk with HeldQuestions, decode the canonical decision to prove exact retention, then retry the same operation with one HeldQuestions field changed. Require provenance.ErrOperationConflict, no duplicate committed result, and complete no delta. Keep existing accepted and changes_requested HeldQuestions validation coverage; do not duplicate all replay axes.
3. Convert the stale accepted to changes_requested/deferred old-ratify test into one two-row table using the complete oracle. Require typed actionable validation rejection and no operation, result, effect, or task-status delta.
4. Keep exactly the two deterministic stale barrier rows: Plan UAT versus Ratify and Implementation UAT versus Land. Require errors.Is(err, provenance.ErrConditionFailed), one exact complete winner, absent loser operation/result, no loser decision/evidence/activity/event/status partial, and expected winner status. Keep the injected rejecting-barrier row and prove complete unchanged state.
5. Keep one wrong Ratify binding and one wrong Land binding. Require errors.As to the Pasture structured validation error with CategoryValidation and binding-specific actionable text, absent rejected operation/result, and a complete zero-write/status footprint across both source and target subjects.
6. Commit Ratify and Land, capture their exact results, committed slots/events, decoded conditions, and complete footprint, close the file-backed tracker, construct a fresh production service, and replay. Require Replayed, identity equality for every result field and EventID, exact selector arms and AssertedJournalIDs, exact committed slots/events, restored task status, and no persisted delta.

Do not add the exhaustive actor matrix, every one-axis replay mutation, every outcome/prerequisite permutation, multi-contender schedules, rework races, built-binary tests, process adapter tests, digests of unrelated tables, or YAML mutation cases. Those remain exclusively assigned to aura-plugins-8cus8.

## Finding mapping

- aura-plugins-mmlkz: live AFK-derived ModeEntry builds a valid accepted/changes_requested to deferred candidate before Apply conflict authority.
- aura-plugins-2f3ap, aura-plugins-pfzj0, aura-plugins-0c52f: one shared non-mode authority/result-slot/event oracle and exact immediate retry no-delta proof.
- aura-plugins-m8g1i, aura-plugins-1r1cm, aura-plugins-0c52f: Ratify/Land reopen replay compares all bindings, exact EventIDs, condition selector arms/JournalIDs, status, committed slots, and complete no delta.
- aura-plugins-dvq49, aura-plugins-jm44q, aura-plugins-0x6a0, aura-plugins-0c52f: complete footprint for stale barrier losers, rejecting barrier, and typed wrong-binding zero-write rejection.
- aura-plugins-sk7ps: production deferred HeldQuestions persistence plus changed-field same-operation conflict and no delta.

## Acceptance criteria

Given an accepted or changes_requested Plan UAT operation and a live AFK interaction mode, when the same OperationID is retried with a valid deferred_by_afk payload, then the service derives the exact live AFK ModeEntry, builds the complete candidate, reaches Provenance Apply, returns provenance.ErrOperationConflict, and changes no persisted row, operation result, or task status; should not fail earlier from a synthetic normal-mode candidate or current subject eligibility.

description:
The supervisor implemented EpochWorkflow correctly but did not implement the two child workflow classes required by the ratified PROPOSAL-11 design.

## Critical Gap
workflow.py contains only EpochWorkflow. The following child workflow classes are entirely absent:
- SliceWorkflow: Represents a single P9_SLICE; runs concurrently with other SliceWorkflows
- ReviewPhaseWorkflow: Represents P10_CODE_REVIEW for a slice; receives ReviewAxis votes via signals

## Requirements (from PROPOSAL-11 / HANDOFF aura-plugins-6zro)

### SliceWorkflow
- @workflow.defn class
- Accepts SliceInput (dataclass with epoch_id, slice_id, phase_spec: SerializablePhaseSpec)
- Executes slice activities (or stubs with R12 docstrings for now)
- Returns SliceResult (or PhaseResult)
- Fail-fast: EpochWorkflow must use workflow.wait(slice_handles, return_when=FIRST_EXCEPTION)
  and cancel remaining handles on first exception

### ReviewPhaseWorkflow
- @workflow.defn class
- Accepts ReviewInput (dataclass)
- @workflow.signal handler for ReviewVoteSignal (axis: ReviewAxis)
- wait_condition until all 3 ReviewAxis members have voted (using ReviewAxis enum members)
- try/except ApplicationError around child_handle.signal() calls (race protection)
- Returns PhaseResult with vote_result

### EpochWorkflow Integration
- P9_SLICE: start N SliceWorkflow children, then workflow.wait(handles, return_when=FIRST_EXCEPTION)
  On first exception: cancel pending handles, propagate
- P10_CODE_REVIEW: start ReviewPhaseWorkflow children; wait for completion

## Acceptance Criteria
- SliceWorkflow class exists with @workflow.defn
- ReviewPhaseWorkflow class exists with @workflow.defn + @workflow.signal for ReviewVoteSignal
- EpochWorkflow.p9_slice_phase() uses workflow.wait(FIRST_EXCEPTION) + cancel-on-failure
- EpochWorkflow.p10_review_phase() starts ReviewPhaseWorkflow child(ren) and waits
- asyncio.gather NEVER used — only workflow.wait()
- Tests: fail-fast behavior verified; signal routing verified
- No regressions in existing tests
