description:
## Finding

In interfaces.py, three dict fields are unparameterized:

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class DataPart:
        data: dict   # should be dict[str, Any]

    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class ToolCall:
        tool_input: dict   # should be dict[str, Any]
        tool_output: dict | None = None   # should be dict[str, Any] | None

Using bare dict (without type parameters) is less precise than dict[str, Any] and loses information for type checkers. PEP 585 (Python 3.9+) and the existing use of from __future__ import annotations means dict[str, Any] is available without runtime overhead.

## Context
The rest of the codebase consistently parameterizes dicts: dict[str, ConstraintSpec], dict[PhaseId, PhaseSpec], dict[str, str] (context field on ConstraintViolation), etc. The unparameterized dict is the exception, not the rule.

## Fix
    from typing import Any
    data: dict[str, Any]
    tool_input: dict[str, Any]
    tool_output: dict[str, Any] | None = None

Note: dict[str, Any] is not actually more restrictive than Any — it still allows nested Any values. But it communicates the intent (string keys) and satisfies type checkers.
title: SLICE-4-REVIEW-C-1-F1: DataPart.data and ToolCall dict fields unparameterized — should be dict[str, Any]

description: File: internal/release/runner.go:225-226 (and git.go GitRollback :115). The comment says the tag-failure path rolls back 'the in-repo commit + file writes', but GitRollback only runs 'git tag -d <tag>' + 'git checkout -- .'. After step 7 commit succeeds, 'git checkout -- .' is a no-op against the new commit, so the release commit is NOT undone. Fix: reword the comment to 'delete the tag and reset the working tree; the release commit is intentionally left (matches aura-release)', or, if undoing the commit IS desired, add 'git reset --soft HEAD~1' to GitRollback. ## Evidence
`internal/lifecycle/waist/event_test.go:156-160` constructs one Identity with kind IdentitySession, native name session_id, and value value, then supplies that exact value-bearing object twice. The required verifier branch is a duplicate kind/native-name pair, not merely a duplicate complete Identity value.

## Impact
This test passes against an implementation that rejects only an identical (kind, nativeName, value) triple but accepts two different values for the same native field. Such an implementation would emit two semantic identities for one declared field and leave the duplicate-pair contract unprotected; the six negative branches are therefore not independently pinned.

## Minimal fix
Construct two separately built identities with the same IdentitySession/session_id pair but different values (for example value-1 and value-2), pass both to NewEvent, and assert the typed validation error and duplicate-pair What text. The existing exact-duplicate case may remain as an additional check, but it must not be the sole duplicate oracle.

- Q 'dedup uniqueness realization': R1 user asked 'What is even audit_events? Why was epoch_id dropped? We have no users... pre-alpha... rebuilding the table entirely is no problem. What is context_edges?' Educated (audit_events = forensic event log; context_edges = BCNF event-context attachment holding epoch as EpochContext since v3->v4 rebuild dropped epoch_id). Would the time-disambiguated UUID solve this?' then 'What does step_seq represent currently? Doesn't it basically represent that inner integer-incremented loop?'. Change dedup key basis from positional (step_seq) to SEMANTIC natural-key-per-event-type. description:
In test_gen_schema.py::TestDiffOutput::test_diff_shown_when_file_exists_and_changed (line 112), the assertion checks for '---' OR '+++' OR 'diff' in the captured stdout. The production code (gen_schema.py line 1740) prints a header 'f"\n--- Unified diff for {output} ---"' which contains '---' regardless of the actual diff content. While the production code only prints this header when diff_lines is non-empty (line 1739), the test assertion would trivially pass by matching the header string even if the body difflib.unified_diff output was absent.

Similarly, test_diff_output_is_unified_format accepts 'No changes' as valid, which means a test run where content is already identical would not catch a missing diff.

Remediation: The test should assert that at least one line starts with '+' or '-' (excluding the '---'/'+++' file headers), confirming that real changed lines are present in the diff body. This makes the test verify the substance of the diff, not just the header.
title: S2-B1-MINOR: Diff presence test relies on wrapper header string, not actual diff content

## Finding
The stale-barrier tests observe ErrConditionFailed and call assertCommittedAbsent for the losing operation, but they do not prove that the loser contributed no decision, evidence, Activity, task event, or status partial. The complete footprint is captured, yet the assertions only require the after-footprint to differ from before because the winner committed; a loser partial can therefore be hidden by the expected winner delta. assertCompleteOperation also checks only a minimal winner shape. The same gap remains in the mode row and both UAT-versus-terminal rows.

## Exact fix
Keep the deterministic barrier cases, but assert the full normalized before/after delta by producer: after the expected winner is accounted for, every loser-operation decision/evidence/event/result/slot is absent, no loser Activity exists, and no task status changed except the winner\x27s expected transition. Assert the winner through the shared complete oracle, including exact emitted events/result slots/conditions. Apply this to TestEpochHumanServiceRejectsStaleModeConditionAfterBarrier and both TestEpochHumanServiceUATTerminalBarrierRows; retain the rejecting-barrier full unchanged-footprint assertion.

## Why blocker
The acceptance contract requires stale-barrier no-partials. A passing typed error plus absent LookupCommitted result does not prove atomic loser rejection across all persisted effect families.
title: BLOCKER: Barrier rows do not prove loser zero-partial footprints

# Rename Aura* SAs → Pasture* SAs

The six Temporal search attributes upserted by every pastured workflow are
named `AuraEpochId`, `AuraPhase`, `AuraRole`, `AuraStatus`, `AuraDomain`,
`AuraLastEventType`. These predate the split into the Pasture Go-port
toolkit and refer to the parent 'Aura protocol' family.

Now that Pasture is the going-forward toolkit and the binaries / docs /
DB tables are all `pasture*`-named, the SA wire names should match.

## Go-side scope (this task)

- `internal/temporal/search_attributes.go`: 6 constant string values
  - SAEpochID    'AuraEpochId'       → 'PastureEpochId'
  - SAPhase      'AuraPhase'         → 'PasturePhase'
  - SARole       'AuraRole'          → 'PastureRole'
  - SAStatus     'AuraStatus'        → 'PastureStatus'
  - SADomain     'AuraDomain'        → 'PastureDomain'
  - SALastEventType 'AuraLastEventType' → 'PastureLastEventType'
- Go variable names (SAEpochID, etc.) stay the same — only the wire
  strings change.
- `scripts/smoke/temporal-e2e.sh`: 2 grep lines that assert on the SA names.
- `AGENTS.md` 'Why Temporal' section: 5 references in tables + prose.
- Parent repo `docs/architecture.md`: 5 references in the SA table.
- Parent repo `docs/ROADMAP.md`: 3 references in §0 and §3c.

## Backward compatibility

- This feature branch (`feat--pasture--initial-golang-port`) has never been
  deployed. No production workflows carry `Aura*` SAs that would be orphaned.
- The Go-side rename is a pure mechanical wire-name swap; no migration logic
  needed.

## Open question — Python aura_protocol side

`scripts/aura_protocol/workflow.py` defines the same SAs with the same
`Aura*` wire names. If the Python implementation is still actively running
workflows somewhere, renaming Go only forks the two implementations at the
wire-name level. Resolution options:

  1. Rename both Python AND Go to `Pasture*` — proper cleanup. Touches
     `scripts/aura_protocol/workflow.py` + `tests/test_workflow.py` (10+
     assertions) + any other Python sites.
  2. Rename Go only; accept the fork. Implies Python is being archived.
  3. Keep both as `Aura*`; leave this task closed-without-action.

Filing as a separate follow-up once the user confirms which path.
title: Rename Aura* search attributes to Pasture* (toolkit-consistent wire names)

The supervisor creates vertical Beads slices and leaf tasks reflecting these

fix-free 0 BLOCKER / 0 IMPORTANT / 0 MINOR round. Carry every supervisor/worker
judgment and deferred choice into the canonical decision ledger. Stop at

Use Proposal 50's complete BDD and validation plan. In particular: exact typed
IR and codec contracts; restart/race/failure-injection coverage; authentic

install/uninstall status; same-package task/AFK compilation; canonical

Provenance, and Aura repository quality gates.

workflow.py:633-642 — SliceWorkflow.run() calls workflow.execute_activity() and then signals the parent workflow, but there is no try/except around the parent_handle.signal() call.

If the parent EpochWorkflow has already completed or been terminated before the child slice signals it, the signal will raise an exception that propagates uncaught, causing SliceWorkflow to fail with an unhandled error rather than a clean SliceResult(success=False, error=...).

Relevant code (workflow.py ~line 633):
    parent_handle = workflow.get_external_workflow_handle(input.parent_workflow_id)
    await parent_handle.signal(
        EpochWorkflow.slice_progress,
        SliceProgressSignal(...),
    )

The parent workflow could reasonably complete or fail before all child slices finish signaling. Without a try/except, this causes an uncontrolled exception in the child rather than a graceful failure result.
title: IMPORTANT: SliceWorkflow.run() no error handling on parent_handle.signal() call

# Product outcome

Pasture users and maintainers need a small typed lifecycle compiler boundary that can accept native events from multiple agent harnesses without duplicating semantic operation selection in each provider handler. The staged current wave delivers OpenCode first and Codex second while preserving the accepted Claude M1 as regression evidence.

End-vision provider set: Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and planned future Strike and Grok Build providers. Strike and Grok Build justify an N-provider boundary but have no inferred host contract or implementation scope in this URD.

Required data path:

native provider event
  -> provider ingress/frontend
  -> existing waist.L2
  -> minimal typed post-L2 plan and Proceed response intent
  -> existing legalize/backend/receipt/Provenance path
  -> bounded provider-correct read-back
  -> mechanical provider response encoder

# Requirements

## R1. Minimal shared post-L2 middle-end

Define and implement one minimal typed post-L2 middle-end shared by the selected providers. It receives verified `waist.L2` input and returns the typed operation/effect plan and provider-neutral Proceed response intent needed by the existing durable path.

Keep the interface constructor-owned, strongly typed, and no larger than the OpenCode/Codex MVP requires. Do not add speculative registries, universal payload schemas, arbitrary string maps, future-provider fields, or fixture-driven abstractions without an observed caller.

Semantic operation selection belongs in Go after L2. Generated TypeScript, Python, shell, environment variables, and external callers remain mechanical transport/encoding boundaries and do not choose Pasture operations.

## R2. Strict milestone sequence

M2 includes the shared middle-end and OpenCode vertical. M2 must complete implementation review and user acceptance before M3 implementation begins. M3 has its own implementation review and user acceptance gate.

GitHub #53 documentation corrections are included as file-disjoint documentation work. They must not change runtime behavior.

## R3. M2 OpenCode vertical

Target exactly installed and captured OpenCode 1.18.10. Do not add dual-version compatibility or a broad support matrix.

Use both selected authentic events in stages:

- `session.created`: ingress/session smoke path.
- `tool.execute.before`: meaningful Proceed gate path.

Carry `tool.execute.before` through provider ingress, L2, the shared typed middle-end, ordered durable occurrence/interpreted/consultation evidence as applicable, bounded read-back, and a mechanical native Proceed encoding. Carry `session.created` far enough to provide the selected provider-correct durable session smoke evidence without claiming gate equivalence.

M2 differential evidence compares authentic OpenCode values with the landed Claude production implementation and committed Claude regression fixture. The Claude side must be labeled non-live. Equivalence covers only the proven common Proceed semantics and must retain provider-specific facts.

Keep selected OpenCode activation default-off during implementation. After M2 independent review and UAT pass, statically enable only the accepted OpenCode 1.18.10 `session.created` and `tool.execute.before` entries.

## R4. M3 Codex vertical

M3 begins only after accepted M2. Target exactly installed and captured Codex 0.146.0. Do not add dual-version compatibility or a broad support matrix.

Use both selected authentic events in stages:

- `SessionStart`: configured-hook session smoke path, not an exact semantic equivalent of OpenCode `session.created`.
- `PreToolUse`: meaningful Proceed gate path and strongest counterpart to OpenCode `tool.execute.before`.

Carry `PreToolUse` through provider ingress, L2, the shared typed middle-end, ordered durable evidence, bounded read-back, and a mechanical native Proceed encoding. Preserve Codex-specific identity, ordering, failure, authority, and mutation-representation facts rather than flattening them into shape-only equivalence.

M3 differential evidence compares live authentic OpenCode and Codex values over the common Proceed semantics. Keep selected Codex activation default-off during implementation. After M3 independent review and UAT pass, statically enable only the accepted Codex 0.146.0 `SessionStart` and `PreToolUse` entries.

## R5. Authentic fixture policy

The user cleared exactly four raw candidates for exact-byte repository import without redaction in later authorized implementation slices:

1. OpenCode `opencode/lifecycle.jsonl` record 1: `session.created`.
2. OpenCode `opencode/lifecycle.jsonl` record 6: first `read` `tool.execute.before`.
3. Codex `1785755740434994199-2327240-SessionStart.json`.
4. Codex `1785755744328519447-2328094-PreToolUse.json`.

This clearance follows a candidate-specific field inventory and a negative high-confidence credential/private-key signature scan. It does not clear any other payload, transcript, PostToolUse/Stop record, final message, database, cache, model catalog, plugin cache, or authentication file.

Each imported fixture needs provenance containing provider, observed runtime version, inspected source revision, UTC capture time, capture method, exact raw SHA-256, source selector, and `redaction: none`, plus a reference to the user clearance in `aura-plugins-a6h3d`.

OpenCode evidence is an authentic runtime callback-object observation serialized by the capture plugin; do not call it a distinct native wire-byte stream. Codex command-hook files preserve exact stdin bytes.

## R6. Provider identity and durable evidence

Every occurrence, interpreted record, consultation, read projection, fixture provenance record, and activation decision must preserve the correct provider and observed version. OpenCode evidence must never be represented as Claude or Codex evidence, and Codex evidence must never activate OpenCode or Claude entries.

Use the existing waist, legalize, backend, receipt, projection, and Provenance contracts. Do not create a second lifecycle IR, journal, store, or provider-specific semantic pipeline.

## R7. Proceed-only semantic MVP

Proceed is the only successful gate intent in M2 and M3. Denial and input mutation remain deferred until authentic behavior evidence and a later user decision. Source schemas may inform future work but do not authorize speculative semantics now.

## R8. Positive-path-only acceptance

The MVP acceptance suites require the selected authentic positive verticals and differential evidence. New rejection tests for malformed input, wrong provider/event/version, invalid provenance/digest, caller-selected operation, and semantic foreign adapters are explicitly deferred. This defers proof cases; it does not authorize caller-selected semantics or semantic logic in foreign adapters.

## R9. File and issue ownership

GitHub #56 owns the M2 shared middle-end/OpenCode runtime vertical and any generated OpenCode source/output assigned to that vertical. GitHub #27 is coordination-only unless a later ratified plan explicitly changes ownership.

Create a dedicated M3 Codex runtime issue analogous to #56. GitHub #24 remains coordination-only for this runtime vertical. The proposal and implementation plan must enumerate every touched generated source and output and assign each file to exactly one issue and slice owner.

Reuse the existing typed runtime contracts from GitHub #40 where valid for the observed versions. GitHub #44 remains umbrella context only.

## R10. Safety and delivery constraints

Never install, enable, or modify Git hooks. Harness lifecycle hooks are in scope; Git hooks are not.

Use isolated worktrees for later implementation. Do not edit generated outputs as source of truth. Regenerate from typed sources and require zero generated drift at integration gates.

Every Go test invocation includes `-race`. Production-path tests exercise the built/generated entrypoints users run, not test-only exports. M2 and M3 remain unauthorized for worker dispatch until proposal review, Plan UAT, ratification, and an implementation plan complete.

# Priorities

1. Ship and accept the minimal shared middle-end plus OpenCode M2.
2. Preserve exact authentic evidence, provider identity, durable read-back, and a mechanical Proceed encoder.
3. Ship Codex M3 only after accepted M2, reusing the same middle-end.
4. Keep APIs minimal until real users and additional authentic fixtures justify expansion.
5. Apply GitHub #53 documentation corrections without coupling them to runtime behavior.

# Normative positive validation cases

## M2-P1: OpenCode session smoke

Given the user-cleared raw OpenCode 1.18.10 `session.created` fixture, when the generated production ingress processes it, then Pasture records and reads back provider-correct session smoke evidence through the selected durable path, should not claim semantic equivalence with a Codex or Claude session event.

## M2-P2: OpenCode Proceed gate

Given the user-cleared raw OpenCode 1.18.10 `tool.execute.before` fixture, when the generated production hook invokes Pasture, then the provider frontend produces verified L2, the shared middle-end produces typed Proceed intent, ordered evidence is durable and readable, and TypeScript mechanically encodes the native Proceed response, should not select a semantic operation outside Go.

## M2-P3: Labeled Claude regression equivalence

Given authentic OpenCode gate values and landed Claude production/regression evidence, when the common Proceed semantics are compared, then the shared semantic result is equivalent and provider-specific source facts remain distinct, should not label the Claude side as a new live capture.

## M2-P4: Accepted activation

## 16. BDD acceptance criteria

1. **Given** a typed Document, **when** constructors accept it, **then** every
   part is immutable/validated with source location and Goldmark AST, **and should
   not** expose a mutable optional-field runtime bag.
2. **Given** the canonical source roots and active-owner manifest, **when**
   inventory and strict compilation run, **then** independent discovery detects
   missing/stale/dead/symlinked owners, the scan is deterministic/read-only, a
   nonzero unclassified count blocks the gate, and post-zero native syntax names
   owner/node/range/fix with no output, **and should not** let the manifest hide
   an unlisted file or use regex-rewrite semantics.
3. **Given** a supported runtime contract, **when** an operation compiles,
   **then** exactly one exhaustive binding preserves its semantic contract and
   native fixtures pass.
4. **Given** an out-of-range/newer host or missing binding, **when** generation
   runs, **then** it fails actionably, **and should not** guess compatibility or a
   similarly named call.
5. **Given** a fresh agent continues an assignment, **when** it starts, **then**
   role/assignment/task/worktree/evidence/decisions/outstanding work are restored,
   **and should not** require session continuity.
6. **Given** SelectMany, **when** native UI lacks parity, **then** validated parent
   text returns the same distinct OptionIDs and verbatim record or reports
   unsupported, **and should not** become SelectOne.
7. **Given** an external typed capability, **when** its package contributes and
   invokes a binding through opaque descriptors, **then** its typed ID/version,
   codecs/effects/postconditions hold and exactly one compatible binding composes
   without editing #40, **and should not** expose a tool name/map or accept a
   missing, duplicate, conflicting, or out-of-range binding.
8. **Given** raw string/ID/wrong descriptor/mismatched input capability fixtures,
   **when** Go compilation/analyzer runs, **then** the specified invalid use fails
   under the accurately documented Go literal boundary.
9. **Given** a process recipe with env/dataflow/pipeline, **when** lowered, **then**
   structured argv/input/output edges preserve it, **and should not** hide
   unsupported constructs in `sh -c`.
10. **Given** any task/graph mutation, **when** Apply commits, **then** state and
    required attribution/events/contexts commit together, **and should not**
    leave either half.
11. **Given** a committed OperationID, **when** retried after reopen or
    concurrently with the same command, **then** the original result/EventIDs
    return; different reuse fails.
12. **Given** two owner changes share the same ExpectedOwner, **when** concurrent,
    **then** one wins and the stale operation writes nothing.
13. **Given** an administrative actor and a material contributor, **when** events
    record, **then** only responsibility/material contribution adds attribution.

    replay is stable, **and should not** accept duplicate start, end-before-start,

    event-list or composed timeline pagination runs, **then** public EventID,
    exclusive cursors, and the first-page snapshot watermark deterministically
    preserve one traversal.

    list` and `task timeline TASK-ID` run, **then** filters use OR-within and
    AND-across dimensions, stored envelopes page by the frozen cursor, and tagged
    point/open/closed/overlapping intervals use their specified start keys and
    source EventIDs, **and should not** create or duplicate journal rows.
18. **Given** typed event contexts, **when** constructed, **then** each built-in or
   named extension constructor accepts only a valid ID in its own domain,

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-28 — Typed multi-harness compiler and authoritative task journal

## 1. Decision and correction from Proposal 27

Pasture will compile opaque, validated Go `Document` values into native Claude
Code, OpenCode, and Codex artifacts. Portable meaning lives in a
protocol-semantic IR. Markdown is parsed with Goldmark, not searched and rewritten
as an operational language. Native runtime calls are emitted only through an
exhaustive, version-bounded runtime contract.

Provenance will own one generic, ordered TaskEvent journal and the transaction
boundary that commits task/graph/Activity state with its events. Current task
tables remain authoritative; the journal explains post-migration changes and is
not an event-sourced replacement for historical state. Pasture owns typed
`pasture.*` event definitions and the `pasture task` CLI that generated workflows
use instead of Beads.

Native plugin registration is deliberately separate from runtime semantics. A
versioned activation contract describes public version probes, exact manager
commands or config mutation, package identities, and standalone destinations.
`pasture install` keeps the user's simple preferences separate from a narrow,
factual installation-state inventory. That inventory records what Pasture
confirmed it installed or removed, what remains, and the last actionable
failure. It is not a pending-operation queue, rollback log, authorization
system, lock, or cross-cell transaction coordinator.

Proposal 28 retains all accepted Proposal 27 invariants and resolves every
Proposal 27 Terra finding. OpenCode hooks are generated as an embedded,
auto-discovered TypeScript file for this wave; no npm publication or native npm
plugin mutation is required before the hook behavior has been verified. Target
packages publish target identity plus RuntimeContractID, while #39 alone binds
those artifacts into opaque activation contracts. Provenance lands as the strict
chain #4 -> #5 -> #14, with #4 dormant until #5 activates atomic journaling and
the migration baseline. Upstream issues publish fixtures/oracles; downstream
Aura issues alone own Home Manager parity and real `pasture-stable` promotion.
The proposal also freezes deployable embedded artifact bundles, observed
installation-state and retry semantics, authenticated-claim-free actor
resolution, one-subject/one-round clean-review evidence, complete event query
and legacy import semantics, the exhaustive nine-cell test matrix, and the
canonical implementation worktrees.

The user explicitly deferred the separate Plan UAT while unavailable. After all
three proposal reviewers reach a clean 0/0/0 consensus, the architect ratifies
this proposal and the same primary agent continues as implementation supervisor.
Planning questions and every agent judgment call are retained in a decision
ledger with alternatives, rationale, affected surfaces, and provisional choice;
they are presented together for explicit disposition at Implementation UAT.
Deferral changes timing, not acceptance coverage, and nothing is silently
dropped.

## 4. Opaque typed Document API

The following shows semantics, not exported mutable field layout:

```go
type Document struct { /* unexported validated parts */ }
type Part interface { /* closed within compiler package */ }

func NewDocument(parts ...Part) (Document, error)
func Markdown(source []byte, at Location) (Part, error)
func Operation(op SemanticOperation, at Location) (Part, error)
func Verbatim(content []byte, at Location) (Part, error)
func TargetLiteral(cases []TargetCase, at Location) (Part, error)
```

`Markdown` parses once through Goldmark. Its unexported AST segments reference an
owned immutable source buffer. Constructors retain source locations and reject
invalid states before a document exists.

`Verbatim` is a portable fragment preserved without operational interpretation.
`TargetLiteral` is a narrow raw-native escape. Across the requested target set it
contains exactly one validated `LiteralFor(RuntimeContractID, content, reason)`
or `LiteralUnsupported(harness, reason)` per enabled harness. Missing, duplicate,
or out-of-range cases fail. Target literals cannot masquerade as portable
operations.

Compilation stages are explicit:

```text
typed Go specs
  -> validated Document and Goldmark AST
  -> semantic/type/dataflow validation
  -> runtime contract selection
  -> exhaustive operation/effect/capability lowering
  -> target rendering and package projection
  -> native schema/loader validation
```

Diagnostics carry canonical owner, file/section and AST source range, semantic
operation, target contract, failed stage/time, caller impact, and concrete fix.
A failed document emits no partial output.

## 5. Protocol-semantic IR

Semantic operations are closed concrete variants behind validating constructors,
not optional-field bags and not tool-name/arguments maps.

### 5.1 Orchestration and logical continuity

The closed orchestration set is:

- `InvokeSkill`
- `DelegateAssignment`
- `ContinueAssignment`
- `SendAssignmentMessage`
- `CollectAssignmentResults`
- `StopAssignment`
- `RequestUserDecision`

Collections plus `independent`, `dependency-ordered`, or `bounded-parallel`
scheduling metadata express parallelism. Claude teams, OpenCode tasks, and Codex
agent handles are backend details.

Every delegation/continuation carries a validated logical context:

```go
type AssignmentContext struct {
    Role        protocol.RoleID
    Assignment AssignmentID
    Task        provenance.TaskID
    Worktree    WorktreeRef
    Evidence    []EvidenceRef
    Decisions   []DecisionRef
    Outstanding []WorkItemRef
}
```

The target may resume an existing agent or spawn a fresh one. Both are correct
only when the full context above is reconstructed. Runtime session identity is
never the assignment identity.

Provenance #5 owns the authoritative assignment aggregate rather than leaving
`AssignmentID` as free evidence supplied by generated prose. Its public IDs are
opaque validated string types (`AssignmentID` and `AssignmentSlotID`), and its
immutable lifecycle projection contains the task, agent, slot, role, status,
start/end EventIDs and timestamps, and optional predecessor assignment. Exactly
one assignment may be active for a `(TaskID, AssignmentSlotID)` pair.

`StartTaskAssignment`, `EndTaskAssignment`, and `ReassignTaskAssignment` use the
same atomic `Apply`/`OperationID` boundary as task mutations. Reassignment ends
the prior assignment and starts its successor in one transaction; it preserves
cumulative attribution and writes ordered task events. A new child assignment
requires either an active parent AssignmentID or a registered bootstrap
SoftwareAgent, so the first assignment is explicit without creating a circular
dependency. The supervisor slot represents current task responsibility and must
agree with `Task.Owner`; reviewer slots represent bounded contributions and do
not change owner. `StartTaskAssignmentBatch` atomically creates the three
reviewer assignments or none. Duplicate, stale, completed, superseded, wrong-
task, wrong-slot, and concurrent-start/end/reassign cases write nothing.

### 5.2 User decisions

`RequestUserDecision` has result modes `SelectOne`, `SelectMany`, and `FreeText`.
It includes the full question, all option IDs/labels/descriptions, any code or
definition shown, result validation, and verbatim answer capture. A native widget
is used only if its request/result contract preserves those semantics. Otherwise
the parent performs a validated textual interaction; if neither is possible, the
operation is unsupported rather than silently narrowed.

### 5.3 Task/workflow effects

Task effects cover the entire approved surface:

- lifecycle: create, show, update, close/reopen, list, ready, blocked, dependency
  tree;
- typed task-to-task relationships: blocked-by, derived-from, supersedes,
  discovered-from;
- owner change with expected-owner CAS;
- typed task-to-Agent attribution add/query;
- label/comment mutations and queries;
- typed task-linked Activity start/end/query using `ActivityID`;
- assignment/review/UAT/skill/git material events;
- secondary event-context add/query; and
- ordered task event/timeline queries.

Work completion is not task closure. A worker ends its task-linked Activity and
records a typed `pasture.assignment.completed` material event, but never closes a
slice. `CloseTask` is the reviewed task-status transition reserved to the
supervisor/protocol owner after the required review gate. There is no ambiguous
`CompleteTask` mutation or `pasture task complete` command.

For an implementation slice, #43 validates a concrete authorization before it
calls generic Provenance state mutation. Review identity is not inferred from
three loosely related events:

```go
type ReviewRoundID string
type ReviewSubjectID string

type SliceCloseAuthorization struct {
    AssignmentID AssignmentID
    RoundID      ReviewRoundID
    SubjectID    ReviewSubjectID
    ReviewEvents [3]provenance.EventID
}
```

`ReviewSubjectID` identifies an immutable typed subject containing repository,
worktree, base/head or tree evidence, and the canonical content digest reviewed.
`pasture task review start` creates one round for exactly one slice and subject
and atomically creates three distinct active reviewer assignments, actors, and
typed axis slots from Provenance's authoritative assignment aggregate.
`pasture task review submit` is the only public path that may create protected
`pasture.review.accepted/v1` or `pasture.review.revised/v1` events. It resolves
the actor from the recorded assignment, requires that assignment's axis and
subject, and records BLOCKER/IMPORTANT/MINOR counts plus `fixes_applied`.
Generic `event record` rejects protected review kinds.

Each `(ReviewRoundID, AssignmentID)` permits exactly one terminal submission.
An ACCEPT seals that reviewer's assignment; a REVISE atomically seals the whole
round as revised. Once revised, later submissions of either vote are rejected
before mutation. Re-review always creates a new ReviewRoundID and three new
reviewer assignments. Concurrent or duplicate submissions have one winner, and
REVISE-before/interleaved/after-ACCEPT cases can never be converted into a
closable round.

A close succeeds only when all three supplied EventIDs are ACCEPT events from
the same current RoundID and SubjectID, their recorded assignments and AgentIDs
are distinct, their axes are exactly correctness/test-quality/elegance, all
three severity counts are zero, every `fixes_applied` is false, the current
content still hashes to SubjectID, and no later REVISE or subject mutation has
invalidated the round. Events from mixed rounds/subjects, self-certified events,
reused assignments, or a fix-applying round write nothing.

The invocation actor is resolved from the recorded AssignmentID, never from an
`--actor` or `--supervisor` override, and must be the slice's current supervisor
assignment. This is explicitly protocol-policy validation, not an authentication
or hostile-user security boundary: anyone able to alter the local task database
or invoke another known assignment is outside the claim. Provenance remains
generic and persists the already-authorized mutation. The slice-specific command
is `pasture task slice close`; generic `pasture task close` rejects slice kinds.
#43 freezes closure policy separately for ordinary tasks and completed review
tasks so no non-slice behavior is inferred from the slice predicate.

The frozen closure policies are explicit by task kind. An ordinary leaf may be
closed only by its active current owner-responsibility assignment from
`in_progress` with no unresolved blocked-by children, emitting
`pasture.task.closed/v1`. A review task closes only as part of its one terminal
`review submit`; generic close rejects it. An implementation slice closes only
through `task slice close` after a clean current round. Protocol documents and
containers (REQUEST, URD, PROPOSAL, IMPL_PLAN, UAT, HANDOFF, and epic) reject
generic close and advance only through their typed transition, supersession, or
landing policy. Every rejected actor/assignment/state/dependency/evidence case
is tested to leave task, graph, assignment, and journal state unchanged.

Task-to-task, task-to-Agent, and task-to-Activity operands are distinct Go types
and operations. The new API does not expose `AddEdge(TaskID, string, EdgeKind)`.

The only MVP backend for this family is the versioned `pasture task` CLI. A
missing or incompatible binary fails actionably. Registered native tools and
semantic-only instructions remain the explicit follow-ups in §2.

### 5.4 Process, Git, and filesystem effects

#38 owns the foundational opaque `EffectID` and `EffectSet` values, including
constructor validation, canonical ordering/deduplication, codec, equality, and
compatibility semantics. #43 contributes named task effects and #46 contributes
the concrete process/Git/filesystem effect definitions; neither redefines the
container. #41 may therefore expose `EffectSet` without depending on #46.

Operational process semantics are not hidden in shell strings:

```go
type RunProcess struct {
    Executable ExecutableRef
    Arguments  []Argument
    Directory  WorkingDirectoryRef
    Environment []EnvBinding
    Stdin      InputRef
    Stdout     OutputRef
    Stderr     OutputRef
    Exit       ExitExpectation
    Effects    EffectSet
}

type Pipeline struct {
    Steps []ProcessStep // typed output-to-input edges
}
```

Environment names/values, literal/file/previous-output stdin, captured/file
stdout/stderr, and exit expectations are validated. Command substitution is an
explicit output reference. A structured `Pipeline` is used only where the
classified inventory needs a pipeline. Redirection, control operators, globbing,
or shell expansion not represented by the MVP types is reported unsupported and
must become a dedicated operation; lowerers do not smuggle it through `sh -c`.

Git effects are typed repository operations/evidence over process primitives and
respect repository policy such as `git agent-commit`. Filesystem effects cover
read, exact write/replace, create directory, move, and remove an exact owned path.
Typing an effect describes intent; it never grants missing user/security
authorization.

### 5.5 Typed external capability escape

```go
type CapabilityID string
type CapabilityContractVersion string

const CapabilityRenderDiagram CapabilityID = "acme.diagram.render"

var RenderDiagram = MustDefineCapability[RenderDiagramInput, RenderDiagramResult](
    CapabilityRenderDiagram,
    CapabilityContractVersion("1.0.0"),
    renderDiagramSemantics,
    renderDiagramEffects,
    renderDiagramInputCodec,
    renderDiagramOutputCodec,
)

type CapabilitySemantics struct {
    Summary        string
    Preconditions  []Condition
    Postconditions []Condition
    Result         ResultContract
}

func DefineCapability[In, Out any](
    id CapabilityID,
    version CapabilityContractVersion,
    semantics CapabilitySemantics,
    effects EffectSet,
    input Codec[In],
    output Codec[Out],
) (Capability[In, Out], error)

func InvokeTool[In, Out any](c Capability[In, Out], input In) SemanticOperation
```

`Capability` is opaque. `InvokeTool` accepts a typed descriptor, not an ID,
string, native name, or untyped payload. External packages declare a typed const
ID and construct an opaque descriptor as a `var` or function result; Go values
returned by `DefineCapability` are never claimed to be constants. Bindings must
accept the descriptor's version and prove the same preconditions,
postconditions, result, and effect set.

Go named string types prevent accidental interchange of typed variables but do
accept assignable untyped literals. The guarantee is stated accurately:

- compile-fail fixtures reject raw strings/IDs/wrong descriptors at
  `InvokeTool` and mismatched typed input;
- raw string variables cannot cross the named-ID boundary without explicit
  conversion;
- a `go/analysis` check requires declared typed constants at canonical
  capability definition sites and rejects untyped literal IDs passed directly
  to `DefineCapability`; and
- registry validation rejects invalid namespaced IDs and conflicting duplicate
  descriptors or versions. A runtime binding declares a compatible
  `CapabilityContractVersion` range in addition to the host RuntimeContract's
  harness-version range.

A completely undescribed tool remains an exhaustive TargetLiteral, never a
generic portable call.

## 6. Runtime harness contracts

Runtime lowering uses a contract distinct from installation:

```go
type RuntimeContractID string
type SemanticOperationID string
type RuntimeContract struct { /* unexported validated profile */ }

type RuntimeBinding interface { runtimeBinding() }
// NativeCall | ParentMediated | SemanticInstruction | Unsupported

type RuntimeBindingContribution interface { runtimeBindingContribution() }

func BindCapability[In, Out any](
    capability Capability[In, Out],
    versions CapabilityVersionRange,
    binding CapabilityRuntimeBinding[In, Out],
) (RuntimeBindingContribution, error)

func NewRuntimeContract(
    id RuntimeContractID,
    harness HarnessID,
    versions VersionConstraint,
    core CoreRuntimeBindings,
    capabilities ...RuntimeBindingContribution,
) (RuntimeContract, error)
func (c RuntimeContract) ID() RuntimeContractID
func (c RuntimeContract) Harness() HarnessID
func (c RuntimeContract) Supports(version HostVersion) bool
func (c RuntimeContract) OperationBinding(op SemanticOperationID) RuntimeBinding
func (c RuntimeContract) EffectBinding(effect EffectID) RuntimeBinding
func LookupCapabilityBinding[In, Out any](
    c RuntimeContract,
    capability Capability[In, Out],
) (CapabilityRuntimeBinding[In, Out], error)
```

Values are opaque and constructor-validated. #40 owns this build-time composition
API; external packages can bind a #41 descriptor without modifying #40, but can
never supply a dynamic name or untyped payload. Construction requires exactly
one binding for every requested operation/effect/capability, validates the
descriptor codec/semantics/effect set and version intersection, and rejects
duplicate or conflicting contributions. Native bindings include exact
request/result schemas and fixtures. Missing bindings, unsupported required
operations, or host versions outside the range fail; no similarly named call is
guessed. `SemanticOperationID` is the protocol identity and is never reused as
Provenance's idempotency `OperationID`; operations, effects, and capability
descriptors cross separate typed lookup surfaces without conversion.

Initial evidence baselines are explicitly pinned:

| Harness | Initial point range | Contract rule |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | exactly CLI 2.1.210 plus pinned official/source schemas | use only Agent/SendMessage/TaskStop-era primitives where exact; never emit removed TeamCreate/TeamDelete semantics |
| OpenCode | exactly CLI 1.17.18 plus official docs/pinned source | use documented skill/task/question surfaces; unverified persistent message/follow-up/wait/close names are mediated, semantic, or unsupported |
| Codex | exactly CLI 0.144.1 plus official docs/pinned source | bind only exact exposed collaboration/request-input functions and preserve logical continuity across replacement agents |

Updating a host requires a new RuntimeContractID or reviewed range expansion.
“Current” and `latest` are not compatibility policies.

## 7. Native activation contracts

Installation mechanics do not enter the semantic IR:

```go
type ActivationContractID string
type ActivationContract struct { /* unexported validated profile */ }
type ActivationStrategy interface { activationStrategy() }
// NativePlugin | DirectFile | NativePluginPendingTrust

func NewActivationContract(
    id ActivationContractID,
    harness HarnessID,
    hostVersions VersionConstraint,
    versionProbe CommandSchema,
    components ExhaustiveComponentActivations,
) (ActivationContract, error)
func NativePluginActivation(manager NativeManagerContract) ActivationStrategy
func DirectFileActivation(bundle artifact.Bundle, destination Destination) ActivationStrategy
func PendingTrustActivation(manager NativeManagerContract, review NativeTrustReview) ActivationStrategy
func (c ActivationContract) ID() ActivationContractID
func (c ActivationContract) Harness() HarnessID
design:
func (c ActivationContract) Component(id ExtensionID) ComponentActivation
```

`ExhaustiveComponentActivations` is opaque and created only by a validating
constructor that requires exactly one skills, agents, and hooks component—no
public mutable map. Each component contains exactly one closed activation
strategy, so invalid nullable marketplace/plugin/config combinations cannot be
constructed. Native strategies carry exact package identity plus
install/list/update/remove schemas. Neutral upstream issue #48 owns package
`artifact`: opaque `Bundle`, `BundleID`, manifest/entry/digest codecs,
constructors, canonical validation, and the `go:embed`/`fs.FS` boundary. Each
#24/#27/#45 target constructs and publishes an `artifact.Bundle`; #39 consumes
that upstream type and adds only activation destination/semantics. Paths must be
clean relative paths; traversal, absolute/duplicate leaves, parent/leaf
symlinks, and unsupported entries are constructor errors. The installed CLI
carries every DirectFile payload and never resolves from cwd/source checkout.
The private nine-cell table stores no mutable installation state itself.

Target artifacts do not carry an ActivationContractID. Each target publishes a
stable target/component identity, its opaque `artifact.Bundle`, and the
RuntimeContractID under which it was compiled. #39's private catalog consumes
those target descriptors
and binds each one to an ActivationContractID and closed strategy. This keeps
target generation upstream of activation without duplicating metadata.

The initial public activation matrix is:

| Harness | Skills | Agents | Harness hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `pasture-skills` native plugin | `pasture-agents` native plugin | `pasture-hooks` native plugin |
| OpenCode | whole directories at `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/` | files at `~/.config/opencode/agent/<role>.md` | embedded `pasture-hooks.ts` at `~/.config/opencode/plugin/pasture-hooks.ts` through pinned auto-discovery |
| Codex | `pasture-skills` native plugin | `~/.codex/agents/pasture_*.toml` | `pasture-hooks` native plugin, followed by native user trust review |

The Go values remain opaque implementation metadata. Cross-language consumers
use one public #39-owned command contract:

```text
pasture install apply-selection \
  --desired <selection-file> \
  --source <installer|home-manager> \
  --json

pasture install apply-cell \
  --harness <claude-code|opencode|codex> \
  --extension <skills|agents|hooks> \
  --enabled=<true|false> \
  --source <installer|home-manager> \
  --json
```

The command never accepts the persisted installer config directly. Both callers
produce this immutable desired-state document:

```yaml
schema: pasture.install.effective-selection/v1
cells:
  claude-code: {skills: false, agents: false, hooks: false}
  opencode:     {skills: false, agents: false, hooks: false}
  codex:        {skills: false, agents: false, hooks: false}
```

The schema requires exactly three harness IDs and exactly three extension IDs,
with no defaults or unknown keys. `apply-selection` validates the desired
`EffectiveSelection`, loads the separate typed installation inventory, inspects
any cell requiring reconciliation, constructs the ordered plan in memory, and
calls `apply-cell`. It writes no preference, rollback data, authorization, lock,
or cross-cell transaction record.

Cell and action order is canonical and public:

```text
claude-code.skills, claude-code.agents, claude-code.hooks,
opencode.skills, opencode.agents, opencode.hooks,
codex.skills, codex.agents, codex.hooks
```

For each cell in that order, desired true plans an idempotent inspect/ensure.
Desired false plans inspect/remove only when the inventory says Pasture manages
that cell or its last confirmed/attempted state is installed or unknown; a
never-recorded false cell plans nothing. Thus an uninstall failure remains
retryable on an ordinary TUI or Home Manager rerun even though the desired
preference is already false. Both commands emit one
transient `pasture.install.apply-result/v1` document. Each planned row contains
`index`, typed harness/extension IDs, `operation`, `management`, and exactly one
status from `completed`, `failed`, `unattempted`, `managed_declaratively`, or
`installed_pending_trust`. At most one row is `failed`; all later planned rows
are `unattempted`. `installed_pending_trust` is a successful Codex-hook install,
not a claim that the hook is active. A result contains `ok`, `source`, and rows
in canonical order. A pre-plan decode/schema/version failure emits
`pasture.install.apply-error/v1` with stage, optional cell/action, cause,
impact, and exact remediation. An action failure emits the same diagnostic in
its failed row, exits nonzero, and still returns the complete ordered result.
Neither result schema is accepted as future state; the narrower inventory below
is the only persisted operational evidence.

For `source=installer`, Pasture derives desired effective cells from the loaded
and confirmed global installer preferences (`harness && extension`), saves only
the new preferences, and applies both native-managed and direct-file cells. For
`source=home-manager`, Nix renders desired effective cells from the current
generation's per-harness options. The command acts only on `NativeManaged` cells;
`DirectFile` cells are explicitly skipped as `managed_declaratively` because
Home Manager adds/removes their links from the pinned Pasture generated tree.
`apply-cell --source home-manager` rejects a direct-file mutation with that
exact declarative remedy instead of writing the path. Thus both callers share
one transition schema and native-manager implementation without pretending they
own the same filesystem cells. `apply-cell` is also the exact idempotent
remediation printed for a failed actionable cell.

### 7.1 Confirmed installation inventory and DirectFile safety

Preferences remain in `~/.config/pasture/config.yaml`. Confirmed operational
state for #39-mutated cells lives separately at
`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pasture/installations.yaml` under the closed
schema `pasture.install.state/v1`. Every recorded cell contains typed
harness/extension/strategy/source IDs, artifact identity and version, whether
the matching pre-existing component was created/updated by Pasture or merely
observed externally, the exact native selector/scope or managed file leaves,
the last confirmed observation (`installed`, `absent`, or `unknown`), native
trust disposition where applicable, and the last action/outcome/diagnostic.
Installer-owned direct-file leaves retain their expected type, content digest,
mode, and Pasture-created parent-directory evidence. Removed cells remain as
absent tombstones, so status can answer what was installed, whether uninstall
completed, and what remains. Home Manager DirectFile links are not inventory
members: Nix owns their declarative lifecycle, while `status --source
home-manager --desired ...` performs a read-only exact inspection and reports
`managed_declaratively` without persisting a second ownership/controller model.

Artifact/state content digests use the closed `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` codec
over exact file bytes; manifest leaves are canonical lexicographic relative
paths with explicit octal permission bits. State YAML rejects unknown/duplicate
cells and serializes the public nine-cell order. Writes use a mode-0600 temp file
in the same state directory, flush, atomic rename, and directory flush; a state
file symlink or unsafe type is rejected before action. No secret is stored.

When upgrading from a release with no inventory, every matching pre-existing
native component or direct file is observed as external and is never adopted or
removed by Pasture, even after a desired-true then desired-false cycle. The sole
exception is the exact published user-scoped Claude v0.0.4 monolith: the frozen
compatibility table recognizes that one legacy identity as an approved migration
candidate. Unknown or near-match scope/version/identity remains external and
causes zero mutation. Mixed simultaneous installer/Home Manager control of a
native cell is unsupported and reported with the recorded source and exact
single-controller repair; no concurrency protocol is introduced.

Native cells persist the prior confirmed observation plus the attempted desired
identity before the native action and replace it with the strongest inspected
postcondition afterward. Installer DirectFile cells additionally persist a full
prior manifest, full attempted manifest, and per-entry preflight/attempt record
before each atomic filesystem step. An entry record includes relative path,
desired/prior type, mode and digest or absence, ownership classification, action,
created-directory evidence, and step outcome. Writes use same-directory temp
files and atomic rename; mkdir and unlink are individual atomic steps. A crash
therefore leaves enough evidence for a newer binary to classify every leaf as
matching prior state, matching attempted state, absent, or external/conflicting.
Prior/attempted matches preserve managed lineage and may reconcile directly to
the newer desired bundle; external/conflicting leaves stop actionably. This is a
narrow per-entry factual record, not a pending-work queue: there is no background
worker, rollback, multi-cell commit, or automatic compensation. State-file
decode/write failures identify path/stage/impact/fix and stop before the next
mutation. Concurrent invocations are explicitly unsupported rather than
coordinated.

`pasture install status [--json]` combines the inventory with live typed native
probes and exact-file inspection. It reports desired, recorded, observed, source,
trust, remaining managed targets, and the exact idempotent repair command. A
normal `pasture install` run performs the same inspection before retrying an
installed/unknown false cell; users need not reconstruct the old preference.

Installer DirectFile reconciliation is exact and conservative:

- an absent manifest leaf is created as a regular file with its declared mode;
- a recorded Pasture-managed leaf may update only when its current digest/type
  still matches the prior record;
- an identical pre-existing unrecorded leaf satisfies desired true but is
  recorded as external and is never removed by Pasture;
- a differing file, directory, dangling/foreign symlink, parent symlink, unsafe
  path, permission failure, or modified managed leaf is an actionable conflict,
  never an implicit overwrite;
- removal unlinks only recorded Pasture-managed leaves whose type/digest still
  match, removes only recorded Pasture-created directories that are empty, and
  preserves every sibling; and
- Home Manager DirectFile links are reported `managed_declaratively` by
  read-only desired/live inspection and remain outside persistent inventory,
  while native actions invoked by Home Manager update the factual native-cell
  inventory.

This work has two dependency-distinct milestones rather than one inverted gate.

**Milestone A — inventory/classification (Pasture #47, after #38):**

   active files, stale entries, dead-owner dispositions, and exclusion drift are

   by byte-for-byte tree hashes before and after. Every classification—including
   neutral false positive and dead owner—is represented by a golden fixture.
4. The classified inventory is an input to #46, #43, and #40; those issues may

**Milestone B — typed migration and strict rejection (Pasture #42, after #47,

## 9. Provenance authoritative task journal

### 9.1 Generic envelope and caller-owned payloads

```go
type EventID int64
type EventKind string
type OperationID string
type EventContextKind string

type EventContext struct { /* opaque validated kind + encoded identity */ }

func TaskContext(TaskID) (EventContext, error)
func ActivityContext(ActivityID) (EventContext, error)
func AgentContext(AgentID) (EventContext, error)
func GitContext(GitOID) (EventContext, error)

type ExtensionContextID interface {
    ~string
    EventContextDomain() EventContextKind
}

type ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID ExtensionContextID] struct { /* opaque */ }
func DefineExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    validate func(ID) error,
) (ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID], error)
func ExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    descriptor ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID],
    id ID,
) (EventContext, error)

type TaskEvent struct {
    ID          EventID
    TaskID      TaskID
    Kind        EventKind
    ActorID     AgentID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    OperationID OperationID
    Contexts    []EventContext
    Payload     json.RawMessage
}
```

EventID is database-generated and exposed once. Queries order ascending by
`(RecordedAt, EventID)` and expose both fields. EventKind/context kinds are
validated namespaced types. `EventContext` has no exported raw `ID string`
constructor or fields. Built-in constructors require the corresponding typed ID
and reject zero or structurally invalid values. Caller namespaces define a named
string-backed ID implementing the marker method plus a typed descriptor and
validator. `DefineExtensionContext` derives its kind from the named ID type's
marker; it takes no duplicate kind argument, rejects every reserved Provenance
built-in kind (task/activity/agent/git), and requires a valid caller-owned
namespace. At value construction the ID's reported kind must still equal the
descriptor kind. Built-in `string` cannot satisfy `ExtensionContextID`, so
`DefineExtensionContext[string]` is a compile failure. Only the internal
persistence codec serializes context kind plus text.

Provenance validates the generic envelope, identity syntax/references, contexts,
and payload well-formedness. It does not import or globally register Pasture
codecs. Pasture constructs an opaque typed event definition, validates its
`pasture.*` payload, encodes it, and passes it across this boundary.

Secondary contexts supplied during event creation commit atomically. A later
context attachment, when necessary, is itself a journalled mutation. Typed
constructors prevent TaskID, ActivityID, GitOID, and caller-defined IDs from
being accidentally interchanged even though storage uses a common textual
encoding. Contexts have set semantics: construction, persistence, operation
canonicalization, and query output deduplicate and sort by
`(EventContextKind, canonical encoded identity)`. Association-row insertion
order is never observable. Each context edge stores the EventID that attached
it (the original event for initial contexts, the journalled attachment event for
later contexts). Snapshot queries include only edges whose attachment EventID is
at or below SnapshotMaxEventID, so a later attachment cannot change an in-flight
filtered traversal.

### 9.2 Atomic command API and durable idempotency

```go
type MutationContext struct {
    ActorID     AgentID
    OperationID OperationID
}

Apply(ctx context.Context, mc MutationContext, command Mutation) (MutationResult, error)
```

Provenance #4 owns the TaskEvent envelope, context storage, ordering/query APIs,
and internal append/schema primitives. It exposes no public OperationID replay,
raw event-append bypass, registered production migration, or baseline side
effect. Its persistence tests activate the schema explicitly in isolated test
databases. Provenance #5 exclusively owns the public command/result table, the
following `Apply` surface, and the production migration that installs the #4
schema, writes baselines, and activates atomic journaling. #4 and #5 ship in one
Provenance release tag after both merge; there is no released state in which a
database has a writable journal but non-journalled mutators.

The closed command family covers task lifecycle, typed relationships, labels,
comments, owner change, explicit attribution, task-linked Activity start/end,
later event-context attachment, and a generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation for
caller-validated material events that change no current task state. Provenance
commits domain row(s), any required attribution, TaskEvent row(s), contexts, and
canonical operation/result through one `internal/sqlite` connection/transaction.
Pasture does not compose a fake transaction across separate tracker/audit
connections.

OperationID is durable idempotency identity. Same ID plus byte-equivalent
canonical command/actor returns the originally committed result/events after
close/reopen or concurrent retry. Same ID with different actor/command fails.
The operation row rolls back with the mutation, so there is no pending state.

Pre-1.0 direct mutator paths migrate to Apply or compatibility wrappers that
require MutationContext and delegate to the same transaction. No exported bypass
may mutate a task/graph without its event.

### 9.3 Owner CAS and cumulative attribution

```go
type ChangeTaskOwner struct {
    Task          TaskID
    ExpectedOwner OwnerExpectation // OwnerIs(agent) or OwnerIsUnassigned()
    NewOwner      AgentID
    Reason        string
}
```

The expected owner is compared inside the same transaction. Two distinct
concurrent transitions have one winner; the stale loser changes no owner,
attribution, operation, or event row and receives an actionable conflict.
This protects task assignment only; it is unrelated to plugin-installation
concurrency and introduces no installer transaction/CAS mechanism.

Task.Owner is current responsibility. Prior/new material contributors retain
idempotent `attributed_to` edges. Administrative actors are not attributed merely
for changing a label/status; attribution occurs only for responsibility or
material contribution commands. Owner events record expected/previous/new owner,
actor, reason, OperationID, time, and EventID.

### 9.4 Activities, relationships, and graph events

`StartTaskActivity` and `EndTaskActivity` carry TaskID, ActivityID, AgentID,
phase/stage, notes, and contexts. Activity row state, task linkage, material event,
required attribution, and contexts commit together. Duration Activities remain
distinct from instantaneous transitions and do not encode structured changes in
notes. The state machine is closed: start requires a new ActivityID, existing
task, and actor resolved from the matching active assignment; a new OperationID
cannot start an existing Activity. End requires the same linked task/agent and
an active Activity. End-before-start, wrong task/agent, invalid transitions, and
a second end under a new OperationID write nothing; same-OperationID retries
return the original result, and concurrent ends have one winner.

Task relationships accept TaskID targets. Attribution accepts AgentID. Activity
links accept ActivityID. A relationship involving two tasks writes a task-local
event to each timeline in one transaction, sharing OperationID and receiving
distinct EventIDs. Blocked-by cycle validation, edge persistence, and both events
share the same consistency boundary.

### 9.5 Current state and legacy migration

Current task/graph/Activity tables remain authoritative. The journal explains
all post-migration changes; it is not used to rebuild pre-journal state. When #5
activates the coordinated production migration, existing tasks each receive one
idempotent `provenance.migration.baseline` event containing the then-current
status/phase/owner and source schema version. It is explicitly labeled as a
migration-time snapshot, not fabricated as the original creation or prior
transition. This marks the historical-completeness boundary.

The #5 production migration executes schema activation and every baseline row
inside one exclusive SQLite migration transaction. A fault after any number of
rows rolls back the schema marker, journal tables/changes, and all baselines;
reopen then performs the same migration from the pre-migration database. Empty
databases, tasks with unassigned owners, repeat startup, and concurrent startup
are explicit fixtures. Baseline ActorID is the registered migrator; the optional
payload owner remains absent rather than being fabricated.

Pasture #43 owns a closed, typed import command; #14 supplies only extraction and
adapter plumbing:

```go
type LegacyAuditRowID string
type LegacySchemaVersion string
type ImportLegacyAuditRow struct { /* unexported validated row */ }

func NewImportLegacyAuditRow(
    schema LegacySchemaVersion,
    row LegacyAuditRowID,
    actor LegacyActorRef,
    recordedAt time.Time,
    definition LegacyEventDefinition,
    contexts []LegacyContext,
    tasks []provenance.TaskID,
) (ImportLegacyAuditRow, error)
```

The constructor validates the source schema/row identity, maps the legacy kind
and payload through a typed #43-owned definition, validates every context, drops
duplicate task IDs, sorts the remaining typed IDs, and resolves the actor before
any Apply call. Unknown kinds/payload shapes or invalid/empty task fan-out fail
without writes. Pasture migrates actual legacy audit history without deleting or
updating source rows; pre/post byte hashes of the legacy tables are acceptance
evidence:

- #14's finite coordinator collects all rows and `context_edges`, validates the
  full extraction, sorts rows by `(recorded time, legacy row ID)`, and imports
  serially, stopping at the first failure so equal-time EventID allocation is
  deterministic across repeat/reopen;
- resolve every unique task ID represented by epoch/slice/review/follow-up task
  contexts;
- invoke one #43-owned `ImportLegacyAuditRow` command containing the source
  schema, legacy row ID, actor mapping, original time/payload, all contexts, and
  the sorted unique TaskIDs; it validates/encodes typed payloads and delegates
  once to Provenance's generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation;
- have that single Apply operation create one canonical TaskEvent per `(legacy
  schema, legacy event ID, resolved TaskID)`, attaching all of that row's legacy
  contexts;
- give the batch one stable migration OperationID derived from `(legacy schema,
  legacy event ID)` and deterministic event insert order `(legacy recorded time,
  legacy row ID, task ID)`; and
- enforce the compound legacy identity uniquely so repeat migration/reopen cannot
  duplicate events.

`ImportLegacyAuditRow` is atomic: every event/context/operation result for one
legacy row commits or none does. A retry with the same source identity returns
the canonical batch result and EventIDs; conflicting source content fails. An
injected failure after the first event rolls back the full row batch. This is a
finite schema import, not an event-sourcing or runtime transaction subsystem.

Migrated real events preserve their original RecordedAt and mapped AgentID. When
an old actor cannot be resolved, the migration uses an explicitly registered
`pasture-legacy-migrator` SoftwareAgent and retains the original actor text in the
typed migration payload; ActorID is never silently nil or forged. Baseline events
use a registered `provenance-migrator` SoftwareAgent and migration time. Stable
OperationIDs derive from the typed legacy-row identity through a documented
constructor, not from process-local counters.

Thus one old row linked to several tasks appears on every relevant task timeline
without losing its many-to-many contexts. #14 owns the separately named,
read-only `pasture legacy-audit event list` API for non-task legacy rows and its
raw source-identity/actor-text/context tests; #43 never folds those rows into a
task timeline. After auto-migration,
`pasture task timeline TASK-ID` reads canonical Provenance TaskEvents only; it
does not perform an unstable runtime merge with rows lacking EventID.

Issue #43 owns the typed task-effect variants, their Provenance-backed execution,
the `pasture.*` material event definitions, closure-policy validation, composed
timeline projection, and this frozen command contract. Pasture #14 owns only the
low-level Provenance dependency adapter and legacy-import plumbing; it does not
define task effects or map them to commands. #43 does not migrate generated
source or remove `bd`; issue #42 consumes the completed contract and owns that

```text

pasture task create|show|update|close|reopen|list
pasture task ready|blocked|dep tree
pasture task relation add|remove|list
pasture task owner change --expected-owner ... --new-owner ...

pasture task event record|list

```

```text

  --round REVIEW-ROUND-ID --subject REVIEW-SUBJECT-ID \
  --review-event correctness=EVENT-ID \
  --review-event test-quality=EVENT-ID \
  --review-event elegance=EVENT-ID
```

Exact flags/JSON schemas are frozen before generation. Generated workflow
mutations carry an AssignmentID and OperationID; the backend resolves ActorID
from the current recorded assignment and never accepts an actor/supervisor
override for review or slice closure. Bootstrap/administrative callers use a
separate registered-agent API and make no authentication claim. Queries are
side-effect free. Generic `task close` rejects slice kinds; the exact slice CLI
includes RoundID, SubjectID, AssignmentID, and three accepted review EventIDs and
applies the §5.3 predicate before Provenance Apply.

`pasture task contract --json` returns the closed
`pasture.task.contract-probe/v1` schema containing CLI semver, TaskContractID,
supported schema IDs/ranges, and a canonical definition digest. Generated
artifacts embed their exact requirement. The runtime probes once before the
first task mutation and fails before writes on a missing command, malformed
probe, adjacent/unsupported version, digest mismatch, or semantic contract
mismatch; this covers separately upgraded generated packages and binaries.

Review/UAT/skill/git evidence uses typed Pasture event definitions. Protected
review definitions cannot pass generic `event record`. `event list` accepts a
versioned `pasture.task.event-query/v1`: TaskIDs are ORed, EventKinds are ORed,
typed contexts are ORed, and the non-empty dimensions combine with AND. The
first page captures `SnapshotMaxEventID`; every later page carries it plus an
exclusive `(AfterRecordedAt, AfterEventID)` cursor and ignores later inserts.
Rows are canonical stored envelopes ordered ascending by `(RecordedAt, EventID)`.
Concurrent/backdated appends therefore appear only in a new traversal, never
duplicate or disappear within the current snapshot.

`timeline TASK-ID` uses `pasture.task.timeline-query/v1` with the same snapshot
watermark and exclusive key. Its tagged rows are `point_event` or
`activity_interval`. A point sorts by `(RecordedAt, EventID)`; an interval sorts
by `(StartedAt, StartEventID)`, carries nullable EndedAt/EndEventID plus both
source EventIDs, and is open when no end event exists at the snapshot watermark.
Overlaps do not alter ordering. Folding creates no journal row, and human/JSON
renderings share the same schema. Non-task legacy rows remain only in #14's
separately named API. Errors name the effect, artifact/command, why/where/when,
impact, and fix. Issue #42's final generated-output gate rejects operational
`bd`.

Workers report completion with `pasture task activity end` followed by the typed
assignment-completed event. `pasture task close` alone mutates task status and is
subject to the protocol's concrete supervisor/review authorization. CLI fixtures
prove that the completion sequence cannot close a slice, a worker cannot close
it directly, and the recorded supervisor can close it only with the current
clean three-axis review evidence.

- Whole skill/support trees survive packaging.
- Each target publishes a stable target/component descriptor plus
  RuntimeContractID and isolated-load oracle. Aura #8 later owns the exhaustive
  nine-cell Home Manager parity proof.
- Hook packages are independent and never transitively selected.

The completed explicit `EmitHarness(sourceRoot, outputRoot, ...)` work remains.
Partial regex runtime/OpenCode output is exploratory and replaced only after the
typed compiler/contracts pass.

## 12. Simple installer

Canonical preferences are exactly:

```yaml
install:
  harnesses:
    claude-code: false
    opencode: false
    codex: false
  extensions:
    skills: true
    agents: true
    hooks: false
```

This is one harness boolean map plus one global extension map—not a per-harness
extension matrix. The TUI has harness checkboxes, one global extension page,
saved choices, exact install/uninstall summary, confirmation, and progress.
Cancellation changes nothing.

After confirmation Pasture preserves unrelated YAML and saves preferences before
native actions. It normalizes the confirmed preferences to one immutable
`pasture.install.effective-selection/v1` desired document, then passes that to
`apply-selection --source installer`. TUI effective cells are
`harness && extension`. The persisted config remains simple global preferences
and never stores the normalized matrix or installation evidence.

The fixed reconciler is deliberately small:

- desired effective true: idempotently ensure present/update, including an
  unchanged true cell;
- desired effective false plus a Pasture-managed installed/unknown inventory
  record: inspect and idempotently remove the exact component; and
- desired false with no Pasture-managed or uncertain record: no mutation.

Thus first-run false harnesses are untouched, a failed uninstall remains visible
and retryable after the preference already says false, and unrelated native
installations or identical external files are observed but never claimed or
removed. A global extension change fans out across the currently desired and
recorded managed cells.

The installer applies all cells, including its own direct-file destinations.
Home Manager independently renders the same effective schema from its per-
harness children but calls only native-managed cells; Nix owns direct-file link
transitions. Schema-validation, normalization, transition, and source-ownership
fixtures prove the two inputs agree for equivalent choices without conflating
their execution responsibilities.

Save failure invokes no native action. Any native/file failure stops immediately;
the postcondition probe updates the factual inventory where possible, earlier
completed actions remain, and later actions are unattempted. The error names what
failed, why, the cell/path/manager and stage, what remains or is unknown, caller
impact, `pasture install status`, and the exact idempotent `apply-cell`
remediation. There is no rollback, background recovery, lock, authorization, or
cross-cell transaction coordinator. Native managers own plugin/update/cache
state; Pasture never writes private caches.

Pasture #45 publishes the exact legacy and split Claude package identities plus
fixtures; #39 alone owns this compatibility behavior. Before mutation #39
classifies native state as empty, exact v0.0.4 monolith only, split only, exact
monolith plus complete/partial known splits, or unknown. Unknown identity,
scope, version, or duplicate/conflicting rows perform zero mutation. For each
known state the frozen order is: probe/list and validate; ensure/update every
desired split; verify it; remove the exact user-scoped v0.0.4 monolith; verify
absence; remove any unselected known split; verify final state; record the
inventory. Failure at every action stops later actions, probes and records what
actually remains, and the next ordinary run resumes reconciliation without
rollback. Codex hooks finish as installed-but-requiring-native-trust-review until
the user approves them in Codex; this trust state is reported, not bypassed.

The v0.0.4 monolith transition is selection-wide and is implemented exclusively
by `apply-selection`, which has every Claude sibling's desired state. While the
monolith or an incomplete legacy transition exists, `apply-cell` fails before
mutation and instructs the caller to rerun the full installer/TUI or Home Manager
activation with an exhaustive desired selection. It never guesses sibling
intent, and a cell-level failure row prints that same full-selection remedy.

## 13. Aura Home Manager migration and parity

New exact option nesting is:

```nix
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".enable = false;
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".skills.enable = true;
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".agents.enable = true;
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".hooks.enable = false;
```

OpenCode and Codex mirror this. Children remain inert until their parent is true.

The live options are not silently dropped. Aura #8 freezes this compatibility
table for one release:

| Old option | Compatibility behavior | New destination |
|---|---|---|
| `commands.enable` with all roles enabled | deprecated alias; enables Claude parent + skills | `harnesses."claude-code".{enable,skills.enable}` |
| `agents.enable` | deprecated alias; enables Claude parent + agents | `harnesses."claude-code".{enable,agents.enable}` |
| `opencode.skills.enable` | deprecated alias; enables OpenCode parent + skills | `harnesses.opencode.{enable,skills.enable}` |
| `opencode.agents.enable` | deprecated alias; enables OpenCode parent + agents | `harnesses.opencode.{enable,agents.enable}` |
| non-default `commands.roles.*` | exact legacy filtered DirectFile projection for one release | no aggregate-plugin equivalent; choose all skills or retain compatibility mode during the window |
| `commands.extraCommands` | additive user DirectFiles | `harnesses."claude-code".skills.extraFiles` |
| `agents.extraAgents` | additive user DirectFiles | `harnesses."claude-code".agents.extraFiles` |

The legacy filtered projection and the new aggregate Claude skills plugin are
mutually exclusive; selecting both is an evaluation error naming both option
paths and the two repairs. Extra files are active only when their harness and
extension are enabled, remain separate from generated plugin ownership, and are
rejected at evaluation when their canonical skill/agent identity collides with
the generated bundle or another extra. Every alias/mode emits its exact
replacement warning. Top-level module enable with no harness parent warns that
parent defaults changed to false. After the one-release window, removed legacy
role-filter options produce an actionable error; the additive `extraFiles`
destinations remain. Packages/protocol options remain unchanged.

Generated Pasture artifacts come only from the pinned Pasture source; explicitly
configured user `extraFiles` remain separately owned inputs and are never folded
into generated bundles.

Home Manager projects those pinned generated trees/files plus the separately
declared extras. Its current generation contains one fully explicit
`pasture.install.effective-selection/v1` desired document rendered from the nine
child options, and activation passes it to
`pasture install apply-selection --source home-manager`. The command
acts only on native-managed cells. Direct-file cells remain ordinary Home Manager
links at their documented paths and return `managed_declaratively` if inspected;
Nix never asks `apply-cell` to mutate them. There is no interactive TUI call,
duplicated native argv, or Nix-side operational state model. #39's native actions
update the same factual installation inventory so a failed native uninstall is
visible and retryable on activation rerun. Hooks require explicit true, Codex
hook activation preserves native trust review, and Aura #9 supplies the
validated aggregate marketplace plus gated `pasture-stable` ref.

## 15. Validation plan
