## Evidence
File: internal/tasks/epoch_human_service_test.go:64-114. The test closes and reopens the file-backed tracker at :64-69, then proves ShowInteractionMode and SetInteractionMode replay at :70-76. Plan UAT, ratify, Implementation UAT, and land are all committed only after that reopen; their retries at :83-114 occur on the same service/store lifetime and assert only Replayed plus DecisionID.

## Why this matters
The implementation has separate fact-query/catalog reconstruction and persisted operation-local precondition restoration, and ratify/land carry non-zero prerequisite CurrentFact conditions. A defect in reopening the Facts query boundary, reconstructing a catalog-issued Ratify/Land draft, or restoring the prerequisite asserted journal ID can therefore ship while the only post-reopen proof (interaction mode) remains green. The downstream aura-plugins-8cus8 exhaustive replay leaf does not remove the need for one representative reopen proof of a prerequisite-bound decision.

## Exact fix
Commit at least one accepted prerequisite-bound operation (preferably Ratify and/or Land) before closing the tracker; reopen the same file and construct the service through NewEpochHumanService; retry the exact original input. Assert Replayed=true and byte/identity equality of DecisionID, ActivityID, and every EventID, then snapshot/query decision, evidence, activity, event, and lifecycle state to prove the retry added no rows. Keep the broader actor/replay matrix in aura-plugins-8cus8.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-11 — Unified multi-harness installation

Supersedes Proposal 10. Proposal 10 remains normative except where this revision replaces it. Round 10 returned REVISE on intent-mode parity, the external commit boundary, start-gate and executable identity, exact lifecycle fixtures, Claude-row projection, the OpenCode commit pin, and role-filter provenance. This revision closes each finding without changing product scope.

## 1. Intent mode is part of the wire contract

```go
type IntentMode string

const (
    EnsureSelected IntentMode = "ensure-selected"
    ReconcileExact IntentMode = "reconcile-exact"
)

type InstallRequest struct {
    Schema       uint32
    Authority    DeliveryAuthority
    Mode         IntentMode
    Operation    InstallOperation
    Selected     []CellID
    EnabledRoles []RoleID
}
```

Companion TUI, flags, and JSON use `ENSURE_SELECTED`: selected cells are installed/upgraded and every unselected cell is out of scope. `--select-none` is therefore a literal no-op. Explicit companion uninstall remains a separate operation over selected cells.

Home Manager uses `RECONCILE_EXACT`: after legacy/default option normalization, its declaration is the complete desired set for Home-Manager-owned cells. Omitted Home Manager cells are removed; companion- or foreign-owned cells are conflicts, not implicit uninstall targets. An empty Home Manager declaration disables only Home-Manager-owned cells. Mode and authority are included in plan and consent digests.

Fixtures run two independent exhaustive suites: all 512 matrices through actual Cobra/TUI/JSON parsing under `ENSURE_SELECTED`, and all 512 normalized Home Manager matrices under `RECONCILE_EXACT`. There is no cross-mode plan-equality assertion. Each suite freezes create/update/remove/no-op actions, ownership effects, empty selection, and repeated clean application.

## 2. Role selection has one typed projection edge

```go
type SkillDescriptor struct {
    ID   SkillID
    Role *RoleID // nil is a core skill and is always retained
}

type ArtifactProjection struct {
    Harness  HarnessName
    Artifact ArtifactID
    Skill    SkillID
    Role     *RoleID
}

type DeliveryPackage struct {
    ID          PackageID
    Harness     HarnessName
    Members     []PackageMember
    Effects     []CellID
    Granularity ProjectionGranularity // member-prunable or indivisible
}
```

The canonical `SkillDescriptor`/`RoleSpec` graph generates one canonically sorted `[]ArtifactProjection`; emitters cannot author a second map. Aura reads this edge from the generated bundle manifest and removes filename-prefix filtering. A role filter affects role-scoped skills only; core skills remain selected and the agent component remains the complete five-agent set.

Claude Code and OpenCode direct skill packages are member-prunable. The Codex skills plugin is indivisible, so selecting Codex skills with any narrowed role set fails before mutation with `UNSUPPORTED_INDIVISIBLE_PROJECTION`, explaining that the plugin would expose the full skill set and how to select all roles or omit that cell. It never claims pruned parity. Fixtures cover all 32 role subsets, each single-role toggle, mixed direct/plugin matrices, manifest membership, active destinations, effect reporting, and Home Manager normalization without ID/path parsing.

## 3. Legacy Claude compares only the Claude row

Legacy discovery is required for a plan whose projected Claude row is nonempty (and for an exact-reconcile transition that touches an already owned Claude cell). It is never keyed to the whole nine-cell selection.

- Active legacy composite + all three Claude cells: those three cells are `EXTERNALLY_MANAGED`; any selected OpenCode/Codex cells still plan normally.
- Active legacy composite + a sparse Claude row: the Claude row is `CONFLICT_LEGACY_COMPOSITE`.
- Inactive legacy composite: modern direct/plugin units plan normally.
- Empty Claude row: no legacy observation prerequisite is introduced by other harnesses.
- Unknown, declined, stale, unavailable-CLI, and apply-race evidence retain Proposal 10's zero-write/discovery rules.

Tests cross all seven nonempty Claude-row subsets with all 64 subsets of the other six cells under active, inactive, unknown, declined, stale, unavailable-CLI, and apply-time-changed observations. They assert that an all-three Claude row is recognized regardless of other-harness selections and that non-Claude action shapes are unchanged by the projection.

## 4. Staging is pre-commit; persistent publication is post-commit

`EXT_CREATED` still embeds the bounded deterministic package ZIP. Before `PREPARED`, `STAGE_SOURCE` expands and fsyncs only a transaction-local source under the Pasture control root, and `STAGE_EXECUTABLE` creates the exact private harness snapshot described below. Both remain abortable transaction state. Full plan/state/lease revalidation runs after staging; only then is `PREPARED` appended and fsynced.

The first post-`PREPARED` external step is `PUBLISH_PERSISTENT_SOURCE`. It atomically promotes the staged source on the same filesystem into the cell- and digest-qualified persistent path, fsyncs the destination and parents, and records its postcondition. Existing-exact is an explicit no-op. Absent, exact stage-only, exact destination-only, published-but-unrecorded, prefix/partial, wrong digest, symlink, and foreign/tampered states are distinct fixtures. No persistent marketplace source exists before `PREPARED`; after it, recovery only rolls forward. Missing or altered committed staging is tampered and preserved, never silently reconstructed from a different binary.

Install begins `PUBLISH_N`; upgrade/downgrade publish N while retaining P until N is verified; uninstall has no publish step. `MATERIALIZE_SOURCE` is removed from the post-commit graph and from all prior fixtures.

## 5. Fail-closed gate and immutable executable object

The runner resolves the pinned CLI through a bounded no-follow path walk, opens the final regular native executable, and copies bytes from that descriptor into a private transaction-owned executable snapshot. It rejects scripts/wrappers, validates the exact pinned release digest and native format, fsyncs file and parent, makes the snapshot non-writable, and records digest/device/inode. This snapshot—not PATH, the original symlink, or a mutable Nix profile—is the operation's executable object. Linux uses descriptor execution where available; Darwin executes the private immutable snapshot path under the still-held transaction/registry authority. The snapshot remains until the unit and recovery are complete.

For each CLI step the runner creates two private channels: an expected-token descriptor preloaded before spawn and a release pipe whose write end exists only in the runner. The wrapper inherits the expected-token read end, release read end, and executable descriptor, but never a release writer. The runner spawns it in a new process group, obtains PID/platform start token, and appends and fsyncs:

```text
STEP_i_CHILD_ARMED { pid, start_token, pgid, executable_digest, device, inode, token_hash }
```

Only after that fsync succeeds does the runner issue one fixed authenticated frame, bounded by `PIPE_BUF`, in one write, and immediately close its sole release writer. The wrapper reads through EOF and performs an exact constant-time comparison, so it can distinguish exactly one complete frame from a short or extended stream before exec. EOF with zero/short/extra/invalid bytes, timeout, runner death, closed expected-token descriptor, or any executable identity mismatch exits with a dedicated no-exec result and closes the executable descriptor. A full release write can race runner death only after `CHILD_ARMED` is durable; recovery then waits for/classifies the exact PID/start token and never retries concurrently. The wrapper closes both gates before exec and creates no shell or daemon child.

Fault tests kill frontend, runner, wrapper, and harness around create/spawn, PID observation, journal append/fsync, release write, exec, exit, and postcheck. They prove zero-child and exactly-one-child shapes, fail-closed EOF, bounded orphan exit, PID/PGID reuse, and recovery after a released child. Path, symlink, inode, executable-content, and Nix-generation swaps before and after `PREPARED` either reject before commit or execute the exact transaction snapshot; they can never switch the exec object.

## 6. Exact external lifecycle graphs and argv

Each external cell has digest-qualified marketplace name `M_<digest>`, persistent source `S_<digest>`, and selector `Q_<digest>=plugin@marketplace`. Old and desired states are P and N. The checked-in YAML oracle freezes these vectors:

| Adapter operation | Claude Code 2.1.207 argv | Codex 0.144.1 argv |
|---|---|---|
| `MARKETPLACE_ADD_N` | `plugin marketplace add --scope user S_N` | `plugin marketplace add --json S_N` |
| `MARKETPLACE_LIST` | `plugin marketplace list --json` | `plugin marketplace list --json` |
| `PLUGIN_ADD_N` | `plugin install --scope user Q_N` | `plugin add --json Q_N` |
| `PLUGIN_REMOVE_P` | `plugin uninstall --scope user Q_P` | `plugin remove --json Q_P` |
| `PLUGIN_LIST` | `plugin list --available --json` | `plugin list --available --json` |
| `MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P` | `plugin marketplace remove --scope user M_P` | `plugin marketplace remove --json M_P` |

No adapter uses `plugin update`: neither command binds an explicit immutable local desired source. The operation graphs are:

```text
INSTALL:
  PUBLISH_N -> MARKETPLACE_ADD_N -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_N ->
  PLUGIN_ADD_N -> PLUGIN_LIST_N -> ASSERT_N

UPGRADE / authorized DOWNGRADE:
  PUBLISH_N -> MARKETPLACE_ADD_N -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_PN ->
  PLUGIN_REMOVE_P -> PLUGIN_LIST_NOT_P ->
  PLUGIN_ADD_N -> PLUGIN_LIST_N ->
  MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_N ->
  CLEAN_P -> ASSERT_N

UNINSTALL:
  PLUGIN_REMOVE_P -> PLUGIN_LIST_ABSENT ->
  MARKETPLACE_REMOVE_P -> MARKETPLACE_LIST_ABSENT ->
  CLEAN_P -> ASSERT_ABSENT
```

Every list is its own journaled observer child, not an opaque postcheck spawn. Pure `ASSERT_*` steps compare the exact observed source/marketplace/plugin vector. Each graph has independent Claude and Codex fixtures for clean install, upgrade, downgrade, uninstall, already-satisfied no-op, crash recovery, cancellation, and P/N/both/absent/foreign/tampered states. The full fault matrix covers source promotion, every step record/fsync/gate/spawn/exit/observation, and exact authorized cleanup. Known intermediates roll forward. Unrelated marketplace/plugin names are outside the projection and remain untouched; an unexpected identity colliding with M_P, M_N, Q_P, or Q_N is foreign and is never removed.

## 7. Correct OpenCode provenance

The OpenCode 1.17.18 tag resolves to commit `b1fc8113948b518835c2a39ece49553cffe9b30c`; the GitHub release `targetCommitish` value used in Proposal 10 is not the tag commit and is removed. Fixtures rederive the four archive hashes, `@opencode-ai/plugin@1.17.18` integrity, `@opencode-ai/sdk@1.17.18` integrity, and locked transitive closure from that single publication. A mismatch-negative fixture substitutes the discarded commit and must fail provenance validation.

## 8. Acceptance additions

Proposal 10's acceptance cases remain, with these replacements/additions:

1. Separate 512-case `ENSURE_SELECTED` and 512-case `RECONCILE_EXACT` suites prove their distinct empty/omitted semantics.
2. All role projections come from `SkillDescriptor -> ArtifactProjection`; direct packages prune correctly and narrowed Codex skills fail actionably as indivisible.
3. Legacy composite matching is the Claude-row projection across `7 × 64` selection shapes and every discovery state.
4. The transaction exposes no persistent source before `PREPARED`; `PUBLISH_N` is the first post-commit step and survives every promotion crash point.
5. Gate EOF/runner death before a full authenticated release executes zero harnesses; after release, durable child identity prevents concurrent retry.
6. The verified transaction snapshot is the exec object despite PATH, symlink, inode, or Nix-generation swaps.
7. Exact Claude/Codex install, upgrade, downgrade, and uninstall graphs pass their P/N vector and full fault suites.
8. OpenCode provenance accepts only tag commit `b1fc8113948b518835c2a39ece49553cffe9b30c` with the frozen matching artifacts.

## Plan UAT decisions

Proposal 10's inherited Plan UAT decisions remain unchanged. Acceptance additionally confirms: companion sparse intent and Home Manager exact intent are deliberately different; a narrowed role filter makes the monolithic Codex skills cell unavailable; external upgrade/downgrade may have a bounded post-commit interval with P removed before N is active but deterministically rolls forward; and harness discovery/verification can leave documented harness-owned initialization/cache files that Pasture reports but does not uninstall.

description:
## Failure

The production CLI accepts required --pasture-revision and --aura-revision values, and PromotionRequest documents that gates run against those exact revisions, but buildPromotionGates executes go test in the current pasture working directory and ValidateMarketplaceFile reads the current on-disk Aura file. It neither checks that either checkout HEAD equals the requested revision nor evaluates files/tests from isolated checkouts of those revisions. PromotionRequest.AuraRevision is never consumed outside request construction/accessor tests; PastureRevision is used only after gates when resolving the commit to push.

Evidence: cmd/pasture-release/promote.go:87-115 constructs the request but builds gates from repository paths/projection/path only; lines 181-203 read the live marketplace and run go test in pastureRepo; line 207 explicitly leaves auraRepo unused for command gates. internal/promotion/promote.go:92-105 runs those gates before resolving only PastureRevision. internal/promotion/validate.go:35-36 reads an arbitrary live path. Repository grep finds AuraRevision() used only in request_test.go. Existing CLI tests pass each repository's current HEAD as both revision flags, so they cannot falsify this mismatch.

## Impact

An operator can request promotion of reviewed commit A while the working tree is at passing commit B (or has uncommitted passing files). The gates pass B, then the command resolves and publishes A. Likewise --aura-revision can name any nonempty value while marketplace validation reads a different live Aura tree. This breaks the mandatory claim that activation/package/marketplace evidence belongs to the promoted revisions and can publish an untested or mismatched release.

## Required fix

Bind every gate to immutable requested commits. Either create isolated temporary worktrees/checkouts for the resolved Pasture and Aura revisions and run all commands/file validation there, or fail closed unless clean checkout HEADs exactly equal the resolved requested commits. Resolve and validate both revisions before gates. Add production-CLI integration cases where requested revision differs from checkout HEAD and where the working tree is dirty; both must fail before any remote ref mutation. Add an exact-revision passing case proving marketplace and activation evidence is evaluated from the requested trees.
title: BLOCKER: Promotion gates are not bound to the requested revisions

Location: internal/effects/process.go (ClassifyShellConstruct, lines 290-319) and internal/effects/classification_test.go / process.go's TestClassifyShellConstructRejectsUnsupported (process_test.go:204-232).

What: ClassifyShellConstruct's own token table lists these unsupported tokens: ShellExpansion {"$(", "${", "`", "$"}, ShellRedirection {">>", "2>&1", ">", "<"}, ShellControlOperator {"&&", "||", ";", "&"}, ShellPipeline {"|"}, ShellGlobbing {"*", "?", "[", "]"}.

TestClassifyShellConstructRejectsUnsupported only exercises: "$(date)", "${VAR}" (expansion), "&&", ";" (control), ">", "2>&1" (redirection), "|" (pipeline), "*" (globbing). That's 8 of the ~15 distinct tokens the function itself checks for. Never exercised as their own case: backtick expansion `` ` ``, bare `$VAR` (no braces/parens), `||`, bare background `&`, `<` (input redirection), `>>` (append redirection), `?` and `[`/`]` (globbing).

Risk is low (each check is an independent `strings.Contains` per token, so a bug in one is unlikely to hide in another), but the doc comment and test name both claim comprehensive negative coverage of "unsupported shell constructs," and half the modeled tokens are currently unverified. A future edit to the token list or the check ordering (note the comment at process.go:297-299 about redirection-before-control-operator ordering for "2>&1") would not be caught by the test suite for the untested tokens.

Fix: extend the `cases` table in TestClassifyShellConstructRejectsUnsupported with one row per currently-untested token: "` (backtick)", "echo $VAR" (bare expansion), "a || b", "cmd &" (background), "cmd < in.txt", "cmd >> out.txt", "ls file?.go", "ls [abc].go".
title: S3.1: ClassifyShellConstruct negative table exercises only half its own token list

# PROPOSAL-5: Review Fixes (Correctness + Test Quality)

Supersedes PROPOSAL-4 (aura-plugins-qaswj). Addresses 2 correctness issues
(Reviewer A) and 5 test quality gaps (Reviewer B). Reviewer C accepted.

All unchanged sections from PROPOSAL-4 remain in effect. This proposal
documents only the fixes.

---

## Correctness Fix 1 (BLOCKER): `state.review_votes` not `state.votes`

**Source:** Reviewer A (aura-plugins-a20y6)

EpochState in `scripts/aura_protocol/state_machine.py:48` defines the field
as `review_votes`, not `votes`.

**Before (PROPOSAL-4):**
```python
@workflow.query
def full_state(self) -> QueryStateResult:
    state = self._sm.state
    return QueryStateResult(
        ...
        votes=dict(state.votes),  # WRONG: AttributeError
        ...
    )
```

**After (PROPOSAL-5):**
```python
@workflow.query
def full_state(self) -> QueryStateResult:
    state = self._sm.state
    return QueryStateResult(
        ...
        votes=dict(state.review_votes),  # FIXED: matches EpochState field name
        ...
    )
```

The `QueryStateResult` field remains named `votes` (cleaner API for CLI
consumers). Only the source reference changes.

## Correctness Fix 2 (IMPORTANT): SqliteAuditTrail query_events type signature

**Source:** Reviewer A (aura-plugins-a20y6)

The AuditTrail Protocol in `scripts/aura_protocol/interfaces.py:140-146`
defines `query_events` with typed parameters:

```python
async def query_events(
    self, *, epoch_id: str | None = None,
    phase: PhaseId | None = None,
    role: RoleId | None = None
) -> list[AuditEvent]: ...
```

**Before (PROPOSAL-4):**
```python
class SqliteAuditTrail:
    async def query_events(self, *, epoch_id: str = "",
                           phase: str = "", role: str = "") -> list[AuditEvent]:
```

**After (PROPOSAL-5):**
```python
class SqliteAuditTrail:
    async def query_events(
        self, *,
        epoch_id: str | None = None,
        phase: PhaseId | None = None,
        role: RoleId | None = None,
    ) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        """Query audit events with optional filters.

        Converts PhaseId/RoleId enums to their .value for SQL WHERE clauses.
        None parameters are omitted from the filter.
        """
        conditions: list[str] = []
        params: list[str] = []
        if epoch_id is not None:
            conditions.append("epoch_id = ?")
            params.append(epoch_id)
        if phase is not None:
            conditions.append("phase = ?")
            params.append(phase.value)
        if role is not None:
            conditions.append("role = ?")
            params.append(role.value)
        ...
```

This matches the Protocol signature exactly. Enum `.value` is used for SQL
string comparison. `None` means "no filter on this dimension."

## Test Quality Fix 1: `signal complete` BDD criteria

**Source:** Reviewer B (aura-plugins-zath7), item 1

**Added BDD criteria:**

**Given** `aura-msg signal complete --epoch-id E1 --slice-id S1 --output "done"` **when** slice workflow running **then** sends SliceCompleteSignal(slice_id="S1", success=True, output="done") **should not** send signal to non-existent workflow (exit 3)

**Given** `aura-msg signal complete --epoch-id E1 --slice-id S1 --error "failed"` **when** signaling failure **then** sends SliceCompleteSignal(slice_id="S1", success=False, error="failed") **should not** set success=True when error is provided

**Given** `aura-msg signal complete` without `--slice-id` **when** parsing **then** prints usage error, exits 1 **should not** send incomplete signal

## Test Quality Fix 3: Exit code BDD criteria

**Source:** Reviewer B (aura-plugins-zath7), item 3

**Added BDD criteria:**

**Given** Temporal server unreachable **when** `aura-msg query state --epoch-id E1` **then** prints "connection error: ..." to stderr, exits 2 **should not** exit 0 or raise unhandled exception

**Given** workflow not found **when** `aura-msg query state --epoch-id nonexistent` **then** prints "workflow error: workflow 'nonexistent' not found" to stderr, exits 3 **should not** print stack trace

**Given** `aura-msg epoch start --epoch-id E1` on already-running workflow **when** Temporal returns WorkflowAlreadyStartedError **then** prints "workflow error: epoch 'E1' already running" to stderr, exits 3 **should not** exit 0

Test implementation: subprocess-based integration tests (same pattern as
test_aurad.py `test_help_output`). For connection errors, pass a bogus
`--server-address localhost:1` to guarantee connection failure.

## Test Quality Fix 4: tmux detection test strategy

**Source:** Reviewer B (aura-plugins-zath7), item 4

The `_check_tmux()` function uses `shutil.which("tmux")`. Test strategy:

```python
# Test via subprocess with modified PATH (no mocking frameworks)
async def test_tmux_not_found():
    env = ActivityEnvironment()
    # Inject empty PATH so shutil.which finds nothing
    import os
    old_path = os.environ.get("PATH", "")
    os.environ["PATH"] = ""
    try:
        result = await env.run(execute_slice_command, "aura-swarm start ...", "s1", "e1")
        assert not result.success
        assert "tmux" in result.error
    finally:
        os.environ["PATH"] = old_path

async def test_tmux_found_command_runs():
    # Only run if tmux actually exists on test system
    if shutil.which("tmux") is None:
        pytest.skip("tmux not available")
    ...
```

Alternative (cleaner): make `_check_tmux` accept an optional `path` parameter
for testability without PATH manipulation:

```python
def _check_tmux(search_path: str | None = None) -> bool:
    return shutil.which("tmux", path=search_path) is not None
```

Then tests pass `search_path="/nonexistent"` or `search_path=<dir-with-mock-tmux>`.
This follows the existing DI pattern (no unittest.mock). Recommend the
`search_path` parameter approach.

## Test Quality Fix 5: Hook/shell script test boundary

**Source:** Reviewer B (aura-plugins-zath7), item 5

Test boundary for `hooks/scripts/session-register.sh`:

```python
# Test the shell script via subprocess with a mock aura-msg on PATH
async def test_session_register_hook():
    """Hook script calls aura-msg session register + query state."""
    # Create a mock aura-msg that records invocations
    mock_dir = tmp_path / "bin"
    mock_dir.mkdir()
    mock_script = mock_dir / "aura-msg"
    mock_script.write_text('#!/bin/sh\necho "$@" >> /tmp/aura-msg-calls.txt\n')
    mock_script.chmod(0o755)

    result = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", "hooks/scripts/session-register.sh"],
        env={
            "PATH": f"{mock_dir}:/usr/bin:/bin",
            "AURA_EPOCH_ID": "test-epoch",
            "CLAUDE_SESSION_ID": "test-session",
        },
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0
    calls = Path("/tmp/aura-msg-calls.txt").read_text()
    assert "session register" in calls
    assert "query state" in calls

async def test_session_register_hook_no_epoch():
    """Hook script exits silently when AURA_EPOCH_ID is not set."""
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", "hooks/scripts/session-register.sh"],
        env={"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin"},  # no AURA_EPOCH_ID
        capture_output=True, text=True,
    )
    assert result.returncode == 0
    assert result.stdout == ""
```

The test boundary is the shell script itself, tested via subprocess with
controlled environment. No Temporal server needed for hook tests.

Evidence: awaitWorkflowResult returns handle.GetResult errors unchanged at dbos_adapter.go:438-448, and Apply returns that error unchanged at dbos_adapter.go:217-220. DBOSDiagnosticClass/Field/Stage constants for step-retry and terminal-retrieval are declared at dbos_contract.go:202-249 but are not used by any production error type. DBOSConfigError and DBOSContextFrameError also expose string fields rather than the declared closed enums.

Impact: after retry exhaustion or same-ID terminal replay, callers receive the SDK error without operation/workflow identity, typed stage/class/field, impact, or repair guidance. They cannot reliably distinguish terminal retrieval from construction/context failures, contrary to the user-approved diagnostics contract.

Requirement: Proposal 54 requires typed closed diagnostic class/field/stage values shared by runtime and fixtures. Infrastructure exhaustion must be wrapped once by DBOSAdapter.Apply with operation/workflow context while preserving errors.Is/errors.As and DBOS error code, and every failure must state what, why, where, when, impact, and fix.

Fix: define the closed typed adapter diagnostic error, wrap terminal GetResult/RunWorkflow failures once with operation and workflow IDs while preserving Unwrap, and change config/context errors to use DBOSDiagnosticField and DBOSDiagnosticStage. Assert these typed fields on first exhaustion and same-ID replay.
title: IMPORTANT: Return typed actionable diagnostics for terminal DBOS errors

# FOLLOWUP_IMPL_PLAN — Proposal 50 delivery (journal architecture amendment)

Status: active. This amendment replaces the Provenance TaskEvent-only
foundation after implementation review exposed duplicated operation, authority,
and lifecycle semantics. Accepted compiler, runtime, installation, and Home
Manager decisions remain in force unless this amendment explicitly changes an
integration contract.

Implementation effort: Deep.

Epoch-local review budget: at most three worker-remediation plus three-axis
review cycles per slice. Attempt to clear every severity. A 0/0/0 round exits
early. After cycle three, progression is allowed only with 0 BLOCKER and 0
IMPORTANT; remaining MINOR findings have the user's confirmed DEFER disposition
and feed this epoch's FOLLOWUP. Any remaining BLOCKER or IMPORTANT is surfaced
to the user. This budget does not modify the general Pasture protocol.

No separate machine-readable GitHub-issue manifest or graph test is created.
This Beads plan/slice graph and live GitHub dependency sections are the
authoritative sequence.

## Architectural correction

Provenance owns one global, append-only journal for persisted domain and
material-work history. Task events are a typed projection of that journal, not
the global ordering primitive.

- `JournalID` is an integer database-generated primary key and the canonical
  deterministic order. Queries order by `JournalID`; `RecordedAt` is audit and
  display metadata only and never establishes causality or authority.
- The journal supertype owns common identity, order, actor, and recorded-time
  fields. Typed subtype tables own task/domain events, committed operations,
  authority lifecycle, decisions/UAT/reviews, and material-work evidence. Common
  fields are not duplicated in subtype rows.
- `OperationID` is a caller-supplied, globally unique, typed alternate key for
  idempotency. It is not the journal primary key and is not duplicated as an
  unrelated source of ordering.
- Every committed logical operation receives a journal entry, including a
  zero-task-event operation. Operation effects and results reference normalized
  journal/effect rows rather than storing competing event-ID lists or JSON
  authorities.
- Authority is normalized into explicit base/bootstrap/assignment lifecycle
  records. Each consuming effect is authorized against the state visible at its
  own `JournalID`. Orphaned evidence and multiply consumed ownership-assignment
  evidence are rejected.
- `Apply` and `Open` use one shared reducer and invariant set. Startup replay,
  live mutation, retry, reopen, cancellation, and projection repair must not
  implement parallel state machines.
- Legacy baseline assignments replay according to the state established at each
  historical `JournalID`, not the final current row. External-schema
  dependencies are preflighted and topology corruption fails closed with an
  actionable error.
- Actor identities are one domain. The Pasture system reserves actor IDs
  0–1023; actor ID 0 is the default Pasture system identity. Ownership changes
  are journaled activities. `Task.Owner` is the current owner while cumulative
  `attributed_to` edges preserve every material contributor.
- Provenance remains usable standalone and may borrow a caller-provided
  DBOS-compatible handle. DBOS integration is built over the journal contract;
  it does not introduce a second persistence or transaction model.

## Worktree boundary

- Aura integration: `/home/minttea/codebases/dayvidpham/aura-plugins/worktree/codex-codegen`
- Pasture integration: `/home/minttea/codebases/dayvidpham/aura-plugins/worktree/codex-codegen/pasture`
- Provenance work is performed in dedicated issue worktrees under the
  Provenance repository's `worktree/` directory.
- Normal worktrees use
  `<repo>-<issue-number>--<semantic-commit>--<short-description>`, where the
  short description is at most three kebab-case words. A dummy or `__dummy__`
  empty checkout may host the named worktree directly in its checkout root.
- Parallel workers receive separate worktrees/branches and commit with
  `git agent-commit`; the supervisor integrates only after prerequisites and
  gates.
- Never use `rm -rf` on a repository, worktree, or user home.

Existing dirty Pasture runtime/codegen work is preserved as an integration
input. Existing Provenance #4/#5 implementation is not treated as canonical
merely because it predates this amendment.

## Revised layer integration points

| Contract | Owning slice | Consumers | Merge timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| global JournalID ordering, typed journal entries/projections, ActorID namespace | S1.0–S1.1 | S1.2–S1.4, S3 | before operation/task integration |
| normalized committed-operation/result/effect and authority lifecycle model | S1.2 | S1.3–S1.4, S3 | after journal base |
| shared Apply/Open reducer, replay/migration invariants, DBOS-compatible borrowed handle | S1.3–S1.4 | S3 | before Pasture task backend |
| opaque Document, semantic IR, EffectSet, typed capability, scanner inventory, neutral artifact bundle | S2 | S3/S4/S5 | S2 before effects/runtime |
| `internal/effects`, Provenance adapter, one `internal/task` package, explicit PolicySet and `ImplUATPayload` | S3 | S4/S6 | after S1+S2 |
| exhaustive version-bounded RuntimeContract plus strict migration gate | S4 | S5 | after S3 |
| native target bundles and simple factual activation/install-state contract | S5 | S6 | after S4 |
| Aura marketplace/Home Manager parity and pinned Pasture promotion | S6 | Impl UAT | after S5 |

`pasture task event list` is a filtered task-event view. The global journal API
and CLI expose complete ordered task, operation, authority, decision, review,
UAT, and material-work history. Downstream code must not infer that every
logical operation produces a task EventID.

## S1 — Provenance global journal and DBOS compatibility

GitHub sequence remains `dayvidpham/provenance#4 -> #5 -> #6`, but those issue
bodies and their Beads leaf graph must be amended before additional production
work is integrated.

### S1.0 — Relational contract and proof corpus (#4)

Document relations, functional dependencies, candidate keys, foreign keys,
BCNF decomposition, typed IDs, journal/subtype totality rules, authority
consumption rules, projection invariants, and legacy-baseline semantics. Add
adversarial histories covering timestamp collisions, zero-task-event
operations, retry/reopen, orphaned and multiply consumed evidence, baseline
transitions, topology corruption, and per-effect authority.

### S1.1 — Journal base and typed projections (#4)

Implement the global journal supertype, database-generated `JournalID`, common
actor/time metadata, typed journal kinds/subtypes, task-event/activity and
attribution projections, system ActorID namespace, and ordered query/API/CLI
surfaces. Establish permanent schema and projection invariant tests.

### S1.2 — Operations, effects, results, and authority (#5)

Implement globally unique typed `OperationID` as an alternate key; normalized
operation/effect/result relations; authority base/bootstrap/assignment
subtypes; atomic append plus domain mutation; zero-task-event operation
anchoring; single-consumption assignment evidence; and exact per-effect
authorization at each `JournalID`.

### S1.3 — Shared reducer, replay, and migration (#5)

Make live `Apply` and startup `Open` call the same reducer/invariant machinery.
Implement idempotent retry, reopen, cancellation/failure recovery, projection
repair, state-at-each-JournalID baseline replay, schema preflight, and fail-closed
topology detection with actionable diagnostics.

### S1.4 — DBOS adapter (#6)

Accept a caller-provided DBOS-compatible handle/abstraction while preserving
standalone construction. Bind deterministic workflow/step guards and restart
semantics to the same `OperationID` and journal contract; do not create a
parallel commit ledger.

### Existing S1 work disposition

Port reusable typed IDs, mutation descriptors/codecs, failure-injection
harnesses, YAML/combinatorial corpora, retry/reopen tests, adversarial histories,
and state-machine proofs into S1.0–S1.4. TaskEvent-only schema, activation,
migration, or duplicated Apply/Open logic is superseded and must be rewritten,
not incrementally declared canonical. Previously reported blockers are retained
as regression cases; they are not patched in isolation when the global-journal
model removes their premise.

## S2 — Typed compiler foundations

Issues: `dayvidpham/pasture#38`, then `#47/#41`; independent `#48`.

Implement opaque Goldmark-backed Document/IR/effects, typed user-decision
request/result, classified scanner inventory, open typed capability API with
`MustDefineCapability`, and neutral deterministic artifact bundle/fs boundary.
This work may continue in parallel where it does not consume the Provenance
contract.

## S3 — Effects and authoritative Pasture task model

Issues: `dayvidpham/pasture#46`, `#14`, `#43`, then same-package `#49`.

Implement process/Git/filesystem effects and opaque guarded-push proof; the
global-journal Provenance/DBOS adapter; task/graph/assignment/review/decision
ledger CLI; AFK, both UAT gates, ratify/land policy, and canonical
`ImplUATPayload`. Preserve the one-way `internal/task -> internal/effects`
package edge.

The decision ledger records both user and agent/system decisions and is
filterable by ActorID. Ownership changes, phase progress, reviews, UAT
decisions, skill runs, assignment start/completion, and attached Git evidence
are typed journal entries. Read-only queries and incidental shell/tool calls are
excluded from this release.

S3 is blocked until S1.0–S1.4 provide the amended contract. Pasture adapters
must consume JournalID-based history and must not reconstruct ordering from
wall-clock timestamps or task-only EventIDs.

## S4 — Runtime contracts and strict source migration

Issues: `dayvidpham/pasture#40`, then `#42`.

Implement exhaustive native/mediated/semantic/unsupported runtime lowering,
logical continuity, version-bounded external bindings, and staged scanner-first
migration followed by the strict rejection gate. Reconcile pre-existing dirty
runtime/codegen work deliberately.

## S5 — Native outputs and activation

Issues: target outputs `#24/#27/#45`, artifact boundary `#48`, then activation
`#39`.

Generate native Claude Code/OpenCode/Codex skills, agents, and default-off hooks;
implement simple installer/config preferences and factual install-state
inventory; use native plugin managers/registries; verify real fixed-output host
artifacts in isolated state. OpenCode hooks are embedded TypeScript, not npm.

## S6 — Aura distribution and Home Manager parity

Issues: `dayvidpham/aura-plugins#9`, then `#8`.

Publish aggregate marketplace/pinned Pasture inputs and nested Home Manager

description:
Files: internal/journal/replay.go (ProjectionDivergenceError, ErrProjectionDivergence),
internal/sqlite/replay.go (ReplayProjections -> diffTaskProjections -> divergence()).

This is the fail-closed convergence guard §9.2/§15 promises: "Open's full
replay ... verifies convergence with the stored incremental projection (§15),
failing closed with a typed ProjectionDivergenceError". It is one of the
three headline typed errors this slice introduces (alongside
MigrationOwnerUnmappableError and SchemaPreflightError) and is part of the
public JournalAPI surface documented in journal_api.go.

`grep -rln "ProjectionDivergenceError\|ErrProjectionDivergence" --include="*_test.go" .`
returns NO results anywhere in the repo. Every existing replay-related corpus
case either (a) exercises the happy convergent path (replay succeeds, no
divergence) or (b) exercises a *schema*-preflight failure (a different typed
error, SchemaPreflightError, raised BEFORE any fold even starts) — none of
them ever drive projectJournalRowLocked/diffTaskProjections into an actual
mismatch between the stored incremental projection and the freshly-replayed
one.

Unlike SchemaPreflightError (covered by
AdversarialAddColumn/AdversarialDropColumn/AdversarialDropTable seams) there
is no adversarial seam that corrupts a task's stored projection out-of-band
(e.g. a raw UPDATE tasks SET owner_id=... bypassing the reducer) so that
ReplayProjections can be proven to detect and reject it. The
divergence-detection code path (snapshotTaskProjectionsLocked +
diffTaskProjections) is therefore completely unverified — a latent bug there
(e.g. wrong before/after snapshot ordering, wrong field comparison) would
ship silently.

Fix: add an adversarial seam (e.g. AdversarialCorruptTaskProjection(task,
field, value) writing directly to tasks.* bypassing the reducer, analogous to
the existing AdversarialAddColumn/AdversarialDropColumn seams) plus a
must-fail corpus case that corrupts a task's stored owner/status/watermark
after a normal Apply, then calls ReplayProjections and asserts a typed
*ProjectionDivergenceError with the corrupted field named and non-empty
why/impact/fix (mirroring the six-field-contract assertions already used for
MigrationOwnerUnmappableError/SchemaPreflightError).

File: internal/sqlite/fact_conditions_test.go, TestConditionFirstFailureIndex (~line 274).

WHAT: TestConditionFirstFailureIndex verifies that the first failing condition's index is reported, but only for the case where BOTH conditions fail (two asserting nonexistent JIDs). It asserts index=0. There is no test where condition[0] passes and condition[1] fails, verifying index=1 is returned.

WHY: checkConditionsLocked iterates in order and returns on first failure. The index field in ConditionFailure must equal the position of the first-failing condition in the slice. This is only meaningful when conditions BEFORE the failing one actually PASS. Without a nonzero index test, a bug that always returns index=0 regardless of position would not be caught.

WHERE: internal/sqlite/fact_conditions_test.go:274-300 — only tests cf.Index == 0

WHEN: At test time.

IMPACT: Missing proof that first-failure index is correct when some conditions pass first. Could mask an off-by-one error in index tracking.

FIX: Add a test: commit a valid decision, then submit an operation with two conditions: condition[0]=CurrentFact asserting the actual latest JID (passes); condition[1]=CurrentFact asserting JID=9999 (fails). Assert cf.Index == 1, cf.Kind == ConditionCurrentFact, cf.Reason == ConditionFactMissing.

acceptance_criteria:
Cancellation changes nothing.

After confirmation Pasture preserves unrelated YAML and saves preferences before
native actions. It normalizes the confirmed preferences to one immutable
`pasture.install.effective-selection/v1` desired document, then passes that to
`apply-selection --source installer`. TUI effective cells are
`harness && extension`. The persisted config remains simple global preferences
and never stores the normalized matrix or installation evidence.

The fixed reconciler is deliberately small:

- desired effective true: idempotently ensure present/update, including an
  unchanged true cell;
- desired effective false plus a Pasture-managed installed/unknown inventory
  record: inspect and idempotently remove the exact component; and
- desired false with no Pasture-managed or uncertain record: no mutation.

Thus first-run false harnesses are untouched, a failed uninstall remains visible
and retryable after the preference already says false, and unrelated native
installations or identical external files are observed but never claimed or
removed. A global extension change fans out across the currently desired and
recorded managed cells.

The installer applies all cells, including its own direct-file destinations.
Home Manager independently renders the same effective schema from its per-
harness children but calls only native-managed cells; Nix owns direct-file link
transitions. Schema-validation, normalization, transition, and source-ownership
fixtures prove the two inputs agree for equivalent choices without conflating
their execution responsibilities.

Save failure invokes no native action. Any native/file failure stops immediately;
the postcondition probe updates the factual inventory where possible, earlier
completed actions remain, and later actions are unattempted. The error names what
failed, why, the cell/path/manager and stage, what remains or is unknown, caller
impact, `pasture install status`, and the exact executor-aware tagged
remediation. There is no rollback, background recovery, lock, authorization, or
cross-cell transaction coordinator. Native managers own plugin/update/cache
state; Pasture never writes private caches.

Pasture #45 publishes the exact legacy and split Claude package identities plus
fixtures; #39 alone owns this compatibility behavior. Before mutation #39
classifies native state as empty, exact v0.0.4 monolith only, split only, exact
monolith plus complete/partial known splits, or unknown. Unknown identity,
scope, version, or duplicate/conflicting rows perform zero mutation. For each
known state the frozen order is: probe/list and validate; ensure/update every
desired split; verify it; remove the exact user-scoped v0.0.4 monolith; verify
absence; remove any unselected known split; verify final state; record the
inventory. Failure at every action stops later actions, probes and records what
actually remains, and the next ordinary run resumes reconciliation without
rollback. Codex hooks finish as installed-but-requiring-native-trust-review until
the user approves them in Codex; this trust state is reported, not bypassed.

The v0.0.4 monolith transition is selection-wide and is implemented exclusively
by `apply-selection`, which has every Claude sibling's desired state. While the
monolith or an incomplete legacy transition exists, `apply-cell` fails before
mutation and instructs the caller to rerun the full installer/TUI or Home Manager
activation with an exhaustive desired selection. It never guesses sibling
intent, and a cell-level failure row prints that same full-selection remedy.

The group probes even for an all-false/no-inventory selection so the approved
monolith exception is discoverable when the supported manager is available. If
that optional read-only probe is missing, out-of-range, nonzero, or malformed,
all three never-recorded false rows are `completed` with operation
`no_op_unavailable` and a nonfatal diagnostic that unverified legacy state was
preserved; no inventory or mutation occurs. A supported valid-empty probe is the
same completed no-op, while an exact monolith enters the group removal.

A syntactically valid optional all-false/no-inventory response containing an
exact split component, near-match monolith, wrong scope/version, unknown selector,
or duplicate/conflicting rows performs zero mutation and writes no inventory.
Exact split components are reported `completed/no_op_preserved_external` with
their observed identity; near-match/unknown/duplicate/conflicting state is
`completed/no_op_preserved_ambiguous` with `ok=true` plus a preservation
diagnostic. This optional mode succeeds because no desired or managed cell
requires authority and preservation is the requested behavior.

If any Claude cell is desired true or has managed/unknown inventory, the same
initial probe failure is terminal before mutation: the first canonical required
row is `failed`, other executable rows are `unattempted`, prior inventory is
unchanged, and remediation names the exact binary/version/response repair.

In required mode, an exact desired split already present without inventory is
observed external and may satisfy desired true without adoption; an exact
external split under desired false is preserved. A near-match, wrong scope/
version, unknown selector, duplicate, or conflicting response is terminal
`failed/ambiguous_native_state` before mutation, leaves prior inventory unchanged,
and uses the appropriate ApplySelection/RerunInstaller or RerunHomeManager tagged
remediation. A managed/unknown inventory record that no longer matches exact live
identity is likewise a terminal conflict, never silently externalized.

The group crosses the classified legacy state with
all eight Claude desired combinations, executes each ensure/remove exactly once,
and skips the three ordinary Claude executors. On failure, it live-inspects all
three cells: rows already satisfying desired state are `completed`; the first
canonical unsatisfied row is `failed` with `group_stage` and the exact native
action; other unsatisfied Claude rows and later executable native rows are
`unattempted`. If all split postconditions match but monolith removal alone
fails, `claude-code.skills` is the fixed control/failure row and the diagnostic
names that shared legacy stage. Home Manager declarative rows remain live-
inspected `managed_declaratively`. Full-selection retry repeats the group probe
and converges without duplicate per-cell actions.

If live inspection after an action failure is itself missing/nonzero/malformed,
only rows with already verified individual postconditions remain `completed`.
The action-owning row is `failed` with both primary action and secondary probe
diagnostics and its inventory observation `unknown`; every other unverified
Claude cell is `unattempted`/`unknown`. No row is guessed from desired state.
Ordinary full-selection retry repairs the probe first and resumes from factual
inventory/live inspection.

## 16. BDD acceptance criteria

1. **Given** a typed Document, **when** constructors accept it, **then** every
   part is immutable/validated with source location and Goldmark AST, **and should
   not** expose a mutable optional-field runtime bag.
2. **Given** the canonical source roots and active-owner manifest, **when**
   inventory and strict compilation run, **then** independent discovery detects
   missing/stale/dead/symlinked owners, the scan is deterministic/read-only, a
   nonzero unclassified count blocks the gate, and post-zero native syntax names
   owner/node/range/fix with no output, **and should not** let the manifest hide
   an unlisted file or use regex-rewrite semantics.
3. **Given** a supported runtime contract, **when** an operation compiles,
   **then** exactly one exhaustive binding preserves its semantic contract and
   native fixtures pass.
4. **Given** an out-of-range/newer host or missing binding, **when** generation
   runs, **then** it fails actionably, **and should not** guess compatibility or a
   similarly named call.
5. **Given** a fresh agent continues an assignment, **when** it starts, **then**
   role/assignment/task/worktree/evidence/decisions/outstanding work are restored,
   **and should not** require session continuity.
6. **Given** SelectMany, **when** native UI lacks parity, **then** validated parent
   text returns the same distinct OptionIDs and verbatim record or reports
   unsupported, **and should not** become SelectOne.
7. **Given** an external typed capability, **when** its package contributes and
   invokes a binding through opaque descriptors, **then** its typed ID/version,
   codecs/effects/postconditions hold and exactly one compatible binding composes
   without editing #40, **and should not** expose a tool name/map or accept a

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-38 — Typed multi-harness compiler and authoritative task journal

## 1. Decision and correction from Proposal 37

Pasture will compile opaque, validated Go `Document` values into native Claude
Code, OpenCode, and Codex artifacts. Portable meaning lives in a
protocol-semantic IR. Markdown is parsed with Goldmark, not searched and rewritten
as an operational language. Native runtime calls are emitted only through an
exhaustive, version-bounded runtime contract.

Provenance will own one generic, ordered TaskEvent journal and the transaction
boundary that commits task/graph/Activity state with its events. Current task
tables remain authoritative; the journal explains post-migration changes and is
not an event-sourced replacement for historical state. Pasture owns typed
`pasture.*` event definitions and the `pasture task` CLI that generated workflows
use instead of Beads.

Native plugin registration is deliberately separate from runtime semantics. A
versioned activation contract describes public version probes, exact manager
commands or config mutation, package identities, and standalone destinations.
`pasture install` keeps the user's simple preferences separate from a narrow,
factual installation-state inventory. That inventory records what Pasture
confirmed it installed or removed, what remains, and the last actionable
failure. It is not a pending-operation queue, rollback log, authorization
system, lock, or cross-cell transaction coordinator.

Proposal 38 retains all accepted Proposal 37 invariants and resolves every
Proposal 37 Terra finding. OpenCode hooks are generated as an embedded,
auto-discovered TypeScript file for this wave; no npm publication or native npm
plugin mutation is required before the hook behavior has been verified. Target
packages publish target identity plus RuntimeContractID, while #39 alone binds
those artifacts into opaque activation contracts. Provenance lands as the strict
chain #4 -> #5 -> #14, with #4 dormant until #5 activates atomic journaling and
the migration baseline. Upstream issues publish fixtures/oracles; downstream
Aura issues alone own Home Manager parity and real `pasture-stable` promotion.
The proposal also freezes deployable embedded artifact bundles, observed
installation-state and retry semantics, authenticated-claim-free actor
resolution, one-subject/one-round clean-review evidence, complete event query
and legacy import semantics, the exhaustive nine-cell test matrix, and the
canonical implementation worktrees.

The user explicitly deferred the separate Plan UAT while unavailable. After all
three proposal reviewers reach a clean 0/0/0 consensus, the architect ratifies
this proposal and the same primary agent continues as implementation supervisor.
Planning questions and every agent judgment call are retained in a decision
ledger with alternatives, rationale, affected surfaces, and provisional choice;
they are presented together for explicit disposition at Implementation UAT.
Deferral changes timing, not acceptance coverage, and nothing is silently
dropped.

## 4. Opaque typed Document API

The following shows semantics, not exported mutable field layout:

```go
type Document struct { /* unexported validated parts */ }
type Part interface { /* closed within compiler package */ }
type RenderedTree struct { /* immutable validated relative files */ }

func NewDocument(parts ...Part) (Document, error)
func Markdown(source []byte, at Location) (Part, error)
func Operation(op SemanticOperation, at Location) (Part, error)
func Verbatim(content []byte, at Location) (Part, error)
func TargetLiteral(cases []TargetCase, at Location) (Part, error)
func Compile(document Document, target Target) (RenderedTree, error)
```

`Markdown` parses once through Goldmark. Its unexported AST segments reference an
owned immutable source buffer. Constructors retain source locations and reject
invalid states before a document exists.

`Verbatim` is a portable fragment preserved without operational interpretation.
`TargetLiteral` is a narrow raw-native escape. Across the requested target set it
contains exactly one validated `LiteralFor(RuntimeContractID, content, reason)`
or `LiteralUnsupported(harness, reason)` per enabled harness. Missing, duplicate,
or out-of-range cases fail. Target literals cannot masquerade as portable
operations.

Compilation stages are explicit:

```text
typed Go specs
  -> validated Document and Goldmark AST
  -> semantic/type/dataflow validation
  -> runtime contract selection
  -> exhaustive operation/effect/capability lowering
  -> target rendering and package projection
  -> native schema/loader validation
```

Diagnostics carry canonical owner, file/section and AST source range, semantic
operation, target contract, failed stage/time, caller impact, and concrete fix.
Compilation and every native schema/loader check operate entirely in memory and
return either one immutable complete #38-owned `RenderedTree` or an error plus no
tree. The compiler never opens an output path before successful validation, so
an existing output tree remains byte-identical on any compile/lower/load error.
Filesystem publication is a later #46 effect with its own explicit per-path
result and failure semantics. Successful publication is exact-tree convergence
over a publisher-owned generated root: reconcile create/update/remove against a
canonical prior-output manifest stored at a derived same-parent sidecar path
`.<payload-root>.pasture-manifest.json`, never inside the payload root, then
verify the payload root's final path/type/mode/content set equals the complete
`RenderedTree`. The payload grammar cannot name the sidecar, and an existing
unowned/unsafe sidecar is an actionable pre-mutation conflict. A failed publish
retains explicit partial results and the last confirmed manifest; retrying the
same RenderedTree may resume only paths whose live state equals either the old
manifest or that desired tree. It never claims rollback or compiler failure.
Unowned roots, unrelated file states, and changing the desired tree across an
unreconciled partial publish fail actionably before further mutation rather than
deleting unknown files. Publication verifies payload equality first and replaces
the sidecar manifest last using create-exclusive temp/write/flush/rename. Success
requires both exact payload and the new manifest; a failure before/during/after
that final replacement is explicit partial state eligible only for same-tree
retry.

## 5. Protocol-semantic IR

Semantic operations are closed concrete variants behind validating constructors,
not optional-field bags and not tool-name/arguments maps.

### 5.1 Orchestration and logical continuity

The closed orchestration set is:

- `InvokeSkill`
- `DelegateAssignment`
- `ContinueAssignment`
- `SendAssignmentMessage`
- `CollectAssignmentResults`
- `StopAssignment`
- `RequestUserDecision`

Collections plus `independent`, `dependency-ordered`, or `bounded-parallel`
scheduling metadata express parallelism. Claude teams, OpenCode tasks, and Codex
agent handles are backend details.

Every delegation/continuation carries a validated logical context:

```go
type AssignmentContext struct {
    Role        protocol.RoleID
    Assignment protocol.AssignmentRef
    Task        protocol.TaskRef
    Worktree    WorktreeRef
    Evidence    []EvidenceRef
    Decisions   []DecisionRef
    Outstanding []WorkItemRef
    Mutations   []MutationContinuation
    Bindings    RuntimeBindings
}

type MutationContinuation struct {
    Ref         protocol.MutationRef
    Authority   MutationAuthority // exact initiating assignment or bootstrap actor
    Request     ResolvedMutationRequest // operation, schema, and immutable canonical request bytes
    Command     CanonicalCommandDigest
    Results     []ResultSlotDeclaration
    Scope       LexicalScopeSnapshot // exact typed bindings visible at construction
}

type MutationAuthority interface { mutationAuthority() }
// InitiatingAssignment(protocol.AssignmentRef) | BootstrapActor(protocol.AgentRef)
```

The target may resume an existing agent or spawn a fresh one. Both are correct
only when the full context above is reconstructed. Runtime session identity is
never the assignment identity.

Core #38 owns only the portable opaque `protocol.AssignmentRef` and
`protocol.TaskRef` used in generated documents. It does not import Provenance or
wait for #5. After the coordinated Provenance release, #14/#43 validate and
convert those refs to Provenance `AssignmentID`/`TaskID`; runtime bindings carry
the portable refs unchanged across a harness boundary. `protocol.RoleID` maps
through #43 to a typed `AssignmentRoleID`, and each Pasture-defined slot
constructor accepts only the matching role/axis. Raw strings never bridge these
ID domains.

Reusable artifacts never embed concrete runtime task, assignment, review, or
Provenance operation IDs. #38 owns opaque typed `BindingKey[T]` and
`ValueRef[T]` values for context inputs and prior operation results. Every
operation declares typed result slots; runtime lowering validates JSON result
schemas, binds concrete `TaskRef`, `AssignmentRef`, `ReviewRoundRef`, and other
values into the current lexical assignment scope, and later operations consume
only matching typed refs. Missing, duplicate, wrong-type, or out-of-scope
bindings fail before invocation.

#38 also owns portable `protocol.MutationRef`, distinct from
`SemanticOperationID` and Provenance `OperationID`. Mutation construction is
explicitly two-stage. After resolving every typed ValueRef, the runtime first
calls #43's pure, side-effect-free `pasture task command canonicalize` API with
the versioned typed operation/request. #43 returns normalized command identity
plus `CanonicalCommandDigest` without a MutationRef or state query. Only then
does the parent mint one fresh MutationRef and durably record the complete
`MutationContinuation`: exact initiating AssignmentRef or registered bootstrap
AgentRef, semantic operation and request schema, immutable canonical resolved
request bytes, canonical digest, typed result declarations, and a frozen lexical
scope snapshot. This durable record is sufficient to reconstruct the exact
request before any stateful attempt; neither a non-invertible digest nor a later
`AssignmentContext` is treated as request storage. The first
stateful attempt receives that continuation; #43 recomputes canonical bytes from
the resolved request and rejects zero/placeholder/mismatched/caller-invented
digests before lookup or mutation. The same continuation is reused across retry
or fresh-agent continuation. #14/#43
validates and deterministically maps it into the durable Provenance OperationID
namespace. Distinct logical invocations always mint distinct refs; conflicting
reuse fails without writes. CLI JSON accepts one typed `--mutation-ref` plus the
typed initiating authority and returns canonical typed result bindings.

For every `pasture task` operation, #43 is the sole producer of canonical task-
command bytes and `CanonicalCommandDigest`. #14 owns a typed, byte-preserving
conversion to Provenance `CommandDigest`; it neither accepts a caller-supplied
digest nor recanonicalizes the command. #5 records exactly that converted digest
in both `LookupCommitted` and `Apply`. #40 passes the typed task request and
MutationContinuation to #43 unchanged and never maps MutationRef/OperationID or
calls #5 directly. The canonicalization CLI/API is read-only and emitted before
every generated task mutation; exact schemas ensure a fresh agent reconstructs
byte-identical request/digest before retry.

Replay lookup uses MutationRef/OperationID, canonical command, historical ActorID,
and exact typed initiating authority identity: AssignmentID plus assignment kind/
slot/task, or registered-bootstrap identity. If that exact
operation already committed, it returns the original result even when the
initiating assignment is now ended or responsibility transferred. If it has not
committed, the same assignment must still be active/current (or the bootstrap
actor registered) inside the conditional batch. A new MutationRef naming an
ended assignment writes nothing. Runtime continuation never re-resolves the
actor from whichever assignment happens to be current later. Two assignments for
the same AgentID, two slots, wrong-task authority, and bootstrap versus assignment
are replay conflicts, not aliases.

Within one ConditionalMutationBatch, #5 owns canonical typed local handles such
as `LocalTaskRef` and `LocalAssignmentRef`. Later mutations in the same batch may
refer to those handles; the canonical result maps them to allocated IDs. Same-
operation replay returns the same map, so `review start` creates and returns its
round, three axis tasks, and assignments atomically without pre-baked IDs.

Provenance #5 owns the authoritative assignment aggregate rather than leaving
`AssignmentID` as free evidence supplied by generated prose. Its public IDs are
opaque validated string types (`AssignmentID`, `AssignmentSlotID`, and
`AssignmentRoleID`), and its
immutable lifecycle projection contains the task, agent, slot, role, status,
start/end EventIDs and timestamps, and optional predecessor assignment. Exactly
one assignment may be active for a `(TaskID, AssignmentSlotID)` pair.

`StartTaskAssignment`, `EndTaskAssignment`, and assignment transfer use the same
atomic `Apply`/`OperationID` boundary as task mutations. A new child assignment
requires either an active parent AssignmentID or a registered bootstrap
SoftwareAgent, so the first assignment is explicit without creating a circular
dependency.

Task responsibility is role-neutral: architect, supervisor, worker, and reviewer
tasks all use the active owner-responsibility assignment as the sole assignment
authority for `Task.Owner`. `TransferTaskResponsibility`
atomically checks expected owner/assignment, ends the predecessor, starts the
successor, updates Owner (including assigned-to-unassigned), preserves
attribution, and writes events. Standalone owner mutation delegates to this
transition or rejects once assignment semantics are active. Closing a task ends
its owner-responsibility assignment and clears Owner in the same transaction. Reopen leaves the
task unassigned and requires an explicit new responsibility assignment; it never
reactivates an ended one.

Generic assignment start/end is limited to non-owner slots. Initial owner
assignment is a transfer from expected unassigned state; an owner-responsibility
assignment cannot end except inside responsibility transfer or task closure.

The IMPL_PLAN's own active owner-responsibility assignment has RoleSupervisor and
authorizes closure of child slices through an explicit `governs(parent, slice)`
relationship; there is no duplicate supervisor slot on the parent and it is
non-owning only relative to each child. Reviewer assignments are owner-
responsibility assignments on their own axis review tasks, with typed
correctness/test-quality/elegance roles. Duplicate, stale, ended, superseded,
wrong-task, wrong-slot, and concurrent start/end/transfer cases write nothing.

### 5.2 User decisions

`RequestUserDecision` has result modes `SelectOne`, `SelectMany`, and `FreeText`.
It includes the full question, all option IDs/labels/descriptions, any code or
definition shown, result validation, and verbatim answer capture. A native widget
is used only if its request/result contract preserves those semantics. Otherwise
the parent performs a validated textual interaction; if neither is possible, the
operation is unsupported rather than silently narrowed.

### 5.3 Task/workflow effects

Task effects cover the entire approved surface:

- lifecycle: create, show, update, close/reopen, list, ready, blocked, dependency
  tree;
- typed task-to-task relationships: blocked-by, derived-from, supersedes,
  discovered-from, contains, and governs;
- responsibility assignment start/end/transfer with owner CAS plus non-owner
  supervision and reviewer assignment operations;
- typed task-to-Agent attribution add/query;
- label/comment mutations and queries;
- typed task-linked Activity start/end/query using `ActivityID`;
- typed transition/supersede/ratify/land operations and assignment/review/UAT/
  skill/git material events;
- secondary event-context add/query; and
- ordered task event/timeline queries.

Work completion is not task closure. A worker ends its task-linked Activity and
records a typed `pasture.assignment.completed` material event, but never closes a
slice. `CloseTask` is the reviewed task-status transition reserved to the
supervisor/protocol owner after the required review gate. There is no ambiguous
`CompleteTask` mutation or `pasture task complete` command.

Review identity is an explicit task-graph aggregate, not three loosely related
events:

```go
type ReviewRoundID string
type DocumentRevisionID string
type TaskCandidateID string
type IntegrationCandidateSetID string

type ReviewSubject interface {
    reviewSubject()
    ReviewRef() ReviewSubjectRef
}
type DocumentRevisionSubject struct {
    ID            DocumentRevisionID
    DocumentTask  TaskID
    ContentDigest ContentDigest
}
type ImplementationCandidateSubject struct {
    ID          TaskCandidateID
    SliceTask   TaskID
    Repository  RepositoryID
    CommitOID   GitOID
    TreeDigest  ContentDigest
}
type IntegrationCandidateSetSubject struct {
    ID              IntegrationCandidateSetID
    IntegrationTask TaskID
    Repositories    []RepositoryCandidate // canonical unique RepositoryID order
}
type ReviewSubjectRef struct {
    Kind       ReviewSubjectKind
    SnapshotID TaskID
}

type SliceCloseAuthorization struct {
    SupervisorAssignmentID AssignmentID
    RoundID      ReviewRoundID
    CandidateID  TaskCandidateID
    ReviewEvents [3]provenance.EventID
}
```

`ReviewSubject` is a closed sum. All variants are immutable protected subject
tasks stored in the ordinary Provenance task/relationship tables. #5 contributes
a generic immutable snapshot task kind/constructor whose payload bytes and
digest can never be update/close/reopened; it also CASes exact typed relationship
sets without learning Pasture semantics. #43 validates the subject variants and
payload codecs before constructing those generic snapshots.
Each variant has exactly one canonical identity, a validated const-string wrapper
over its immutable snapshot TaskID. `ReviewRef()` derives the closed sum-level
`ReviewSubjectRef{Kind, SnapshotID}` from that sole identity; it is never stored
as a second independently supplied ID. Constructors prove kind and payload
agreement. `DocumentRevisionID` is deliberately not named `TaskRevisionID`, so
it cannot be confused with Provenance's mutable-task CAS revision token.

`DocumentRevisionSubject` snapshots the exact protocol task ID, immutable body
revision ID, and canonical sha256 digest of title plus every reviewed body field
(description, design, acceptance, and typed amendment fields). Labels, comments,
owner/status, and audit metadata are excluded and cannot change the reviewed
body. `protocol create` creates the initial revision subject plus one reserved
`current-revision` relationship atomically. A PROPOSAL body is never edited:
changes create PROPOSAL-N+1 and supersede the old task. Other protocol documents
use typed `protocol revise` to create a new immutable revision and atomically
replace `current-revision`; if a round is live it closes/cancels/terminally
disposes it and resolves its dependencies in that same batch, and any prior
finalized review/UAT evidence remains historical but ineligible. Plan
review start/finalize, the typed Plan-UAT deferral event, and ratify all require
the same exact current revision relationship and digest.

Proposal replacement never uses document `revise`. Typed `protocol supersede`
accepts the expected canonical proposal/revision plus a newly created
PROPOSAL-N+1 revision. In one conditional batch it makes the new proposal the
sole canonical proposal, relates the successor as `supersedes` the old proposal,
terminalizes any live old review round and all axes/assignments/dependencies,
invalidates any old Plan-UAT decision/deferral, and marks the old proposal
superseded. Finalized review and UAT records remain immutable history but are
ineligible for the successor. Concurrent review start/submit/finalize, Plan UAT,
ratify, and competing supersede operations have one winner; every stale loser
writes nothing. Ratification CASes the sole canonical proposal relationship.

`ImplementationCandidateSubject` stores repository identity, exact immutable Git
commit OID, base evidence, and canonical tree digest. Initial
`pasture task slice candidate set --expected none --commit ...` creates the
protected subject and `current-candidate` relationship only when the slice has no
candidate and no live round. Later deliverable bytes use only typed `slice
rework`, whose reason is a closed sum:

- `address_findings` is legal only after all three axis inventories have
  submitted. It requires at least one finding, a distinct replacement commit/tree
  identity, and a typed `FindingDisposition` for every finding across all three
  inventories. Each disposition binds the FindingID to worker Activity, Git
  evidence, test evidence, and the exact C2 subject claimed to address it.
- `independent_content_replacement` is legal whenever the slice/integration task
  is not closed/landed and has no live finding-bearing round: before any round,
  during a partial or all-submitted clean round, after clean finalize, after UAT,
  or after publication. It requires a distinct replacement, material-work
  Activity, and explicit drift/change reason. A live partial round is invalidated
  without claiming complete inventories; finalized review/UAT/publication remain
  immutable history but lose current eligibility.

Omitting a finding/evidence from `address_findings`, attempting that mode before
all three submissions, using independent replacement while a finding belongs to
the current subject/current live round,
binding evidence to a different replacement, or attempting C1 -> C1 writes
nothing.

The exact rework state table is total:

| Old subject state | Legal mode | Preserved terminal state | Batch changes before C2 swap |
|---|---|---|---|
| no round | independent | none | no review branch to terminalize |
| partial/all-submitted clean live round | independent | already-closed groups/axes and already-ended `submitted_clean` assignments remain byte-identical | close only open groups/axes as `invalidated_by_independent_subject_replacement`, end only live assignments, close round with that outcome |
| live finding-bearing round with fewer than three submissions | neither | submitted inventory remains live | reject until all three inventories submit |
| all three submitted with findings | address_findings | already-terminal clean axes/assignments remain byte-identical | close open findings/groups/finding-bearing axes, resolve dual-parent edges, close round `REVISE_REPLACED` |
| clean finalized, post-UAT, or post-publication | independent | finalized ACCEPT round, UAT decision, and publication events remain immutable history | invalidate/remove only their current eligibility relations and coverage; no second terminal disposition |
| slice closed or integration landed | neither | terminal artifact | reject with no writes |

The `address_findings` batch closes submitted findings as
`addressed_by_candidate_rework`; their severity groups close as
`superseded_by_candidate_rework`; BLOCKER edges to both group and reviewed task
are resolved; only still-open finding-bearing axis tasks close
`superseded_by_candidate_rework`; already-terminal clean axes/assignments are
unchanged; the round closes `REVISE_REPLACED`; and all old
dependency/current-round edges resolve. The batch then creates C2, binds every
finding disposition and fix evidence to C2, and swaps the exact
`current-candidate` relationship. Independent replacement follows the table,
invalidates any current UAT/publication/close authorization, installs C2, and
swaps the relation; it never rewrites a prior terminal task/disposition or emits
`addressed_by_candidate_rework`.
The old candidate and finding graph remain immutable history. A successor round
can start only on C2 and later relates itself to the terminal predecessor; the
same subject can never be the successor of a finding-bearing round.

`IntegrationCandidateSetSubject` is the final multi-repository deliverable. Each
epoch has one authoritative integration task governed by its IMPL_PLAN. Initial
`integration candidate-set --expected none` is legal only with no current set or
live integration round. It creates exactly one immutable
`RepositoryCandidate{RepositoryID,CommitOID,TreeDigest,ExpectedRemoteRef,
ExpectedOldOID}` per repository and atomically attaches the canonical unique set
through `current-integration-candidate`.

Every later merge, rebase, fix, repository-set, commit, tree, or ref change uses
typed `integration rework`, never `candidate-set`. One conditional batch checks
the expected current set and requires a distinct new set. It uses the same closed
reason sum and total algorithm as slice rework. Finding-addressing replacement
waits for all three inventories and binds every finding/group/BLOCKER edge to
complete Activity/Git/test evidence for the new set. Independent replacement is
allowed in every nonterminal no-finding state in the total table and records that
partial inventories were invalidated, not completed. Every open axis, live assignment,
round, and dependency receives its mode-specific terminal state before the exact
current-set swap. The batch also invalidates current
Implementation-UAT and publication-evidence relations, creates the new immutable
set, and swaps `current-integration-candidate`. Finalized review/UAT/publication
evidence remains historical but ineligible. A successor review can start only on
the new set, so no obsolete finding or `current-round` can strand the integration
task. Per-slice reviews prove slices; only a clean-reviewed and currently
accepted integration set is eligible to publish and land.

Plan and Implementation UAT are closed protected decisions, not comment
conventions. They distinguish ordinary interview interaction from actionable
feedback and from questions deliberately held for a later gate:

```go

type UATFeedbackItemID string

type LedgerEntrySource interface { ledgerEntrySource() }

}

}
```
