
The decision ledger is revisioned by the same `DocumentRevisionID` and reserved
`current-revision` relationship as every other protected protocol document; it
does not define a competing ledger-specific revision identity or topology. Each
entry has one stable `DecisionLedgerEntryID`, a closed source, exact
question/decision and stimulus digests, alternatives, rationale, and affected
surfaces. UAT requirement is derived, never caller supplied. The ordinary
owner-authorized append producer always derives `SourceAgentJudgment` from the
exact mutation authority and requires user coverage until a typed UAT resolution
names that EntryID. `SourceUserConfirmed` can be produced only by referencing an
exact protected registered-human decision/interaction evidence ID whose task,
human decider, question, complete options/definition/command stimulus, verbatim
answer, and decision digests match the new ledger entry. The command revalidates
that evidence atomically; unbacked, stale, wrong-task, wrong-entry, wrong-human,
wrong-stimulus, cross-ledger, legacy, or otherwise unproven input is never
user-confirmed and conservatively becomes/requires `SourceAgentJudgment`
coverage. Appending any entry creates a successor `DocumentRevisionID` that
preserves all prior entry IDs and exact bytes. A Plan deferral binds its exact
revision; Implementation UAT binds the exact current successor revision and
proves that it extends the Plan-bound revision without modifying/removing any
prior entry.

`DECISION_LEDGER` is a protected protocol-document kind owned by #43. Typed
`protocol create --kind decision-ledger` creates the ledger task, its initial
immutable `DocumentRevisionSubject`, the sole `current-revision` relation, and a
RoleArchitect owner-responsibility assignment. Typed `protocol revise --kind
decision-ledger --expected-revision ... --append-agent-judgment ...` is the
ordinary owner mutation; a separate closed `--append-user-confirmed
--human-decision-evidence ...` form is accepted only after the exact protected
evidence checks above. These are its only
content mutation. It accepts one or more new stable EntryIDs, requires every
prior entry byte-identical and in the same order, rejects duplicate/modified/
removed entries, creates one immutable successor snapshot, and swaps the current
relation in one conditional batch. At handoff the ordinary responsibility-
transfer primitive changes the ledger owner from architect to the governing
RoleSupervisor while preserving attribution/history; only the active ledger
owner may append. Same-MutationRef replay returns the same revision/EntryIDs;
concurrent/stale append has one winner and every fault commits all rows or none.
`protocol show`/ordinary task show reads a named revision without mutation.

Every Plan UAT decision binds the exact current ledger revision, regardless of
verdict. Appending any ledger entry after accepted Implementation UAT
atomically invalidates/removes `current-implementation-uat` and its land
eligibility while preserving the decision snapshot as history. Land CASes the
exact current ledger revision and recomputed required-entry/coverage digest from
the accepted UAT. Append/UAT/land races therefore have one winner: append-first
requires a fresh complete UAT; land-first makes the epoch terminal and later
ledger append rejects.

`pasture task uat plan-decide` resolves the registered human and architect-controlled
Plan-UAT task and exact canonical proposal revision. Every interaction must
preserve its exact question, all option descriptions, any definition/command
shown, and verbatim answer; it needs no disposition. Every actionable feedback
item must preserve the user's verbatim feedback and one user-confirmed FIX-NOW
or DEFER disposition. The total Plan decision table is disjoint:

| Reported verdict | Required shape | Forbidden shape | Ratify effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accepted` | exact current ledger revision; zero held questions; no FIX-NOW feedback | deferral text; any held question | eligible |
| `changes_requested` | exact current ledger revision; zero held questions; at least one confirmed FIX-NOW | deferral text | ineligible |
| `deferred_to_implementation_uat` | nonempty verbatim deferral; at least one stable held question; exact immutable ledger revision; no FIX-NOW feedback | missing/duplicate held IDs, mutable TaskID-only ledger, or fabricated held answer/disposition | eligible only under this user's explicit authorization |

`accepted` produces protected
`pasture.plan-uat.accepted/v1`, transitions that UAT
task to accepted, and installs its immutable decision snapshot through
`current-plan-uat`. `changes_requested` produces
`pasture.plan-uat.changes-requested/v1`, transitions the UAT task accordingly,
and is not ratify-eligible. The exact deferral produces protected
`pasture.plan-uat.deferred/v1`, transitions the task to deferred, and is the only
non-accepted result eligible for this user-authorized ratification. It does not
discard acceptance: held questions, prior interactions, feedback, and the ledger
must be presented at Implementation UAT.

`pasture task uat implementation-decide` resolves the registered human,
supervisor-controlled Implementation-UAT task, exact current integration set,
exact current Plan decision, and exact current ledger revision. It computes the
required closed set: every Plan feedback ID deferred at that gate, every
`SourceAgentJudgment` ledger entry in the current successor revision that lacks a
prior typed user resolution, and—only for the
`deferred_to_implementation_uat` verdict—every HeldQuestionID. A non-deferred
Plan decision requires zero held-answer rows. The supplied resolutions must be a
bijection over the required set—no omission, duplicate, unknown ID, changed stimulus, stale/superseded
decision or ledger, or cross-variant ref. Held questions require one verbatim
answer; Plan feedback requires a freshly user-confirmed FIX-NOW/DEFER; ledger
entries require one verbatim CONFIRM/REPLACE/DEFER judgment. REPLACE and FIX-NOW
force changes-requested. User-confirmed DEFER items are the only follow-up feed.
Its total result table is:

| Valid user input | Stored effective outcome/event | Current relation/status | Gate/follow-up effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| reported accepted; complete carry-forward bijection; no FIX-NOW/REPLACE; ordinary interactions plus no feedback or all feedback confirmed DEFER | `pasture.implementation-uat.accepted/v1` with coverage digest | immutable snapshot through `current-implementation-uat`; UAT task accepted | land-eligible; confirmed DEFER resolutions/feedback become the sole follow-up feed |
| reported changes_requested, any confirmed FIX-NOW, or any ledger REPLACE | `pasture.implementation-uat.changes-requested/v1` with reported verdict, exact structured reasons, and complete coverage digest | immutable snapshot through `current-implementation-uat`; UAT task changes_requested | never land-eligible; FIX-NOW/REPLACE stays current-wave work; confirmed DEFER still feeds follow-up |
| partial/empty/duplicate/unknown/stale carry-forward; modified stimulus; malformed interaction; unconfirmed/invalid feedback; changes_requested without FIX-NOW/REPLACE | no event/snapshot/relation/status write | prior state byte-identical | actionable validation error |

Thus an accepted report containing FIX-NOW cannot authorize land and cannot be
silently dropped: it is durably normalized to changes-requested evidence. Both
commands store exact event kind/payload, decision snapshot, UAT status and
current relation in one conditional batch. Accepted Implementation UAT and land
both require the same complete carry-forward coverage digest. Proposal supersede or integration
rework invalidates the corresponding current relation in its own batch while
retaining historical decisions. Missing/wrong task, actor, proposal/set,
duplicate/conflicting, stale, and losing races write nothing. Same-MutationRef
replay returns the original snapshot/EventID; a fresh decision after rework uses
a new UAT task and operation.

`pasture task review start` uses one Provenance ConditionalMutationBatch to
create a `review-round` task plus exactly three axis `review` tasks, their typed
round/subject/axis relationships, parent-blocked-by-child edges, three distinct
owner-responsibility reviewer assignments/AgentIDs, and the protected round-
started event. The reviewed proposal/slice is blocked by the round; the round is
blocked by its axis tasks. `ReviewRoundID` and each ReviewTaskID are distinct
validated wrappers over stored TaskIDs. The immutable round-start event owns the
typed subject variant and axis mapping; the task graph and assignment rows are
the authoritative query projection. Review start CAS-captures the reviewed
task's exact `current-revision` or `current-candidate` relationship. A generic
exact-relationship-set precondition and one protected `current-round`
relationship allow at most one live round per reviewed task, regardless of
candidate.

Review kind is closed as `plan` or `implementation`. Plan review remains the
binary three-axis proposal vote. Implementation review covers slice and final
integration-set review and owns the mandatory EAGER severity tree. Its start
batch additionally creates, for each axis, exactly three group tasks:
`BLOCKER`, `IMPORTANT`, and `MINOR`. The axis is blocked by all three groups;
groups exist even when empty and carry exact round/axis/severity relationships.

Review start/finalize requires a typed `ReviewControl`: the reviewed task's
active owner-responsibility assignment for plan review, or the governing
IMPL_PLAN's active RoleSupervisor owner-responsibility assignment plus exact
`governs` edge for slice review. Integration-set review uses the IMPL_PLAN/
integration task's own active RoleSupervisor owner assignment and exact
`current-integration-candidate` relationship. The batch uses canonical local handles and
returns all created IDs through typed CLI result bindings. Unauthorized, ended,
wrong-subject/task, start/start under different MutationRefs, and start/finalize
races have one winner or no writes; same-MutationRef replay returns identical IDs.
`pasture task review submit` is the only public path that may create protected
review-submission events. Review start, finalize, proposal/candidate rework, and
supersede own their distinct protected lifecycle event kinds. Submit resolves the actor from that axis task's active responsibility
assignment and requires its current round/subject/axis.

For plan review, submit records exactly one binary ACCEPT or REVISE vote, closes
that axis task, and ends only that axis assignment. All three axes submit so the
immutable review contains complete correctness, test-quality, and elegance
judgments. Submit never closes the round or cancels siblings. `review finalize`
is the sole Plan-round terminal owner: it accepts only when all three EventIDs
are ACCEPT, otherwise closes REVISE, resolves the dependency branch, and records
the three submitted dispositions. Proposal supersede is the only path that may
invalidate an unfinished Plan round and end unsubmitted siblings.

Implementation submit accepts one validated findings document, never trusted
numeric counters. In one batch it declares the axis inventory; creates one
immutable finding leaf per item with verbatim description, location, evidence,
and severity; adds `severity group --blocked-by finding`; and for BLOCKER also
adds `reviewed slice/integration task --blocked-by finding`. Empty groups close
in that batch. Counts/events derive from stored finding leaves. All three axes
submit even if another found issues: submission ends that reviewer assignment
but never cancels siblings. A zero-finding axis closes its groups and axis task;
a finding-bearing axis stays dependency-blocked through its groups.

Findings are never resolved in place against the reviewed subject. A round with
no finding ever created finalizes ACCEPT as a fix-free clean 0/0/0 round. If any
finding exists, the round cannot finalize ACCEPT or start a successor on the
same subject. The governing supervisor invokes typed `slice rework` or
`integration rework` with a distinct replacement subject plus the complete
finding-to-Activity/Git/test evidence map. That one batch terminalizes the old
finding graph as `REVISE_REPLACED` and installs the replacement as described
above; a new eager round then reviews only the replacement. On review-budget
exhaustion, unresolved findings stay live in the old graph and are surfaced at
Implementation UAT for a budget/stop decision; they cannot land and no review
severity enters a follow-up epic.

Generic `event record` rejects protected review kinds.
The protected-kind registry is closed and also includes every event consumed by
ratify, UAT, slice close, and land, especially
`pasture.git.remote-ref-verified/v1`; generic `event record` rejects these kinds
before Apply. Only their owning typed commands can append them.

Each `(ReviewRoundID, AssignmentID)` permits at most one submission. Every
assignment receives exactly one terminal disposition: `submitted_accept`,
`submitted_revise`, `submitted_clean`, `submitted_findings`, or
`invalidated_before_submission` when supersede/rework wins. Once terminal, later
submissions write nothing. Re-review creates a new round/task/assignment/severity
graph for the replacement subject and relates it as superseding the old.
Concurrent submit/rework/finalize has one winner.

`pasture task review finalize` names exact submission EventIDs and uses one
conditional batch to verify kind-specific task/assignment/event/group/finding
state, exact relationship sets, control, and unchanged subject. It closes a Plan
round with `ACCEPT` or `REVISE`, and an implementation round only with `ACCEPT`;
a finding-bearing implementation round terminates only through subject rework as
`REVISE_REPLACED`.
Every terminal round has zero active reviewer assignments. A round is never
inferred complete from an out-of-transaction query.

A close succeeds only when all three supplied EventIDs are ACCEPT events from
the same current RoundID and TaskCandidateID, their recorded assignments and AgentIDs
are distinct, their axes are exactly correctness/test-quality/elegance, all
eager groups are closed with zero unresolved findings, `fixes_applied` is false,
the slice's current-candidate relationship still names that TaskCandidateID, and
the round is accepted rather than
revised. Events from mixed rounds/subjects, self-certified events,
reused assignments, or a fix-applying round write nothing.

The invocation actor is resolved from the governing IMPL_PLAN's active
RoleSupervisor owner-responsibility AssignmentID, never from an `--actor` or
`--supervisor` override. That assignment must be connected to the slice through a
typed `governs` relationship. This is protocol-policy validation, not an authentication
or hostile-user security boundary: anyone able to alter the local task database
or invoke another known assignment is outside the claim. Provenance remains
generic; #43 lowers policy to generic in-transaction preconditions and one
ConditionalMutationBatch. The slice-specific command
is `pasture task slice close`; generic `pasture task close` rejects slice kinds.
#43 freezes closure policy separately for ordinary tasks and completed review
tasks so no non-slice behavior is inferred from the slice predicate.

The frozen closure policies are explicit by task kind. An ordinary leaf may be
closed only by its active current owner-responsibility assignment from
`in_progress` with no unresolved blocked-by children; the same batch ends that
assignment, clears Owner, and emits `pasture.task.closed/v1`. Reopen leaves it unassigned.
Plan-axis tasks close through submit; implementation finding/group/axis tasks
close only through findings submission or typed subject rework. A Plan round and
a clean implementation round close through typed finalize; a finding-bearing
implementation round closes only through typed subject rework. An implementation slice closes only
through `task slice close`, ending its worker responsibility assignment,
clearing Owner, and CAS-checking the exact current candidate in the same batch,
after a clean current round. Protocol documents and
containers (REQUEST, URD, PROPOSAL, IMPL_PLAN, UAT, HANDOFF, DECISION_LEDGER, and epic) reject
generic update/close for status, phase, owner, or kind and advance only through
the frozen `transition`, `supersede`, `ratify`, or `land` command schemas. Every
rejected actor/assignment/state/dependency/evidence case
is tested to leave task, graph, assignment, and journal state unchanged.

The public mutation-policy matrix is closed:

| Task kind | generic descriptive update | generic reopen | generic relation mutation | typed authority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ordinary leaf | yes | yes, to unassigned open state | unprotected blocked-by/derived-from only | close/assignment/dependency commands |
| review axis/round/severity group/finding | no reserved fields | never | never | review start/submit/finalize plus slice/integration rework |
| implementation slice | no generic body/state update | never | never after typed creation | slice create/candidate set/rework/close |
| REQUEST/URD/PROPOSAL/IMPL_PLAN/UAT/HANDOFF/DECISION_LEDGER/epic | no generic body/state update | never | never | protocol create/revise/transition/supersede/ratify/land; ledger revise is append-only |

`contains`, `governs`, current-revision/current-candidate, review subject/axis/current-round, and `supersedes` edges
are reserved. Generic relation add/remove/repoint cannot create them or touch a
protected task. #5's conditional API includes exact typed incoming/outgoing
relationship-set equality, not only presence/absence, wherever cardinality is
claimed. Typed `rework` creates a new candidate/round/task branch; it never
resurrects a terminal round, axis, slice, or protocol container.

Task-to-task, task-to-Agent, and task-to-Activity operands are distinct Go types
and operations. The new API does not expose `AddEdge(TaskID, string, EdgeKind)`.

The only MVP backend for this family is the versioned `pasture task` CLI. A
missing or incompatible binary fails actionably. Registered native tools and
semantic-only instructions remain the explicit follow-ups in §2.

### 5.4 Process, Git, and filesystem effects

#38 owns the foundational opaque `EffectID` and `EffectSet` values, including
constructor validation, canonical ordering/deduplication, codec, equality, and
compatibility semantics. #43 contributes named task effects and #46 contributes
the concrete process/Git/filesystem effect definitions; neither redefines the
container. #41 may therefore expose `EffectSet` without depending on #46.

Operational process semantics are not hidden in shell strings:

```go
type RunProcess struct {
    Executable ExecutableRef
    Arguments  []Argument
    Directory  WorkingDirectoryRef
    Environment []EnvBinding
    Stdin      InputRef
    Stdout     OutputRef
    Stderr     OutputRef
    Exit       ExitExpectation
    Effects    EffectSet
}

type Pipeline struct {
    Steps []ProcessStep // typed output-to-input edges
}
```

Environment names/values, literal/file/previous-output stdin, captured/file
stdout/stderr, and exit expectations are validated. Command substitution is an
explicit output reference. A structured `Pipeline` is used only where the
classified inventory needs a pipeline. Redirection, control operators, globbing,
or shell expansion not represented by the MVP types is reported unsupported and
must become a dedicated operation; lowerers do not smuggle it through `sh -c`.

Git effects are typed repository operations/evidence over process primitives and
respect repository policy such as `git agent-commit`. #46 exclusively defines
`GuardedPushExactCommit`: it verifies the local commit/tree, compares the exact
remote ref to ExpectedOldOID (including explicitly absent), pushes only
`CommitOID:RemoteRef`, re-reads the remote, and returns opaque
`VerifiedGuardedPush`. A remote already at the exact candidate is a
successful idempotent retry; a stale/racing/different ref is a no-evidence
failure. The value has no codec/JSON/result-slot form and is consumed only inside
the versioned application/#40 composite process before public EventID output.
The effect never claims atomicity with SQLite or across repositories.
Filesystem effects cover
read, exact write/replace, create directory, move, and remove an exact owned path.
Typing an effect describes intent; it never grants missing user/security
authorization.

### 5.5 Typed external capability escape

```go
type CapabilityID string
type CapabilityContractVersion string

const CapabilityRenderDiagram CapabilityID = "acme.diagram.render"

var RenderDiagram = MustDefineCapability[RenderDiagramInput, RenderDiagramResult](
    CapabilityRenderDiagram,
    CapabilityContractVersion("1.0.0"),
    renderDiagramSemantics,
    renderDiagramEffects,
    renderDiagramInputCodec,
    renderDiagramOutputCodec,
)

type CapabilitySemantics struct {
    Summary        string
    Preconditions  []Condition
    Postconditions []Condition
    Result         ResultContract
}

func DefineCapability[In, Out any](
    id CapabilityID,
    version CapabilityContractVersion,
    semantics CapabilitySemantics,
    effects EffectSet,
    input Codec[In],
    output Codec[Out],
) (Capability[In, Out], error)

func InvokeTool[In, Out any](c Capability[In, Out], input In) SemanticOperation
```

`Capability` is opaque. `InvokeTool` accepts a typed descriptor, not an ID,
string, native name, or untyped payload. External packages declare a typed const
ID and construct an opaque descriptor as a `var` or function result; Go values
returned by `DefineCapability` are never claimed to be constants. Bindings must
accept the descriptor's version and prove the same preconditions,
postconditions, result, and effect set.

Go named string types prevent accidental interchange of typed variables but do
accept assignable untyped literals. The guarantee is stated accurately:

- compile-fail fixtures reject raw strings/IDs/wrong descriptors at
  `InvokeTool` and mismatched typed input;
- raw string variables cannot cross the named-ID boundary without explicit
  conversion;
- a `go/analysis` check requires declared typed constants at canonical
  capability definition sites and rejects untyped literal IDs passed directly
  to `DefineCapability`; and
- registry validation rejects invalid namespaced IDs and conflicting duplicate
  descriptors or versions. A runtime binding declares a compatible
  `CapabilityContractVersion` range in addition to the host RuntimeContract's
  harness-version range.

A completely undescribed tool remains an exhaustive TargetLiteral, never a
generic portable call.

## 6. Runtime harness contracts

Runtime lowering uses a contract distinct from installation:

```go
type RuntimeContractID string
type SemanticOperationID string
type RuntimeContract struct { /* unexported validated profile */ }

type RuntimeBinding[In, Out any] interface { runtimeBinding() }
// NativeCall | ParentMediated | SemanticInstruction | Unsupported

type OperationDescriptor[In, Out any] struct { /* opaque */ }
type EffectDescriptor[In, Out any] struct { /* opaque */ }

type RuntimeBindingContribution interface { runtimeBindingContribution() }

func BindCapability[In, Out any](
    capability Capability[In, Out],
    versions CapabilityVersionRange,
    binding CapabilityRuntimeBinding[In, Out],
) (RuntimeBindingContribution, error)

func NewRuntimeContract(
    id RuntimeContractID,
    harness HarnessID,
    versions VersionConstraint,
    core CoreRuntimeBindings,
    capabilities ...RuntimeBindingContribution,
) (RuntimeContract, error)
func (c RuntimeContract) ID() RuntimeContractID
func (c RuntimeContract) Harness() HarnessID
func (c RuntimeContract) Supports(version HostVersion) bool
func LookupOperationBinding[In, Out any](
    c RuntimeContract,
    operation OperationDescriptor[In, Out],
) (RuntimeBinding[In, Out], error)
func LookupEffectBinding[In, Out any](
    c RuntimeContract,
    effect EffectDescriptor[In, Out],
) (RuntimeBinding[In, Out], error)
func LookupCapabilityBinding[In, Out any](
    c RuntimeContract,
    capability Capability[In, Out],
) (CapabilityRuntimeBinding[In, Out], error)
```

Values and all three descriptor families are opaque and constructor-validated.
#40 owns this build-time composition
API; external packages can bind a #41 descriptor without modifying #40, but can
never supply a dynamic name or untyped payload. Construction requires exactly
one binding for every requested operation/effect/capability, validates the
descriptor codec/semantics/effect set and version intersection, and rejects
duplicate or conflicting contributions. All lookup surfaces return explicit
errors for invalid, missing, duplicate, unbound, or incompatible descriptors;
there is no meaningful zero binding. Native bindings include exact
request/result schemas and fixtures. Missing bindings, unsupported required
design:
operations, or host versions outside the range fail; no similarly named call is
guessed. `SemanticOperationID` is the protocol identity and is never reused as
Provenance's idempotency `OperationID`; operations, effects, and capability
descriptors cross separate typed lookup surfaces without conversion. Named
string IDs remain metadata exposed by descriptors, never direct lookup operands,
so Go's assignable untyped-literal rule cannot bypass descriptor validation.

Initial evidence baselines are explicitly pinned:

| Harness | Initial point range | Contract rule |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | exactly CLI 2.1.210 plus pinned official/source schemas | use only Agent/SendMessage/TaskStop-era primitives where exact; never emit removed TeamCreate/TeamDelete semantics |
| OpenCode | exactly CLI 1.17.18 plus official docs/pinned source | use documented skill/task/question surfaces; unverified persistent message/follow-up/wait/close names are mediated, semantic, or unsupported |
| Codex | exactly CLI 0.144.1 plus official docs/pinned source | bind only exact exposed collaboration/request-input functions and preserve logical continuity across replacement agents |

Updating a host requires a new RuntimeContractID or reviewed range expansion.
“Current” and `latest` are not compatibility policies.

## 7. Native activation contracts

Installation mechanics do not enter the semantic IR:

```go
type ActivationContractID string
type ActivationContract struct { /* unexported validated profile */ }
type ComponentDescriptor struct { /* opaque validated harness/extension identity */ }
type ActivationStrategy interface { activationStrategy() }
// NativePlugin | DirectFile | NativePluginPendingTrust

func NewActivationContract(
    id ActivationContractID,
    harness HarnessID,
    hostVersions VersionConstraint,
    versionProbe CommandSchema,
    components ExhaustiveComponentActivations,
) (ActivationContract, error)
func NativePluginActivation(manager NativeManagerContract) ActivationStrategy
func DirectFileActivation(bundle artifact.Bundle, destination Destination) ActivationStrategy
func PendingTrustActivation(manager NativeManagerContract, review NativeTrustReview) ActivationStrategy
func (c ActivationContract) ID() ActivationContractID
func (c ActivationContract) Harness() HarnessID
func LookupComponentActivation(
    c ActivationContract,
    component ComponentDescriptor,
) (ComponentActivation, error)
```

`ExhaustiveComponentActivations` is opaque and created only by a validating
constructor that requires exactly one skills, agents, and hooks component—no
public mutable map. Each component contains exactly one closed activation
strategy, so invalid nullable marketplace/plugin/config combinations cannot be
constructed. Lookup accepts only an opaque validated component descriptor and
returns an explicit error for wrong harness, missing/unbound, or incompatible
components; raw ExtensionID/string literals and zero activations are not a
public surface. Native strategies carry exact package identity plus
install/list/update/remove schemas. Neutral upstream issue #48 owns package
`artifact`: opaque `Bundle`, `BundleID`, manifest/entry/digest codecs,
constructors, canonical validation, and the `go:embed`/`fs.FS` boundary. #48 is
an independent foundation with no #38 dependency. Construction walks the input
FS, requires an exact declared file set, snapshots every validated byte into
private immutable storage, derives `BundleID` as a domain-separated SHA-256 over
the canonical path/type/mode/content-digest manifest, and discards the backing
FS. `Open` accepts only declared leaves and returns a fresh read-only handle;
source mutation after construction cannot affect the bundle. Each
#24/#27/#45 target constructs and publishes an `artifact.Bundle`; #39 consumes
that upstream type and adds only activation destination/semantics. Paths must be
clean relative paths; traversal, absolute/duplicate leaves, parent/leaf
symlinks, and unsupported entries are constructor errors. The installed CLI
carries every DirectFile payload and never resolves from cwd/source checkout.
The private nine-cell table stores no mutable installation state itself.

Target artifacts do not carry an ActivationContractID. Each target publishes a
stable target/component identity, its opaque `artifact.Bundle`, and the
RuntimeContractID under which it was compiled. #39's private catalog consumes
those target descriptors
and binds each one to an ActivationContractID and closed strategy. This keeps
target generation upstream of activation without duplicating metadata.

The initial public activation matrix is:

| Harness | Skills | Agents | Harness hooks |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `pasture-skills` native plugin | `pasture-agents` native plugin | `pasture-hooks` native plugin |
| OpenCode | whole directories at `~/.config/opencode/skills/<name>/` | files at `~/.config/opencode/agent/<role>.md` | embedded `pasture-hooks.ts` at `~/.config/opencode/plugin/pasture-hooks.ts` through pinned auto-discovery |
| Codex | `pasture-skills` native plugin | `~/.codex/agents/pasture_*.toml` | `pasture-hooks` native plugin, followed by native user trust review |

The Go values remain opaque implementation metadata. Cross-language consumers
use one public #39-owned command contract:

```text
pasture install apply-selection \
  --desired <selection-file> \
  --source <installer|home-manager> \
  --json

pasture install apply-cell \
  --harness <claude-code|opencode|codex> \
  --extension <skills|agents|hooks> \
  --enabled=<true|false> \
  --source <installer|home-manager> \
  --json
```

The command never accepts the persisted installer config directly. Both callers
produce this immutable desired-state document:

```yaml
schema: pasture.install.effective-selection/v1
cells:
  claude-code: {skills: false, agents: false, hooks: false}
  opencode:     {skills: false, agents: false, hooks: false}
  codex:        {skills: false, agents: false, hooks: false}
```

The schema requires exactly three harness IDs and exactly three extension IDs,
with no defaults or unknown keys. `apply-selection` validates the desired
`EffectiveSelection`, loads the separate typed installation inventory, inspects
any cell requiring reconciliation, constructs the ordered plan in memory, and
uses private `executeOrdinaryCell` steps or one selection-aware
`executeClaudeLegacyGroup`. The public context-free `apply-cell` is a separate
single-cell remediation surface and is never recursively called by the group.
The selection command writes no preference, rollback data, authorization, lock,
or cross-cell transaction record.

Cell and action order is canonical and public:

```text
claude-code.skills, claude-code.agents, claude-code.hooks,
opencode.skills, opencode.agents, opencode.hooks,
codex.skills, codex.agents, codex.hooks
```

For each cell in that order, desired true plans an idempotent inspect/ensure.
Desired false plans inspect/remove only when the inventory says Pasture manages
that cell or its last confirmed state is installed or unknown; a
never-recorded false cell plans nothing. Thus an uninstall failure remains
retryable on an ordinary TUI or Home Manager rerun even though the desired
preference is already false. Both commands emit one
transient `pasture.install.apply-result/v1` document. Each planned row contains
`index`, typed harness/extension IDs, `operation`, `management`, and exactly one
status from `completed`, `failed`, `unattempted`, `managed_declaratively`, or
`installed_pending_trust`. At most one row is `failed`; all later planned rows
requiring command execution are `unattempted`. Home Manager declarative rows are
live inspections, not command attempts, and remain `managed_declaratively`
regardless of an earlier/later native failure. `installed_pending_trust` is a successful Codex-hook install,
not a claim that the hook is active. A result contains `ok`, `source`, and rows
in canonical order. A pre-plan decode/schema/version failure emits
`pasture.install.apply-error/v1` with stage, optional cell/action, cause,
impact, and exact remediation. An action failure emits the same diagnostic in
its failed row, exits nonzero, and still returns the complete ordered result.
Neither result schema is accepted as future state; the narrower inventory below
is the only persisted operational evidence.

For `source=installer`, the TUI caller alone loads preferences, presents and
saves the user's confirmed global choices, derives the immutable effective
selection (`harness && extension`), then invokes `apply-selection`; the command
itself never reads or writes preferences and applies both native-managed and
direct-file cells from that document. `apply-cell` is only an explicit
single-cell remediation and also never changes preferences. For
`source=home-manager`, Nix renders desired effective cells from the current
generation's per-harness options. Aura #8 orders declarative link realization
before the Pasture native activation node. `apply-selection` first live-inspects every
declarative row, then acts only on `NativeManaged` cells in canonical native-
subset order;
`DirectFile` cells are explicitly skipped as `managed_declaratively` because
Home Manager adds/removes their links from the pinned Pasture generated tree.
`apply-cell --source home-manager` rejects a direct-file mutation with that
exact declarative remedy instead of writing the path. Thus both callers share
one transition schema and native-manager implementation without pretending they
own the same filesystem cells.

Every diagnostic carries one closed tagged `Remediation` rather than assuming
one command fits every executor: `ApplyCell{argv}` for ordinary installer-owned
cells, `ApplySelection{desired_document, source}`/`RerunInstaller` for the Claude
selection-wide group, `RerunHomeManager{option,path}` for declarative rows, or
`ManualNativeTrust{instructions}` for Codex trust, or
`ManualRepair{inspection,instructions}` for irreducible state-save/external
ambiguity. The selected remedy must be
executable for the failing state; Claude legacy errors never print the public
`apply-cell` command that is required to reject them.

### 7.1 Confirmed installation inventory and DirectFile safety

Preferences remain in `~/.config/pasture/config.yaml`. Confirmed operational
state for #39-mutated cells lives separately at
`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/pasture/installations.yaml` under the closed
schema `pasture.install.state/v1`. Every recorded cell contains typed
harness/extension/strategy/source IDs, artifact identity and version, whether
the matching pre-existing component was created/updated by Pasture or merely
observed externally, the exact native selector/scope or managed file leaves,
the last confirmed observation (`installed`, `absent`, or `unknown`), native
trust disposition where applicable, and the last action/outcome/diagnostic.
Installer-owned direct-file leaves retain their expected type, content digest,
mode, and Pasture-created parent-directory evidence. Removed cells remain as
absent tombstones, so status can answer what was installed, whether uninstall
completed, and what remains. Home Manager DirectFile links are not inventory
members: Nix owns their declarative lifecycle, while `status --source
home-manager --desired ...` performs a read-only exact inspection and reports
`managed_declaratively` without persisting a second ownership/controller model.

Artifact/state content digests use the closed `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` codec
over exact file bytes; manifest leaves are canonical lexicographic relative
paths with explicit octal permission bits. State YAML rejects unknown/duplicate
cells and serializes the public nine-cell order. A state file symlink or unsafe
type is rejected before action, and no secret is stored. State save uses an
ordinary same-directory create-exclusive temporary file, flush, rename, and
directory flush. The live process best-effort removes only the exact temp it
successfully created. A crash orphan is never discovered, deleted, reused, or
treated as recovery input by a later run; the committed state file alone is
authoritative and a later save uses a fresh random temp. This deliberately avoids
a temp ledger, marker protocol, or crash-recovery subsystem.

When upgrading from a release with no inventory, every matching pre-existing
native component or direct file is observed as external and is never adopted or
removed by Pasture, even after a desired-true then desired-false cycle. The sole
exception is the exact published user-scoped Claude v0.0.4 monolith: the frozen
compatibility table recognizes that one legacy identity as an approved migration
candidate. Unknown or near-match scope/version/identity remains external and
causes zero mutation. Mixed simultaneous installer/Home Manager control of a
native cell is unsupported and reported with the recorded source and exact
single-controller repair; no concurrency protocol is introduced.

The inventory changes only after a postcondition is live-confirmed or after a
normal action failure is live-inspected. It stores last confirmed cell/managed-
leaf identity plus the last action/outcome/diagnostic; it does not persist a
prior/attempted manifest, per-entry step, nonce, temp path, or pending desired
state before action. Installer DirectFile replacement uses one create-exclusive
same-parent temp regular file per leaf, writes/flushes/closes it, and atomically
renames it to the sibling destination. The current process best-effort removes
only the exact temp it created if the operation fails before rename. After a
crash, a later run never scans, cleans, reuses, or infers ownership from temp
names; it live-inspects only final manifest destinations and creates a fresh
temp. Orphans are harmless external siblings and may be reported if explicitly
encountered, but are never automatic recovery state.

If an external action succeeds but inventory save fails, the command reports
that exact ambiguity and live state; the next run conservatively treats a
matching unrecorded component as external rather than adopting it. This is the
intentional cost of the user-approved simple model. State decode/write failures
identify path/stage/impact/fix and stop before the next mutation. Concurrent
invocations remain unsupported rather than coordinated. There is no background
worker, rollback, compensation, pending-work queue, temp ownership marker, or
same/newer-binary crash reconciliation.

`pasture install status [--json]` combines the inventory with live typed native
probes and exact-file inspection. It reports desired, recorded, observed, source,
trust, remaining managed targets, and the exact tagged executable remediation. A
normal `pasture install` run performs the same inspection before retrying an
installed/unknown false cell; users need not reconstruct the old preference.

Installer DirectFile reconciliation is exact and conservative:

- an absent manifest leaf is created as a regular file with its declared mode;
- a recorded Pasture-managed leaf may update only when its current
  `(type, digest, mode)` exactly matches the prior record;
- an identical pre-existing unrecorded leaf satisfies desired true but is
  recorded as external and is never removed by Pasture;
- a differing file, directory, dangling/foreign symlink, parent symlink, unsafe
  path, permission failure, or modified managed leaf is an actionable conflict,
  never an implicit overwrite;
- removal unlinks only recorded Pasture-managed leaves whose
  `(type, digest, mode)` still exactly matches, removes only recorded
  Pasture-created directories that are empty, and
  preserves every sibling; and
- Home Manager DirectFile links are reported `managed_declaratively` by
  read-only desired/live inspection and remain outside persistent inventory,
  while native actions invoked by Home Manager update the factual native-cell
  inventory.

Generated packages carry immutable target/component identities,

## 8. Goldmark inventory and finite migration

This work has two dependency-distinct milestones rather than one inverted gate.

**Milestone A — inventory/classification (Pasture #47, after #38):**

1. A read-only scanner parses every active generated Markdown owner through
   Goldmark and reports candidate harness syntax with owner, file/section, AST
   node/range, snippet, and candidate class.
2. Maintainers explicitly classify each candidate as orchestration, decision,
   task/process/Git/filesystem effect, portable Verbatim, exhaustive
   TargetLiteral, neutral false positive, or dead owner.
3. The scanner independently walks a code-owned closed list of canonical source
   roots and explicit output/vendor/test-fixture exclusions, rejecting symlinked
   owners. It compares that discovered set with the checked-in owner manifest;
   the manifest is classification input, never the discovery source. Missing
   active files, stale entries, dead-owner dispositions, and exclusion drift are
   errors. The scan emits deterministic source/AST order and is proved read-only
   by byte-for-byte tree hashes before and after. Every classification—including
   neutral false positive and dead owner—is represented by a golden fixture.
4. The classified inventory is an input to #46, #43, and #40; those issues may
   not freeze their closed algebras/contracts before consuming it.

**Milestone B — typed migration and strict rejection (Pasture #42, after #47,
#46, #43, and #40):**

5. Canonical Go specs migrate every classified orchestration, task,
   process/Git/filesystem, and decision occurrence to the typed Document/effect
   API. This issue alone removes operational `bd` instructions. Proposal 20's
   `runtime.go` regex and global string replacements are deleted, not retained as
   compatibility parsing.
6. The unclassified active-candidate count reaches zero. Any nonzero
   unclassified count prevents strict-mode activation; the classified inventory
   remains required input and is not itself an error.
7. Strict mode permanently rejects newly introduced unclassified harness syntax
   in Markdown and emits no target output.

The scanner recognizes legacy lexical forms only to report them. It never assigns
semantics or rewrites production output. The malformed
`TeamCreate({...}) -> task(({...})` case remains a regression fixture.

## 9. Provenance authoritative task journal

### 9.1 Generic envelope and caller-owned payloads

```go
type EventID int64
type EventKind string
type OperationID string
type EventContextKind string

type EventContext struct { /* opaque validated kind + encoded identity */ }

func TaskContext(TaskID) (EventContext, error)
func ActivityContext(ActivityID) (EventContext, error)
func AgentContext(AgentID) (EventContext, error)
func GitContext(GitOID) (EventContext, error)

type ExtensionContextID interface {
    ~string
    EventContextDomain() EventContextKind
}

type ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID ExtensionContextID] struct { /* opaque */ }
func DefineExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    validate func(ID) error,
) (ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID], error)
func ExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    descriptor ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID],
    id ID,
) (EventContext, error)

type TaskEvent struct {
    ID          EventID
    TaskID      TaskID
    Kind        EventKind
    ActorID     AgentID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    OperationID OperationID
    Contexts    []EventContext
    Payload     json.RawMessage
}
```

EventID is database-generated and exposed once. Queries order ascending by
`(RecordedAt, EventID)` and expose both fields. EventKind/context kinds are
validated namespaced types. `EventContext` has no exported raw `ID string`
constructor or fields. Built-in constructors require the corresponding typed ID
and reject zero or structurally invalid values. Caller namespaces define a named
string-backed ID implementing the marker method plus a typed descriptor and
validator. `DefineExtensionContext` derives its kind from the named ID type's
marker; it takes no duplicate kind argument, rejects every reserved Provenance
built-in kind (task/activity/agent/git), and requires a valid caller-owned
namespace. At value construction the ID's reported kind must still equal the
descriptor kind. Built-in `string` cannot satisfy `ExtensionContextID`, so
`DefineExtensionContext[string]` is a compile failure. Only the internal
persistence codec serializes context kind plus text.

Provenance validates the generic envelope, identity syntax/references, contexts,
and payload well-formedness. It does not import or globally register Pasture
codecs. Pasture constructs an opaque typed event definition, validates its
`pasture.*` payload, encodes it, and passes it across this boundary.

Secondary contexts supplied during event creation commit atomically. A later
context attachment, when necessary, is itself a journalled mutation. Typed
constructors prevent TaskID, ActivityID, GitOID, and caller-defined IDs from
being accidentally interchanged even though storage uses a common textual
encoding. Contexts have set semantics: construction, persistence, operation
canonicalization, and query output deduplicate and sort by
`(EventContextKind, canonical encoded identity)`. Association-row insertion
order is never observable. Each context edge stores the EventID that attached
it (the original event for initial contexts, the journalled attachment event for
later contexts). Snapshot queries include only edges whose attachment EventID is
at or below SnapshotMaxEventID, so a later attachment cannot change an in-flight
filtered traversal.

### 9.2 Atomic command API and durable idempotency

```go
type MutationContext struct {
    ActorID     AgentID
    Authority   OperationAuthorityID // exact assignment or registered bootstrap identity
    OperationID OperationID
    Command     CommandDigest // opaque caller-domain canonical command identity
}

Apply(ctx context.Context, mc MutationContext, command Mutation) (MutationResult, error)

type CommittedOperationLookup interface {
    LookupCommitted(
        ctx context.Context,
        operation OperationID,
        expectedActor AgentID,
        expectedAuthority OperationAuthorityID,
        expectedCommand CommandDigest,
    ) (CommittedOperationResult, error)
}

// CommittedOperationResult is exactly one of Absent or Committed. Reuse of an
// OperationID with a different actor, authority, or command returns Conflict.
```

Provenance #4 owns the TaskEvent envelope, context storage, ordering/query APIs,
and internal append/schema primitives. It exposes no raw event-append bypass,
registered production migration, or baseline side effect. Its persistence tests
activate the schema explicitly in isolated test databases. Provenance #5
exclusively owns the public command/result table, `Apply`, and the read-only
`LookupCommitted` surface. #5 owns opaque validated `OperationAuthorityID`
constructors for exact AssignmentID-based and registered-bootstrap identities;
the ID includes authority kind and canonical underlying identity, never merely
AgentID. `Apply` records the supplied opaque CommandDigest and
the independently derived generic MutationDigest. On an already-committed
OperationID it compares actor plus CommandDigest and returns the stored result
before interpreting a newly supplied mutation; on first execution it also stores
the actual mutation digest for audit. ActorID, OperationAuthorityID, and
CommandDigest must all match for replay; exact ended authority may replay, while
same-Agent predecessor/successor assignments, slots/tasks, and bootstrap paths
conflict. The trusted typed adapter owns command-
identity construction—Provenance does not decode caller semantics.

Lookup performs no mutation: `Absent` means the
operation has never committed; exact actor/command agreement returns the stored
result map and EventIDs even when the initiating assignment has since ended; and
any OperationID reuse with different actor/command identity returns `Conflict`.
It never executes an absent command or revalidates current authority. #5 also
owns the production migration that installs the #4
schema, writes baselines, and activates atomic journaling. #4 and #5 ship in one
Provenance release tag after both merge; there is no released state in which a
database has a writable journal but non-journalled mutators.

The closed command family covers task lifecycle, typed relationships, labels,
comments, responsibility/supervision assignments, explicit attribution,
task-linked Activity start/end,
later event-context attachment, and a generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation for
caller-validated material events that change no current task state. Provenance
commits domain row(s), any required attribution, TaskEvent row(s), contexts, and
canonical operation/result through one `internal/sqlite` connection/transaction.
Pasture does not compose a fake transaction across separate tracker/audit
connections.

#5 also owns opaque `ConditionalMutationBatch` construction. It is a closed,
extension-safe declarative composition of existing generic mutations plus
caller-validated opaque material events; it is not a callback, raw SQL, or an
untyped predicate escape hatch. Its built-in preconditions cover exact task
kind/status/owner, exact active/ended assignment and active-slot set, typed
relationship presence/absence and exact incoming/outgoing typed set equality,
exact task revision plus immutable subject task/current-subject relationships, exact immutable EventID/task/kind/context
evidence, and absence of unresolved blocked-by children. Canonical typed local
handles let later batch mutations reference earlier allocated tasks/assignments;
the result returns their stable ID map. Preconditions are
rechecked inside the same SQLite transaction immediately before the ordered
mutations. Domain rows, assignment transitions, relationships, events,
contexts, attribution, and operation result all commit or roll back together.
Pasture #43 compiles review/transition/closure policy into these generic
preconditions and mutations; Provenance never decodes a `pasture.*` payload.

The closed batch API also owns one narrow zero-domain/event form:
`ConditionalExistingIDResult`. Exact typed preconditions create unforgeable
`ExistingTaskHandle`, `ExistingAssignmentHandle`, `ExistingActivityHandle`, or
`ExistingEventHandle` values; typed result-slot bindings may project only those
handles into the operation result. The form requires at least one exact current-
state/authority precondition and one handle projection, permits no allocation,
literal/scalar/arbitrary-map result, domain mutation, or event draft, and rechecks
all predicates in the Apply transaction. Success commits only the canonical
operation row and typed existing-ID result rows; rejection/fault commits nothing.
Publication uses an ExistingEventHandle produced by the exact canonical-evidence
precondition, so `pushed|already_at_target` is decoded from that protected event's
stored payload rather than injected as a result literal.
The public four-handle sum is validated table-wise in #5 and through #14: task,
assignment, Activity, and event each cover positive exact projection,
cross-domain rejection, zero and multiple projection rejection, response loss,
restart/replay, state/authority races, and every fault rollback boundary. No
public branch exists without these fixtures.

OperationID is durable idempotency identity. Same ID plus byte-equivalent
canonical command/actor/exact authority returns the originally committed
result/events after close/reopen or concurrent retry. Same ID with different
actor, authority, or command fails.
The operation row rolls back with the mutation, so there is no pending state.

Pre-1.0 direct mutator paths migrate to Apply or compatibility wrappers that
require MutationContext and delegate to the same transaction. No exported bypass
may mutate a task/graph without its event.

### 9.3 Responsibility CAS and cumulative attribution

```go
type TransferTaskResponsibility struct {
    Task          TaskID
    ExpectedOwner OwnerExpectation // OwnerIs(agent) or OwnerIsUnassigned()
    ExpectedAssignment AssignmentExpectation
    Successor     OptionalAssignmentDraft // absent means become unassigned
    Reason        string
}
```

The expected owner and current responsibility assignment are compared inside
the same transaction. Transfer ends the predecessor, optionally creates the
successor, changes Owner, and records attribution/events atomically. Two
distinct concurrent transitions have one winner; the stale loser changes no
owner, assignment, attribution, operation, or event row and receives an
actionable conflict. `ChangeTaskOwner` is only a compatibility constructor that
delegates to this transition when its full assignment expectation is supplied;
otherwise it rejects once the assignment migration is active.
This protects task assignment only; it is unrelated to plugin-installation
concurrency and introduces no installer transaction/CAS mechanism.

Task.Owner is role-neutral current responsibility. Prior/new material contributors retain
idempotent `attributed_to` edges. Administrative actors are not attributed merely
for changing a label/status; attribution occurs only for responsibility or
material contribution commands. Owner events record expected/previous/new owner,
actor, reason, OperationID, time, and EventID.

### 9.4 Activities, relationships, and graph events

`StartTaskActivity` and `EndTaskActivity` carry AssignmentID, ActivityID,
phase/stage, notes, and contexts; TaskID and AgentID are derived and validated
from that exact active assignment. Activity row state, task linkage, material event,
required attribution, and contexts commit together. Duration Activities remain
distinct from instantaneous transitions and do not encode structured changes in
notes. The state machine is closed: start requires a new ActivityID, existing
task, and actor resolved from the supplied active assignment; a new OperationID
cannot start an existing Activity. End requires the same linked task/agent and
an active Activity. End-before-start, wrong task/agent, invalid transitions, and
a second end under a new OperationID write nothing; same-OperationID retries
return the original result, and concurrent ends have one winner.

Task relationships accept TaskID targets. Attribution accepts AgentID. Activity
links accept ActivityID. A relationship involving two tasks writes a task-local
event to each timeline in one transaction, sharing OperationID and receiving
distinct EventIDs. Blocked-by cycle validation, edge persistence, and both events
share the same consistency boundary.

### 9.5 Current state and legacy migration

Current task/graph/Activity tables remain authoritative. The journal explains
all post-migration changes; it is not used to rebuild pre-journal state. When #5
activates the coordinated production migration, existing tasks each receive one
idempotent `provenance.migration.baseline` event containing the then-current
status/phase/owner and source schema version. In that same exclusive transaction,
every nonterminal assigned task receives a deterministic migration-time active
owner-responsibility assignment; every terminal assigned task receives an ended
migration assignment and has current Owner cleared; unassigned tasks receive no
assignment. Assignment IDs derive from schema version plus TaskID. Provenance
uses only its generic `provenance.role.legacy-owner` and
`provenance.slot.owner-responsibility`; it never invents a Pasture role. The task
baseline EventID is the active assignment's StartEventID at migration RecordedAt.
For a terminal legacy owner, a second ordered migration-time assignment-ended
event supplies EndEventID at the same RecordedAt; both are explicitly snapshot
events and never claim historical start/end time.

Legacy owner text that is not already a registered AgentID maps to a
deterministically registered `legacy-owner/<sha256>` SoftwareAgent whose payload
retains the original text; invalid/duplicate registration fails the entire
migration. Attribution and migration events retain that mapped owner but are
explicitly labeled snapshot/baseline evidence, never fabricated historical
start/end times. The post-migration invariant holds for every task kind: a
nonterminal nonnil Owner has exactly one matching active responsibility
assignment, while every terminal task has nil Owner and no active responsibility.
This marks the historical-completeness boundary.

The #5 production migration executes schema activation and every baseline row
inside one exclusive SQLite migration transaction. A fault after any number of
rows rolls back the schema marker, journal tables/changes, and all baselines;
reopen then performs the same migration from the pre-migration database. Empty
databases, every assigned/unassigned × terminal/nonterminal × task-kind case,
unmappable legacy owner text, repeat startup, and concurrent startup are explicit
fixtures. Baseline ActorID is the registered migrator; an absent legacy owner is
never fabricated.

Before any `pasture task` protocol/review/slice command is enabled against the
coordinated Provenance schema, the #43/application startup coordinator calls
#14's read-only legacy-assignment extraction API. #14 never invokes #43. #43
classifies only tasks carrying a reserved, versioned Pasture protocol kind and
validates the exact required topology before building one idempotent
`NormalizeLegacyAssignmentRoles` conditional batch. That batch performs
same-owner responsibility transfers from generic legacy-owner assignments to
the typed role/slot, preserving predecessor, attribution, and ordered events.
There is no separate normalization marker, table, task, snapshot, or event: the
authoritative completion predicate is a deterministic post-batch requery proving
that every eligible active assignment already has its exact mapped role/slot and
no eligible generic assignment remains. An empty eligible set therefore succeeds
without inventing a marker host.

The v1 mapping is closed and exhaustive:

|---|---|
| REQUEST, ELICIT, URD, PROPOSAL, Plan-UAT, HANDOFF, and their FOLLOWUP forms | RoleArchitect |

Terminal or unassigned eligible tasks require no active transfer but are still
validated. A reserved known kind with missing/conflicting topology, or an
unknown future reserved Pasture kind, fails the entire batch and leaves the
database unchanged. Ordinary Provenance tasks and leaves without a reserved Pasture
kind are explicitly ineligible: their generic legacy-owner role remains valid,
they do not enter the batch, and they cannot block Pasture activation. Fault/
restart repeats the extraction and state-derived normalization safely. Protocol
commands remain unavailable until the deterministic post-batch inspection
succeeds.

The expected owner and current responsibility assignment are compared inside
the same transaction. Transfer ends the predecessor, optionally creates the
successor, changes Owner, and records attribution/events atomically. Two
distinct concurrent transitions have one winner; the stale loser changes no
owner, assignment, attribution, operation, or event row and receives an
actionable conflict. `ChangeTaskOwner` is only a compatibility constructor that
delegates to this transition when its full assignment expectation is supplied;
otherwise it rejects once the assignment migration is active.
This protects task assignment only; it is unrelated to plugin-installation
concurrency and introduces no installer transaction/CAS mechanism.

Task.Owner is role-neutral current responsibility. Prior/new material contributors retain
idempotent `attributed_to` edges. Administrative actors are not attributed merely
for changing a label/status; attribution occurs only for responsibility or
material contribution commands. Owner events record expected/previous/new owner,
actor, reason, OperationID, time, and EventID.

### 9.4 Activities, relationships, and graph events

`StartTaskActivity` and `EndTaskActivity` carry AssignmentID, ActivityID,
phase/stage, notes, and contexts; TaskID and ActorID are derived and validated
from that exact active assignment. Activity row state, task linkage, material event,
required attribution, and contexts commit together. Duration Activities remain
distinct from instantaneous transitions and do not encode structured changes in
notes. The state machine is closed: start requires a new ActivityID, existing
task, and actor resolved from the supplied active assignment; a new OperationID
cannot start an existing Activity. End requires the same linked task/agent and
an active Activity. End-before-start, wrong task/agent, invalid transitions, and
a second end under a new OperationID write nothing; same-OperationID retries
return the original result, and concurrent ends have one winner.

Task relationships accept TaskID targets. Attribution accepts ActorID. Activity
links accept ActivityID. A relationship involving two tasks writes a task-local
event to each timeline in one transaction, sharing OperationID and receiving
distinct EventIDs. Blocked-by cycle validation, edge persistence, and both events
share the same consistency boundary.

### 9.5 Current state and legacy migration

Current task/graph/Activity tables remain authoritative. The journal explains
all post-migration changes; it is not used to rebuild pre-journal state. When #5
activates the coordinated production migration, existing tasks each receive one
idempotent `provenance.migration.baseline` event containing the then-current
status/phase/owner and source schema version. In that same exclusive transaction,
every nonterminal assigned task receives a deterministic migration-time active
owner-responsibility assignment; every terminal assigned task receives an ended
migration assignment and has current Owner cleared; unassigned tasks receive no
assignment. Assignment IDs derive from schema version plus TaskID. Provenance
uses only its generic `provenance.role.legacy-owner` and
`provenance.slot.owner-responsibility`; it never invents a Pasture role. The task
baseline EventID is the active assignment's StartEventID at migration RecordedAt.
For a terminal legacy owner, a second ordered migration-time assignment-ended
event supplies EndEventID at the same RecordedAt; both are explicitly snapshot
events and never claim historical start/end time.

Legacy owner text that is not already a registered ActorID maps to a
deterministically registered `legacy-owner/<sha256>` SoftwareAgent whose payload
retains the original text; invalid/duplicate registration fails the entire
migration. Attribution and migration events retain that mapped owner but are
explicitly labeled snapshot/baseline evidence, never fabricated historical
start/end times. The post-migration invariant holds for every task kind: a
nonterminal nonnil Owner has exactly one matching active responsibility
assignment, while every terminal task has nil Owner and no active responsibility.
This marks the historical-completeness boundary.

The #5 production migration executes schema activation and every baseline row
inside one exclusive SQLite migration transaction. A fault after any number of
rows rolls back the schema marker, journal tables/changes, and all baselines;
reopen then performs the same migration from the pre-migration database. Empty
databases, every assigned/unassigned × terminal/nonterminal × task-kind case,
unmappable legacy owner text, repeat startup, and concurrent startup are explicit
fixtures. Baseline ActorID is the registered migrator; an absent legacy owner is
never fabricated.

Before any `pasture task` protocol/review/slice command is enabled against the
coordinated Provenance schema, the #43/application startup coordinator calls
#14's read-only legacy-assignment extraction API. #14 never invokes #43. #43
classifies only tasks carrying a reserved, versioned Pasture protocol kind and
validates the exact required topology before building one idempotent
`NormalizeLegacyAssignmentRoles` conditional batch. That batch performs
same-owner responsibility transfers from generic legacy-owner assignments to
the typed role/slot, preserving predecessor, attribution, and ordered events.
There is no separate normalization marker, table, task, snapshot, or event: the
authoritative completion predicate is a deterministic post-batch requery proving
that every eligible active assignment already has its exact mapped role/slot and
no eligible generic assignment remains. An empty eligible set therefore succeeds
without inventing a marker host.

The v1 mapping is closed and exhaustive:

| Persisted Pasture kind/topology | Normalized active owner role |
|---|---|
| REQUEST, ELICIT, URD, PROPOSAL, Plan-UAT, HANDOFF, and their FOLLOWUP forms | RoleArchitect |
| plan-review round/container | RoleArchitect |
| IMPL_PLAN, integration task, Implementation-UAT, landing container, supervisor-created follow-up epic | RoleSupervisor |
| implementation slice and explicitly typed Pasture implementation leaf | RoleWorker |
| code-review round/container and eager severity group | RoleSupervisor |
| implementation-review finding leaf | RoleWorker |
| review axis with exact correctness relationship | RoleReviewerCorrectness |
| review axis with exact test-quality relationship | RoleReviewerTestQuality |
| review axis with exact elegance relationship | RoleReviewerElegance |

Terminal or unassigned eligible tasks require no active transfer but are still
validated. A reserved known kind with missing/conflicting topology, or an
unknown future reserved Pasture kind, fails the entire batch and leaves the
database unchanged. Ordinary Provenance tasks and leaves without a reserved Pasture
kind are explicitly ineligible: their generic legacy-owner role remains valid,
they do not enter the batch, and they cannot block Pasture activation. Fault/
restart repeats the extraction and state-derived normalization safely. Protocol
commands remain unavailable until the deterministic post-batch inspection
succeeds.

Pasture #43 owns a closed, typed import command; #14 supplies only extraction and
adapter plumbing:

```go
type LegacyAuditRowID string
type LegacySchemaVersion string
type ImportLegacyAuditRow struct { /* unexported validated row */ }

func NewImportLegacyAuditRow(
    schema LegacySchemaVersion,
    row LegacyAuditRowID,
    actor LegacyActorRef,
    recordedAt time.Time,
    definition LegacyEventDefinition,
    contexts []LegacyContext,
    tasks []provenance.TaskID,
) (ImportLegacyAuditRow, error)
```

The constructor validates the source schema/row identity, maps the legacy kind
and payload through a typed #43-owned definition, validates every context, drops
duplicate task IDs, sorts the remaining typed IDs, and resolves the actor before
any Apply call. Unknown kinds/payload shapes or invalid/empty task fan-out fail
without writes. Pasture migrates actual legacy audit history without deleting or
updating source rows; pre/post byte hashes of the legacy tables are acceptance
evidence:

- #14's finite coordinator collects all rows and `context_edges`, validates the
  full extraction, sorts rows by `(recorded time, legacy row ID)`, and imports
  serially, stopping at the first failure so equal-time EventID allocation is
  deterministic across repeat/reopen;
- resolve every unique task ID represented by epoch/slice/review/follow-up task
  contexts;
- invoke one #43-owned `ImportLegacyAuditRow` command containing the source
  schema, legacy row ID, actor mapping, original time/payload, all contexts, and
  the sorted unique TaskIDs; it validates/encodes typed payloads and delegates
  once to Provenance's generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation;
- have that single Apply operation create one canonical TaskEvent per `(legacy
  schema, legacy event ID, resolved TaskID)`, attaching all of that row's legacy
  contexts;
- give the batch one stable migration OperationID derived from `(legacy schema,
  legacy event ID)` and deterministic event insert order `(legacy recorded time,
  legacy row ID, task ID)`; and
- enforce the compound legacy identity uniquely so repeat migration/reopen cannot
  duplicate events.

`ImportLegacyAuditRow` is atomic: every event/context/operation result for one
legacy row commits or none does. A retry with the same source identity returns
the canonical batch result and EventIDs; conflicting source content fails. An
injected failure after the first event rolls back the full row batch. This is a
finite schema import, not an event-sourcing or runtime transaction subsystem.

Migrated real events preserve their original RecordedAt and mapped ActorID. When
an old actor cannot be resolved, the migration uses an explicitly registered
`pasture-legacy-migrator` SoftwareAgent and retains the original actor text in the
typed migration payload; ActorID is never silently nil or forged. Baseline events
use a registered `provenance-migrator` SoftwareAgent and migration time. Stable
OperationIDs derive from the typed legacy-row identity through a documented
constructor, not from process-local counters.

Thus one old row linked to several tasks appears on every relevant task timeline
without losing its many-to-many contexts. #14 owns the separately named,
read-only `pasture legacy-audit event list` API for non-task legacy rows and its
raw source-identity/actor-text/context tests; #43 never folds those rows into a
task timeline. After auto-migration,
`pasture task timeline TASK-ID` reads canonical Provenance TaskEvents only; it
does not perform an unstable runtime merge with rows lacking EventID.

Every mutation accepts `--mutation-ref MUTATION-REF` and its exact initiating
`--assignment ASSIGNMENT-REF` or `--bootstrap-agent AGENT-REF`; typed JSON results expose
named bindings for created TaskRef/AssignmentRef/ReviewRoundRef values. Exact

carry typed ValueRefs plus the complete MutationContinuation; #14/#43 converts
them to authoritative Provenance IDs, resolves ActorID from the retained
historical initiating authority for committed replay and from that same active
authority for a new operation, and never accepts an actor/supervisor
override for review or slice closure. Bootstrap/administrative callers use a
separate registered-agent API and make no authentication claim. Queries are
side-effect free. Generic `task update` is available only to ordinary leaves and
changes only non-reserved descriptive metadata; it rejects every protected
subject/review/slice/protocol task and all status, phase, kind, owner, assignment,
body-revision, or relationship changes. `transition` accepts a kind-specific expected/from/to transition;
`supersede` atomically makes the successor the sole canonical proposal, relates
the successor as superseding the old artifact, and transitions the old one;
`ratify` requires accepted review-round evidence plus accepted Plan-UAT or an
exact same-epoch `deferred_by_afk` event bound to the DocumentRevisionSubject,
epoch root, input/output ledger revisions, agent actor, and AFK mode-entry cursor.
For AFK deferral it also folds the current ledger in the same transaction and
requires that exact entry still be the latest interaction-mode entry with result
AFK. Normal selection or any later mode entry makes the old deferral historical
and ineligible; AFK->normal->AFK requires a fresh Plan deferral.
`land` performs no Git operation. It requires resolved dependencies plus clean
review and Implementation-UAT evidence bound to the same exact current
IntegrationCandidateSetSubject and one #43-owned typed
`pasture.git.remote-ref-verified/v1` material event per repository candidate.
It also CASes the exact current ledger `DocumentRevisionID` and recomputed required-
entry coverage digest named by that accepted UAT; any successor ledger revision
invalidates the UAT relation and defeats land.
That event is protected from generic recording. The sole executable producer is
the versioned application/#40 composite command `pasture task integration
publish-repository`. Its typed argv names exact current IntegrationCandidateSetID,
RepositoryID, CommitOID, TreeDigest, RemoteRef, ExpectedOldOID, controlling
AssignmentID, and MutationRef. In one Pasture process it executes this closed
sequence:

1. Before the first attempt, #40 passes the fully resolved typed request to
   #43's pure `command canonicalize` API. #43 canonicalizes one versioned
   `PublicationIntent` containing every task-command field except MutationRef and
   authority and returns its typed digest. The surviving parent then mints
   MutationRef and retains the complete continuation in AssignmentContext.
2. #40 passes the same request and complete continuation to #43's internal,
   side-effect-free `PrepareRepositoryPublication`. #43 recomputes and validates
   exact identity, rejects placeholders/mismatch, and asks #14 to map the ref,
   exact assignment-or-bootstrap authority, historical actor, and digest to #5.
   The returned opaque
   `PublicationPreparation` contains exactly the OperationID/CommandDigest pair
   plus OperationAuthorityID that any later #14 `Apply` records. An exact committed lookup returns the
   original status/EventID/result map without touching Git, including after
   authority has ended or Git is unavailable; `Conflict` fails; `Absent`
   continues. Neither #40 nor a caller can supply or inspect either digest.
3. The same #43 preparation performs a read-only publication preflight. It requires the exact current
   integration set and repository tuple, the controlling active supervisor
   assignment, one current fix-free accepted integration-review round, one
   accepted current Implementation-UAT decision, and either no canonical
   publication evidence or the one exact existing event for
   `(IntegrationCandidateSetID, RepositoryID)`. Stale, unreviewed, unaccepted,
   unauthorized, mismatched, or conflicting evidence fails before Git. Exact
   existing evidence produces an `existing_evidence` preparation without Git.
4. Only an eligible absent-evidence result calls #46 guarded push or verified
   already-at-target and retains that non-serializable success value in memory.
5. #40 returns the opaque preparation plus #46 result to #43. For
   `existing_evidence`, #43 uses #14's closed
   `ConditionalExistingIDResult`: the exact canonical-evidence precondition
   produces an ExistingEventHandle; the same current set/repository/review/UAT/

   only this OperationID's typed EventID result. It creates no domain row/event
   and cannot bind an arbitrary ID or scalar. For verified Git, #43 rechecks every preflight predicate inside
   one ConditionalMutationBatch and installs exactly one event/relation. The
   process-local Git proof gates this method but is excluded from
   `PublicationIntent`, so preparation, lookup, and Apply share identical command
   bytes. If a distinct operation wins the canonical evidence race, #43
