the UI/Home Manager message tells the user to review them through Codex's native
hooks UI. Pasture never writes private hook-trust hashes or claims the hooks are
active before native approval.

Generated packages carry immutable target/component identities,
RuntimeContractIDs, and point host ranges. #39 binds those descriptors to its
ActivationContractIDs. Every action probes the public host version first. A
manifest host constraint appears only when the native schema documents it.
These compatibility checks remain stateless contract validation. Their observed
postconditions feed the separate installation inventory; they are not inferred
from it.

## 8. Goldmark inventory and finite migration

This work has two dependency-distinct milestones rather than one inverted gate.

**Milestone A — inventory/classification (Pasture #47, after #38):**

1. A read-only scanner parses every active generated Markdown owner through
   Goldmark and reports candidate harness syntax with owner, file/section, AST
   node/range, snippet, and candidate class.
2. Maintainers explicitly classify each candidate as orchestration, decision,
   task/process/Git/filesystem effect, portable Verbatim, exhaustive
   TargetLiteral, neutral false positive, or dead owner.
3. The scanner independently walks a code-owned closed list of canonical source
   roots and explicit output/vendor/test-fixture exclusions, rejecting symlinked
   owners. It compares that discovered set with the checked-in owner manifest;
   the manifest is classification input, never the discovery source. Missing
   active files, stale entries, dead-owner dispositions, and exclusion drift are
   errors. The scan emits deterministic source/AST order and is proved read-only
   by byte-for-byte tree hashes before and after. Every classification—including
   neutral false positive and dead owner—is represented by a golden fixture.
4. The classified inventory is an input to #46, #43, and #40; those issues may
   not freeze their closed algebras/contracts before consuming it.

**Milestone B — typed migration and strict rejection (Pasture #42, after #47,
#46, #43, and #40):**

5. Canonical Go specs migrate every classified orchestration, task,
   process/Git/filesystem, and decision occurrence to the typed Document/effect
   API. This issue alone removes operational `bd` instructions. Proposal 20's
   `runtime.go` regex and global string replacements are deleted, not retained as
   compatibility parsing.
6. The unclassified active-candidate count reaches zero. Any nonzero
   unclassified count prevents strict-mode activation; the classified inventory
   remains required input and is not itself an error.
7. Strict mode permanently rejects newly introduced unclassified harness syntax
   in Markdown and emits no target output.

The scanner recognizes legacy lexical forms only to report them. It never assigns
semantics or rewrites production output. The malformed
`TeamCreate({...}) -> task(({...})` case remains a regression fixture.

## 9. Provenance authoritative task journal

### 9.1 Generic envelope and caller-owned payloads

```go
type EventID int64
type EventKind string
type OperationID string
type EventContextKind string

type EventContext struct { /* opaque validated kind + encoded identity */ }

func TaskContext(TaskID) (EventContext, error)
func ActivityContext(ActivityID) (EventContext, error)
func AgentContext(AgentID) (EventContext, error)
func GitContext(GitOID) (EventContext, error)

type ExtensionContextID interface {
    ~string
    EventContextDomain() EventContextKind
}

type ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID ExtensionContextID] struct { /* opaque */ }
func DefineExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    validate func(ID) error,
) (ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID], error)
func ExtensionContext[ID ExtensionContextID](
    descriptor ExtensionContextDescriptor[ID],
    id ID,
) (EventContext, error)

type TaskEvent struct {
    ID          EventID
    TaskID      TaskID
    Kind        EventKind
    ActorID     AgentID
    RecordedAt  time.Time
    OperationID OperationID
    Contexts    []EventContext
    Payload     json.RawMessage
}
```

EventID is database-generated and exposed once. Queries order ascending by
`(RecordedAt, EventID)` and expose both fields. EventKind/context kinds are
validated namespaced types. `EventContext` has no exported raw `ID string`
constructor or fields. Built-in constructors require the corresponding typed ID
and reject zero or structurally invalid values. Caller namespaces define a named
string-backed ID implementing the marker method plus a typed descriptor and
validator. `DefineExtensionContext` derives its kind from the named ID type's
marker; it takes no duplicate kind argument, rejects every reserved Provenance
built-in kind (task/activity/agent/git), and requires a valid caller-owned
namespace. At value construction the ID's reported kind must still equal the
descriptor kind. Built-in `string` cannot satisfy `ExtensionContextID`, so
`DefineExtensionContext[string]` is a compile failure. Only the internal
persistence codec serializes context kind plus text.

Provenance validates the generic envelope, identity syntax/references, contexts,
and payload well-formedness. It does not import or globally register Pasture
codecs. Pasture constructs an opaque typed event definition, validates its
`pasture.*` payload, encodes it, and passes it across this boundary.

Secondary contexts supplied during event creation commit atomically. A later
context attachment, when necessary, is itself a journalled mutation. Typed
constructors prevent TaskID, ActivityID, GitOID, and caller-defined IDs from
being accidentally interchanged even though storage uses a common textual
encoding. Contexts have set semantics: construction, persistence, operation
canonicalization, and query output deduplicate and sort by
`(EventContextKind, canonical encoded identity)`. Association-row insertion
order is never observable. Each context edge stores the EventID that attached
it (the original event for initial contexts, the journalled attachment event for
later contexts). Snapshot queries include only edges whose attachment EventID is
at or below SnapshotMaxEventID, so a later attachment cannot change an in-flight
filtered traversal.

### 9.2 Atomic command API and durable idempotency

```go
type MutationContext struct {
    ActorID     AgentID
    OperationID OperationID
}

Apply(ctx context.Context, mc MutationContext, command Mutation) (MutationResult, error)
```

Provenance #4 owns the TaskEvent envelope, context storage, ordering/query APIs,
and internal append/schema primitives. It exposes no public OperationID replay,
raw event-append bypass, registered production migration, or baseline side
effect. Its persistence tests activate the schema explicitly in isolated test
databases. Provenance #5 exclusively owns the public command/result table, the
following `Apply` surface, and the production migration that installs the #4
schema, writes baselines, and activates atomic journaling. #4 and #5 ship in one
Provenance release tag after both merge; there is no released state in which a
database has a writable journal but non-journalled mutators.

The closed command family covers task lifecycle, typed relationships, labels,
comments, responsibility/supervision assignments, explicit attribution,
task-linked Activity start/end,
later event-context attachment, and a generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation for
caller-validated material events that change no current task state. Provenance
commits domain row(s), any required attribution, TaskEvent row(s), contexts, and
canonical operation/result through one `internal/sqlite` connection/transaction.
Pasture does not compose a fake transaction across separate tracker/audit
connections.

#5 also owns opaque `ConditionalMutationBatch` construction. It is a closed,
extension-safe declarative composition of existing generic mutations plus
caller-validated opaque material events; it is not a callback, raw SQL, or an
untyped predicate escape hatch. Its built-in preconditions cover exact task
kind/status/owner, exact active/ended assignment and active-slot set, typed
relationship presence/absence and exact incoming/outgoing typed set equality,
exact task revision plus immutable subject task/current-subject relationships, exact immutable EventID/task/kind/context
evidence, and absence of unresolved blocked-by children. Canonical typed local
handles let later batch mutations reference earlier allocated tasks/assignments;
the result returns their stable ID map. Preconditions are
rechecked inside the same SQLite transaction immediately before the ordered
mutations. Domain rows, assignment transitions, relationships, events,
contexts, attribution, and operation result all commit or roll back together.
Pasture #43 compiles review/transition/closure policy into these generic
preconditions and mutations; Provenance never decodes a `pasture.*` payload.

OperationID is durable idempotency identity. Same ID plus byte-equivalent
canonical command/actor returns the originally committed result/events after
close/reopen or concurrent retry. Same ID with different actor/command fails.
The operation row rolls back with the mutation, so there is no pending state.

Pre-1.0 direct mutator paths migrate to Apply or compatibility wrappers that
require MutationContext and delegate to the same transaction. No exported bypass
may mutate a task/graph without its event.

### 9.3 Responsibility CAS and cumulative attribution

```go
type TransferTaskResponsibility struct {
    Task          TaskID
    ExpectedOwner OwnerExpectation // OwnerIs(agent) or OwnerIsUnassigned()
    ExpectedAssignment AssignmentExpectation
    Successor     OptionalAssignmentDraft // absent means become unassigned
    Reason        string
}
```

The expected owner and current responsibility assignment are compared inside
the same transaction. Transfer ends the predecessor, optionally creates the
successor, changes Owner, and records attribution/events atomically. Two
distinct concurrent transitions have one winner; the stale loser changes no
owner, assignment, attribution, operation, or event row and receives an
actionable conflict. `ChangeTaskOwner` is only a compatibility constructor that
delegates to this transition when its full assignment expectation is supplied;
otherwise it rejects once the assignment migration is active.
This protects task assignment only; it is unrelated to plugin-installation
concurrency and introduces no installer transaction/CAS mechanism.

Task.Owner is role-neutral current responsibility. Prior/new material contributors retain
idempotent `attributed_to` edges. Administrative actors are not attributed merely
for changing a label/status; attribution occurs only for responsibility or
material contribution commands. Owner events record expected/previous/new owner,
actor, reason, OperationID, time, and EventID.

### 9.4 Activities, relationships, and graph events

`StartTaskActivity` and `EndTaskActivity` carry AssignmentID, ActivityID,
phase/stage, notes, and contexts; TaskID and AgentID are derived and validated
from that exact active assignment. Activity row state, task linkage, material event,
required attribution, and contexts commit together. Duration Activities remain
distinct from instantaneous transitions and do not encode structured changes in
notes. The state machine is closed: start requires a new ActivityID, existing
task, and actor resolved from the supplied active assignment; a new OperationID
cannot start an existing Activity. End requires the same linked task/agent and
an active Activity. End-before-start, wrong task/agent, invalid transitions, and
a second end under a new OperationID write nothing; same-OperationID retries
return the original result, and concurrent ends have one winner.

Task relationships accept TaskID targets. Attribution accepts AgentID. Activity
links accept ActivityID. A relationship involving two tasks writes a task-local
event to each timeline in one transaction, sharing OperationID and receiving
distinct EventIDs. Blocked-by cycle validation, edge persistence, and both events
share the same consistency boundary.

### 9.5 Current state and legacy migration

Current task/graph/Activity tables remain authoritative. The journal explains
all post-migration changes; it is not used to rebuild pre-journal state. When #5
activates the coordinated production migration, existing tasks each receive one
idempotent `provenance.migration.baseline` event containing the then-current
status/phase/owner and source schema version. In that same exclusive transaction,
every nonterminal assigned task receives a deterministic migration-time active
owner-responsibility assignment; every terminal assigned task receives an ended
migration assignment and has current Owner cleared; unassigned tasks receive no
assignment. Assignment IDs derive from schema version plus TaskID. Provenance
uses only its generic `provenance.role.legacy-owner` and
`provenance.slot.owner-responsibility`; it never invents a Pasture role. The task
baseline EventID is the active assignment's StartEventID at migration RecordedAt.
For a terminal legacy owner, a second ordered migration-time assignment-ended
event supplies EndEventID at the same RecordedAt; both are explicitly snapshot
events and never claim historical start/end time.

Legacy owner text that is not already a registered AgentID maps to a
deterministically registered `legacy-owner/<sha256>` SoftwareAgent whose payload
retains the original text; invalid/duplicate registration fails the entire
migration. Attribution and migration events retain that mapped owner but are
explicitly labeled snapshot/baseline evidence, never fabricated historical
start/end times. The post-migration invariant holds for every task kind: a
nonterminal nonnil Owner has exactly one matching active responsibility
assignment, while every terminal task has nil Owner and no active responsibility.
This marks the historical-completeness boundary.

The #5 production migration executes schema activation and every baseline row
inside one exclusive SQLite migration transaction. A fault after any number of
rows rolls back the schema marker, journal tables/changes, and all baselines;
reopen then performs the same migration from the pre-migration database. Empty
databases, every assigned/unassigned × terminal/nonterminal × task-kind case,
unmappable legacy owner text, repeat startup, and concurrent startup are explicit
fixtures. Baseline ActorID is the registered migrator; an absent legacy owner is
never fabricated.

Before any `pasture task` protocol/review/slice command is enabled against the
coordinated Provenance schema, #14 extracts all active generic legacy-owner
assignments and #43 validates an exhaustive task-kind/context mapping. One
idempotent `NormalizeLegacyAssignmentRoles` conditional batch performs same-owner
responsibility transfers from each generic assignment to the correct typed
Pasture role/slot, preserving predecessor, attribution, and ordered events, then
commits a Pasture normalization marker. IMPL_PLAN maps to RoleSupervisor, slices
to RoleWorker, proposal/planning containers to RoleArchitect, and live review
axes only through their validated axis relationships. An ambiguous/missing/
conflicting kind or relationship fails actionably with the whole normalization
batch and marker absent. Startup exposes no protocol command until the marker is
present; fault/restart repeats safely. Terminal/unassigned tasks need no active
role normalization.

Pasture #43 owns a closed, typed import command; #14 supplies only extraction and
adapter plumbing:

```go
type LegacyAuditRowID string
type LegacySchemaVersion string
type ImportLegacyAuditRow struct { /* unexported validated row */ }

func NewImportLegacyAuditRow(
    schema LegacySchemaVersion,
    row LegacyAuditRowID,
    actor LegacyActorRef,
    recordedAt time.Time,
    definition LegacyEventDefinition,
    contexts []LegacyContext,
    tasks []provenance.TaskID,
) (ImportLegacyAuditRow, error)
```

The constructor validates the source schema/row identity, maps the legacy kind
and payload through a typed #43-owned definition, validates every context, drops
duplicate task IDs, sorts the remaining typed IDs, and resolves the actor before
any Apply call. Unknown kinds/payload shapes or invalid/empty task fan-out fail
without writes. Pasture migrates actual legacy audit history without deleting or
updating source rows; pre/post byte hashes of the legacy tables are acceptance
evidence:

- #14's finite coordinator collects all rows and `context_edges`, validates the
  full extraction, sorts rows by `(recorded time, legacy row ID)`, and imports
  serially, stopping at the first failure so equal-time EventID allocation is
  deterministic across repeat/reopen;
- resolve every unique task ID represented by epoch/slice/review/follow-up task
  contexts;
- invoke one #43-owned `ImportLegacyAuditRow` command containing the source
  schema, legacy row ID, actor mapping, original time/payload, all contexts, and
  the sorted unique TaskIDs; it validates/encodes typed payloads and delegates
  once to Provenance's generic `AppendTaskEventBatch` mutation;
- have that single Apply operation create one canonical TaskEvent per `(legacy
  schema, legacy event ID, resolved TaskID)`, attaching all of that row's legacy
  contexts;
- give the batch one stable migration OperationID derived from `(legacy schema,
  legacy event ID)` and deterministic event insert order `(legacy recorded time,
  legacy row ID, task ID)`; and
- enforce the compound legacy identity uniquely so repeat migration/reopen cannot
  duplicate events.

`ImportLegacyAuditRow` is atomic: every event/context/operation result for one
legacy row commits or none does. A retry with the same source identity returns
the canonical batch result and EventIDs; conflicting source content fails. An
injected failure after the first event rolls back the full row batch. This is a
finite schema import, not an event-sourcing or runtime transaction subsystem.

Migrated real events preserve their original RecordedAt and mapped AgentID. When
an old actor cannot be resolved, the migration uses an explicitly registered
`pasture-legacy-migrator` SoftwareAgent and retains the original actor text in the
typed migration payload; ActorID is never silently nil or forged. Baseline events
use a registered `provenance-migrator` SoftwareAgent and migration time. Stable
OperationIDs derive from the typed legacy-row identity through a documented
constructor, not from process-local counters.

Thus one old row linked to several tasks appears on every relevant task timeline
without losing its many-to-many contexts. #14 owns the separately named,
read-only `pasture legacy-audit event list` API for non-task legacy rows and its
raw source-identity/actor-text/context tests; #43 never folds those rows into a
task timeline. After auto-migration,
`pasture task timeline TASK-ID` reads canonical Provenance TaskEvents only; it
does not perform an unstable runtime merge with rows lacking EventID.

## 10. `pasture task` algebra, Provenance backend, and CLI (#43)

Issue #43 owns the typed task-effect variants, their Provenance-backed execution,
the `pasture.*` material event definitions, closure-policy validation, composed
timeline projection, and this frozen command contract. Pasture #14 owns only the
low-level Provenance dependency adapter and legacy-import plumbing; it does not
define task effects or map them to commands. #43 does not migrate generated
source or remove `bd`; issue #42 consumes the completed contract and owns that
finite conversion.

```text
pasture task contract --json
pasture task create|show|update|close|reopen|list
pasture task ready|blocked|dep tree
pasture task relation add|remove|list
pasture task assignment start|end|transfer|list
pasture task attribute add|list
pasture task label add|remove|list
pasture task comment add|list
pasture task activity start|end|list
pasture task event record|list
pasture task protocol create|revise|transition|supersede|ratify|land
pasture task review start|submit|finalize|rework
pasture task slice create|candidate set|rework|close
pasture task integration candidate-set|uat-bind
pasture task context add|list
pasture task timeline TASK-ID [--json]
```

```text
pasture task slice close TASK-ID --assignment ASSIGNMENT-ID \
  --round REVIEW-ROUND-ID --subject REVIEW-SUBJECT-ID \
  --review-event correctness=EVENT-ID \
  --review-event test-quality=EVENT-ID \
  --review-event elegance=EVENT-ID
```

Every mutation accepts `--mutation-ref MUTATION-REF` and its exact initiating
`--assignment ASSIGNMENT-REF` or `--bootstrap-agent AGENT-REF`; typed JSON results expose
named bindings for created TaskRef/AssignmentRef/ReviewRoundRef values. Exact
flags/JSON schemas are frozen before generation. Generated workflow documents
carry typed ValueRefs plus the complete MutationContinuation; #14/#43 converts
them to authoritative Provenance IDs, resolves ActorID from the retained
historical initiating authority for committed replay and from that same active
authority for a new operation, and never accepts an actor/supervisor
override for review or slice closure. Bootstrap/administrative callers use a
separate registered-agent API and make no authentication claim. Queries are
side-effect free. Generic `task update` is available only to ordinary leaves and
changes only non-reserved descriptive metadata; it rejects every protected
subject/review/slice/protocol task and all status, phase, kind, owner, assignment,
body-revision, or relationship changes. `transition` accepts a kind-specific expected/from/to transition;
`supersede` atomically relates old/new artifacts and transitions the old one;
`ratify` requires accepted review-round evidence plus UAT or an explicit typed
user waiver/deferral event bound to the exact current DocumentRevisionSubject.
`land` performs no Git operation. It requires resolved dependencies plus clean
review and Implementation-UAT evidence bound to the same exact current
IntegrationCandidateSetSubject and one #43-owned typed
`pasture.git.remote-ref-verified/v1` material event per repository candidate.
#40 maps only a successful exact #46 GuardedPushResult into that event schema;
#43 does not import #46. Generated workflow composition runs each #46 guarded
push, verifies all remotes, records the events, and only then invokes #43 land.
If a push succeeds but evidence or
Apply fails, retry treats the already-exact remote as success and recreates the
evidence; partial multi-repository success is reported and resumed without
rollback. Any candidate/tree/ref change invalidates the set/evidence and requires
new integration review/UAT. Generic `task close` rejects slice, review, and protocol-
container kinds. The exact slice CLI includes RoundID, SubjectID, AssignmentID,
and three accepted review EventIDs and lowers the §5.3 predicate and mutations
into one ConditionalMutationBatch.

`pasture task contract --json` returns the closed
`pasture.task.contract-probe/v1` schema containing CLI semver, TaskContractID,
supported schema IDs/ranges, and a canonical definition digest. Generated

# PROPOSAL-5: Versioned SDLC codebook, provenance, control, and context planes

## Status, authority, and disposition

This is a required pivot after post-hoc Plan UAT. The full question text, every
option, examples shown, and the user responses **verbatim** are authoritative in
`aura-plugins-q5ams`; this proposal does not paraphrase or replace that
transcript. The requirements it implements include append-every-occurrence with
no deduplication, the temporary lifecycle exit-0 posture, broad automated
provenance writes, deterministic normative control, and FSM-driven progressive
context disclosure.

**PROPOSAL-4 must be superseded.** The audit demonstrates an incompatible
architectural change, not a narrow correction:

1. its replay key, payload digest, `RecordReplayed`, and one-record-per-bytes
   rule silently lose genuine occurrences, contrary to the accepted UAT decision;
2. `Semantics{EventSemantic, Blocking, Identities}` gives every occurrence one
   interpretation and conflates evidence, gate consultation, and a human answer;
3. retaining `LifecycleEventMapping` in an `Event` lets a native transport
   classification masquerade as a target-agnostic semantic interpretation;
4. the same-package `BackendView` boundary is not compiler-enforced: `lower.go`
   can read `event.origin.behaviour` directly, as demonstrated by
   `aura-plugins-mgn58`;
5. the plan has no model for an evolving executable SDLC codebook, application
   identity, interpretation history, causal artifact lineage, or context
   disclosures.

The compiler-hourglass finding remains valid: generated host artifacts are
mechanical, native parsers live in Go, and policy belongs in one middle-end. The
M2 draft is informative only. It is not authority to preserve prototype
interfaces that conflict with this plan.

## Scope and non-goals

In scope:

- all 30 pinned Claude events, each appended as an occurrence and audited below;
- an explicit three-plane model: evidence/provenance, normative control, and
  context disclosure;
- immutable version identity for native runtime contract, codebook, and Pasture
  Epoch implementation;
- causal provenance queries from exact code/artifact to human signal, agent,
  turn, tool call, subagent, context, and controlling transition;
- real host response capability, initially exit-0/continue only, with a safe
  future allow/deny/ask protocol;
- replacement rather than preservation of the M1 prototype where needed.

Out of scope for this proposal: automatic truth claims from a file path alone,
installation of Git hooks, a generic programmable policy language, a second
workflow ledger/FSM beside the existing Epoch/Provenance path, or an immediate
solution to all payload retention choices. Git hooks remain prohibited absent
separate explicit user approval.

## The three planes and operation legend

A native hook is an ingress point, not an authority grant. One occurrence may
produce several independently versioned facts across all three planes.

| Plane | Purpose | Write rule |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence/provenance | immutable fact that a host occurrence, human signal, agent action, tool exchange, environment change, artifact observation, or causal relation was observed | broad append is expected; every delivery receives a new database row ID |
| Normative control | current Epoch FSM state, legal transition, approval, assignment, gate and authority | only a separately authorized engine commit may alter it; candidates are not commits |
| Context disclosure | phase/role/actor scoped instructions, constraints, capabilities, refreshes, and revocations | codebook projects it; planned, delivered, acknowledged, and revoked are separately recorded |

The hook table uses these explicit operation codes.

- **AE** append an occurrence-evidence record; **AT** attach it to known native
  session/turn/agent/tool/request/task/worktree bindings; **H** record a human
  input or decision claim; **A** record an agent action/output/artifact claim.
- **PT** propose a candidate FSM transition; **CT** commit a normative FSM or
  binding transition; **CG** consult current gate/phase state.
- **IX** inject, refresh, mutate, or revoke disclosed context; **AD** answer
  allow, deny, ask, or the temporary neutral continue response; **NO** means no
  operation in that plane.

`H(asserted)` is deliberately weaker than authenticated identity: Claude has
reported user-facing input, but only a registered Pasture human actor plus a
Pasture-issued request/capability can authorize a normative decision. A native
occurrence has no power to manufacture that authority.

## Native transport and unclassified occurrence waist

The current IR must be replaced by a typed, target-independent **native
occurrence** waist. It represents only an authenticated-as-transport native
claim, never its final SDLC meaning.

```go
// pkg/protocol: opaque constructors validate canonical form.
type OccurrenceID uint64               // SQLite AUTOINCREMENT row identity
type CodebookID string                 // stable logical family, e.g. pasture-epoch
type CodebookVersion string            // immutable validated release/version label
type CodebookDigest [32]byte            // canonical definition bytes, not payload bytes
type RuntimeContractRef struct {
    ID     ir.RuntimeContractID
    Version runtime.HostVersion
    Digest  ContractDigest
}
type EpochImplementationRef struct {
    Product        ApplicationID
    Release        ApplicationVersion
    VCSRevision    RevisionID       // full source revision when available
    SourceDigest   SourceTreeDigest // required for reproducible identity
    BuildArtifact  BuildDigest
    Dirty          bool
    BuildMetadata  BuildMetadataID  // compiler, module graph, build flags/profile
}
type CodebookRef struct {
    ID      CodebookID
    Version CodebookVersion
    Digest  CodebookDigest
}

type NativeOccurrence struct {
    ID              OccurrenceID
    Contract        RuntimeContractRef
    NativeEvent     NativeEventKind // typed member of that contract, not semantic
    ReceivedAt      time.Time       // descriptive, never an identity component
    CaptureBuild    EpochImplementationRef
    ParseStatus     ParseStatus     // parsed, unsupported-schema, malformed, etc.
    NativeBindings  []NativeBinding // session/turn/request/tool/agent/message only
    Payload         EvidencePayloadRef
}
```

`OccurrenceID` alone disambiguates deliveries. `ReceivedAt` is descriptive.
There is no `PayloadDigest`, `ReplayKey`, `RecordReplayed`, payload-based unique
index, or replay suppression anywhere in evidence ingress. A duplicate delivery
gets a second `OccurrenceID`, even when bytes and every extracted field are
identical. Control-plane idempotency remains necessary but is independent: a
single-use authority capability and engine operation identity protect a
normative commit without deleting evidence of repeated native deliveries.

`NativeEventKind` is the typed occurrence kind requested by this pivot. The
runtime profile remains a static host contract, but is narrowed to native facts:
exact event spelling, complete known payload schema, identity extraction schema,
and host interaction/response capability. It must not contain `EventSemantic` or
an SDLC operation mapping. `EventByNativeName` from `aura-plugins-57lhx` is
retained as the one validating native-token-to-typed-event lookup.

The frontend returns an unclassified occurrence or an unclassified occurrence
plus a structured parse issue. Capture happens before interpretation, so a
malformed, unknown-field, or unknown-event delivery is still appended with the
available transport coordinates and a redacted payload reference. It is not
silently lost and it is not assigned a guessed semantic meaning.

## Codebook, implementation identity, and interpretation persistence

The codebook is executable metadata, not analytics labels. It has four compiled
views: occurrence classification, causal-edge rules, transition/gate authority
rules, and context-disclosure rules. Work backwards from the required query:
old occurrences must be explainable under the exact codebook and executable
that interpreted them, even after a future codebook changes.

```go
type InterpretationBatchID uint64
type InterpretationRef struct {
    Batch          InterpretationBatchID
    Codebook       CodebookRef
    Implementation EpochImplementationRef
}
type InterpretedFact struct {
    ID             FactID
    Occurrence     OccurrenceID
    Interpretation InterpretationRef
    Kind           CodebookScopedFactKind
    Subject        ProvenanceNodeRef
    Attributes     []TypedAttribute
}
type CandidateTransition struct {
    ID             CandidateTransitionID
    Interpretation InterpretationRef
    Epoch          EpochID
    Proposed       CodebookTransitionID
    Basis          []FactID
    Required       AuthorityRequirement
}
type ControlCommit struct {
    ID             ControlCommitID
    Candidate      CandidateTransitionID
    Authority      AuthorityGrantID
    ExpectedState  EpochStateVersion
    EngineResult   EngineCommitRef
    Interpretation InterpretationRef
}
type ContextDisclosure struct {
    ID             ContextDisclosureID
    Interpretation InterpretationRef
    Recipient      ActorSessionBindingID
    Scope          CodebookContextScope
    Material       ContextMaterialRef
    State          DisclosureState // planned, delivered, acknowledged, revoked
    Basis          []FactID
}
```

Persist immutable `codebook_definitions` and `epoch_implementations` before
writing any dependent record. Persist `runtime_contract_definitions` or a
canonical immutable snapshot for every referenced `RuntimeContractRef`.
`occurrences` carries its runtime contract and capture build. Every session
binding, interpreted fact, causal edge, candidate, control commit, context
disclosure, and artifact edge carries an `InterpretationRef`, either directly or
through an immutable interpretation-batch parent that queries must join. The
parent is never mutable; denormalized `CodebookRef`/implementation columns on
facts are recommended for forensic queries and checked against the parent.

A Git revision is not sufficient implementation identity: the same commit can
be rebuilt with different dependency graphs, flags, generated schemas, or local
dirty changes; a dirty tree may have no faithful public commit at all. The build
must stamp a release version, full VCS revision when present, dirty status,
source-tree digest, binary digest, module/build profile, and generated-codebook
digest. `debug.ReadBuildInfo` is supplemental only; release/Nix builds must
inject a reproducible manifest. A record whose source/build identity is absent
is explicitly marked non-reproducible, never silently represented as a commit.

Definitions are a combination of static typed Go data and persisted canonical
documents: source code/generation produces closed Go enums and validators for a
shipped codebook; its canonical schema/document is embedded and persisted with
its digest. Database records use codebook-scoped typed identifiers, not free
strings. Importing a new codebook is an explicit migration/release operation
that validates the immutable definition before it becomes selectable.

No interpretation is changed in place. Reclassification creates another
`InterpretationBatch` and new facts/edges that name both the same occurrence and
the new codebook ref. The prior facts remain queryable. A view may select a
preferred interpretation, but it may not overwrite history.

## Public provenance and control interfaces

These are public behavior-oriented contracts; storage row IDs and codecs stay
internal.

```go
type ProvenanceReader interface {
    ExplainArtifact(context.Context, ArtifactRef) (ArtifactLineage, error)
    ExplainHumanSignal(context.Context, ArtifactRef) (HumanSignalLineage, error)
    ActorContextHistory(context.Context, ActorSessionBindingID) ([]ContextDisclosure, error)
    ExplainTransition(context.Context, ControlCommitID) (TransitionLineage, error)
}
type OccurrenceAppender interface {
    AppendOccurrence(context.Context, NativeOccurrenceDraft) (OccurrenceID, error)
}
type Interpreter interface {
    Interpret(context.Context, CodebookRef, OccurrenceID) (InterpretationBatchID, error)
}
type ControlService interface {
    Propose(context.Context, CandidateTransitionInput) (CandidateTransitionID, error)
    Commit(context.Context, CommitTransitionInput) (ControlCommit, error)
}
type ContextProjector interface {
    Project(context.Context, ContextProjectionInput) ([]ContextDisclosure, error)
}
```

`ArtifactLineage` returns nodes and typed causal edges with confidence and the
`InterpretationRef` that classified each edge. It must answer: which human
signal prompted, designed, motivated, architected, and verified an artifact;
which agents, turns, tool calls, sessions, and subagents transformed it; which
codebook/Epoch build classified every link; what context was disclosed; and
which fact proposed, authorized, and committed a transition.

Causal edge kinds are closed typed values, including `PromptedBy`, `DesignedBy`,
`MotivatedBy`, `ArchitectedBy`, `VerifiedBy`, `DelegatedTo`, `ExecutedTool`,
`ProducedArtifact`, `ObservedPath`, `SnapshotOf`, and `CommittedAs`. Each edge
has `Observed`, `Correlated`, or `Verified` confidence. `FileChanged` carrying
only `file_path` creates at most `ObservedPath`; it cannot prove diff, content,
commit, or motivating prompt lineage. Exact lineage needs an explicit enrichment
point: a VCS worktree snapshot/diff, a tool I/O record that names the snapshot,
or a commit/ref observation. Those payloads have material privacy and storage
costs and are covered below.

## Normative authority and host response

The control path is deliberately separate:

```text
native occurrence append
  -> versioned interpretation/facts
  -> candidate transition and context projection
  -> authority/correlation verification
  -> Epoch engine compare-and-swap commit
  -> target-neutral response intent
  -> pinned host response encoder
```

A commit requires all applicable conditions in one transaction: active exact
session binding; actor/role and assignment allowed by the selected codebook;
required evidence facts; an unexpired single-use Pasture-issued capability tied
to the native request/session/task/tool scope; selected registered human actor
where human authority is required; and expected Epoch state revision. The engine
uses the existing canonical Provenance/Apply path and current-fact conditions;
this proposal does not create another FSM or ledger.

For now every lifecycle command exits **0**, reports redacted actionable internal
failures on stderr, and returns the pinned native neutral/continue result. This
applies even to a blocking host hook. It is a temporary transport posture, not a
claim that Pasture never denies a tool. Before allow/deny/ask is enabled, define
a lifecycle-specific response disposition and verify it against each pinned
runtime contract; never reuse general CLI connection exit code 2 as a host deny.

turn a host callback into unreviewed authority.

## Privacy, storage, and security

Prompts, elicitation responses, tool input/output, transcripts, paths, errors,
and diffs can contain secrets and personal data. Occurrence metadata and raw
content must be separated. The default design stores typed metadata and a
`EvidencePayloadRef` with retention class; content is either omitted/redacted,
encrypted in a separately permissioned local/blob store, or represented by an
external reference. It is never printed in hook stderr or normal CLI output.

Bound all input, content references, context packets, tool I/O, and query
traversals. Encrypt content at rest where retained; use per-record access policy
and deletion/retention tombstones that preserve non-sensitive lineage metadata.
Do not use raw host payload hashing to reintroduce deduplication. VCS snapshots
and diffs must be opt-in because they provide the needed exact code linkage but
can be large and highly sensitive.

Every control operation validates untrusted host input at ingress, verifies
issued capability scope and expiry in the same transaction as the expected-state
condition, and records only structured actionable diagnostics. Native host
identity is a claim until bound to a registered Pasture actor/session.

## Validation checklist and BDD acceptance criteria

- [ ] Contract/capture coverage enumerates each of the 30 Claude events exactly once and emits a visible unsupported-schema fact rather than silently dropping an event.
- [ ] Two byte-identical deliveries append two rows with different `OccurrenceID`s; no replay/digest column, key, or outcome exists.
- [ ] Malformed and unknown-schema payloads append an unclassified occurrence plus parse issue, exit 0 temporarily, and do not create a normative fact.
- [ ] One occurrence interpreted under two immutable codebook versions retains both batches/facts and identifies each implementation/build.
- [ ] A lowering package cannot compile if it accesses host behavior because the behavior is absent from occurrence types and inaccessible across package boundaries.
- [ ] A path-only `FileChanged` query returns observed-path confidence; it cannot claim diff/commit/prompt lineage until explicit VCS/tool enrichment exists.
- [ ] Tool and stop gates append consultation evidence and return neutral continue before P4; an internal failure is redacted stderr plus exit 0, never accidental deny.
- [ ] ElicitationResult without a Pasture-issued request capability remains evidence only; a valid request, registered human, schema-valid answer, codebook rule, and expected state produces exactly one authorized control commit.
- [ ] Context disclosures record codebook/build, recipient binding, material version, delivery/revocation state, and basis facts.
- [ ] Retention tests prove sensitive payloads do not appear in standard query output, logs, or error diagnostics.

**Given** identical native bytes arrive twice, **when** ingress runs, **then** it appends two separate occurrence records with distinct database IDs, **and should not** suppress either delivery through payload content, timestamp, or a replay key.

**Given** a tool use is reported before a future tool gate is implemented, **when** the host waits for the hook, **then** Pasture appends evidence and returns exit 0/neutral continue while reporting an internal failure only on stderr, **and should not** return an accidental host deny.

**Given** a code artifact has only a `FileChanged` path observation, **when** a user asks which human signal created it, **then** the query reports the missing verified causal link, **and should not** invent a diff, commit, or motivating prompt.

**Given** an ElicitationResult cites an exact issued request and registered human actor, **when** its codebook rule permits a decision and the engine state matches, **then** the engine records the evidence, candidate, authority, and control commit atomically, **and should not** allow a host callback alone to advance the FSM.

**Given** an actor crosses a codebook phase boundary, **when** context is projected, **then** the disclosure record identifies the exact codebook, build, recipient scope, content material, and reason, **and should not** claim host acknowledgement without evidence.

## Follow-up Plan UAT decision tree

These are concrete engineering choices for the next Plan UAT; no option is
silently selected by this proposal.

1. **Evidence content retention.** (A) metadata/redaction only: minimum exposure,
   weaker ability to quote a prompt/tool output; (B) encrypted local content with
   retention controls: richer forensic lineage, key-management and device-risk;
   (C) external immutable evidence store: strongest cross-machine audit, largest
   operational/privacy footprint.
2. **Context delivery.** (A) statically generated start/compaction material:
   simplest and reproducible, less adaptive; (B) dynamic, per-contract response
   injection: phase-accurate and bidirectional, requires exact host response
   contract and blocking reliability; (C) explicit `pasture epoch context` pull:
   transparent and host-neutral, less automatic.
3. **Automation authority.** (A) asserted registered human plus scoped
   Pasture-issued local capabilities: consistent with current URE, practical but
   not cryptographic identity; (B) host-session correlation alone: simple but
   spoofable and not recommended; (C) signed/provider authentication now:
   strongest provenance, materially heavier local/CI setup.
4. **Exact code provenance enrichment.** (A) commits and paths only: low cost,
   cannot prove uncommitted transformations; (B) encrypted VCS snapshots/diffs:
   exact local lineage with sensitive storage cost; (C) external content store:
   durable cross-machine evidence with highest operational cost.
5. **Codebook distribution.** (A) release-embedded generated codebooks only:
   strongest reproducibility, slower evolution; (B) validated signed import:
   faster governed evolution, requires signature/rollout administration; (C)
   editable database rows: flexible but non-reproducible and rejected.

## Exit state

This proposal is intentionally unratified. It requires independent correctness,
test-quality, and elegance review, followed by the focused Plan UAT decision
tree above. No current implementation task may treat PROPOSAL-4 or its M1
prototype as authoritative after this pivot.

# PROPOSAL-3: Canonical lifecycle IR waist

Supersedes PROPOSAL-2. Round 2 returned REVISE on all three axes, with three
axes independently reporting the same four defects. That convergence is the
useful signal: the *architecture* stopped being contested after round 1, and
round 2 found only places where the declared contract could not actually be
implemented. This revision closes those.

| Defect | Reported by |
|---|---|
| D8 reverse lookup does not exist and was deliberately excluded | A (blocker), C (important) |
| D5 payload dedup unimplementable — no payload reaches the IR | A (blocker), C (blocker) |
| `Lower` forbidden to read `Origin`, yet must pass it to `ActorResolver` | A, B, C (all blocker) |
| `Outcome` declared frozen while incomplete | B (blocker), C (blocker), A (important) |

## 0. Provenance

Authority: `llm/research/hooks-ir-compilers-architecture-lessons.md`. Axis A
correctly objected again that two rows still laundered derivation as citation.

| This plan | Research | Relationship |
|---|---|---|
| §2 hourglass waist | §2 | **stated** |
| §3 Go frontend is not "JSON as API" | §13.1 | **stated** |
| middle-end owns operation selection | §6 | **stated** |
| legalization failure is first-class | §8 | **stated** |
| no IR serialization yet | §9 | **stated** |
| differential equivalence proves a waist | §11 | **stated** |
| `Semantics`/`Origin` split | §7 | **derived** |
| type erasure at `BindEvent` | §7 | **derived** |
| *one exported* `Lower` symbol | §6 | **derived** — research requires middle-end ownership, not one symbol |
| constructor-enforced invariants | §8 | **derived** — research requires verification at pass boundaries, not a specific mechanism |
| replay key from payload digest | §8 | **derived** |

## 1. The waist

The equivalence that the M2 test must prove is what fixes the waist's width.
Claude `PreToolUse` against OpenCode `tool.execute.before`:

```
                    Claude PreToolUse      OpenCode tool.execute.before
  semantic          gate-consultation      gate-consultation        SAME
  blocking          blocking               blocking                 SAME
  stop-loop         not-applicable         not-applicable           SAME
  identity kinds    session, tool-call     session, tool-call       SAME
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  surface           claude-command-json    opencode-named-output    DIFFERS
  mutation          input                  output-object            DIFFERS
  order             concurrent-native      sequential-load          DIFFERS
  reconciliation    host-native            sequential-mutation      DIFFERS
  failure           exit-2-blocks          throw-fail-fast          DIFFERS
```

**Five** of the eight axes differ (A and C both corrected PROPOSAL-2's "six";
`stopLoop` matches here). The five that differ describe how to speak back to one
specific host — target description, which research §7 says the L2 dialect drops.

```go
// THE WAIST. Target-agnostic: nothing here names a harness or a wire format.
type Semantics struct {
    Semantic   runtime.EventSemantic
    Blocking   runtime.BlockingMode
    Identities []SemanticIdentity   // sorted; see §4.3
}

// Occurrence identity, stripped of native field naming (axis C).
type SemanticIdentity struct {
    Kind  runtime.NativeIdentityKind
    Value string
}
```

## 2. Origin, and the death of D8

PROPOSAL-2 said the response backend could recover the five target axes by
looking them up from `(Contract, NativeEventName)`. Axis A found this is
impossible and axis C independently found the same: `LifecycleContract.Mapping`
is generic over `E`, `Origin` erases `E`, and `internal/runtime/lifecycle.go`
**deliberately has no native-name lookup** — its doc comment says so explicitly.

D8 is withdrawn. Neither offered fix is taken wholesale: adding a reverse lookup
would re-open the string-keyed lookup that `runtime` was designed to forbid.

DECISION D9 — `Event` retains the immutable `LifecycleEventMapping` it was
bound to, unexported, exposed only through a backend-facing accessor.

```go
type Origin struct {
    Contract        ir.RuntimeContractID
    NativeEventName NativeEventName
    PayloadDigest   Digest      // §3
    // unexported: mapping runtime.LifecycleEventMapping
}

func (o Origin) Harness() ir.HarnessID   // derived; no stored field (axis C minor)

// Backend-only. Lower must not call this; see §5.
func (o Origin) TargetBehaviour() runtime.LifecycleEventMapping
```

This preserves D8's actual intent. The anti-drift worry was a *copy that can
diverge from the table*; a value read from the immutable table at `BindEvent`
and never mutated cannot diverge from it. And the impossible reverse lookup
disappears rather than being built.

## 3. Replay identity — one rule

PROPOSAL-2's two-branch `DedupScope` was unimplementable: `DedupByPayload`
needs the payload, and no payload reaches the IR. The Claude frontend discards
`file_path`, so the field distinguishing two `FileChanged` occurrences was gone.
Axis C also noted the table omitted Codex's `IdentityTurn`.

Rather than complete the table, delete it. The frontend digests the raw native
payload it received and carries the digest as origin provenance:

```
replay key = (Contract, NativeEventName, PayloadDigest)
```

DECISION D5 (final) — one rule, total by construction. Identity values live
inside the payload, so identity-based dedup is subsumed; the `IdentityTurn` gap
and every future one closes automatically. A byte-identical redelivery
collapses, which is the retry case dedup exists for. Two different file changes
carry different paths, therefore different digests, therefore different records.

`Digest` is a bounded, fixed-width value (SHA-256) computed over the exact bytes
read, before any parsing, so it is well-defined even for payloads that fail to
parse. Wall-clock time is not in the key.

**Named residual:** two genuinely distinct occurrences with byte-identical
payloads collapse into one record. This is narrow and documented, and replaces
PROPOSAL-2's silent universal collapse. The acceptance criterion in §10 is
worded to match this, rather than claiming a guarantee the design cannot make
(axis A's contradiction finding).

## 4. Declared surface

### 4.1 Frontend (restored — axis B found it dropped)

```go
type Frontend interface {
    Harness() ir.HarnessID
    Parse(payload []byte, requested NativeEventName) (Event, error)
}
```

Pure: no effects, no store, no clock. Golden-IR tests need no host and no
database. `MaxNativePayloadBytes` bounds the read at the process boundary.

### 4.2 Construction

```go
func BindEvent[E comparable](c runtime.LifecycleContract[E], event E) (EventBinding, error)

type EventBinding struct{ /* unexported */ }
func (b EventBinding) DeclaredIdentities() []runtime.NativeIdentityField
func (b EventBinding) NewEvent(digest Digest, identities []Identity) (Event, error)

type Event struct{ /* unexported */ }
func (e Event) Semantics() Semantics
func (e Event) Origin() Origin
```

D1 (confirmed by all three axes, twice) — the constructor derives `Semantics`
and the mapping from the binding. It accepts only what the binding cannot know:
the payload digest and the extracted identity values.

### 4.3 Equivalence — honest about what it proves

Axis B found the relation too coarse: Claude `UserPromptSubmit` and `Stop` both
reduce to (gate-consultation, blocking, [session]) and would compare equivalent
despite being unrelated events. That is correct, and it means `EquivalentTo`
alone cannot be the M2 test.

```go
// Coarse SHAPE relation over the waist. Necessary, NOT sufficient.
func (s Semantics) EquivalentTo(other Semantics) bool

// Deterministic rendering. Identities sorted by (Kind, Value); duplicates of
// the same Kind retained in sorted order; fields joined with a reserved
// separator that cannot occur in an identity value.
func (s Semantics) CanonicalKey() string
```

The M2 differential test is therefore specified as three assertions, not one:

1. each frontend produced the **expected native event** (`Origin.NativeEventName`
   is `PreToolUse` on one side, `tool.execute.before` on the other);
2. each side carries the **exact expected identity values**;
3. the two `Semantics` are `EquivalentTo`.

Without (1) and (2) the test would pass even if a frontend produced the wrong
event, which is precisely the bug class it exists to catch.

### 4.4 Lowering

```go
func Lower(ctx context.Context, deps Deps, event Event) (Outcome, error)

type Deps struct {
    Recorder ObservationRecorder   // required
    Actors   ActorResolver         // required
    Clock    func() time.Time      // required; no time.Now fallback
    Logger   *slog.Logger          // required; no slog.Default fallback
}
```

All fields required and validated; nil is an actionable error, never a silent
default. Axis B is right that fallbacks to `time.Now` or `slog.Default`
reintroduce the hidden global state the injection exists to remove.

`Clock`'s only consumer is the observed-at timestamp on the recorded activity.
It is deliberately *not* in the replay key (§3), so a fake clock cannot change
dedup behaviour.

```go
// Consumer-owned, narrow. Not protocol.TaskTracker wholesale.
type ObservationRecorder interface {
    RecordObservation(ctx context.Context, o ObservationRecord) (RecordOutcome, error)
}

type ObservationRecord struct {
    Actor      provenance.AgentID
    Actee      Origin           // what was observed
    Semantics  Semantics
    ObservedAt time.Time
    ReplayKey  string           // §3
}

type RecordOutcome uint8
const (
    RecordCreated RecordOutcome = iota + 1  // new activity + event written
    RecordReplayed                          // replay key already present; no write
)

// Fails closed. Must verify the resolved ID is non-zero and registered.
type ActorResolver interface {
    ResolveHookActor(ctx context.Context, o Origin) (provenance.AgentID, error)
}
```

Axis B's finding that `ActivityRecord`/`EventRecord` were undefined is
addressed by collapsing them: the activity and the task event are written
together or not at all, so exposing two calls invited a partial write. One call,
one transaction, one typed outcome that distinguishes a write from a replay.

### 4.5 Outcome — provisional by declaration

```go
type Outcome struct {
    Kind   OutcomeKind
    Record RecordOutcome   // meaningful when Kind == OutcomeRecorded
}

type OutcomeKind uint8
const (
    OutcomeRecorded OutcomeKind = iota + 1
)
```

DECISION D10 — M1–M3 declare **only** `OutcomeRecorded`. Axis B and C both
found PROPOSAL-2 repeating, one level smaller, the same error that got
`Responder` withdrawn: freezing `OutcomeAllow`/`OutcomeDeny`/`OutcomeMutate`
with no payloads and no consumers. `OutcomeMutate` in particular cannot be
specified while the IR carries no mutation input.

`Outcome` is a struct rather than a bare enum specifically so M5 can add
variants and payloads without breaking callers, and it is declared
**provisional**: the observation path is frozen, the gate path is not yet
designed. Saying so is more honest than implying a stability the design has not
earned.

## 5. What keeps the middle-end target-agnostic

All three axes found the contradiction: PROPOSAL-2's criterion said `Lower`
reads only `Semantics`, but actor resolution and the replay key both need
`Origin`. The criterion was wrong, not the design.

The property actually wanted is that **`Lower`'s behaviour does not vary by
harness**. Restated precisely and checkably:

- `Lower` MAY read `Semantics` and `Origin`'s coordinates.
- `Lower` MUST NOT call `Origin.TargetBehaviour()`. Those five axes govern how
  to speak back to a host; a middle-end that branches on them is not
  target-agnostic.
- `Deps` deliberately contains no lifecycle-table accessor, so harness-varying
  lookups can only happen behind `ActorResolver`. `Lower` itself contains no
  harness branch.

## 6. Level traversal is not uniform

```
  observation      L2 ──────────────────────> L4 effects   (terminal pass)
  gate             L2 ──> L3 protocol op ───> L4 ──> response
  human response   L2 ──> L3 protocol op ───> L4 ──> response
```

L3 is the protocol dialect (`StartReview`, `RecordPlanUAT`, `Land`). An
observation is not a protocol transition: a host reporting that a session
started is *evidence*, not authority to advance a phase (research §13.3).
Axis A and C both accepted this as a genuine resolution when named as a
**terminal observation-effect pass**, which is how §6 now labels it.
Consequence: M1–M3 never touch `AdapterOperation`.

## 7. Blocking events are refused until M5

Axis A: since no response encoding exists before M5, a blocking event processed
at M1–M3 would leave the host awaiting a result it never receives.

DECISION D11 — M1–M3 refuse any event whose `Semantics.Blocking` is not
`NonBlocking`, with an actionable error naming M5. Refusing loudly is the
legalization behaviour research §8 requires; hanging or silently allowing is
the failure mode this work exists to remove.

## 8. Response encoding — M5, with constraints

`Responder` stays withdrawn. Two constraints recorded so M5 is not designed blind:

**C1** — one canonical process-boundary response form; each harness trampoline
applies a fixed mechanical mapping to its native dialect. Per-surface knowledge
is emitted statically by the generator from the pinned table, not selected at
runtime.

**C2** — verified by axis B against `AGENTS.md` and
`internal/errors/errors.go:226-255`: exit code 2 means `CategoryConnection`,
but exit 2 is exactly how Claude and Codex hooks signal *deny*. M5 needs a
distinct typed lifecycle response disposition rather than reusing the general
CLI exit-code contract.

## 9. Milestones

| # | Milestone | Status |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | Contract freeze + Claude observation spine | committed |
| M2 | OpenCode frontend + differential equivalence + lazy actor derivation | committed |
| M3 | Codex frontend | committed |
| M4+ | Context binding, gates, human response, escape hatch, retire drift | directional |

M3 is the Codex **frontend only** — axis C found PROPOSAL-2 claiming strict
failure semantics at M3 while deferring all response encoding to M5.

Actor coverage (D6, unchanged): the static registry has 9 `HookHandler` agents
against 30/10/42 pinned events. Do not expand it to 82 — that is a second copy
of the pinned tables and will drift. Derive lazily from `(harness, native name)`
at M2. M1 uses the registered `SessionStart` agent and fails closed otherwise.
`ActorResolver` must verify the resolved ID is non-zero and registered, and must
remain compatible with the existing `pasture/automaton/hook/<name>` naming.

## 10. Acceptance criteria

- GIVEN any environment, WHEN an event is processed, THEN the operation is
  selected only by `Lower` from verified IR, AND SHOULD NOT be influenced by any
  env var, argv value, or generated script.
- GIVEN `Lower`, WHEN it executes, THEN it never calls `Origin.TargetBehaviour()`
  and contains no harness branch.
- GIVEN the same logical occurrence from Claude and OpenCode, WHEN both are
  lowered, THEN each carries its own expected native event name and exact
  identity values, AND their `Semantics` are `EquivalentTo`.
- GIVEN an `Event`, WHEN constructed, THEN semantics and target behaviour are
  derived from the pinned contract, AND SHOULD NOT be caller-supplied.
- GIVEN an actor, assignment, JournalID or revision, WHEN placing it in an
  `Event`, THEN no field exists to hold it.
- GIVEN two occurrences with **different** native payloads, WHEN both are
  lowered, THEN two records exist, AND SHOULD NOT collapse.
- GIVEN the identical payload delivered twice, WHEN both are lowered, THEN one
  record exists and the second returns `RecordReplayed`.
- GIVEN a blocking event before M5, WHEN lowered, THEN it is refused with an
  actionable error naming M5, AND SHOULD NOT be silently allowed.
- GIVEN an event with no registered actor, WHEN lowered, THEN it fails closed,
  AND SHOULD NOT invent an actor.
- GIVEN a nil `Deps` field, WHEN `Lower` is called, THEN it fails actionably,
  AND SHOULD NOT fall back to `time.Now` or `slog.Default`.
title: PROPOSAL-3: Canonical lifecycle IR waist

Axis-C finding (Elegance/Type Consistency).

All other SchemaSpec fields return rich typed dataclasses (RoleSpec, CommandSpec, HandoffSpec, LabelSpec, ReviewAxisSpec). But SchemaSpec.constraints uses dict[str, tuple[str, str, str, str]] — a raw 4-tuple of strings.

This breaks consistency of the API surface. Callers of parse_schema() must know the tuple field order (given, when, then, should_not) as a convention rather than getting named field access. Every other entity in SchemaSpec has a typed dataclass — constraints should too.

The existing ConstraintSpec dataclass is already defined in types.py and has exactly these 4 fields. The parser currently creates tuples instead of ConstraintSpec instances (schema_parser.py line 371: result[cid] = (given, when, then, should_not)).

Fix: Change _parse_constraints() return type to dict[str, ConstraintSpec] and return ConstraintSpec(id=cid, given=given, when=when, then=then, should_not=should_not). Update SchemaSpec.constraints field type annotation accordingly.

## Scope

Add 4 new subcommands under `pasture task`: `events`, `timeline`, `contexts`, `agents` (with sub-verbs `list` and `show`). Add 1 new top-level command: `pasture migrate [--dry-run]` (NOT under `pasture task` — db-level). Each routes through `protocol.TaskTracker`. The `pasture migrate` command and `OpenTaskTracker`'s auto-on-open path share **one** `audit.Migrate` implementation (no duplicate code). Use the existing handler-pattern (`cmd/<verb>.go` Cobra `RunE` thin wrapper → `internal/handlers/<verb>.go` standalone function) per `pasture/CLAUDE.md`. Subprocess CLI tests cover happy + error paths.

- `pasture migrate --dry-run` does NOT modify the file (SHA-256 unchanged before/after).

description:
Axis-C finding (Elegance/DRY — the most significant elegance concern across all 4 slices).

Both gen_schema.py (lines 49-99) and context_injection.py (lines 140-311) define:
  - _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS: dict[RoleId|str, ...]
  - _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS: dict[PhaseId|str, ...]

These two dicts represent the same domain knowledge: which constraints apply to which roles and phases. They exist in two different modules for two different purposes:
  - gen_schema.py uses them to emit role-ref/phase-ref attributes in schema.xml (str-keyed)
  - context_injection.py uses them to build ConstraintContext objects at runtime (PhaseId/RoleId-keyed)

The proposal docstring in context_injection.py (line 28-29) even acknowledges: 'gen_schema.py (SLICE-2) reads _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS and _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS to emit role-ref and phase-ref attributes into schema.xml (UAT-3).'

But gen_schema.py defines its own separate copies\! If someone adds a new constraint in types.py and updates context_injection.py's mappings, they must also update gen_schema.py's mappings, or schema.xml will be out of sync with the runtime context.

Fix: Consolidate. context_injection.py should be the single definition of these mappings. gen_schema.py should import _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS and _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS from context_injection.py, or both should be moved to a shared types.py location. The direction Python→schema.xml should read from the same Python definitions that the runtime injection uses.
title: SLICE-2-REVIEW-C-1-F6: _ROLE_CONSTRAINTS and _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS duplicated between gen_schema.py and context_injection.py

## Finding
The generated files installed for OpenCode still instruct agents to use foreign Claude Code interfaces. The pinned OpenCode contract names `question`, `skill`, and `task` as its native tools and explicitly classifies `Agent`, `SendMessage`, `TaskStop`, and `AskUserQuestion` as foreign (`internal/codegen/opencode_target_test.go:17-27`). Nevertheless, the committed selectable definitions repeat `AskUserQuestion` (`.opencode/agent/architect--openai--gpt-5-6-sol.md:87-91`), `Task tool` and `subagent_type=Explore` (`.opencode/agent/supervisor--openai--gpt-5-6-sol.md:134-138,205-220,229-232`), and Claude-specific `model: haiku` / `model: sonnet` routing (`.opencode/agent/supervisor--openai--gpt-5-6-sol.md:166-176,218-220`). The same shared bodies are emitted into all provider variants, including the 35 files added by this commit.

The integration test only rejects literal `~/.claude` and `Claude Code` (`internal/codegen/opencode_agent_test.go:305-337,393-414`), so it passes while foreign native calls documented by the project itself remain in end-user-loaded output. Aura dynamically installs these exact files under `~/.config/opencode/agent/` (`nix/hm-module.nix:38-43,88-89,273-280`). Users following the definitions can therefore request nonexistent tools/parameters or Claude-only model aliases, breaking orchestration behavior despite valid frontmatter.

## Required Fix
Render operational guidance through an OpenCode-aware projection: use the pinned OpenCode `question`/`task` semantics and supported OpenCode agent/model selection fields, or express unsupported operations semantically without invented calls. Extend the complete agent-output oracle to reject every foreign native call in `foreignNativeCallNames` plus Claude-only `subagent_type`/model-alias guidance, regenerate all affected `.opencode/agent` files, and prove the installed 45-file tree is clean.
title: BLOCKER: OpenCode variants ship foreign Claude tool and model guidance

## Evidence
