# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-3 — Native Codex distribution from Pasture

Supersedes Proposal 2. All Proposal 1 architecture findings remain resolved. This revision closes every Round 2 finding by separating observers from recovery, naming a real deterministic agent-loader observable, freezing release checksums and clean-machine prerequisites, projecting one executable version, refusing unknown managed content, assigning buildable file ownership, and fixing the exact Codex marketplace object. URD Amendments 1–3 are normative, with the newest amendment governing conflicts.

## Product boundary

Pasture remains the sole source of truth for protocol implementation, generated skills, generated agent bodies, and their Codex projection. It emits a portable Codex plugin whose 32 skills are complete without native agents. The plugin also carries one verified bundle of five optional native leaf-agent TOMLs. Because Codex plugins do not currently install custom agents, a user explicitly selects exactly one personal agent authority: the Pasture companion CLI or Aura Home Manager.

The feature does not add a Codex backend to `aura-swarm`, mutate Git configuration, install hooks, infer all projects, or claim plugin-native agent registration. Aura remains distribution/operational glue and adds no Python protocol engine.

## 1. Roots, catalog, and structural runtime compiler

Adopt prerequisite `aura-plugins-oj7we`: every codegen operation receives `GenerationRoots{SourceRoot, OutputRoot}`, canonical inputs are read only below SourceRoot, and generated writes are contained below OutputRoot.

Replace `roleSkillDirs`, `commandSkillDirs`, target verbatim inventories, and any new parallel skill-key map with one ordered `SkillDescriptor{Key, Directory, SourceKind, RoleID, CommandID, SupportID}` catalog. It describes the 31 canonical skills; the Codex-only `install-codex-agents` support descriptor is the 32nd output. Paths, runtime invocations, UI inventory, archive inventory, and target metadata project from this catalog. `ProtocolCommandName` and effective `SkillInvocation` are distinct typed values.

Runtime-sensitive prose is structural, never `...any`, global replacement, or a rendered-string reparse:

```go
type RuntimeText struct { parts []RuntimePart }
type RuntimePart interface { runtimePart() }
type Literal struct { Text string }
type Ref struct { Value RuntimeRef }
```

Private closed `RuntimeRef` variants cover activation/self-activation; agent purpose, delivery, lifetime, fan-out, work tier, and context inheritance; initial spawn, follow-up, notification, and barriers; user-input fallback; commit policy; instruction source; prerequisites; and attribution. `RuntimeContext` supplies harness, surface, owner descriptor/role, canonical location, and delivery capability. A coverage sentinel proves every production text owner is visited: constraints, workflows, transitions, procedures, checklists, review axes, fragments, command/role fields, recipes, figures, schema fields, and normative assets. Unknown combinations and forbidden raw operations fail with the six actionable-error fields.

Claude stays byte-identical except separately golden-reviewed intentional install/runtime corrections. OpenCode retains exact path/byte inventory. Codex emits native collaboration syntax and registry-derived `$pasture:<directory>` addresses. Every actionable address in the final archive resolves exactly once.

## 2. Target-owned support assets and complete render graph

Codex `protocol` and `install-cli` are not recursive copies of Claude skills. The dialect-aware emitter owns the normative protocol set: `SKILL.md`, `PROCESS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONSTRAINTS.md`, `SKILLS.md`, `README.md`, a Codex runtime document, and target-local `schema.xml`. Codex install-cli is generated from typed install semantics and exact release/checksum inputs. Claude-only history and examples remain outside Codex active links; any comparative fixture needs a file/line/reason golden.

Scan every Markdown, XML, YAML, JSON, and TOML file in the final plugin. Link-walk an installed cache. Direct assertions cover known protocol, schema, and installer hotspots; there is no blanket support-skill exemption. Exact empty-root and in-place output manifests detect missing and stale owned paths.

## 3. Default-depth orchestration

The supported entry path is the root Codex thread invoking `$pasture:epoch` or another Pasture role skill. With Codex's recommended default `agents.max_depth=1`, the root owns phase transitions, consensus, fan-out, worker/reviewer dispatch, waits, follow-ups, and consolidation. Architect/supervisor coordination executes as root skills when coordination is required. All spawned explorers, workers, and reviewers are depth-1 leaves.

Native agent projections are bounded leaves, not a nested hierarchy:

- `pasture_epoch`: analysis/status/root guidance; directs full orchestration to the root skill.
- `pasture_architect`: bounded requirements/proposal/handoff artifact.
- `pasture_supervisor`: bounded implementation-plan/progress artifact.
- `pasture_worker`: implementation or review-fix work.
- `pasture_reviewer`: plan or code review with required Beads writes.

Plugin-only delivery uses a current built-in/default leaf with a self-contained prompt whose first directive activates the exact namespaced skill. Healthy installed delivery may select `pasture_*` and elide redundant activation. Unavailable custom types fall back to plugin-only. Self-contained Beads handoffs inherit no conversation; follow-ups target the persistent leaf. Fan-out batches or serializes when thread capacity is small. Model, reasoning, sandbox, MCP, and skill overrides are omitted so live parent policy wins.

## 4. Plugin, skill metadata, and canonical agent bundle

Pasture emits `plugins/pasture/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, all 31 canonical skills, and `skills/install-codex-agents`. Skill frontmatter uses unqualified name/description; installed invocations are namespaced. Every skill has exhaustive `agents/openai.yaml` with compatible display name, 25–64 character short description, and a default prompt naming its skill. `install-codex-agents` and the explicitly Claude-backed `swarm` set `allow_implicit_invocation=false`.

The rich compatible plugin manifest includes documented identity/interface/skills only—no agents field, install hook, unbacked app, or MCP declaration. Plugin add installs skills and zero native agents.

The setup skill owns exactly one bundle:

```text
skills/install-codex-agents/assets/agent-bundle/
  manifest.json
  agents/pasture_epoch.toml
  agents/pasture_architect.toml
  agents/pasture_supervisor.toml
  agents/pasture_worker.toml
  agents/pasture_reviewer.toml
```

The manifest freezes bundle schema and installer protocol; plugin/bundle semver; exact compatible CLI release tag and semver; minimum/tested Codex versions; checksum artifact name; supported OS/architecture matrix; and each canonical role ID, public name, safe relative path, SHA-256, and execution-policy projection. Both installer and Home Manager consume these exact bytes. The Go wire implementation is private `internal/codexbundle`; the JSON schema is the shared contract.

## 5. Exact CLI and setup contract

```text
pasture codex agents capabilities --format=json
pasture codex agents plan --bundle M [--project-root P|--no-project-check] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents install --bundle M --plan-digest D [--allow-downgrade] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents status [--bundle M] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents recover --format=text|json
pasture codex agents uninstall --format=text|json
```

Stable JSON schemas and exit categories are black-box tested through the built Cobra binary. `capabilities` is a static zero-write report of CLI release tag/semver, protocols, supported platforms, and features. Bundle-less status reports only ledger/disk/journal integrity; `--bundle` adds desired version/hash comparison. Optional plugin observation is labeled unknown when unavailable and never constructs cache paths.

`plan` and `status` acquire the installer lock without writing, wait for active mutations, and inspect one coherent ledger/generation/journal snapshot. An interrupted journal is reported, never repaired. Plan is explicitly non-authoritative and writes zero bytes. Its digest binds the canonical bundle bytes, resolved Codex home identity, ledger/current generation, journal state, collisions, explicit project decision, and options.

`recover`, `install`, and `uninstall` are authorized mutators and take the exclusive lock. Install reruns all validation. If it first recovers an interrupted transaction, the old digest is stale and activation stops until the user sees and approves a fresh plan. Downgrade requires an audited flag.

The setup skill resolves its own bundle without cache-path inference, checks exact CLI capability, Codex compatibility, `bd`, Git, conditional repository commit policy, and optional `aura-swarm`. If CLI bootstrap is needed it invokes `$pasture:install-cli` with the bundle's exact tag. It displays plan, obtains scoped permission, installs with the bound digest, verifies status, and requires a fresh thread. It never changes Git config or hooks. Landing uses `git agent-commit` only when repository policy requires it and stops actionably when required but unavailable.

## 6. Recoverable managed-generation transaction

Threat model: untrusted bundle input, accidental corruption, crashes, concurrent Pasture commands, and path replacement—not a continuously racing privileged or malicious same-UID process.

```text
CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed/       complete companion generation
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.json    committed ledger
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock    persistent advisory-lock path
CODEX_HOME/pasture/transactions/<id>/    journal, staged new, old backup
```

Before a mutation, lstat every path component and recursively compare the complete managed generation against the ledger. Expected regular files, hashes, and relevant modes must match; expected directories must be present; unknown, missing, modified, or type-changed entries and all symlinks are TAMPERED. They stop with zero mutation and preservation/repair guidance.

The mutator stages and fsyncs a complete same-filesystem generation, journals `PREPARED`, moves the validated prior directory to the control-area backup and journals `OLD_MOVED`, renames the staged directory into the loader tree and journals `NEW_ACTIVE`, atomically writes/fsyncs the ledger and journals `COMMITTED`, then removes only transaction-owned content whose recorded identity still matches. Uninstall uses the same state machine. Recovery restores or completes the only unambiguous journal state; if loader-visible or backup content changed after journaling, it preserves every candidate and stops rather than guessing.

The honest guarantee is crash-recoverable quiescent installation: a concurrent Codex start can see the complete old set, a brief absence, or the complete new set, never a mixed Pasture generation. A fresh thread begins only after healthy status. Identical install is a true no-op preserving mtimes. No option in this feature adopts, overwrites, or deletes unknown/modified content.

Real subprocess tests SIGKILL after every durable boundary, then invoke explicit recovery. They cover first install, no-op, upgrade, explicit downgrade, uninstall, every journal state, read/write contention, two mutators, persistent unheld lock file, stale consent, symlink/path swap, short write/ENOSPC, permissions, cleanup failure, tampered backups, and supported Linux/macOS directory semantics.

## 7. Ownership scope and Home Manager

Exclusive authority applies only to one personal `CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed`: companion XOR Home Manager. Project `.codex/agents` directories are independent higher-precedence layers. `--project-root` checks exactly the resolved named project for same-name overrides; `--no-project-check` records the explicit skip. No global discovery or project ownership is claimed.

Aura adds only `CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.codex.agents.enable = false`; it does not sync Codex skills. Nix evaluation parses the canonical bundle manifest and derives the five mappings after schema/version/path/name/hash validation—there is no second role list.

When enabled, Home Manager owns one symlink at default `~/.codex/agents/pasture-managed` to an immutable generated store directory containing the exact TOMLs and an ownership manifest. A pre-link activation guard rejects a companion ledger, a regular managed directory, an arbitrary symlink, or malformed/modified ownership manifest before link mutation. It accepts absent state or a previous Home Manager-owned immutable target with exact membership, enabling repeat activation and upgrade. Companion symmetrically rejects the managed symlink. Disable removes only the Home Manager-owned link. A non-default `CODEX_HOME` is a separate companion target.

A pinned Home Manager fixture tests default, malformed bundle, enable, repeat enable, upgrade, companion/stale-ledger conflict with zero mutation, disable/removal, modified or arbitrary links, and preservation. Pinned Codex proves directory-symlinked TOMLs load and disappear.

## 8. One version, strict checksums, and release readiness

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` stores the canonical bare semver. `pasture-release` is its sole mutating writer; codegen reads it and deterministically emits equal Codex plugin and bundle versions. Change `cmd/pasture/root.go` from `const version` to linker-injectable `var version = "dev"`. Release builds inject canonical `vX.Y.Z`; one parser exposes both tag and bare semver. CLI `--version`, capabilities, bundle constraint, generated versions, release tag, and release verification must agree.

Supported release tuples are exactly linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, and darwin/arm64. A release publishes `pasture`, `pastured`, and `pasture-release` for each tuple plus `SHA256SUMS`: exactly 12 lexicographically sorted, newline-terminated lines of `<64 lowercase hex><two spaces><basename>`, with no path separators. Bootstrap rejects missing, duplicate, extra, malformed, unsupported, version/tag-mismatched, untrusted redirect, and mismatched artifacts. It verifies the exact current-platform `pasture` in a private same-filesystem stage before rename or execution, then fsyncs and activates.

Fake-release tests exercise every negative case. After publish, a gate fetches the immutable actual tag/checksum roster and runs `pasture codex agents capabilities` for all four tuples on declared native/emulated runners. Aura cannot mark the entry AVAILABLE until this passes. `make generate` emits `claude-code,opencode,codex` and extends PR #35's drift gate. Release invokes generation; it does not rewrite generated sibling versions independently.

## 9. Exact Aura marketplace contract

Aura creates/updates its repo Codex marketplace at `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and appends Pasture after existing entries. The entry is frozen as:

```json
{
  "name": "pasture",
  "source": {
    "source": "git-subdir",
    "url": "https://github.com/dayvidpham/pasture.git",
    "sha": "<40 lowercase hex commit>",
    "path": "./plugins/pasture"
  },
  "policy": {
    "installation": "NOT_AVAILABLE",
    "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"
  },
  "category": "Productivity"
}
```

It contains no `ref`, `repo`, products, plugin version, mutable branch, or default-install policy. The feature PR uses the immutable Pasture feature commit and NOT_AVAILABLE. A later release-backed change may set AVAILABLE only after the matching release/checksum/capability gate succeeds and the SHA is repinned to that immutable release commit.

## 10. Deterministic validation and clean-machine coverage

Mandatory hermetic tests cover roots/containment, the sole catalog, structural parts and full visitor, dialects/invocations, complete plugin/assets/link graph, manifest/TOML/schema/hash validation, transaction and CLI black boxes, exact target inventories/stale output, version parity, and Home Manager evaluation/activation. Every actionable error asserts what, why, where, operation/when, caller impact, and repair.

A pinned Codex 0.144.1 compatibility test uses fresh processes and isolated `HOME`/`CODEX_HOME`. App-server `skills/list` and plugin list/read prove 32 namespaced skills and zero plugin-installed agents. A local fake Responses-compatible provider captures the outbound model request's collaboration tool schema and asserts the exact `pasture_*` type enum before/after companion and Home Manager install/removal; debug prompt/config is not used for enumeration. A separately labeled network/model UAT demonstrates actual selection and the default-depth plugin-only and installed paths.

Clean-machine fixtures vary isolated PATH/repository state for absent/incompatible/compatible Codex and Pasture, absent/present `bd` and Git, required present/missing `git agent-commit`, optional swarm, no repository, and fully provisioned setup. They assert fallback or exact failure plus no changes to hooks, Git configuration, default home, unrelated task DB, or cache.

Repo-owned Go/Nix checks are mandatory. Skill/plugin creator validators are recorded compatibility evidence with exact script hashes and interpreter dependencies, never ambient-home CI dependencies.

## 11. Buildable ownership and implementation sequence

One root implementor executes sequentially; exploration and adversarial reviewers do not edit.

1. Foundation owns `GenerationRoots`, the one catalog, structural runtime semantics/compiler, canonical assets/projections, and their tests. It does not register Codex or own target renderers.
2. Bundle-contract leaf creates private `internal/codexbundle` and freezes its JSON schema/fixtures.
3. Codex distribution owns all `codex_*` renderers/templates/tests, the complete 32-entry UI overlay, plugin/bundle emission, generated plugin tree, and the single final `harness.go` registration edit after its package builds independently.
4. Agent CLI owns `internal/codexagents`, `cmd/pasture/codex_agents*`, lifecycle/fake-release/black-box tests, and consumes only the frozen bundle contract.
5. Release integration alone owns `cmd/pasture/root.go`, release packages/tests, Makefile, checksum workflow/docs, all-target generation wiring, and version parity.
6. Aura owns `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, Home Manager module/fixture, README/inputs/lock, and the Pasture gitlink; it consumes the frozen bundle.

Any newly shared file is reassigned in Beads before editing. Sequence is roots/catalog/runtime → bundle schema → Codex emitter/integration → CLI/lifecycle → release/generate → immutable Pasture commit → Aura consumer. PR #35 stays the base until merged. Pasture merges/releases before a later Aura AVAILABLE change.

## BDD acceptance

1. Default `max_depth=1` reaches plan review, worker implementation, and code review with only root-to-leaf delegation.
2. The plugin-only path is complete; healthy custom types may be selected without duplicate activation and missing types fall back.
3. Empty and in-place all-target generation match exact paths/bytes and report stale owned outputs.
4. The final plugin contains 32 valid namespaced skills, all links/assets resolve, and no unapproved Claude operation remains.
5. Plugin add creates zero custom agents; explicit companion or Home Manager delivery exposes exactly five namespaced types without shadowing built-ins.
6. `capabilities`, `plan`, and `status` write zero bytes in healthy and interrupted states; status is coherent under concurrent mutation.
7. Consent is bound to exact state. Recovery, collision, project decision, or any state change invalidates the digest before activation.
8. SIGKILL at every durable boundary recovers to one complete generation or preserves ambiguous candidates with a precise TAMPERED/INTERRUPTED report.
9. Unknown, modified, missing, symlinked, malformed, downgraded, or unowned content is never silently moved, overwritten, adopted, or deleted.
10. Identical install preserves bytes and mtimes; uninstall removes only an exact owned generation.
11. Home Manager conflict fails before mutation; enable/repeat/upgrade/load/disable/removal succeeds from the canonical bundle.
12. A fake provider observes exact custom-agent schema types; real model UAT separately demonstrates actual selection.
13. Strict checksum/bootstrap negatives fail before verified binary activation; the actual-release gate is required before marketplace availability.
14. One canonical version projects equal plugin/bundle/CLI/tag/checksum values, and release generation stays clean.
15. The exact Aura marketplace object is immutable and NOT_AVAILABLE in the stacked feature PR.
16. Any review finding causes a revised proposal or implementation and another three-axis round; progression requires a fix-free 0/0/0 wave.
17. After clean gates and user implementation UAT, evidence-backed Pasture and Aura PRs open in Pasture-before-Aura order.

## Out of scope

- Plugin-native custom agents or automatic install hooks.
- Raised-depth or nested Codex orchestration.
- Global project discovery, project ownership/export, or a project Home Manager mode.
- Codex backend for `aura-swarm`.
- Aura Codex skill sync.
- Git hook installation or Git configuration mutation.
- Silent adoption/deletion of tampered managed content.
- Vercel skills CLI, oh-my-codex, npm packaging, and ChatGPT-web local-agent claims.

description:
What: collectReassignedObjs (capabilitylint.go, cycle-3) marks Objects assigned via *ast.AssignStmt with Tok != DEFINE. A range clause with '=' — e.g. `for _, id = range ids { ir.MustDefineCapability(id, ...) }` (or `for id = range map[ir.CapabilityID]V{...}`) — rebinds the parameter on every iteration but is an *ast.RangeStmt (Tok token.ASSIGN), not an AssignStmt, so the parameter stays in the allowed set despite not being forwarded verbatim. Pointer-indirect writes (`p := &id; *p = ...`) are likewise unseen (LHS is *ast.StarExpr). The rule-2 doc claims 'any assignment to the parameter's *ast.Object, direct or via a capturing closure, removes it from this allowance' — Go-spec-wise a range clause with '=' IS an assignment, so the doc currently overclaims relative to the implementation.

Why MINOR, not higher (explicit calibration): the natural reassignment spellings (`id = ...`, multi-assign, compound ops, incl. through capturing closures) ARE caught; these residual shapes require deliberate contortion, and the already-ACCEPTED disclosed residual (urfrx(a): one-hop wrapper call sites are never inspected) strictly dominates them in both ease and power — a launderer needs no in-body rebinding at all. The enforcement's purpose is claim-honesty on the natural path, which holds; this finding is about closing the cheap remaining gap and making the claim exact.

Where/when: capabilitylint.go collectReassignedObjs + rule-2 package doc; S2.3 round-3 (final) correctness review of commit 1cb4870.

Required correction: (a) add a `case *ast.RangeStmt` to collectReassignedObjs — when Tok == token.ASSIGN, mark the Objects of Key/Value *ast.Idents as reassigned (3 lines); rejected fixture (`for _, id = range` then constructor call) + test. (b) Document pointer-indirect writes (`*p = ...` through `&id`) as deliberately out of scope alongside the existing function-value-aliasing recognition-boundary paragraph (same dataflow-not-syntax class; same runtime backstop). (c) Tighten the rule-2 doc claim to enumerate exactly what is tracked. Suitable for the epoch budget's MINOR-DEFER disposition if the wave closes 0B/0I.
title: S2.3-REVIEW-A-3-FINDING-M1: collectReassignedObjs misses range-clause rebinding — 'for _, id = range ...' is an assignment per the Go spec but not an ast.AssignStmt

### B2: YAML error-path tests — RESOLVED

### B3: workflow_ref validity sync test — RESOLVED
Test: `Workflow.figure.workflow_ref == Workflow.id` for all workflows with figures.
Since figures are now embedded ON the workflow, this is a structural invariant — the figure's workflow_ref must match its parent Workflow's id. This is actually STRONGER than the original Gap-3 (which only checked that workflow_ref pointed to a valid key in WORKFLOW_SPECS). Now the test verifies identity, not just existence.

### B4: Positional assertion for inline rendering — RESOLVED
3 positional tests specified:

### B5: Figure type attribute sync test — RESOLVED
Test: `<figure type='...'>` values in schema.xml match Figure.type strings in WORKFLOW_SPECS.
Plus test_all_schema_figures_in_python and test_figure_count_matches for bidirectional sync.
Addresses Gap-5. The plain string type (no enum) means the sync test compares string-to-string rather than enum-to-schema, which is simpler but equally correct.

## C1-C2 Elegance Revision Assessment

### C1: Embed figure on Workflow — CORRECTLY APPLIED
Workflow dataclass gains `figure: Figure | None = None`. WORKFLOW_SPECS entries have `figure=Figure(...)` for the 3 MVP figures. No separate FIGURE_SPECS dict. No figure_by_workflow lookup dict in gen_skills.py. Template uses `{% if wf.figure %}`. context_injection populates figure.content when building workflows. This is the exact change Reviewer C requested: the HAS-A relationship is expressed in the type system.

### C2: Drop FigureType enum — CORRECTLY APPLIED
Figure.type is plain `str` (e.g., 'ascii-diagram'). No FigureType enum defined. YAGNI applied correctly: promote to enum when second type arrives. The sync test (B5) still verifies schema.xml type attributes match the string values.

## Internal Consistency Check

### Frozen Dataclass Constraint
Workflow is a frozen dataclass. Adding `figure: Figure | None = None` as a default field at the end is valid because it has a default value and all preceding fields are positional. Figure itself is frozen. Immutability chain is preserved: Workflow.figure returns an immutable Figure.

### context_injection Data Flow
get_role_context() filters WORKFLOW_SPECS by role_ref (existing pattern, line 466-470). The proposal extends this to: for each filtered workflow, if workflow.figure is not None, load YAML content and return a new Workflow with figure.content populated. Since both Workflow and Figure are frozen, this requires constructing new instances (e.g., via dataclasses.replace). The proposal states "return a new Workflow with figure.content populated" which implies replace(). This is consistent with how frozen dataclasses are modified elsewhere in the codebase.

### Template Data Flow
gen_skills.py passes `role_ctx.workflows` to the template as `workflows`. The template iterates `{% for wf in workflows %}` (line 134). Adding `{% if wf.figure %}` after exit conditions (line 153) and before `{% endfor %}` (line 154) is correct insertion point. No changes needed to gen_skills.py's context construction — zero new plumbing, as claimed.

### Schema Round-Trip
gen_schema.py iterates WORKFLOW_SPECS, emits <figure> for workflows with figure != None. schema_parser.py parses <figure> elements into SchemaSpec.figures dict. The round-trip is: types.py -> gen_schema.py -> schema.xml -> schema_parser.py -> SchemaSpec.figures. This parallels workflows, checklists, coordination_commands.

## Minor Observations (non-blocking)

1. **dataclasses.replace chain**: Populating figure.content requires two replace() calls: one for Figure (to set content) and one for Workflow (to set the new figure). The proposal does not spell out this detail explicitly, but it is the only correct approach for frozen dataclasses. Implementation should handle this.

2. **section_ref redundancy**: With figures embedded on Workflow, section_ref is always 'workflows' and is derivable from context. The field is kept per URD R5, which is fine, but it will carry no discriminating information for MVP. If non-workflow figures arrive later, this field becomes meaningful again.

3. **Figure.id == Workflow.id**: In WORKFLOW_SPECS, each Figure's id matches its parent Workflow's id (e.g., Figure(id='ride-the-wave') on Workflow(id='ride-the-wave')). This is a design choice — the figure shares identity with its workflow. The B3 test checks this invariant. If figures ever need independent identity (e.g., multiple figures per workflow), this would need to change. Acceptable for MVP.

4. **YAML workflow_ref field**: The proposal adds workflow_ref to existing YAML files (layer-cake.yaml, ride-the-wave.yaml). Currently these YAMLs have no workflow_ref field. The YAML workflow_ref would need to match the Figure.workflow_ref in types.py, but the proposal does not specify whether _load_figure_content reads and validates workflow_ref from YAML or ignores it. Since metadata lives in types.py and YAML is only content source, the YAML workflow_ref is informational/redundant. Implementation should clarify whether it is validated or ignored.

## Specification
Manage epoch lifecycle state and validate transitions against the protocol. Pure Python — no Temporal dependency.

### Key Types
- EpochState (mutable runtime state)
- TransitionRecord (frozen, immutable audit entry)
- TransitionError (exception with violations list)
- EpochStateMachine (main class)

### Key Behaviors
- advance(to_phase) — validates and executes transitions
- validate_advance(to_phase) — dry-run validation
- record_vote(axis, vote) — record reviewer votes
- has_consensus() — check 3/3 ACCEPT
- record_blocker(resolved) — track BLOCKER count
- available_transitions property

### Transition Rules (from schema.xml)
- Sequential forward: p1→p2→p3→p4→p5→p6→p7→p8→p9→p10→p11→p12→complete
- Review revision loops: p4→p3 (REVISE), p10→p9 (BLOCKER fix)
- Consensus gate: p4→p5 requires 3 ACCEPT, p5→p6 requires UAT pass
- BLOCKER gate: p10→p11 requires blocker_count == 0

- tests/test_state_machine.py (NEW)

- AC1: Given epoch in P1 when advance(p2) then transitions, records transition should not allow p1→p8
- AC2: Given epoch in P4 with 2/3 ACCEPT when advance(p5) then TransitionError should not proceed without consensus
- AC3: Given epoch in P4 with REVISE when checking transitions then only p3 available
- AC4: Given epoch in P10 with blockers when advance(p11) then TransitionError should not proceed to UAT

- [ ] TransitionRecord frozen dataclass

## Problem Space

The pasture Go codebase has 329 tests across 31 files, all using manual if/error assertions with no YAML fixture infrastructure. Four coverage gaps exist: CLI binaries at 0% coverage, RunAgentSession with only a connect-error test, config YAML file loading never exercised end-to-end, and ContentBlock dual Content/Text fields ambiguous and untested.

**Axes:**
- **Parallelism:** Test cases are independent; Go subtests run in parallel naturally via t.Parallel()
- **Distribution:** Per-package testdata/ directories (D1), not centralized
- **Has-a:** Fixture loader HAS test case structs; test files HAVE testdata/ YAML files
- **Is-a:** Each coverage gap IS a separate test file with its own YAML schema

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Option Chosen | Rationale |
|----------|--------------|-----------|
| Fixture location | Per-package testdata/ | Go-idiomatic, go test recognizes testdata/ (D1) |
| Assertion library | testify/assert | Already in go.mod v1.10.0, more readable (D2) |
| Fixture style | Full table-driven (inputs+expected) | YAML defines everything, Go just runs it (D3) |
| Dependencies | None new | testify + yaml.v3 both already available (D4) |
| Loader location | internal/testutil/fixtures.go | Shared across all packages |

package testutil

import (
    "os"
    "path/filepath"
    "testing"

    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
    "gopkg.in/yaml.v3"
)

// LoadFixtures reads a YAML fixture file from testdata/{name}.yaml relative
// to the caller's package directory, and unmarshals it into target.
//
// Fails the test immediately (via require) if the file cannot be read or
// parsed — fixture loading errors are infrastructure failures, not test
// failures.
//
// Usage:
//   var cases MyFixtureStruct
//   testutil.LoadFixtures(t, "cli_smoke", &cases)
func LoadFixtures(t *testing.T, name string, target any) {
    t.Helper()
    // testdata path is relative to the test file's directory
    path := filepath.Join("testdata", name+".yaml")
    data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
    require.NoError(t, err, "fixture file %s", path)
    require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(data, target), "unmarshal %s", path)
}

**File:** cmd/pasture-msg/main_test.go

\`\`\`go
package main

import (
    "bytes"
    "os/exec"
    "testing"

    "github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/internal/testutil"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

type CLISmokeCase struct {
    ID                 string   \`yaml:"id"\`
    Args               []string \`yaml:"args"\`
    WantExit           int      \`yaml:"want_exit"\`
    WantStdoutContains string   \`yaml:"want_stdout_contains"\`
    WantStderrContains string   \`yaml:"want_stderr_contains"\`
}

type CLISmokeFixtures struct {
    Tests []CLISmokeCase \`yaml:"tests"\`
}

func TestCLISmoke(t *testing.T) {
    // Build the binary once for all subtests.
    binPath := buildBinary(t, "pasture-msg")

    var fixtures CLISmokeFixtures
    testutil.LoadFixtures(t, "cli_smoke", &fixtures)
    require.NotEmpty(t, fixtures.Tests, "no test cases loaded")

    for _, tc := range fixtures.Tests {
        t.Run(tc.ID, func(t *testing.T) {
            t.Parallel()
            cmd := exec.Command(binPath, tc.Args...)
            var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
            cmd.Stdout = &stdout
            cmd.Stderr = &stderr

            err := cmd.Run()

            // Check exit code.
            exitCode := 0
            if err != nil {
                if exitErr, ok := err.(*exec.ExitError); ok {
                    exitCode = exitErr.ExitCode()
                } else {
                    t.Fatalf("unexpected exec error: %v", err)
                }
            }
            assert.Equal(t, tc.WantExit, exitCode, "exit code")

            if tc.WantStdoutContains != "" {
                assert.Contains(t, stdout.String(), tc.WantStdoutContains, "stdout")
            }
            if tc.WantStderrContains != "" {
                assert.Contains(t, stderr.String(), tc.WantStderrContains, "stderr")
            }
        })
    }
}

// buildBinary compiles the binary in a temp dir and returns its path.
func buildBinary(t *testing.T, name string) string {
    t.Helper()
    tmpDir := t.TempDir()
    binPath := filepath.Join(tmpDir, name)
    cmd := exec.Command("go", "build", "-o", binPath, ".")
    cmd.Dir = "."  // current package directory
    out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
    require.NoError(t, err, "go build: %s", out)
    return binPath
}

func TestRunAgentSession_YAML(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()

    var fixtures RunAgentSessionFixtures
    testutil.LoadFixtures(t, "run_agent_session", &fixtures)
    require.NotEmpty(t, fixtures.Tests)

    binPath := buildFakeAgent(t) // reuses existing helper

    for _, tc := range fixtures.Tests {
        t.Run(tc.ID, func(t *testing.T) {
            t.Parallel()
            trail := audit.NewInMemoryAuditTrail()
            acts := newActivities(trail)

            suite := &testsuite.WorkflowTestSuite{}
            env := suite.NewTestActivityEnvironment()
            env.RegisterActivity(acts)

            agentCmd := binPath
            if tc.AgentCmd != "" {
                agentCmd = tc.AgentCmd
            }

            input := temporal.RunAgentSessionInput{
                AgentCmd:  agentCmd,
                AgentArgs: buildFakeAgentArgs(t, tc.AgentUpdates),
                EpochID:   "epoch-" + tc.ID,
            }

            if tc.AgentHangs {
                // For hang tests, use context with cancellation
                // (Temporal test env handles this differently)
                input.AgentCmd = binPath
                input.AgentArgs = []string{} // no output = hangs
            }

            val, err := env.ExecuteActivity(acts.RunAgentSession, input)

            if tc.Want.Error {
                assert.Error(t, err, "expected error")
                return
            }
            require.NoError(t, err)

            var result temporal.RunAgentSessionResult
            require.NoError(t, val.Get(&result))

            assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, result.EntriesRecorded, tc.Want.EntriesRecordedMin)
            if tc.Want.SessionID != "" {

            }
            if tc.Want.StopReason != "" {

type ConfigLoadingCase struct {

    Description    string            \`yaml:"description"\`

    WantPastureMsg *PastureMsgWant   \`yaml:"want_pasture_msg"\`
    WantError      bool              \`yaml:"want_error"\`
    ErrorContains  string            \`yaml:"error_contains"\`
}

type PasturedWant struct {
    Namespace     string \`yaml:"namespace"\`
    TaskQueue     string \`yaml:"task_queue"\`
    ServerAddress string \`yaml:"server_address"\`
    AuditTrail    string \`yaml:"audit_trail"\`
}

type PastureMsgWant struct {
    Namespace     string \`yaml:"namespace"\`
    TaskQueue     string \`yaml:"task_queue"\`
    ServerAddress string \`yaml:"server_address"\`
    DefaultFormat string \`yaml:"default_format"\`
}

type ConfigLoadingFixtures struct {
    Tests []ConfigLoadingCase \`yaml:"tests"\`
}

func TestConfigYAMLLoading(t *testing.T) {
    var fixtures ConfigLoadingFixtures
    testutil.LoadFixtures(t, "config_loading", &fixtures)
    require.NotEmpty(t, fixtures.Tests)

    for _, tc := range fixtures.Tests {
        t.Run(tc.ID, func(t *testing.T) {
            clearAllEnvVars(t) // ensure clean slate

            var cfgPath string
            if tc.UseMissingPath {
                cfgPath = filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "nonexistent.yaml")
            } else {
                dir := t.TempDir()
                cfgPath = filepath.Join(dir, "config.yaml")
                require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(cfgPath, []byte(tc.YAMLContent), 0o644))
            }

            cmd := newPasturedTestCmd()
            cfg := config.ResolvePasturedConfigFromFile(cmd, cfgPath)

            // Note: ResolvePasturedConfigFromFile does not return errors;
            // malformed YAML falls through to defaults. Test accordingly.
            if tc.WantPastured != nil {
                assert.Equal(t, tc.WantPastured.Namespace, cfg.Connection.Namespace)
                assert.Equal(t, tc.WantPastured.TaskQueue, cfg.Connection.TaskQueue)
                assert.Equal(t, tc.WantPastured.ServerAddress, cfg.Connection.ServerAddress)
                assert.Equal(t, types.AuditBackend(tc.WantPastured.AuditTrail), cfg.AuditTrail)
            }
        })
    }
}

package acp_test

import (
    "testing"

    "github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/internal/acp"
    "github.com/dayvidpham/pasture/internal/testutil"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

type ContentBlockCase struct {
    ID         string        \`yaml:"id"\`
    Description string       \`yaml:"description"\`
    Block      ContentInput  \`yaml:"block"\`
    WantText   string        \`yaml:"want_text"\`
    WantSource string        \`yaml:"want_source"\`
}

type ContentInput struct {
    Type    string \`yaml:"type"\`
    Content string \`yaml:"content"\`
    Text    string \`yaml:"text"\`
}

type ContentBlockFixtures struct {
    Tests []ContentBlockCase \`yaml:"tests"\`
}

func TestContentBlockDualFields(t *testing.T) {
    t.Parallel()

    var fixtures ContentBlockFixtures
    testutil.LoadFixtures(t, "content_block", &fixtures)
    require.NotEmpty(t, fixtures.Tests)

    for _, tc := range fixtures.Tests {
        t.Run(tc.ID, func(t *testing.T) {
            t.Parallel()
            block := acp.ContentBlock{
                Type:    tc.Block.Type,
                Content: tc.Block.Content,
                Text:    tc.Block.Text,
            }

            // Test the indexer's resolution logic: Content wins over Text
            update := acp.SessionUpdate{
                SessionID: "test-session",
                Role:      "assistant",
                Content:   []acp.ContentBlock{block},
            }

            indexer := acp.NewSharedIndexer()
            entries := indexer.Index(update)

            if tc.WantText == "" {
                // For non-text blocks or empty text, preview may be nil
                if len(entries) > 0 && entries[0].ContentPreview != nil {
                    assert.Empty(t, *entries[0].ContentPreview,
                        "expected empty preview for %s", tc.ID)
                }
            } else {
                require.NotEmpty(t, entries, "expected indexed entries")
                require.NotNil(t, entries[0].ContentPreview,
                    "expected non-nil ContentPreview for %s", tc.ID)
                assert.Contains(t, *entries[0].ContentPreview, tc.WantText,
                    "content preview should contain expected text")
            }
        })
    }
}

## BDD Acceptance Criteria

**AC1: Fixture Loader**
- Given a testdata/example.yaml file exists in the calling package
- When LoadFixtures(t, "example", &target) is called
- Then target is populated with the unmarshalled YAML data
- Should not silently ignore missing or malformed YAML files

**AC2: CLI Smoke Tests**
- Given pasture-msg binary is compiled via go build
- When executed with --help
- Then exit code is 0 and stdout contains "pasture-msg"
- Should not require Temporal server running

**AC3: CLI Smoke Tests (pasture-release)**
- Given pasture-release binary is compiled via go build
- When executed with an unknown subcommand
- Then exit code is non-zero and stderr contains an error message
- Should not require git repository or version files

**AC4: RunAgentSession Happy Path**
- Given a fake agent binary that emits session/update JSON-RPC lines
- When RunAgentSession is executed via Temporal test environment
- Then result.EntriesRecorded >= 1, result.SessionID matches, result.StopReason matches
- Should not require a real Temporal cluster

**AC5: Config YAML File Loading**
- Given a temp YAML config file with connection.namespace set to "yaml-ns"
- When ResolvePasturedConfigFromFile is called with no CLI flags or env vars
- Then cfg.Connection.Namespace equals "yaml-ns"
- Should not mutate global state or leak env vars between tests

**AC6: ContentBlock Dual Fields**
- Given a ContentBlock with both Content="canonical" and Text="wire"
- When indexed by SharedIndexer
- Then the ContentPreview contains "canonical" (Content wins)
- Should not use Text when Content is non-empty

A1 (stricter bar + DEFER-only FOLLOWUP + rename): SIMPLIFICATION. PROPOSAL-3 gave FOLLOWUP a heterogeneous two-source feed (MINOR severity + DEFER'd UAT items). Rename FragSupImportantMinorFollowup->FragSupDeferredFollowup is warranted: the old name now lies (it no longer routes IMPORTANT/MINOR). Rename enumeration verified complete (specs.go:112/146, specs_data_fragments.go:104, behaviorRef :90/:1833, header :29).

A2 (drop request-type axis/enum; fix-intent trigger): NET SIMPLIFICATION, no lost capability. The request-type axis was architect-invented and not in source requirements; the user clarified the need is just 'REQUEST whose user-intent is fix', recognized semantically as today's classification already does. C-fix-validation-cases + FragFixValidationCases (elicit+uat+worker) fully preserve the validation-case lifecycle. Removes an unneeded 5th classification axis, Go enum, and bd-type coupling.

A3 (all 6 edges + retire StoragePattern + drop allowlist): MORE elegant, not over-reach. PROPOSAL-3's per-edge allowlist was accidental complexity — its own consensus comment flagged the incoherent byte-identical-but-opposite treatment of architect_handoff:200 vs architect_ratify:102. Retiring the whole mechanism eliminates the special-case axis: 'no allowlist because nothing legitimately remains' is the simplest invariant, and a future edge needs no allowlist decision. G2 becomes a blunt zero-occurrence sweep (simpler + stronger than a semantic allowlist-aware check). StoragePattern sentinel ('beads-task-body') is cleaner than removing the field: keeps schema struct shape stable (no ripple through schema.go/schema_types.go/fixtures) while the field still answers 'where is the handoff stored'. Anchors verified: schema.go:842, schema_types.go:351, fixtures :91/:283.

---

  request: aura-plugins-oc1tm

## Summary

Port the Python codegen tooling (gen_skills.py, gen_schema.py, gen_agents.py, context_injection.py) to Go, using the templ library for template rendering. The Go types already exist in pkg/protocol/ and internal/types/ — this builds the generation layer on top.

## Scope

### In Scope
1. **context_injection.go** — Role/phase context builder (port of context_injection.py)
2. **gen_schema.go** — schema.xml generation from Go types (port of gen_schema.py)
3. **gen_skills.go** — SKILL.md header generation with BEGIN/END markers (port of gen_skills.py)
4. **gen_agents.go** — Agent definition markdown generation (port of gen_agents.py)
5. **Makefile generate target** — orchestrate all codegen
6. **Tests** — round-trip validation, output parity checks

### Out of Scope
- gen_types.go (one-time bootstrap tool — Go types already hand-written)
- schema_parser.go (schema.xml → types direction — not needed since Go types are canonical)
- Modifying existing Go types in pkg/protocol/ or internal/types/

## Architecture

### Data Flow (same as Python)
```
Go types (canonical)
    ├─→ gen_schema.go ──→ schema.xml
    ├─→ gen_skills.go ──→ skills/{role}/SKILL.md headers
    │       ↑ context_injection.go
    └─→ gen_agents.go ──→ agents/{role}.md
            ↑ context_injection.go
```

### Package Structure
```
pasture/
  internal/
    codegen/
      context.go        — RoleContext, PhaseContext builders
      context_test.go
      schema.go         — schema.xml generation (encoding/xml)
      schema_test.go
      skills.go         — SKILL.md generation with BEGIN/END markers
      skills_test.go
      agents.go         — agent definition generation
      agents_test.go
      markers.go        — BEGIN/END marker text surgery
      markers_test.go
      templates/        — templ template files (.templ)
        skill_header.templ
        skill_sub_figure.templ
        agent_definition.templ
  cmd/
    pasture-codegen/    — CLI entry point
      main.go           — cobra commands: gen-schema, gen-skills, gen-agents, gen-all
```

### Key Design Decisions

**D1: templ for templates** — User-specified. templ compiles templates to type-safe Go code, catching template errors at compile time rather than runtime. Templates produce text output (not just HTML).

**D2: encoding/xml for schema.xml** — gen_schema builds XML programmatically (same as Python's ElementTree approach). No templates needed for XML — struct marshalling + custom builders.

**D3: internal/codegen package** — All codegen lives in one internal package with clear file boundaries. Not exported — only consumed by cmd/pasture-codegen.

**D4: Same canonical lookup dicts pattern** — Port ROLE_SPECS, COMMAND_SPECS, CONSTRAINT_SPECS etc. as Go maps with typed keys. These already partially exist in Go types; codegen adds the context-injection layer.

**D5: BEGIN/END marker strategy** — Same as Python: validate markers exist, replace between them, preserve hand-authored content below END marker. MarkerError type for strict validation.

**D6: Constraint mapping inversion** — Same as Python: hand-authored role→constraints and phase→constraints maps, inverted at init time for schema generation.

## Vertical Slices

| Slice | Wave | Scope | Files |
|-------|------|-------|-------|
| S1 | 1 | Canonical spec dicts + context injection | internal/codegen/context.go, context_test.go |
| S2 | 1 | BEGIN/END marker text surgery | internal/codegen/markers.go, markers_test.go |
| S3 | 2 | schema.xml generation | internal/codegen/schema.go, schema_test.go |
| S4 | 2 | SKILL.md generation (templ templates) | internal/codegen/skills.go, skills_test.go, templates/*.templ |
| S5 | 2 | Agent definition generation | internal/codegen/agents.go, agents_test.go |
| S6 | 3 | CLI entry point + Makefile | cmd/pasture-codegen/main.go, Makefile |

Wave 1 (S1, S2) — foundation types and utilities
Wave 2 (S3, S4, S5) — the 3 generators (parallel, independent)
Wave 3 (S6) — CLI wiring + build integration

## Acceptance Criteria

AC1: Given Go types exist, when running gen-schema, then output schema.xml matches Python-generated schema.xml structure
AC2: Given a SKILL.md with BEGIN/END markers, when running gen-skills, then generated header replaces marker region and hand-authored body is preserved
AC3: Given a role with tools defined, when running gen-agents, then agents/{role}.md is generated with constraints, phases, and checklists
AC4: Given no SKILL.md exists, when running gen-skills --init, then markers are prepended to create initial file
AC5: Given make generate is run, then all 3 generators execute and output is up-to-date

## Open Questions

Q1: templ library generates HTML by default — need to verify it supports plain text/markdown output mode, or if we need text/template as fallback for non-HTML output
Q2: Should the Go codegen consume the same schema.xml as input (like gen_types.py), or should Go types remain the canonical source and schema.xml be purely output?
title: PROPOSAL-1: Port codegen (gen_skills, gen_schema, gen_agents) to Go pasture

description:
**File:** internal/sqlite/activity_replay.go, foldActivityCreateLocked

**What:** Even in a scenario where Step 1 (INSERT OR IGNORE) inserts a fresh activities row (0 prior conflict), the audit attribution fields (agent_id, phase_id, stage_id, notes, started_at) are written from the operation's eff.Activity* fields without any post-insert verification that the DB row matches. This matters because the INSERT statement at Step 1 ignores a return value confirming how many rows were actually affected, and the code relies on the implicit assumption that any non-error result means the correct row now exists. A subsequent write to journal_activity_creations then serves as the authoritative 'birth record' without confirming the activities row carries the correct attribution.

**Why:** The code conflates 'INSERT succeeded without error' with 'the intended row exists with the intended fields'. For the exact-replay comment justification ('the row may already exist from a prior rolled-back attempt'), the comment describes a partial-write that SQLite's ROLLBACK should have reverted — making the scenario described impossible under SAVEPOINT semantics.

**Fix:** After Step 1, either (a) SELECT back the just-inserted activities row and verify its fields match the expected attribution (then return an attribution conflict if not), or (b) use INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO FAIL instead of INSERT OR IGNORE to ensure we never silently adopt a pre-existing row.
title: SLICE-1.2-REVIEW-A-3 IMPORTANT-2: ActivityCreate audit attribution fields are not verified on collision/IGNORE path before journaling birth

`dbos_wire.go:118-121` deliberately transports `RecordedAt`, while `dbos_outcome.go:325-342` hashes the complete `input.Context`. `internal/journal/operations.go:343` defines `RecordedAt` as audit/display only, and the canonical replay key excludes it. Therefore an exact logical retry that reconstructs the same OperationID, actor, authority, command digest, and canonical mutation but supplies a refreshed timestamp receives a second V2 workflow ID and executes another durable step/replay rather than attaching to the original workflow. This creates multiple DBOS workflow authorities for one logical operation and makes workflow identity stricter than the canonical journal authority.

Impact: domain writes remain protected by Journal.Apply, but durable workflow identity and retry semantics diverge; historical/reconstructed callers can accumulate duplicate completed workflows and cannot honestly retrieve the original checkpoint by logical operation identity.

Fix: keep RecordedAt in the persisted V2 input for audit, but derive the V2 workflow/step fingerprint from the canonical replay identity only (contract/version + OperationID + actor + authority + command digest + canonical mutation bytes). Add an integration test that changes only RecordedAt on a completed retry and proves the same workflow is attached with zero DBOS callbacks beyond the read-only preflight.
title: BLOCKER: Exclude audit RecordedAt from V2 durable workflow identity

**Has-a relationships:** The supervisor role HAS constraints, behaviors, invariants, standing-teams, workflows. The Ride the Wave workflow HAS stages (plan, build, review). The review cycle HAS exit conditions.

**Is-a relationships:** The supervisor IS an agent definition (agents/supervisor.md). Explore subagents ARE ephemeral (not standing). Reviewers ARE ephemeral subagents (same as Phase 4).

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Option A | Option B | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|----------|----------|--------|-----------|
| T1: Exploration model | Standing Cartographers (3 persistent agents) | Ephemeral Explore subagents per query | B: Ephemeral | Supervisor stays lean; no standing team overhead; simpler lifecycle (URD D1) |
| T2: Review model | Cartographer role-switch to reviewer | Ephemeral reviewer subagents per round | B: Ephemeral | Consistent with Phase 4 pattern; no persistence between rounds (URD D2) |

- _HANDOFF_REQUIRED_TRANSITIONS: frozenset[...] = frozenset(...)

_SAME_ACTOR should follow the same pattern.

## Fix
Move _SAME_ACTOR to module scope:
    _SAME_ACTOR_TRANSITIONS: frozenset[tuple[PhaseId, PhaseId]] = frozenset(
        {(PhaseId.P5_UAT, PhaseId.P6_RATIFY), (PhaseId.P6_RATIFY, PhaseId.P7_HANDOFF)}
    )
Consistent naming with _HANDOFF_REQUIRED_TRANSITIONS.

File: internal/tasks/epoch_assignment_service.go:265-296 (especially 287-294).

`resolveAssignment` returns `resolution.authority`, but `apply` discards it and sends `AuthorityJournalID: &s.authority`, the fixed system/bootstrap authority. The barrier is immediately before Apply, so an assignment can end or transfer after preflight and the operation still commits its task, evidence, event, activity, and projection effects because bootstrap governs every task. This violates exact current role/assignment authority and the required zero-write loser behavior for synchronized stale races.

Exact fix: bind each assignment mutation to the resolved assignment authority/episode inside the same transactional authority check (and explicitly handle any allocation-parent authorization without falling back to bootstrap as the sole authority); carry the exact assignment binding in the replay identity. Add barrier tests for end/transfer versus every mutation and assert typed stale failure plus byte/row-zero writes.

close_reason: VERIFIED-FIXED cycle-2 (pasture dd1b820): legacyImportMutationRef now length-delimits (netstring-style) its hash input before sha256, making the encoding injective. Verified via shipped regression tests + reviewer's independent standalone Go repro of the original NUL-collision pair plus a length-prefix-confusion variant — no collisions. See aura-plugins-d156j cycle-2 comment for full attack detail.
description:
WHAT: legacyImportMutationRef (internal/tasks/legacy_import.go) derives the stable
source-keyed idempotency ref as:
  sha256(row.SourceTable + "\x00" + row.LegacyRowID)

WHY THIS IS WEAK (theoretical, not currently exploitable): plain concatenation
with a single \x00 separator is ambiguous when either field can itself contain a
\x00 byte. Two distinct (SourceTable, LegacyRowID) pairs that differ only in where
the \x00 falls produce byte-identical hash input and therefore the SAME
OperationID:
  SourceTable="A\x00B", LegacyRowID="C"   ->  "A\x00B" + "\x00" + "C" = "A\x00B\x00C"
  SourceTable="A",      LegacyRowID="B\x00C" -> "A" + "\x00" + "B\x00C" = "A\x00B\x00C"
Both hash to the same OperationID, so importing the second row after the first
would either short-circuit as a "replay" (if payload/fan-out happen to match the
digest) or be wrongly rejected as a compound conflict — a genuine identity
collision between TWO DIFFERENT SOURCE ROWS, which is exactly what the
source-keyed OperationID is supposed to make impossible (per the axis charter's
"two distinct source rows must never collide" requirement).

WHY NOT A BLOCKER: SourceTable and LegacyRowID are supplied by a caller-implemented
provadapter.LegacyAuditSource (internal/provadapter/legacyaudit.go) — in this
delta's own call sites these are drawn from a closed set of legacy table names and
integer/UUID row ids, none of which can contain a NUL byte in practice. There is
no currently-reachable path that lets an attacker or malformed data choose
SourceTable/LegacyRowID content, so this is a robustness/defense-in-depth gap, not
a live vulnerability.

WHERE: internal/tasks/legacy_import.go, legacyImportMutationRef.

FIX: Use an unambiguous encoding before hashing, e.g. length-prefix each field
(fmt.Sprintf("%d:%s%d:%s", len(SourceTable), SourceTable, len(LegacyRowID),
LegacyRowID)) or hash each field separately and concatenate the two digests. Add a
unit test asserting two constructed (SourceTable, LegacyRowID) pairs that would
collide under naive concatenation produce distinct OperationIDs.
title: S3.3-REVIEW-B MINOR-1: legacyImportMutationRef's SourceTable+\x00+LegacyRowID concatenation is ambiguous (theoretical OperationID collision)

  support report `{harness, contract, events[]}`, per-event
  `{event, state, reason(omitempty), captureProof(omitempty),
  productionProof(omitempty)}`, proofs set only on Enabled, exhaustiveness

  trailing newline, emitted UNCONDITIONALLY at hooks/pasture-activation.json via
  writeFullGeneratedFile. Matches D2's byte-for-byte structure claim precisely.

## Assessment

This is a genuinely right-sized wrap-up plan. Complexity is proportional in both
directions; the proposal makes the correct YAGNI calls explicitly rather than by
omission:

- **No over-engineering.** Extend `Emit` in place (no new emitter type, no
  registration-surface change); NO schema-version tag (Claude report has none —
  parity is the requirement); NO shared cross-harness report builder (explicitly

  justify an abstraction mid-wrap-up); NO fixture generator (content-only
  refresh). Each is the smallest honest mechanism. Verified the Claude precedent
  really has no schema tag and really emits unconditionally, so parity is faithful.

- **Not too thin for Stage 2-4.** The duplicated inline report struct is
  *symmetric* duplication of an existing precedent, not a novel shape that would
  constrain Stage 2. If Stage 2's inventory/registry work (URD R2.5/R2.6) ever
  pays for a shared builder, it consolidates Claude + Codex together at that
  point. Duplicating now does not create a shape the arch-refactor stage will
  regret — it creates exactly the parity a future consolidation folds. Clean.

- **Each R1.x item = smallest mechanism.** R1.1 conflict-free merge; R1.3
  defaults untouched; R1.4/R1.6 doc edits; R1.5 content-only fixture refresh
  keeping all existing cases/negative case/markers; R1.7 mirror-the-precedent
  emitter + in-place test flip keeping the name and all cross-harness
  assertions; R1.8 named-branches-only with an explicit scope fence against the
  repo-wide sweep (URD non-goal). No invented abstraction, no gratuitous process.

- **Single-PR composition is proportional and reviewable.** The URD mandates ONE
  Aura PR; the proposal respects it. The submodule bump beyond the URD's literal
  "flake.lock advance" is coherence, not scope-creep: two pins of the same
  dependency telling two stories is the disproportionate option; precedent
  28d52d1 bumps both together, and the addition is explicitly flagged for Plan
  UAT. Merge + lock + submodule + fixtures + docs is one revert unit and does
  not cram unrelated changes.

- **Stage boundary is clean.** D8 acknowledges Stages 2-4 as later gated
  proposals and pre-implements none of their machinery; deferrals reconfirmed
  verbatim. Slice sketch (SLICE-P1 pasture → R_audit; SLICE-A1 aura gated on
  R_audit; COORD-C1 supervisor-run hygiene) has exactly one cross-slice contract

```python
class AcpEventType(StrEnum):
    """Discriminator for inbound ACP SessionUpdate event types."""
    PHASE_ADVANCE = 'phase_advance'
    REVIEW_VOTE   = 'review_vote'

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AcpRawSignal:
    """Frozen wrapper for an inbound ACP SessionUpdate at the Temporal boundary."""

    event_type:   AcpEventType   # was: str — now strongly typed StrEnum
    payload_json: str             # full event as JSON string

@workflow.signal

    self._pending_acp_raw.append(raw)
```

map_acp_event activity — ValidationError guard (B-2 MUST FIX #2):

```python
@activity.defn
async def map_acp_event(raw: AcpRawSignal) -> AcpMappedSignal:
    try:
        update = acp.schema.SessionUpdate.model_validate_json(raw.payload_json)
    except pydantic.ValidationError:
        # Non-transient — malformed ACP payload. Return noop (no retry will fix this).
        return AcpMappedSignal.noop()
    return DefaultAcpEventMapper().map_to_signal(update)
```

run() drain loop — ActivityError guard (B-2 MUST FIX #3):

```python
# Inside run() loop, draining _pending_acp_raw:
for raw in draining_list:
    try:
        mapped = await workflow.execute_activity(
            map_acp_event, args=[raw],
            start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=10),
        )
    except ActivityError:
        # Permanently-failed activity (non-retryable or exhausted retries).
        # Log and skip — preserve epoch liveness. Same pattern as TransitionError.
        workflow.logger.warning(
            'map_acp_event permanently failed for session=%s event_type=%s — skipping',
            raw.session_id, raw.event_type,
        )
        continue
    if mapped.advance: self._pending_advance.append(mapped.advance)
    if mapped.vote:    self._pending_votes.append(mapped.vote)
```

### 2.3 AcpMappedSignal — noop() factory + __post_init__ guard (C-2 SHOULD FIX #3)

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AcpMappedSignal:
    """Result of mapping an inbound ACP event to Temporal domain signals.
    
    Exactly one of advance or vote must be set, OR use AcpMappedSignal.noop()
    to represent an intentional no-op (unknown/unmappable event).
    """
    advance: PhaseAdvanceSignal | None = None
    vote:    ReviewVoteSignal | None   = None
    _is_noop: bool = False  # private sentinel; use noop() factory, not direct field

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self._is_noop and self.advance is None and self.vote is None:
            raise ValueError(
                'AcpMappedSignal must carry at least one signal. '
                'Use AcpMappedSignal.noop() for intentional no-ops.'
            )

    @classmethod
    def noop(cls) -> 'AcpMappedSignal':
        """Return a sentinel no-op instance (unknown/unmappable ACP event)."""
        return cls(_is_noop=True)
```

D13: run() drain loop catches ActivityError around map_acp_event dispatch — same pattern as TransitionError at workflow.py:284-299. Log session_id + event_type. Epoch liveness preserved on permanently-failed activities.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-56: Provenance-backed epoch aggregate, lifecycle hook adapters, and executable test contract

## 1. Revision Decision

This proposal supersedes FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-55 (`aura-plugins-s6j4f`) and still
amends ratified Proposal 50 (`aura-plugins-jdj2x`). It preserves Proposal 55's
architecture and approved commands without modification. Its substantive revision
is to freeze the complete executable test contract required by independent Reviewer
B (`aura-plugins-vqprx`).

The amendment establishes one authoritative, journal-backed Pasture workflow
application aggregate under `pasture epoch`. It uses existing Provenance agents,
activities/events, entities/tasks, assignments/roles, decisions, evidence, graph
edges, and atomic journal operations. It does not introduce another graph, generic
finite-state-machine framework, storage framework, protected decision-ledger task,
revision protocol, or payload-codec framework.

Pasture remains:

1. A scriptable deterministic SDLC engine.
2. A Provenance-backed replacement for Beads task and knowledge management.
3. A stable CLI contract invoked by version-bounded harness lifecycle adapters.
4. The authority for workflow state and gate enforcement, rather than generated
   Markdown instructions.

Provenance remains the shared backbone. Pasture defines the workflow application
profile. Benchmark, item, guideline, annotation, review, assessment, and quality
provenance remain a separate future application profile over the same backbone.

## 2. Problem Space and Architecture Axes

### 2.1 Proposal 50 contradiction

Proposal 50 requires live review, interaction-mode, UAT, ratify, slice,
integration, and land operations, but its frozen interface:

- places most lifecycle operations beneath `pasture task`;
- exposes `--reported-user-result-file`, expected ledger revisions, and internal
  codec concepts;
- derives a human decider from assignment or protected epoch-root state and
  forbids explicit caller-supplied human identity;
- treats ratify and land chiefly as protocol transitions consuming prior
  decisions;
- describes a protected `DECISION_LEDGER` task/revision aggregate not present in
  the integrated production tree.

The implementation contains useful pure policies and projections, including
`PolicySet`, interaction-mode folding, UAT validation, review graph planning,
material events, and the Provenance adapter. It does not contain one production
aggregate that resolves an epoch, validates its graph and evidence, records a
typed decision or assignment-controlled action, and atomically commits the
resulting Provenance operation.

### 2.2 Axes

| Axis | Decision |
|---|---|
| Parallelism | Reviews and slices may proceed concurrently; mutations against one epoch serialize through Provenance journal ordering and atomic preconditions. |
| Distribution | CLI and harness processes may be separate, but Provenance is the sole authoritative store. No distributed transaction or second ledger is introduced. |
| Frequency | Reads are frequent and side-effect free. Lifecycle decisions are less frequent, high-value atomic operations. |
| Cardinality | One epoch has many tasks, assignments, reviews, candidates, decisions, and evidence records, but one lifecycle projection derived from the Provenance graph and journal. |
| Authority | User gates require an explicitly asserted registered human. Review, slice, and integration operations require exact active assignments/roles. These authority classes never substitute for one another. |
| Trust | `--actor` records an asserted registered human. Authentication, signatures, and identity-provider verification are future evidence. |
| Extensibility | Workflow operations extend the Pasture profile. Benchmark provenance extends a separate profile. |
| Harness variation | Thin version-bounded adapters preserve observe/blocking distinctions and native transports. |
| Recovery | Internal operation identity and Provenance replay provide idempotency. Ordinary CLI users do not handle operation IDs, revisions, or codecs. |
| Testability | Acceptance is proven through the built binary, file-backed real Provenance stores, exact persisted deltas, process restart, synchronized races, and pinned native loaders. |

### 2.3 Relationships

- An epoch **has** tasks, assignments, reviews, candidates, decisions, evidence,
  and graph relationships.
- A task **is** a Provenance entity with lifecycle events and assignments.
- A user-gated action **is** a typed Provenance decision and visible workflow
  activity/event.
- A review, slice, or integration mutation **is** assignment/role controlled, not
  a human decision.
- Ratification **is** a human decision authorized by reviewed evidence, not merely
  a status transition.
- Landing **is** a human decision authorized by accepted UAT and publication
  evidence, not a Git command.
- A harness adapter **is** transport plumbing to stable Pasture operations, not a
  workflow authority or harmonized daemon.
- A corpus mutant **is** a derived test case with a named typed mutation and a
  declared oracle, not an ad hoc modified fixture.
- Benchmark provenance **is** a separate application profile over the same
  Provenance backbone.

## 3. Requirements Traceability

| Source | Requirement | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| URD comments 4238-4248 | Typed workflow effects use Pasture/Provenance rather than Beads. | Generic operations remain under `pasture task`; epoch lifecycle uses `pasture epoch`. |
| URD 4239 | `pasture task` is the harness-neutral Beads-replacement baseline. | Preserved for generic task/knowledge operations, not all SDLC commands. |
| URD 4240-4244 | Mutable responsibility, cumulative attribution, ordered lifecycle journal, material-work events. | Preserved through Provenance assignments, activities, events, evidence, and edges. |
| URD 4245-4247 | Strongly typed IDs, version-bounded harness contracts, semantic user decisions. | Preserved. |
| URD 4248 | Typed YAML corpus, must-pass/must-fail classification, provenance and mutation metadata, bounded deterministic expansion, non-vacuity. | Frozen concretely in sections 12-14. |
| Accepted Plan UAT | Compiler, Provenance/DBOS, AFK, installer, Home Manager, and five deferrals accepted. | Preserved except where later architecture decisions amend lifecycle UX. |
| Architecture transcript | Shared backbone with separate workflow and benchmark profiles. | Normative. |

## 4. Normative Command Hierarchy

### 4.1 User-approved exact baseline

The following baseline is already user-approved. It is normative, unchanged, and
not subject to another Plan UAT:

```text

pasture task show
pasture task update
pasture task close
pasture task relation add
pasture task assignment transfer
pasture task comment add
pasture task timeline

pasture epoch interaction-mode show --epoch <epoch-id>
```

### 4.3 Structured command input

Scalar arguments remain flags or positional enums. Structured payloads are used
only for collections that cannot be represented safely as repeated scalar flags:

- review findings inventories;
- complete finding dispositions and fix evidence for rework;
- multi-repository integration candidate sets;
- structured FIX-NOW/DEFER feedback and carry-forward resolutions for non-accept
  UAT branches.

The proposed transport for those additional commands is one versioned typed JSON
value on stdin selected by `--input -`. The spelling and schemas are part of the
genuine Plan UAT decision. No arbitrary filename is accepted. Shell redirection
may feed stdin, but Pasture gains no report-file abstraction.

This is not the rejected raw harness-report UX: the JSON schema belongs to one
specific Pasture command, contains only its semantic typed fields, rejects unknown
fields/trailing values, and is canonicalized internally before Apply. It is not a
transcript, raw harness response, `--reported-user-result-file`, or generic codec.

Approved accept, ratify, land, and interaction-mode commands require no structured
payload and retain their exact forms.

### 4.4 Hidden adapter invocation contract

Ordinary CLI exposes no `--operation-id`, revision token, codec, or storage
identity. Direct human commands mint operation identity internally.

Generated adapters use a hidden Cobra command absent from help and completion:

```text
pasture __adapter invoke
```

It accepts one `pasture.adapter-invocation/v1` JSON envelope on stdin containing a
typed semantic operation, validated arguments, pinned harness contract ID, and a
private stable native-invocation identity. It cannot invoke an operation absent
from `EpochService`, bypass actor/assignment validation, supply storage revisions,
or submit raw native payloads. Direct and adapter entry points call the same
production aggregate.

### 4.5 Forbidden ordinary CLI concepts

Ordinary help exposes none of:

```text
--operation-id
--expected-revision
--reported-user-result-file
--report-file
--payload-codec
--decision-codec
--raw-report
--decider
--trust
```

## 6. Authority Classes

### 6.1 User gates

Interaction-mode, Plan UAT, ratify, Implementation UAT, and land require explicit
`--actor <registered-human-id>`. The aggregate verifies a registered human and
never derives that human from an assignment, owner, default, or system actor.

### 6.2 Assignment/role-controlled operations

Review, slice, and integration operations require existing Provenance assignments
and Pasture roles. Where the approved `review start` command carries no assignment
flag, the aggregate resolves controlling active authority from the epoch graph and
fails if absent or ambiguous. Proposed commands may identify an assignment, but the
transaction verifies it. Assignment-controlled operations never manufacture human
decisions; human-gated operations never treat assignments as human identity.

## 7. Atomic Provenance Mapping

| Command family | Existing concepts | One atomic application operation |
|---|---|---|
| `task create|update|close` | Task/entity, assignments, lifecycle events | Validate policy; commit state, assignment changes, attribution, and events together. |
| `task relation add` | Graph edge and event | Add validated edge and journal event. |
| `task assignment transfer` | Assignment, role, actors, attribution, activities/events | End prior, start successor, update responsibility, preserve attribution. |
| `task comment add` | Comment/evidence, actor, edge, event | Create/link evidence and journal it. |
| `task show|timeline` | Tasks, events, activities, evidence | Read only. |
| Interaction mode | Human, decision, activity/event | Record explicit mode decision and event. |
| Review start/submit/finalize | Subject, assignments, review decisions/evidence, findings, edges, events | Resolve role authority and commit the complete review mutation. |
| Slice create/candidate/rework/close | Slice/candidate entities, assignments, findings, Git/test evidence, edges, events | Commit one complete slice mutation under assignment authority. |
| Integration create/rework/publish | Candidate set, assignments, repository and publication evidence | Commit one complete integration mutation; guarded Git then journal evidence remains sequential. |
| Plan UAT | Human, decision, proposal, activity/event | Record first-class UAT decision and eligibility. |
| Ratify | Human, decision, proposal/review/UAT evidence, activity/event | Record ratification and ratify proposal. |
| Implementation UAT | Human, decision, candidate/review evidence, activity/event | Record UAT and land eligibility. |
| Land | Human, decision, candidate/UAT/publication evidence, activity/event | Record landing and terminalize epoch. |

All graph, assignment, decision, evidence, activity, event, journal, and projection
changes for one command commit together or not at all. Git publication is not
misrepresented as transactionally atomic with SQLite.

## 8. First-Class Decisions and Events

The production `PolicySet` includes interaction mode, Plan UAT, ratification,
Implementation UAT, and landing descriptors.

| Decision | Authority | Subject | Evidence | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Interaction mode | Explicit human | Epoch | Valid epoch | Record mode decision/event; derive `normal` or `afk`. |
| Plan UAT | Explicit human | Proposal | Current proposal | Record accepted/changes/deferred decision and eligibility. |
| Ratify | Explicit human | Proposal | Accepted review and eligible Plan UAT | Record ratification decision/event and ratify. |
| Implementation UAT | Explicit human | Integration candidate | Current clean review | Record accepted/changes decision and land eligibility. |
| Land | Explicit human | Candidate/epoch | Accepted UAT and publication evidence | Record landing decision/event and terminalize. |

Events reference decision IDs rather than duplicate decision payloads. Interaction
mode is decision-derived, not a permission matrix or separate mutable row.

## 9. Asserted Actor and Future Verification

`--actor` states who the record claims acted. Registration proves the identifier
exists and is human; it does not authenticate the caller. Signatures,
identity-provider attestations, hardware credentials, and authenticated channels
remain future verification evidence attached separately to the immutable decision.
Benchmark provenance remains a separate profile and may later review or contest
these assertions without changing the workflow profile.

## 10. Harness Adapter Architecture

Schema issue #6 is research input only. This proposal does not import or recreate
its proposed `HookEvent`, `HookDecision`, daemon API, merge lattice, event store, or
harmonized transport.

Adapters distinguish:

1. **Observation:** correlated session/tool/file/assignment events may record typed
   task/activity/evidence facts; occurrence alone changes no gate.
2. **Gate consultation:** blocking hooks may query an existing typed Pasture gate
   and translate it to native allow/deny/defer without creating approval.
3. **Explicit human response:** only a deliberate human response supplying a
   registered actor invokes interaction-mode, Plan UAT, ratify, Implementation
   UAT, or land. Arbitrary `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, Stop, or tool events
   cannot manufacture those decisions.

| Harness | Native transport and distinctions | Pasture adapter behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | Pinned command-hook config; JSON stdin, structured stdout, event-specific exits; observe/blocking distinction; `PostToolBatch`; request identity; stop-loop state. | Record correlated evidence, consult existing gates, or forward explicit human lifecycle responses. |
| Codex CLI | Pinned per-event executable runner; strict JSON; input mutation; blocking exit; `stop_hook_active`; concurrent native handlers; unstable transcript. | Same semantic split; no transcript parsing or invented merge semantics. |
| OpenCode | Pinned Bun/OpenCode plugin loader; named handlers, mutable output, catch-all/SSE observation, sequential load order, fail-fast throws. | Await gate queries in named handlers; catch-all/SSE remains observation; explicit human responses call user gates. |
| Antigravity | No recoverable public contract. | Actionable unsupported result; no guessed mapping. |
| Pi | Inspiration-only extension/RPC research. | No adapter shipped. |

Decision-evidence research remains separate from the decision/result. It does not
implement signed authentication or authorize lifecycle decisions.

## 11. Idempotency, Replay, Concurrency, and Errors

- Every mutation has one internal `provenance.OperationID`.
- Direct CLI mints identity internally; generated adapters pass private stable
  identity only through `pasture.adapter-invocation/v1`.
- Exact replay returns identical bindings without duplicate effects.
- One-axis-at-a-time identity conflicts write nothing.
- Concurrent commands validate graph/evidence inside the atomic operation.
- Competing ratify/supersede and UAT/rework/land operations have one eligible
  winner.
- Reads write nothing; timestamps support display while journal order establishes
  causality.
- Errors identify command, failed authority/evidence, object, stage, commit or
  publication impact, and exact public remediation without exposing revisions,
  codecs, WAL details, or CAS tokens.
