# Axis C - Elegance, proportionality, and maintainability

VOTE: REVISE

## Decision

The one-Journal/one-FSM direction is proportionate to the requested deterministic SDLC, lossless fine-grained provenance, and progressive context. The simpler append-native-events-plus-labels design cannot preserve exact codebook/interpreter/build attribution, explicit causal paths, candidate-versus-authority separation, or immutable disclosure history. Proposal-8 also closes the prior per-event activation, canonical occurrence, replay-vocabulary, hostcontract, and file-ownership findings.

Two remaining design contradictions would force workers to create either a dependency cycle or a second mutable source of truth. They require correction before UAT and ratification.

## BLOCKER findings

1. The shared-write end-to-end test is owned by S1 but needs S2 after S2 is blocked on S1. PROPOSAL-8 sections 3.4, 15.1 item 8, 16, 17.1, 17.3, and 17.4; planned path internal/engine/shared_write_budget_test.go.

TestSliceStartDeadlineUnderHookWriteLoad must drive the real generated registration and built binary. Those are S2-CLAUDE-ACTIVATION L3 outputs. Yet the test is S1-RECEIPT L2 work, while IP-2 requires S1 L3 before S2 can enable an event. An S1 L2 test cannot become green until S2 L3; S2 L3 cannot begin its enabled-registration vertical until S1 L3. This contradicts the stated L1 -> L2 -> L3 execution/merge model and makes the M1 resource gate owner ambiguous.

Fix: move the end-to-end engine/load file and its M1 gate ownership to S2, retaining it as the sole named exception to S8 engine-file ownership. Keep an S1-only receipt-service test for one Apply, lock deadline, and transaction-count mechanics. Set timing to S1 L3 -> S2 L3 -> S2-owned shared-file black-box test -> M1 completion. This has one owner and no cyclic L2/L3 dependency.

2. Definition status is represented inside an immutable snapshot and also as later journal state. PROPOSAL-8 section 6.1: DefinitionSnapshot.Status, DefinitionActivationInput.Snapshot.Status, and DefinitionReadQuery.Statuses versus the text requiring separate activation and retirement evidence.

A definition snapshot cannot both be immutable and change from Active to Retired. Leaving Status in the snapshot permits either stale query results or a mutable definition/status table, violating the proposal journal-only truth rule.

Fix: remove Status from DefinitionSnapshot and activation input. Make Activate and Retire append separate immutable definition-state facts, with active resolution and status-filtered reads folded from those facts in JournalID order. If a reader needs status, return a derived DefinitionStateRecord with the source status JournalID; historical lookup returns only the immutable body/ref.

## IMPORTANT findings

1. Disclosure identifiers are inconsistent and DisclosureAttemptID is an unearned second identity. PROPOSAL-8 sections 3 and 9.2-9.3.

The proposal defines DisclosurePlanID, DisclosureAttemptJournalID, and DisclosureResultID, but public plan/attempt/result inputs return or accept bare provenance.JournalID fields. It also introduces a random DisclosureAttemptID without showing a selected channel that needs a separate host-visible correlation token. The attempt JournalID plus the operation ID already identify the durable attempt and exact retry.

Fix: use typed IDs at every plan/attempt/result boundary and expose JournalID accessors where needed. Remove DisclosureAttemptID now. If the UAT-selected channel needs a nonce that cannot expose a JournalID, introduce a bounded channel-specific DeliveryCorrelationToken in that adapter and record its relation to the attempt; do not make it a generic lifecycle identity.

2. Several context/control inputs promise static bounds but name no bounds or deterministic selection rule. PROPOSAL-8 sections 3.1, 7.2, 9.1-9.2, and 10.2.

ContextProjectionInput.Basis, PriorPlans, and Acknowledgements; DisclosureResultInput.Evidence; and CapabilityScope.Sources have slices but no stated maximum or snapshot/truncation behavior. In a long-lived multi-agent epoch, history grows with every delivery, so these can defeat the 1 MiB operation and hook-lock budgets.

Fix: assign explicit constructor limits and a snapshot-bounded selection rule, such as current disclosure state plus bounded newest-first history, for each collection. Return a typed truncation/suppression result where completeness is required, and test it at the public service boundary.

## MINOR findings

- OccurrenceRecord duplicates equal identity fields OccurrenceID and EvidenceJournalID, and InterpretationResult duplicates equal ones Interpretation and JournalID: sections 4.2 and 7.3. Retain the typed ID and add a JournalID accessor, rather than making callers maintain equality invariants.
- The S1 exception for an engine-directory test is otherwise justified: the shared-file contention budget belongs to the receipt path, and S8 owns named control production files rather than the whole directory. It becomes safe once the end-to-end test owner/timing is corrected.

## Prior Axis-C verification

- CLOSED: fixture-granular activation/Withheld report (section 5); one public immutable post-T1 OccurrenceRecord (section 4); no lifecycle replay vocabulary (sections 4.2 and 15.3); one hostcontract plus regeneration guard (section 5.3); explicit M1-M6 paths and transfers (section 17).
- CLOSED: Journal.Apply and JournalID-derived projection identity are the only proposed semantic substrate (section 2); the existing mutable FSM/projection writers in pkg/protocol/state_machine.go lines 20-26 and 72-110, internal/engine/workflow.go lines 98-158, and internal/engine/projection.go lines 44-81 have a one-cutover replacement direction (section 10).
- CLOSED in direction: Codebook, interpreter, implementation, and context-policy refs are separate only where those definitions can evolve independently; facts/results cite their batch/plan instead of copying the full envelope (sections 6-9). The status correction above is required to keep this from becoming a mutable parallel registry.
- CLOSED in direction: generic capability operations are finite and scope candidates rather than hooks (section 10.2), and Interpreter, Enricher, and ContextProjector stay small typed seams rather than a plugin system (sections 7 and 9).

## Engineering axes and end-user impact

- Parallelism/frequency: many independent hook processes share one SQLite writer; bounded one-transaction T1 and the measured contention gate protect hook latency and engine progress.
- Distribution: MVP stays one local multi-process database, not a consensus system.
- Many versus one: many occurrences/facts/links/disclosures are journal records; one immutable phase law and one control writer govern state.
- Has-a versus is-a: occurrence has capture/bindings; interpretation has bounded outputs; disclosure has plan/attempt/result history. Candidate, observation, projection, and capability are not transitions, truth, or authority by themselves.
- Change/cost: exact immutable definition refs let the provisional codebook evolve without rewriting history. Metadata-first retention and bounded readers protect privacy/storage; staged activation and a neutral response protect blocking-hook users.

## Checks

Read-only design review. Read PROPOSAL-8 description and Revision-2 continuations; full UAT q5ams; URD hznvh; PROPOSAL-7 rrv7f; prior Axis-C reviews avkc0/q85i6; contention findings ay4yn/cvlu6; hooks-IR research; existing lifecycle, FSM, codegen, engine, audit, and Provenance journal layout. Inspected planned production paths and current mutable writers. No tests/builds run because this is design-only. No source edits, commits, pushes, dependency changes, implementation, ratification, or severity tree.

## Finding
The four typed EffectEvidence constructors validate only that the evidence subject matches value.Candidate, then delegate to generic serialization. They do not validate the typed authority values or enforce canonical member/publication order. A same-package producer can pass a malformed implementationReviewAuthority, integrationCandidateManifest, candidatePublicationSet, or implementationUATReviewBinding literal and persist it through the returned Provenance Effect. This violates the frozen contract that constructors validate typed values before creating authority evidence and lets malformed authority enter the sole store.

## Exact fix
At each typed effect constructor, run the corresponding closed validator before serialization. For manifest/publication values, require the input is already the normalized canonical order (or replace it with the normalized copy only if the API explicitly defines normalization); reject duplicates, empty values, malformed refs/OIDs, invalid states, and zero/invalid bindings before returning the Effect. Add direct constructor tests using malformed same-package literals and assert no Effect is returned; retain real Apply proofs.

## Evidence
newReviewAuthorityEvidenceEffect, newCandidateManifestEvidenceEffect, newCandidatePublicationSetEvidenceEffect, and newImplementationUATReviewBindingEvidenceEffect call only validateEvidenceSubject/newTypedEvidenceEffect. newTypedEvidenceEffect validates subject/result slot and canonical JSON, not the authority DTO.

### R1 [I1] Orchestration: TeamCreate-Opus + idle-supervisor protection
- Phase 7→8 supervisor launch guidance flips from `aura-swarm` to **TeamCreate with Opus supervisor + Opus workers**. Primary edit: specs_data_body_architect_handoff.go (behavior 16-22, Step3 96-103, example 114-176, IMPORTANT 187-195) + epoch skills-table launch note.

### R3 [I3] Interface-first decomposition — Strong SHOULD
- Architect SHOULD default to an interface-first horizontal slice (all public types/signatures) when it unlocks parallel implementation slices, and MUST justify in the IMPL_PLAN when choosing a linear integration-point chain instead. Edit supervisor-plan-tasks/architect decomposition guidance + PROCESS.md.

### R4 [I4] Verbatim capture incl. code shown in option previews
- Extend C-ure-verbatim Then (specs_data.go:469) to require capturing ALL stimuli shown to the user, including any code/interface/snippet rendered inside AskUserQuestion option labels/descriptions or definition blocks.

### R5 [I5] MR template in protocol materials
- Create static skills/protocol/MR_TEMPLATE.md (blank reusable skeleton sourced from improvements.md MR template: Summary / Testing / Screenshots / Related Issues / Changes / Blast Radius / Checklist / Reviewer Notes). EXAMPLE_MR_DESCRIPTION.md already exists.

- Add a **request-type axis** (fix | feature | chore | refactor) to Phase 1 classification (user_request body ~70-74).

All 10 improvements implemented, generated + hand-authored docs in sync, guard tests + `go test -race ./...` green, GitHub issue #5 enriched to self-contained design writeup.

## End-Vision Goals
A self-hosting epoch protocol whose own process improvements (verbatim capture, clean re-review, fix-validation lifecycle, correct teammate topology) are encoded in the schema/skills it generates — eating its own dogfood.

The production Land Apply resolves the current clean review, exact immutable manifest, and complete current publication set, and its CurrentFact/ExactFact conditions do reject stale authority. At internal/tasks/epoch_human_service.go:295-358, the fresh Land path passes only a generic implementation-UAT reference to commit; commitWithAuthority emits candidate state, that generic UAT reference, and generic precondition snapshots, but no typed review-fact, manifest-fact, or publication-set-fact binding. This breaks the ratified consumer contract preserved in aura-plugins-mblbb and adopted by aura-plugins-9fgj7: Land must bind the exact accepted UAT, current clean review, immutable manifest, and complete current publication set in typed evidence emitted by the same Apply, and exact retry must restore those bindings without reselecting current facts. The gate conditions alone do not provide the required typed Land provenance/evidence record.

Add a private, canonical typed Land-authority binding (or equivalent existing typed authority evidence) to the Land effect set, containing the exact UAT binding and the selected review/manifest/publication JournalIDs and candidate/epoch identity. Emit it in the fresh Land Apply after validating the complete membership. Persist the same binding in the operation-local effects and reconstruct it from the committed operation on immediate/reopen retry; do not query newer authority for replay. Extend the focused real-store oracle to require the binding and its producer anchor alongside the existing four condition snapshots, then rerun the required race-enabled gates. description:
Axis-C finding (Elegance/API Completeness).

_PHASE_CONSTRAINTS in context_injection.py has 12 entries (P1_REQUEST through P12_LANDING). PhaseId also has a COMPLETE sentinel value.

get_phase_context() uses:
  constraint_ids = _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS.get(phase, frozenset())

This silently returns empty frozenset for COMPLETE, which is acceptable behavior (COMPLETE is a terminal state with no constraints). However, the pattern is consistent with a silent failure for any missing PhaseId added in the future.

Additionally, _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS is a plain dict[PhaseId, frozenset[str]], not an exhaustive mapping. If a new PhaseId is added to the enum, _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS will not raise any error — it will silently return no constraints.

This is a minor concern because: (1) COMPLETE is a known case that legitimately has no constraints; (2) the .get() fallback is the right behavior for the terminal state.

Suggestion: Add an explicit comment in _PHASE_CONSTRAINTS noting that COMPLETE is intentionally absent (terminal state, no constraints apply). Or add PhaseId.COMPLETE: frozenset() with a comment. This makes the omission deliberate rather than accidental.

description:
Rescoped after the user changed the MVP retention decision.

USER VERBATIM: "Actually: we should just keep all bodies, for all objects. at a later date, we can decide to truncate or filter uninteresting bodies. SQLite is great for the MVP. just put the blob there."

## What the MVP now does, so this epic starts from the right baseline

M1 stores the raw native payload body for EVERY occurrence, content-addressed, in the existing SQLite database. No external store, no selective predicate, no truncation. The occurrence row references a body by digest; identical bodies collapse.

This epic therefore no longer covers "should we store bodies" - that is answered and shipped. It covers what to do once volume makes storing everything untenable.

## Scope

1. TRUNCATION AND FILTERING - the named later lever.
   Decide which bodies are uninteresting and what to do with them. Options to weigh when volume data exists: size-capped truncation with the truncation recorded explicitly (the OpenTelemetry convention - a bound that silently discards is indistinguishable from a bug); age-tiered retention, full body hot for N days then digest-only, which is the APM standard; and predicate-based filtering, where the Sentry pattern of keeping the interesting minority becomes a pruning rule rather than an ingestion rule. Note that pruning is strictly better than the original selective-ingestion design: the decision is made with real data in hand rather than guessed at ingest.

2. EXTERNAL CONTENT-ADDRESSED STORAGE, only if measurement demands it.
   SQLite is genuinely good at this size class - blobs under roughly 100 KiB read faster from SQLite than from individual files, and payloads are bounded at 1 MiB. Move out only when database growth or write volume is demonstrated to hurt, not on principle.
   If moved: use the OCI image-layout blobs/<algorithm>/<hex> - a published spec rather than an invented scheme, inspectable with ordinary tools. Adopt Git's two-hex-character sharding if blob counts grow enough to pressure directories and inodes; OCI layout is flat and that is fine only at low counts. Extract the BlobStore / BlobWriter interface shape from distribution/distribution, the CNCF reference registry, which already solves resumable writes, Stat, Open and verification on commit - take the pattern, not the dependency.
   The crash-ordering hazard applies the moment storage leaves the transaction: write blob, then commit occurrence. An orphan blob is harmless and reclaimable; a dangling reference is corruption. This ordering is already required in the MVP because the blob write is split out of the occurrence commit for lock-hold reasons, so the discipline is in place before the storage moves.

3. GARBAGE COLLECTION AND DELETION.
   A blob is live iff some occurrence references its digest. GC is "delete blobs no occurrence references" - Git reachability GC and the OCI untagged-blob problem, both well understood. Privacy deletion is delete the blob, null the references, keep the occurrence metadata so the ledger stays complete.

4. REDACTION BOUNDARY.
   Structured allow-lists, never deny-lists - Stripe and Datadog both learned that deny-lists always miss a field. Relevant because store-all makes every prompt, tool input and file content persistent by default.

## Already settled, do not relitigate

- github.com/opencontainers/go-digest v1.0.0 is the digest type. Verified in-tree: already an indirect module requirement, `go list -deps` returns nothing outside the standard library, so it is pure Go, cgo-free and adds zero new transitive dependencies. Adoption only promotes it to direct. Supervisor approval granted per the AGENTS.md dependency rule.
- Content addressing stays regardless of backend. With store-all the dedup value increased, not decreased.

## Surveyed and rejected, with reasons

- folbricht/desync (casync, pure Go): chunk-level dedup for large similar files. Payloads are bounded at 1 MiB and usually far smaller, so chunking costs more than it returns.
- go-git storage layer: correct model, pure Go, but a large dependency for blob storage alone. Take the sharding idea, not the module.
- Bazel Remote Execution API CAS: proven at scale but gRPC and distributed; unjustified for a local single-user store.
- restic, Perkeep: sound designs, whole systems rather than embeddable components.

## Trigger

Revisit when database growth or shared-file write volume is measured to affect the start_slice deadline budget (aura-plugins-cvlu6) or backup and sync cost. Not before - the MVP position is deliberate and the data does not exist yet.

# URD — OpenCode compilation target for pasture codegen

Single source of truth. THIS epic = **OpenCode skills + agents only**; Codex AND OpenCode hooks (.mjs) deferred to future epics.

## Requirements
- R1 — **Target abstraction in codegen.** Typed `HarnessName` + `Target` registry + `-targets` flag in `tools/codegen/main.go` (default `claude`, output unchanged). Thread a template-name through `renderSkill`/`renderSubSkill`. Static compile-time registry (mirrors internal/acp/adapter.go); no plugin system. MUST be designed so a future OpenCode-hooks (.mjs) emitter and a future Codex target slot in without rework.
- R2 — **OpenCode skill output.** Emit pasture's 29 skills (5 roles + 24 commands) as OpenCode SKILL.md under a per-harness `.opencode/` dir (NOT shared tree). Reuse name/description frontmatter as-is. Decide pasture: prefix (O-4).
- R3 — **OpenCode agent files.** Per-role `.opencode/agent/<role>.md` (mode/model/permission) from RoleSpec. Pin Tools→permission (O-PERM), opus/sonnet→provider-id (O-MODEL), role→mode (epoch/supervisor/architect=primary, worker/reviewer=subagent).
- R4 — **Committed manifest distribution (pasture's OWN codegen).** Generate + commit `opencode.json` (+ `.opencode/`) so OpenCode users install/discover pasture skills directly. Pin manifest schema from OpenCode source/docs (O-2). Version-sync owned by pasture-release.
- R5 — **Hand-authored skills.** protocol + install-cli — provide OpenCode equivalents (CopyVerbatim, per-harness dirs).

## Hard constraints (user clarifications, verbatim intent)
- NO build-on-top of / dependency on vercel-labs--skills or its `skills` CLI (`npx skills add` OUT). vercel-labs informed the skillgen ARCHITECTURE only.
- NO adoption of oh-my-codex; its reserved names / native-agent model irrelevant.
- NO `.mjs` runtime glue THIS epic — BUT OpenCode hooks (.mjs) for runtime context injection (on phase transitions / specific events) is a ROADMAPPED FUTURE epic, NOT rejected. The Target/OpenCode design MUST leave the door open for it. (The report's O-7/O-9 'no per-session state' rationale is FALSE/superseded — runtime context injection is on the roadmap.)

## Priorities
P1: R1 + R2. P2: R3, R4. P3: R5.

## Design choices
- Per-harness `.opencode/` dir (not shared tree) → CopyVerbatim for hand-authored skills.
- Skills + agents this epic; manifests via pasture codegen + pasture-release.
- The `Target` abstraction is shared infra: the future OpenCode-hooks emitter and the deferred Codex target both reuse it — design for that extensibility now (without building them).

## MVP (definition of done)
`pasture` codegen with `-targets=claude,opencode` emits valid `.opencode/` skills + agent files + `opencode.json` from the typed specs; default `-targets=claude` unchanged; an OpenCode user installs + discovers pasture skills via the committed manifests (no vercel CLI); quality gates green.

## Out of scope (this epic)
- Codex targets (#24, deferred — confirm against a real Codex install when scheduled).
- OpenCode hooks / `.mjs` runtime context injection (ROADMAPPED future epic — design must not preclude it).
- vercel `skills` CLI dependency; oh-my-codex; npm-published plugins.

## End-vision / roadmap (context)
Multi-harness pasture: one typed protocol source → Claude + OpenCode (+ later Codex) skill/agent/manifest outputs from one codegen pipeline, PLUS OpenCode hooks (.mjs) that inject runtime context on phase transitions / events (future).

description:
internal/install/directfile/directfile.go Ensure() and Remove() both call
os.Lstat(dest) to reject a symlink, then separately call identify(dest) which
does a second, independent os.ReadFile(path) + os.Stat(path) by path (not by
the already-open fd/handle). Between the Lstat check and the ReadFile/Stat
calls inside identify(), a local attacker with write access to the same
directory could swap the regular file for a symlink, and identify() would
follow it (os.ReadFile/os.Stat both dereference symlinks).

Actual exploitable impact is low in the normal single-user deployment model
this issue targets (an attacker able to race writes into
~/.config/opencode/... etc. already has the user's own write access to that
directory, so they could achieve most of the same outcome directly), and the
subsequent mutation is still safe (writeLeaf renames onto dest, which does
not follow a symlink; os.Remove unlinks the directory entry, not the symlink
target) — so this is a read-side information-disclosure/DoS-of-correctness
window (arbitrary-file content could be hashed/compared, potentially causing
a spurious "modified leaf" rejection or a spurious external-match accept),
not a write-outside-root vector.

Where: internal/install/directfile/directfile.go identify(), called from
Ensure() (~line 134) and Remove() (~line 206).

Fix (optional hardening): open dest via os.OpenFile(dest, O_RDONLY) once,
os.Lstat is redundant with an fd-based fstat via file.Stat() after opening
with O_NOFOLLOW where available (Go's os package doesn't expose O_NOFOLLOW
portably; alternatively re-Lstat immediately before use and accept the
narrow race, documenting it, since Go's stdlib does not offer an atomic
open-if-not-symlink primitive on all platforms). At minimum, document the
accepted race window in the package doc comment so it isn't mistaken for a
closed threat model.
title: MINOR: identify() TOCTOU window between Lstat symlink-check and read-by-path

description:
WHAT: foldDomainMutation's bounded BUSY/LOCKED retry (dbos_adapter.go isTransientLock/foldDomainMutation, lines ~186-220) is wired ONLY into the DBOSAdapter's own workflow step. borrowedJournal.Apply (dbos_store.go line 383-388) — the SAME public JournalAPI.Apply that any direct caller uses on a borrowed tracker (a fully documented, supported surface: doc.go/dbos_store.go call the As()-based direct-write path the 'standalone convenience surface', and Journal().Apply() is equally public) — passes straight through to the inner bridge connection with ZERO retry and ZERO transient-vs-permanent classification.

WHERE: dbos_store.go borrowedJournal.Apply (delegates unconditionally to j.inner.Apply(in)); the retry machinery lives exclusively in dbos_adapter.go (foldDomainMutation, isTransientLock, isInfrastructureError), private to *DBOSAdapter and unreachable from the tracker/journal layer.

WHEN: reproduced running the review's own verbatim gate command, 'CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -race -count=1 ./...', from a clean nix develop shell, base c3b9fce + 9021fd7:
  --- FAIL: TestMatrix_AbsentConflict_TypedConflict (1.25s)
      dbos_matrix_test.go:128: direct Apply: insert journal row (kind operation): sqlite: step: database is locked
Re-ran 'go test -race -count=3 -run TestMatrix .': failed 2 of 3 iterations, always at a DIRECT tracker.Journal().Apply() call (TestMatrix_AbsentConflict_TypedConflict / TestMatrix_AbsentExact_ReplaySucceeds — both call s.tracker.Journal().Apply(op) directly, bypassing the adapter). The CGO_ENABLED=0 (non-race) run passes because it runs too fast to hit the contention window; -race slows execution enough to expose it deterministically. This is exactly the review charter's named attack surface ('shared-WAL concurrency').

WHY IT HAPPENS: the whole premise of Option-B is that the borrowed bridge and the DBOS system connection share ONE WAL file (dbos_adapter.go's own comment: 'The borrowed bridge and the DBOS system connection share one WAL, so a domain commit can momentarily lose the single-writer lock'). DBOS runs its own background writers on that shared handle (queue_runner dequeue/checkpoint activity, visible in the failing run's log). PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000 (internal/sqlite/db.go) only extends SQLITE_BUSY retries at the C-library level and does not reliably cover SQLITE_LOCKED under this driver/build, which is why the adapter needed its OWN Go-level isTransientLock retry loop in the first place — but that fix was applied only where the adapter itself writes, not where the tracker/journal type it wraps is used directly.

IMPACT: any caller of the borrowed tracker's public JournalAPI.Apply() (not just tests — this is the same public method type documented as directly usable) can receive a raw, non-actionable 'sqlite: step: database is locked' error instead of either (a) succeeding after the same bounded backoff the adapter gets, or (b) a properly wrapped, actionable StoreUnavailableError/typed transient error satisfying C-actionable-errors. This silently degrades the durability promise Option-B exists to provide, and violates C-actionable-errors (raw driver string, no what/why/where/when/impact/fix).

FIX: move the isTransientLock bounded-retry (or an equivalent wrapper) down into borrowedJournal.Apply (and any other borrowedJournal/borrowedTracker method that performs a write against the shared file), so EVERY public write through a borrowed tracker gets the same shared-WAL contention protection the adapter's own step enjoys — not just the one write path DBOSAdapter happens to drive. Add a regression test that calls tracker.Journal().Apply() directly, concurrently with live DBOS background activity, under -race, and asserts it never surfaces a raw sqlite error.
title: BLOCKER: shared-WAL transient-lock retry scoped only to DBOSAdapter step; direct borrowed Journal().Apply() leaks raw unretried sqlite errors under real DBOS WAL contention

## VOTE: ACCEPT

### Axis: B (Test Quality) -- Round 2

### Round 1 Findings Resolution

All three Round 1 blocker/structural findings have been addressed:

1. **BLOCKER (A+B): C-blocker-dual-parent kwarg mismatch** -- FIXED. The YAML now uses `slice_id: "slice-1"` which matches the method signature `check_blocker_dual_parent(self, blocker_task_id: str, severity_group_id: str, slice_id: str)`. Verified against constraints.py line 782-786.

2. **Structural (C): _coerce_violation_args removed** -- ADDRESSED. The proposal now has a single coercion point: `phase` string to `PhaseId` enum (needed only for C-supervisor-cartographers). All other types (bool, int, str, list) pass through YAML natively. This is minimal and correct.

3. **Structural (C): _factory removed** -- ADDRESSED. The proposal extends violation_state YAML with an optional `transition_history` list. The fixture_loader builds TransitionRecord objects from the YAML entries, then populates state.transition_history post-construction (EpochState is mutable, not frozen). No _factory, no special dispatch path.

### Three-Way Dispatch Verification

The proposed dispatch logic in test_protocol_combinatorial.py:

```python
if tc.violation_state is not None:
    violations = _CHECKER.check_state(tc.violation_state)
elif tc.violation_method is not None:
    method = getattr(_CHECKER, tc.violation_method)
    violations = method(**tc.violation_args)
else:
    assert tc.violation_from_phase is not None
    violations = _CHECKER.check_handoff_required(...)
```

This three-way dispatch is complete and correct:
- **Branch 1 (violation_state):** Covers existing 4 state-based constraints (C-review-consensus, C-severity-not-plan, C-severity-eager, C-worker-gates) plus the 2 newly-extended audit constraints (C-audit-never-delete, C-audit-dep-chain). Total: 6.
- **Branch 2 (violation_method):** Covers the new method-based constraints. Total: 19 as listed, but see important observation below.
- **Branch 3 (fallthrough):** Covers C-handoff-skill-invocation (transition-based). Total: 1.
- **Safety net:** The `assert tc.violation_from_phase is not None` in branch 3 ensures that if a case reaches the fallthrough without the expected fields, the test fails explicitly rather than silently.

### Violation Args Correctness Audit (All 19 Method-Based)

I verified every proposed violation_args against the actual check method signature AND the method's violation-triggering logic. All 19 method-based entries will correctly trigger violations:

| Constraint | Method | Args | Triggers Because |
|---|---|---|---|
| C-review-binary | check_review_binary | vote: "MAYBE" | "MAYBE" not in VoteType values |
| C-dep-direction | check_dep_direction | parent_id: "", child_id: "child-abc" | empty parent_id (line 490) |
| C-blocker-dual-parent | check_blocker_dual_parent | blocker_task_id: "leaf-1", severity_group_id: "", slice_id: "slice-1" | empty severity_group_id (line 801) -- FIXED from R1 |
| C-followup-timing | check_followup_timing | has_important_or_minor: true, followup_created: false | findings exist, no followup |
| C-vertical-slices | check_vertical_slices | production_code_path: "src/module.py", owner_ids: ["worker-1", "worker-2"] | 2 owners (>1) |
| C-supervisor-no-impl | check_supervisor_no_impl | role: "supervisor", action_type: "file_edit" | supervisor + impl action |
| C-supervisor-cartographers | check_supervisor_cartographers | phase: "p8" (coerced to PhaseId), has_explore_team: false | at p8 without team |
| C-integration-points | check_integration_points | has_integration_points: false | no integration points |
| C-slice-review-before-close | check_slice_review_before_close | slice_closed_by_worker: true, review_completed: false | closed without review |
| C-max-review-cycles | check_max_review_cycles | review_cycle_count: 4 | exceeds max of 3 |
| C-slice-leaf-tasks | check_slice_has_leaf_tasks | slice_id: "slice-1", leaf_task_ids: [] | empty leaf tasks |
| C-ure-verbatim | check_ure_verbatim | question: "Q?", options: [], response: "A" | empty options |
| C-frontmatter-refs | check_frontmatter_refs | task_description: "No frontmatter here", required_ref_keys: ["urd"] | no --- frontmatter |
| C-followup-leaf-adoption | check_followup_leaf_adoption | leaf_task_id: "leaf-1", severity_group_id: "", followup_slice_id: "fs-1" | empty severity_group_id |
| C-worker-gates | check_worker_gates | has_todos: true, tests_pass: false, typecheck_pass: false | gates not met |
| C-agent-commit | check_agent_commit | commit_command: "git commit -m 'feat: something'" | "git commit" without "agent-" |
| C-proposal-naming | check_proposal_naming | title: "SLICE-1: Bad proposal title" | no PROPOSAL-N: prefix |
| C-review-naming | check_review_naming | title: "PROPOSAL-1: Wrong type for review" | no SCOPE-REVIEW-axis-round pattern |
| C-followup-lifecycle | check_followup_lifecycle | followup_task_title: "URE: Missing FOLLOWUP prefix" | no FOLLOWUP_ prefix |

All 19 will produce non-empty violation lists. None will accidentally pass.

### Audit Constraint Extension (transition_history)

The violation_state extension for C-audit-never-delete and C-audit-dep-chain is correct:

- **C-audit-never-delete:** EpochState at p2 with empty transition_history. check_audit_trail (line 664-668) fires because `current_phase != P1_REQUEST and not state.transition_history`. Correct.
- **C-audit-dep-chain:** EpochState at p2 with one TransitionRecord where `triggered_by: ""`. check_audit_trail (line 686) fires because `not record.triggered_by` (empty string is falsy). Correct.
- **TransitionRecord construction:** The proposal correctly creates TransitionRecord(from_phase=PhaseId(...), to_phase=PhaseId(...), triggered_by=..., condition_met=..., timestamp=datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)). The `success` field defaults to True, which is fine.
- **EpochState mutability:** `state.transition_history.extend(transition_history)` works because EpochState is a regular dataclass (not frozen). Verified at state_machine.py line 36.

These 2 constraints will NOT break existing state-based tests because they route through the same `check_state()` -> `check_audit_trail()` aggregation path. The only change is that the YAML now provides the transition_history data that was previously missing.

### Test Isolation (start_local)

Each of the 4 Temporal sandbox tests creates its own `WorkflowEnvironment.start_local()` context manager. This provides full isolation -- each test gets its own ephemeral server with registered search attributes. No shared state between tests.

The `_temporal_sandbox_works()` probe also switches to `start_local()`, ensuring the probe accurately reflects whether the actual test infrastructure works.

The 1-second real sleep in test_submit_vote_signal_delivery_e2e is acceptable per URD R1.

### Important Observation (Non-Blocking)

**C-worker-gates YAML duplication risk.** The proposal lists C-worker-gates among the "15 constraints -- use check_structural as violation_method" entries. However, C-worker-gates already exists as one of the 5 runnable state-based entries (violation_state at p10 with blocker_count=1). In YAML, duplicate mapping keys silently override (last wins). If both entries appear in the final protocol.yaml, the method-based entry would silently overwrite the state-based entry, losing the `check_state()` aggregation test for C-worker-gates.

The implementer should either:
(a) Remove C-worker-gates from the violation_method list (reducing to 14 structural + 4 naming = 18 method-based), or
(b) Keep both by giving the method-based entry a different key (e.g., "C-worker-gates-method") -- though this would need fixture_loader awareness.

Option (a) is simpler and preserves the checklist math: 5 existing runnable + 18 method-based + 2 extended state-based = 25 runnable, 1 skipped. The prose count of "15 structural" should be "14 structural." The validation checklist item "20 formerly-skipped constraint tests pass via violation_method dispatch" should read "18 via violation_method + 2 via violation_state = 20 total."

This is not REVISE-worthy because:
1. The implementer will naturally discover this when writing the YAML (duplicate key is a common YAML pitfall)
2. The test count assertion `test_constraint_cases_have_five_runnable` (currently asserts 5) will be updated to 25, and the total constraint count (26 via CONSTRAINT_SPECS) will flag any missing entries
3. The worst case (silent overwrite) still results in a passing test -- it just tests via method dispatch instead of state dispatch

I note this as an implementation-time correction, not a design-level blocker.

### Minor Notes

1. **Import gap:** The fixture_loader extension code references `TransitionRecord` and `datetime`/`timezone` which are not currently imported. The implementer needs to add `from datetime import datetime, timezone` and update `from aura_protocol.state_machine import EpochState, TransitionRecord`. Standard implementation detail.

2. **violation_args default to {}:** If YAML has violation_method but no violation_args, `dict(entry.get("violation_args", {}))` produces `{}`, and `method(**{})` would raise TypeError for methods requiring arguments. This is a YAML authoring error, not a framework bug. All 19 entries specify violation_args. Acceptable.

### End-User Alignment

1. **End-users:** Developers running the test suite.
2. **What they want:** All testable constraints exercised; clear output when constraint logic breaks.
3. **Impact:** 24 formerly-skipped tests become passing (not 25 -- C-actionable-errors remains). Honest coverage replaces false confidence.
4. **Implementation gaps:** C-worker-gates duplication risk noted above (non-blocking).
5. **MVP scope:** Appropriate -- all check methods already exist, this is plumbing only.
6. **Validation checklist:** Complete and verifiable. The count items are slightly imprecise (20 via violation_method should be 18 via violation_method + 2 via violation_state) but the totals are correct (25 runnable, 1 skipped).

### Verdict

**VOTE: ACCEPT** -- All Round 1 findings addressed. The three-way dispatch is complete, all violation_args correctly trigger violations, the transition_history extension is sound, and test isolation with start_local() is properly designed. ## Requirements

### R1: Machine-Executable 12-Phase Protocol (v1 MVP)
Extend validate_schema.py to enforce workflow state transitions. Add a state machine (Python, Temporal SDK) that validates phase ordering, review consensus gates, and dependency chain integrity. Temporal provides durability, audit trail, and search attributes for forensic queryability.

### R2: Schema.xml Runtime Context Injection (v2)
Parse schema.xml at agent startup and inject the relevant phase/role/constraint context into the agent's prompt. Single source of truth — eliminates SKILL.md drift. Constraints checked at injection time.

### R3: Full Temporal Workflow Engine (v3)
Implement the 12-phase protocol as Temporal workflows. Phases become workflows, handoffs become signals, constraints become activity guards. Agents orchestrated by Temporal rather than reading SKILL.md.

### R4: Hybrid Schema Strategy
- Core: Typed enums (Python newtype pattern) for universal fields (session_id, model_id, role, phase)
- Deltas: Per-harness extension modules for harness-specific transcript fields
- Feature guards: Cross-cutting constraints verified by SAT solver (z3 or python-sat)
- Matches unified-schema's existing BCNF approach but extends it for the aura protocol dimensions

### R5: A2A/MCP Type Compliance
- Adopt A2A Part discriminated union (TextPart/FilePart/DataPart) for content representation
- Adopt MCP ToolUseContent/ToolResultContent for tool call representation
- Adopt A2A TaskState enum as superset of all protocol lifecycle states
- Extend with: reasoning field (ACP TrajectoryMetadata), source field (harness+model), tool/system roles
- Use models.dev {provider_id}/{model_id} for stable model identifiers

### R6: Integration Interfaces (End Vision)
Define interfaces that bridge:
- aura-plugins (protocol definition + constraint enforcement)
- unified-schema (transcript ingestion + analytics — NOT modified by us)
- agentfilter (security filtering — NOT modified by us)
- nix-openclaw-vm (Temporal runtime — eventual execution backend)

### R7: Python-Only in aura-plugins
All code in aura-plugins must be Python. Temporal Python SDK for workflow engine. No Go in this repo (Go lives in unified-schema and nix-openclaw-vm).

### R8: Beads Coordination (Transitional)
Beads (bd CLI) remains the inter-agent task coordination mechanism for now. Eventually superseded by our own solution using the APIs we develop. The orchestration layer must integrate with beads, not replace it prematurely.

## Priorities (User-Stated)
1. v1 MVP: Constraint validator + state machine with Temporal (Python SDK)
2. Cross-project integration interfaces (define, don't implement outside aura-plugins)
3. A2A/MCP type compliance for future interop
4. Hybrid schema for variant-rich harness support

## Design Choices (From Elicitation)
- Temporal throughout all versions (Python SDK)
- unified-schema team owns SessionEntry DB schema (we don't modify)
- Hybrid schema: typed enums (core) + deltas (harness-specific) + feature guards (cross-cutting)
- Beads is transitional; Temporal audit trail is the long-term solution

## MVP Goals (v1)
1. Python state machine that models the 12-phase aura protocol transitions
2. Temporal workflow that wraps the state machine with durable execution
3. Constraint validators (extending validate_schema.py) that check runtime state
4. Search attributes on Temporal for forensic queries (phase, role, agent, status)
5. Integration interface definitions (Python protocols/ABCs) for unified-schema and agentfilter

## End-Vision Goals
Completely auditable agent workflow engine for open-source development:
- Agents orchestrated by Temporal workflows with durable state
- schema.xml as single source of truth — runtime context injected, not read from SKILL.md
- Cross-project integration: protocol enforcement (aura-plugins) + ingestion (unified-schema) + security (agentfilter) + execution (Temporal)
- Open contribution: the orchestration APIs become the "Application Document Interface" for agent-native development
- Audit trail: every phase transition, constraint check, handoff, and review decision is recorded in Temporal event history with search attributes

description:
Axis: SLICE-1.2N-REVIEW-C-1 (Migration/API coherence). Files:
internal/journal/operations.go, internal/sqlite/operations.go.

WHAT: journal.CommittedResultKind declares a closed 3-variant enum
(CommittedAbsent/CommittedExact/CommittedConflict) and CommittedResult carries a
`Conflict *OperationConflict` field; journal.OperationConflict{OperationID, Field}
implements the `error` interface (has an Error() string method). This shape
strongly signals a typed, errors.As-extractable conflict result, matching the
repo's established named-field actionable-error convention cited at §13.1
(StoreUnavailableError/CheckpointDivergenceError).

In practice, internal/sqlite/operations.go Apply() signals the §9.4/§11
OperationID-reuse conflict *only* via a wrapped sentinel:

    conflict := &journal.OperationConflict{OperationID: in.OperationID, Field: field}
    txErr = fmt.Errorf(\"%w: %s\", journal.ErrOperationConflict, conflict.Error())
    return journal.CommittedResult{}, txErr

`conflict` itself is never wrapped (no second %w) — only its stringified
`.Error()` text is appended after the sentinel. The returned CommittedResult is
the zero value (Kind == CommittedAbsent, Conflict == nil) on *every* Apply error
path (genesis violation, actor mismatch, authority-scope violation, etc.), not
just the conflict path — Kind is never meaningfully CommittedConflict anywhere
in the codebase (grep confirms CommittedConflict is referenced only in its own
declaration/String()/re-export, never assigned to a CommittedResult.Kind field).

WHY: This happened because Apply signals failures via Go `error` uniformly, but
the CommittedResult sum type and OperationConflict's Error() method were
designed for the LookupCommitted-style \"closed variant, total function\" pattern
from the (superseded) historical #5 body. The two designs were partially melded:
the enum/struct scaffolding was kept but never wired into Apply's actual
error-reporting path.

WHERE: internal/sqlite/operations.go:271-276 (the conflict branch in Apply);
internal/journal/operations.go:251-263 (CommittedResultKind), :292-301
(CommittedResult.Conflict), :303-320 (OperationConflict).

WHEN: Confirmed via the only test that exercises this path,
TestApplyRejectsOperationIDReuseWithDifferentIdentity
(journal_operations_corpus_test.go:905-935), which asserts only
`errors.Is(err, ErrOperationConflict)` — never `errors.As(err, &conflict)` and
never inspects `res.Kind`/`res.Conflict`. No test anywhere in the diff
constructs or checks a CommittedResult with Kind == CommittedConflict.

IMPACT: A caller written against the documented \"typed conflict\" contract
(errors.As(err, &conflict) to recover {OperationID, Field}, or switching on
res.Kind) will silently fail to extract structured conflict data — errors.As
returns false, and res.Kind reads CommittedAbsent (a semantically wrong signal:
CommittedAbsent is documented as \"never-applied operation\", but here it's
returned for arbitrary Apply failures including genesis/authority-scope/actor
violations, not just conflict or absence). This will surface as a real bug for
the first S1.3/S3 consumer that builds an actionable error message from the
conflict's Field/OperationID, since the only way to get them today is
string-parsing conflict.Error()'s prose.

FIX (either is acceptable, pick one and make Apply/CommittedResult consistent):
  (a) Make the conflict errors.As-extractable: wrap the *OperationConflict value
      itself, e.g. `txErr = fmt.Errorf(\"%w: %w\", journal.ErrOperationConflict, conflict)`
      (Go 1.20+ supports multiple %w verbs) instead of stringifying it. Add a
      test that does `var conflict *journal.OperationConflict; errors.As(err, &conflict)`
      and asserts .OperationID/.Field.
  (b) If Apply is intended to return conflicts via the CommittedResult sum type
      instead of `error` (matching LookupCommitted's total-function style),
      change Apply's conflict branch to return
      `(CommittedResult{Kind: CommittedConflict, Conflict: conflict}, nil)` and
      update TestApplyRejectsOperationIDReuseWithDifferentIdentity plus any
      other conflict-path callers/docs accordingly.
Whichever is chosen, remove the dead alternative (either the CommittedConflict
enum value + Conflict field, or the unused wrapping/errors.As expectation) so
the type doesn't advertise a shape the code never produces.
title: IMPORTANT: Apply's OperationID-conflict path is unreachable through CommittedResult/errors.As — CommittedConflict and OperationConflict fields are dead code

## Evidence
File: internal/tasks/epoch_human_service_test.go:79-96. The only Plan UAT flow records one accepted decision and immediately ratifies it after one seeded accepted review. There is no accepted -> changes_requested/deferred -> Ratify(old accepted) regression.

## Why this blocks acceptance
The independent Axis-A review already found the live production defect at internal/tasks/epoch_human_service.go:210-216 and :678-688: Ratify conditions only on the `DecisionPlanUATAccepted` kind, so a later changes-requested or AFK-deferred Plan UAT does not make the older accepted fact non-current. The current green flow therefore cannot detect that shipping behavior: it can close a proposal using stale acceptance. This is a required representative lifecycle proof, not the exhaustive matrix delegated to aura-plugins-8cus8.

Add a real file-backed production-service regression that records accepted Plan UAT A, then records changes_requested (and/or deferred_by_afk) B for the same proposal, then calls RatifyPlan referencing A. Assert the typed condition/eligibility rejection and a complete zero-write delta for decision, evidence, activity, event, operation, and task status. Keep the exact current-family implementation fix tracked by the Axis-A finding aura-plugins-6m3br; this test must remain as the regression oracle.

# Reviewer A: Correctness and end-user alignment

## Preserved contracts
Proposal 56 preserves the user-approved generic `pasture task` and lifecycle `pasture epoch` baseline, explicit registered-human decisions, first-class ratify and land, assignment-controlled review/slice/integration operations, the existing Provenance graph/journal/Apply backbone, a separate benchmark provenance profile, and version-bounded native Claude/Codex/OpenCode hook boundaries. The Reviewer B additions generally tighten Slice 5 through production-binary, real-store, mutation, replay/race, and authentic-loader tests without changing those product contracts.

## Correctness blocker
Section 14.3 and AC-12 require every user gate to reject a `wrong registered human (registered but not eligible for the asserted gate context)`. This is not defined by the approved authority contract. Sections 6.1 and 9 say an explicit `--actor` is valid when it identifies a registered human, and the proposal intentionally removes protected epoch-root UserActorID, membership, defaults, and prior-decision attribution as authority. The `EpochService` user-gate inputs carry no participant/eligibility reference, and current Pasture/Provenance code supplies no alternate eligibility source. The proposed negative case therefore either invents an unapproved hidden human-eligibility policy or cannot have a deterministic oracle.

Actionable revision: align the matrix with the approved explicit-registered-human contract by testing missing, unknown, ML, software, and system actors as failures and a different valid registered human as an exact-attribution success; alternatively, define the typed persisted source that makes one registered human eligible and another ineligible and submit that new authority rule to Plan UAT. Do not reintroduce implicit owner, assignment, default, protected membership, or prior-decision actor fallback.

## Vote
VOTE: REVISE - The architecture and scope preservation are otherwise correct, but the executable authority contract must not add an undefined registered-human eligibility rule.

__init__.py exports types.PhaseResult (via 'from aura_protocol.types import ...').
workflow.py's PhaseResult is accessed as aura_protocol.workflow.PhaseResult.
tests import from aura_protocol.workflow.

This creates a maintenance hazard: a future developer doing
'from aura_protocol import PhaseResult' gets a different class than
the one ReviewPhaseWorkflow.run() actually returns.

Fix: rename workflow.py's PhaseResult to ReviewPhaseResult (or ReviewResult)
to make the distinction clear and eliminate the name shadow.

## What
StartReview computes a CurrentFact/absence condition for the subject review authority, but allocateReviewBatch receives it as an ignored `_ []provenance.Condition` parameter and never serializes it into the composed batch request.

## Why
The current-round check is only a check-then-act read. Two different OperationIDs can both observe an absent or finalized round and both commit a new 4/13-child review batch; a finalization/restart race has the same gap.

## Where
internal/tasks/epoch_review_commands.go:305-321 computes the condition; internal/tasks/epoch_review_commands.go:343-375 discards it before RunAllocateComposedBatch.

## When
Whenever concurrent StartReview calls or a StartReview call races a current-round transition.

## Impact
The production path can persist duplicate current review-round authorities and duplicate reviewed-task children, so one subject no longer has a unique authoritative review round and later submissions/finalization can target the wrong batch.

## Fix
Extend the trusted composed-allocation contract/reducer with an immutable Conditions field evaluated in the same transaction snapshot (or an equivalent atomic current-round gate), pass the computed condition through allocateReviewBatch, and add a barrier-synchronized StartReview race test proving one winner, one typed conflict, and zero loser task/evidence/event/activity/audit writes.
title: BLOCKER: StartReview drops its current-round conditions

description:
inventory.Load (internal/install/inventory/inventory.go) checks the state file
is a regular file (Lstat + IsRegular) before reading, but never inspects or
enforces the file's permission bits. fsatomic.WriteFile always writes at
0o600 (inventory/codec.go writeState), so a freshly Pasture-created state file
is 0600, but Load places no requirement on pre-existing files.

Reproduced with a scratch test (removed after verification, not committed):
wrote a valid pasture.install.state/v1 document to a temp path at mode 0644
(simulating a file from an older Pasture version before this mode was
introduced, a manual edit, or an external tool touching it), then called
inventory.Load — it succeeded silently (err=nil) and the file's mode remained
0644 afterward. Load neither rejects the weak mode nor repairs it to 0600.

This partially undercuts the confidentiality intent documented at
internal/install/inventory/inventory.go:9 ("The file is written with a
mode-0600 symlink-safe atomic replace") — the write-time guarantee is real,
but nothing re-establishes it on read for a file Pasture did not just write,
so the invariant "the confirmed-state file is 0600" does not actually hold
for the whole file's lifetime, only immediately after Pasture's own writes.

Where: internal/install/inventory/inventory.go Load().

Fix: either (a) reject a state file whose Perm() != 0600 with the same
actionable-Fault shape as the existing regular-file check ("mode-0600 or
absent"), or (b) repair it in place (chmod 0600) before proceeding to read,
whichever matches the intended trust model. Add a test asserting the chosen
behavior for a pre-existing 0644 state file (currently untested either way).
title: IMPORTANT: confirmed-state file mode-0600 not enforced or repaired on read

# PROPOSAL-1: aurad + aura-msg Full Implementation

## Problem Space

**Axes:** CLI ergonomics (nested subcommands), configuration layering (YAML+env+CLI), durable state (SQLite+Temporal SA), workflow execution (signal-driven slices), observability (Claude Code hooks)

**Has-a relationships:**
- `aura-msg` HAS-A TemporalClient, ConfigLoader, OutputFormatter
- `aurad` HAS-A AuditTrail (pluggable), Worker, ConfigLoader
- `SliceWorkflow` HAS-A execution mode (shell + signal-driven + heartbeat)
- Plugin HAS-A hooks.json for Claude Code session integration

**Is-a relationships:**
- `SqliteAuditTrail` IS-A AuditTrail (Protocol)
- `DualWriteAuditTrail` IS-A AuditTrail (composes SQLite + Temporal SA)
- `InMemoryAuditTrail` IS-A AuditTrail (existing)

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Options | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|---------|--------|-----------|
| Subcommand style | flat (`query-state`) vs nested (`query state`) | Nested | Natural grouping, extensible (e.g. `query transitions` later) |
| Config format | TOML vs YAML | YAML | User preference, consistent with other aura tooling |
| Config files | separate vs single | Single `aurad.config.yaml` | Avoids connection setting duplication |
| AuditTrail storage | SQLite-only vs Temporal-SA-only vs dual | Dual-write | SQLite for rich queries, SA for forensic Temporal UI lookup |
| SliceWorkflow execution | stub vs shell-only vs signal-driven | All three combined | Shell command via activity, signal-driven lifecycle, timeout+heartbeat |
| Output format | JSON-only vs text-only vs --format flag | `--format json\|text` | Hooks use JSON, humans use text |

### 4. `scripts/aura_protocol/dual_audit.py` — Dual-Write AuditTrail

```python
class DualWriteAuditTrail:
    """Composes SqliteAuditTrail + Temporal search attribute upserts.

    record_event() writes to SQLite AND upserts Temporal SA in parallel.
    query_events() reads from SQLite only (richer query capability).
    """

    def __init__(self, sqlite_trail: SqliteAuditTrail):
        self._sqlite = sqlite_trail

    async def record_event(self, event: AuditEvent) -> None:
        await self._sqlite.record_event(event)
        # SA upsert happens in the workflow context, not here
        # (activities cannot call workflow.upsert_search_attributes)

    async def query_events(self, **kwargs) -> list[AuditEvent]:
        return await self._sqlite.query_events(**kwargs)
```

Note: Temporal SA upserts happen in workflow code after activity returns, not inside the activity. DualWriteAuditTrail manages the SQLite side; the workflow manages SA upserts. This respects the Temporal determinism boundary.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SliceExecutionConfig:
    """Configuration for how a slice should execute."""
    command: str | None = None        # Shell command to run (None = signal-only)
    timeout_seconds: int = 3600       # Max execution time (default 1h)
    heartbeat_interval_seconds: int = 60  # Heartbeat every 60s

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SliceInput:
    epoch_id: str
    slice_id: str
    phase_spec: str
    parent_workflow_id: str
    execution_config: SliceExecutionConfig = field(
        default_factory=SliceExecutionConfig
    )

# New signals for SliceWorkflow:
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SliceStartSignal:
    """External signal to begin slice execution."""
    command_override: str | None = None  # Override execution_config.command

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SliceCompleteSignal:
    """External signal that slice work is done."""
    success: bool
    output: str = ""
    error: str | None = None

# New activity for shell execution:
@activity.defn
async def execute_slice_command(
    command: str, slice_id: str, epoch_id: str
) -> SliceResult:
    """Run a shell command for a slice. Reports heartbeat periodically."""
    ...

@workflow.defn
class SliceWorkflow:
    """Revised: supports shell execution, signal-driven lifecycle, timeout+heartbeat."""

    @workflow.run
    async def run(self, input: SliceInput) -> SliceResult:
        if input.execution_config.command:
            # Shell execution mode: run command via activity with heartbeat
            return await workflow.execute_activity(
                execute_slice_command,
                args=[input.execution_config.command, input.slice_id, input.epoch_id],
                start_to_close_timeout=timedelta(seconds=input.execution_config.timeout_seconds),
                heartbeat_timeout=timedelta(seconds=input.execution_config.heartbeat_interval_seconds * 2),
            )
        else:
            # Signal-driven mode: wait for external complete signal
            await workflow.wait_condition(
                lambda: self._complete_signal is not None,
                timeout=timedelta(seconds=input.execution_config.timeout_seconds),
            )
            ...

    @workflow.signal
    def start_execution(self, signal: SliceStartSignal) -> None: ...

    @workflow.signal
    def complete_execution(self, signal: SliceCompleteSignal) -> None: ...

    @workflow.signal
    def slice_progress(self, signal: SliceProgressSignal) -> None: ...

## BDD Acceptance Criteria

**Given** `aura-msg query state --epoch-id E1 --format json` **When** epoch E1 is running **Then** stdout contains JSON with `current_phase`, `current_role`, `available_transitions` **Should Not** output to stderr on success

**Given** `aura-msg epoch start --epoch-id E1 --description "test"` **When** Temporal server is running **Then** exit 0, stdout contains `{"workflow_id": "E1", "run_id": "..."}` **Should Not** leave orphan workflows on failure

**Given** `aura-msg signal vote --axis correctness --vote accept` **When** `--epoch-id` is missing **Then** exit 1 with usage error to stderr **Should Not** connect to Temporal for validation errors

**Given** YAML config with `aura-msg.server_address: "remote:7233"` **When** no CLI `--server-address` and no `TEMPORAL_ADDRESS` env **Then** connect to `remote:7233` **Should Not** fall back to `localhost:7233`

**Given** `aurad --audit-trail sqlite` **When** worker starts **Then** SQLite DB created at XDG path, events persisted across restarts **Should Not** lose events on `aurad` restart

**Given** SliceWorkflow with `timeout_seconds=60` **When** no completion signal within 60s **Then** workflow times out and returns `SliceResult(success=False, error="timeout")` **Should Not** hang indefinitely

**Given** SliceWorkflow with `command="python run_slice.py"` **When** command exits 0 **Then** `SliceResult(success=True, output=stdout)` **Should Not** suppress stderr

**Given** Claude Code session with `AURA_EPOCH_ID=E1` **When** SessionStart hook fires **Then** hook queries epoch state and outputs context **Should Not** fail if aurad is not running (graceful degradation)

## Decision Log

D1: Nested subcommands (`query state`) over flat (`query-state`) — extensible, natural grouping
D2: YAML config over TOML — user preference
D3: Single config file `aurad.config.yaml` with sections — avoids duplication
D4: Dual-write AuditTrail — SQLite for queries, Temporal SA for forensic UI
D5: SA upserts in workflow code, not in activity — respects Temporal determinism boundary
D6: SliceWorkflow combines shell+signal+heartbeat — all three selected by user
D7: `--format json|text` with json default — hooks parse JSON, humans use text
D8: Exit codes 0/1/2/3 — structured error classification for hook branching
D9: pyyaml + aiosqlite as new deps — minimal, well-maintained, no heavy frameworks
D10: Hook graceful degradation — session-register.sh must not fail if aurad is down

### AC1: Schema Parser Bootstrap
**Given** schema.xml (1,314 lines) **when** parse_schema() is called **then** returns SchemaSpec with 12 phases, 5 roles, 35 commands, 23 constraints, 6 handoffs, 21 labels, 3 review axes **should not** silently skip entities or lose attributes

### AC1a: Schema Parser Error Paths
**Given** malformed XML (truncated, missing <phases>, missing required attributes) **when** parse_schema() is called **then** raises SchemaParseError with descriptive message **should not** return partial SchemaSpec or silently succeed

### AC2: Python as Source of Truth
**Given** types.py with expanded specs **when** gen_schema.py runs **then** produces schema.xml that passes validate_schema.py with 0 errors **should not** require manual XML editing

### AC3: Round-Trip Consistency (Field-Level)
**Given** Python types.py **when** generating schema.xml then parsing it back **then** every entity matches field-by-field: ConstraintSpec.given/when/then/should_not, HandoffSpec.required_fields, SubstepSpec.startup_sequence, etc. **should not** pass on count-only match with truncated fields

### AC4: SKILL.md Generation with Markers
**Given** a role SKILL.md with markers and hand-written body **when** gen_skills.py runs **then** header between markers is updated, body is preserved **should not** overwrite hand-written content

### AC4a: SKILL.md Marker Edge Cases
**Given** a SKILL.md with missing END marker **when** gen_skills.py runs **then** raises MarkerError. **Given** a new file with no markers **when** gen_skills.py runs **then** generates full content. **Given** reversed markers **when** gen_skills.py runs **then** raises MarkerError. **Should not** silently discard manual body on any boundary error.

### AC5: Role Context Injection
**Given** role=SUPERVISOR **when** get_role_context is called **then** returns phases p7-p12, relevant constraints (C-supervisor-no-impl, C-supervisor-explore-team, etc.), supervisor commands, and handoff specs **should not** include constraints for unrelated roles

**Given** role=SUPERVISOR **when** get_role_context is called **then** does NOT include C-worker-gates in constraints. **Given** role=WORKER **then** does NOT include C-supervisor-no-impl. **Should not** return the entire CONSTRAINT_SPECS dict.

**Given** phase=P10_CODE_REVIEW **when** get_phase_context is called **then** returns C-severity-eager, C-review-consensus, C-blocker-dual-parent, review axis specs, severity labels **should not** include constraints for unrelated phases

**Given** phase=P4_REVIEW **when** get_phase_context is called **then** does NOT include C-severity-eager (code review only). **Given** phase=P9_SLICE **then** does NOT include C-review-consensus. **Should not** return all constraints regardless of phase.

### AC7: No Regressions
**Given** expanded types.py and new modules **when** running full test suite **then** all 554 existing tests pass **should not** break state_machine, constraints, workflow, or interfaces

### AC8: Jinja2 Template Quality (Parametrized)
**Given** each of 4 role templates (architect, supervisor, worker, reviewer) **when** rendered with StrictUndefined using real Python specs **then** produces valid markdown with no undefined variable errors **should not** fail for any role

### AC9: Expanded Type Coverage
**Given** all new spec types and canonical dicts **when** tested **then** enum coverage 100%, ROLE_SPECS has 5 entries, COMMAND_SPECS has 35, LABEL_SPECS has 21, REVIEW_AXIS_SPECS has 3, and test_schema_types_sync.py validates all new dicts against schema.xml **should not** have untested dicts

## Questions and Responses

### Round 1: Exploration Model
Q: For codebase exploration, the supervisor currently delegates to 3 standing Cartographer teammates. With cartographers removed, how should the supervisor gather codebase context?
Options:
- Ephemeral Explore subagents (Recommended): Supervisor spawns short-lived Explore subagents (via Agent tool, subagent_type=Explore) per query. No standing team. Each query gets a fresh agent that returns findings and exits. Supervisor stays lean.
- Single standing Explore teammate: One persistent teammate via TeamCreate with /aura:explore. Supervisor sends scoped queries via SendMessage. Reuses context across queries. Still a standing agent but only 1 instead of 3.
- No exploration agents at all: Supervisor reads the handoff doc and beads tasks only. All codebase exploration is the architect's job (Phase 1/3). Workers explore their own slice scope.
A: Ephemeral Explore subagents (Recommended)

### Round 1: Review Model
Q: For code review (Phase 10), with cartographers removed, how should reviewers be spawned?
Options:
- Ephemeral reviewer subagents (Recommended): Supervisor spawns 3 independent reviewer subagents (via Agent tool) per review round. Same pattern as Phase 4 plan review. Fresh agents each round — no persistence between rounds.
- Reviewer teammates via TeamCreate: Supervisor creates 3 reviewer teammates that persist across review-fix cycles within a wave. Can re-review without respawn. But adds TeamCreate complexity alongside worker teammates.
A: Ephemeral reviewer subagents (Recommended)

### Round 2: Worker Spawning
Q: When should the supervisor use TeamCreate teammates vs Agent tool subagents for workers?
Options:
- Default subagents, teammates only for high-integration (Recommended): Workers are Agent tool subagents by default. Only use TeamCreate teammates when slices have many shared integration points requiring cross-worker coordination via SendMessage. The skill documents this decision criteria.
- Always subagents, never teammates: Workers are always Agent tool subagents. No TeamCreate for workers ever. Simpler but loses ability to coordinate between workers mid-slice.
- Always teammates via TeamCreate: Workers are always TeamCreate teammates. Supervisor coordinates via SendMessage. More control but heavier overhead.
A: Default subagents, teammates only for high-integration (Recommended)

### Round 2: Supervisor Tools
Q: For the supervisor agent definition (agents/supervisor.md), which tools should the supervisor have access to?
Options:
- Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Skill (Recommended): Read-only codebase access for checking worker output + Bash for git operations and bd commands + Skill for invoking sub-skills. NO Edit, Write, NotebookEdit. Delegates exploration to Explore subagents.
- Bash + Skill only: Absolutely minimal — supervisor can only run shell commands (git, bd) and invoke skills. Cannot even read files directly. Forces all file reading through Explore subagents.
- Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Skill + Agent/Task tools: Same as recommended but explicitly listing Agent and Task spawning tools. Note: these may be implicitly available regardless of the tools field.
A: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Skill + Agent/Task tools

### Round 3: User Gates
Q: Which phases should require explicit user approval (gate on user input) vs proceed autonomously?
Options:
- Phase 1 (research depth), Phase 2 (URE), Phase 5 (Plan UAT), Phase 6 (Ratification), Phase 11 (Impl UAT) (Recommended): User gates at: research depth confirmation, URE survey, plan UAT, ratification confirmation, and implementation UAT. Everything else proceeds autonomously — classification, exploration, proposal, plan review, handoff, impl plan, worker slices, code review, landing.
- Phase 2 (URE), Phase 5 (Plan UAT), Phase 11 (Impl UAT) only: Minimal gates — only the three interview rounds. Research depth auto-selected from classification. Ratification auto-proceeds after 3 ACCEPTs.
- Custom selection: You want to specify a different set of user-gated phases.
A: Phase 1 (research depth), Phase 2 (URE), Phase 5 (Plan UAT), Phase 6 (Ratification), Phase 11 (Impl UAT) (Recommended)

### Round 3: Clean Review Definition
Q: For the 'clean review exit' requirement: should IMPORTANT findings also block exit, or only BLOCKERs?
Options:
- No BLOCKERs AND no IMPORTANTs = clean (Recommended): A clean review round means zero BLOCKER and zero IMPORTANT findings from all reviewers. MINOR findings are acceptable. This matches your stated requirement.
- No BLOCKERs only = clean: Only BLOCKERs prevent exit. IMPORTANT findings go to follow-up epic but don't block the wave from ending. Looser definition.
A: No BLOCKERs AND no IMPORTANTs = clean (Recommended)

### Catch-all
Q: Is there anything else about the supervisor rework, autonomous progression, or worker-reviewer loop that the above questions didn't cover?
Options:
- Nothing else: The above covers everything. Proceed to URD and proposal.
- Additional requirements: I have more to add (will type in the text box).
A: Additional requirements — "Proposal should be focused on editting the various skill, markdown, and yaml generator mechanisms so that the new workflow, constraints, and roles are generated. Out-of-date and stale handwritten sections will also need to be identified, re-worked, or removed."

## VOTE: REVISE

### Axis: Elegance (Architectural Quality and Proportionality)

---

### Finding 1: SLICE-E (figures/ directory pipeline) is over-engineered for 2-3 YAML files

**Problem:** SLICE-E proposes 80-120 lines of new code to build a typed YAML loader with Figure dataclass, role_ref filtering, a new __init__.py module, a new output directory pipeline, and a new test file. All of this to host 2-3 YAML files (ride-the-wave ASCII tree, layer cake diagram, bd update frontmatter example).

**Why this matters for elegance:** The innate complexity of "store 2-3 hand-written text blobs and include them in generated output" does not warrant a typed Figure dataclass, a YAML loader module, role_ref filtering, or a separate gen_figures.py pipeline. This is a classic case of premature abstraction -- building infrastructure for a scale that does not yet exist and may never exist.

**Simpler alternative:** Place the content directly as CodeExample instances on appropriate constraints or procedure steps (which is already what SLICE-A does). The CodeExample dataclass already has lang, label, code, and also_illustrates fields -- it can carry ASCII diagrams just fine (lang=text or lang=markdown). If the content truly does not belong on any constraint/step, a simple dict literal in types.py (e.g., `FIGURES: dict[str, str] = {"ride-the-wave": "...", ...}`) with 0 new files and 0 new pipelines would suffice.

**Recommendation:** Merge SLICE-E content into SLICE-A. Use CodeExample for content that attaches to a constraint/step. For any remaining orphan content, use a simple dict in types.py. Eliminate the entire figures/ pipeline. This removes 1 slice, ~100 lines of new code, 2 new directories, and 1 new test file.

---

### Finding 2: 5 slices is excessive for ~200 lines of changes -- merge B+D

**Problem:** The proposal decomposes 15 findings across 5 slices. Slices B, C, and D are each 15-40 lines of changes. SLICE-B (test hardening: 15-20 lines) and SLICE-D (template + XML improvements: 30-40 lines) are both "independent, can start immediately" and both touch test infrastructure and rendering concerns. Together they would be ~50-60 lines -- still a comfortable single slice.

**Why this matters for elegance:** Each slice carries coordination overhead (beads task creation, dependency wiring, handoff, worker assignment, code review). For changes this small (many are 1-3 line fixes), the overhead of 5 separate slices exceeds the cognitive overhead of the changes themselves. The dependency graph already shows B and D are independent -- meaning they have no ordering constraint, and merging them loses nothing.

**Simpler alternative:** Merge SLICE-B and SLICE-D into a single "Test Hardening + Template/XML Improvements" slice. This reduces total slices from 5 to 4 (or 3 if SLICE-E is also merged per Finding 1). The A-depends-on-D.FR12 dependency becomes A-depends-on-BD.FR12, which is equivalent.

**Recommended decomposition (3 slices):**
1. **SLICE-BD:** Test hardening + template/XML improvements (FR4, FR8, FR9, FR10, FR11, FR12, FR13) -- ~50-60 lines
2. **SLICE-A:** CodeExample population + vacuous test fix + remaining figures content (FR1, FR2, FR3, FR14, FR15) -- depends on SLICE-BD for CDATA -- ~60-80 lines
3. **SLICE-C:** DRY refactor + docstring + checklist (FR5, FR6, FR7) -- independent -- ~20-30 lines

Total: 3 slices, ~150-170 lines. Same scope, less coordination overhead.

---

### Finding 3: DRY refactor (FR5) is the right level of abstraction

**Positive observation:** The proposal correctly identifies that gen_skills.py lines 292-318 duplicate exactly the same 4 filter loops that context_injection.py get_role_context() already performs (checklists, coordination_commands, workflows, review_axes). The proposed fix -- call get_role_context() and destructure its fields -- is clean, proportionate, and eliminates real duplication without introducing unnecessary indirection. The function already exists, is already tested, and returns exactly the fields needed.

The only subtlety: get_role_context() returns tuples (immutable) while the current code builds lists. The template does not care -- Jinja2 iterates both. No conversion needed.

---

### Finding 4: SLICE-A dependency on SLICE-D for CDATA is legitimate but weak

**Observation:** The proposal says SLICE-A depends on SLICE-D.FR12 (CDATA wrapping) "for clean XML output." This dependency is technically correct -- adding CodeExample data (SLICE-A) before CDATA wrapping exists (FR12) means the XML output will use XML escaping instead of CDATA. However, this is a cosmetic concern in generated XML, not a functional one. xml.etree.ElementTree handles both correctly; schema_parser.py parses both correctly (as noted in the proposal itself: "CDATA is parsed as text content, so parser changes may be unnecessary").

**Impact:** The dependency is not wrong, but labeling it as a hard dependency overstates the coupling. If SLICE-BD (merged) ships first, great. If SLICE-A ships first without CDATA, the output is still correct -- just less elegant XML. This could be noted as a soft ordering preference rather than a blocking dependency.

---

### Finding 5: FR14 ride-the-wave decision is sound

The proposal's decision to NOT modify the Workflow dataclass to add an examples field, and instead place the ride-the-wave ASCII tree either on a constraint/step or in figures/, is architecturally proportionate. Adding an examples field to Workflow/WorkflowStage for a single ASCII diagram would be over-engineering. The recommendation to defer to figures/ is fine -- but per Finding 1, this content should just go on a BehaviorSpec or ConstraintSpec as a CodeExample instead.

---

### Summary

The proposal is well-researched and the individual FRs are correct. The issues are structural:

1. **SLICE-E is over-engineered** -- the figures/ pipeline is not proportionate to 2-3 text blobs. Merge into SLICE-A using existing CodeExample or a simple dict.
2. **Too many slices** -- 5 slices for ~200 lines creates more coordination overhead than the changes warrant. Consolidate to 3 slices.
3. **DRY refactor is well-targeted** -- no objection.

description:
File: scripts/aura_protocol/workflow.py, lines 82-89 (EpochResult docstring) and line 320 (transition_count assignment)

EpochResult.transition_count is documented as:
    transition_count: total number of phase transitions made

But the value is computed as:
    transition_count=len(self._sm.state.transition_history)

Since SLICE-4 now appends failed TransitionRecord entries to transition_history (with condition_met='FAILED: {error}'), the count includes both successful transitions AND failed attempts. A completed epoch with N phases advanced and K failed attempts will report transition_count = N + K.

This directly contradicts the docstring ('transitions made' implies only successful phase changes), and will produce incorrect totals visible to any caller that reads EpochResult.transition_count.

The test test_full_forward_path_completes verifies len(transition_history) == 12 for the pure state machine, which is correct. But the EpochResult produced by the workflow for the same 12-phase path with any failed signals in between will report >12.

Options:
A) Update the docstring to say 'total number of transition records (including failed attempts)' — honest about what it counts.
B) Compute transition_count as: len([r for r in history if not r.condition_met.startswith('FAILED:')])  — counts only successful transitions.
C) Add a separate failed_transition_count field and keep transition_count for successes only.

Option A is lowest-risk (no behavior change, just document accurately). Option B or C gives callers precise metrics without docstring ambiguity.
title: SLICE-4: EpochResult.transition_count includes failed transition records, contradicting its docstring
