# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-7 — Native Codex distribution from Pasture

Supersedes Proposal 6. The Round 6 correctness and elegance reviews were clean; this revision closes the test-quality findings by classifying every honest partial stage through journaled canonical-byte intents, flattening every cleanup tree to atomic unlink/rmdir entries, and fault-injecting every journal record append/fsync—including PREPARED and recovery checkpoints. URD Amendments 1–7 are normative, with the newest amendment governing conflicts.

## Product boundary

Pasture remains the sole source of truth for protocol implementation, generated skills, generated agent bodies, and their Codex projection. It emits a portable Codex plugin whose 32 skills are complete without native agents. The plugin also carries one verified bundle of five optional native leaf-agent TOMLs. Because Codex plugins do not currently install custom agents, a user explicitly selects exactly one personal agent authority: the Pasture companion CLI or Aura Home Manager.

The feature does not add a Codex backend to `aura-swarm`, mutate Git configuration, install hooks, infer all projects, or claim plugin-native agent registration. Aura remains distribution/operational glue and adds no Python protocol engine.

## 1. Roots, catalog, and structural runtime compiler

Adopt prerequisite `aura-plugins-oj7we`: every codegen operation receives `GenerationRoots{SourceRoot, OutputRoot}`, canonical inputs are read only below SourceRoot, and generated writes are contained below OutputRoot.

Replace `roleSkillDirs`, `commandSkillDirs`, target verbatim inventories, and any new parallel skill-key map with one ordered `SkillDescriptor{Key, Directory, SourceKind, RoleID, CommandID, SupportID}` catalog. It describes the 31 canonical skills; the Codex-only `install-codex-agents` support descriptor is the 32nd output. Paths, runtime invocations, UI inventory, archive inventory, and target metadata project from this catalog. `ProtocolCommandName` and effective `SkillInvocation` are distinct typed values.

Runtime-sensitive prose is structural, never `...any`, global replacement, or a rendered-string reparse:

```go
type RuntimeText struct { parts []RuntimePart }
type RuntimePart interface { runtimePart() }
type Literal struct { Text string }
type Ref struct { Value RuntimeRef }
```

Private closed `RuntimeRef` variants cover activation/self-activation; agent purpose, delivery, lifetime, fan-out, work tier, and context inheritance; initial spawn, follow-up, notification, and barriers; user-input fallback; commit policy; instruction source; prerequisites; and attribution. `RuntimeContext` supplies harness, surface, owner descriptor/role, canonical location, and delivery capability. A coverage sentinel proves every production text owner is visited: constraints, workflows, transitions, procedures, checklists, review axes, fragments, command/role fields, recipes, figures, schema fields, and normative assets. Unknown combinations and forbidden raw operations fail with the six actionable-error fields.

Claude stays byte-identical except separately golden-reviewed intentional install/runtime corrections. OpenCode retains exact path/byte inventory. Codex emits native collaboration syntax and registry-derived `$pasture:<directory>` addresses. Every actionable address in the final archive resolves exactly once.

## 2. Target-owned support assets and complete render graph

Codex `protocol` and `install-cli` are not recursive copies of Claude skills. The dialect-aware emitter owns the normative protocol set: `SKILL.md`, `PROCESS.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CONSTRAINTS.md`, `SKILLS.md`, `README.md`, a Codex runtime document, and target-local `schema.xml`. Codex install-cli is generated from typed install semantics and exact release/checksum inputs. Claude-only history and examples remain outside Codex active links; any comparative fixture needs a file/line/reason golden.

Scan every Markdown, XML, YAML, JSON, and TOML file in the final plugin. Link-walk an installed cache. Direct assertions cover known protocol, schema, and installer hotspots; there is no blanket support-skill exemption. Exact empty-root and in-place output manifests detect missing and stale owned paths.

## 3. Default-depth orchestration

The supported entry path is the root Codex thread invoking `$pasture:epoch` or another Pasture role skill. With Codex's recommended default `agents.max_depth=1`, the root owns phase transitions, consensus, fan-out, worker/reviewer dispatch, waits, follow-ups, and consolidation. Architect/supervisor coordination executes as root skills when coordination is required. All spawned explorers, workers, and reviewers are depth-1 leaves.

Native agent projections are bounded leaves, not a nested hierarchy:

- `pasture_epoch`: analysis/status/root guidance; directs full orchestration to the root skill.
- `pasture_architect`: bounded requirements/proposal/handoff artifact.
- `pasture_supervisor`: bounded implementation-plan/progress artifact.
- `pasture_worker`: implementation or review-fix work.
- `pasture_reviewer`: plan or code review with required Beads writes.

Plugin-only delivery uses a current built-in/default leaf with a self-contained prompt whose first directive activates the exact namespaced skill. Healthy installed delivery may select `pasture_*` and elide redundant activation. Unavailable custom types fall back to plugin-only. Self-contained Beads handoffs inherit no conversation; follow-ups target the persistent leaf. Fan-out batches or serializes when thread capacity is small. Model, reasoning, sandbox, MCP, and skill overrides are omitted so live parent policy wins.

## 4. Plugin, skill metadata, and canonical agent bundle

Pasture emits `plugins/pasture/.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, all 31 canonical skills, and `skills/install-codex-agents`. Skill frontmatter uses unqualified name/description; installed invocations are namespaced. Every skill has exhaustive `agents/openai.yaml` with compatible display name, 25–64 character short description, and a default prompt naming its skill. `install-codex-agents` and the explicitly Claude-backed `swarm` set `allow_implicit_invocation=false`.

The rich compatible plugin manifest includes documented identity/interface/skills only—no agents field, install hook, unbacked app, or MCP declaration. Plugin add installs skills and zero native agents.

The setup skill owns exactly one bundle:

```text
skills/install-codex-agents/assets/agent-bundle/
  manifest.json
  agents/pasture_epoch.toml
  agents/pasture_architect.toml
  agents/pasture_supervisor.toml
  agents/pasture_worker.toml
  agents/pasture_reviewer.toml
```

The manifest freezes bundle schema and installer protocol; plugin/bundle semver; exact compatible CLI release tag and semver; minimum/tested Codex versions; checksum artifact name; supported OS/architecture matrix; and each canonical role ID, public name, safe relative path, SHA-256, and execution-policy projection. Both installer and Home Manager consume these exact bytes. The Go wire implementation is private `internal/codexbundle`; the JSON schema is the shared contract.

## 5. Exact CLI and setup contract

```text
pasture codex agents capabilities --format=json
pasture codex agents plan --bundle M [--project-root P|--no-project-check] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents install --bundle M --plan-digest D [--allow-downgrade] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents status [--bundle M] [project flags] --format=text|json
pasture codex agents recover --format=text|json
pasture codex agents uninstall --format=text|json
```

Stable JSON schemas and exit categories are black-box tested through the built Cobra binary. `capabilities` is a static zero-write report of CLI release tag/semver, protocols, supported platforms, and features. Bundle-less status reports only ledger/disk/journal integrity; `--bundle` adds desired version/hash comparison. Optional plugin observation is labeled unknown when unavailable and never constructs cache paths.

The persistent lock is an empty regular mode-0600 file created only by an authorized mutator. After rejecting unknown control entries, every first mutator performs the same secure mkdir and O_EXCL attempt; exactly one creates the inode. EEXIST means no-follow open/identity validation and blocking acquisition of that same inode, while transient ENOENT or replacement retries to the command deadline before CONCURRENT_CHANGE. A creator crash after mkdir leaves an exact empty bootstrap namespace that `recover`—or install carrying a still-valid pristine plan digest—may finish without deleting content. There is no loser protocol that waits forever on an absent inode.

When a valid lock exists, `plan` and `status` open it read-only with no-follow, verify regular type, identity, owner, link count, and restrictive mode, take a shared lock, wait for a mutator, and inspect one coherent snapshot without changing bytes or mtimes. When the lock is absent, they read two complete snapshots of lock identity, exact control entries, ledger, transactions, and managed generation. Stable all-absent snapshots are pristine and linearize before a later mutation; lock appearance or any identity change retries through the locked path; stable non-pristine state without a lock is BOOTSTRAP_INTERRUPTED/TAMPERED. Bounded retry exhaustion is CONCURRENT_CHANGE. An interrupted journal is reported, never repaired. Plan is non-authoritative and writes zero bytes. Its digest binds canonical bundle bytes, resolved Codex-home identity, ledger/current generation, journal state, collisions, explicit project decision, and options.

The lock inode is coordination metadata, not semantic installer state: absent pristine and a valid unheld lock with no ledger/journal/generation normalize to the same PRISTINE plan state. `recover`, `install`, and `uninstall` take the exclusive lock. Install reruns all validation; concurrent first installs with the same digest serialize, the winner proceeds, and later contenders reject stale consent after the committed semantic state changes. Transaction recovery invalidates consent and requires a fresh plan. Downgrade requires an audited flag.

The setup skill resolves its own bundle without cache-path inference, checks exact CLI capability, Codex compatibility, `bd`, Git, conditional repository commit policy, and optional `aura-swarm`. If CLI bootstrap is needed it invokes `$pasture:install-cli` with the bundle's exact tag. It displays plan, obtains scoped permission, installs with the bound digest, verifies status, and requires a fresh thread. It never changes Git config or hooks. Landing uses `git agent-commit` only when repository policy requires it and stops actionably when required but unavailable.

## 6. Recoverable managed-generation transaction

Threat model: untrusted bundle input, accidental corruption, crashes, concurrent Pasture commands, and path replacement—not a continuously racing privileged or malicious same-UID process.

```text
CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed/       complete companion generation
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.json    committed ledger
CODEX_HOME/pasture/agent-install.lock    persistent advisory-lock path
CODEX_HOME/pasture/transactions/<id>/    journal, staged new, old backup
```

With no journal, lstat every path component and recursively compare the complete managed generation against the committed ledger. Expected regular files, hashes, and relevant modes must match; expected directories must be present; unknown, missing, modified, or type-changed entries and all symlinks are TAMPERED. They stop with zero mutation and preservation/repair guidance. During an interrupted transaction, the journal—not the old ledger alone—is the identity authority.

Before staging, the first complete CREATED journal record stores operation/schema/transaction ID, contained candidate paths, prior generation+ledger identity `P` (or ABSENT), desired identity `N` (or ABSENT), and base64 canonical bytes/size/SHA-256/fixed temp+final paths for every generated agent and next-ledger payload. Recovery is self-contained after CREATED and never needs the plugin, bundle, network, or cache. The journal is a framed append-only hash chain: magic/schema, bounded length, canonical payload, monotonic sequence, previous-record hash, and SHA-256. Appends and directory changes are fsynced; there is no journal-replacement temp.

Staging itself is journaled. MKDIR_INTENT accepts its safe directory absent/present. WRITE_FILE_INTENT accepts its fixed temp absent or a regular file whose bytes are an exact prefix of the CREATED payload and whose length is at most expected. Full bytes must match size/hash and be fsynced. PUBLISH_FILE_INTENT accepts full temp/final absent or temp absent/final exact around atomic rename and parent fsync; FILE_PUBLISHED advances the deterministic path order. `next-ledger.json` follows the same protocol. Oversize/non-prefix bytes, wrong types, dual temp+final, unjournaled paths, or changed final bytes are TAMPERED, not honest partial writes. A partial first CREATED record has no oracle and is preserved STAGING_INCOMPLETE unless its transaction directory is empty. PREPARED is appended only after every final stage payload and fsync is exact.

Install/upgrade/downgrade uses this write-ahead automaton (`P` optional, `N` present):

| Journal state | Allowed physical shape(s) | Recovery direction |
|---|---|---|
| CREATED/STAGING | active+ledger=P; only declared staging candidates may be partial | journaled ABORT cleanup |
| PREPARED | active+ledger=P; generation-stage=N; next-ledger=N; backup absent | roll forward |
| MOVE_OLD_INTENT, only P present | before: active=P/backup absent; after: active absent/backup=P; both stages=N, ledger=P | roll forward both |
| OLD_MOVED, only P present | active absent; backup=P; both stages=N; ledger=P | roll forward |
| ACTIVATE_NEW_INTENT | before: active absent/generation-stage=N; after: active=N/stage absent; backup=P if any; ledger=P; next-ledger=N | roll forward both |
| NEW_ACTIVE | active=N; backup=P if any; generation-stage absent; ledger=P; next-ledger=N | roll forward |
| COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT | before: ledger=P/next-ledger=N; after: ledger=N/next-ledger absent; active=N | roll forward both |
| COMMITTED/CLEANUP | active+ledger=N; only recorded prior/cleanup suffix remains | ordered cleanup |

First install has `P=ABSENT` and skips MOVE_OLD_INTENT/OLD_MOVED. `next-ledger.json` is generated, hashed, fsynced, and journaled before PREPARED, then atomically renamed over the control ledger at COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT. Appending/fsyncing PREPARED happens only after consent and all validation/candidate fsyncs and is the semantic commit point; every later state completes N.

Uninstall uses a separate automaton (`P` present, `N` absent):

| Journal state | Allowed physical shape(s) | Recovery direction |
|---|---|---|
| CREATED/STAGING | active+ledger=P; only declared transaction candidates may be partial | journaled ABORT cleanup |
| PREPARED | active+ledger=P | roll forward |
| MOVE_OLD_INTENT | before: active=P/backup absent; after: active absent/backup=P | roll forward both |
| OLD_MOVED | active absent; backup=P; ledger=P | roll forward |
| COMMIT_LEDGER_INTENT | before: ledger=P/retired-ledger absent; after: ledger absent/retired-ledger=P; active absent | roll forward both |
| COMMITTED/CLEANUP | active+ledger absent; exact backup/retired-ledger cleanup suffix | ordered cleanup |

Uninstall has no ACTIVATE_NEW_INTENT or NEW_ACTIVE. It atomically renames the validated control ledger to journaled `retired-ledger.json` rather than unlinking it. PREPARED is also its semantic commit point, so all later states complete ABSENT. Thus journal state always selects one direction; generic `N=ABSENT` inference and restore-old rollback are forbidden.

Recovery uses the last complete hash-chained record. A partial tail may be truncated only when it is a prefix of the one canonical next record permitted by the observed physical state; otherwise all candidates are preserved. A transaction with no complete first record is STAGING_INCOMPLETE and removable only when empty.

One cleanup engine closes recovery-of-recovery, and it never calls recursive RemoveAll. Before deleting anything it journals a fully flattened deterministic lexicographic-postorder `CleanupEntry[]`: one unlink for every authorized regular/temp/next/retired file with exact or WRITE_FILE-prefix identity, followed by one rmdir for each now-empty directory. Symlinks and unknown types are never followed or deleted. For pre-PREPARED abort, `CLEANUP_INTENT{kind:ABORT, terminal:P}` lists only transaction-local authorized entries. For post-COMMITTED disposal, `kind:COMMIT`, terminal N/ABSENT lists the exact backup/retired/transaction entries.

At each `CLEANING{next_index}`, recovery validates path and parent identities, performs at most one unlink or rmdir, fsyncs that parent, then appends/fsyncs the next checkpoint. The current entry may be present or absent after a crash; two uncheckpointed missing entries, nonempty rmdir, out-of-order deletion, or changed content is TAMPERED. `CLEANUP_COMPLETE` requires the terminal active+ledger identity and no candidate except the journal. The journal remains until all other candidates are gone; after journal unlink, only an empty secure well-formed transaction-ID directory may be removed. No post-PREPARED recovery renames P back into the loader tree.

The honest guarantee is crash-recoverable quiescent installation: a concurrent Codex start can see the complete old set, a brief absence, or the complete new set, never a mixed Pasture generation. A fresh thread begins only after healthy status. Identical install is a true no-op preserving mtimes. No option in this feature adopts, overwrites, or deletes unknown/modified content.

All record writes use one named fault-injected append primitive. Tests cover before append, every injected short-write offset, complete bytes before file fsync, after file fsync, and after applicable parent fsync for CREATED, MKDIR_INTENT, WRITE_FILE_INTENT, PUBLISH_FILE_INTENT, FILE_PUBLISHED, PREPARED, every forward intent/milestone, COMMITTED, CLEANUP_INTENT, every CLEANING index, and CLEANUP_COMPLETE. A full valid PREPARED observed after restart commits even if the process did not observe fsync return; absent/partial PREPARED leaves STAGING as the last complete state and aborts.

Real subprocess tests also SIGKILL before/after each atomic unlink/rmdir/rename and kill every subsequent recovery process before running recover again. Coverage includes every payload prefix length and wrong-prefix position, oversize/dual temp-final, recursive postorder trees, nonempty rmdir, one- versus two-deletion successors, partial journal tails, first install/no-op/upgrade/downgrade/uninstall, all corrupt/forged/tampered candidates, two and three first mutators, stale consent, symlink/path swap, permissions, cleanup failure, and supported Linux/macOS semantics. Fresh `plan`/`status` tests compare complete bytes and mtimes before/after.

## 7. Ownership scope and Home Manager

Exclusive authority applies only to one personal `CODEX_HOME/agents/pasture-managed`: companion XOR Home Manager. Project `.codex/agents` directories are independent higher-precedence layers. `--project-root` checks exactly the resolved named project for same-name overrides; `--no-project-check` records the explicit skip. No global discovery or project ownership is claimed.

Aura adds only `CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.codex.agents.enable = false`; it does not sync Codex skills. Nix evaluation parses the canonical bundle manifest and derives the five mappings after schema/version/path/name/hash validation—there is no second role list.

When enabled, Home Manager owns one symlink at default `~/.codex/agents/pasture-managed` to an immutable generated store directory containing the exact TOMLs and an ownership manifest. A pre-link activation guard rejects a companion ledger, a regular managed directory, an arbitrary symlink, or malformed/modified ownership manifest before link mutation. It accepts absent state or a previous Home Manager-owned immutable target with exact membership, enabling repeat activation and upgrade. Companion symmetrically rejects the managed symlink. Disable removes only the Home Manager-owned link. A non-default `CODEX_HOME` is a separate companion target.

A pinned Home Manager fixture tests default, malformed bundle, enable, repeat enable, upgrade, companion/stale-ledger conflict with zero mutation, disable/removal, modified or arbitrary links, and preservation. Pinned Codex proves directory-symlinked TOMLs load and disappear.

## 8. One version, strict checksums, and release readiness

`.claude-plugin/plugin.json` stores the canonical bare semver. `pasture-release` is its sole mutating writer; codegen reads it and deterministically emits equal Codex plugin and bundle versions. Change `cmd/pasture/root.go` from `const version` to linker-injectable `var version = "dev"`. Release builds inject canonical `vX.Y.Z`; one parser exposes both tag and bare semver. CLI `--version`, capabilities, bundle constraint, generated versions, release tag, and release verification must agree.

Supported release tuples are exactly linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, and darwin/arm64. A release publishes `pasture`, `pastured`, and `pasture-release` for each tuple plus `SHA256SUMS`: exactly 12 lexicographically sorted, newline-terminated lines of `<64 lowercase hex><two spaces><basename>`, with no path separators. Bootstrap rejects missing, duplicate, extra, malformed, unsupported, version/tag-mismatched, untrusted redirect, and mismatched artifacts. It verifies the exact current-platform `pasture` in a private same-filesystem stage before rename or execution, then fsyncs and activates.

Fake-release tests exercise every negative case. After publish, a gate fetches the immutable actual tag/checksum roster and runs `pasture codex agents capabilities` for all four tuples on declared native/emulated runners. Aura cannot mark the entry AVAILABLE until this passes. `make generate` emits `claude-code,opencode,codex` and extends PR #35's drift gate. Release invokes generation; it does not rewrite generated sibling versions independently.

## 9. Exact Aura marketplace contract

Aura creates/updates its repo Codex marketplace at `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` and appends Pasture after existing entries. The entry is frozen as:

```json
{
  "name": "pasture",
  "source": {
    "source": "git-subdir",
    "url": "https://github.com/dayvidpham/pasture.git",
    "sha": "<40 lowercase hex commit>",
    "path": "./plugins/pasture"
  },
  "policy": {
    "installation": "NOT_AVAILABLE",
    "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"
  },
  "category": "Productivity"
}
```

It contains no `ref`, `repo`, products, plugin version, mutable branch, or default-install policy. The feature PR uses the immutable Pasture feature commit and NOT_AVAILABLE. A later release-backed change may set AVAILABLE only after the matching release/checksum/capability gate succeeds and the SHA is repinned to that immutable release commit.

## 10. Deterministic validation and clean-machine coverage

Mandatory hermetic tests cover roots/containment, the sole catalog, structural parts and full visitor, dialects/invocations, complete plugin/assets/link graph, manifest/TOML/schema/hash validation, transaction and CLI black boxes, exact target inventories/stale output, version parity, and Home Manager evaluation/activation. Every actionable error asserts what, why, where, operation/when, caller impact, and repair.

A pinned Codex 0.144.1 compatibility test uses fresh processes and isolated `HOME`/`CODEX_HOME`. App-server `skills/list` and plugin list/read prove 32 namespaced skills and zero plugin-installed agents. A local fake Responses-compatible provider captures the outbound model request's `spawn_agent` tool. Its `agent_type` schema is a plain string; the test parses the deterministic `Available roles:` entries in its description and asserts exact five custom names/descriptions/order, built-in preservation, and exact absence after removal. Stub responses issue each installed `pasture_*` tool call and verify it spawns; removed/unknown names yield the pinned validation error. Debug prompt/config and a nonexistent enum are not used. A separately labeled network/model UAT demonstrates actual selection and the default-depth plugin-only and installed paths.

Clean-machine fixtures vary isolated PATH/repository state for absent/incompatible/compatible Codex and Pasture, absent/present `bd` and Git, required present/missing `git agent-commit`, optional swarm, no repository, and fully provisioned setup. They assert fallback or exact failure plus no changes to hooks, Git configuration, default home, unrelated task DB, or cache.

Repo-owned Go/Nix checks are mandatory. Skill/plugin creator validators are recorded compatibility evidence with exact script hashes and interpreter dependencies, never ambient-home CI dependencies.

## 11. Buildable ownership and implementation sequence

One root implementor executes sequentially; exploration and adversarial reviewers do not edit.

1. Foundation owns `GenerationRoots`, the one catalog, structural runtime semantics/compiler, canonical assets/projections, and their tests. It does not register Codex or own target renderers.
2. Bundle-contract leaf creates private `internal/codexbundle` and freezes its JSON schema/fixtures.
3. Codex distribution owns all `codex_*` renderers/templates/tests, the complete 32-entry UI overlay, plugin/bundle emission, generated plugin tree, and the single final `harness.go` registration edit after its package builds independently.
4. Agent CLI owns `internal/codexagents`, `cmd/pasture/codex_agents*`, lifecycle/fake-release/black-box tests, and consumes only the frozen bundle contract.
5. Release integration alone owns `cmd/pasture/root.go`, release packages/tests, Makefile, checksum workflow/docs, all-target generation wiring, and version parity.
6. Aura owns `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, Home Manager module/fixture, README/inputs/lock, and the Pasture gitlink; it consumes the frozen bundle.

Any newly shared file is reassigned in Beads before editing. Sequence is roots/catalog/runtime → bundle schema → Codex emitter/integration → CLI/lifecycle → release/generate → immutable Pasture commit → Aura consumer. PR #35 stays the base until merged. Pasture merges/releases before a later Aura AVAILABLE change.

## BDD acceptance

1. Default `max_depth=1` reaches plan review, worker implementation, and code review with only root-to-leaf delegation.
2. The plugin-only path is complete; healthy custom types may be selected without duplicate activation and missing types fall back.
3. Empty and in-place all-target generation match exact paths/bytes and report stale owned outputs.
4. The final plugin contains 32 valid namespaced skills, all links/assets resolve, and no unapproved Claude operation remains.
5. Plugin add creates zero custom agents; explicit companion or Home Manager delivery exposes exactly five namespaced types without shadowing built-ins.
6. `capabilities`, `plan`, and `status` write zero bytes in healthy, pristine, bootstrap-interrupted, and transaction-interrupted states; the absent-lock double snapshot and existing-lock read path are race-safe.
7. Consent is bound to exact state. Recovery, collision, project decision, or any state change invalidates the digest before activation.
8. PREPARED is a durable roll-forward commit point; every prior partial stage has an exact byte-prefix oracle, and SIGKILL during atomic forward/flattened-cleanup steps resumes one direction or preserves all candidates.
9. Unknown, modified, missing, symlinked, malformed, downgraded, or unowned content is never silently moved, overwritten, adopted, or deleted.
10. Identical install preserves bytes and mtimes; uninstall removes only an exact owned generation.
11. Home Manager conflict fails before mutation; enable/repeat/upgrade/load/disable/removal succeeds from the canonical bundle.
12. A fake provider observes exact custom-role prose in `agent_type.description` and deterministically calls each installed/removed role; real model UAT separately demonstrates selection.
13. Strict checksum/bootstrap negatives fail before verified binary activation; the actual-release gate is required before marketplace availability.
14. One canonical version projects equal plugin/bundle/CLI/tag/checksum values, and release generation stays clean.
15. The exact Aura marketplace object is immutable and NOT_AVAILABLE in the stacked feature PR.
16. Any review finding causes a revised proposal or implementation and another three-axis round; progression requires a fix-free 0/0/0 wave.
17. After clean gates and user implementation UAT, evidence-backed Pasture and Aura PRs open in Pasture-before-Aura order.

## Out of scope

- Plugin-native custom agents or automatic install hooks.
- Raised-depth or nested Codex orchestration.
- Global project discovery, project ownership/export, or a project Home Manager mode.
- Codex backend for `aura-swarm`.
- Aura Codex skill sync.
- Git hook installation or Git configuration mutation.
- Silent adoption/deletion of tampered managed content.
- Vercel skills CLI, oh-my-codex, npm packaging, and ChatGPT-web local-agent claims.

# PROPOSAL-1: Codegen Body Integration

## Problem Space

**Axes:**
- **Parallelism:** 7 skill files can be converted independently (one slice per skill or per type change)
- **Distribution:** Single codebase — all work happens in `internal/codegen/` and `skills/`
- **Reliability:** Existing `TestGenerateIdempotent` tests for all 6 skill files provide safety net; goldmark adds structural validation

**Has-a / Is-a relationships:**
- A SkillFile *has-a* header (already generated) and *has-a* body (currently hand-authored)
- Body content *has-a* set of ProseSection, *has-a* set of code examples, and *has-a* set of bd command recipes
- ProseSection *is-a* titled, ordered markdown block (paragraph, table, list)
- BodyBehavior *is-a* ConstraintSpec (reuses existing G/W/T format)
- A CodeExample *is-a* unified Example (merging ExampleElem + ConstraintExampleElem)

## Engineering Tradeoffs

| Decision | Option A | Option B | Choice | Rationale |
|----------|----------|----------|--------|-----------|
| Body data structure | Flat markdown strings in specs_data.go | Typed Go structs (ProseSection, RecipeBlock) | **B: Typed structs** | Structured data enables validation, template composition, and future tooling. Raw markdown is opaque |
| Example type unification | Keep ExampleElem + ConstraintExampleElem separate | Merge into single Example type (Code optional) | **B: Merge** | URD R6 requires it; removes duplicate types; Code already exists as a field on Example — ConstraintExampleElem is redundant |
| Template structure | One mega-template for entire skill file | Extend existing skill_header.go.tmpl with body section | **Extend existing** | The template already renders header; adding body below END marker keeps the pipeline simple. Rename from `skill_header.go.tmpl` to `skill.go.tmpl` since it now renders the full file |
| Goldmark usage | Test-only (current) | Production code for validation | **Production** | URD R3 requires it; validates generated heading structure matches expectations |
| Migration approach | Incremental (one skill at a time) | All 7 at once | **All 7 at once** | URD R7 requires it; shared types (ProseSection, RecipeBlock) must exist before any skill can use them |

## Scope: What Changes

### 1. Type Cleanup (R6) — Unblocks Everything

**Current state:** `schema_types.go` has both `ExampleElem` (line 154) and `ConstraintExampleElem` (line 422). They are nearly identical — ConstraintExampleElem adds a `Code string` field.

**Change:** Delete `ConstraintExampleElem`. The existing `Example` type in `specs.go` (line 22) already has `Code string`. All constraint examples already use `Example` in `ConstraintSpec.Examples`. The `ConstraintExampleElem` in `schema_types.go` is used only for documentation of the XML shape — update the comment to reference `Example` instead.

**Impact:** `schema_types.go` loses one type. No functional change — `ConstraintExampleElem` was already NOT used for xml.Marshal (it was doc-only). The `Example` type in `specs.go` is the unified type.

### 2. New Types in `specs.go`

```go
// ProseSection is a titled block of markdown content for skill body rendering.
// Content is pre-formatted markdown (paragraphs, tables, lists, code blocks).
// Sections are rendered in Order within their parent context.
type ProseSection struct {
    ID      string // unique within the skill body, e.g. "sup-first-steps"
    Title   string // markdown heading text, e.g. "First Steps"
    Level   int    // heading level: 2 = ##, 3 = ###, etc.
    Order   int    // render order within body
    Content string // pre-formatted markdown content
}

// RecipeBlock is a phase-specific bd command recipe with context.
// Used for beads task creation templates, severity tree procedures, etc.
type RecipeBlock struct {
    ID          string // e.g. "arch-phase1-request"
    Title       string // e.g. "Phase 1: REQUEST Task"
    PhaseRef    protocol.PhaseId // optional phase association
    Order       int    // render order within section
    Description string // context paragraph before the code block
    Lang        string // code block language, typically "bash"
    Code        string // the actual bd command template
}

// SkillBody is the complete body content for a role or sub-skill.
// It replaces hand-authored content below the END marker.
type SkillBody struct {
    Preamble     string         // optional intro text before first section (e.g., link to PROCESS.md)
    Sections     []ProseSection // ordered prose sections
    Recipes      []RecipeBlock  // ordered bd command recipes
    Behaviors    []ConstraintSpec // body-specific G/W/T behaviors (reuses ConstraintSpec)
}
```

### 3. New Data in `specs_data.go`

Add a new top-level map:

```go
// SkillBodySpecs maps skill identifiers to their body content.
// Skill IDs are either role IDs (e.g., "supervisor") or command skill
// directory names (e.g., "supervisor-plan-tasks", "impl-review").
var SkillBodySpecs = map[string]SkillBody{
    "supervisor":              supervisorBody,
    "supervisor-plan-tasks":   supervisorPlanTasksBody,
    "supervisor-spawn-worker": supervisorSpawnWorkerBody,
    "worker":                  workerBody,
    "architect":               architectBody,
    "reviewer":                reviewerBody,
    "impl-review":             implReviewBody,
}
```

Each body is a package-level var containing structured data transcribed from the current hand-authored markdown. For example:

```go
var supervisorBody = SkillBody{
    Preamble: `**-> [Full workflow in PROCESS.md](../protocol/PROCESS.md#phase-8-implementation-plan)** <- Phases 7-12`,
    Sections: []ProseSection{
        {ID: "sup-ride-the-wave-detail", Title: "Ride the Wave — Operational Detail", Level: 2, Order: 1,
         Content: `### Stage 1: Plan _(sequential)_

- Read RATIFIED_PLAN and URD via ` + "`bd show`" + `
- Spawn ephemeral Explore subagents ...
...`},
        // ... more sections
    },
    Recipes: []RecipeBlock{
        {ID: "sup-create-impl-plan", Title: "Step 1: Create the IMPL_PLAN task", PhaseRef: protocol.PhaseImplPlan, Order: 1,
         Description: "Create the IMPL_PLAN task after reading the ratified plan:",
         Lang: "bash", Code: `bd create --labels "aura:p8-impl:s8-plan" \
  --title "IMPL_PLAN: <feature>" \
  ...`},
    },
}
```

**Estimated data volume:** ~2,112 lines of body content → ~2,500 lines of Go struct literals in specs_data.go (overhead from struct field names). Total specs_data.go grows from ~2,031 to ~4,500 lines.

### 4. Template Changes

**Rename** `skill_header.go.tmpl` → `skill.go.tmpl` (since it now renders the full file).

**Add body section** below the END marker:

```
<!-- END GENERATED FROM aura schema -->
{{- if .Body }}

{{ .Body.Preamble }}
{{- range .Body.Sections }}

{{ repeat "#" .Level }} {{ .Title }}

{{ .Content }}
{{- end }}
{{- range .Body.Behaviors }}

**Given** {{ .Given }} **when** {{ .When }} **then** {{ .Then }} **should never** {{ .ShouldNot }}
{{- end }}
{{- range .Body.Recipes }}

### {{ .Title }}

{{ .Description }}

```{{ .Lang }}
{{ .Code }}
```
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
```

The END marker stays in the output for visual separation (URD R4) but both sections are generated.

### 5. Update `skillHeaderContext` in `skills.go`

Add `Body *SkillBody` field to `skillHeaderContext`. Look up from `SkillBodySpecs` keyed by the skill directory name.

### 6. Update `GenerateSkill` and `GenerateSubSkill` in `skills.go`

- `GenerateSkill`: Full-file overwrite (no more marker-bounded replacement). The template renders the entire file.
- `GenerateSubSkill`: Same pattern — template renders full file content for sub-skills that have body content.

### 7. Goldmark Validation (R3)

Add a `ValidateSkillStructure` function that:
1. Parses generated markdown with goldmark
2. Walks the AST to extract heading hierarchy
3. Validates: no duplicate H2 titles, proper nesting (H3 under H2), all expected sections present
4. Called by `GenerateSkill` after rendering, before writing to disk

This catches structural regressions — e.g., a template change that produces `## Foo\n## Foo` (duplicate heading).

### 8. Test Strategy

- **TestGenerateIdempotent** (existing): Already tests all 6 skill files. After migration, these tests validate the complete file matches the golden output. This is the primary regression guard.
- **TestValidateSkillStructure** (new): Unit test for goldmark heading validation. Provide valid and invalid markdown inputs, assert correct pass/fail.
- **TestSkillBodySpecsCompleteness** (new): Verify every skill with a body in `SkillBodySpecs` has all required fields populated (non-empty Sections or Recipes).
- **TestExampleTypeUnified** (new): Verify `ConstraintExampleElem` no longer exists (compile-time check via type deletion).

### 9. Migration Tool (one-time)

A small `cmd/migrate-bodies/main.go` tool that:
1. Reads each skill file
2. Extracts body content (below END marker)
3. Prints Go struct literal for each body section

This is a development aid, not production code. It speeds up the transcription of ~2,112 lines of markdown into Go structs. Deleted after migration.

## Public Interfaces

```go
// specs.go — new types
type ProseSection struct { ID, Title string; Level, Order int; Content string }
type RecipeBlock struct { ID, Title string; PhaseRef protocol.PhaseId; Order int; Description, Lang, Code string }
type SkillBody struct { Preamble string; Sections []ProseSection; Recipes []RecipeBlock; Behaviors []ConstraintSpec }

// specs_data.go — new map
var SkillBodySpecs map[string]SkillBody

// skills.go — updated context
type skillHeaderContext struct { /* existing fields... */ Body *SkillBody }

// validation.go — new
func ValidateSkillStructure(markdown []byte) error
```

## Vertical Slice Decomposition

### SLICE-1: Type cleanup + new types
- Delete `ConstraintExampleElem` from `schema_types.go`
- Add `ProseSection`, `RecipeBlock`, `SkillBody` to `specs.go`
- Add `SkillBodySpecs` map skeleton to `specs_data.go`
- Update tests

### SLICE-2: Template + generation pipeline
- Rename `skill_header.go.tmpl` → `skill.go.tmpl`
- Add body rendering to template
- Update `skillHeaderContext` with `Body` field
- Update `GenerateSkill` for full-file overwrite
- Update `GenerateSubSkill` similarly
- Add `repeat` template function for heading levels
- Update `tools/codegen/main.go` template reference

### SLICE-3: Encode supervisor body content (609L)
- Transcribe supervisor/SKILL.md body into `supervisorBody` var
- Includes: Ride the Wave operational detail, First Steps, Exploration, Spawning Workers, FOLLOWUP lifecycle, Severity Tree, Tracking

### SLICE-4: Encode supervisor sub-skill bodies (596L)
- Transcribe supervisor-plan-tasks/SKILL.md body (372L) into `supervisorPlanTasksBody`
- Transcribe supervisor-spawn-worker/SKILL.md body (224L) into `supervisorSpawnWorkerBody`

### SLICE-5: Encode worker + architect bodies (420L)
- Transcribe worker/SKILL.md body (216L) into `workerBody`
- Transcribe architect/SKILL.md body (204L) into `architectBody`

### SLICE-6: Encode reviewer + impl-review bodies (481L)
- Transcribe reviewer/SKILL.md body (76L) into `reviewerBody`
- Transcribe impl-review/SKILL.md body (405L) into `implReviewBody`

### SLICE-7: Goldmark validation + final integration
- Add `ValidateSkillStructure` function
- Wire validation into `GenerateSkill` pipeline
- Move goldmark from test-only to production dependency
- Add `TestValidateSkillStructure`
- Add `TestSkillBodySpecsCompleteness`
- Run full `go generate` and verify all files are zero-diff with current output
- Delete hand-authored body content from skill files (now fully generated)

## Validation Checklist

- [ ] `ConstraintExampleElem` deleted from `schema_types.go`
- [ ] `ProseSection`, `RecipeBlock`, `SkillBody` types added to `specs.go`
- [ ] `SkillBodySpecs` map populated for all 7 skill files
- [ ] `skill_header.go.tmpl` renamed to `skill.go.tmpl` with body rendering
- [ ] `GenerateSkill` does full-file overwrite (not marker-bounded)
- [ ] `GenerateSubSkill` updated similarly for sub-skills with bodies
- [ ] `ValidateSkillStructure` validates heading hierarchy via goldmark
- [ ] `go generate ./internal/codegen/...` produces complete skill files
- [ ] All `TestGenerateIdempotent` tests pass with zero diff
- [ ] `TestValidateSkillStructure` covers valid and invalid inputs
- [ ] `TestSkillBodySpecsCompleteness` verifies all entries have content
- [ ] No hand-authored content remains below END markers
- [ ] Existing schema.xml generation unaffected (type cleanup is backward-compatible)
- [ ] `go test -race ./...` passes

## BDD Acceptance Criteria

**Given** `go generate ./internal/codegen/...` is run **when** all skill body content has been encoded into `SkillBodySpecs` **then** generated skill files match the current hand-authored content with zero diff **should not** produce files with missing sections, duplicate headings, or structural regressions

**Given** a `ProseSection` with content **when** the template renders **then** the heading level matches `Level`, content is rendered verbatim, and sections appear in `Order` **should not** re-wrap or reformat the markdown content

**Given** `ValidateSkillStructure` receives generated markdown **when** validating **then** it reports no duplicate H2 headings and proper nesting **should not** silently accept malformed heading hierarchies

**Given** `ConstraintExampleElem` is deleted from `schema_types.go` **when** the codebase compiles **then** all references use `Example` from `specs.go` instead **should not** have any remaining references to the deleted type

**Given** the migration tool extracts body content from a skill file **when** the extracted content is encoded in `SkillBodySpecs` and regenerated **then** the output matches the original hand-authored body byte-for-byte **should not** lose any content, reorder sections, or introduce formatting changes

# Independent Axis B: Test Quality and Validatability

VOTE: ACCEPT

## Finding

No blocking test-quality or validatability finding. PROPOSAL-7 converts the
load-bearing claims into independently falsifiable production-path, host-corpus,
append, malformed-ingress, version-evolution, authority-race, context, lineage,
privacy, compiler-boundary, one-substrate, one-FSM, replay, and bounded-resource
proofs at the milestone that first exposes each behavior.

Two implementation-plan guardrails do not require proposal revision:

1. If delivery is activated progressively before the all-30 M1 claim, each
   enabled event must have its own independent manifest row and authentic fixture
   for the exact host/runtime version, and support reporting must name only that
   verified subset. PROPOSAL-7 already prevents a false full-catalogue claim by
   keeping aura-plugins-9umx1 as a direct blocker for broad registration and M1.
2. The M3 forward/reverse lineage proof must instantiate the promised
   human-signal -> agent -> tool/VCS enrichment -> artifact/commit chain and its
   reverse, including ambiguity and missing-link cases, rather than use an
   arbitrary synthetic graph. Sections 1, 6.2, 7, and 14.4 already bind that
   outcome; the supervisor should preserve it as a named acceptance case.

## Review Against Assigned Questions

1. **Independent host oracle and progressive activation: adequate.** Section 11
   makes the private hostcontract the single production source while requiring
   one authentic fixture per event as an independent oracle. Section 14.1 runs
   all 30 exact-host fixtures through generated registration and the built
   process, preserves raw JSON/binary bytes outside YAML normalization, and keeps
   aura-plugins-9umx1 directly blocking broad registration/M1. This corrects the
   current identity-containment-only check at
   `internal/codegen/claude_hooks_test.go:66-112` and the self-derived catalogue
   loop at `internal/lifecycle/claude/frontend_test.go:495-529`. The hand-written
   seven-case tolerance table at
   `internal/lifecycle/claude/frontend_test.go:329-357` is useful but cannot
   authenticate the complete pinned host contract. Progressive activation is
   safe only under the subset guardrail above; otherwise the proposal waits for
   all 30 and makes no partial-support claim.

2. **Required connected black-box path: adequate and milestone-correct.** Section
   14.1 names three non-substitutable tests: generated registration/trampoline ->
   exact built binary/stdin -> file-backed SQLite -> T1 -> public bounded reader
   at M1; the same path through T2 facts/links/candidates at M2; and a real
   hook-produced candidate through production authority/T3 at M6. Direct
   interpreter calls, direct Apply calls, projection writers, and test-only
   exports explicitly do not satisfy the gate. The current spine reaches a real
   binary but asserts the superseded audit/activity path and digest collapse at
   `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:204-260`, while the recorder writes
   direct audit/activity SQL at `internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder.go:399-510`;
   neither can accidentally count as the new proof.

3. **Append and malformed matrix: adequate.** Sections 3.2, 5.3, 5.4, 14.1, and
   the M1 essential gate require a fresh non-payload operation for every host
   invocation, byte-identical double delivery, concurrent receipts, and the
   generated built-process path against one file. The invalid matrix states each
   append/no-append outcome: trusted known event plus malformed fields/bytes,
   duplicate key, invalid UTF-8, truncation, over-limit, unsupported schema, or
   event mismatch appends bounded T1 parse evidence and nothing later; an
   untrusted unknown event or unregistered coordinate appends nothing; store
   failure makes no false receipt claim. Missing, invalid, redacted, and
   over-limit capture states cannot become confident T2 facts. The implementation
   plan must realize the concurrent case with distinct binary processes or
   independently opened handles, not only goroutines sharing one tracker. The
   old opposite assertions are visible at
   `cmd/pasture/hook_lifecycle_spine_test.go:231-240,262-408`,
   `internal/handlers/hook_lifecycle_test.go:44-109`, and
   `internal/tasks/lifecycle_recorder_test.go:104-134`.

4. **Immutable definitions and exact version envelope: adequate.** Sections 4.2,

All 365 statements are named only sqlStatement001 through sqlStatement365 and owned by one 1,128-line switch, while argument construction and row decoding remain in domain files. This avoids duplicate SQL sink ownership, but replaces it with opaque cross-file coupling: reviewers must jump between a numeric call site and a distant global case to understand one query, and unrelated SQLite/DBOS changes all contend on the same enum and switch. The tiny taskEventQueryOrder wrapper demonstrates a second mapping layer rather than semantic statement identity.

Impact: no current public or DBOS runtime regression was observed, and the full/race suites pass, but future stacked DBOS and SQLite branches incur unnecessary merge conflicts and can mis-pair a numeric ID with options/result decoding without locally meaningful names. The centralization cost grows linearly with every query and is not proportional to the safety invariant.

Fix: retain one structurally checked execution boundary while giving statements semantic typed identities and domain-local ownership through sealed descriptors/constructors that the package-wide AST test can enumerate. Keep each query adjacent to its argument/result contract or generate the central table from those typed declarations. Add duplicate-query/identity and full-wiring checks so decentralizing declaration does not reopen arbitrary SQL strings.

authority for a new operation, and never accepts an actor/supervisor
override for review or slice closure. Bootstrap/administrative callers use a
separate registered-agent API and make no authentication claim. Queries are

## 12. Simple installer

Canonical preferences are exactly:

```yaml
install:
  harnesses:
    claude-code: false
    opencode: false
    codex: false
  extensions:
    skills: true
    agents: true
    hooks: false
```

This is one harness boolean map plus one global extension map—not a per-harness
extension matrix. The TUI has harness checkboxes, one global extension page,
saved choices, exact install/uninstall summary, confirmation, and progress.
Cancellation changes nothing.

After confirmation Pasture preserves unrelated YAML and saves preferences before
native actions. It normalizes the confirmed preferences to one immutable
`pasture.install.effective-selection/v1` desired document, then passes that to
`apply-selection --source installer`. TUI effective cells are
`harness && extension`. The persisted config remains simple global preferences
and never stores the normalized matrix or installation evidence.

The fixed reconciler is deliberately small:

- desired effective true: idempotently ensure present/update, including an
  unchanged true cell;
- desired effective false plus a Pasture-managed installed/unknown inventory
  record: inspect and idempotently remove the exact component; and
- desired false with no Pasture-managed or uncertain record: no mutation.

Thus first-run false harnesses are untouched, a failed uninstall remains visible
and retryable after the preference already says false, and unrelated native
installations or identical external files are observed but never claimed or
removed. A global extension change fans out across the currently desired and
recorded managed cells.

The installer applies all cells, including its own direct-file destinations.
Home Manager independently renders the same effective schema from its per-
harness children but calls only native-managed cells; Nix owns direct-file link
transitions. Schema-validation, normalization, transition, and source-ownership
fixtures prove the two inputs agree for equivalent choices without conflating
their execution responsibilities.

Save failure invokes no native action. Any native/file failure stops immediately;
the postcondition probe updates the factual inventory where possible, earlier
completed actions remain, and later actions are unattempted. The error names what
failed, why, the cell/path/manager and stage, what remains or is unknown, caller
impact, `pasture install status`, and the exact executor-aware tagged
remediation. There is no rollback, background recovery, lock, authorization, or
cross-cell transaction coordinator. Native managers own plugin/update/cache
state; Pasture never writes private caches.

Pasture #45 publishes the exact legacy and split Claude package identities plus
fixtures; #39 alone owns this compatibility behavior. Before mutation #39
classifies native state as empty, exact v0.0.4 monolith only, split only, exact
monolith plus complete/partial known splits, or unknown. Unknown identity,
scope, version, or duplicate/conflicting rows perform zero mutation. For each
known state the frozen order is: probe/list and validate; ensure/update every
desired split; verify it; remove the exact user-scoped v0.0.4 monolith; verify
absence; remove any unselected known split; verify final state; record the
inventory. Failure at every action stops later actions, probes and records what
actually remains, and the next ordinary run resumes reconciliation without
rollback. Codex hooks finish as installed-but-requiring-native-trust-review until
the user approves them in Codex; this trust state is reported, not bypassed.

The v0.0.4 monolith transition is selection-wide and is implemented exclusively
by `apply-selection`, which has every Claude sibling's desired state. While the
monolith or an incomplete legacy transition exists, `apply-cell` fails before
mutation and instructs the caller to rerun the full installer/TUI or Home Manager
activation with an exhaustive desired selection. It never guesses sibling
intent, and a cell-level failure row prints that same full-selection remedy.

The group probes even for an all-false/no-inventory selection so the approved
monolith exception is discoverable when the supported manager is available. If
that optional read-only probe is missing, out-of-range, nonzero, or malformed,
all three never-recorded false rows are `completed` with operation
`no_op_unavailable` and a nonfatal diagnostic that unverified legacy state was
preserved; no inventory or mutation occurs. A supported valid-empty probe is the
same completed no-op, while an exact monolith enters the group removal.

A syntactically valid optional all-false/no-inventory response containing an
exact split component, near-match monolith, wrong scope/version, unknown selector,
or duplicate/conflicting rows performs zero mutation and writes no inventory.
Exact split components are reported `completed/no_op_preserved_external` with
their observed identity; near-match/unknown/duplicate/conflicting state is
`completed/no_op_preserved_ambiguous` with `ok=true` plus a preservation
diagnostic. This optional mode succeeds because no desired or managed cell
requires authority and preservation is the requested behavior.

If any Claude cell is desired true or has managed/unknown inventory, the same
initial probe failure is terminal before mutation: the first canonical required
row is `failed`, other executable rows are `unattempted`, prior inventory is
unchanged, and remediation names the exact binary/version/response repair.

In required mode, an exact desired split already present without inventory is
observed external and may satisfy desired true without adoption; an exact
external split under desired false is preserved. A near-match, wrong scope/
version, unknown selector, duplicate, or conflicting response is terminal
`failed/ambiguous_native_state` before mutation, leaves prior inventory unchanged,
and uses the appropriate ApplySelection/RerunInstaller or RerunHomeManager tagged
remediation. A managed/unknown inventory record that no longer matches exact live
identity is likewise a terminal conflict, never silently externalized.

The group crosses the classified legacy state with
all eight Claude desired combinations, executes each ensure/remove exactly once,
and skips the three ordinary Claude executors. On failure, it live-inspects all
three cells: rows already satisfying desired state are `completed`; the first
canonical unsatisfied row is `failed` with `group_stage` and the exact native
action; other unsatisfied Claude rows and later executable native rows are
`unattempted`. If all split postconditions match but monolith removal alone
fails, `claude-code.skills` is the fixed control/failure row and the diagnostic
names that shared legacy stage. Home Manager declarative rows remain live-
inspected `managed_declaratively`. Full-selection retry repeats the group probe
and converges without duplicate per-cell actions.

If live inspection after an action failure is itself missing/nonzero/malformed,
only rows with already verified individual postconditions remain `completed`.
The action-owning row is `failed` with both primary action and secondary probe
diagnostics and its inventory observation `unknown`; every other unverified
Claude cell is `unattempted`/`unknown`. No row is guessed from desired state.
Ordinary full-selection retry repairs the probe first and resumes from factual
inventory/live inspection.

## 13. Aura Home Manager migration and parity

New exact option nesting is:

```nix
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".enable = false;
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".skills.enable = true;
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".agents.enable = true;
CUSTOM.programs.aura-config-sync.harnesses."claude-code".hooks.enable = false;
```

OpenCode and Codex mirror this. Children remain inert until their parent is true.

The live options are not silently dropped. Aura #8 freezes this compatibility
table for one release:

| Old option | Compatibility behavior | New destination |
|---|---|---|
| `commands.enable` with all roles enabled | deprecated alias; enables Claude parent + skills | `harnesses."claude-code".{enable,skills.enable}` |
| `agents.enable` | deprecated alias; enables Claude parent + agents | `harnesses."claude-code".{enable,agents.enable}` |
| `opencode.skills.enable` | deprecated alias; enables OpenCode parent + skills | `harnesses.opencode.{enable,skills.enable}` |
| `opencode.agents.enable` | deprecated alias; enables OpenCode parent + agents | `harnesses.opencode.{enable,agents.enable}` |
| non-default `commands.roles.*` | exact legacy filtered DirectFile projection for one release | no aggregate-plugin equivalent; choose all skills or retain compatibility mode during the window |
| `commands.extraCommands` | additive user DirectFiles | `harnesses."claude-code".skills.extraFiles` |
| `agents.extraAgents` | additive user DirectFiles | `harnesses."claude-code".agents.extraFiles` |

The legacy filtered projection and the new aggregate Claude skills plugin are
mutually exclusive; selecting both is an evaluation error naming both option
paths and the two repairs. Extra files are active only when their harness and
extension are enabled, remain separate from generated plugin ownership, and are
rejected at evaluation when their canonical skill/agent identity collides with
the generated bundle or another extra. Every alias/mode emits its exact
replacement warning. Top-level module enable with no harness parent warns that
parent defaults changed to false. After the one-release window, removed legacy
role-filter options produce an actionable error; the additive `extraFiles`
destinations remain. Packages/protocol options remain unchanged.

Generated Pasture artifacts come only from the pinned Pasture source; explicitly
configured user `extraFiles` remain separately owned inputs and are never folded
into generated bundles.

Home Manager projects those pinned generated trees/files plus the separately
declared extras. Its current generation contains one fully explicit
`pasture.install.effective-selection/v1` desired document rendered from the nine
child options, and activation passes it to
`pasture install apply-selection --source home-manager`. The command
acts only on native-managed cells. Direct-file cells remain ordinary Home Manager
links at their documented paths and return `managed_declaratively` if inspected;
Nix never asks `apply-cell` to mutate them. There is no interactive TUI call,
duplicated native argv, or Nix-side operational state model. #39's native actions
update the same factual installation inventory so a failed native uninstall is
visible and retryable on activation rerun. Hooks require explicit true, Codex
hook activation preserves native trust review, and Aura #9 supplies the
validated aggregate marketplace plus gated `pasture-stable` ref.

# FOLLOWUP_PROPOSAL-41 — Typed multi-harness compiler, authoritative task journal, and AFK mode

## 1. Decision and correction from Proposal 40

Pasture will compile opaque, validated Go `Document` values into native Claude
Code, OpenCode, and Codex artifacts. Portable meaning lives in a
protocol-semantic IR. Markdown is parsed with Goldmark, not searched and rewritten
as an operational language. Native runtime calls are emitted only through an
exhaustive, version-bounded runtime contract.

Provenance will own one generic, ordered TaskEvent journal and the transaction
boundary that commits task/graph/Activity state with its events. Current task
tables remain authoritative; the journal explains post-migration changes and is
not an event-sourced replacement for historical state. Pasture owns typed
`pasture.*` event definitions and the `pasture task` CLI that generated workflows
use instead of Beads.

Native plugin registration is deliberately separate from runtime semantics. A
versioned activation contract describes public version probes, exact manager
commands or config mutation, package identities, and standalone destinations.
`pasture install` keeps the user's simple preferences separate from a narrow,
factual installation-state inventory. That inventory records what Pasture
confirmed it installed or removed, what remains, and the last actionable
failure. It is not a pending-operation queue, rollback log, authorization
system, lock, or cross-cell transaction coordinator.

Proposal 41 retains all accepted Proposal 40 invariants and resolves every
Proposal 40 Terra finding. OpenCode hooks are generated as an embedded,
auto-discovered TypeScript file for this wave; no npm publication or native npm
plugin mutation is required before the hook behavior has been verified. Target
packages publish target identity plus RuntimeContractID, while #39 alone binds
those artifacts into opaque activation contracts. Provenance lands as the strict
chain #4 -> #5 -> #14, with #4 dormant until #5 activates atomic journaling and
the migration baseline. Upstream issues publish fixtures/oracles; downstream
Aura issues alone own Home Manager parity and real `pasture-stable` promotion.

This epoch's original Plan-UAT skip is an explicit authorization scoped only to
REQUEST `aura-plugins-ydhf9`; it is not retroactively treated as a general rule.
Separately, the user now requests a reusable product feature: explicit,
default-off, per-epoch lower-interaction AFK mode. A session may toggle between
normal and AFK at will without ending any running agent session. AFK mode may
defer Plan-UAT questions and continue review/fix, ratification, implementation,
and review/fix progression, while recording every user and agent decision with
typed decider identity. Implementation UAT stops autonomous progression without
terminating agents. The DBOS-backed ledger itself is the canonical decision
producer: mode/UAT/agent commands append entries atomically with their state
changes. AFK never authorizes landing,
hooks, destructive operations, secrets, unrelated external effects, or scope
outside its epoch. The current epoch continues under its existing Beads
authorization; future epochs use the typed AFK contract.
